Name: Atelier Moessmer Norbert Niederkofler
Address: Via Walther Von der Vogelweide 17, Brunico, 39031, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Situated in a vast historic park near the centre of Brunico, this restaurant occupies a villa that was once part of the Moessmer textile factory – to illustrate the fact, an interesting fabric book dating from the early 20C is displayed on a large central table in the dining room. Here, the chef’s “Cook the Mountain” philosophy takes centre stage with a focus on top-quality produce sourced from the surrounding mountains, and a seasonal approach which ensures that flavours and ingredients are always at their best. Dinner starts with delicious appetisers served in the small lounge, perhaps accompanied by an aperitif. Having enjoyed this delicious prelude, you then move to the dining room or to the counter with its stools facing the kitchen. Wherever you choose to sit, you continue with the chef’s single tasting menu – a series of superb dishes that confirm this chef from the Ahrntal valley as one of the masters of contemporary Italian cuisine.

Name: Casa Perbellini 12 Apostoli
Address: Vicolo Corticella San Marco 3, Verona, 37121, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Verona’s quintessential historic and elegant restaurant, this is where Chef Perbellini, already two-starred at a previous location, achieved the coveted three stars. Expect a sumptuous, refined setting, rich with color and historical references, paired with extraordinary cuisine expressed through three tasting menus, with dishes also available à la carte. “Io e Silvia” showcases the chef’s latest creations; choose “L’Essenza” for a vegetarian journey; while “Storie di Casa” presents the chef’s signature dishes in a contemporary key. But there is yet another option: the chef’s table, in effect a separate room with five intimate tables set amid the open kitchen, featuring a single menu and the exhilarating experience of dining among the cooks.

Name: Da Vittorio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Now among the most celebrated restaurants in Italy, Da Vittorio has retained the warmth of its delightfully familial management. Both in the kitchen and in the dining room, members of the Cerea family are ever-present, and the dishes themselves speak to their talent for elevating top-quality ingredients into beautifully presented, deeply flavorful recipes, all in pursuit of a comforting, satisfying style of cooking. Generosity is another hallmark here, evident from the breadth of the offering! In addition to the à la carte menu, guests may choose from 4 tasting menus: “Gli esordi di papà Vittorio” (eight meat-based courses inspired by traditional recipes), “Dalla nostra campagna” (eight courses centered on vegetables from the estate garden and the Planet Farm), “Senza Confini” (twelve courses for a singular experience, guided by the chefs’ unfettered creative freedom), “Nella tradizione di Vittorio” (eight courses featuring fish and shellfish, prepared with the freshest market arrivals). The finale is elevated further by a superb cheese trolley and an array of sucreries to close the meal on a high note.

Name: Dal Pescatore Santini
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Three-starred since 1996 – a record in Italy – and approaching its centenary, this restaurant is an unmissable landmark for understanding the history of Italian gastronomy. In Runate, a small hamlet in the countryside between Cremona and Mantua, a family osteria of long standing has been transformed into a place of rare elegance and genuine hospitality. In the dining room, Antonio Santini, flanked by his family, welcomes guests with warmth, while in the kitchen a tradition of rigour, sensitivity and continuity is lovingly perpetuated. The interiors, balanced between memory and contemporaneity, create a refined atmosphere in which space and light enhance every detail. The menu celebrates great dishes that have traversed the decades, evolving with quiet discretion and never yielding to fashion, in constant pursuit of pleasure at the table. Among the specialities, roasts and braises – using meats from the Cascina Runate – stand alongside emblematic preparations such as the Petit Gris snails of the plain with herb and sweet garlic sauce. The desserts merit particular mention: united by a measured indulgence, they strike a perfect balance between intensity and refinement, embodying the most accomplished meeting of pleasure and elegance. The meringues with pistachio and almond mousse and Marsala zabaione are irresistible, and display great harmony throughout.

Name: Enoteca Pinchiorri
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the world of fine dining, Via Ghibellina is synonymous with Enoteca Pinchiorri: the magnificent seventeenth-century palazzo that houses it is home to one of the most iconic restaurants in Italy, a true legend of gastronomy. Opened in 1972 by Annie Féolde and Giorgio Pinchiorri, what began as a modest wine shop with a kitchen has over time become a great restaurant, in which Florentine history and elegance intertwine among paintings, frescoes and vivid arrangements of fresh flowers. At the stove, the cooking aspires to a refinement free of ostentation, eschewing fleeting fashions in favour of luxurious ingredients and a profound Italian identity, its flavours at once intense and rounded, destined to linger long in the memory. A fundamental role is played by the pastry kitchen, where Francesco Federici produces extraordinary desserts, among them the indispensable soufflé. In the dining room, an impeccable crew is led by the experienced Alessandro Tomberli, a historic figure at the Enoteca. And the wine cellar? A unique and quite simply mythological treasure, completing one of the most celebrated and cherished gastronomic experiences the country has to offer.

Name: Enrico Bartolini al Mudec
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: In his Milanese restaurant, the headquarters of the Bartolini international galaxy, the great chef – far from taking a break – continues to craft new dishes alongside resident chef Davide Boglioli, always focusing on fullness and intensity of flavors. There's nothing overly cerebral, though you can delve into the layers, references, and echoes if you wish. Or simply enjoy the perfect balance of the results. There are two tasting options: "Best Of" and "Mudec Experience," but dishes can also be selected à la carte. During our last visit, we were particularly struck by the creaminess and harmony of the beetroot risotto with “Evoluzione” gorgonzola sauce. And speaking of cheeses, we recommend trying (off-menu) "Our Tasting of 5 Creative Cheeses," with rare and intriguing pairings. All of this is set on the third floor of Mudec, the Museum of Cultures, in a refined and elegantly contemporary lounge space.

Name: La Pergola
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The new Pergola, following meticulous refurbishment, welcomes guests into surroundings that seem to breathe with the city: the hues of travertine, reflections of Roman red, soft light gliding across surfaces echo the soul of the capital and transform it into atmosphere. The terrace, too, has been renewed, yet the true spectacle remains unchanged: Rome, as evening falls, spreads silently at the foot of Monte Mario, a sea of rooftops and domes appearing suspended, as if holding its breath. At the stoves since 1994, Heinz Beck continues to drive his cooking towards new sensitivities, moving effortlessly between classic elegance and contemporary creativity. Many preparations are completed and finished directly at the table, releasing aromas and gestures that add theatre to the moment: vapours, textures, small details that come to life before the guest’s eyes, rendering the experience yet more immersive. In his pursuit of healthfulness and lightness, Beck deepens techniques and studies, selecting sustainable ingredients and transforming them with an almost scientific rigour, giving rise to dishes that are lucid, calibrated, vibrant in flavour yet delicate in structure. This is cooking that speaks to the palate but also to the mind, with intelligence and luminosity. Completing the journey, the extraordinary wine list finds in sommelier Marco Reitano a flawless interpreter: a master in the art of pairing, he welcomes guests with a smile and rare expertise, truly adding that finishing touch that renders the evening unforgettable.

Name: La Rei Natura by Michelangelo Mammoliti
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: This young yet already established Piedmontese chef, of part-Calabrian heritage, offers a creative and personal cuisine deeply anchored in its raw materials, particularly vegetables, the majority of which are sourced from his own kitchen gardens and greenhouses, managed according to biodynamic principles.Three tasting menus are available, from which individual dishes may also be chosen à la carte: De Rerum, comprising ten courses, presents the most complete and current expression of the chef’s vision; MAD 100% Natura places the plant world at the very centre, with animal protein in a discreet supporting role; and Voyage, which conveys bolder flavours reflecting the influences gathered during his international experiences. Among the dishes, the red mullet fillet in valenciana sauce stands out for its intensity and precision. The gastronomic offering finds its natural counterpoint in an outstanding wine list: in the heart of the Langhe, Barolo reigns supreme, presented in an extensive selection of crus and vintages. A young, dynamic, and efficient front-of-house team contributes to making the overall experience harmonious and engaging.

Name: Le Calandre
Address: Via Liguria 1, località Sarmeola, Rubano, 35030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Leaving the provincial road and commercial zone behind, one enters the fabulous world of Le Calandre and the Alajmo family: soft lighting – achieved even by day – serves almost as a design element in the pared-back dining room, conceived by brothers Massimiliano and Raffaele, who also designed most of the porcelain used in service. The offering unfolds through three tasting menus: Classico, Max, and Raf, with the generous option to mix them freely or compose a meal as if ordering à la carte. Suspended between comforting flavors and whimsical touches, Max’s cuisine occasionally references itself through restaurant classics, such as the cuttlefish cappuccino in squid ink alongside the more modern Murrina version, an homage to the famed island of Murano and its colorful blown glass. The inspector recommends: Suono N'uovo, a tagliatella whose dough incorporates specially treated eggshell, adding an unexpected and delightful crunch.

Name: Osteria Francescana
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: On arriving in Via Stella, one immediately senses how naturally this restaurant frees itself from frills and accolades, embracing instead a sober elegance, enhanced by major works of contemporary art that reflect Massimo Bottura’s personal passion. The same measured language returns in the kitchen, where greatness is expressed through control, balance and vision: a narrative that begins in Modena and Emilia before reaching towards the great international classics, reinterpreted by the chef with that playful lightness which reminds us that food should first and foremost be pleasure, memory and culture. The most innovative tasting menu of the moment, Miseria e Nobiltà, takes its inspiration from Eduardo De Filippo’s celebrated work and offers a journey that elevates essential ingredients and “humble” resources with surprising refinement. Among the emblematic dishes, Jazz Duck stands out: duck presented in several preparations to showcase every part of the bird, served alongside an unusual glazed panettone that perfectly completes its intensity. Alternatively, guests may choose from the à la carte menu, which features some of the chef’s great classics: “An eel swimming up the River Po”, Modenese tortellini in a silky 36-month Parmigiano Reggiano sauce, and hot-and-cold zuppa inglese, together with the finest dishes from tasting menus of years past. The wine list, exceptionally rich in outstanding labels, nevertheless also includes lesser-known bottles, the result of research into small producers capable of telling the stories of often unfamiliar places and terroirs, rounding off a gastronomic experience that unites local identity, curiosity and great culinary culture.

Name: Piazza Duomo
Address: Vicolo dell'Arco 12, Angolo Piazza Risorgimento 4, Alba, 12051, Italy
Description: The now famous red door ushers you into this temple of Italian cuisine. Once you cross the threshold, stairs lead up to the first floor, where pink walls and a fresco by Francesco Clemente welcome you, as do the friendly front-of-house staff. From here on, the focus is on chef Enrico Crippa's very personal cuisine, presented in three tasting menus (a fourth, shorter menu is available at lunchtime only): one linked closely to the vegetable gardens and the seasons, another intimately connected to the local area, and the last taking you on a journey through Italy and beyond. What emerges from every single delicious mouthful is the chef's passion for the plant world: vegetables, flowers and aromatic herbs, both cultivated and wild, are harvested daily and used to create memorable and aesthetically perfect dishes. The iconic appetiser, with its thousand and one delicious ingredients, continues to delight the eyes of the Inspectors. It goes without saying that we are in a land with a passionate love of wine, and indeed there are three whole volumes dedicated to it: Solopiemonte is a superb tribute to the region, while Tuttoilresto (divided into red and white wines) celebrates France. Simply put, the wine list is so extensive and varied that it alone is reason enough to visit the restaurant. And if you prefer to order by the glass, let yourself be intrigued by Sorsi: a small selection offering themed tastings, to be enjoyed according to personal preference or following a menu-based flight, with each glass telling a different story.

Name: Reale
Address: Contrada Santa Liberata, località Casadonna, Castel di Sangro, 67031, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: On the first hilly slopes that embrace the village, amidst vineyards and silent gardens, the austere simplicity of the former 16th century monastery perfectly reflects the culinary language of one of the most recognisable fine dining experiences in Italy. Niko Romito continues to define - and refine - his vision here: a rigorous minimalism that never relinquishes sensory depth, expressed through dishes based on the measured use of just a few ingredients – be they vegetables or proteins – orchestrated with almost ascetic precision.The research continues relentlessly, as does the link with Abruzzo: products, recipes and culinary heritage come together in a constant drive towards evolution, keeping all the intensity of flavour and clarity on the palate intact.The bread and the entire range of baked goods are excellent, as always. The result of the almost maniacal selection of flours, long and carefully controlled proving times, and a bakery dedicated exclusively to doughs and breads of all kinds. The bread is so carefully crafted that it could almost be considered a course in its own right, capable of conveying the establishment’s methods and philosophy all on its own.

Name: Uliassi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: A perfect protagonist of summer postcards, the Adriatic Riviera becomes a canvas – or, if you prefer, an auteur film – through the compelling interpretation of Mauro Uliassi. The restaurant appears almost hidden among the beach establishments that dot the Senigallia shoreline: it is difficult to imagine that, amid parasols and breaking waves, one of Italy's most celebrated tables lies concealed – the holder of 3 MICHELIN Stars! The strength and originality of Uliassi's cuisine reside in his capacity to begin with what surrounds him, engaging with the most familiar gastronomic traditions of this coast and transforming them into personal, surprising and contemporary creations. In business since 1990, the restaurant has over the years built a repertoire of iconic dishes that still today form the backbone of the offering: from the smoked spaghetti with clams and roasted datterini tomatoes to the Marche-style woodpigeon, the red prawn with orange, ginger, and cinnamon, a preparation that is only apparently simple, capable with extraordinary elegance of celebrating all the freshness and intensity of the crustacean. Those wishing to explore the chef's most recent intuitions may entrust themselves to the Lab tasting menu, while lovers of bolder flavours will find in the Caccia menu a journey of great character.

Name: Villa Crespi
Address: Via Fava 18, Orta San Giulio, 28016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A short walk from the fairytale village and its postcard-perfect view of the lake and the island of San Giulio, the setting of this three-star restaurant is no less dazzling: a late nineteenth-century villa in Moorish style, an aristocratic dwelling where the Crespi family life unfolded, as imposing in its exterior appearance as it is fascinating in its interior rooms. Here the veranda offers glimpses and plays of natural light, while the other three rooms are embellished with elaborate ceilings and marvelous parquet floors. Today the star of the villa is Antonino Cannavacciuolo, a brilliant chef at the head of a small empire of starred restaurants, who here in Orta San Giulio has his flagship: the most awarded and celebrated establishment! From Vico Equense in Campania, over the years his dishes have become the quintessence of Mediterranean and Italian taste. In all offerings you’ll find that passion, those colors and that intensity of flavors typical of his region of origin, which we are grateful he has never abandoned. In the two tasting menus, as well as in the extensive à la carte menu, an uninterrupted fil rouge of refinement and goodness flows generously through seafood, meat, and even vegetarian recipes. You’ll be pampered by service that runs like a metronome, supported in turn by a profound wine list, where two chapters of great importance dedicated to Krug and Domaine de la Romanée-Conti stand out.

Name: ACQUOLINA | Nuova Cucina Mediterranea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Just steps from Piazza del Popolo, the elegant First Roma welcomes guests with courteous, impeccable hospitality before leading them into a dining room of understated design, in keeping with contemporary taste, yet with tables still set with style and attentive service described as “dynamic” by its own team. At center stage is the cuisine of Daniele Lippi, who interprets the Mediterranean in its broadest sense, reaching well beyond national borders. Two tasting menus are offered: Periplo, dedicated to the aquatic world, and Anabasi Catabasi, which incorporates meat as well. Both conclude with a generous selection of desserts, the perfect finale to a gastronomic journey that is as intriguing as it is indulgent. Equally noteworthy is the wine offering, enhanced by an extensive list and the expertise of sommelier Francesco Aldieri.

Name: Agli Amici
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Agli Amici is one of the finest examples of contemporary Friulian cuisine, a restaurant that uses food to showcase the many facets of a border region, rich in cultural influences and extraordinary ingredients. The menu centres on two tasting menus, one of which is dedicated to plant-based dishes, complemented by a selection of ‘favourite dishes’ that trace the restaurant’s history through some of its most iconic creations, each accompanied by the year they were first created. It is, however, in the tasting menus that Emanuele Scarello’s gastronomic vision is most accomplished, based on constant research and a deep understanding of the local area. The pastures, vegetable gardens, woods and mountains of Friuli-Venezia Giulia serve as a source of inspiration for refined and distinctive dishes, often enhanced by ingredients from other regions in a harmonious blend of tradition and openness. Among the most memorable dishes are the variation of tender shoots and courgette flowers served with the rare centrolofo, presented both raw and cooked, and the elegant take on Kvarner scampi, enhanced by a delicate layer of rhubarb and lard on a raspberry cream base, rounded off with a delicious shellfish crème brûlée. In the dining room, Michela leads a close-knit team that stands out for its professionalism, warmth and genuine sense of hospitality, helping to ensure that the experience lives up to the restaurant’s name: making guests feel truly among friends.

Name: Andrea Aprea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: On the top floor, reached by lift, of the Fondazione Luigi Rovati, within a magnificent historic building that also houses a highly refined art museum, chef Andrea Aprea is entirely at home: a space of great impact, entirely oriented towards the open kitchen, with the walls of the central dining room clad in bucchero (the characteristic black ceramic with which the Etruscans crafted their jars). The gastronomic offering centres on three tasting menus: Contemporaneità, the most concise, with four courses dedicated to Aprea’s latest inventions; Partenope, a six-course journey in which the Neapolitan chef (though now a long-adopted Milanese) revisits certain Campanian classics; and Signature, eight dishes that retrace some of Aprea’s defining creations. In the secret green courtyard of the palazzo at Corso Venezia 52, the Caffè Bistrot is also to be found, where from breakfast to dinner the classic flavours of Italy may be savoured.

Name: Antica Corona Reale
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated between the Langhe and Monviso, this historic restaurant was founded in 1815. Run by the Vivalda family for five generations, it started out as a dairy farm before gaining a well-earned reputation for its cuisine. Owner-chef Gian Piero Vivalda creates top-quality menus featuring expertly prepared, colourful and aromatic dishes. Popular with food-lovers from Italy and abroad, Antica Corona Reale is also a point of reference for many local businesses who supply it with capon, guinea fowl, veal, Carmagnola peppers, porcini mushrooms and much more besides. The menu offers an array of enticing flavours, with modern dishes featuring alongside classic favourites, including a delicate raviolo of bagna càuda served with the restaurant’s legendary bouillabaisse, which has made a reappearance on the menu after guests’ insistent requests. In summer, dine alfresco in the shade of a beautiful pergola, while two small private rooms are available for intimate dinners, one of which is in the wine cellar surrounded by legendary bottles of wine. There’s also a charming garden with an English-style rose garden and other beautiful flowers, which are often used in the delicious desserts, as demonstrated by the superb rose tart.

Name: Antica Osteria Cera
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Regarded as one of the most popular destinations for seafood lovers, the restaurant offers an extensive menu that combines classic dishes with modern creations, fine-tuned season after season. The atmosphere here is elegant, modern and minimalist, purposely distanced from the idea of a traditional “osteria”, with a section called “Solo Verde” dedicated specifically to vegetarians.The kitchen focuses on raw seafood and charcoal-grilled dishes, the restaurant’s real strengths. The highlight among the starters is the cold spaghettino with essence of molluscs, along with references to Venetian tradition, such as “cicchetti crudi” (raw fish or meat appetisersi) and, in season, fried “moeche” (green crabs). For those who love shellfish, “la catalana” is a classic plateau not to be missed, while the “risotto della laguna” precisely interprets the taste and identity of the territory.

Name: Arnolfo
Address: Viale della Rimembranza 24, Colle di Val d'Elsa, 53034, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: With sharp lines created by the use of iron and glass, this modern building is especially designed to allow guests to admire the views from wherever they’re sitting. To the rear of the dining room, the large open-view kitchen framed by a superb yellow Siena marble wall is home to chef Gaetano Trovato (Mentor Chef Award 2024) and his team. Although there are three tasting menus available, one of which is vegetarian, any of the courses can also be chosen à la carte style. We could say so much about Arnolfo’s cuisine, but we’ll limit ourselves to mentioning the bread (which has been central to this chef’s work from the very beginning), duck, Chianina beef, Valdarno chicken and the ice-cream which always features among the desserts. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the delightful amuse-bouche with which guests are welcomed, the caponata with Taggiasca olives and basil, and the mullet served with white asparagus, peas and mint. The wine list is impressive, both for its quality and for the extensive selection of wines not only from Italy and France but also from other countries around the world – 7,000 different labels in total.

Name: Caino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: The cuisine of Valeria Piccini is a declaration of love for the Maremma and for Tuscany; here everything speaks of territory and family, of warmth and memory. It is a vision of cooking that steers clear of artifice and strange pairings: one comes here to eat, and to eat very well, not to be astonished. Such is the case with the bread filled with extraordinary ricotta, the family’s own-produced oil, and, naturally, the dishes themselves. To name but a few: Angela’s tripe and the lampredotto sandwich (an extraordinary duo of starters), the ricotta gnudi with peas and Orbetello bottarga, the caciucco and the charcoal-grilled lamb. An astonishing cellar, with around 2,500 labels. And, staying on the theme of the local area, after dinner do not fail to visit the nearby castle square: romantic and picturesque, it is the heart of this small stone village.

Name: Campo del Drago
Address: Località Castiglion del Bosco, Montalcino, 53024, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Allow yourself to be guided along the evocative Tuscan white roads, immersed in lush vegetation and between orderly rows of vines that compose the landscape with an almost painterly harmony: the journey itself becomes an integral part of the experience. On arrival, guests are welcomed into a fascinating medieval hamlet, complete with tower and frescoed chapel, which is home to Rosewood Castiglion del Bosco – awarded Three Michelin Keys – and to one of the most interesting restaurants in the area. It is here that chef Matteo Temperini offers a personal and creative reading of regional cuisine, celebrating also the produce of the property’s kitchen garden. The offering extends across three tasting menus, with the option of choosing à la carte as well (minimum three courses). The dishes are served in a contemporary and elegant dining room, enhanced by a panoramic terrace. The wine list, with over 700 labels, favours the local area while opening up to the rest of Italy and some international selections. The by-the-glass offering is of interest, with a notable Montevertine 2020 deserving particular mention.

Name: Castel fine dining
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in an independent wing of the hotel and with its own private entrance, the restaurant welcomes guests on the first floor with a dramatic open kitchen that immediately sets the tone for the gastronomic experience to follow. Beyond an elegant entrance salon, the dining room unfolds around just five tables looking onto broad panoramic windows, through which the gaze sweeps across the Val Venosta in a captivating 180-degree panorama. Chef Wiesner's proposal takes shape through a single tasting menu that selects high-quality ingredients without limiting itself to the regional confines. The cuisine is distinguished by a contemporary style, precise in its execution and consistently attentive to the balance of flavours. Among the dishes that best express his philosophy, the grilled wagyu fillet with peppers and potatoes stands out: a preparation that is only apparently simple, elevating an exceptional raw material through impeccable technique and a flavour that is full and deeply satisfying.

Name: D'O
Address: Piazza della Chiesa 14, loc. San Pietro all'Olmo, Cornaredo, 20007, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: On a charming piazza presided over by an elm tree and a seventeenth-century church, tables in two of the three dining rooms overlook the scene, while the contemporary elegance of D’O unfolds inside. Chef Davide Oldani, now a defining figure of Italian cuisine, crafts dishes that distill twenty years of work and formative experiences, including memorable stints with Marchesi and Ducasse. Creative ideas rooted in Italian taste, impeccable technique, and presentations that are both essential and playfully pop: as exemplified by the Cuttlefish in its ink with pickled porcini and dill. Among the tasting menus, Molteplicità and Leggerezza (10 courses) represent the fullest expression of his creative freedom, while Esattezza revisits signature classics. Completing the experience is the brilliant sommelier Manuele, who delights with playful and surprising pairings.

Name: Duomo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: In the heart of Ibla, one of Italy’s most charming historic centres, Ciccio Sultano’s restaurant remains an unmissable stop for anyone wishing to discover the true soul of Sicily. Just a stone’s throw from the Cathedral of San Giorgio, in a classic and elegant setting, the hospitality is in the hands of a young and skilled team, capable of combining professionalism with warmth, also in their carefully curated wine list.With his deep knowledge of his homeland, Sultano has, over the years, developed a cuisine that has become a true labour of love for Sicily: a gastronomic narrative that interprets the island’s identity, heritage and future prospects, making him today an extraordinary international ambassador for Sicilian culture. In the restaurant’s intimate dining rooms, his cuisine comes to life with vigour and character, through dishes that combine technical skill, depth and a distinct regional influence.The ‘Stupor Mundi’ tasting menu, comprising eight courses, represents the most complete embodiment of his vision: a culinary journey capable of leaving a vivid and lasting impression, featuring intense flavours and refined compositions. As well as the set menus, there is also an à la carte option, allowing you to explore the menu at your leisure. Among the dishes, creations such as free-range lamb with Sicilian ‘mole’, grilled green beans and a vegetable jus combining flavours from the sea and the mountains stand out – a prime example of a cuisine that is at once distinctive, original and deeply evocative.

Name: Enoteca La Torre
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Within the captivating 1911 architecture of Villa Laetitia, the restaurant occupies a sumptuous dining room rich in stucco work and columns, enhanced by broad windows opening onto the exclusive garden: the ideal setting for an evening in grand style. The cooking, which does not forget the Campanian roots of the chef, returns to these echoes at several moments throughout the menu, alternating iconic recipes with more personal creations. Among the dishes that have become representative of the house, the egg, buffalo taleggio and black truffle of woodland character stands out, while the indulgent selection of desserts invites one to surrender to the pleasures of the final course, culminating in the characteristic trolley of petit fours. The experience is further enhanced by a skilled service, discreet and impeccable both in the management of the dining room and in the stewardship of the remarkable wine list, rich in prestigious labels and well-considered offerings by the glass. A refined destination, one that succeeds in uniting elegance, technique and hospitality of the highest order.

Name: Famiglia Rana
Address: Via Feniletto 2, località Vallese, Oppeano, 37050, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within the Feniletto nature reserve, the restaurant looks out over a tree-lined garden, an organic kitchen garden and an orchard that speak directly to the cooking. The warm and intimate interiors recall an elegant domestic drawing room, with wood, soft lighting and a welcome of homey character. At the stove is chef Francesco Sodano, who offers exclusively blind tasting menus: the guest chooses one of three journeys and the number of courses, while the dishes arrive as a surprise. The ‘Ricomincio da tre’ menu pays homage to Campania and gathers some of the chef’s signature dishes, among them a reinterpreted pastiera that preserves the aromas and identity of the traditional dessert while presenting it in a contemporary guise. ‘The Doors’ is the creativity menu, where technique and research shape a freer and more experimental cuisine. Those who prefer the freshness of the vegetable world may opt for ‘Vegetale’, dedicated to the produce of the kitchen garden, the protagonist of preparations that celebrate seasonality, fragrance and precise cooking. A young but well-prepared service accompanies the experience with quiet discretion, contributing to a journey that is harmonious and deeply pleasurable.

Name: George Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Housed on the top floor of the Grand Hotel Parker's, Naples' oldest hotel, George Restaurant enjoys a privileged position with splendid views over the Gulf and Vesuvius. The elegant dining room, looking onto the open kitchen and extending onto a terrace of particular beauty at sunset, is accompanied by excellent service: professional, relaxed and capable of presenting each dish with expertise and natural ease. Chef Domenico Candela offers a cuisine deeply rooted in Campania yet open to French and Japanese influences, with fermentation and contemporary techniques at the service of flavour. Two tasting menus are available: Since 2018, dedicated to the chef's iconic dishes, and Viaggio Goloso, inspired by seasonality. Emblematic of his philosophy is [POMOD'ORO], his personal interpretation of pasta al pomodoro, built around seven varieties of Campanian tomato, presented in different textures. Each variety contributes its own nuances of sweetness and acidity, expressing the full aromatic richness of the fruit at the peak of ripeness. A false tomato, fashioned from gelatin, encloses a heart of mozzarella, while basil appears in several forms: a snow that lends fresh aromatic notes, and a soft steamed bun, the ideal vessel for the irresistible final scarpetta.

Name: Glam Enrico Bartolini
Address: Calle Tron, sestiere Santa Croce 1961, Venice, 30135, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Among quiet alleyways opens the entrance to Palazzo Venart, one of the most exclusive residences in the city. Beyond the gate, two gardens – one at the entrance and one overlooking the Grand Canal – offer an unexpected oasis of calm in the heart of Venice. The dining room, intimate and gathered, counts just six tables and is enriched by a dramatic silk-road-inspired wallpaper. At the stove, chef Donato Ascani offers two tasting menus, the more creative Arte, Orti e Laguna and I Classici del Glam, alongside the option of choosing from the à la carte. His cuisine is born from listening to the lagoon and its rhythms, reinterpreting the local area with contemporary technique and great sensitivity. Through a constant dialogue with fishermen and market gardeners from the islands – from Sant'Erasmo to Cavallino – wild herbs, vegetables, early-season produce and hand-gathered shoots become the stars of his preparations. Particularly convincing is his use of the grill, capable of enhancing the raw material without overwhelming it, in a gastronomic journey of great elegance.

Name: Harry's Piccolo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: In the heart of Trieste’s historic centre, the grand halls of the former Palazzo della Borsa now house the sophisticated dining concept created by Matteo Metullio and Davide De Pra. The elegant, contemporary setting retains a precious link to the past in the original motifs decorating the window panes – the one historical feature that has been carefully restored. The undisputed star of the show is the spectacular open kitchen – a veritable theatre of haute cuisine – which offers an immersive experience to guests seated at tables overlooking the kitchen team and, even more so, to those who choose a seat at the counter.The menu is structured around various tasting menus that highlight the technique, balance and identity of the ingredients, which are easily recognisable and showcased in their purest form. One of the standout items on the menu is the selection dedicated to the sea and the spirit of Trieste, featuring dishes such as cold spaghettino with beetroot, lemon ponzu, yuzu mayonnaise and tuna tartare with chives. Alongside this, there are menus that explore the combination of meat and fish, as well as a selection of the restaurant’s great classics, including the iconic Harrysotto. Whichever path they choose, Metullio and De Pra’s cuisine continues to rank among the most brilliant, innovative and captivating on the Italian gastronomic scene.

Name: I Tenerumi
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Make sure you arrive at the restaurant before sunset: the view of the Aeolian Islands offers a scene of rare beauty, the ideal prelude to a remarkable dining experience. In the kitchen, Davide Guidara rejects the labels ‘vegetarian’ or ‘vegan’, choosing instead to define his work as authentically ‘plant-based’ – an expression of free and personal thinking. From the open kitchen, a unique surprise tasting menu takes shape, conceived as a dynamic sequence of often playful bites that capture the essence of the vegetable garden and the seasons with great precision. The focus is on winter produce, which is brought to the fore through fermentation, maceration and preservation techniques, in harmony with fresh ingredients. The experience is accompanied by an original pairing featuring kombucha and herbal cordials, with the wine cellar available to those who wish to explore the wine selection. To round it all off, the young and knowledgeable service staff are able to establish a direct and spontaneous rapport with guests: an increasingly unmissable culinary destination.

Name: Il Pagliaccio
Address: Via dei Banchi Vecchi 129/a, Rome, 00186, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: In the heart of Rome, a true gastronomic journey without boundaries begins, articulated through different menus according to the experience chosen: from Circus, “an itinerary that knows no limits”, to Scintille, centred on essential flavours and creative gestures, through to Parallels, an exclusive experience served in a private room of even greater intimacy.Guiding this narrative is Anthony Genovese, cosmopolitan chef-patron of personal vision and crystalline talent, capable of surprising even in moments closest to tradition, such as the Tortello, evocative of childhood memories, or the original green tomato, caviar, and crème fraîche dessert.The experience unfolds in an elegant and intimate setting, sustained by service of the highest order: sommelier Luca Belleggia curates a wine list of some 2,000 labels with great expertise, supported by Veronica Loachamin, consistently impeccable and welcoming. Together, they create a dining room of precision, warmth, and great distinction.

Name: Il Piccolo Principe
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This is the gourmet restaurant of the iconic Grand Hotel Principe di Piemonte, the undisputed emblem of hospitality in Versilia. On the ground floor, an elegant contemporary-styled dining area unfolds, extending into an exclusive wing adorned with bespoke art and furniture. Talented chef Giuseppe Mancino—of Campanian origin—melds traditions with Tuscan ingredients in his dishes, reinventing them with flair and creativity, along with options from other regions. The choices oscillate between three tasting menus: a vegetarian one, another devoted to the chef’s classics, and lastly, the longer and more elaborate ‘experience’. Among the intriguing recipes, the pizzaiola-style red mullet, bitter herb risotto with zimino sauce, and cuttlefish ink mayonnaise stand out, not forgetting the sea steak. A special mention for the exceptional farro and rye flour bread.

Name: Krèsios
Address: Via San Giovanni 59, Telese Terme, 82037, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An ancient farmhouse serves as the laboratory home of ‘engineering-minded’ Chef Giuseppe Iannotti, who presents a single, long tasting menu that arrives at blind. An intriguing journey centring on flavour, featuring daring combinations paired with interesting techniques and experiments to entertain the guests. Throughout this gastronomic voyage, you'll find slight references to Campania, yet primarily the journey leads worldwide, through reinterpretations of familiar recipes reimagined with personal creativity, fermentations, macerations, extractions, and some nods to the chef's past. All accompanied by a selection of wines sourced from small producers, often natural, for after all, Krésios was none other than Bacchus.

Name: L'Olivo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Upon arrival, guests are invited to begin with an aperitif in the refined bar area with its terrace, an ideal setting in which to savour a magnificent island sunset. We are in Anacapri, in its greener and more residential aspect, far from the more intense currents of Capri’s tourist flow. It is here that the Capri Palace, among the island’s most exclusive hotels, provides the introduction to its two-Michelin-starred restaurant, set within a spacious and elegant room that recalls a contemporary salon. In the kitchen, Andrea Migliaccio delivers a proposal that celebrates the Italian, and above all Campanian, tradition with great vitality, reinterpreted with a modern sensitivity yet always faithful to the generosity of its flavours and its vivid character. The dishes impress with intensity and precision, the first courses in particular, the true protagonists of the journey: from the pasta with reef fish to the richly constructed risotto al ragù napoletano. A deeply satisfying and joyful experience, which finds its natural complement in a stroll through the lanes of Anacapri or along the mule track leading to Villa Axel Munthe, perfect for immersing oneself in the island’s most authentic atmosphere.

Name: La Madia
Address: Corso Filippo Re Capriata 22, Licata, 92027, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Park in the surrounding streets and get ready for a culinary journey into the very heart of Sicily; thanks to Pino Cuttaia’s vision, Licata has, over the years, become a must-visit destination for food lovers from all over Italy and abroad. His cuisine, deeply rooted in the island, eschews any stylistic flourishes for their own sake, focusing instead on the essence of the ingredients and the memory of flavours, reinterpreted with extraordinary contemporary sensitivity. Examples include dishes such as pasta with a shellfish broth or Nebrodi black suckling pig with Sunday sauce. The two dining rooms, modern and minimalist, create an elegant and relaxed atmosphere, while the service, led by Vincenzo and his close-knit team, stands out for its professionalism, experience and genuine hospitality. The wine list is also of particular interest, featuring a carefully curated selection of wines and numerous large-format bottles, among which many outstanding Sicilian wines stand out – wines that, in the glass, reflect the very same regional identity that inspires the cuisine.

Name: La Peca
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: 2027 will mark forty years of business: a story made up of aromas, flavours and traditions, the story of the Portinari family, who have carved their name among the pillars of Venice's restaurant scene and beyond. Chef Nicola Portinari welcomes guests to La Peca with one clear goal: to give them pleasure, letting them choose freely from an extensive and inviting menu (for those who prefer a guided experience, there are three tasting menus, including a vegetarian option). Leafing through it, it is easy to be seduced by dishes that speak to the palate and the mind. His creations are technical, but never ostentatious: harmonies rich in flavour, without ever being contrived. It's always hard to choose because there's so much to tempt you: the ravioli filled with venison, wrapped in a delicate jelly, accompanied by mushrooms and completed with a clear, fragrant consommé, are unforgettable; for those who love game, the mallard is a tribute to the season, with variations that enhance its nobility. And then there is the dessert, which ends the journey with one last embrace: creme brulée and ancient citrus ravioli are the historic signature dish, but there are also surprising reinterpretations of classics such as the Sachertorte, made intriguing by peanuts and Ghital cheese ice cream, and the Mont Blanc, enhanced by a delicate hint of green tea. A monumental wine cellar with around two thousand labels and a generous selection of natural wines completes the experience.

Name: Locanda Sant'Uffizio Enrico Bartolini
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: In one of the most picturesque corners of Monferrato, within an ancient monastic building that has been converted into an elegant five-star hotel, a truly enchanting culinary experience takes shape. Under the guidance of multi-starred chef Enrico Bartolini, the kitchen is led by Gabriele Boffa, a Piedmontese chef with a solid international background, who is able to combine a deep understanding of the local area with remarkable technical skill. The menu features tasting courses that alternate between faithful interpretations of regional classics – the agnolotti del plin are particularly memorable – and more personal creations, all of which remain firmly rooted in local produce, flavours and traditions. Here and there, Latin American influences and bolder touches emerge, though they are handled with balance and restraint. The dining experience takes place in an elegant dining room with just a few tables, where attentive service accompanies a sequence of dishes brimming with character, from carefully crafted amuse-bouches to homemade baked goods, right through to dishes that showcase excellent ingredients. The wine list is also of a high standard, supported by a competent and close-knit front-of-house team.

Name: Madonnina del Pescatore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: It opened in 1984, but to call it a historic restaurant is misleading: Moreno Cedroni is one of Italy’s most innovative – as well as most talented – chefs. It was from this restaurant in Marzocca, a hamlet south of Senigallia, that ideas emerged which have found their way onto many dining tables across Italy and beyond. Today more than before, the Madonnina del Pescatore is a hotbed of innovation, which Moreno blends with extraordinary ease and good taste into the cuisine of the Marche region and his childhood memories, in a constant interplay between local traditions and gastronomic journeys, even as far afield as the Far East. The setting is a room overlooking the beach – home to the chef’s marine garden – and the sea, in an atmosphere of refined elegance. The service is orchestrated by the natural and gentle grace of his wife, Mariella, who creates an atmosphere of genuine well-being in the dining room, free from stiffness and formality – a place where you can relax and enjoy an extraordinary meal.

Name: Magnolia
Address: Via Pelliciano 35, loc. Montilgallo, Longiano, 47020, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within the refined Relais Villa Margherita, an eighteenth-century residence transformed into an elegant boutique retreat with a handful of rooms, parkland and a swimming pool, Magnolia represents its contemporary soul. The light-filled veranda dining room opens onto the landscape of the Romagna hills, the gaze stretching as far as the distinctive peak of San Marino, in a continuous dialogue between indoors and out. At the helm, chef Alberto Faccani lucidly interprets a gastronomic journey that alternates memory and exploration: alongside more classic dishes that tell the story of his professional career, room is found for original creations, the expression of a restless evolutionary drive. His style is elegant and measured, built on refined balances and pairings that are never predictable, as in the delicate harmony of coconut and milk that accompanies baby cuttlefish with caviar and peas, or in the intense signature dish of squid carbonara with black truffle. More exotic flourishes are not lacking, well integrated into the overall narrative, as in the lobster with peas, coconut and lemongrass, where freshness and fragrance meet with natural ease. The welcome is gracious, the service precise and engaging, while the broad and carefully curated wine list finds a capable interpreter in the passionate work of the sommelier.

Name: Piazzetta Milù
Address: Corso Alcide De Gasperi 23, Castellammare di Stabia, 80053, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: It would be impossible to describe this venue without beginning with the welcome, the authentic hallmark of the Izzo family: a warmth and attentiveness that transforms every visit into a memorable experience. Leading the gastronomic proposal is Maicol, who expresses his vision through a seasonal and surprise tasting menu in constant evolution: the number and sequence of dishes remain unknown, leaving space for a free narrative constructed in the moment.The experience unfolds across several different rooms in a dynamic itinerary that may vary throughout the year: it often begins in the kitchen, before moving to the evocative historic cellar, surrounded by bottles from around the world, where each guest has their own private table, and concluding in the dining room, with possible further interludes beside the chef.The cuisine fuses technique and creativity to remarkable effect, as in the tagliolini with cardoncelli mushrooms, butter and aged Parmigiano, finished with white truffle and accompanied by a curious “fake crumb” fashioned from the same mushroom. The experience is orchestrated with precision by Emanuele and Valerio in the dining room, while the cellar – broad and carefully selected – helps make the experience even more immersive. The portions, well judged in size, allow guests to navigate the entire journey with ease, arriving at the close entirely satisfied.

Name: San Domenico
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In business since 1970, San Domenico is one of the flag-bearers of classic Italian dining. In the historic centre of Imola, inside you will find a succession of elegant rooms and an atmosphere that seems straight out of an English club. The menu alternates classic dishes accumulated over many years of activity with some more modern inventions from chef Massimiliano Mascia. An extraordinary wine list features more than two thousand labels.

Name: Seta by Antonio Guida
Address: Via Monte di Pietà 18, Milan, 20121, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within the Mandarin Oriental, a symbol of Milanese luxury hospitality, Antonio Guida’s kitchen elegantly interprets the city’s cosmopolitan taste. Three tasting menus are offered: one dedicated to the chef’s classics, one to seasonality, and one to a single featured ingredient. In winter, dishes of great finesse come to the fore, from game to veal sweetbreads with cinnamon, through to a raspberry risotto, with desserts of a distinctly contemporary character. The wine list is of a high standard, available by the glass as well as by the bottle, and enhanced by magnums of notable vintages, alongside a thoughtful selection of non-alcoholic beverages for more moderate consumption. For after dinner, the Mandarin Garden next door to Seta confirms its place as one of Milan’s most exclusive late-night destinations, with signature cocktails and contemporary music setting the tone. The restaurant’s social engagement is worthy of note, with active involvement in education and inclusion projects.

Name: St. George by Heinz Beck
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Set within the prestigious The Ashbee Hotel, an elegant early 20th-century villa overlooking one of Taormina’s finest views, the St. George offers a dining experience that combines sophistication, stunning views and haute cuisine. After passing through the residence’s charming rooms, the view opens out onto the garden and the spectacular terrace, where palm trees frame the view of the Strait of Messina. The culinary concept stems from a collaboration between Heinz Beck and the resident chef, Salvatore Iuliano, who combines the renowned master’s insights with his own personal sensitivity, shaped by his Calabrian roots – evident in his use of signature ingredients such as ’nduja. The cuisine is characterised by a balance between technical precision and expressive elegance, resulting in dishes that are as surprising in flavour as they are in presentation. The starters are truly emblematic – veritable masterpieces of culinary craftsmanship, in which ingredients and shapes are transformed into elements of refined visual poetry. Among the most memorable creations, the “Aubergine, fig leaf and oxidised chocolate” stands out as an original fusion of local produce, creativity and precision in execution. The experience is rounded off by attentive, impeccable service and the expertise of the young sommelier, who guides diners through the meal with passion and a keen eye for the ideal pairings.

Name: Taverna Estia
Address: Via Guido De Ruggiero 108, Brusciano, 80031, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Welcomed by a fragrant garden of aromatic herbs, guests may take their seats in the warmer months in romantic alcoves shaded by jasmine pergolas, while inside the elegant dining room, looking onto the open kitchen and the cellar, offers an atmosphere that is intimate and refined, made all the more evocative by a lit fireplace in the winter months. At the helm of the restaurant are brothers Mario and Francesco Sposito: the former responsible for the welcome and the dining room, the latter the architect of the gastronomic offering. Building on the family legacy and still supported today by their mother, they have succeeded in transforming the restaurant into one of the most admired addresses in the region. The cuisine finds expression across several tasting menus, with the option of choosing à la carte as well, in a narrative that weaves together contemporary technique and refined echoes of Campanian tradition. Completing the experience, a cellar of great depth with over a thousand labels, particularly rich in French references, brought to life by the attentive and expert service of the sommelier.

Name: Terra The Magic Place
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Terra – The Magic Place begins to work its magic from the moment you begin the ascent along the road that climbs from Sarentino to an altitude of 1622 metres, winding through beech and fir woods. The restaurant is situated on a sunny alpine pasture with breathtaking views of the Dolomites, where the Schneider family has transformed the chalet built in 1940 by their grandfather Johann into a place that is truly unique. The gastronomic experience unfolds through à la carte dishes and an elaborate tasting menu, featuring little masterpieces of aesthetics and taste: the emulsion of brown trout with dill, chamomile and heather jelly is a revelation, as are the spaghetti made with beetroot, yeast flour and yarrow. The wine list – which also includes alcohol-free options – is lovingly curated by Gisela, the chef's sister. For those who wish to prolong the magic, the secluded resort completes a truly unforgettable experience.

Name: Torre del Saracino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Gennaro Esposito, one of the leading figures in contemporary Campania cuisine, has moved his restaurant to the historic Bellevue Syrene in Sorrento, a refined hotel overlooking the gulf and home to a valuable art collection commissioned by the family who own it. The experience unfolds between an intimate and romantic dining room, adorned with frescoed walls, and the splendid panoramic terrace overlooking the sea. The dishes, whether seafood or meat-based, combine creativity, technical skill and a deep connection to the region: visually striking creations that capture the colours, aromas and vitality of the Mediterranean, without losing sight of flavour. A fine example of this is the refined basil risotto with Saracen-style mussels and freshly squeezed plum juice. The experience is rounded off by elegant service and an extensive, carefully curated wine list.

Name: Verso Capitaneo
Description: Once through the entrance onto Piazza Duomo, a lift takes you to the second floor, where the restaurant is located: an intimate space with three long tables overlooking the open-plan kitchen, allowing diners to sit literally opposite the chefs as they finish preparing the dishes, while still offering – for those who prefer it – more traditional tables. At the helm are the Capitaneo brothers who, while drawing on their Apulian roots, bring a personal, creative vision to their cuisine, one that is also open to influences from the Milanese tradition – the city that has welcomed them. The true value of the experience also lies in the theatrical aspect of the service: watching the kitchen team at work, in synchrony, is a small spectacle of precision and rigour, characterised by measured movements, glances and impeccable technique. A prime example of this is the ‘Blue lobster, Wagyu and tonka bean’, a striking dish that combines a balanced flavour profile with aesthetic refinement, a true showcase of their cuisine.

Name: Villa Elena
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: One must climb the steep, scenic Via San Vigilio, just steps from the beating heart of Città Alta, immersed in an exclusive hillside setting, to reach Villa Elena, one of the most majestic residences in the Bergamo hills. The garden terrace opens like a balcony suspended over the panorama, where on clear days lunch begins caressed by light and the fragrance of fresh air. Inside, amid stuccoes that resemble velvet, mirrors multiplying reflections, cool marbles, and frescoes that tell stories, the cuisine of Marco Galtarossa comes to life, the fruit of a creative dialog with Italy’s most decorated chef, Enrico Bartolini: a perfect harmony with the opulence of the surroundings. Complex, refined dishes, occasionally unfolding in multiple acts, elevated by aromatic herbs and vegetables that release intense fragrances; the close bond with local producers makes this venue an essential destination for memorable experiences, not only on grand occasions. The scampi with quince and hillside escarole is an extraordinary prelude, while the lemon spaghetto and sole with chanterelles and sea buckthorn continue the symphony of flavors. Recent additions to the dining room team confirm hospitality and service as further strengths, completing a picture of excellence.

Name: Villa Feltrinelli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Within the eponymous villa, one of the most spectacular hotels on Lake Garda, the experience unfolds in a setting of extraordinary beauty: the lake before you, the mountains behind, and all around a park of absolute tranquillity. The interiors, finished to the last detail, express a refined elegance enriched by fine fabrics and floral arrangements. The evening begins with an aperitif in the garden, accompanied by an unforgettable view of the lake, before continuing in the refined inner rooms or on the terrace. The gastronomic offering takes the form of a single, elaborate surprise tasting menu, in which seafood, lake fish, and meat alternate seamlessly, with particular attention given to vegetables, the chef’s true hallmark, highlighted through a wide variety of aromatic herbs and occasionally exotic inflections.The wine selection favours Italy, with a significant representation of Champagne.

Name: daní maison
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: “A casa di Nino” is not merely an evocative name but a promise fulfilled: guests truly do enter the home of chef Di Costanzo, set among the hills of a quiet residential area of the island. Beyond the threshold, a path through the garden – tended with great care and dominated by Mediterranean scrub – captivates with its richness of plants and flowers; it is here, on milder evenings, that aperitifs and after-dinner drinks are enjoyed, in a setting of rare charm. Inside, beneath a typical vaulted ceiling, just a handful of tables ensure an intimate and personal experience, while those wishing to observe the kitchen up close may take a seat facing the stove, watching the chef at work. The dishes are notable for their complexity, technical rigour and inventiveness: the expression of a conceptual cuisine capable of surprising even on a visual level. The cellar merits a visit: interesting and well-stocked, ranging across historic labels and a selection of prestigious sparkling wines, with names such as Ferrari and Dom Pérignon.

FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Named after the birthday of chef Flavio Costa’s twin daughters, 21.9 reflects both his Ligurian origins and his deep ties to Piedmont. Set within a wine estate whose cellar dates back to the 15th century, with sweeping views over vineyards and rolling hills, the restaurant offers a creative cuisine at the crossroads of land and sea, marrying Piedmontese recipes and ingredients with those of Liguria, while also embracing more contemporary influences. All this is expressed through three tasting menus, with dishes also available à la carte. In season, a menu dedicated to game is also available.

Name: ARIA
Address: Via Loggia dei Pisani 2, Naples, 80133, Italy
Description: The ambience at this hushed and discreet restaurant couldn’t be more different from the hustle and bustle of the elegant district in which it is situated. The softly lit dining rooms are elegant and minimalist in style, with lamps creating pools of light illuminating the dishes conjured up by Paolo Barrale. Originally from Cefalù but now settled in Campania, the chef’s cuisine is inspired by the culinary traditions of both regions which he reinterprets with ease, occasionally creating more personalised dishes. Generous in every way, from the warm welcome to the cuisine right up to dessert, Paolo offers guests a top-quality dining experience ably assisted by his well-trained, professional staff.

Name: Abba
Description: In the heart of Milan's Certosa District, Abba is set in a former brush factory and welcomes guests with Nordic elegance: an open kitchen, only eight well-spaced tables, minimalist furnishings, and natural light streaming through large windows. In the kitchen, Abbattista offers two paths that tell his vision: excellent ingredients and modern techniques merge into delicious and surprising dishes. Among the must-tries, the tomato water risotto with parsley oil and mantis shrimp cream, or the whitefish, elegantly served on black lentils and turmeric. To end beautifully, the hazelnut soufflé is an indulgence not to be missed. The wine list is essential but carefully curated, with some natural and organic options. At lunch, there’s also a business lunch with selections from the menus.

Name: Abbruzzino Oltre
Address: Piazza Salvo d'Acquisto 16, Lamezia Terme, 88046, Italy
Description: A historic palazzo that once served military and ecclesiastical functions now presides over the main promenade with understated grandeur. Inside, minimalist elegance converses with modern art objects perfectly integrated into the setting, creating a refined space of contemporary character. Here, Luca Abbruzzino explores his Calabria with a personal, engaging vision: a vibrant, modern cuisine that showcases technique and sensitivity through dry-aged fish, well-balanced contrasts, and masterful use of local ingredients. Bergamot takes the lead in the dessert course, while savory highlights include amberjack and grouper, prawns with sea urchin, and an oyster risotto that merits unequivocal recommendation. The menu, however, is a surprise: one entrusts the day’s selection to the chef, confident he will captivate with fresh, coherent intuitions. Intimate spaces, impeccable service, and a naturally romantic atmosphere complete an experience uniting history, elegance, and a cuisine that looks to the future without losing its bond to the land.

Name: Abocar Due Cucine
Description: Among the streets of the city centre, one “approaches” – the meaning of abocar in Spanish – Mariano’s cuisine, where Argentine origins and a decidedly globetrotting spirit, shared with his partner Camilla, give rise to an original gourmet proposal, capable of fusing two cultures in a personal and harmonious gastronomic language. The choice ranges from a concise à la carte selection to tasting menus of varying length, dedicated either to fish – with adherence to the Hadria 37 project for sustainable fishing – or to meat; those wishing to create an individual journey may nevertheless freely choose any dish, including those featured on the menus. The dining room, with its contemporary atmosphere, is gracefully furnished: there is almost the feeling of eating in an elegant private home, an intimate setting that invites guests to slow down and allow themselves to be guided by the experience. In summer, those wishing to sit outdoors are advised to book well in advance.

Name: Achilli al Parlamento
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the Parliament building, this elegant restaurant’s origins as a wine shop are visible in the many wine bottles that line the walls of the dining room. Today, the restaurant offers elegant cuisine, divided into two tasting menus, one more traditional and the other more adventurous, as well as an à la carte menu featuring creative dishes such as the “Senza spaghetto alle vongole” and well-executed dishes inspired by the Campania region.Chef Gallo reveals a sure hand and remarkable skill in making the most of entirely plant-based ingredients, from which he conjures up interesting flavours and textures. There is a wide selection of wines by the glass, while bottled wines can be chosen directly from the wine shop’s shelves. At the entrance, there is a bistro that is also open for lunch, offering simpler dishes in an informal setting.

Name: Acqua
Address: Via Filippo Corridoni 1, Olgiate Olona, 21057, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Family tradition is renewed with a contemporary spirit at this venue overlooking the historic Ma.Ri.Na. The philosophy here is clear: exceptional raw materials, carefully selected and showcased by chef Menoncin and patron Davide Possoni. The latter enjoys sitting down with guests at the start of the evening to guide them toward offerings best suited to personal tastes: fish, crustaceans, and mollusks interpreted in original recipes, occasionally with pleasing spicy accents, always generous and elegantly plated. The crudo selection is unmissable – notably the sumptuous crustacean trio of scampi, impressively sized caramote prawns, and red prawns – while among the hot dishes, we highlight the seared red mullet with Tuscan kale velouté and gorgonzola gelato, sampled on our last visit and truly memorable. The wine list favors Champagnes, with numerous labels available by the glass. In summer, the outdoor terrace adds an extra touch of pleasure.

Name: Acqua Pazza
Address: Via Dietro la Chiesa 3/4, Ponza, 04027, Italy
Description: Arranged on a series of multi-levelled terraces, the tables at this restaurant boast breathtaking views of the semicircular port, as well as much of the island, extending out to sea as far as Gavi and Zannone – one of the most spectacular views in Italy! In business for over 30 years (20 of those with a Michelin star), Luigi Pesce and Patrizia Ronca delight guests with their fine cuisine which focuses almost exclusively on fish and seafood in classic, unfussy dishes which allow the ingredients to take centre stage (the selection of raw seafood dishes at the beginning of the menu is proof of the high quality), along with the surrounding scenery! An impressive wine list completes the picture.

Name: Acquerello
Description: The word “modern” sums up the cuisine here, although more than one word is needed to do justice to this restaurant. Housed in an old courtyard typical of Lombardy, Acquerello focuses on flavour rather than colour, with dishes created by a chef who enjoys being in the kitchen away from the spotlight. Although the restaurant offers an à la carte, our inspectors recommend the tasting menu with its fine balance of delicate flavours and original combinations that offer a hint of Eastern influence and pleasing contrasts in cooking methods and temperatures. The wine selection reflects the owner’s tastes: a slight emphasis on sparkling wines from the other side of the Alps, but also something for everyone.

Name: Ada
Description: Just a few hundred metres from the church of Sant’Ercolano in a narrow alleyway in the heart of Perugia’s historic centre, this restaurant is home to chef Ada Stifani who serves expertly prepared contemporary cuisine with a regional flavour. There are two dining rooms here: one with an open-view kitchen and the other with a modern and elegant mezzanine. Among the highlights, don’t miss the tagliatelle with cardoncelli mushrooms and scampi which is full of perfectly balanced, intense flavours.

Name: Al Gambero
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: A long-established restaurant in the Lower Brescia region, where the elegant, meticulous service is skilfully overseen by the owner, Al Gambero is the perfect choice for anyone in search of cuisine that is full of flavour and prepared using skilful, modern techniques, and in which taste is everything. The restaurant opened in 1880 in the oldest house in the village and is now run by descendants of the same family. After so many years in business, the menu has accumulated a number of unmissable signature dishes, from its famous risottos to roast kid.

Name: Al Gatto Verde
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Inside Maria Luigia, the welcoming country house envisioned by Massimo Bottura and Lara Gilmore to host a cosmopolitan clientele, the cuisine of Jessica Rosval revolves around fire, presenting dishes that are both visually striking and deeply appetizing. Her philosophy celebrates the finest local produce and the estate’s own farm, with cooking techniques that find their signature expression over live embers. Exemplary is the smoked meat selection, alternating various cuts and culminating in a wood-grilled beef rib, intense and succulent. Service is warm and attentive, while the knowledgeable and curious sommelier offers stimulating pairings that accompany the gastronomic journey with elegance.

Name: Al Madrigale | Nuova Cucina Rurale
Description: Within a fascinating medieval palazzo, a spectacular spiral staircase leads to an elegant dining room where Liberty-style floor tiles and chestnut tables speak of taste and tradition. This is where the gastronomic project led by the talented Gian Marco Bianchi takes shape, encapsulated in his motto: new rural cuisine. The journey invites guests to rediscover the flavours of the land through a contemporary sensitivity. Today the offering is structured across two distinct itineraries: Misera/Mente, a five-course menu, and Migra/Azione, a complete nine-step experience. In both, dishes such as the shepherd’s raviolo with sheep’s ricotta and lamb jus impress with depth and intensity, while the grilled lamb with “cacio e ovo”, accompanied by a zabaione served alongside, delivers a moment of pure gastronomic expressiveness. The ideal toast comes from the local area: a sparkling wine from malvasia with a touch of sangiovese, made by the méthode champenoise and aged 36 months on the lees: a refined and identity-rich opening to an experience destined to leave its mark.

Name: Al Metrò
Address: Via Magellano 35, San Salvo Marina, 66050, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the premises that once housed the family pastry shop, the Fossaceca brothers have breathed new life into a space now consecrated to signature gastronomy. The interior, minimal and contemporary in its neutral tones, seems deliberately to step aside and allow the cooking of Nicola to take centre stage, while the outdoor area – bright, intimate, and with the unhurried atmosphere of a small piazza – offers a livelier and more airy prospect. The modern and technically rigorous cooking pays measured homage to the ingredients of the local area, beginning with the finest catch the Adriatic has to offer, handled with a light touch and great precision. The leavened products are excellent, the fruit of selected Abruzzese flours and careful work with fermentation, as is the refined coffee list, which brings the meal to a close with a degree of attentiveness that is not to be taken for granted. The glass-fronted wine cabinet in the dining room is a delight in itself: a natural invitation to yield to the temptation of a fine bottle, or to let oneself be guided by Antonio, a most accomplished and passionate host.

Name: Al Sorriso
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: This restaurant is a true shrine to Italian cuisine, which continues to tell the story of the passion and dedication of two great professionals who have marked a turning point in the industry. Luisa Marelli, who has a degree in literature and is self-taught in the kitchen for love, creates dishes that have become true classics, rich in references to tradition and with a special focus on the seasonality of ingredients. Her husband, Angelo Valazza, is the master of the dining room par excellence, a true “maître” that all those aspiring to this profession should work alongside for a while. His elegance, his dialectic and his knowledge of wines, cheeses and many other delicacies are unparalleled!

Name: Alici
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Borgo Santandrea is a luxurious hotel along the Amalfi Coast, just outside Conca dei Marini, and Alici is its fineding, both symbols of Italian beauty.
