Beyond an interior dining room with vintage-style furniture, dinners always take place on the magnificent terrace with its blue and azure majolica floor, reverberating the splendour of the sky and sea. Chef Crescenzo Scotti clearly loves pleasant places: we remember him previously in Ravello and before that - with a star - on the island of Vulcano. Here he returns with skill and expertise to his favourite territory, that is, the flavours of the Amalfi Coast (sfusato amalfitano can be found in many recipes), but also those of Naples and his native Ischia, always adding a touch of fantasy. The inspector liked: “Cappuccino Mediterraneo”, that is, morsels of boiled lobster served in a cup with a soft and delicate potato and soya cream, as well as the fake cocoa on the surface which is nothing more than powdered squid ink to add flavour to the dish.

Name: All'Enoteca
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: At the start of the refined Corso Roma, the city’s elegant promenade dotted with gourmet shops, this restaurant welcomes guests on the first floor of a thirteenth-century palazzo, which also houses the Cantina Regionale del Roero. Here, chef Davide Palluda continues, year after year, to impress with a cuisine that speaks for itself: dishes of exceptional caliber, at times truly memorable, revealing a confident hand and rare sensitivity. The menu looks to Piedmontese roots while embracing modern, personal interpretations. Among these, one dish stands out for its unexpected delicacy, despite featuring game: fallow deer with grapes, peated whisky, and fermented cacao. Special mention goes to the dessert chapter as well, with indulgent sweets and a generous sequence of petits fours to close the experience alongside coffee.

Name: All'Oro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in the basement of The H'All Tailor Suite, this restaurant boasts two contemporary-style dining rooms, with tables outside in fine weather. Here, Riccardo Di Giacinto serves regional and Italian specialities which he reinterprets with skill and flair, playing with traditional recipes and transforming these with surprising results. Including dishes such as a “summary” of carbonara, cappelletti in “dry broth”, Roman-style lamb, and tiramisù in both savoury (with potatoes and salted cod) and sweet versions, the cuisine here is both astonishing and satisfying.

Name: Alpenroyal Gourmet
Address: Via Meisules 43, Selva di Val Gardena, 39048, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This is the gourmet restaurant at the hotel of the same name, one of the most luxurious in the Val Gardena. The elegant, contemporary dining room has an intimate and minimalist feel, which provides the backdrop for cuisine created by chef Mario Porcelli. Although originally from Puglia, Porcelli has been working in the Dolomites for many years and he is equally at home with local dishes as he is with recipes from his native region. He offers three tasting menus (Tradizione in evoluzione, Omaggio alle Dolomiti, and the vegetarian Terra), from which dishes can also be chosen à la carte style. A choice of delicious and memorable desserts and cakes, as well as an excellent selection of bread and pastries, completes the picture.

Name: Alto
Address: Via Circondariale San Francesco 2, Fiorano Modenese, 41042, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The top floor of the Executive Spa Hotel opens up like a lounge suspended between the sky and the hills: fine dining by chef Mattia Trabetti overlooks an elegant rooftop, where glass walls let in soft light and a relaxing view of the Sanctuary of the Blessed Virgin of the Castle. Before sitting down, you can start – or end – the evening in the adjacent Cocktail Bar Aria, also up there, among reflections and panoramic views. There are two tasting menus (but each dish is also available à la carte): “Modena Safari” and the vegetarian “Emilia vegetale”. Browsing the menu, a small map shows the origin of the ingredients, tracing a journey through Modena, the Apennines and Emilia, interpreted in a contemporary key. The recipes are a blend of memory and creativity: the fresh-egg pasta tortellini are absolutely memorable, a monument to these lands, filled with oxtail and served in a clear broth of meat and savoy cabbage, with a light touch of spicy oil that sets the palate alight. The wine list is a world unto itself: approximately a thousand labels from the region and as far afield as France, with service also by the glass, inviting guests to explore.

Name: Amistà
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: The sense of wonder begins even before you reach the restaurant: inside the Byblos Art Hotel, the sumptuous 16th-century villa that houses it is adorned with stunning works of contemporary art. A blend of styles that continues in Donato De Leonardis’s kitchen. His dishes are often original and feature combinations that are at times daring; a multitude of ingredients come together to create visually sophisticated creations. There are three tasting menus, one of which is vegetarian, although the dishes can also be ordered à la carte. Don’t miss the dessert section – it’s absolutely brilliant.

Name: Ancòra
Description: Created by Iacobucci, who previously made a name for himself at Castel Maggiore, this Romagna-based venture is set within an elegant villa that many enthusiasts will remember as the historic home of the two-star Magnolia restaurant, which has now moved to Longiano. In refined and welcoming surroundings, enhanced by an elegant outdoor dining area beneath a cool pergola – ideal for the warmer months – the resident chef, Marco Garattoni, creates contemporary cuisine characterised by great technical precision, the result of experience gained in high-profile restaurants. His dishes, which are also carefully presented, focus on balance, colour and an immediate, often mouth-watering appeal, with a predominance of fish dishes alongside vegetarian options and meat dishes. Among the signature dishes, alongside the famous triple-risen babà – light as air, aromatic and simply impeccable – the unmissable ‘cuttlefish and peas’ also stands out, served in four different ways (raw, fried, grilled and in a ragù), a compelling example of technical skill and creativity.

Name: Andrea Larossa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Across the Po from the city center, where ample, convenient parking invites a stress-free stop, a luminous dining room awaits, one that once hosted recreational gatherings and social events. Today it retains that same spirit of conviviality, marked by genuine smiles, attentive service, and measured professionalism. In the kitchen, Andrea Larossa demonstrates a deep command of Piedmontese ingredients and traditions, enriched by Southern Italian influences inherited from his family origins and a natural inclination toward contemporary creativity. Two tasting menus favor pleasure over ingredient rarity, free from the dogmas and rigidity of tradition. Both unfold in a generous sequence of small bites, almost a playful prelude that introduces the journey like a fan of appetizers.

Name: Andrea Monesi - Locanda di Orta
Address: Via Olina 14, Orta San Giulio, 28016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Situated in the historic centre of one of the most romantic lakeside villages in Italy, and offering a picture-postcard view of bygone days, this small building houses a contemporary-style restaurant with a small private dining room and three romantic outdoor terraces (book well in advance). The cuisine here is creative and precise, with a menu that features fish and seafood alongside top-quality meat from the Piedmont. Each recipe is personalised, often focusing on contrasting flavours and textures (don’t miss the unstructured elderberry crêpe with pollen and pan brioche). The wine list is overseen by an excellent sommelier who is happy to guide you through the superb wine list.

Name: Andreina
Address: Via Zona Industriale Brodolini, 2, Loreto, 60025, Italy
Description: More than sixty years after Nonna Andreina first opened her doors, this establishment continues to tell a family story deeply rooted in the region. In the elegant surroundings of a former farmhouse, the service stands out for its professionalism and discretion, while the cuisine reaffirms its identity through a focus on game, open fires and charcoal-grilling techniques. Here, the fireplace and the grill are not merely decorative features, but the very heart of the dining experience. The aromas of the spit feature in most of the dishes, enhanced by personal touches and ingredients, some of which are home-grown. There are two tasting menus on offer, ‘Fuoco’ and ‘Fumo’, featuring dishes that will surprise you and offer an original take on tradition. The wine list is well put together.

Name: Angelo Sabatelli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: In the maze of picturesque alleys of the historic center, housed in a 16th-century building with an elongated dining room under a vaulted stone ceiling, are a few tables and a fireplace. This is Angelo Sabatelli's niche, featuring his refined cuisine woven with Apulian inspirations and personal creativity. In the dining room, his son Daniele, an excellent sommelier, will guide you through one of the most extraordinary wine cellars in the region, spanning two volumes with approximately three thousand labels.

Name: Anima
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Housed inside the prestigious Milano Verticale | UNA Esperienze hotel in the Corso Como and Piazza Gae Aulenti district of the city, this restaurant is run by multi-Michelin-starred chef Enrico Bartolini. Minimalist elegance and design are the key words to describe the stylish decor here, inspired by Gio Ponti’s city of the second half of the 20C. Resident chef Michele Cobuzzi prepares dishes with a modern flavour, prepared using top-quality ingredients which are mostly sourced from his native region of Puglia. Given his origins, it’s no surprise that this chef is highly skilful in his preparation of vegetables and bread-making. The wine list is enhanced by an interesting selection of cocktails, including original and exciting drinks from around the world alongside more classic options.

Name: Anna Stuben
Description: Although many brilliant “Anna’s” have cooked in this family-run restaurant over the years, in recent times there has been a superb male chef – Reimund Brunner – at the helm. Since December 2024, the restaurant has occupied a new purpose-built dining room (next to the hotel entrance) – this modern Stube has a few round tables, large windows and a summer terrace overlooking the centre of the small town. The cuisine is inspired by the Alto Adige, yet also remains open to ingredients from further afield, including fish and seafood, in dishes which are lighter and fresh in style with a reduced use of butter and sugar. Our inspector particularly recommends the organic duck serve with late radicchio and black poplar mushrooms.

Name: Antica Corte Pallavicina
Address: Strada del Palazzo Due Torri 3, Polesine Parmense, 43016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: A fairy-tale setting for a property of almost castle-like aspect, originally built as a customs post on the River Po in the fourteenth century. Today Massimo Spigaroli, whose family were once sharecroppers on the surrounding land, is its owner and has transformed the complex into a complete destination: guest rooms, the Hosteria del Maiale bistrot and spaces for private events. Completing the experience are a visit to the Museo del Culatello and a ‘gastrofluvial’ cuisine deeply bound to the traditions of the local area. Among the historic dishes, the frogs’ legs stand out, golden with sweet garlic and parsley upon a velouté of sweet potato and saffron, while the more contemporary offerings also convince, among them a Carnaroli risotto with asparagus, peas, Parizzi snails and lemon zest: balanced and of refined harmony.

Name: Antica Osteria Nonna Rosa
Address: Via Laudano 1, Loc. Pietrapiana, Vico Equense, 80069, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: In the dining room one breathes the genuine warmth of a Campanian home of times past, enriched by personal touches such as the nativity scene that also depicts the chef alongside his grandmother Rosa. For those seeking a more intimate setting, two secluded alcoves accommodate as many tables, perfect for a private dinner. Among dove-grey walls and carefully designed lighting, the kitchen stands out for its originality and creativity, never losing its connection to tradition and to the produce of the Campanian region, often sourced from the restaurant’s own production. The offering is structured across four tasting menus that alternate chef’s surprises, great house classics and interpretations tied to the produce of the Montechiaro kitchen garden, to which one of the menus is dedicated. A vision well summarised in the words of chef-patron Giuseppe Guida: “An intriguing journey through flavours of times past, with forays into more imaginative territory, never renouncing its origins.”

Name: Antonello Colonna Labico
Address: Via di Valle Fredda 52, Labico, 00030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in a scenically impressive setting nestling in the Vallefredda countryside and housed in an original, avant-garde building, this sophisticated restaurant serves carefully balanced and elegant dishes that underline its proximity to Rome and its close connection with Lazio’s rural traditions. Here, nature and modernity go hand in hand: the restaurant is home to large, almost museum-like rooms adorned with works of art and surrounded by parkland. The dishes, on the other hand, are classic in style, in deliberate contrast to the striking, contemporary backdrop in which they are served, and are inspired by many of Italy’s different culinary traditions. We highly recommended booking a table on the lawn under the mature chestnut trees in summer.

Name: Apostelstube
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In beautiful Bressanone, the historic Hotel Elephant, housed in a building whose oldest section dates back to the late 15th century, is one of the city’s true icons. Managed by the same family since 1773, it is now in the hands of the eighth generation. In the intimate and exquisitely elegant dining room, with just four tables and the watchful eyes of the twelve apostles that, in the form of statuettes, observe you from the walls, Chef Mathias Bachmann presents a unique, extensive, and exclusive tasting menu. Drawing ingredients and techniques from around the world, with a special fondness for Japan, he reinterprets them with contemporary flair. Service is entrusted to Michael and Eleonora, whose expertise and innate warmth will also delight you with the incredible tale of the elephant that once passed through the city. In the warm season, aperitifs are served in the pleasant garden; during the colder months or inclement weather, they are offered in the elegant lounge, also on the first floor, just like the dining room.

Name: Aqua Crua
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Just a few tables arranged in a simple, minimalist dining room, facing the open kitchen: the focus here is on chef Giuliano Baldessari and his creative culinary interpretations. There is a restricted selection of dishes available à la carte but, if you really want to enter his culinary world, opt for one of the surprise tasting menus, the first of which consists of ten dishes, served if you’re visiting for the first time, while the last comprises sixteen. Whatever you choose, you can expect sophisticated, imaginative cuisine of the highest standard.

Name: Aroma
Description: From the ground floor, the lift leads to one of the city’s most evocative roof gardens: a terrace which, in winter, is enclosed and covered – thus usable in every season – directly overlooking the Colosseum. To your right unfolds the view of the Domus Aurea, in the distance a corner of the Altare della Patria can be glimpsed and, just beyond, the great dome of St Peter’s. The kitchen offers four tasting menus (of which one is vegetarian), with the option of also ordering individual dishes freely. Between classics of Roman tradition, Campanian influences and more contemporary creations unfolds the offering from chef Giuseppe Di Iorio, who draws on extensive experience here and in other prestigious hotel establishments – both in Rome and internationally. We are, indeed, guests of Palazzo Manfredi.

Name: Assonica
Address: Via Don Santo Carminati 9, Sorisole, 24010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the hills just beyond Bergamo, this smart, elegant and well-run restaurant has the Manzoni brothers (Alex and Vittorio) at the helm in the kitchen, where they create some of the most interesting cuisine in the region, while the capable Giovanna Danzo oversees the excellent service in the dining room. Creative and surprising, the dishes here are striking for their complex and original flavours, which combine vegetables with a clever use of herbs and spices without overwhelming the palate. The chargrilled veal sweetbreads (slightly crunchy on the outside and soft inside) are delicious, served with a selection of mushrooms and a fir extract that provides a hint of bitterness. There’s a strong focus on sourcing local ingredients in order to create cuisine which is both contemporary and sustainable at the same time.

Name: Atelier
Description: The Ossola gastronomic atelier offers a safe harbour for lovers of good food and drink in the town centre. The Bartolucci family's tradition has soared thanks to dynamic chef patron Giorgio and entrepreneurial sister Elisabetta, joined by Katia, whose smile and professionalism are invaluable to guest comfort. In addition to the welcoming service, the cuisine beckons clientele from afar. The evening menu is packed with revisited Ossola citations (among others, gathered in the tasting menu "Flavours and Aromas of the Mountains") alongside contemporary Italian culinary nods. In certain occasional dishes you’ll find the fusion of meat and fish, cooked with such skill and experience that the - not easy - balance aligns perfectly. Such is the case with small local veal rolls stuffed with apple and scampi tartare. A splendid selection of wines is available by the glass, where pairing them with your dishes will be both a pleasure and a delight. At lunch, the Bistrot is open.

Name: Atto di Vito Mollica
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A few steps from the Duomo, within the Corte degli Imperatori of Palazzo Portinari, the historic former residence of the Salviati family, the restaurant occupies a setting of rare beauty, enriched by sixteenth-century frescoes by Alessandro Allori and the soothing sound of a fountain. An authentic Renaissance salon transformed into a refined dining room. The kitchen distinguishes itself through technical precision and elegance, bringing out the very best of the highest-quality produce in dishes that are creative yet always balanced and never contrived. Emblematic is the lightly seared langoustine, served over two mirror sauces – one sweet and aromatic with carrot and orange, the other more acidic and buttery with Champagne. Attentive and considered service accompanies the experience with expertise, from the wine pairing through to the final dedication to coffee.

Name: Berton
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the heart of Porta Nuova, the elegant, contemporary-style dining room at this restaurant has recently been expanded with a veranda that has given a new look to the façade and is perfectly in tune with the character of this new, futuristic district. Here, Andrea Berton’s cuisine focuses on just a few ingredients transformed into attractive dishes which are simple in style without being minimalist. Creative and modern, the chef’s meat and fish dishes are showcased on tasting menus from which courses can also be chosen à la carte style. His “Non Solo Brodo” menu has become a real classic – it is dedicated to different broths served with the dishes (for example, the squid with cherries and aubergines is enhanced by an intensely flavoured squid broth poured over the dish at your table), while in other dishes the broth is served as an accompaniment (lamb with cardamom and coffee served with fragrant chard, accompanied by a cardamom-flavoured lamb broth served in a glass alongside the dish). A business lunch is available on weekdays.

Name: Bistrot
Address: Viale Franceschi 14, Forte dei Marmi, 55042, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Bistrot by name, but in fact an excellent gourmet restaurant, this is the flagship establishment of the Vaiani family, highly professional restaurateurs and true masters of hospitality, who have entrusted the kitchen here to the talent of chef Andrea Mattei. This collaboration has consolidated the style of the Bistrot over the years, maintaining a balance between tradition and modernity, with the quality of the ingredients setting the standard.The establishment’s reputation is linked particularly to the excellence of its fish, largely sourced from the Tyrrhenian Sea, but equally interesting is the use of two wood-fired ovens, thanks to which the chef creates extraordinary baked products and dishes with a unique character. Worth mentioning in this sense is the unmissable rosemary lobster with beans and herring roe, a dish that makes the most of wood-fired cooking to bring out its aromas and textures.At lunchtime, a smaller, more casual selection complements the main menu, without compromising on attention to detail or technical expertise. Completing the experience is a wine cellar of great prestige: nearly 2,000 carefully selected labels, with a special mention for the rich selection of Champagne and Burgundy wines.

Name: Bluh Furore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: The former Furore Inn hotel has reopened with a new contemporary Mediterranean look and a new name (the Furore Grand Hotel ), along with a new gourmet restaurant, the Bluh Furore. Boasting a white colour scheme, minimalist decor and attractive sea views, the restaurant is headed by executive chef Vincenzo Russo under the banner of famous three-Michelin-starred Enrico Bartolini, who is behind some of its legendary signature dishes, such as the half-fried prawn. The menu focuses on modern dishes that feature recipes and ingredients from Campania. A vegetarian tasting menu completes the picture.

Name: Borgo San Jacopo
Address: Borgo San Jacopo 62 r, Florence, 50125, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: The name of this restaurant in the Hotel Lungarno refers to its location in one of the most charming districts in Florence, namely Oltrarno, just beyond the Ponte Vecchio. Here, lucky diners will get the chance to sit at one of two tables on the balcony for an unforgettable dining experience – although wherever you sit, the superb cuisine created by Claudio Mengoni will linger long in the memory. Showcased on two tasting menus and an à la carte, the meat and fish dishes served here are creative and of the highest quality, with the occasional Tuscan influence.

Name: Borgo Sant'Anna
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled among the vineyards and overlooking the gentle hills of the Langhe, this restaurant helmed by chef Pasquale Laera presents a cuisine of distinct identity, where Apulian roots dialog with Piedmontese terroir in a personal, measured balance. In the tasting menus and à la carte offerings, seafood, seasonal vegetables, and select meats coexist, always treated with precise technique and keen gustatory sensitivity. Among the most striking dishes, the hay-smoked buffalo mozzarella with buttermilk and Senise pepper remains a signature course, effectively encapsulating the chef’s philosophy.

Name: Bracali
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: In the center of the small hamlet of Ghirlanda, in the heart of the Colline Metallifere, a discreet entrance leads to the elegant restaurant run by the Bracali brothers. Chef Francesco skillfully navigates between two tasting menus (with dishes also available à la carte), offering modern creations of both meat and fish. Luca, on the other hand, manages the dining room and passionately oversees the wine cellar, which is extensive, well-structured, and divided into two distinct sections: Italy and the rest of the world. Special attention is given to vertical tastings, curated with genuine dedication. Note: Reservations are mandatory!

Name: Butterfly
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Housed in a charming 19th‑century farmhouse and surrounded by a magnificent garden that delights in every season, Butterfly offers a setting as enchanting as its name suggests. The glass‑enclosed veranda dining room adds further appeal: in summer it opens fully onto the lawn, offering fresh air and relaxation, while in winter it remains closed and heated, still allowing diners to enjoy views of the greenery. In the kitchen, father and son Fabrizio and Andrea Girasoli complement each other with perfect harmony, presenting a wide and versatile menu that confidently balances meat and seafood. Their impeccable technique highlights both comforting flavors of tradition – such as unforgettable Tyrrhenian scampi grilled on blazing lava stone with liquid Catalana sauce, baby radish salad, and green mango – and imaginative creations, such as a delicious cocoa cigar filled with foie gras, apple, and hazelnut, a tribute to maestro Puccini. Hospitality is marked by a genuine family spirit, delivered with refined professionalism: Mariella, Fabrizio’s wife, gracefully and attentively orchestrates the service.

Name: Ca' Matilde
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Surrounded by verdant landscapes, this attractive restaurant with a pleasant outdoor dining space is functional in style due to the use of simple materials such as wrought iron and wood, and as such boasts a distinctly minimalist style. A continual quest for cuisine that is both contemporary and rustic in flavour is reflected in owner-chef Vezzani’s reinterpretation of local recipes, which he enhances with interesting combinations and produce grown in the restaurant’s own biodynamic kitchen garden. The restaurant offers five surprise tasting menus: “Gli Intramontabili” (a tribute to the region, often with pairings of the best Lambrusco wines), “Oltremare” (inspired by the sea), “Terramadre” (a regional focus), “Cielo” (a journey between land and sea), and “Hortus” (vegetarian), all of which demonstrate a playful use of flavours and combinations with a keen focus on seasonal ingredients.

Name: Ca' Vittoria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: For generations, the Musso family has been synonymous with hospitality in the heart of one of the region’s most charming villages, where they welcome guests with the attention to detail, professionalism and elegance that characterise the finest Piedmontese tradition. While in the past the cooking of Grandma Gemma and Mum Sandra was deeply rooted in regional recipes, today the restaurant also bears the signature of Massimiliano, a chef who has transformed his passion for Asia and his frequent travels to the East into a contemporary, personal menu rich in culinary influences. This gives rise to dishes such as amberjack prepared using Japanese techniques and grilled on a yakitori skewer, served with various interpretations of courgettes from the family vegetable garden, or desserts that showcase ingredients such as yuzu. Fish plays an important role on the menu, without, however, straying from the cuisine’s roots. Indeed, the restaurant’s plin and its famous signature risotto – often served directly at the table rather than featured on the menu – bear witness to its connection with tradition. During the white truffle season, too, the great classics of the region’s cuisine take centre stage. The winery pays particular attention to Piedmontese wines, complementing its most historic labels with a dynamic and contemporary selection; among the Barolos, there is no shortage of fine vintage bottles, including some dating back to the 1970s.

Name: Cannavacciuolo Bistrot
Description: Antonino Cannavacciuolo – the three-Michelin-starred chef of Villa Crespi – has chosen to set up his Turin establishment in the heart of Borgo Po, one of the city’s most intimate and elegant residential neighbourhoods, just a stone’s throw from the Gran Madre. The dining areas form a series of contemporary, intimate and meticulously designed rooms, the last of which looks directly onto the kitchen for those who'd like to watch the culinary magic unfold. This is where Gabriele Bertolo creates modern cuisine inspired by regional traditions — starting off with those from Campania — reinterpreted with his own personal touch and technique. Two tasting menus and an intriguing à la carte selection complete the youthful, thoughtful and well-prepared dining experience. Booking is essential, even for lunch.

Name: Cannavacciuolo Countryside
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This restaurant is an intimate and deeply personal narrative, inseparably bound to the life story of chef Antonino Cannavacciuolo. It stands on the ground of his own memories, where once his grandfather kept the olive press, and presents itself today as a space rich in resonance, in which an authentic vision of hospitality is brought back to life.The kitchen, entrusted with great sensitivity to resident chef Nicola Somma, consistently interprets the chef’s vision: a continuous dialogue between North and South, between homeland and adopted home, expressed through harmonious and recognisable dishes. Considerable attention is given to the plant world, which features as the centrepiece of a dedicated tasting menu, while the highest-quality produce is sourced partly from local suppliers and partly from the property’s own kitchen garden and orchard, all in a spirit of preserving and celebrating tradition.The wine list, curated with passion and expertise, stands out for its depth and dynamism, offering refined pairings to satisfy even the most discerning enthusiast. The result is an experience that marries gastronomic pleasure with bucolic surroundings, further enriched by a tangible commitment to sustainability, evidenced by the installation of a new photovoltaic system.

Name: Cannavacciuolo Le Cattedrali Asti
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the hills outside Asti, this modern inn with guestrooms is nestled in around 18 hectares of woodland and meadows. The interior decor here is contemporary and minimalist, while the cuisine is overseen by the famous three-Michelin-star chef Antonino Cannavacciuolo, with resident chef Gianluca Renzi, who has already earned his spurs at other top-quality restaurants, at the helm in the kitchen. Originally from Rome (his focaccia is excellent!) and having trained professionally in various locations, Renzi creates cuisine that combines personal imaginative touches with regional influences, including traditional flavours from the Piedmont. The young front-of-house team includes a number of excellent female staff. The superb wine list features more than 2 000 labels, while the cheese trolley focuses on local options.

Name: Cannavacciuolo Vineyard
Address: Via del Teatro 8, Casanova di Terricciola, 56030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Renowned chef Antonino Cannavacciuolo offers a warm welcome amid the rolling hills of Tuscany, in an area of the province of Pisa that remains relatively undiscovered by the general public but is rich in charm and lush green landscapes, where the sunsets provide unforgettable views; the resort blends harmoniously with the village, and the dining room combines contemporary comforts with the charm of its historic ceilings, while in the kitchen, following the changeover in 2026, the resident chef, Lodovico Eulogio – formerly the sous-chef – has imbued the menu with a more minimalist yet consistently refined style, paying equal attention to flavours and balance as well as the elegance of presentation; the service remains of the highest standard and rounds off a relaxing stay, with spacious and cosy apartments and breakfast served directly in your room for a revitalising start to the day.

Name: Cannavacciuolo by the Lake
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within the elegant boutique hotel Laqua by the Lake – part of the Cannavacciuolo family of properties – the view over the lake, enjoyed from the splendid terrace in the warmer months, accompanies the gastronomic experience with natural refinement. In the kitchen, resident chef Gianni Bertone offers dishes of a pronounced Mediterranean character, interpreted with creativity and contemporary sensitivity. Two tasting menus are available: “Brezza”, inspired by the suggestions of the lake, and “Acquolina”, of more Neapolitan evocation; the à la carte remains available for those who prefer to compose their own journey. Among the dishes not to be missed: the John Dory in an aromatic crust and the sequence of desserts, which closes with an indulgent selection of petit fours.

Name: Capogiro
Address: Località Li Mucchi Bianchi, Baia Sardinia, 07021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Among the numerous luxurious resorts of the Costa Smeralda, the stunning 7Pines Sardinia stands out, with its fine dining evening restaurant, Capogiro. The name encapsulates the essence of the experience on the beautiful panoramic terrace: a breathtaking view of the sunset over Baja Sardinia and the sea and coast. Campanian chef Pasquale D’Ambrosio strives to match this beauty with modern Mediterranean cuisine, served on refined Sardinian porcelain and offered through three tasting menus, with à la carte options available. One standout dish features specially made Gragnano dry pasta: fusilloni with black lemon butter and mussel water, accompanied by large mussels and spirulina "caviar." An excellent dish, well-balanced in taste and acidity. The service is perfectly aligned with the location's charm, marked by kindness and professionalism.

Name: Capriccio
Address: Piazza San Bernardo 6, località Montinelle, Manerba del Garda, 25080, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In business since 1965, at Capriccio you'll find a charming covered terrace overlooking a glimpse of the lake, but if the weather doesn't permit outdoor dining, the elegance of the indoor dining rooms will cause no regrets. In Giuliana Germiniasi's kitchen, the dishes are predominantly seafood, with often classic settings that leave experimentation aside and aim for taste satisfaction. Timeless offerings include eggplant parmigiana and lobster and lime spaghettone, on the menu since the opening. An interesting wine selection that will not disappoint fans of Champagne and German Rieslings

Name: Caracol
Address: Via Faro 44, località Capo Miseno, Bacoli, 80070, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: The Campania coast, particularly the Gulf of Naples, is full of breathtaking views, but these are among the most enchanting. Head towards the Cala Moresca hotel, leave your car in the car park, and the staff will accompany you to the restaurant from there. In the tranquillity of a headland surrounded by greenery, you’ll be welcomed by a terrace overlooking the sea: before you lies Procida, set against the backdrop of Ischia; to your left, the unmistakable silhouette of Capri; and to your right, the mainland with Mount Procida. Marvellous. In the kitchen, Angelo Carannante faces the daunting task of rising to the challenge posed by such a spectacular show. He does it in style, with an extensive tasting menu, featuring numerous courses that arrive as a surprise, drawing on regional traditions while giving them a fresh twist with creativity and exotic touches… the results are stunning! The inspector was impressed: tuna belly with white bean purée and caramelised onion.

Name: Carignano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Davide Scabin, one of the most celebrated Piedmontese chefs of the contemporary scene and former holder of two Michelin Stars at Rivoli, now opens a new chapter in one of Turin’s most iconic settings: the historic Grand Hotel Sitea, which in 2025 celebrated its first century. Here the chef gives shape to a radical project, entirely oriented towards the sea, expressed in a single and elaborate tasting menu, “Sangon Beach” – a cultured and ironic homage to the song by Gipo Farassino. The journey subverts convention and hierarchy, beginning with the order of courses: following an “up & down” logic, it opens with intense and structured flavours, such as the turbot with Jerusalem artichoke à la bourguignonne and red wine fish glaze, before gradually lightening towards more vegetable-led, fresh and acidic preparations. Completing the experience, the welcome and service are equally transformed in an immersive key: before being seated, guests are provided with sandals to walk on the sand that covers the floor – specially imported from Spain – while the soundtrack evokes maritime atmospheres and seaside suggestions, contributing to a narrative that is coherent and wholly outside the ordinary.

Name: Casa Bertini
Description: This unexpected gourmet restaurant is housed in a sports centre just outside the charming historic centre of Recanati, birthplace of famous Italian poet Giacomo Leopardi (a visit, either before or after your meal, to the Casa Leopardi and the hill which inspired his famous poem “L’Infinito” is a must, in our opinion). At the helm in the kitchen, young, talented chef Andrea Bertini has returned to his native region where he reinterprets the traditions of the Marche (with a focus on meat) to create light, simple and unfussy dishes. The same simple style is echoed in the decor, which is elegant and very understated. Dishes are showcased on two surprise tasting menus and an à la carte which also features a few fish options.

Name: Casa Buono
Address: Corso Cuneo 28, Località Trucco, Ventimiglia, 18039, Italy
Description: This unexpected Ligurian gem is situated in Trucco, a small village in the Val Roia just inland from Ventimiglia. There’s no à la carte here, just the “Orto e Mare” tasting menu to which guests can also add a meat dish and a selection of cheeses from the well-stocked cheese trolley. Although the dishes are occasionally influenced by Ligurian traditions, they are for the most part creative, surprising and beautifully prepared. Given its success, the restaurant has recently been extended while at the same time retaining its simple, colourful and welcoming ambience. The high-quality service comes courtesy of the chef’s friendly wife, ably assisted by her professional and capable staff.

Name: Casa Leali
Address: Via Valle 1, Puegnago sul Garda, 25080, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The eponymous restaurant of the Leali brothers has, over the course of a decade, become a solid gastronomic point of reference for the area. The cooking displays an increasingly signature style: the dishes are precise and technical, built upon original and carefully considered recipes, while a growing interest in the vegetable world emerges with ever greater clarity, even as sound offerings of fish and meat remain on the menu. Among these, the rainbow trout stands out, served with a mayonnaise drawn from its own roe, a parsley sauce and a kind of Brescian ceviche also based on trout: an emblematic example of their approach. In the dining room, the service is attentive and passionate, with a particular affection for sparkling wines and Champagne, alongside a solid grounding in still wines. The elegant dining room – created from the restoration of a fifteenth-century farmhouse – continues to improve with each visit, confirming the considered and welcoming character of this establishment. A venue of consistent and well-deserved growth.

Name: Casa Mazzucchelli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At certain times of day, the tempting aroma of freshly baked bread greets you as soon as you step into this restaurant, leaving you in no doubt as to the nature of the restaurant’s newest venture. Other dishes are also baked in the oven here, such as wild boar served with a red wine babà and sage mayonnaise. There are two tasting menus available (Attimi di cucina and Momento contemporaneo), both of which showcase traditionally influenced cuisine full of distinct flavours.

Name: Casa Sgarra
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: A restaurant bearing the surname of three brothers who crafted this gourmet Trani address: two in the dining area, one in the kitchen. An atmosphere elegant and contemporary; the service cradles guests like family, whilst Felice Sgarra at the stove astonishes with dishes sometimes drawn from Apulian traditions, as well as those from other regions, all closely interpreted and elaborated personally. If cheese is your passion, don’t miss the remarkable trolley showcasing Piedmont and French offerings.

Name: Casamatta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just a few kilometres from Manduria, the home of Primitivo, Casamatta is situated within the Vinilia Wine Resort, housed in an elegant early 20th-century castle surrounded by a picturesque park of centuries-old olive trees. The bright and lively interiors strike a balance between references to tradition and retro-style details inspired by the 1950s and 1960s, while in the warmer months you can sit outside. At the helm of the kitchen is Pietro Penna, who, in 2026, celebrated ten years at the helm of the restaurant, demonstrating remarkable culinary consistency. His modern and creative menu showcases seasonal ingredients and local produce, while also offering a fresh take on some of Apulia’s great classics, such as the famous braciola, reimagined with tomato, garlic and lime. The menu features three tasting menus, one of which is vegetarian, all of which are also available à la carte.

Name: Casin del Gamba
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Run by the same family since 1976, this restaurant is accessed via a steep winding road and yet the many loyal guests who return here time and time again are proof that the journey is well worth the effort. Once here, the warm welcome offered by the whole family, the attractive dining room with a fireplace, and the delicious cuisine all add to the appeal. Showcasing substantial cuisine with a focus on local flavours (the winter menu featuring game dishes and mushrooms is extraordinary), the menu offers traditional dishes that appeal to the eyes and the palate. The equally superb wine list includes various organic and biodynamic labels.

Name: Cavallino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the rooms of an old farmhouse that “Drake” Enzo Ferrari purchased, along with the entire area now dedicated to the iconic Maranello factory and symbol of Italy in the world, to make it a company canteen later transformed from 1950 into a proper restaurant, today the creative vein of Massimo Bottura is expressed through the work of his student Riccardo Forapani and of Virginia Cattaneo. The most orthodox regional cuisine – the tortellini from Tortellante are unmissable – is therefore also represented with refined customizations, as with Mòdna, the Sachertorte in a customized version with sour cherries. Interesting wine list with many by-the-glass options; all in an atmosphere with charmingly vintage tones.

Name: Cetaria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Overlooking the main street of Baronissi, within a historic palazzo, this small restaurant draws its strength from the passion and close partnership of the couple who animate it: Salvatore in the kitchen and Federica in the dining room, winner of the MICHELIN Service Award 2024. A handful of tables, contemporary furnishings, and an intimate atmosphere provide the setting for a welcome that is warm and spontaneous, enriched by an attentive narration of both the cellar and the gastronomic offering. The kitchen reinterprets Campanian ingredients and recipes with contemporary touch, favouring seafood and quality produce sourced also from a kitchen garden and a small family farm in Calabria, Federica's homeland. The proposal develops across two tasting menus: Senza Copione, entrusted to the chef's creative instinct, and Nero su Bianco, inspired by the sea and the surrounding hills, with the occasional international digression. Salvatore's cooking is precise and full of flavour without being overly elaborate; particularly accomplished is the bitter herb, seafood and black lemon risotto, a refined reinterpretation of a traditional local soup. The creamy and intense mantecatura is enriched by the iodine-laced flavours of oyster and a pesto of wild herbs gathered by the chef himself, while the balance between vegetal bitterness and marine umami finds further depth in the lightly seared oysters and melted cheese.

Name: Colline Ciociare
Description: A historic restaurant in the Ciociaria region, chef Salvatore Tassa has, over the years, demonstrated a creativity often rooted in the local area, which has left a lasting mark. Today, it is presented as a tasting menu available in two versions – with five or seven courses – revisiting some of his classics while introducing innovative new dishes. The cuisine at Trattoria NU' is more traditional.

Name: Condividere
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within the Nuvola complex of Lavazza, alongside recommending a visit to the Coffee Museum, Condividere springs from an idea and the consultancy of famed Spanish chef Ferran Adrià. It's the precise and extraordinary style of Chef Federico Zanasi that pampers its patrons. The dining room itself is unique, colourful, and vibrant, where music seems as prominent as the decor. Two tasting menus are offered: Festival and the longer Gran Festival, featuring a series of dishes and sometimes tastings that highlight the quality of raw materials, crafting recipes from few ingredients, occasionally technical and simpler at times, always brimming with flavour and often storytelling about the great Italian cuisine. For desserts, diners relocate to the lounge veranda, where they will smile at a sequence of small sweet delights. Since their opening, they've made a mark on the hearts of Turin residents—booking well in advance is highly advised.

Name: Contrada
Address: Località Monastero d'Ombrone 19, Castelnuovo Berardenga, 53019, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the charming setting of an old hamlet, chef Davide Canella, who has plenty of experience behind him, serves delicious, elegant cuisine presented on a tasting menu and an à la carte on which meat takes centre stage (although a few fish options also feature). Dishes include exquisite prawns and panzanella, and duck breast served with hosomaki. Manuela, the friendly, professional sommelier, oversees the front of house, offering excellent recommendations on the best wine pairings. In other words, a delightful all-round dining experience thanks to the competence and enthusiasm of all involved.

Name: Contrada Bricconi
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Leaving the Val Seriana behind, the road climbs through hairpin turns leading to a small fifteenth-century stone village perched above a breathtaking panorama. Here, a group of young visionaries has breathed new life into this remote Alpine corner, reviving ancient customs and building a self-sufficient ecosystem of cultivation and husbandry founded on quality, sustainability and animal welfare. The tasting menu unfolds in a harmonious crescendo of flavours: classic techniques such as the grill and fermentation meet modern impulses, as in the refined ravioli of calf’s head with plum broth and kimchi oil. Worthy of particular mention are the bread course, served with the house’s own churned butter, and the closing sweet: a light and yielding pan brioche accompanied by a silky zabaione of pollen. Behind this cooking is the young Michele Lazzarini, a chef of remarkable ability who transforms his mountains into an intense and compelling gastronomic narrative, deeply rooted in the territory yet startlingly contemporary.

Name: Contraste
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Following recent refurbishment, this restaurant in a period building that conjures up an image of old Milan has a bright and colourful feel thanks to its shades of blue, red and green. The courtyard, a small, tranquil space that adds an unexpected touch of greenery to this urban setting, is perfect for a cigar or aperitif. Once inside chef Matias Perdomo’s home, you have a choice between the “Riflesso” menu (traditional dishes yet prepared using modern techniques) and the “Riflessioni” menu (bolder and more innovative options featuring unusual combinations). Contraste’s philosophy lies in the chef’s ability to bring his ingredients to life, using imaginative combinations that delight and appeal to the palate. Overseen with professionalism by an excellent team that will offer recommendations for the best pairings (either wine or non-alcoholic options), the wine list includes a selection of labels from around the world, with a particular focus on France.

Name: Coria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Having left its historic home in Caltagirone in 2024, Coria has relocated to the heart of Catania's historic centre, within a period palazzo. The interiors, enriched by red sofas, gilded details and works by Nunzio Fisichella dedicated to Etna, offer an atmosphere that is elegant and contemporary, accompanied by attentive and discreet service. The cuisine remains deeply rooted in Sicilian tradition, reinterpreted with refined technique and modern awareness without losing its balance. Three tasting menus are offered – Equilibrio, Origini and Magma – alongside the option of composing one's own menu from the à la carte. Among the most interesting dishes, the almond-filled Bottone, the Linguina with clams and mantis shrimp, and the Lamb "abbuttunatu come un'impanatigghia" stand out as examples of a cuisine that interprets the local area with elegance and personality. The wine list offers a broad selection ranging from Sicily across the whole of Europe.

Name: Cortile Spirito Santo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: At the southernmost tip of Ortigia, steps from Castel Maniace, there is one of the most refined expressions of Syracusan gastronomy and, more broadly, one of the most fully realised interpretations of Sicilian culinary identity. Within the spaces of Palazzo Salomone Luxury Suites, Giuseppe Torrisi presents a creative and technical cuisine of almost baroque character, capable of combining intensity of flavour with elegance of execution, often to memorable effect. Particularly striking are the monkfish meunière with wild fennel and asparagus, and the “Assoluto di mandorla” (Made in Sicily), a curious and accomplished homage to the island, even reproduced in its shape. The wine list is broad and well structured: one may range across the interesting local productions, from Etna to the western coast, or entrust oneself to the expertise and discretion of sommelier Antonino, to explore a selection of international scope as well. Completing the experience is the pleasure of dining in the cool and relaxing outdoor terrace, amid soft lighting and gentle lounge music.

Name: Cracco Portofino
Description: In Portofino, the celebrated chef Cracco has installed himself in the building that was once no less than Il Pitosforo, right in front of the small harbour, guaranteeing his lucky guests a view of it, the piazzetta and the enchanting gulf. Through the skill and expertise of executive chef Mattia Pecis, it offers a moderately modern line of cuisine, in two tasting courses - 7 courses or 11 courses - which do not lack beautiful references to Ligurian recipes and ingredients (many vegetables directly from the Fescion Farmer's vegetable garden, a short distance away, in the mountains), with the novelty of the cold room for “maturing” the fish. The charming terrace, open in fine weather from 6.30 p.m. onwards, is the ideal location for aperitifs and dinners in the open air.

Name: Cracco in Galleria
Address: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, Milan, 20121, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II is one of the most iconic sights in Milan and as such it is apt that it is home to this star of Italian cuisine, whose professional career is one of the most impressive in Italy with influences that include the culinary master Alain Ducasse and wine expert Giorgio Pinchiorri. Together with owner Carlo, resident chef Luca Sacchi creates top-quality cuisine with impeccable technique. He showcases his dishes on a carefully composed tasting menu and an à la carte, with references to contemporary Italian cuisine in dishes such as the open ravioli and reinterpretations of classic favourites, such as vitello alla Milanese (breaded veal cutlet). The wine list is an experience in itself, offering one of the best and most comprehensive selections of French wines in Italy, as well as an excellent choice of wines by the glass. Guests also have the opportunity to taste wines from the organic Vistamare estate, owned by the chef and situated in the Romagna hills. The most popular tables are those by the window with views of the Octagonal building – these should be booked well in advance.

Name: Crocifisso
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: In the historic upper section, close to the namesake church, lies one of the most compelling culinary offerings. Within rooms exuding a modern and essential vibe, blanketed in dusky evening lighting, Marco Baglieri’s excellent cuisine becomes sophisticated and almost baroque, paying homage to the urban style of one of Sicily's most enchanting cities. Both the artichoke cooked two ways on brioche with anchovy sauce and the cod with leek foam and cuttlefish ink, embellished with black truffle and basil oil—sampled on our last visit—were exceptional. The scope also extends to meat and vegetarian dishes. The exterior proudly displays a glass-walled cellar showcasing the breadth and order of its selection.

Name: Cucina Cereda
Address: Via Piazzini 33, Ponte San Pietro, 24036, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A charming entrance through the courtyard, where in summer a few tables are set beneath the open sky, leads into what was once a sixteenth-century monastery. Inside, the atmosphere turns more classic and elegant, but the spotlight belongs entirely to the cuisine: excellent ingredients transformed with creativity (the staff’s recommendations on fresh arrivals are worth heeding), in meat and fish dishes that weave Italian roots with local touches, offered both à la carte and as a tasting menu. Among the creations that won us over: a creamy risotto with langoustines and lemon, paccheri bathed in fish soup, and to finish, “Mi piace il sole,” a Mediterranean dessert redolent of Sicily.

Name: D.one Ristorante Diffuso
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: A few kilometres into the first hills of the Adriatic hinterland are well worth the journey to reach the tranquil village of Montepagano. Here one finds a restaurant of original and engaging character, which defines itself as a ‘ristorante diffuso’: a concept given tangible form by a succession of rooms, dining spaces and intimate period salons, punctuated by strikingly contemporary works of art, as though one were moving through a miniature village within the village. The gastronomic direction is entrusted to a chef of considerable ability, capable of conveying through simple yet imaginative recipes a personal interpretation of the territory and its ancient traditions, with occasional echoes of his native Puglia. His work is enhanced by the contribution of the proprietress, who receives guests with engaging stories drawn from the history of the place, lending warmth and depth to the experience. Worthy of particular note is the current celebratory menu ‘10 anni, 10 piatti, 10 euro a piatto’: each creation represents a year, an evolution and a memory, offering a compelling and comprehensive panorama of the culinary identity of the house and the talents of chef Davide Pezzuto.

Name: Da Gorini
Address: Via Verdi 5, San Piero in Bagno, 47021, Italy
Description: This restaurant in San Piero in Bagno’s historic centre takes its name from its young chef Gianluca da Gorini, who prepares original and creative cuisine inspired by the traditions of this beautiful hilly region as well as his own more imaginative creations. Frequently used ingredients include mushrooms, game, freshwater fish and Mora Romagnolo suckling pig, often combined with other more exotic fare. There’s a particular emphasis on dishes cooked over the barbecue grill, which gives ingredients such as lamb, eel and pigeon a particularly pleasant texture and flavour.

Name: Da Lucio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This restaurant boasts an impressive setting on the end of a jetty surrounded by the sea in Rimini docks. The entrance stands next to the open-view kitchen (a spectacle in itself!), which then leads into the long dining room. Nearly all the fish here (which comes from the Adriatic) is aged to allow water to evaporate so that the flavours are concentrated; it is then grilled or baked in a wood-fired oven, as well as served raw, with surprising and remarkable results.

Name: Dalla Gioconda
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At the highest point of the town, in Gabicce Monte, a short tunnel with porthole windows leads to a lift and from there to the restaurant: an enchanting terrace (enclosed by glass walls when the weather demands) commanding views over the sea and the surrounding hills. We recommend arriving at sunset: when weather conditions are favourable, the sunset from here is spectacular. Much the same can be said of Davide Di Fabio’s cooking, which draws inspiration from various gastronomic traditions – local and otherwise – to which the chef brings a personal and thoroughly accomplished interpretation. An exceptional wine list is a further accomplice, extending to French labels and offering a generous choice by the glass.

Name: Damini Macelleria & Affini
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: You’ll be surprised by the entrance to this restaurant – the door opens into one of the region’s best-stocked butcher’s, delicatessen and general retailer of niche food products. It’s well worth taking time to browse the shelves before making your way to the dining room to the rear, where wine bottles line the walls (the wine cellar is also superb). Meat takes centre stage at Damini, including top-quality meat from the region and further afield. The menu features classic dishes alongside more creative options, plus a few more exotic ingredients.

Name: Dattilo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Nestled in the countryside and surrounded by the vineyards of the family estate, this restaurant offers cuisine deeply rooted in the region and the rhythm of the seasons. Most of the ingredients come directly from the farm, while the wines served at the table are produced on the estate, as part of a gastronomic experience that authentically reflects the identity of the place. Susy and Roberto are on hand to welcome guests, and their warm hospitality helps to create a warm and genuine atmosphere. The property also features a number of recently refurbished rooms and a swimming pool set among the greenery, next to a majestic, centuries-old olive tree that dominates the landscape.

Name: Del Cambio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This historic restaurant, a jewel of Piedmont and with few equals in Europe, dates back to the 18th century. The Risorgimento room retains its 19th-century charm, enhanced by meticulous restoration. The creaking of the original parquet accompanies footsteps in a place that is also part of Italy's history: Cavour once sat here, with a view of Palazzo Carignano, the first Parliament of the unified nation. Behind it, the Pistoletto room offers a simpler, more informal atmosphere. The cuisine celebrates tradition with classic Piedmontese dishes – from vitello tonnato to agnolotti del Plin – but it's in the second courses that it truly shines: the pigeon alla Maredo is unforgettable, executed with mastery and served with great professionalism. Another distinctive feature is the extensive and carefully selected wine list, with important verticals, especially regional and among German Rieslings, perfect for pairing with delicacies such as steamed scampi in red sauce. Del Cambio also serves as a bistro for lunch and a "pharmacy" (in the sense of a boutique and taste lab), where you can sample delights from the talented pastry chef.

Name: Dissapore di Andrea Catalano
Description: Nestled in the heart of the labyrinth of alleyways in the historic centre, this small, elegant restaurant welcomes guests beneath a striking domed ceiling. At the helm are Andrea and Franca, a close-knit couple both in their personal and professional lives: he’s in the kitchen, while she’s in the dining room, where she coordinates the attentive service with professionalism and warmth. Their philosophy is as simple as it is effective: to make each guest feel at home. In the kitchen, the superb ingredients from Apulia take centre stage in dishes that blend creativity with respect for tradition, ranging from regional flavours to national and international influences. A prime example is the famous mille-feuille, presented here with coffee namelaka, red berry gelée, vanilla ice cream and lime sorbet.

Name: Dolada
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: An idyllic picture-postcard setting in a panoramic location overlooking Santa Croce lake, surrounded by villages and mountain peaks. This is matched by an elegant interior with a mix of antique and modern furnishings, and a succession of stylish small dining rooms and lounges, including an open fireplace where many of the ingredients are cooked. For over a century, this restaurant has told the story of the De Pra family and their love for the mountains which is clearly evident in the cuisine served here. Chef Riccardo has strengthened this connection by intensifying his search for local ingredients (game, mushrooms, freshwater fish etc) and cultivating his own kitchen garden and vineyard. The fragrant ingredients are prepared simply yet with technical expertise, with flavour always the primary focus – an infallible recipe for resounding success!

Name: Dolce Stil Novo alla Reggia
Address: Piazza della Repubblica 4, Venaria Reale, 10078, Italy
Description: A truly regal setting, and it couldn’t be otherwise: the restaurant entrance is located in the inner courtyard of the Reggia di Venaria, the splendid Savoy hunting residence. A lift takes guests up to the fourth floor, where elegant dining rooms inspired by the style of the 1950s and 60s open out onto a terrace overlooking the gardens. In fine weather, dining outdoors is an experience within the experience, thanks to a truly unique panorama. The cuisine starts from the extraordinary products of Piedmont’s valleys, then ranges to the rest of the region and, sometimes, beyond, with dishes that swing between tradition, featuring a significant vegetable component. At lunch, only a carefully composed à la carte selection is offered, while in the evening there are also tasting menus, with dishes chosen at the chef’s discretion.

Name: Dolomieu
Address: Via Castelletto Inferiore 10, Madonna di Campiglio, 38086, Italy
Description: Though structurally connected to the DV Chalet hotel, it has its own independent entrance. The dining room’s modern elegance still pays tribute to its roots, with photographs on the walls honoring renowned local climbers. Trentino-born chef Fiorenzo Perremuto explores his home region, uncovering culinary treasures from Lake Garda to the Dolomites through refined, creative cooking.

Name: Don Alfonso 1890
Address: Corso Sant'Agata 11, Sant'Agata sui Due Golfi, 80061, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: In Sant'Agata, poised between two gulfs, Don Alfonso represents an image of southern Italy, the family and Mediterranean cuisine found in few other restaurants. Boasting an enchanting garden, splendid guestrooms and an elegant dining room, Don Alfonso 1890’s reputation was established by Livia and Alfonso, who are still here, greeting guests as though they were old friends. They have now been joined by their sons Ernesto and Mario (the former in the kitchen and the latter front of house). The legendary wine list, as well as a good selection of spirits, plus the organic kitchen garden at Punta Campanella which provides many of the vegetables on the menu, add to one of the most beautiful family stories in Italian gastronomy.

Name: Don Geppi
Address: Corso Marion Crawford 40, Sant' Agnello, 80065, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Just twelve covers within the Majestic Palace Hotel make for an intimate and exclusive experience, enhanced by walls decorated with a large plant-themed canvas that echoes the romantic views visible from the windows. The gaze opens onto one of the most enchanting gardens on the coast, where citrus trees and olives – including a thousand-year-old specimen – coexist alongside an organic kitchen garden that supplies part of the vegetables featured on the menu. Chef Mario Affinita presents four tasting menus, with the possibility of combining courses (from a minimum of four), in a continuous dialogue between his Campanian roots and the influences gathered through his international experience. The result is a complex and rigorous cuisine, built on technique and precision, perfectly attuned to the elegance and harmony of its surroundings.

Name: Due Camini
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated within Borgo Egnazia, one of the most exclusive and luxurious resorts in the region (and further afield), this restaurant is home to chef Domingo Schingaro who showcases typical Puglian cuisine by placing vegetables centre stage. Working with local growers and often using heritage varieties, the chef creates an array of dishes, making the most of every single part of his ingredient in order to reduce food waste. His elegant presentations and intense flavours are sure to win you over, even if you’re not vegetarian. Attentive, welcoming and friendly service completes the picture.

Name: Due Colombe
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Le Due Colombe boasts a picturesque setting in a charming village in the heart of the Franciacorta region. The main dining room, housed in an old hay barn, boasts stone walls, a ceiling with wooden beams and a parquet floor, all of which add to the intimate and welcoming atmosphere. The fine cuisine celebrated here includes historic dishes that have become classic favourites and which can be chosen from the three tasting menus. A good example is the beef cooked with olive oil and served with polenta: “Nonna” Elvira made this dish in the post-war period and her grandson Stefano follows the same recipe today. The menu also includes a few fish dishes, while wine-enthusiasts shouldn’t hesitate to ask sommelier Federica for her recommendations – you won’t regret it!

Name: El Molin
Description: The creak of the ancient wooden floor welcomes you to this seventeenth-century mill, where chef-owner Alessandro Gilmozzi – an authentic alpine guide of gastronomy – conveys his deep passion for the territory. On the table, freshly executed smoking techniques, an extraordinary use of local herbs, barks, lichens, and resins are combined with rare cheeses, intensely flavored game, and freshwater fish, all interpreted with creativity and distinctive cooking methods. Three tasting menus are now offered: one of four courses, the other two of eight. The wine list features appealing labels, also available by the glass.

Name: Elementi
Address: Via del Colle 38, località Brufa, Torgiano, 06089, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Elementi: a name that encapsulates the essence of the project, built on people, ingredients, and ideas. Inside, Chef Andrea Impero's kitchen takes you on a journey of intense flavors, creativity, and respect for the excellence of the Lazio region. The attentive and friendly service completes the experience, turning every dinner into a memorable moment.

Name: Equilibrio
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: The young Jacopo Chieppa, captivated early on by a passion for cooking, began his career working with doughs and leavened products, before training in prestigious establishments such as Mirazur in Menton and Antica Corona Reale in Cervere. Today, in a skilfully restored former mill, he offers cooking that is playful and indulgent, contemporary in form yet rooted in classic ingredients, including those from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden adjacent to the premises. The gastronomic experience unfolds through two distinct tasting menus: Identità, which brings together the signature dishes most representative of the chef’s vision, and Evoluzione, the creative menu that follows the seasons and ideas of the moment. Also worthy of note is the dessert section, imaginative and precise in its balance, never overly sweet and always carefully presented.

Name: Esplanade
Address: Via Lario 3, Desenzano del Garda, 25015, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: A historic restaurant on Lake Garda; the view of the lake from the outdoor tables is extraordinary. For the more romantic among you – weather permitting, of course – a table (for two to six people) is set up for dinner on the restaurant’s jetty. The menu is extensive, with a focus on fish, but also featuring a range of meat dishes, including both classic and more creative recipes, created by chef Massimo Fezzardi. An extraordinary wine cellar.

Name: FRE
Address: Località San Sebastiano 68, Monforte d'Alba, 12065, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled among the vineyards of the Réva resort less than 4km from the delightful village of Monforte d'Alba, you’ll find the FRE restaurant run by chef Francesco Marchese, who offers a perfect combination of sophisticated French techniques and fine ingredients from the Langhe with refined simplicity. For all their sophistication, the dishes are always full of rich flavours – the ravioli del plin with crispy sweetbreads, onion cooked in milk and dehydrated beer yeast is a perfect example. There’s a superb wine list with labels also available by the glass, while more informal fare is served at the Piccolo FRE Bistrot.

Name: Fradis Minoris
Description: Fradis Minoris is a naturalistic and sustainable venture, inspired by the distant allure of the Nora Lagoon Natural Park. This captivating environment serves as a muse for creating a distinctive journey within the realm of fine dining. After parking, guests take a short walk of a few hundred metres along the isthmus, entering a protected marine area managed by the restaurant owners themselves. It seems almost inevitable that the culinary direction here embraces a fully circular approach. The menu features a single tasting option, deeply rooted in the seasonality of local ingredients: the catch is often sourced directly from the lagoon, or at most, the southern Sardinian sea. Additionally, wild herbs are gathered from the lagoon, and a variety of vegetables are sourced from nearby Campidano's small-scale producers. Creativity and the technical prowess of chef Francesco Stara shape exquisite and novel tasters. The wine list, with its profound focus on discovering small-scale producers scattered across the island, mirrors a strong attention to the region, complemented by an intriguing wine pairing suggested by the sommelier. Supporting this offering is their bistrot version, FradisLab.

Name: Gambero Rosso
Address: Via Montezemolo 65, Marina di Gioiosa Ionica, 89046, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: A restaurant that passionately celebrates the catch of the Ionian Sea, showcasing fish and shellfish through preparations that highlight their pure flavors: from pristine crudo to lightly dressed dried pastas, to grilled selections accompanied by sauces of unmistakable regional character, dominated by bergamot and chili pepper. Among the standout choices is the fresh scampi, offered grilled in its purest form or enhanced with a dressing that balances acidity and gentle heat, always maintaining impeccable clarity of taste. The cellar presents an appealing array of Calabrian labels, complemented by national and international selections to satisfy both traditionalists and those drawn to modern interpretations. Not to be missed is the SP1, a traditional-method sparkling wine from Gaglioppo grapes, an ideal companion for raw fish, thanks to its vibrant freshness and fine bubbles. A venue that pays tribute to the sea with authenticity and restraint.

Name: Gellivs
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Gellivs boasts a unique and atmospheric setting within the Antica Opitergium museum, surrounded by archaeological remains that tell the story of the town from the beginning of the Roman period, although the contemporary-style furniture and decor here bring us right into the modern day. Here, chef Alessandro Breda creates cuisine that is reassuringly traditional in dishes such as potato mousse, cooked and raw cod, quince and puntarella greens, and more modern in specialities such as the Treviso-Tokyo lobster. An impressive wine list which includes Italian and international labels completes the picture.

Name: Glass Hostaria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: In the heart of the most authentic Trastevere, among streets bustling with trattorias, Glass is located in what was once a carriage workshop – a detail still perceptible from the high ceilings – now transformed into a modern, refined restaurant. The cooking of Cristina Bowerman, while allowing certain echoes of Lazio’s culinary traditions to surface, expresses itself above all in a creative register, drawing with ease upon influences from other gastronomic cultures, from Asia to Latin America. Considerable care is devoted to the sourcing of ingredients, selected through trusted and sustainable suppliers, as well as to the reduction of waste in all its forms. The wine list is also very well curated, enriched by an interesting selection of liqueurs and spirits. A contemporary and cosmopolitan venue, capable of bringing fresh energy to the neighbourhood while remaining perfectly attuned to its lively spirit.

Name: Glicine
