FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated just outside Amalfi with the elegant Mediterranean landscapes of the Amalfi Coast as a backdrop, this fine-dining restaurant at the beautiful Santa Caterina hotel is perched above the sea and boasts stunning views and a tranquil ambience. Talented chef “Peppe” Stanzione from Salerno is at the helm here, having gained experience in renowned Michelin-starred restaurants in places as far afield as California, Australia, China and Thailand. While his passion for Asia is obvious in some dishes, it is the flavours and recipes of Campania that are to the fore, combined with other more exotic influences. Examples include the delicious tuna cooked in an infusion of sake and soy sauce and accompanied by smoked aubergine cream topped with crispy saffron onions and yuzu. There’s also a good choice of vegan, vegetarian and gluten-free dishes.

Name: Gourmetstube Einhorn
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: What was once an old coaching inn at the end of the 13th century has now become the elegant Hotel Stafler. At the heart of the property lies a refined gourmet restaurant, set within a charming medieval wooden stube that seats just five tables, offering an experience of rare intimacy. Chef Peter Girtler offers a four- or five-course tasting menu that celebrates tradition and the region, alternating between meat, freshwater fish and vegetables, most of which come from the family’s own vegetable garden, where the animals are also reared. Among the most successful dishes, the Mediterranean influence on the menu stands out, best exemplified by the risotto with salsa verde and shellfish, complemented by onion jelly with vinegar, horseradish foam and sea fennel: an elegant, balanced dish.

Name: Grow Restaurant
Description: Technique, creativity and a focus on and respect for the past are just some of the criteria that guide chef Matteo Vergine. His modern dishes aim to reflect the ancestral flavours of Brianza and Lombardy in bygone days when hunting, freshwater fishing, growing vegetables and gathering wild herbs were all part of everyday life. In the evening, choose between three tasting menus – in an effort to minimise food waste, guests are required to make their choice at the time of booking. We particularly enjoyed the quail served with its own broth and a brioche, and the gnocchi with stracchino cheese, caramel and venison bottarga. Lighter and less expensive options are available at lunchtime, as well as a convivial table for eight which can be shared with “strangers”. This love for the region extends to the whole of Italy when it comes to the wine list, which is concise yet personal and exclusively features natural Italian wines, all of which are served skilfully and with a wealth of information by sommelier Riccardo.

Name: Grual
Address: Via Alpe di Grual 16, Pinzolo, 38086, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed within the Lefay Resort & Spa Dolomiti, an elegant hotel that dominates Pinzolo and is one of the best hotels in the Trentino region, this gourmet restaurant takes its name from the mountain behind the hotel (the Grual). Here, in the evening, chef Matteo Maezza serves his own reinterpretations of typical mountain cuisine inspired by the three different altitudes from which he sources his ingredients. For example, the bottom of the valley (“fondovalle”) is the inspiration for his marinated whitefish from Lake Garda, served with different types of turnip and Mugo pine milk; the Alpine pasture region (“alpeggio”) has inspired the delicious rib of beef with mustard and carrots; while the high mountain area (“alta montagna”) is behind the elaborate saddle of venison with cardoon gratin with a beef marrow and creamed rye crust. There’s also an impressive wine list featuring an impressive selection of champagnes.

Name: Gucci Osteria da Massimo Bottura
Description: In Piazza della Signoria, one of Florence’s most iconic locations, stands the building that houses Gucci Osteria, the result of a collaboration between the Florentine fashion house and Massimo Bottura. The elegant and refined interiors impress with details such as the magnificent hand-painted parquet flooring, creating a setting worthy of a kitchen where aesthetics are a defining feature. At the helm is Takahiko Kondo, who blends Tuscan, Italian and international influences into dishes that are visually and gustatorily striking. A standout dish is the ‘Sogno di cacciucco’, a refined take on one of the great classics of the Livorno tradition: scallops and almonds harmonise with raw tuna belly with its Eastern influences, before giving way to a bowl of authentic cacciucco that brings the story back to its roots.

Name: Guido
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: From the outside, it recalls an elegant bathing establishment overlooking a blue expanse that seems to know no bounds; once across the threshold, the interiors reveal a whispered, unexpected elegance. Now in its third generation – since the grandfather opened the first establishment in 1946 – Guido is a meeting place for seafood cuisine which, although it begins with apparently simple dishes, reveals nuances of refined elegance and subtle technique. The ingredients are those most typical of the upper Adriatic, woven into recipes that have nourished family memory and are reinterpreted with personal, original sensitivity, without ever losing the essence of cooking that is rich, generous and full of flavour. Examples include the sea snails alla marinara, red mullet with its pastry, and open stuffed squid, to name only a few of the house’s emblematic dishes.

Name: Guidoristorante
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: It was 1961 when Lidia and Guido Alciati opened their restaurant, giving life to a revolution that would forever change the face of Italian gastronomy. With dedication and sacrifice, they marked an epochal turning point: they were among the first to understand the value of the territory, passionately seeking out small niches of gastronomic excellence. Lidia, at the stove, enhanced these products with cooking that was immediate and respectful of the raw materials, while Guido oversaw exceptional service and an extraordinary cellar. Today their legacy lives on and is renewed in the sumptuous halls of the royal estate of Fontanafredda, where their sons, Ugo and Piero, continue the path traced by their parents. In the kitchen Ugo brings sensitivity and precision, while in the dining room Piero welcomes guests with experience and warmth: together they offer the best of Piedmontese food and wine, through dishes that celebrate the richness of the territory with an elegance made of authenticity and simplicity. Symbol of this tradition is the celebrated plin – the pinch with which Lidia closed her agnolotti – which has become a worldwide icon, still served today with the same enchantment: a velvety roast jus that envelops thin pasta, a treasure chest of fragrant meat and vegetable filling. And in a hall of ancient elegance, with sober charm, the modern fireplace creates an ideal bridge between past and present.

Name: Gusto by Sadler
Address: Via Tavolara, località Lu Fraili di Sotto, San Teodoro, 07052, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: To the north of San Teodoro, within the Baglioni Resort, the restaurant offers a Mediterranean-inspired cuisine that strikes a balance between more classical references and contemporary accents. On the one hand, dishes such as the lobster salad with sweet-and-sour vegetables and yellow cherry tomato gazpacho, or the hearty pan-fried shellfish dish; on the other, more modern creations such as the dessert ‘Black Forest’ with cherries in wine, cardamom shortcrust pastry and hazelnut ice cream. The menu is rounded off with a vegetarian tasting menu, designed to showcase the seasonality and freshness of the ingredients. The setting is highly appealing: dinner is taken overlooking a beautifully kept garden with a swimming pool, immersed in a relaxed atmosphere that embodies the spirit of a holiday.

Name: Horto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Norbert Niederkofler comes to Milan, bringing his commitment to sustainability with him. The kitchen offers three tasting menus - L'Ora Etica, Il Lago, Vegetali Mon Amour - Norbert Niederkofler comes to Milan, bringing his commitment to sustainability with him. The kitchen offers three tasting menus - L'Ora Etica, Il Lago, Vegetali Mon Amour - in which the search for local ingredients (no more than an hour from the regional capital) is a must. In summer, the terraces, with views stretching from the spires of the Duomo to the Castello Sforzesco, are an added bonus, making it the ideal place for an aperitif thanks to its extensive cocktail list. The interior, with its natural wood tables, creates an understated and refined atmosphere suitable for both fine dining and a casual lunch, although in this second case the menu is simpler.

Name: Hyle
Address: Contrada Torre Garga SS 107, San Giovanni in Fiore, 87055, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: In the heart of the Sila, Hyle offers contemporary cuisine that draws its most authentic inspiration from the region. Rather than simply reinterpreting tradition, the restaurant explores its potential through ongoing research into ingredients, seasonality and mountain biodiversity. Vegetables, wild herbs, fermented foods, freshwater fish and local meats give rise to original and personal creations, often characterised by surprising combinations yet harmonious in flavour, as in the case of the ‘candele spezzate’ with lichen, vanilla and pecorino. The refined and finely balanced technique is designed to enhance the flavour, seeking balance through measured contrasts, well-defined acidity and vegetal nuances. The experience is rounded off by a carefully curated selection of Italian and international wines, with a particular focus on Calabrian wine-growing, complemented by a range of interesting craft beers brewed on the premises.

Name: I Castagni
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: In the Vigevano countryside, a rustic farmhouse with a portico, almost a private villa, welcomes guests amid antique furniture and paintings by local artists adorning the walls. Enrico Gerli, alongside his wife who oversees the dining room, has since 1989 been dedicated to a classic-modern cuisine executed with commitment and professionalism. He knows the Lombard area intimately, yet proves equally at ease with seafood preparations. Among the specialties are duck and goose, animals typical of the area, which appear in various dishes: a foie gras composition among the starters, braised duck tortelli, and goose leg confit cooked in its own fat.

Name: I Portici
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Occupying the atmospheric setting of the Eden theatre, a former late-19C musical café, this restaurant adorned with beautiful Liberty-style frescoes is the perfect backdrop for elegant, well-balanced Mediterranean-inspired dishes. Young, talented chef Nicola Annunziata offers three tasting menus of five (L’Ora Precisa), seven (La Spudorata) and nine (La Luce) courses with wine pairings recommended by the knowledgeable sommelier. If you’re looking for a quieter and more romantic ambience, book a table in the 14C icehouse, with its glass floor providing glimpses of the well-stocked wine cellar below.

Name: I Pupi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Having moved behind its old premises during 2025 (now home to TuMa, a modern osteria run by the same team), chef Tony Lo Coco’s new restaurant now occupies the lower part of the Villa Palagonia, a large historic 18C palazzo once visited and described by the poet Johann Wolfgang von Goethe. The cuisine continues to focus on Sicilian recipes and ingredients (meat and fish alike), which are personalised and imaginative, showcased on four tasting menus and an extensive à la carte. Various elegant dining rooms, a chef’s table for four guests who can observe the chef working close at hand, a well-stocked wine cellar on the first floor (home to around 1 300 labels), and a mezzanine space for more intimate dining all add to the appeal.

Name: INEO
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: On the dramatic semicircular sweep of Piazza della Repubblica, the entrance beneath the travertine porticoes stands adjacent to that of the Anantara Palazzo Naiadi hotel, which in effect houses the restaurant. The interiors, luxurious and bathed in soft light, captivate through their elegance and atmosphere. The cooking rises to considerable heights thanks to chef Heros De Agostinis, a genuine globetrotter who draws upon his travels and the experience accumulated in some of the most prestigious three-starred restaurants. His dishes are refined yet intense in flavour, with an intelligent use of spices and, in particular, of heat that is always calibrated with consummate skill. Special mention must be made of the bread trolley: a true spectacle, with five or six different varieties, each executed with impeccable care, a joy for both the eye and the palate. A truly remarkable gastronomic destination.

Name: IYO
Address: Via Piero della Francesca 74, Milan, 20154, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An elegant, contemporary restaurant that has over time become a point of reference in Italy for enthusiasts of Japanese cuisine. Guests are welcomed into modern, bright and relaxing spaces, ideal for showcasing a broad and stimulating gastronomic offering. At lunch, there is also a more streamlined à la carte selection, while the experience may begin, according to preference, with two tasting menus: one devoted to the most recent creations, the other to the restaurant’s iconic dishes, such as wagyu gyoza with vegetable and soy emulsion. Sushi and sashimi follow in numerous interpretations, alongside light tempura and specialities prepared on the robatayaki, the traditional Japanese barbecue, together with many other offerings. The style has by now become a recognisable signature: a personal fusion of Japanese, Oriental and European elements, reinterpreted in a contemporary key and built around quality ingredients. An establishment where the pleasure of dining is joined by an authentic and entertaining experience.

Name: IYO Kaiseki
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Kaiseki represents the most traditional and codified form of Japanese cuisine, structured as a succession of courses alternating raw preparations with cooked dishes, following techniques faithful to Japanese tradition and skillfully interpreted by the chef. In this modern structure at the foot of one of the Porta Nuova skyscrapers, a minimal, pared-back dining room, illuminated by natural light filtering through floor-to-ceiling windows, introduces guests to classic Japanese cuisine through a broad and distinctive menu. For a first encounter with Iyo Kaiseki, we suggest the chef’s menu: a sequence of sashimi, carpacci, and nigiri for the raw courses, complemented by traditional cooking methods – from steaming to preparations with bold, distinctly Asian flavors. Exemplary is the Iberian pork with leeks and sautéed mushrooms, draped in negimiso sauce and served on a hoba (magnolia) leaf: a dish as striking visually as it is on the palate. A recommended stop is in the back, where the open kitchens offer a captivating show. Not to be missed, by reservation, is Iyo Omakase: a completely independent journey at the sushi counter, in authentic omakase experience experience style.

Name: Iacobucci
Address: Via Ronco 1, Villa Zarri, Castel Maggiore, 40013, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in Villa Zarri, a historic family residence where one of the most famous brandies in Italy was created, this restaurant is home to chef Agostino Iacobucci, who creates a culinary bridge between his native Campania and the Bologna region. His dishes include a delicious rabbit alla genovese, a type of Neapolitan stew, served with a scamorza cheese and herb cream and topped with shavings of local black truffle. The impressive wine list boasts a selection of vertical labels including prestigious wines such as Sassicaia and Tignanello, with over ten different vintages available. The villa also offers a convenient car park and a delightful garden which is perfect for a stroll either before or after your meal.

Name: Idylio by Apreda
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: In an elegant dining room decorated in shades of blue and orange, Francesco Apreda’s cuisine takes shape: a gastronomic narrative that weaves together Asian influences and Italian tradition, the result of the chef’s experiences in the East. The offering unfolds through clear tasting menus: ‘Iconic Signature’, dedicated to the dishes that have defined his career; ‘Eco dal Mare’, centred on the marine world; and the vegetarian ‘Green Butterfly’. Alongside these is ‘Idylio’s Butterfly’, a four-course menu that allows you to choose from a range of great classics and new creations, offering the utmost freedom of choice. The wine list is well-curated and extensive, with particular emphasis on the wines available by the glass.

Name: Il Bavaglino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Although this restaurant now occupies new premises in an old building once used for salting fish, its style of cuisine (featured on three tasting menus, “Storie e passioni”, “Mura di Casa”, and the vegetarian “Erba Terra Foglie”, from which dishes can also be chosen à la carte style) remains unchanged. Inspired by regional traditions, chef Giuseppe Costa creates personalised and imaginative dishes that are influenced by local flavours and his past culinary experience, proving himself to be equally at ease with fish and meat options. Our inspector particularly recommends the local purple prawns, served raw with caviar and olives and a lemon and ginger coulis.

Name: Il Buco
Address: II rampa Marina Piccola 5, Sorrento, 80067, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the heart of Sorrento, the restaurant offers guests the chance to choose from a range of dining areas, each with its own distinct charm but all equally atmospheric. You can dine in the historic dining room, which was converted from a 16th-century cellar once used by the monks as a storeroom, or in the more contemporary areas, which feature a spectacular open-plan wine cellar housing over 1,600 bottles. In the warmer months, the outdoor tables set out along the picturesque entrance staircase add further charm to the experience. The cuisine draws primarily on the traditions of Campania, alternating between seafood and meat dishes, while also incorporating personal interpretations and creative touches that enrich the menu. The dining experience can be tailored either through tasting menus or by choosing freely from an extensive and varied à la carte menu. Among the most impressive dishes were the tacos with ‘minestra maritata’ and tomato ice cream – a successful example of cuisine that blends tradition with modernity.

Name: Il Cantinone e Sport Hotel Alpina
Address: Via A. De Giacomi 39, Madesimo, 23024, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A family restaurant run with passion and pride, Il Cantinone welcomes guests on a culinary journey dedicated to the region’s gastronomic treasures, from the mountains to the lake. Buckwheat, trout and eel, venison, polenta, mushrooms, potatoes and truffles are just some of the ingredients that define the authentic spirit of the contemporary dishes created by chef Stefano Masanti.Every now and then, exotic twists appear, inspirations gathered during his travels and brought back to his beloved mountains, capable of adding depth and intrigue to the culinary offering.Working alongside him is Thomas Locatelli, a remarkably talented and highly creative young chef, whose presence brings a touch of freshness and innovation to the kitchen, helping to refine and expand Il Cantinone’s gastronomic identity.

Name: Il Cantuccio
Description: This welcoming, beautifully kept restaurant in the heart of the verdant Brianza region has two dining rooms: one with exposed stonework that gives it a rustic feel, the other more modern and elegant in style. Chef Mauro Elli moves easily between classic Italian favourites, occasionally adding his own individual touch to the dishes. His imaginative reinterpretations demonstrate a fascination with the sea (despite the restaurant’s geographical location), while the menu also offers “daily game specials” throughout the year. One of the most delicious dishes on the menu is the bottoni pasta in a Milanese sauce, served with tender quail and parmesan cream.

Name: Il Cappero
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Today, the cuisine stands out for its exceptionally high standard of quality, underpinned by a clear and distinctive vision. The two tasting menus – available in a more basic version and a more extensive one – showcase a concept centred on the ingredients themselves, which are predominantly local and seasonal, interpreted with technical precision within a contemporary Mediterranean style. At the heart of this philosophy lies the single-protein approach: each dish showcases a single main ingredient, bringing out its full flavour and minimising any superfluous elements. In this context, the care taken in the ageing of the fish stands out in particular; this practice imparts depth and complexity without altering the product’s original character. There is no shortage of elegant nods to European culinary tradition, such as the measured use of French-style sauces or the judicious use of fermentation techniques, which are incorporated with balance, without overpowering. The dessert course is a moment of genuine pleasure: after an initial tasting served at the table, the experience moves to the pastry corner, where the final dessert is prepared on the spot according to the guests’ preferences. To top it all off, the Therasia Resort enjoys a spectacular setting on the Vulcanello headland, from where the terrace offers an unrivalled view of the Aeolian archipelago, often enhanced by sunsets of extraordinary colour.

Name: Il Centro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: A breath of immortality hovers over this restaurant, where great Piedmontese cuisine finds one of its finest expressions thanks to the Cordero family. Elide at the stoves, her husband Enrico and son Giampiero in the dining room – the latter a profound wine connoisseur and guardian of an extraordinary, ever-growing cellar – carry forward with passion a venue taken over by Giampiero’s grandparents in 1956. Here, tradition takes center stage with hearty, flavor-rich dishes that never tire: from bread agnolotti filled with anchovy and a hint of thyme to the classic braised cheek with caramelized figs. In summer, the offering lightens with some seafood options, while an autumn visit calls for a proper white truffle dish; we suggest the classic egg tajarin. In January, February, and March, the legendary fritto misto del Centro returns, an epic 12-course sequence from savory to sweet, to be reserved well in advance. Just steps from the restaurant are the elegant rooms of Dimora Cordero.

Name: Il Convivio Troiani
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: A restaurant of solid tradition, born in the early 1990s from the vision of three brothers from the Marche region – Angelo, Giuseppe, and Massimo: the first at the stoves, the others in the dining room. Over time, this establishment has become a benchmark in Roman dining thanks to a cuisine of strong authorial character, presented through two elaborate tasting menus – one entirely dedicated to the vegetable world. These menus can be adapted in length and are structured by seasonal rhythms and a constant dialog with Italy’s gastronomic roots. Iconic dishes are available to complement the experience, such as the celebrated “Amatriciana dei Troiani,” on the menu since 1996, or the local lamb. In the cellar, some 3,600 labels form a monumental wine list, featuring vertical selections dating back to the 1990s, true rarities for connoisseurs and collectors. Thanks to Coravin, several of these gems can also be enjoyed by the glass.

Name: Il Desco
Address: Via Dietro San Sebastiano 7, Verona, 37121, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Housed in a fifteenth-century palazzo, the dining room showcases hand-painted exposed ceiling beams paired with exquisite taste alongside Murano glass lamps and chandeliers, complemented by contemporary artwork. Guests sink into the signature leather armchairs to savor an outstanding meal in what may well be one of Verona’s most refined drawing rooms. Opened in 1982 by patriarch Elia, the restaurant is now in the capable hands of his talented son, Matteo Rizzo, who presents a series of tasting menus alongside a focused à la carte selection offering three to five courses. An exceptional wine list is expertly guided by the knowledgeable sommelier.

Name: Il Fagiano
Address: Corso Zanardelli 190, Fasano del Garda, 25083, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Set within the elegant surroundings of the Grand Hotel Fasano, the restaurant welcomes guests into a refined dining room where wood, the dominant feature of the décor, helps to create a warm and cosy atmosphere. In the warmer months, however, it is hard to resist the splendid panoramic terrace – the property’s real highlight – from which the view stretches out over the lake, offering a sight of rare beauty. Maurizio Bufi’s culinary offering comprises tasting menus – including one dedicated to plant-based dishes – and an à la carte selection. While there are certainly references to Puglia, his homeland, and to the lake district where he is based, his cuisine stands out above all for its creative and contemporary approach, which draws freely on ingredients and influences from various Italian regions, while respecting the seasonality and quality of the raw ingredients.

Name: Il Falconiere
Address: Località San Martino a Bocena 370, Cortona, 52044, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: To get to this exclusive restaurant, you drive through an idyllic landscape of small lanes lined with dry-stone walls and fields belonging to the Baracchi farm estate, of which Il Falconiere and the magnificent hotel of the same name are a part. Many of the ingredients served here, such as wine and olive oil, are produced on the estate and the restaurant’s strong connection with its local landscapes is evident. Specialities such as Chianina beef, local garlic and pici pasta feature in dishes spiced with aromatic herbs and full of the strong flavours of Tuscany.

Name: Il Flauto di Pan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Perched on the promontory of Ravello, Villa Cimbrone is one of the most fascinating and romantic historic residences in Italy. Surrounded by centuries-old gardens that culminate in the celebrated Terrazza dell'Infinito, one of the most iconic panoramas on the Amalfi Coast, it offers a setting of rare beauty. The gastronomic restaurant, housed within the elegant spaces of the villa, allows guests to dine both in the refined interior dining room and on the terrace overlooking the sea. Before dinner, guests may access the Terrazza dell'Infinito, a privilege that renders the experience all the more memorable. The service is attentive and professional, and the cellar represents one of the great strengths of this establishment. The chef offers seafood, meat and vegetarian tasting menus, with an elegant and contemporary cuisine that celebrates the produce of the local area.

Name: Il Fuoco Sacro
Address: Strada di Buddeo, San Pantaleo, 07026, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: The very name of the resort where it is situated, Petra Segreta, evokes a secluded and picturesque spot, nestled among the Mediterranean scrub that surrounds the village of San Pantaleo. Il Fuoco Sacro overlooks a magnificent garden and enjoys a spectacular view stretching all the way to the coast. Luigi Bergeretto and Alessandro Menditto are at the helm in the kitchen, offering a contemporary menu that showcases the quality of the ingredients and pays close attention to the local area. Particular emphasis is placed on the aromatic herbs and vegetables grown in the estate’s vegetable garden, which feature prominently in many dishes, while a few beehives provide a small supply of artisan honey. An interesting selection of wines rounds off the experience. Finally, Enrico Bartolini is orchestrating the culinary project, a presence that serves as further assurance of excellence.

Name: Il Gallo Cedrone
Address: Via Cima Tosa 80, Madonna di Campiglio, 38086, Italy
Description: Attention: closed for renovation!Within the Hotel Bertelli, the restaurant’s dining room offers an authentically alpine atmosphere, with a style that inspires both elegance and conviviality. The kitchen presents two tasting menus (plus a vegetarian alternative): the first inspired by the territory, the second featuring classics from other regions with seafood. Dishes may also be selected à la carte according to preference. Equally impressive is the wine cellar, with over 800 labels carefully curated by owner Marco Masè alongside veteran sommelier Giuseppe Greco, and a particular passion for gin and tonic.

Name: Il Luogo Aimo e Nadia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A leading figure on the Milanese gastronomic scene for over sixty years, this historic establishment continues to attract lovers of haute cuisine thanks to a menu that celebrates Italian produce and regions with a contemporary twist. The two tasting menus created by Alessandro Negrini and Fabio Pisani elegantly highlight the Lombard roots of the former and the Apulian roots of the latter. As well as the set menus, you can also choose from the à la carte menu, selecting at least two dishes in addition to a dessert. Aimo’s ‘Piatti del Cuore’ are a must-try, including the iconic durum wheat spaghettoni with fresh spring onions, chilli, extra virgin olive oil and Ligurian basil. The extensive wine list, which can be viewed on a tablet, is also well worth a look; it features rare wines and real gems for connoisseurs. The attentive and considerate service discreetly complements the whole experience.

Name: Il Marin
Address: Calata Cattaneo, 15, Edificio Millo, Porto Antico, Genoa, 16121, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At the Old Port, within the same building’s floor that houses Eataly, the dining area thrives on simplicity to accentuate the panorama witnessed through glazed walls, while competent service, primarily female, tends to guests warmly. The cuisine pivots around 'territory', primarily maritime, yet is rejuvenated through modern techniques and ideas; for example, the Martini cocktail spaghetti, shaken in the dining room by Chef Marco Visciola, enriched with algae butter, Martini sauce, caviar, and nebulised Taggiasco gin, as well as the roasted monkfish cooked in bay leaf, almond hummus, kale, and caper Mugnaia. A varied selection exists, also à la carte, within the three tasting formulae presented.

Name: Il Palagio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Il Palagio is the ideal choice for anyone wishing to enjoy an evening of elegance and timeless charm. Housed in the extraordinary Palazzo della Gherardesca, it winds its way through sumptuous rooms leading to the restaurant, featuring fine marble, elegant furnishings and splendid Murano chandeliers. The gastronomic offering features three tasting menus, one of which is vegetarian, as well as the option to choose from the à la carte menu. The cuisine focuses on high-quality ingredients, prepared with restraint and a contemporary sensitivity, avoiding unnecessary excess and prioritising balance and flavour. A first-class experience, set against one of Florence’s most picturesque backdrops.

Name: Il Papavero
Description: Papavero is the Italian for poppy, a plant which grows tall and has strong roots, making it an apt symbol for this restaurant housed in a palazzo in the town centre. In a few classic-style rooms, the chef offers a menu that focuses on fish and seafood, although ingredients from the surrounding countryside also feature. Simple, solid recipes made with just a few ingredients, exactly as described on the menu, and a passionate dedication to the Mediterranean result in attractive cuisine which also offers good value for money. In fine weather, meals are served outdoors under the jasmine in a romantic garden. A restaurant that appeals to the heart as well as the palate.

Name: Il Patio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: After more than thirty years of business at its historic premises in Pollone, the Vineis family’s restaurant has moved to the centre of Biella, inside the so-called ‘Palazzone’, in completely refurbished premises that once housed private clubs. The project is currently being developed along two distinct but complementary paths. On the one hand, there is Il Patio, the restaurant’s most contemporary venue, where Simone Vineis – supported by his father Sergio’s expertise and presence – offers a menu that follows the seasons and the inspiration of the moment, with a particular focus on meat, while also venturing into other culinary territories. On the other hand, there’s Il Circolo Bistrot, a more informal and relaxed setting, designed for those seeking the pleasure of good food in a convivial and laid-back atmosphere. Two establishments under one roof, united by a long family history and a well-established culture of hospitality.

Name: Il Pellicano
Address: Località Lo Sbarcatello, Porto Ercole, 58018, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Chef Michelino Gioia from Campania, now a Tuscan by adoption, is in charge of fine dining at the famous resort Il Pellicano, whose terrace overlooking the sea, enhanced by the scent of rosemary in the air, makes it one of the most romantic addresses in Italy. Michelino, thanks to a good technique, is highly skilled in creating different textures in the same dish while retaining the precise flavours of the excellent ingredients used, both land and sea (excellent, for example, the cooking of the pezzogna, which remains soft, accompanied by small quenelles of pappa al pomodoro in a creamy version, mussels and lovage). His work is - finally - enhanced by a very extensive wine list and, above all, by the friendly and professional service offered by the numerous staff.

Name: Il Piastrino
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The home of Claudia and Riccardo, Il Piastrino is the realization of a long‑nurtured dream, lovingly refined and enriched year after year amid the rolling hills of Montefeltro. Here, the warmth and simplicity of the countryside blend harmoniously with contemporary details and furnishings. At the heart of it all is chef Agostini’s cuisine which, supported by technical mastery and creativity, brings out the best in seasonal, locally sourced ingredients. His complex and carefully constructed dishes never feel contrived, but instead convey his vision with balance and flavour, occasionally extending their reach into Tuscany. No sea fish here, but freshwater species such as trout and eel, meat dishes are more frequent, and particular interest is shown in aromatic herbs, as well as the outstanding mushrooms of a picturesque territory between hill and mountain.

Name: Il Pievano
Address: Località Spaltenna 13, Gaiole in Chianti, 53013, Italy
Description: In the kitchen, a contemporary cuisine with a distinctive character takes shape, skilfully blending Mediterranean flavours and international influences while remaining firmly rooted in the Tuscan region that is its home. The culinary offering is organised around two tasting menus, ‘Brace Ardente’ and ‘Transverberazione’, which differ in their inspiration and composition but are united by a meticulous focus on ingredients and remarkable precision in execution. In the warmer months, the experience is made even more enjoyable thanks to the tables set up in the romantic tranquillity of the ancient courtyard. When it comes to wine, let yourself be guided by a cellar of exceptional depth, boasting over 800 wines and a particularly well-curated selection by the glass.

Name: Il Refettorio
Address: Via Roma 2, Conca dei Marini, 84010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Within the Monastero Santa Rosa – one of the most iconic and captivating hotels on the Amalfi Coast, whose religious past dates to the seventeenth century, and of which many traces remain to this day – the restaurant occupies a terrace whose view sweeps from the garden and pool to the sea, in the silence of a timeless place. Chef Alfonso Crescenzo interprets Mediterranean cuisine through a philosophy encapsulated in his own motto: "Nothing is more complex than simple cooking." His offering is born from the celebration of the finest Campanian produce, much of it from the family's own organic farm, and unfolds across two tasting menus alongside the à la carte, with a perfect balance between sea, land and kitchen garden. Among the signature dishes, the Mafalda stands out: a homage to the traditional Neapolitan Sunday lunch – Gragnano pasta filled with buffalo ricotta, Agerola moscione cheese and fried aubergine, completed by small meatballs and Neapolitan ragù. The finale is devoted to the celebrated sfogliatella Santa Rosa, born in this very monastery, here reinterpreted in a contemporary version that preserves its echoes of ricotta, citrus and sour cherry preserve.

Name: Il Ristorante Alain Ducasse Napoli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Located within the Hotel ROMEO Napoli, the Alain Ducasse Napoli Restaurant is a place where the fusion of local specialities inspires an elegant, refined and daring cuisine, celebrating the culture and gastronomic richness of Campania. In the heart of the city, the chef, ever passionate about the Mediterranean, draws inspiration from the region’s wonderful ingredients: Paestum artichokes, purple prawns from the island of Ischia, Sorrento lemons and fresh fish from the Tyrrhenian Sea. Working alongside executive chef Alessandro Lucassino, Ducasse pays tribute to these ingredients with a personal and refined vision, where respect for Campania’s traditions meets contemporary haute cuisine. Each ingredient is carefully brought to the fore: brief cooking times preserve the intensity of the flavours, while the preparation methods focus on the essence of the ingredient. French influences blend with an authentic Italian approach, while being guided by the philosophy of naturalness. French culinary techniques refine each detail, paying tribute to the richness of the Campania region with dishes that evoke the sea and the land, the fire of Vesuvius and the wind that dries the ‘piennoli’.

Name: Il Ristorante di Guido da Costigliole
Address: Località San Maurizio 39, Santo Stefano Belbo, 12058, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Perched in a panoramic setting amid extraordinary rolling hills, this restaurant is housed in a seventeenth-century former monastery transformed into the refined Relais San Maurizio, one of the region’s most exclusive venues. Andrea Alciati and Monica Magnini preserve and reimagine the legacy of Guido and Lidia Alciati, legendary figures in Piedmontese gastronomy. In the kitchen, Cuneo-born chef Fabio Sgrò carries on the family tradition with respect and passion, interpreting it through a modern lens: his revisited menu also features freshwater fish and a selection of off-menu specials that enrich the offering. Among the vegan options, the grilled endive with almond cream and vegetable jus stands out, an intense yet surprisingly harmonious dish. Equally unmissable is the glazed eel with kale, remarkable for its balance and depth of flavor. The wine cellar deserves special mention: an extraordinary selection featuring verticals and rare bottles that adds further allure to the experience.

Name: Il Saraceno
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: The chef’s Amalfi origins re-emerge in great style in this restaurant at the gates of Bergamo, with a chiefly seafood cuisine of great quality. From raw seafood to spaghetti with sea urchins and breadcrumbs, from seabream to the fish of the day, it is a feast for the palate, culminating in the desserts. The quality of the leavened products is noteworthy, from bread to focaccia with oregano and cherry tomatoes. The wine list is good too, starting with the selection of Champagnes.

Name: Il Sereno Al Lago
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Leaving the road that runs through the village, you descend almost to the lakeshore to find the restaurant within the luxurious Il Sereno hotel, an elegant new structure enhanced by the architectural creativity of Patricia Urquiola. In the summertime, the restaurant is hosted on the terrace with arched openings, offering views of the blue expanse and the villages on the opposite shore. The mastery of the brilliant Neapolitan chef Raffaele Lenzi spans all kinds of cuisine with equal success and balance: some regional references, vegan dishes, Asian influences, Lombard and lake-inspired creations, and a lot of creativity. The interesting wine list includes a rich selection of fine Italian reds, with verticals featuring older vintages.

Name: Il Tiglio
Address: Via Isola San Biagio 34, Montemonaco, 63088, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: It is certainly worth the trip to the steep slopes at the foot of the Sibillini Mountains, where Enrico Mazzaroni has created a culinary concept deeply rooted in the local area. The cuisine is, in fact, based on top-quality ingredients – mushrooms, trout, venison, potatoes and many other local produce – often sourced directly from the family’s farm holiday accommodation. This solid foundation is complemented by a distinct creative flair that results in original, contemporary dishes, underpinned by precise technique and a balanced interplay of flavours, as demonstrated by the combination of trout, veal diaphragm and mushrooms. Over the years, the presentations have also taken on a greater sense of theatrical elegance, without losing sight of the substance. The service helps to make the experience particularly enjoyable, thanks to a successful balance between long-standing professionalism and the enthusiasm of the younger generation. The wine cellar is also very well stocked; alongside a wide selection of local and regional wines, it offers an interesting range of artisan wines from various parts of Italy.

Name: Il Tino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Within the Nautilus shipyard, stairs lead to the first floor attic dining room with windows overlooking the marina. Elegant and refined, also in service, chef Daniele Usai creates highly original seafood cuisine, distinguished above all by a skilful use of aromatic herbs, of which the chef is a true master and connoisseur, also of uncommon varieties. The offering is structured around two tasting menus: one featuring his most classic dishes accompanied by their year of creation, the other with his latest creations. Dishes may, however, also be chosen freely from the carte, starting from two courses and a dessert.

Name: Il Visibilio
Address: SP 9 di Pievasciata 32, Castelnuovo Berardenga, 53019, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: At the end of a dirt road leading from the contemporary art village of Pievasciata to the cultivated hills, you will find the impressive gate of The Club House hotel. Il Visibilio is a small gourmet restaurant that offers a delightful combination of Tuscan cuisine and the creativity of chef Iannotti from the two-Michelin-starred Krèsios restaurant in Telese Terme. Iannotti brings to Siena a formula similar to that offered at his restaurant. A single blind tasting menu, a long gastronomic journey consisting of surprise dishes that alternate between ingredients from land and sea, with extensive use of vegetables. Numerous technical flourishes ensure a top-quality fine-dining experience, starting with the introductory finger food. The inspector recommends: the pigeon with its delicious rhubarb and absinthe sauces.

Name: Impronta d'Acqua
Address: Via Aurelia 2121, Cavi di Lavagna, 16030, Italy
Description: Between the sea and the railway, an open-space restaurant with a minimalist, contemporary design welcomes guests with its open kitchen, where chef and owner Ivan Maniago and his team transform ingredients from Liguria into sensory experiences. The philosophy is clear: 90% of the products come from small local producers. Three tasting menus offer an original interpretation of Liguria: Altitudine, a jouney from the coast towards inland Liguria; Profondità, an immersion in the wonders of the sea; and Vege-table, dedicated to green freshness.

Name: Imàgo
Address: Piazza Trinità dei Monti 6, Rome, 00187, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: One of the capital’s most iconic gastronomic rooftop venues, this restaurant enjoys a setting of rare distinction: perched atop the celebrated Spanish Steps at Trinità dei Monti, within the Hotel Hassler, it is reached by lift and counts among Rome's most renowned dining rooms, recently renovated to include an open kitchen, new flooring, and carefully considered lighting. Here one dines surrounded by large windows looking out over the city’s most emblematic monuments, from the twin bell towers of Trinità dei Monti to views stretching along the horizon, a constant invitation to rediscover the urban icons. In the kitchen, the brigade led by Andrea Antonini offers two tasting menus that alternate between great classics and more recent creations: a sequence of small, refined, and visually striking dishes that reinterpret local traditions and ingredients, guiding diners towards unexpected pairings and contemporary interpretations full of playfulness and creativity.

Name: In Viaggio - Claudio Melis
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: The name of this restaurant gives a good indication of the experience you can expect here: a culinary voyage through the chef’s varied selection of recipes and ingredients, some from the Alps, others from countries across the globe. Dishes are served on tasting menus of five, seven or nine courses in a quiet dining room with just a few tables, where the chef himself explains his dishes to guests.

Name: Indaco
Address: Piazza Santa Restituta 1, Lacco Ameno, 80076, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Don’t miss the appointment with sunset: as the sun sets behind you, the sea before you ignites with marvellous hues, thus revealing the meaning behind the restaurant’s name. We find ourselves in an exclusive area of the Hotel Regina Isabella, a small marina from which the view embraces Lacco Ameno, Casamicciola, the island of Procida, Vesuvius, Bacoli... a unique and unforgettable panorama, with the sea enclosed between lands and islands as if in an enchanted bay. In the kitchen, Ischia-born Pasquale Palamaro evokes his island memories through refined and creative dishes. The offering takes shape in two seafood tasting menus, whose dishes can also be ordered individually à la carte, complemented today by a new entirely plant-based proposal, conceived with the same care and depth of flavour. Of exceptional note is the wine accompaniment, which combines an extensive selection – over one thousand labels – with the passionate and knowledgeable advice of the sommelier.

Name: Inkiostro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Calabrian chef Salvatore Morello brings a breath of fresh air to the city synonymous with gastronomy. Drawing on an international background, he presents a cuisine that weaves together recipes and ingredients from diverse culinary worlds, united by finesse, personality, and a striking cohesion. Exceptional raw materials, occasionally accented by exotic notes, find precise balance in every course. Special mention goes to the bread program: the loaf, crafted from sourdough and minimally refined flours and baked in a cast-iron pot, captivates with its pronounced crust and unexpected lightness. Equal care is devoted to the focaccias and grissini, all of outstanding quality. The list offers a thoughtfully curated selection of wines, craft beers, sake, and spirits, ideal companions to the dining experience.

Name: Iris Ristorante
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Within an extraordinary palazzo in the historic center, the experience begins in the fifteenth-century cellars, where an amuse-bouche is served in an evocative atmosphere before guests ascend to the sixteenth-century dining room. Amid frescoes, exposed stone, and brick, with the open kitchen visible at the far end, this ranks among the most elegant restaurants in the region. At the stove, Giacomo Sacchetto offers several tasting menus, with dishes that may be freely selected from one list or another. Both seafood and land-based offerings, elaborate and creative, leave the mark of a thrilling gastronomic experience.

Name: Italo Bassi Confusion Restaurant
Address: Via Aga Khan 1, Promenade du Port, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
Description: Now established as a reference point in Porto Cervo, this restaurant occupies an elevated position overlooking the marina. Mirrors, golden accents, and glass details complement the open kitchen, where Italo Bassi leads his team. Technique and refined presentation stand out, whether in fish dishes (such as the textbook-perfect sole with mint-marinated zucchini and an exquisite beurre blanc foam recalling the classic à la meunière) or in meat preparations. Guests enjoy absolute freedom of choice: two tasting menus are available – one featuring the restaurant’s classics, the other with new creations, offered in various lengths – or they may order à la carte, which also includes luxury ingredients served in pure form, such as oysters, caviar, and raw seafood. On the lower floor, the Bubble Bar & Bistrot offers aperitifs and more informal dishes.

Name: Johannesstube
Address: Via San Valentino 3, Nova Levante, 39056, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This fascinating restaurant within the elegant Engel resort has had a complete makeover, adding a contemporary feel to both the cuisine and the decor here. The dining room boasts a natural elegance, in which wood, stone and other local materials blend together harmoniously – the Dolomia chef’s table acts as an intimate setting for aperitifs and appetisers served by the chef himself. At the helm in the kitchen, young, talented Philip Lochmann is a real ambassador for sustainability and the local region. His cuisine is light and full of flavour, demonstrating impeccable technique and a meticulous attention to presentation. Local ingredients, especially seasonal vegetables, take centre stage, all of which are transformed with creativity and respect. To enhance your experience even further, friendly, professional sommelier Daniela is on hand with wine recommendations, so that you can enjoy the perfect wine for every course, choosing from a selection that showcases the best labels from the region and further afield.

Name: Joia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: When you walk through the door, it's like stepping into a world suspended between philosophy and taste. This restaurant, the first in Italy to have introduced vegetarian and natural dishes to fine dining, conveys a message in every single detail: respect, awareness and harmony. Today, under the leadership of young chefs Sauro Ricci and Raffaele Minghini, Pietro Leemann's legacy translates into dishes that resemble works of art, evocative even in their names: Col favore della luna (With the favour of the moon), Ombelico del mondo (Navel of the world), La rosa che non colsi (The rose I did not pick). Creations that speak through vibrant colours, delicate textures and aromas that caress the senses, in a journey that is both real and dreamlike. Two tasting menus define the experience, while, at lunchtime, the Piatto Quadro offers five taster dishes for a quick but refined break. The restaurant's simple, understated and bright design completes a journey that nourishes both body and soul.

Name: Kitchen
Description: Nestled amid the greenery of a private park, Kitchen is an elegant restaurant which serves creative Italian cuisine with a focus on seasonal ingredients and a perfect balance between produce, technique and flavour. The chef uses herbs and vegetables from the restaurant’s own biodynamic kitchen garden which can be seen in front of the entrance. This natural bounty provides the basis for the Green tasting menu; the other tasting menu is called Experience; there’s also an excellent à la carte. Service is attentive plus there’s an excellent selection of wines.

Name: Kuppelrain
Address: Via Stazione 16, località Maragno, Castelbello, 39020, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The many positive adjectives that can be used to describe the Trafoier family can be summed up by simply saying that they are unique! Their individual talents come together in the natural and engaging welcome they offer guests, demonstrating a warmth and professionalism that is typical of the Kuppelrain experience. Chef Kevin, who is as skilful as his father Jorg (now front of house), demonstrates precise, excellent techniques in his search for comforting and appealing flavours that bring out the full flavour of his ingredients with no frills or unnecessary fuss. Local produce takes pride of place, such as fruit and vegetables from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden, and meat and fish from the region. The desserts, as well as the imaginative pralines, are made by daughter Natalie. Wine-enthusiasts will also be in their element here, thanks to the excellent wine list (including a fine selection by the glass, as well as magnums and 3-litre double magnums) which is overseen by talented Sonya (the winner of the 2022 Michelin Sommelier Award!), who creates unique wine pairings. Bistro service only at lunchtime.

Name: L'Argine a Vencò
Address: Località Vencò 15, Dolegna del Collio, 34070, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This perfectly restored old mill is home to a chef who creates original cuisine that demonstrates her connection with her region and showcases ingredients grown in the restaurant’s own kitchen garden, especially the aromatic herbs that are a characteristic feature of many of the dishes served here. Antonia Klugmann’s house stands in attractive unspoilt scenery near the Slovenian border and in the middle of two major wine-producing areas, namely the Colli Orientali del Friuli and the better-known Collio, both of which are well represented on the extensive wine list.

Name: L'Asinello
Address: Via Nuova 6, Località Villa a Sesta, Castelnuovo Berardenga, 53019, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Housed in a skilfully restored former stable, L’Asinello is now an intimate and tastefully decorated restaurant, blending seamlessly into the authentic atmosphere of the Tuscan village in which it is situated. In the warmer months, the experience is further enhanced by the tables set up in the garden – a peaceful and charming spot nestled within one of the region’s most picturesque landscapes. In the kitchen, Senio Venturi draws on his Tuscan culinary roots, using local produce and bold flavours to create his own distinctive style that also embraces contemporary creativity. In the dining room, Elisa welcomes guests with elegance, warmth and great professionalism, helping to create a warm and relaxed atmosphere that makes the whole experience particularly enjoyable.

Name: L'Erba del Re
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Adjacent to the church of Santa Maria della Pomposa, which is one of Modena’s oldest religious buildings, this elegant restaurant occupies a historic palazzo and welcomes guests into modern, pared-back interiors enriched by contemporary works on the walls and a deliberately intimate capacity of just nine tables. The gastronomic offering unfolds across several tasting menus: one dedicated to the great recipes of Emilian tradition, from tortellini in capon broth to tagliatelle with Modenese ragù; the "Alla Brace" menu, which celebrates cooking over live fire and is renewed in line with the seasons; and "Espressione", the ten-course signature menu that represents the most complete synthesis of the chef's cuisine. These are complemented by an à la carte selection gathering some of the most emblematic dishes in the restaurant's history. A well-structured cellar, with a carefully curated selection of Italian and international labels, completes the experience.

Name: La Bandiera
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The journey to get there is long, no matter where you come from, but it's truly worth it! An entire family – second and third generation – walks side by side along the path set since 1977, devoting themselves with great passion to the art of gourmet hospitality. The cuisine, crafted and executed by father Marcello together with his son Mattia, is founded on a deep respect for the land and the seasonality of the ingredients. These principles often lead to self-production: products from their two gardens, one conventional and one synergistic, appear in almost every dish, as well as their EVO oil. From a technical standpoint, the offerings embrace modern preparations, making them true flagbearers of quality Abruzzo cuisine. Unforgettable during our last visit was the taste of "Arrosti-GIN 2025": IGP mountain meat flavored with juniper, truly mouth-watering! The other son, Alessio, passionately and competently manages the dining room and the wine cellar, offering a selection that will delight pairing enthusiasts: beginning with a rich selection of options by the glass, including top-tier wines.

Name: La Buca
Description: Choose a table on the outdoor summer terrace (right over the water!) at this restaurant in order to best appreciate its location overlooking the picturesque canal port and its period houses. The indoor dining room is also attractive, with its open-view kitchen and modern and elegant feel, while the menu focuses almost exclusively on fish, often served with vegetables, some of which are organic. Enjoy a wide selection of raw antipasti to start (some simple in their preparation, while others are more elaborate), then choose from an array of beautifully presented, modern dishes, such as stuffed mullet with pickled plums and lemon salad, perhaps accompanied by one of the many champagnes included on the wine list.

Name: La Capinera
Address: Via Nazionale 177, località Spisone, Taormina, 98039, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Sea & Air - Earth & Fire: the four elements come together on the tasting menus at this restaurant, where some dishes are named after movies (the Benjamin Button dish features fresh pasta “buttons” served with veal ragout and rosemary oil). Other highlights include the “cacao meravigliao”, a dish of delicious seafood tagliolini with red prawns and mozzarella foam, in which the delightfully fresh, raw Mazzara prawns have a wonderful texture. Elegant service, soft background music which creates a pleasant holiday atmosphere, and a vast selection of regional, Italian and European wines complete the picture.

Name: La Caravella dal 1959
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: La Caravella’s history is intricately linked to that of gastronomic tourism on the Amalfi Coast, so much so that it’s impossible to mention all the famous personalities who have dined here and fallen in love with the Dipino family’s cuisine. The food is proudly inspired by local and family traditions, while at the same time constantly seeking to reinterpret these traditions and create new imaginative recipes. Examples include pears cooked in Aglianico wine served with raw shrimps and cow’s ricotta cheese, and raw fish and seafood options accompanied by a careful selection of seasonal vegetables. Two important features here are the focus on simple, traditional cooking techniques and the speed of preparation. The menu showcases the best of the area’s fresh fish, including pezzogna (a variety of sea bream), swordfish and tuna, supplemented when necessary by options from the nearby Cilento region. Other ingredients include tomatoes (which feature in almost half the dishes), Amalfi’s famous lemons (the classic lemon soufflé is highly recommended), basil and Agerola bread – you’ll want to order almost everything on the menu! The excellent wine list features reds, whites, sparkling, sweet, young and vintage wines, with legendary labels such as La Tâche listed alongside smaller, unknown, rare and organic wines. Whatever your preference, sommelier Tonino has that rare talent (also found at the Enoteca Pinchiorri) of finding just the right wine for you.

Name: La Ciau del Tornavento
Description: In the Barbaresco hills, in a characteristic building dating back to 1931 that used to be a nursery school, the large dining room is the stage for a magnificent performance that unfolds over the hills through the glass walls. You can enjoy it even more if you take a few minutes between courses to step out onto the terrace and admire the view which, on clear days, stretches all the way to the Alps. The culinary creations of Maurilio Garola and Marco Lombardo take you on a journey of flavours with refined tasting menus and a rich à la carte menu featuring succulent meat dishes and fresh fish. The desserts are a real treat: don't miss the freshly made, velvety smooth and fragrant vanilla ice cream. The wine cellar is an experience all of its own: shelves like works of art, bottles that tell stories. For those who love good wine, including vintage wines, this is a place where losing yourself is an absolute pleasure.

Name: La Coldana
Address: Cascina Coldana, via del Costino, Lodi, 26900, Italy
Description: On the outskirts of Lodi, yet already in a green and almost rural setting, the interior of this farmhouse creates an atmosphere of considerable refinement, with a series of elegantly appointed dining rooms in which an elaborate and creative cuisine is served. The wine accompaniment is not to be overlooked, not only for the quality of the selection, but also for the opportunity to purchase bottles directly from the wine list.

Name: La Credenza
Address: Via Cavour 22, San Maurizio Canavese, 10077, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Three dining rooms of contemporary atmosphere receive guests, one of which overlooks a delightful garden where, during the warmer months, just three tables are available: advance booking is therefore advisable. The cooking is firmly rooted in the Piedmontese tradition, yet allows itself to be pleasingly enriched by creative impulses and occasional forays of Oriental inspiration. Should you wish, the chef-patron himself will guide you through the menu, enriching the experience with exact and passionate explanations of each dish. Of considerable note also is the cellar, which numbers some 1,700 labels gathered across two elegant volumes, complemented by a significant offering of wines by the glass.

Name: La Favellina
Address: Via Cosari 4/6, località San Tomio, Malo, 36034, Italy
Description: You follow winding roads up into the Lessini hills to get to this small paradise, a rustic setting which is home to an elegant, family-run restaurant where everyone works hard to ensure that you enjoy your evening. Federico Pettenuzzo and his mother are at the helm in the kitchen (the latter responsible for the delicious pastas), while Federico’s brother Riccardo oversees the front of house. The creative cuisine is prepared from ingredients sourced from all over Italy and further afield, with some occasionally original combinations.

Name: La Locanda del Borgo
Address: Località Monte Pugliano 1, Telese Terme, 82037, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Chef Luciano Villani creates menus that focus on simplicity, organic produce from the Sannio region and an uncompromising philosophy. The restaurant is situated within the Hotel Acquapetra Resort&Spa, once an old farmhouse transformed into a luxurious hamlet, where antique furnishings and modern cutting-edge facilities combine to ensure a delightful stay in elegant surroundings. The gourmet restaurant adds to its appeal, featuring cuisine that is delicious and always recognisably regional, albeit with the occasional influence from elsewhere. There are two tasting menus: Aqua (fish dishes only) and Petra (dedicated to meat dishes). Aperitifs and drinks are served in the charming bar next to the restaurant.

Name: La Magnolia
Address: Viale Morin 46, Forte dei Marmi, 55042, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: In the Byron Hotel, one of the gems of the Forte's hôtellerie, the Magnolia's cuisine will be remembered for its technique and sophistication, with refined and impressive presentations. Meat and fish are on the menu with local and international references, while the bread deserves special mention for its remarkable quality. The inspector recommends: choice of fish with grilled artichokes, cuttlefish lard and lactume - charcoal-grilled suckling pig, broad beans, borage and citron - citrus pavlova, vanilla and cardamom. The chef's table must be booked well in advance!

Name: La Palta
Address: Località Bilegno 67, Borgonovo Val Tidone, 29011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Still on the plain, yet already at the foot of the hills that can be glimpsed on the horizon, what from the outside presents itself as a typical country house surprises within with an elegant dining room that opens into a sort of veranda overlooking the garden and the greenery of the lower Piacenza countryside. The atmosphere is relaxed and most agreeable, ideally suited to a refined yet never formal lunch or dinner. The menu features references to local ingredients and recipes, alongside the excellent focaccia with ciccioli served among the bread course, a true speciality of the house. The cooking follows a measured and considered creative line, more intent on satisfying the palate than on surprising at any cost: three tasting menus are on offer – Sei nella mia terra, Sei nelle mie mani, and one dedicated entirely to pasta (to order) – with the option, alternatively, of choosing freely from the carte.

Name: La Parolina
Description: Just a few kilometres from Acquapendente, a historic stop on the Via Francigena, the restaurant enjoys a peaceful and scenic location, overlooking the Tuscia countryside. Here, Iside De Cesare and Romano Gordini offer cuisine deeply rooted in the region, based on local produce and authentic flavours, enhanced by a subtle technical finesse. Examples include dishes such as chilled chickpea hummus with local extra virgin olive oil, or the lentil ‘caviar’ that kicks off the dining experience. Among the most typical dishes, the tender and succulent pigeon – when available – stands out, served with bruschetta topped with chicken liver ragù and a canederlo in broth. Rounding off the experience are a well-stocked wine cellar, featuring a range of mature vintages, and the pleasant terraces, which are ideal for enjoying the tranquillity of the surrounding countryside.

Name: La Pineta
Address: Via dei Cavalleggeri Nord 27, Marina di Bibbona, 57020, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The name gives you a hint of what’s in store, but not everything – and certainly not the biggest surprise: after crossing a pine forest and leaving your car in the car park, you reach the restaurant and its stunning view – we’re practically on the beach! Opened in 1969 by the same family who still run it today – now in the next generation – the sea almost seems to spill into the dining room, where time seems to have stood still. The atmosphere is simple and retro, evoking memories of family holidays, happy times and days at the beach. The cuisine is in keeping with this setting: naturally seafood-based, the dishes are prepared according to traditional recipes, with the quality of the catch taking centre stage.

Name: La Preséf
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Set within the La Fiorida complex – a low‑impact, farm‑stay operation – the restaurant La Preséf serves a modern cuisine that is deeply rooted in the local terroir. Most ingredients come from the property’s own garden and the adjoining farm (zero‑kilometer, farm‑to‑table sourcing). The venue features a traditional feeding trough (called a “preséf” in the local dialect) and an on‑site creamery. It stands out for its visual and sensory experimentation, a hallmark of a cuisine deeply rooted in the local area. Guests who love alpine products can choose between two tasting menus, selected online at the time of booking: the first is a shorter, more traditional route; the second is slightly more creative while still staying firmly anchored to local tradition. The wine list also offers an excellent selection of indigenous labels.

Name: La Primula
Address: Via San Rocco 47, San Quirino, 33080, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Set in the enchanted heart of Magredi, between Pordenone and Aviano, this elegant restaurant is steeped in over 150 years of history under the ownership of the Canton family, now re-energised by the return of their son Marco, a passionate sommelier. Time and tradition go hand in hand here, making this restaurant a timeless classic in the province and an example of reliable, refined gourmet dining. The dining room, with its majestic fireplace, wraps guests in a warm welcome, while in the kitchen, Andrea composes dishes from land and sea, adding modern touches and creating comforting flavours. The wine cellar is a treasure in its own right: a rich selection and bespoke service, even by the glass, with some of the most reasonable mark-ups in Italy. The same building is home to Osteria alle Nazioni, which serves more informal lunches, where the food celebrates Friulian tradition simply and deliciously.

Name: La Rucola 2.0
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the famous castle in Sirmione’s historic centre, this restaurant is immediately striking for its elegant and creative feel. The choice here focuses on four tasting menus, from which guests can choose individual courses à la carte style if they prefer. Francesco Turturro’s cuisine is creative in feel, including various fish and seafood dishes alongside a few meat options and a menu dedicated exclusively to vegetables.

Name: La Sala dei Grappoli
Address: Castello di Poggio alle Mura, Montalcino, 53024, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The emotion begins along the approach, between vineyards, cypress trees and olive groves that compose the landscape of the most classic Tuscan countryside, culminating in the dramatic arrival before the imposing Castello Banfi, of medieval origin. The restaurant fits naturally into this setting of great evocativeness, recognisable also through the wine-themed frescoes that decorate the interior rooms. When the weather allows it, however, the terrace is the privileged space: here the panorama, attentive service and the quality of the cuisine combine to create a memorable experience. In the kitchen, chef Domenico Francone, originally from Puglia, with a measured hand introduces touches of his homeland, from taralli to small, flavourful panzerotti. The offering is articulated across three tasting menus that speak of philosophy, territory and a particular attentiveness to the plant world. A well-calibrated selection of desserts brings the meal to a fine close, between indulgence and lightness: among them, the milk foam with toffee caramel and peanuts stands out for its balance and pleasantness.

Name: La Speranzina Restaurant & Relais
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the heart of Sirmione, La Speranzina is a romantic retreat suffused with the scent of the Mediterranean. The bright interiors, decorated in pale lours, convey a timeless elegance, while, in summer, the terrace offers rare emotional experiences: the sparkling lake, the castle reflected in the water, tables suspended between water and sky. In the kitchen, Delfo Schiaffino creates flavours with an expertise that produces technical yet harmonious dishes, in which blue lobster meets caviar and wagyu beef merges with hints of French haute cuisine, in a dance of textures and aromas that seduces the senses. Every morsel is a story, every glass a journey: the wine cellar celebrates Champagne and great labels like Gaja, while three panoramic suites invite you to prolong the dream.

Name: La Stüa de Michil - Simone Cantafio
Address: Strada Col Alt 105, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: To get to this restaurant you head up towards the church in the prettiest part of Corvara, where you’ll find the La Perla hotel, one of the best in the valley, on your left. Once inside the hotel, you’ll be accompanied to La Stüa (stube in Ladin), where the profusion of wood lends an intimate and romantic feel to the decor. Although the setting is typical of the region, Simone Cantafio’s cuisine will take you on an extraordinary culinary journey. Originally from Calabria, this chef worked for many years in Japan, just one of his many formative experiences. As a result, his dishes feature different influences, often with a focus on vegetables. The name of the restaurant is a reference to owner and manager Michele Costa, an indefatigable and extraordinary figure in the world of Ladin tourism.

Name: La Tana Gourmet
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: To reach Tana Gourmet one must ascend to the Asiago plateau, where Alessandro Dal Degan has built one of the most personal and innovative gastronomic experiences in the Italian landscape. His cuisine reflects a vision deeply bound to the concepts of travel, exploration and research: key words defining a culinary journey in continuous evolution. The distinctive character of the offering lies in its capacity to surprise through unusual pairings, refined techniques and a constant creative tension.
