Particularly significant is the decision to forgo added salt and sugar: a choice that does not limit gustatory intensity but, on the contrary, enhances the identity and depth of the flavours. In the dining room, alongside Dal Degan, Enrico Maglio pursues an equally original exploration of the world of beverages, constructing pairings conceived as an integral part of the gastronomic narrative rather than mere accompaniment. The result is an immersive, coherent and strongly individual experience that confirms Tana Gourmet as one of the most original and stimulating tables in Italy.

Name: La Terrazza
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the top floor of the Hotel Eden, the restaurant offers one of the most captivating views of the capital: through the large windows, the view stretches from the Quirinale to the dome of St Peter’s, with Rome taking centre stage in the panorama. In the kitchen, a menu with great character is taking shape, deeply rooted in Mediterranean cuisine and enhanced by a measured yet distinctive use of spices, aromatic herbs and seasonal ingredients. Examples include chlorophyll-stuffed buttons, served with a rich mussel cream sauce, or chicken with peppers, a sophisticated reinterpretation of a traditional Roman classic. The experience is rounded off by a wine list with an international flavour, curated with a focus on depth and careful selection rather than simply the breadth of the selection.

Name: La Torre
Address: Strada Spicciano 7, Tavarnelle Val di Pesa, 50028, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The magic of Castello del Nero, a splendid 12th-century residence nestled in the Chianti hills, offers an experience that captures the very essence of Tuscany from the moment you arrive. Panoramic views, history and charm come together in the estate’s elegant surroundings, while extra virgin olive oil, wines and local produce are showcased to the full, thanks in part to a particularly well-stocked wine cellar. At the heart of the dining experience lies a style of cooking that is technically skilful, creative and, at the same time, deeply flavourful, presented with an aesthetic that is in keeping with the setting. The restaurant offers three tasting menus: ‘Evoluzione Vegetali’, ‘La Terra’ and ‘Il Mare’, complemented by an exceptional selection of pastries, as evidenced by imaginative desserts and a refined assortment of petits fours served at the end of the meal.

Name: La Tortuga
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: In Gragnano, La Tortuga has been synonymous with quality and reliability for decades. The dining room, intimate and romantic in atmosphere, is made all the more agreeable by the welcoming manner of Signora Orietta, professional yet pleasingly informal, and a discerning judge of wine: the list bears eloquent testimony to this, with some interesting labels also in vintages. The kitchen delivers a reassuring and accomplished repertoire, built upon excellent produce, from lake fish – as in the very successful spaghettini with lake ragù – to the finest of sea fish. Among the dishes that drew particular admiration from our Inspectors, the fillet of sea bass stands out, cooked with precision and set alongside a raw prawn marinated in liquorice, resting upon a delicate fennel broth and potato cream: a great classic, interpreted with restraint and elegance.

Name: La Trattoria Enrico Bartolini
Address: Località Badiola, Castiglione della Pescaia, 58043, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Beyond the gate, a long and dramatic avenue lined alternately with cypresses and maritime pines leads to L’Andana, one of the most evocative hotels in the area. On reaching the restaurant, do not be misled by the name: what awaits is not the atmosphere of a trattoria, but refined dining rooms and the cuisine of Enrico Bartolini, here working in partnership with Gabriele Verri. The latter’s Ligurian roots find an echo in certain dishes, others embrace Tuscany, and creativity inspires the rest.

Name: La Trota
Address: Via Santa Susanna 33, località Piedicolle, Rivodutri, 02010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Before entering this restaurant, stop for a moment to admire the crystal-clear waters of the Santa Susanna canal which runs opposite the building. La Trota has revolutionised and raised the standard of cooking freshwater fish, elevating it to the level of other produce traditionally considered to be more refined. At this restaurant, the Serva brothers, ably assisted by their respective children, showcase ingredients such as trout, tench, freshwater crayfish, pike and catfish, which are sourced from the clean waters nearby and which feature on the menu alongside a few meat dishes. They also make good use of wild herbs – guests are given an extract of these to take home, which they can use to make a warm herbal tea or a cool drink. There’s also an excellent choice of wine to accompany your meal, plus a surprising selection of cognacs and liqueurs. In fine weather, guests have the option of dining on the small wooden bridge spanning the canal. The restaurant celebrates its 60th anniversary in 2023.

Name: La Zanzara
Address: Via per Volano 52, località Porticino, Codigoro, 44021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: In the heart of the Po Delta, a farmhouse nestled in the tranquillity of a small islet offers an experience that goes far beyond a simple culinary stop. Surrounded by enchanting lagoon landscapes, the restaurant is set in a natural setting of rare beauty, where the silence is paced by the calls of the birds that inhabit these watery lands. On the table, the cuisine pays tribute to local produce with a menu centred on fresh fish and seafood, prepared with respect and simplicity. From crispy fried dishes to fish dishes prepared according to local tradition, each course showcases the freshness of the ingredients and the connection with the surrounding environment. An authentic spot that captures the true spirit of the Delta through distinctive flavours and a timeless atmosphere.

Name: Laite
Description: Within two magnificent wood-paneled stuben from the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, nestled in a traditional mountain house in a quiet area of authentic charm, chef Fabrizia Meroi draws from tradition and reinterprets it according to season and personal inspiration. Local aromas and fresh ingredients guide every dish: no virtuosity for its own sake, but a precise and sensitive reading of flavors. Emblematic is the treatment of tongue, which acquires a subtle smoky note from yakitori-style cooking before being veiled in a delicate licorice glaze. The wine cellar is equally impeccable, offering a window onto the world; it is overseen with passion by Elena, Fabrizia’s daughter, whose youthful spirit shines through especially in her excellent by-the-glass recommendations, offered strictly verbally. In essence, Laite remains a dining destination of singular atmosphere, capable of leaving the fortunate few with emotions and memories that endure.

Name: Lanterna Verde
Address: Frazione San Barnaba 7, Villa di Chiavenna, 23029, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Thanks to its fireplace, the welcoming, classic-style dining room at this restaurant is perfect for winter dining, while its garden terrace attracts guests in summer. Whatever time of year you visit, you’ll enjoy cuisine which balances traditional recipes with more contemporary options and fish from the lake. The Tonola family have been renowned throughout the province (and further afield) for their gourmet cuisine and welcoming hospitality for over 40 years. Their appeal is even greater today, thanks to the combined efforts of young chef Roberto, who provides a skilful, modern touch in the kitchen, and his experienced parents who oversee the front of house. The latter also make helpful wine suggestions from the impressive wine list that features labels from all over Italy, including a few rare bottles.

Name: Lazzaro 1915
Description: Once a coaching inn and, later, a canteen for the workers at the old sugar factory that stood opposite, Lazzaro is now an elegant family-run restaurant with a contemporary feel. In the dining room, the service is professional and attentive, while the cuisine reflects a personal vision that showcases ingredients and producers of the region through skilful technique and creativity. The menu offers a range of options: from the ‘A Gianni’ lunch – quick but well-prepared – to the ‘Campagna Liquida’ à la carte menu, which focuses mainly on products from the Veneto region, right through to the themed menu named ‘W.I.P. - Work in Progress’, which is constantly evolving. For those seeking a more comprehensive experience, there is ‘DNA’, the restaurant’s most ambitious tasting menu, available for just one week a month and dedicated to exploring seasonal produce and the local supply chain. The experience is rounded off by a well-curated wine list and an original selection of teas, herbal teas and infusions, all featured in a dedicated menu.

Name: Le Monzù
Description: Situated within the iconic Punta Tragara hotel, a building designed by Le Corbusier and overlooking one of the island’s most spectacular panoramas – between Marina Piccola and the clifftop headlands – the restaurant enjoys a view of rare magnificence that permeates the gastronomic experience itself. In the kitchen, the current chef constructs a proposal structured across several tasting menus, among which Le Origini stands out: a collection of the house’s most representative creations, including the “Bottone al cremoso affumicato, essenza di crostacei e gambero rosso”, a successful synthesis of technical elegance and gustatory depth, with a texture of remarkable precision.

Name: Le Petit Bellevue
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This is an exquisite gem within one of the region's most renowned and romantic hotels, the Bellevue Hotel & Spa, holder of two Michelin keys. With just five tables, two of which overlook the valley ending spectacularly with Gran Paradiso, Tuscan chef Niccolò de Riu celebrates the Valle d'Aosta in his kitchen with very few deviations, char and roe deer being excellent examples. Following the savoury part of the meal and preceding the talented pastry chef, Roberto from Bergamo will challenge your resistance with an excellent cheese cart, featuring mainly regional cheeses. Dinner will be overseen by the skilled maître Pietro, representing the fifth generation of the family that owns the restaurant, and by the renowned sommelier Rino, who was awarded the Passion for Wine Award a few years ago. The outstanding wine cellar is now also open to wines from unusual countries such as Japan, Turkey and Georgia, from which we recommend a highly impressive orange wine: the 2019 Rkatsiteli Zedashe. Vertical, dry, exquisite, with light balsamic notes.

Name: Le Trabe
Address: Via Capo di Fiume 4, Paestum, 84047, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Set within the Tenuta Capodifiume estate, Le Trabe offers an experience that extends well beyond the purely gastronomic. The welcome begins in the ancient tufa-hewn cellar, where aperitifs and amuse-bouches are served, before guests make their way to the terrace overlooking the gardens and surrounding mountains. The dining room, guided with professionalism and warmth by Simone Munzillo, accompanies guests through the discovery of the estate's philosophy, deeply rooted in self-sufficiency and the celebration of the local area. The contemporary cuisine of chef Marco Rispo finds expression across three tasting menus: Caput Aquae, dedicated to the identity of the Trabe river; Intro by Nonna Lina, a homage to family tradition; and Zerottantuno, an eight-course journey built around zero-kilometre ingredients. The stars of the table are the estate's own products, from extra-virgin olive oil to vegetables, through to buffalo milk and its derivatives, celebrated in identity-defining dishes such as Bufala Bufala Bufala: spaghetti cooked in mozzarella whey, which lends the dish both savouriness and a delicate acidic note, completed by buffalo ricotta, smoked buffalo cream, and black pepper, in a balance in which the smokiness adds aromatic depth without overwhelming the delicacy of the buffalo milk.

Name: Leon d'Oro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Stepping into the Leon d’Oro means immersing yourself in an atmosphere of genuine hospitality, with rustic yet tastefully appointed surroundings, two elegant dining rooms and a lovely garden which, in the warmer months, becomes the ideal spot for dinner. The cuisine draws inspiration from both the region and the sea, alternating between traditional dishes and more contemporary creations. The offering comprises two tasting menus, ‘La cucina in cascina’ and ‘Marenostrum’, complemented by an extensive and intriguing à la carte menu. Among the dishes not to be missed are the marubini with a rich and well-balanced Marsala and Parmigiano reduction as well as the sturgeon au gratin with Mediterranean chopped vegetables, milk and sprouts. The selection of desserts is also excellent, with the lemon delicacy with capers and liquorice standing out in particular. The experience is rounded off by a wine list of remarkable depth, featuring a wealth of old vintages and prestigious vertical tastings of grand crus.

Name: Li Galli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: This restaurant housed within the elegant Villa Franca hotel in the upper part of Positano boasts a small, bright dining room with distinctive black marble tables (just seven of them!), a glass ceiling and floor-to-ceiling windows that open in summer to create an outdoor dining space. The beautiful view looks out to sea and Li Galli, the island after which the restaurant is named. Following the end of the restaurant’s partnership with Nino Di Costanzo, chef Savio Perna (originally from Torre del Greco) now steps into the spotlight on his own. He takes his inspiration mainly from the local region, although the pigeon in one of his more interesting dishes is sourced from one of the best breeders in Tuscany. Much of Perna’s technique focuses on beautiful presentation and a light touch, while the excellent service also adds to guests’ overall enjoyment of the dining experience. The trolleys that display a selection of olive oils, excellent bread and a choice of tempting desserts are also worth a special mention. The wine list practically spans the globe with around 1 000 different labels – France and Italy take centre stage, with a focus on champagne (especially Krug), with many wines also available by the glass.

Name: Linfa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Inside the walls, but easily accessible from the car parks outside, a small treasure chest of elegance, with contemporary artwork on the walls, and congeniality. Here chef Giovanni Cerroni, with a lengthy experience in fine dining, offers two tasting menus: Mimesis with the great classics and A mano libera, where his talent is best expressed according to the client's tastes as well. For wines, one quietly relies on the expertise of Cesario Delle Donne. Finally, the choice of using books as centrepieces is very much appreciated: the one on Tuscan proverbs illustrated by Renato Bellabarba is not to be missed. In short, a well-rounded experience in one of Tuscany's tourism gems

Name: LoRo
Description: Imaginative, light, and genuinely healthy: that's the cuisine at LoRo. Sea flavors dominate, especially in the appetizers and first courses, creatively and enticingly titled on the menu. Chef Pierantonio Rocchetti often starts with classic Italian traditions, reinterpreting them with flair and originality. Portions are generous, and the flavors are intense, culminating in desserts that provide moments of delightful indulgence.

Name: Local
Address: Salizzada dei Greci, sestiere Castello 3303, Venice, 30122, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Modern and minimalist, with an open kitchen, Local is one of the best and most exciting restaurants in Venice, the result of the synergy between the extremely friendly owner, who works front of house, and talented chef, Salvatore Sodano. With a 7 or 9-course tasting menu, it is an experience not to be missed! Extraordinary wine cellar with almost a thousand labels, most of them Italian.

Name: Locanda Don Serafino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Along the road that encircles Ibla (one of the most evocative and picturesque historic centres in Sicily), the restaurant welcomes guests into a spectacular dining room that appears carved from the rock. The space, however, eschews all rusticity in favour of a refined elegance, accompanied by service of a high order: an ideal setting for a romantic and gastronomic evening. Vincenzo Candiano confirms himself as a chef of great talent, engaged in a continual exploration that places dishes now considered classics, which are indispensable fixtures on the menu, alongside more innovative creations, often inspired by the island. The welcome is very pleasant, with a small garden of aromatic herbs – wild fennel, mint, rosemary and other essences – whose fragrances provide a fitting prelude to the gastronomic experience. The cellar is also impressive, now numbering some 2,880 labels.

Name: Locanda Mammì
Description: In an evocative rural setting, among stone farmhouses, absolute tranquillity and a summer terrace that opens onto the surrounding hills, chef Stefania Di Pasquo presents an authentic cuisine, firmly rooted in the produce of her land and enhanced by a personal and unaffected touch. The variation of lamb is impeccable: a freshly cooked cutlet, a slow-braised preparation with onions, and alongside it a richly flavoured liver stew, together composing a coherent narrative of technique and memory. Equally remarkable is the dessert inspired by the traditional peasant breakfast, in which caramelised bread meets a surprising caciocavallo ice cream – a fitting homage to Agnone, not without reason known as the ‘city of cheese’ – finished with a delicate wine sauce. In the dining room, the chef’s husband, Tomas Torsiello, receives guests with grace and quiet assurance in a warm and romantic setting enriched by a fireplace and copper details. His is also the stewardship of the wine list, which reveals a marked predilection for Champagnes. The property also offers pleasant guest rooms, ideal for those wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Locanda Margon
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: With spectacular views over Trento and the Adige Valley, the restaurant invites you to discover the cuisine of Edoardo Fumagalli, a chef who skilfully combines technique, creativity and a contemporary sensitivity. The experience is structured around three tasting itineraries, the most notable of which is ‘Passione Bollicine’, designed to showcase Ferrari’s iconic Trentodoc wines through carefully selected pairings. The region’s produce plays a central role, particularly on the menu dedicated to Trentino, but it also features in dishes that draw inspiration from ingredients and culinary traditions from other Italian regions. For those who prefer greater freedom of choice, there is also a small menu featuring some of the most representative dishes from the tasting menus. Next to the restaurant, the Bistrot offers a more informal alternative, serving authentic Italian cuisine and providing the pleasant option of dining al fresco.

Name: Locanda San Lorenzo
Address: Via IV Novembre 79, Puos d'Alpago, 32016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: For over a century, the history of this establishment has been intertwined with that of the Dal Farra family. It all began in 1900 with an inn set up to welcome and feed the workers from the nearby mill; in the 1950s, the business passed to the second generation, eventually coming to Renzo Dal Farra, now the chef-owner, who earned a Michelin star in 1997. In a modern and welcoming setting, the restaurant showcases the produce of the region through two tasting menus, one of which is vegetarian, as well as an à la carte menu. Trout, game, mushrooms, pulses, cereals, cheeses and Alpago lamb are among the ingredients that best reflect the identity of these mountains. Rounding off the experience is a remarkably extensive wine cellar, which boasts a particularly rich selection of Piedmontese wines, while also extending well beyond the region’s borders.

Name: Locanda de Banchieri
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Chef Giacomo Devoto from Sarzana has transformed an old 17th-century farmhouse, surrounded by greenery, into a charming inn complete with rooms and a working farm, where tranquillity and hospitality reign. On the bright panoramic veranda, where the gaze reaches as far as the coast and the sea, guests can savour his creations devoted to the most authentic flavours of Lunigiana. The recipes, imaginative yet firmly rooted in the seasons, rest on the fragrance of the ingredients: vegetables – like the extra virgin olive oil – come largely from his extensive kitchen garden, while proteins are selected both from the inland area and from the sea very close by. It is precisely the variety of his garden that also allows him to offer Flora, an entirely green menu that brings together a full range of seasonal vegetables, interpreted with a delicate hand and a deep knowledge of the ingredients. The wine selection carefully accompanies this cuisine rooted in the territory: interesting labels ranging across Italy and France, choosing small producers and established names with the same attention that characterises every detail of the house.

Name: Locanda del Pilone
Address: Frazione Madonna di Como 34, Alba, 12051, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just a few kilometres from the town, yet already surrounded by the charm of the surrounding hills, the restaurant enjoys a privileged location from which the view takes in some of the most picturesque vineyard landscapes in the area. Neat rows of vines frame the landscape in each direction, offering particularly spectacular views during the autumn. In its elegant, classically styled dining rooms, the kitchen thoughtfully interprets the time of year and traditions, bringing them to life through a solid and measured approach. A variety of tasting menus, which are flexible and can be tailored to your preferences, including à la carte options, allow you to create a tailored culinary experience. The wine list is also worth noting, with a particularly interesting selection of Champagne. Finally, in the warmer months, the bistro on the stunning terrace allows you to enjoy the experience in an even more relaxed setting with panoramic views.

Name: Lorelei
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Whether or not the weather encourages you to spend time outdoors, it’s worth treating yourself to an aperitif on the terrace overlooking the Gulf, from where you can admire sunsets of rare beauty. As evening falls, the spotlight turns to Ciro Sicignano, a chef originally from Gragnano and a masterful interpreter of the Campania culinary tradition. His cuisine reinterprets local produce and recipes with technical skill, personality and imagination, finding expression in dishes such as Gragnano spaghetti with clams, baby squid with citrus and caponata coulis, or sole with courgettes, flowers and shoots, accompanied by a delicate cream made from Sorrento lemons. This concept, which is closely linked to the world of plants, is further enhanced by the two vegetable gardens at the chef’s disposal, a carefully curated selection of oils, and the elegant setting of Lorelei Londres, overlooking the sea at Sorrento.

Name: Lorenzo
Address: Via Carducci 61, Forte dei Marmi, 55042, Italy
Description: A historic restaurant in Forte, Da Lorenzo has welcomed many famous personalities who have enlivened the Versilia seasons. In the well-kept succession of three rooms, you can feel the love for classic and timeless dining. The menu reflects this, featuring essential dishes that attract a global clientele season after season. The tradition of preparing mayonnaise tableside is a highlight, along with offerings such as the grand raw seafood platter, seafood bavette, Versilia-style spaghetti, and some meat dishes. A vast wine selection, detailed in two elegant bound volumes, showcases depth and exploration, featuring both Italian and international labels, including classics and contemporary discoveries. For the daring, there are even bottles from remote regions of the world.

Name: Luca's by Paulo Airaudo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of artistic and monumental Florence, on the first floor of Hotel La Gemma, a small L-shaped dining room of contemporary and elegant taste is concealed, distinguished by an original green boiserie and enriched by carefully considered details. The kitchen favours an essential and creative approach: each dish in the tasting menu (minimum four courses) is built from a small number of elements, worked with precision to express personal and distinctive ideas. The dessert is emblematic, a goat’s milk flan crowned with a thin caramel crust of strawberry, delicately finished with measured drops of aged balsamic vinegar.

Name: Luisl Stube
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Schlosswirt Forst is a charming 16th-century residence housing a traditional restaurant, some rooms, and most notably, the Luisl Stube: a small gem set among beautiful antique woods and traditional chandeliers of a historic stube. With more candles than tables (only 4), it offers a truly intimate and timelessly romantic atmosphere. The culinary approach is contemporary, thanks to chef Luis Haller, who explores local products while also incorporating some exotic or seafood ingredients. He offers two tasting menus – one vegetarian and the other with animal proteins – that can be mixed as if they were one menu. Talented sommelier Nicola Spimpolo enhances the experience with uniquely intriguing wine pairings, exploring older vintages to evoke memorable enological emotions.

Name: Lunasia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: One of the most imaginative and original chefs in Versilia, offering a showcase restaurant inside the luxurious Plaza e de Russie hotel. In a modern and bright dining room overlooking the famous Viareggio promenade, Luca Landi's menu features three tasting options: one dedicated to fish, another combining seafood and vegetables, and a third focused on meats, with the possibility to mix and match dishes à la carte. The courses are elegantly crafted, showcasing creativity that is substantial and not just for show, with presentations that truly impress. Supported by excellent ingredients, the chef honors the region, using local seafood and inland products, sourcing as much as possible from trusted small producers, and maintaining a focus on circular cooking to reduce waste. The wine list is a journey through around 800 labels, with a special emphasis on Piedmont, Tuscany, and Burgundy; prices are accessible, and the by-the-glass selection is notably unique.

Name: Lux Lucis
Address: Viale A. Morin 67, Forte dei Marmi, 55042, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Inside the Hotel Principe in Forte dei Marmi, a lift leads up to the elegant rooftop: on clear days, the terrace offers a splendid view of the coastline and is the ideal spot for an aperitif at sunset. From here, you enter the dining room, which opens onto the open-plan kitchen, where the chef, originally from the hills around Modena, brings his menu to life. His cuisine is elegant and contemporary, underpinned by technical precision and creative flair, and is well represented by dishes such as glazed red mullet with citrus fruits, almonds and olives, cacciucco-style clams, mallard duck in a marinara sauce, and a mousse made with caramelised bread, chocolate and Vin Santo. The experience is rounded off by an original wine list, organised by grape variety, presented with expertise and discretion by the head waiter and sommelier, Sokol Ndreko, who has been working alongside the chef since the restaurant first opened: his ability to guide guests in their choices plays a key role in the quality of the hospitality.

Name: Līmū
Description: In a town renowned for its splendid villas built by the Palermo aristocracy, this restaurant occupies a small 16C tower on the edge of the historic centre. The name is a tribute to lemon, a fruit that grows in abundance in Bagheria. The restaurant has two elegant, contemporary-style floors, where dinner starts on the small terrace-cum-lounge – the setting for sampling a whole host of delicious appetisers. This is guests’ first encounter with a technical and creative cuisine that sensitively uses the finest local ingredients, while often following paths born from personal and imaginative ideas. The courteous and precise service is overseen by Giandomenico Gambino, a knowledgeable guide for pairings from the rich, well-stocked wine cellar.

Name: Maeba Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Nestled in the tranquillity of the countryside and off the beaten track, this elegant restaurant is housed in a former 18th-century oil mill, where the charming stone-walled rooms still shelter the historic wine cellar. The contemporary, light and tastefully designed interiors open out onto a garden overlooking rolling hills dotted with olive trees. Chef Salvatore Ciccarelli creates surprise tasting menus comprising 4, 6 or 9 courses, based on the finest local ingredients. The cuisine, contemporary and refined, places particular emphasis on plant-based ingredients without compromising on intensity and character. One of the signature dishes is the warm tubetto with tomato, oyster, spring onion and fennel, a dish that offers a wonderfully balanced flavour and surprising depth of taste.

Name: Malga Panna
Address: Strada de Sort 64, località Sorte, Moena, 38035, Italy
Description: The story of the Donei family is intertwined with that of this ancient Alpine dairy, transformed into a restaurant in the 1950s, when the parents of current chef-owner Paolo delighted early vacationers with wholesome dishes, helping establish it as one of Val di Fassa’s most celebrated tables. Today, only the name and panoramic setting remain from the original structure, suspended above the village and overlooking the valley, now admired from a new Alpine-style dining room enclosed entirely in glass. The rest is haute cuisine, thanks to the chef’s talent for reinterpreting the flavors of the territory with contemporary sensitivity. The wine list is organized into two sections, whites and reds, with a selection that highlights labels rooted in research and local terroir.

Name: Marco Bottega Ristorante
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant is situated within Dimora Genista, a dreamlike property nestled in a park filled with olive trees and other fruit trees, which also offers rooms should you wish to extend your stay. This is chef Marco Bottega’s fine-dining restaurant, set in a space of contemporary elegance, ideal for a special occasion meal. His cuisine is often inspired by traditional dishes, which the chef reinterprets in a creative way. An extensive wine list: over 3,000 wines, including 800 Champagnes.

Name: Marco Martini Restaurant
Description: One arrives by ascending to the first floor of a charming period building, where both the terrace for the warmer months and a light-filled dining room housed in a winter garden are to be found. Here natural light, lush plants and the delicate floor tiles create an atmosphere that is at once refined and welcoming. From the kitchen come creative offerings with pairings that are at times surprising, yet never betray the gastronomic soul of Rome: the flavours of tradition are reinterpreted through new textures and presentations, always maintaining a full and assertive taste capable of satisfying the palate. On the ground floor of the same building sits Mantis, ideal for an aperitivo or an informal dinner, thanks to more immediate signature cooking that is indulgent and convivial in equal measure.

Name: Marotta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Nestled among the green hills of upper Caserta, this venue is one of the most interesting realities in the local area. In the kitchen, young chef Domenico Marotta pursues a gastronomic exploration deeply connected to the plant world and to local resources, many of which come directly from the property's own kitchen garden. From this vision is born *Botanika*, a journey that places herbs, vegetables and biodiversity at its centre, interpreted through a cuisine that is contemporary, essential and full of personality. Each dish pairs the protein element with a specific botanical family, further celebrated through illustrated cards that recount its characteristics and particularities. Examples include creations such as Spaghetto, Lamiaceae, goat's cheese and lime, or Amberjack and Leguminose. The offering unfolds across several tasting menus and a selection of à la carte dishes. Completing the experience are the attentive service and the knowledgeable sommelier, who accompanies guests with precise and engaging explanations.

Name: Massimo Camia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A new chapter for the Camia family, historic interpreters of haute cuisine in the Langhe. Chef Massimo, together with his daughter Elisabetta, starts anew in a refined location among vineyards and hills, where a renovated rustic building becomes inn and restaurant. Here, Langhe tradition dresses in contemporary elegance; dishes that tell the story of the territory with character, such as risotto with local snails and Roero asparagus, while in the dining room his sommelier son will know how to recommend the right pairing from an almost encyclopedic choice of wines available in the cellar. A few rooms complete the experience, for those who want to stay and savor every detail.

Name: Mater1apr1ma
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A brilliant couple make this gourmet spot in the heart of the small town a must-visit. Sara, who is extremely knowledgeable about her own wine list, offers an original range of choices to those who put their trust in her expertise, and oversees a service that is both attentive and very welcoming. In the kitchen, Fabio creates original dishes that bring out the best in the produce of the Agro Pontino region. The chef also demonstrates sensitivity in a dish such as lamb, where he combines local produce with Indian influences, as if to encourage integration with the many Indian immigrants living in these areas. The ‘non-sweet desserts’ served at the end of the meal are particularly interesting, drawing inspiration from unusual ingredients such as Black Forest cake, lichens and spruce.

Name: Materia
Description: There may be no lake view, but Davide Caranchini’s cuisine alone makes this restaurant with its modern atmosphere well worth a visit – a style of cooking that will particularly appeal to those who prefer to step away from tradition and try more creative and experimental dishes, sometimes building on classic foundations. If we had to single out one dish in particular, we’d mention the ‘Latte & Miele’ dessert – delicious, original and refined.

Name: Mec Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: In the heart of monumental Palermo, set in a 16th-century palazzo almost opposite the Cathedral (after your meal, ask to step out onto the balcony: a fitting finale to a special evening), this distinctive restaurant shares its space with an exhibition dedicated to Steve Jobs. Diners are welcomed into one of three elegant rooms, beneath frescoed ceilings and surrounded by photographs and memorabilia tracing the story of the computer pioneer. In the kitchen, chef Carmelo Trentacosti reinterprets Sicilian recipes and ingredients with a personal touch: his famous caponata, for example, becomes a velvety sauce enhanced with shavings of Modica chocolate – irresistible with house-made bread. Before dessert, a fine cheese trolley makes its appearance, all complemented by attentive, courteous service.

Name: Miramonti l'Altro
Address: Via Crosette 34, località Costorio, Concesio, 25062, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: An Italian‑French couple runs this charming villa with a classic atmosphere on the outskirts of Brescia, with some tables set in bay windows overlooking the garden. Miramonti l’Altro has made history in Brescia and Lombardy dining by bringing together diverse gastronomic traditions: chef Philippe Léveillé’s French origins introduce some of the finest ingredients from across the Alps, combined with reinterpretations of classic Italian dishes, including Mediterranean favorites. Not to be missed is the glorious and essential cheese cart, extraordinarily well‑stocked.

Name: Moebius Sperimentale
Description: Carved from a former textile warehouse, the restaurant presents itself today as a multifunctional space of contemporary design in a semi-central district of the city. On the ground floor, bistrot and cocktail bar sit comfortably side by side, while a few steps up leads to a gourmet dining room of just 12 covers, dramatically suspended at the heart of the space: six seats are arranged at the counter, affording a close view of the kitchen at work. Here, a distinctly experimental offering takes shape, one that nonetheless sets out from a rigorous selection of quality produce. There are three tasting menus: Mare, Terra and Libertà (Sea, Land and Freedom), their names evoking the origin of the ingredients. The dishes give expression to the creativity of chef Croatti, drawing upon personal impulses and echoes of past experience, from Romagna to Spain. The service, attentive yet never rigid, preserves an informal tone throughout, with the chef himself invariably taking time to engage with his guests.

Name: Moma
Address: Via di San Basilio 42, Rome, 00187, Italy
Description: At lunchtime, enjoy informal dishes on the ground floor of this restaurant, while more creative gourmet cuisine is served by attentive and professional staff in the dining room on the first floor. Talented Roman chef Andrea Pasqualucci is at the helm in the kitchen, where he prepares creative and imaginative dishes. There are just a few typical Roman dishes on the menu here, and so the experience at Moma will appeal more to those keen on trying new ingredients and combinations.

Name: Nazionale
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: As soon as you step through the doors of the hotel of the same name – a refined mountain retreat – the restaurant’s two dining rooms welcome guests into a warm and cosy atmosphere, with crackling fireplaces, natural wood and elegant furnishings. In the kitchen, animal proteins continue to play a central role, alongside a growing emphasis on plant-based ingredients, thanks to produce from three vegetable gardens, two of which are on the restaurant’s own land. The ‘Habitat’ tasting menu offers a more creative dining experience, deeply rooted in the produce and seasonal offerings of the surrounding mountainous region, while the à la carte menu allows you to freely tailor your meal by choosing two or three courses, plus a dessert. The experience is rounded off by the shop opposite the restaurant, where you can buy the bread served at your table and other house specialities.

Name: Nin
Address: Via Zanardelli 5, Brenzone sul Garda, 37010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Together with the owners of the Belfiore Hotel, which houses the restaurant, the young and talented Trentino-born chef Andrea De Lillo has created a contemporary and creative cuisine, centred on locally sourced ingredients. Thus, even seemingly unusual ingredients such as shiitake mushrooms or wagyu beef fit seamlessly into the menu, as they are sourced from nearby farms and livestock: the famous Japanese beef, for example, comes from the slopes of Monte Baldo. Elegant, skilfully prepared dishes feature on a number of tasting menus that alternate between meat and fish from the lake, with a significant emphasis on vegetables, many of which are sourced from the restaurant’s own small farm. To round off the experience, there is a truly charming room on the first floor overlooking Lake Garda, particularly from the few tables on the veranda – which should be booked in advance.

Name: Nostrano
Description: Overlooking the Pesaro seafront, the dining room opens in fine weather onto the promenade in a seaside atmosphere while being distinguished by its own elegance. At the stove, Stefano Ciotti presents a cuisine that is predominantly seafood-led, with some meat dishes as well, and is fundamentally creative in its approach.

Name: Nove
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Within the spectacular Villa della Pergola, set among an elegant botanical park overlooking the sea, a contemporary cuisine takes shape that is deeply connected to the territory and to the plant world. Many of the ingredients are sourced directly from the property’s own kitchen garden and biodynamic farm, an expression of an approach that is both distinctive and consistent.Two tasting menus are offered: Terræ, which brings together the signature dishes created by chef Romano during his years at Nove, and Rêverie, the more recent expression of his creative vision. À la carte dining is also available. To complete the experience, charming bedrooms offer an exclusive stay with views over Alassio.

Name: O Me O Il Mare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The name pays homage to the chef’s father, himself a cook, an ultimatum issued by his then-girlfriend to “force” him ashore from cruise ship work, which has since become something of a family mantra. The talented sommelier is his wife; together they worked in various gourmet restaurants along the Campanian coast before realizing their dream of ownership here, in Luigi Tramontano’s hometown.

Name: Oasis - Sapori Antichi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: For almost forty years, the Fischetti family has been running this authentic gastronomic oasis, a landmark of local cuisine since 1988. A symbolic year, celebrated both in the wine list, which opens with a selection of prestigious wines from that vintage, and in the ever-present inclusion of a dish that has become iconic: ricotta ravioli with walnut sauce and burnt garlic, a recipe created by the founder’s mother. Today, the tradition lives on thanks to Michelina Fischetti and her granddaughter Serena Falco, who champion an authentic cuisine that reflects their identity, based on the careful selection of local, mostly organic, ingredients that capture the essence of the region and the rhythm of the seasons. The recipes are updated with a contemporary sensitivity and an eye to new dietary requirements, without straying from the essence of a cuisine that is simple, ethical and deeply rooted in tradition. Rounding off the experience is the impeccable and warm service, led by the Fischetti brothers.

Name: Olio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within The Box, a multifunctional space with vintage cars and contemporary art surrounded by a garden with splendid olive trees, you’ll find the restaurant (bistro service at lunch) and above all excellent seafood cuisine with a small menu dedicated to oysters and caviar. Flavorful and substantial recipes supported by remarkable ingredients, traditional foundations with just the right amount of creativity, nothing excessive. Many memorable dishes, particularly the first courses, including an extraordinary rice with basil pesto, raw and cooked seafood, and cherry tomato extract.

Name: Olmo
Address: Piazza della Chiesa 7, loc. San Pietro all'Olmo, Cornaredo, 20007, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The name pays tribute to the great elm tree that dominates the village’s small pedestrianised square, a symbol of the village and the very heart of the project. This cosy and exclusive restaurant has just three tables and the same number of seats at the counter overlooking the kitchen, offering guests the chance to watch the kitchen team at work up close. The culinary offering takes the form of a tasting menu that interprets the seasonality of the ingredients with creativity and precision, playing with textures, temperatures and balanced flavour contrasts. The result is a contemporary, minimalist and precise style of cooking, which successfully combines technical skill with expressive immediacy. At lunchtime, there is also a more flexible set menu, offering a choice of three dishes, which is particularly good value for money. Among the most compelling dishes, the refined combination of Grana and tomato stands out: Grana cream, tomato confit served with its own jam, and a surprising Parmigiano ice cream, coming together in a harmonious whole, rich in nuances and of great gustatory elegance.

Name: Orma Roma
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Orma is today one of the most interesting venues on the city's gastronomic scene, thanks to a contemporary cuisine that transcends geographical boundaries without losing balance or identity. Chef Roy Caceres – Colombian by birth, Italian by adoption, and a genuine citizen of the world – weaves influences from Latin America, Asia and the Mediterranean with natural ease, giving life to a proposal that is personal and refined. Two tasting menus of five or seven courses, with dishes also available à la carte, complemented at lunchtime by a more flexible formula. Among the iconic dishes, "Fregula, ricci e salsa XOrma" stands out: Sardinian fregula – a homage to the chef's wife's origins – meets Mexican mole and Hong Kong XO sauce in an intense and harmonious whole, in which the sweet savouriness of sea urchin, the fermented notes of the sauce and the aromatic complexity of the mole merge in perfect equilibrium. Great attention is also devoted to the vegetable element, fed in part by the restaurant's own kitchen gardens on the outskirts of the city. The experience is completed by a service that is elegant yet informal, impeccable without feeling contrived.

Name: Oro Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Reaching Oro means beginning the experience before even sitting down to table: the transfer by private motorboat from Piazza San Marco to the legendary Hotel Cipriani, on the island of Giudecca, introduces guests to a context of rare elegance. The restaurant opens onto the lagoon through broad picture windows, while walls lined with mirrored panels, a dramatic gilded dome and geometric marble floors define an interior that is both refined and luminous. The cuisine of Ferrara-born chef Vania Ghedini interprets the great Italian tradition with a contemporary touch, giving life to dishes that are balanced and not overcomplicated. Numerous references celebrate Venice: the recurring use of gold, for instance, evokes not only the name of the restaurant but also the city's extraordinary artistic heritage, from Byzantine mosaics to the gold backgrounds of Venetian painting. Ingredients from the lagoon engage in dialogue with produce from Emilia-Romagna and with measured Moroccan influences, the legacy of the chef's professional journey. Among the most interesting dishes, the seaweed and herb broth risotto stands out, mantecato with butter and cheese and completed by horseradish: it captivates through the intensity of its marine aromas, the elegance of the mantecatura and the perfect equilibrium between the sweetness of the rice, the pungent note of the horseradish and the savouriness of the sea vegetables.

Name: Oseleta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A few kilometers from Lake Garda, on gentle vine‑clad slopes, the entrance to Villa Cordevigo, home to L’Oseleta, makes a grand impression as it opens between two rows of cypress trees. Inside are two intimate dining rooms, but the best tables are in the elegant veranda with wide glass windows, where views of the gardens and pool create a charming atmosphere, made even more delightful by impeccable service. In the kitchen, Marco Marras offers two tasting menus (one of which is vegetarian) and an à la carte selection, featuring creative dishes that move effortlessly between references to the Verona and Lake Garda regions and international influences, ensuring a truly enchanting evening in an intimate setting.

Name: Osmosi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Set in open countryside, surrounded by orderly rows of vineyards, a historic villa houses Fattoria Svetoni, an estate devoted to hospitality, with elegant guest rooms, and to winemaking since 1865. It is here that the restaurant finds its home, arranged partly within the evocative ancient walls of the interior and partly in a strikingly modern glazed veranda that opens onto a pleasant and verdant prospect. The cooking of Mirko Marcelli expresses itself through a creativity that is measured and never excessive: the dishes possess a strong identity without ever imposing themselves, and the pairings are distinguished by balance and coherence, each complementing the other in harmonious fashion. The menu offers three tasting journeys – Materia, Sostanza and Concentrazione (Matter, Substance and Concentration) – from which certain dishes emerge as particularly representative: the excellent ‘constructed’ artichoke, making use of every part of the vegetable, and the sheep meat, presented in an interesting and creative pairing with oysters and endive. On the subject of wine, one may place oneself confidently in the hands of a broad and well-detailed list, and in the passion of Simone, who leads the service alongside the smiling and attentive Elena.

Name: Osteria Acquarol
Address: Via Johann Georg Plazer 10, San Michele, 39057, Italy
Description: Centrally located and with a plain, almost minimalist interior and a small charming outdoor space on the pedestrianised street for summer dining, Osteria Acquarol serves dishes which are strongly rooted in the region yet prepared with modern techniques and very much influenced by the character of the owner-chef here. Regionally sourced sustainable ingredients often feature in its highly original cuisine, including aromatic and wild herbs grown in the chef’s own garden. In 2023, the restaurant’s kitchen garden was extended so vegetables now play a more dominant role in the two tasting menus served here (seven and nine courses, with dishes that can be chosen à la carte style) – examples include the cold minestra soup entitled “L'orto dietro l'angolo” (“the garden around the corner”) and the unusual green tagliatelle with its carefully balanced bitter flavours. Originally from Cremona, chef Alessandro Bellingeri showcases the region in interesting and original ways.

Name: Osteria Altran
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A small gourmet restaurant surrounded by the verdant landscapes of the Friuli countryside. In what was once a simple farm, owner Guido Lanzellotti has brought this seemingly rustic yet delightfully romantic restaurant to life, creating modern dishes that focuses on top-quality ingredients and careful preparation. Alessio Devidè’s cuisine includes a few local specialities alongside classic Italian dishes which he has reinterpreted with his own personal twist. There’s a huge wine cellar, and if you’re a wine-enthusiast, it’s well worth having a word with the restaurant owner – he has extensive knowledge of the world of wine which he is delighted to share with guests, at the same time as recommending the best labels to accompany your meal.

Name: Osteria del Viandante
Description: Situated on the first floor of the 13C military fort in the centre of Rubiera, this elegant restaurant boasts five dining rooms, each one more delightful than the last and all frescoed, with the exception of the old limonaia which is decorated with wallpaper depicting its former function. This stylish and romantic setting provides the backdrop for young and enthusiastic chef Jacopo Malpeli who, having been born and raised between Parma and Reggio, creates cuisine that reflects the grandeur and opulence of local culinary traditions. Among his many interesting dishes, a particular favourite is the savarin di riso, which pays tribute to the legendary Mirella and Peppino Cantarelli and their former two-Michelin-starred restaurant in Samboseto. The extraordinary wine list includes several French wines alongside Italian labels and champagnes.

Name: Osteria della Brughiera
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Perched in the foothills embracing Bergamo, a garden leads to an elegant country house where parquet floors, exposed beams, and a striking fireplace set the stage for refined hospitality – ideal for an intimate dinner. A fresh wind blows through the kitchen: Bergamo native Paolo Cortinovis, whose impressive credentials include international experience and a previous tenure here, now works alongside Beatrice Arrigoni, who carries on her family’s culinary legacy under her father Stefano’s guidance. Available as both a tasting menu and à la carte, the offerings are broad and dynamic. The cuisine draws from Italy’s varied regional traditions before venturing into more contemporary territory, alternating effortlessly between fish and meat. Heritage staples – such as house-cured salumi – share the stage with more refined ingredients, from lobster to caviar, reflecting a well-calibrated balance of roots and ambition.

Name: Osteria di Passignano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within the Antinori universe, in one of the most beguiling villages of the Chianti Classico, stands the Osteria di Passignano: a restaurant of great elegance housed within walls steeped in history, alongside the ancient Badia di Passignano, still inhabited by monks and guardian of the barrel cellar of the wine that bears its name, produced from the vineyards that surround the monastery. The setting is of the very highest order, where history, craftsmanship and extraordinary landscapes are woven together. In the kitchen, chef Matteo Lorenzini maintains a close bond with the territory and its produce, articulating the offering between a solid local tradition and a more contemporary reading, frequently open to seafood – as in the accomplished crab salad with caviar and zest from the estate’s own citrus trees. Considerable attention is paid to seasonality, with vegetables and herbs drawn from the Orto della Badia, while the sumptuous wine list, with over a thousand labels from around the world, pays natural and fitting homage to the great Tuscan reds, beginning with those bearing the host’s own signature.

Name: Otto Geleng
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within the enchanting Hotel Timeo, a handful of tables on a bougainvillea-adorned terrace overlooking Taormina, the Bay of Naxos and Etna: against this backdrop of extraordinary beauty, chef Roberto Toro presents a cuisine that unites the flavours of Sicily with international techniques and inspirations, without losing its connection to the local area. The offering unfolds across several tasting menus dedicated to fish, meat and vegetables – alongside the option of composing a three-course à la carte menu. Among the dishes that most impressed our Inspector, the Prawn in Two Textures stands out: the Sicilian crustacean is served raw with tomato sauce, almond cream and caviar, whose refined savouriness enhances the natural sweetness of the flesh, while a frozen grapefruit delivers a pleasantly citrus freshness to the finish. The experience is completed by impeccable service, capable of uniting professionalism, spontaneity and genuine hospitality. The wine list, with over 400 labels, celebrates Sicily without forgoing a rich Italian and French selection, and includes interesting productions from small local winemakers.

Name: Paca
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Please note: relocated to Via delle Ginestre 45, Carmignano. This elegant restaurant reinterprets contemporary Italian cuisine through a meticulous selection of ingredients, sourced largely from small local producers and, where possible, from zero-kilometre supply chains. One of the standout specialities is Colonnata lard, often served alongside a fine selection of artisan breads, ranging from those made with rice flour to those made with chestnuts. A cuisine that focuses on the essence of flavour, complemented by impeccable service that helps to make the experience particularly enjoyable and memorable.

Name: Paolo Griffa al Caffè Nazionale
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A historic city restaurant, overlooking Aosta's main square, has been brought back to life by the passion of young chef Paolo Griffa. It offers colourful, balanced and contemporary cuisine, available in 3, 5 or 7-course tasting menus. Always attentive to the harmony of flavours and chromatic beauty of dishes, the chef demonstrates a growing skill in handling vegetables, as evidenced by the vegetarian dishes always on the menu. The service is of an excellent standard and the wine offerings of great depth. Of course, as the name suggests, some spaces are dedicated to excellent coffee, equipped with an excellent pastry corner, making this place recommended for any time of the day, from breakfasts to aperitifs!

Name: Paolo e Barbara
Description: A historic address in the heart of the city, this restaurant retains a charm of a bygone era and offers a seafood cuisine firmly rooted in its territory, placing the highest value on the quality of local produce. There is also modest but noteworthy self-production, including extra-virgin olive oil from the Val Nervia, which – among other offerings – accompanies the excellent snails served with an aromatic cream of twelve wild herbs. Among the first courses, the cappelletti filled with Sanremo prawns, delicately dressed with vegetable broth and saffron, stands out as a dish of great refinement and balance. In the dining room, Barbara guides guests through a selection of wines with considerable expertise, with a particular focus on Ligurian labels, whilst Paolo in the kitchen delivers a solid and coherent experience. Reservations are recommended.

Name: Pascucci al Porticciolo
Address: Viale Traiano 85, angolo via Fiumara 2, Fiumicino, 00054, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Just steps from the harbour of Fiumicino, Pascucci al Porticciolo surprises with the unassuming elegance of a bright dining room, pale in tone and classical in atmosphere, attuned to the authentic character of the locality. The welcome extended by Vanessa Melis and her front-of-house brigade is impeccable: professional, spontaneous and capable of putting each guest at their ease. In the kitchen, Gianfranco Pascucci delivers one of the most convincing interpretations of so-called "produce-led cuisine", in which a technique of absolute precision is placed at the service of exceptional raw materials. Amberjack, king prawns, turbot and the rest of the catch impress through their freshness and quality, while the preparations eschew all virtuosity for its own sake, favouring balance, harmony and respect for the ingredient. Among the most memorable dishes, the white grouper tataki with curried herbs, barbecued escarole and green tomato cream stands out. This is a creation that evokes Asian suggestions without losing its Mediterranean identity.

Name: Pashà
Address: Contrada Torre Catena 874, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Set within the evocative surroundings of a fourteenth-century masseria, nestled within a park of centuries-old trees, this venue presents one of the most interesting gastronomic experiences in the Puglian countryside near Polignano. At the time of our visit, the menu takes the form of a single tasting menu available in five or seven courses, through which Michele Spadaro interprets the flavours of regional tradition with creative verve. We are told that a more accessible option for the interior dining room is also forthcoming, designed for guests spending longer in this setting of great allure. The cellar is exceptional, counting over a thousand labels and featuring a striking communal table set among the bottles. A carefully managed service and an environment of great visual impact, enveloped in the green of the Puglian countryside, complete the experience.

Name: Per Me Giulio Terrinoni
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated just a few metres from Via Giulia in the heart of the historic city, this restaurant is home to chef Giulio Terrinoni who, over the years, has built a reputation for his superb fish and seafood cuisine which he serves in classic, unfussy style with a focus on top-quality ingredients (meat and vegetarian options also feature on the menu). If you’d like to watch the chef at work and experience a more creative surprise menu, book one of the two seats at the counter facing the open-view kitchen.

Name: Piano35
Description: On the ground level of what has become one of the symbols of the Turin skyline, the Intesa Sanpaolo skyscraper designed by Renzo Piano, there is the entrance to the restaurant. From here, a lift takes you quickly up to a height of 150 metres, but before taking your seat, it’s worth stopping off at the panoramic terrace, which offers a splendid view of the city. In the bright dining room surrounded by the conservatory, the menu is organised into three tasting menus: one dedicated to Piedmont, one inspired by the cuisine and flavours of Italy, which also features seafood dishes such as turbot with a sauce of saffron, rosemary and candied lemon, and a third menu that is vegetarian. At lunchtime, however, the menu takes on a more informal feel, thanks to a bistro-style offering that is simpler and more straightforward.

Name: Pipero Roma
Address: Corso Vittorio Emanuele II 250, Rome, 00186, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated opposite the church of Santa Maria in Vallicella (known to locals as Chiesa Nuova or new church), this restaurant is named after its owner Alessandro Pipero. Ciro Scamardella, a young chef from Campania who is not yet in his forties, is at the helm in the kitchen, where he prepares modern and creative meat and fish dishes with a focus on the seasons (the beef with spinach, bay leaf and black garlic sauce is particularly good), including a few specialities from his native region. His recipes feature ingredients such as rapini, escarole and lemons and his beautifully presented cuisine demonstrates a continuous search for balance and colour. Front of house, friendly Achille Sardiello leads a team that is fully focused on the needs of guests.

Name: Poggio Rosso
Address: Località San Felice, Castelnuovo Berardenga, 53019, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Set in the heart of the Chianti hills, Borgo San Felice Resort offers an experience that captures all the charm of the most authentic Tuscany, amid vineyards, olive groves and an atmosphere of great elegance. In this refined and relaxing setting, Stelios Sakalis presents a culinary experience that stems from the fusion of Tuscan culinary heritage and the wealth of experience the chef has gained in leading European kitchens. The dishes combine technique, balance and a contemporary sensitivity, enriched by references to his Mediterranean roots. The experience is rounded off by attentive and well-organised service, which guides guests with professionalism and discretion in a setting of great charm.

Name: Porcino
Description: Inside the modern Badia Hill hotel, patron Marco Verginer offers two tasting menus: one focused on seasonality, the other inspired by his creativity, featuring ingredients such as Wagyu beef produced in Alto Adige. The pairings are flavorful and lively, with extensive use of vegetables, often from the home garden. The result is an excellent dining experience served in a contemporary setting surrounded by glass walls that offer splendid views of the surrounding landscape. The menu presents a succession of mountain territory references combined with Mediterranean and international touches in highly elaborate dishes.

Name: President
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: From the kitchen emerges a personal reinterpretation of Campanian traditions, which in certain details – such as the *siligineus* bread, inspired by recipes of ancient Rome – draws roots from distant eras. The dishes, always carefully considered in both flavour and presentation, are arranged across several tasting menus, with the option of freely composing one’s own journey, also from the à la carte selection. We followed the thread of the sea, appreciating preparations such as the “Rosso Pompeiano”, in which red mullet and beetroot engage in an elegant dialogue, and the salt cod acqua pazza, interpreted in a more contemporary key; but the land-based offering is equally distinguished by its solidity and quality. In the dining room, direction is entrusted to the expertise and courtesy of the chef’s wife, ready to suggest well-judged wine pairings, with the option of tasting notable labels by the glass as well. Alongside her, the new generation of a family that has made hospitality and fine cooking a true vocation is beginning to make its mark.

Name: Prezioso
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Leaving Merano behind, a panoramic road that winds through apple orchards, chestnut groves and vineyards leads within a few kilometres to Castel Fragsburg, a historic seventeenth-century residence immersed in greenery. Here, amid the charm of South Tyrolean aristocratic architecture and an understated alpine elegance, the Prezioso restaurant finds its home. In the warmer months, the terrace suspended above the valley offers a spectacular view that contributes greatly to the evocative quality of the experience. The beauty of the setting is matched by a solid cuisine firmly rooted in the local area, built around its produce and clean, precise flavours. Freshwater fish such as Arctic char and trout appear frequently in the tasting menus, alongside preparations that celebrate the quality of the meats. Among the most convincing dishes, the veal served in two acts: first accompanied by roasted onion, tarte tatin and meat jus, then with an intense sweetbread served with onion cream and wild herbs, a mouthful of real character and gustatory depth.

Name: Primo Restaurant
Description: Primo Restaurant is the place where contemporary, refined cuisine – deeply rooted in the Apulian region – takes shape, skilfully blending aesthetic appeal with intense flavours. The menu features a number of tasting menus of varying lengths, while those who prefer to choose freely can opt for the ‘signature’ dishes – those that have proved most popular since the restaurant opened. Among these, the extraordinary Gallipoli-style scapece ravioli with anchovies, beurre blanc and saffron is particularly worth mentioning – an ideal blend of tradition and contemporary flair. Each menu showcases creative, technically skilful and balanced cuisine, making this restaurant one of the region’s most interesting gastronomic destinations.

Name: Principe Cerami
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Massimo Mantarro presents a cuisine that interprets Sicily with contemporary sensitivity, without losing its connection to the local area. Clean flavours, vivid colours, and refined pairings accompany the guest on an ideal journey through the island, from the sea to the hills of the interior and through to the suggestions of Etna. Seasonality guides each offering: vegetables, fruit and aromatic herbs take on a central role in creative and harmonious dishes where technique, elegance and exploration bring out the very best of Sicily's exceptional raw materials.

Name: Procaccini
Address: Via Giulio Cesare Procaccini 33, Milan, 20154, Italy
Description: Talented chef Emin Haziri, originally from Kosovo but raised in Italy and with significant professional experience behind him, now signs a line of contemporary and personalised cuisine. Alongside the more creative and imaginative offerings we find another with raw seafood, from oysters to caviar, from Sicilian shrimp to scampi. In the elegant and refined dining room with harmonious colours and fine furnishings, the open kitchen and marble counter with velvet stools stand out. The restaurant also has the soul of a cocktail bar where you are led once you enter for a welcome drink, before sitting down accompanied by live piano and vocal background music. And, as if that were not enough, kudos to the good Eduardo, sommelier and maître who will guide you through the wine selection, which is not very wide, but well conceived. We had pleasure in pairing a Mazzara red shrimp with a 2023 Etna Graci, fresh and mineral.

Name: Pulejo
Description: In the refined Prati quarter, the elegance of the surroundings finds a natural extension in the interiors of the restaurant that – with an only apparent ‘j’ – bears the surname of its chef-patron. Dinner is taken in a romantically subdued light, in a dining room that continues to evolve with both consistency and taste, supported by service of the highest professionalism: discreet, watchful, and perfectly timed to anticipate each moment of need. The cooking plays upon balance and variety, weaving references to the flavours of Lazio together with influences gathered during the chef’s earlier career. The result is a series of creative and accomplished recipes, among them razor clams paired with nervetti and finished with a broth drawn from the crustacean’s trimmings, enriched with a vegetable gremolata, oil of celery and bone marrow – a clear homage to his starred past in Milan. Dish after dish is marked by careful attention to detail, underpinned by excellent produce and cooking of the utmost precision.

Name: Qafiz
Address: Località Calabretto, Santa Cristina d'Aspromonte, 89056, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: A captivating journey through the wild countryside and olive groves of Aspromonte serves as a prelude to an almost mystical experience at Qafiz, where Chef Nino Rossi tells the story of Calabria and its roots through an instinctive, profound, and remarkably accomplished cuisine. Guests are seated around a small kitchen in omakase style, embarking on an immersive gastronomic journey supported by an impeccable wine selection and service that keeps the energy of the moment alive. For those wishing to fully immerse themselves in the spirit of the place, Casa Qafiz offers the possibility of an intimate, refined stay, while at AsproCocktail Bar one can savor a signature spirit beside the crackling fireplace. A perfect conclusion to an experience that unites authenticity, terroir, and a contemporary vision of Calabria’s gastronomic heritage.

Name: Quadri
Address: Piazza San Marco 121 (primo piano), Venice, 30124, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Il Quadri showcases traditional Venetian dishes interpreted with a contemporary twist by chef Sergio Preziosa, who focuses on ingredients from the lagoon, such as fish from its shallow waters, vegetables from SantʼErasmo island, shellfish and game in season. Ask the staff for wine recommendations and you’ll discover some unusual labels on the extensive and varied wine list, such as the Adega do Vulcão Ameixambar, a white wine from the Azores with mineral notes and great flavour – the perfect accompaniment to the rich, tasty cuisine served here.

Name: Quellenhof Gourmetstube 1897
Address: Via Passiria 47, Saint Martin in Passeier, 39010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A young chef and a brilliant maître-d’ work together at this restaurant, where the cuisine is full of character and has its roots firmly anchored in the region. The menu allows guests to choose from four to six courses, all prepared using local ingredients such as lamb raised on a nearby farm served with parsnips and a refined jus, or reinterpreted dumplings served with morel mushrooms and spring peas. Matteo oversees the wine list, guiding guests on a unique journey through Italian and international labels collected over the past twenty years, all offering excellent value for money. Three impressive wine cellars can be visited by guests, while fine wines and historic vintages (especially from Tuscany and Bordeaux) are evident on the wine list. Excellent bread and dessert options complete the picture.

Name: Quintessenza
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: What a fascinating historical context: the Swabian castle is right in front of the restaurant, the dining rooms, on two levels, are also within period walls, and finally there is the possibility, when the weather permits, to eat on a panoramic terrace from which you can also see the famous bell tower of Trani cathedral (as well as a table set up in a small room used as a wine cellar for dining among the bottles). No less than four brothers, between the dining room and the kitchen, share the restaurant's tasks; at the cooker, Stefano Di Gennaro, who creates a cuisine rich in substance and flavour, avoids unnecessary complications and virtuosity and aims firmly at satisfying the palate, in dishes that mostly reinterpret the classic Italian tradition using various Apulian products.

Name: Re Santi e Leoni
Description: Steps from the cathedral, within a refined historic palazzo, a luminous passageway leads guests towards the open kitchen, through contemporary interiors of essential design. At the table, the quality of the raw material is the starting point of a gastronomic offering that is precise and dynamic, enhanced by excellent artisan breads and desserts of notable elegance. Three tasting menus are available, complemented by an à la carte that follows the rhythm of the seasons and interprets the cuisine with balance, technique and clarity of flavour. The chef presents personal and measured dishes, capable of uniting rigour and creativity with a contemporary touch. Completing the experience, a broad and well-constructed cellar with a selection that pays homage to the most interesting expressions of the Italian wine landscape.

Name: Relais Blu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Overlooking Capri, in a simply spectacular setting, the restaurant offers one of the most breathtaking views of the Sorrento Peninsula: from the windows and the terrace, your gaze is drawn to the island’s unmistakable silhouette, suspended between sea and sky. In the kitchen, Fumiko Sakai interprets the local area with his own personal touch and a wealth of experience, gained through years of working along the Amalfi Coast.
