His menu is firmly rooted in the culinary traditions of Campania, making the most of ingredients sourced from the restaurant’s own vegetable garden, while occasionally incorporating subtle Eastern influences that enrich certain dining experiences. The offering is presented as four tasting menus, with the option to order à la carte as well. The star of the show is, of course, the sea, with plenty of focus on fresh fish, while also showcasing excellent local meats such as Caserta black piglet and Laticauda lamb, alongside more cosmopolitan creations that blend Mediterranean influences and Japanese touches in an original and finely balanced harmony.

Name: Retroscena
Address: Largo del Teatro 3, Porto San Giorgio, 63822, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of Porto San Giorgio’s picturesque old town, among the exposed brick houses, is a dining room of refined minimalist elegance, with just a few tables and an intimate atmosphere. When guests are not captivated by the dishes, they will find themselves fascinated by the open kitchen, where the crew works with precision, creating courses that express the restaurant’s contemporary signature style, characterised by a deft use of acidity as a distinctive note. Although the team is young, the technical level is high and the cuisine, while retaining a few echoes of its Modenese training, develops above all through an inventiveness capable of stirring deep emotions. For a broad and creative overview, the ten-course Labor Limae tasting menu is the ideal choice, designed to capture nuances and ideas in constant evolution. The wine offering is excellent too: a cellar in continual expansion, with carefully curated selections and well-conceived by-the-glass options. Completing the picture is a convincing selection of cocktails, spirits and liqueurs, further enriching the overall experience.

Name: Rezzano Cucina e Vino
Address: Via Asilo Maria Teresa 34, Sestri Levante, 16039, Italy
Description: The historic family restaurant on the Ligurian Levant sees young Matteo in the kitchen, marking the fifth generation of Rezzano involved in this field. This year they've also recruited Jorg Giubbani, who boasts stellar experiences in the area, further elevating the quality of the offering with three tasting menus primarily dedicated to seafood and gardens (three in total) to deliver dishes consistently delicate but flavourful, balanced in pairings, never contrived and visually striking. We were particularly conquered by the caponata of mackerel and desserts, all served in the lovely veranda overlooking the setting sun and central square or at tables just beyond the welcoming, wooden-toned entrance.

Name: Ristorante del Lago
Address: Via Acquapartita 147, Bagno di Romagna, 47021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Leaving the main road behind, a series of hairpin bends leads up to Acquapartita, a hamlet at an altitude of almost 800 metres, where one of the most interesting places in the area is to be found. Here, the Bravaccini brothers have built a solid and well-balanced venture, naturally dividing their roles: in the kitchen, Simone proudly champions the restaurant’s connection to the local area, creating a menu that showcases local produce such as game, mushrooms and trout; among the most representative dishes are the ‘Spaghetto cacio e pepe with marinated trout’, which was also praised by the inspectors, and the flavourful ‘Charcoal-grilled quail, stuffed with livers and black truffle’, not to mention a selection of delicious and well-crafted desserts. In the dining room, Andrea welcomes guests with expertise and a friendly, convivial manner, orchestrating precise and attentive service while managing a truly encyclopaedic wine list, divided into two volumes featuring some 1,600 labels: there is a strong focus on Italian wines and an equally extensive selection of French wines, accounting for nearly 40% of the range; in addition to its breadth, the quality of the selection and the excellent service are particularly impressive.

Name: Romano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Celebrating its 60th anniversary in 2026, the timeless Romano continues to serve top-quality fish and seafood, occasionally updated yet always maintaining the traditions which have made it one of Versilia’s culinary institutions. Although this long-established restaurant’s philosophy has not changed over the years, current chef Nicola Gronchi should be applauded for adding a hint of contemporary flavour and technical expertise to the cuisine, bringing it in line with the times, while still retaining everything that this restaurant does best, namely serving fish of the highest quality (there are also a few meat dishes), including the occasional typical Versilian recipe. Front of house, talented Roberto and his team guarantee an enjoyable all-round dining experience, including wine recommendations.

Name: Rossellinis
Address: Via San Giovanni del Toro 28, Ravello, 84010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking
Description: The famous fine-dining restaurant at the beautiful Palazzo Avino hotel features classic, elegant dining rooms and a stunning terrace boasting views of one of the most spectacular stretches of the Amalfi Coast. Dinner begins with a flute of champagne served in the fabulous garden below the terrace (offering the same magical views as far as Minori and beyond), accompanied by delicious and imaginative finger food served on superb ceramic tableware. Your experience then continues with fine regional cuisine created by chef Gianni Vanacore, which is full of light and balanced flavours. Skilful sommelier Luigi Nitto is also at hand to assist with your wine selection from an extensive and exhaustive list that includes a vast choice of options from around the world.

Name: Sadler
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Housed in the Casa Baglioni hotel, a beautiful Art Nouveau building dating from 1913, this restaurant has a contemporary feel with an elegant dining room featuring colourful armchairs. The cuisine is precise and distinctive, with a harmonious balance of traditional and innovative flavours thanks to the top-quality ingredients used. The wine list is also top-notch, featuring excellent Italian and international wines, including some rare and exclusive labels. An interesting business lunch is available at midday, while the Rooftop Bar on the seventh floor boasts 360° views of Milan and serves a selection of aperitifs designed especially by the chefs (open daily from 6pm-1am).

Name: San Giorgio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: At the helm of the restaurant is the owner, Danilo Scala, a passionate host and connoisseur of wine, who is able to guide guests on an engaging, original culinary and wine journey. There is a perfect rapport with the young chef Alessandro Marino, who, following significant international experience, has chosen to return to his native Genoa to create a contemporary, personal and creative Mediterranean cuisine, built on high-quality ingredients and finely honed technique. Among the dishes worthy of a special mention, the inspector recommends the delicate raw prawns with Swiss chard, green olives and Vermouth sauce, while among the main courses, the refined lamb with onions, cherries and morels stands out as a fine example of his balanced cuisine, rich in character. The wine list is notably above average, internationally awarded, and includes an entire volume dedicated to Italian and, above all, French sparkling wines.

Name: San Martino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: San Martino is a classic and elegant grand restaurant with timeless appeal, which makes your dining experience here truly memorable. The restaurant boasts two important characters: Paolo Colleoni who, with his extensive knowledge and skills, is the perfect front-of-house host, welcoming guests with joy and enthusiasm and always finding exactly the right words; and, at the helm in the kitchen, Stefano Locatelli, a chef who is equally at ease with the restaurant’s historic dishes (the restaurant has held a Michelin star for decades) and more modern creations. Although fish continues to take centre stage (starting with the legendary “plateau royal”), meat dishes also feature on the menu, and there is also a superb cheese trolley. There are plenty of French options on the wine list, with some remarkable labels also available by the glass.

Name: San Martino
Address: Piazza Cappelletto 1, Località Rio San Martino, Scorzè, 30037, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Michela offers guests a friendly welcome at this restaurant, where chef Raffaele creates intensely flavoured recipes enhanced by the use of vegetables fresh from the garden. Unmissable dishes include a delicious tortello pasta with sea snails which is full of fresh and decisive flavours, and lightly seared scallops served (in season) with mixed mushrooms and a delicate peach compote, as well as pigeon cooked in two different ways. The wine list features an extensive selection of Italian and international options, including a choice of some vintage labels. The dining room here is contemporary in style, with a beautiful modern fireplace adding warmth on cold winter evenings. Book a table in the wine cellar (only available in summer!) for a unique dining experience.

Name: SanBrite
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just outside Cortina, yet already surrounded by meadows, it is here, in a dining room with a Dolomite-inspired atmosphere, that Riccardo Gaspari’s cuisine embodies the culinary essence of the Ampezzo and Alpine regions. On his farm, cattle, goats and pigs are reared with respect for the animals; vegetables are also grown and cheese is produced, which are then used to meet some of the kitchen’s needs as part of a waste-reduction initiative. The dishes are delicious and bursting with flavour, starting with the famous whipped butter. It’s a must-visit for anyone keen to discover the local culinary delights.

Name: Sapio
Description: Despite his young age, Alessandro Ingiulla creates mature cuisine which showcases the best Sicilian ingredients, including olive oil, fruit and vegetables from his own garden, with skill and imagination. The restaurant occupies an old warehouse that has been fully restored to create an elegant, contemporary space which also hosts art exhibitions with works by artists from the region and further afield. In addition to the dining room, there’s a chef's table in the spacious kitchen and convivial tables in the wine cellar, where guests dine surrounded by bottles from all over Sicily. The excellent service comes courtesy of Roberta, the chef’s partner, and Andrea, the discreet and competent sommelier. You may need to be patient when looking for a parking space nearby, but it’s well worth it!

Name: Saporium
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Beautifully nestled in the tranquillity of the Tuscan countryside, near the Abbey of San Galgano, Saporium is the restaurant at Borgo Santo Pietro, the elegant resort awarded three Michelin Keys. The estate covers 120 hectares of gardens, vegetable plots, livestock farms and croplands – an asset that finds its most authentic expression in the cuisine. At the helm is Ariel Hagen, a chef with an extraordinary sensitivity to botanicals, who crafts a culinary journey deeply rooted in Tuscany and the estate’s own ingredients. Although I am not a vegetarian, what strikes me most about the experience is the central role played by the world of plants and aromatics, interpreted with precision and creativity. The salad on the seasonal menu is a real highlight, made up of 25 different ingredients and enhanced by a memorable dill cream.

Name: Saporium Firenze
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: At this restaurant, Ariel Hagen, a young and friendly chef who, despite his name, hails from Florence, divides his time between the open-view kitchen and the tables in the dining room, where he happily explains dishes to guests and shares his enthusiasm for sustainability. His dishes are showcased on tasting menus but can also be chosen individually à la carte style from either menu depending on your preference. Among the desserts, don’t miss the Caterina De' Medici’s rose, a modern version of the traditional Florentine “zuccotto” cake with a beautiful combination of milk and Alkermes liqueur. The wine list is of the same high quality as the cuisine, featuring excellent labels with an impressive choice of wines by the glass, as well as some extremely rare labels from the 1980s and 90s that will be appreciated by wine connoisseurs. There’s also a choice of excellent Borgo Santo Pietro wines.

Name: Sarri
Address: Lungomare C. Colombo 108, Borgo Prino, Imperia, 18100, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This fine restaurant enjoys a pleasant location in the charming Borgo Prino, a string of houses painted in typical pastel colours right in front of the sea. The legendary mildness of the Ligurian climate makes it possible to eat outdoors often, but should that not be possible the charm of the indoor dining room, an old shed furnished with excellent contemporary taste, will be anything but an afterthought. Service is elegant and impeccable, headed gracefully by hostess Alessandra. Last but not least, the cuisine of the chef-patron, as well as husband, Andrea Sarri: the extraordinary quality of the ingredients, indicated by seasonality and sourced from the Ligurian Sea, as well as vegetables and sprouts grown in organic gardens, give rise to original proposals such as the vertical of raw food or the shellfish of Oneglia casserole with aromatic herbs. The desserts also appear to be really interesting, including a must-try hazelnut crunch, salted caramel, mango compote and passion fruit sorbet.

Name: Schöneck
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: With over 30 years’ experience behind them, the Baumgartner brothers’ restaurant is an excellent choice for classic specialities from the Alto Adige, offering a menu that focuses on regional dishes yet also includes a few fish-based options. The most important feature here is that all specialities are made from top-quality ingredients (often locally sourced), prepared by chef Karl with an expertise that ignores modern trends and passing fashions. Meals are served in rooms that are elegantly decorated with local wood, including a beautiful lounge space with a piano in front of the bar, Stube-style dining rooms and a veranda, while in summer the cool, shady terrace is particularly appealing. Last but not least, the excellent wine list is as impressive as the cuisine.

Name: Sciabola
Address: Via XX Settembre 28, Forte dei Marmi, 55042, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Inside the elegant St. Mauritius hotel, chef Alessandro Ferrarini, supported by a trusted team, creates colorful, delicious, and balanced dishes using impeccable, often local ingredients. These are available in both tasting menus and à la carte. The focus is mainly on seafood (we especially remember the anchovy butter ravioli with bread and raisins, and the Mediterranean-style sea bass with cherry tomatoes, olives, and capers), but there are also various land-based options. Service is led by an experienced maître who coordinates a young and cheerful team.

Name: Sensi
Description: All five senses will be satisfied by a visit to the gourmet restaurant of the Hotel Residence. Housed in a splendid 18C palazzo just a few metres from the famous cathedral, the restaurant boasts an interior design which combines modern and functional features with the building’s classic look, using a colour scheme which is typical of the Amalfi Coast. Although the cuisine focuses mainly on Mediterranean fish and seafood, the menu also features a few meat specialities.

Name: Senso Lake Garda Alfio Ghezzi
Address: Via IV Novembre 86, Limone sul Garda, 25010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: We recommend arriving early at this restaurant housed within the “EALA – My Lakeside Dream” hotel so that you can admire the spectacular daytime views of the lake through the floor-to-ceiling windows in the two dining rooms. Here, Alfio Ghezzi creates two tasting menus (from which dishes can be chosen à la carte style) which celebrate the region, starting with a focus on freshwater fish. His unmistakeable style results in dishes that are elegant and occasionally minimalist (but not simple), while avoiding unnecessary frills so that the flavours of the superb ingredients shine through.

Name: Serrae Villa Fiesole
Address: Via Fra' Giovanni da Fiesole detto l'Angelico 35, Fiesole, 50014, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within a historic villa now transformed into the FH55 boutique hotel, this restaurant stands out for its contemporary, light-filled interiors, with an open kitchen directed by the chef and his team. Through the large picture windows and from the summer terrace, a captivating view of Florence unfolds below. The gastronomic proposal draws deep roots from Italian tradition, with evident Tuscan resonance, expressed in a creative key across meat, fish, and a sound vegetarian selection. A carefully curated wine list, alongside a cocktail offering, completes the experience.

Name: Shalai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Choose from four tasting menus at this restaurant, including one which changes depending on the chef’s inspiration and another which focuses on fish and seafood, all of which feature dishes that can also be chosen à la carte style. We particularly enjoyed the creamy Provola cheese risotto with lemon, wild herbs and black truffles, and the lemon dessert which made a fitting conclusion to our memorable dinner.

Name: Signum
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Having grown up in the world of Signum, Martina Caruso has transformed her family’s legacy into a personal vision: after training away from the island, she returned to Salina and now leads a team of nine, while her brother Luca oversees hospitality at the elegant establishment. In the kitchen, he interprets the local area with a contemporary sensitivity, making the most of produce from the vegetable garden and the sea, and playing with balance and flavour without distorting the nature of the ingredients. There are three tasting menus: Sigillo (9 or 12 courses) featuring the chef’s signature dishes, Oltremare – an eight-course menu dedicated to aged fish – a vegetarian menu and à la carte options. The wine cellar, with over 1,500 wines, stands out for its breadth and international outlook.

Name: Silene
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In a tiny village at the foot of Mount Amiata, chef-patron Roberto Rossi captivates his guests within elegant and relaxed settings, offering decidedly Tuscan cuisine meticulously prepared, consolidating classic cooking techniques that reveal the fragrant flavour of prime materials. Moreover, when in season, the chef’s own garden plays a principal role in the menu (it’s a pleasure to visit and admire its “design”): excellent pigeon ravioli, alongside bread—which is among the chef’s passions—and a steadfast presence of fish dishes. The entire menu is seasoned with the chef's own Evo oil produced using olives from Seggiano.

Name: Sine by Di Pinto
Description: One of Italy’s greatest culinary traditions, that of Campania, is brought to life in this restaurant in an extraordinary way, not only through its many dishes but also through the extensive selection of breads served from a trolley. A Neapolitan – though he has been living in Milan for several years – Roberto Di Pinto has not forgotten his roots and offers some of the best-known Neapolitan classics, with a contemporary twist, alongside more creative dishes and a few international influences, as well as a vegetarian menu featuring vegetables from his own vegetable patch in the Oltrepò Pavese.

Name: Sintesi
Description: A refined and elegant restaurant where the modern atmosphere of the dining room may be far removed from the familiar image of the fraschette (the traditional taverns of Castelli Romani), yet the dishes of Matteo Compagnucci and Sara Scarsella represent one of the most accomplished and convincing expressions of cooking in the area. Centred on produce – whether local, such as cave-grown cardoncelli mushrooms, lake fish and herbs gathered from the hills, or ingredients from the sea and elsewhere – the result, enhanced in certain dishes by an effective use of the grill, is of a very high standard. The dining-room service also deserves praise.

Name: Sissi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: As you cross the threshold into this restaurant, you come into an elegant Art Nouveau-style dining room with sparkling chandeliers, patterned flooring and other fascinating retro details that make this a real gem. Owner-chef Andrea Fenoglio is the heart and soul of Sissi, dividing his time between the kitchen and front of house so that he can take time to chat with guests. His cuisine has solid classic foundations with a contemporary and personalised touch, and a good choice of dishes on the à la carte, plus a tasting menu (“Settepiatti”) which changes every year (as does the ceramic tableware on which it is served!). The cuisine is comforting and full of generous flavours, yet also creative and always surprising with elegant presentation and unusual combinations. Whatever dish you choose, you can be sure of finding the perfect wine pairing for your meal thanks to friendly, knowledge sommelier Arianna, who will be happy to make recommendations from the wine list.

Name: Spinechile
Address: Contra' Pacche 2, località Tretto, Schio, 36015, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: We recommend allowing plenty of time to get to this restaurant, which is accessed via a winding uphill road that can’t be rushed. However, the journey is more than compensated by the romantic dining room housed in an old rustic mountain building. The entrance is through the old stables, while the dining room itself occupies the first floor of an old hay barn, where a large floor-to-ceiling window boasts views of the valley, especially from the closest tables (there are only four tables in total, plus a small private room). At the helm in the kitchen, chef Corrado Fasolato, who has plenty of experience in Michelin-starred restaurants, conjures up creative, regionally influenced dishes with his customary enthusiasm.

Name: Storie d'Amore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This small, welcoming restaurant in the province of Padova is run by its two owners, one at the helm in the kitchen, the other overseeing the warm and beautifully decorated dining room. The cuisine is complex and elaborate rather than minimalist, with chef Davide Filippetto either creating different dishes from the same ingredient or preparing different ingredients in imaginative combinations. An abundant and generous menu, which includes an extensive wine list.

Name: Stube Hermitage
Address: Via Castelletto Inferiore 69, Madonna di Campiglio, 38086, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: In a quiet and secluded location, inside the Biohotel Hermitage, the restaurant occupies an early twentieth-century stube: a wooden treasure chest with few tables, where you can be lulled into an evening of romance and haute cuisine, offered through three tasting menus. In the chef’s dedicated menu, Domenico Sepe brings his Ischian roots to Trentino, introducing seafood ingredients sometimes paired with meat. This talented young chef proves equally at ease embracing Trentino tradition, as demonstrated in the Cena in Famiglia menu. Vegetarian enthusiasts, meanwhile, will opt for the Cappuccetto Verde menu.

Name: Suinsom
Address: Strada Puez 12, Selva di Val Gardena, 39048, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: In Ladin, Suinsom means “at the top” and this is a name that alludes not only to the position but also to the summit of a sophisticated gastronomic journey. In two welcoming stube clad in light-coloured wood, guests discover gourmet cuisine with a polished Mediterranean accent, enriched by international influences. In addition to dishes that honour the chef's Tuscan roots, the menu features recipes with a distinctly Mediterranean flavour, such as the delicate citrus-infused yellowtail sashimi with caviar and dandelion, or the lobster with Jerusalem artichoke cream, foie gras and caviar beurre blanc. The wine list, carefully organised by grape variety, offers a wide and interesting selection ranging from the finest Italian labels to prestigious international wines, adding the finishing touch to a truly exquisite dining experience.

Name: Tancredi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Having trained with Antonino Cannavacciuolo, young chef Vincenzo Manicone has, with his wife Sara, embarked on a new venture in this elegant restaurant with a glass-fronted dining room and a terrace suspended between the lake and the sky. Showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte, the chef’s cuisine demonstrates a maturity that pays close attention to colour and flavour, with beautifully presented dishes prepared from top-quality, well-balanced ingredients. Also evident is the aim, currently in vogue, of reducing food waste by using every single part of the animal (as in the case of the excellent amberjack, curly salad and sea urchin dish that we very much enjoyed). In summer, we recommend requesting a table at the front of the terrace, right over the lake.

Name: Taverna del Capitano
Address: Piazza delle Sirene 10/11, Marina del Cantone, 80061, Italy
Description: A series of hairpin bends leads up to Marina del Cantone, a picturesque bay on the Sorrento Peninsula, framed by crystal-clear waters and the silhouette of the Tre Pizzi. This is where the Taverna del Capitano is located, a long-established local restaurant offering two different dining experiences. On the lower floor, in the areas dedicated to Casa Caputo, you’ll find a more traditional and unpretentious cuisine, while the gourmet restaurant is situated on the building’s rooftop, offering a splendid view of the beach and the sea, accompanied by the constant sound of the waves in the background. In the open-plan kitchen, Matteo Caputo, supported by his father Alfonso’s expertise, showcases locally caught fish through a menu that is distinctly Mediterranean and true to its roots, with the occasional foray into the world of meat. You can tailor your experience by choosing from a selection of tasting menus – including one dedicated to lobster – or by selecting from a comprehensive menu that reflects the restaurant’s philosophy. The wine list is also of an excellent standard – extensive and well-organised – while in the dining room, the family’s new generation of women is helping to revitalise a tradition of hospitality that is one of the restaurant’s key strengths.

Name: Terrazza Bosquet
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: In the heart of Sorrento, a magnificent garden leads, like an elegant avenue, to the Excelsior Vittoria, one of the most iconic and prestigious hotels on the Sorrento Peninsula. Here, weather permitting, the tables of the gourmet restaurant are set out on a spectacular panoramic terrace overlooking the Gulf of Naples and the sunsets along the coast; alternatively, the experience continues in the elegant dining rooms inside. In the kitchen, Antonino Montefusco offers a range of tasting menus, including one dedicated to plant-based cuisine, in which ingredients and traditions from Campania are reinterpreted with a contemporary sensitivity and great attention to presentation. The quality of the raw ingredients is brought to the fore through meticulous preparation and combinations that are anything but run-of-the-mill, while maintaining the generous portions of the dishes. Among the most impressive dishes, the red mullet served in a ‘tortiera’ with marinated red onion and green beans stands out, but the lavish selection of amuse-bouches that kicks off the dining experience is also unforgettable. To round off the experience, there is a particularly extensive wine list, with a remarkable selection of wines also available by the glass.

Name: Tilia
Description: This glass and steel cube in the middle of the garden of the former Grand Hotel in Dobbiaco has been home to the Tilia restaurant since 2010 and is now more intimate than ever, with just five tables and seating for 12 diners (booking is highly recommended). Chef Chris Oberhammer’s menu is enticing, featuring just under 20 dishes with a modern yet regional flavour. Many of the ingredients (such as the flour and some of the meat) are sourced from the “Klaude” farm which is run by one of the chef’s childhood friends with whom he works very closely, while other more exotic fare comes from further afield, adding luxury ingredients such as caviar, truffles (in season) and prawns to the mix. Anita Mancini oversees the front of house with skill and professionalism, as well as taking care of the wine list which includes a selection of international labels.

Name: Tivoli
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Along the road leading to the Falzarego Pass, at the foot of the Tofane mountains, in a typical Alpine house just outside the town centre, Graziano Prest offers a wide range of dishes ranging from traditional mountain fare to more creative creations, featuring both meat and fish, with a particular flair that is also evident in the desserts, as well as a vegetarian menu. An extraordinary selection of wines: the cellar houses more than 1,300 wines from leading producers, historic vintages and superb French wines of the very highest quality. The panoramic terrace offers picture-postcard views of the centre of Cortina – the same view that can be admired from inside, provided you book one of the two sought-after tables by the window well in advance.

Name: Trattoria Zappatori
Description: Beyond the porticoes, a secluded courtyard leads to an early twentieth-century building that now houses a historic trattoria, transformed by chef Christian Milone into a restaurant of refined elegance. Its original features have been intelligently preserved and enhanced by contemporary touches, creating a harmonious dialogue between past and present. At carefully laid tables, almost tailored in their precision, the culinary offering unfolds through two distinct routes: on the one hand, the “1975… le mie origini” menu, which revisits Piedmontese roots with balance and understated imagination; on the other, “Materie Prime”, a freer expression of creativity in which individual ingredients become the focus of entire tasting experiences. Particular attention is paid to the provenance of the produce, much of it coming from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden or from carefully selected local suppliers. For a more immersive experience, a chef’s table overlooking the kitchen is also available.

Name: Trattoria al Cacciatore - La Subida
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the heart of Collio, among gentle hills just steps from the Slovenian border, this restaurant stands as a true gastronomic ambassador of the territory, celebrating tradition with consistency and warm hospitality in relaxing surroundings where time seems to slow down. The menu embraces the most authentic cuisine – the zlikrofi, potato-and-chive-filled tortelli served with pan juices and shavings of aged Montasio are emblematic – alongside more contemporary interpretations, such as an elegant, restrained squab presented in two services. The carefully curated cellar tells the story of the land through an almost climate-based organization of labels, enriched by numerous reserves and captivating vertical selections.

Name: Trattoria contemporanea
Description: A young team led by talented chef Davide Marzullo surprises guests with modern techniques and cuisine, offering dishes that showcase both national and international flavours and combinations, including a completely vegetarian - Istinto - menu, including a not-to-be-missed risotto with goat's milk, capers, liquorice and soya. At lunchtime, the menu is lighter, but you can also enjoy à la carte specialities and three tasting menus (with varying numbers of courses). The industrial redevelopment of a former cotton mill provides a fitting backdrop for all this energy.

Name: Trattoria da Amerigo
Description: In the foothills just beyond Bologna, Amerigo celebrates the idea of the traditional Italian trattoria, taking us on a nostalgic journey into the past that is part of our collective memory. It is situated just a few metres from the village’s main square and also has a shop, should you wish to take home a culinary souvenir from the area (wines, sauces and other delicacies). A number of function rooms – including what was once the town’s first TV lounge – each one more charming than the last, featuring period memorabilia and a pleasantly informal atmosphere. Alberto Bettini is in charge of the whole operation, offering an extraordinary selection of the produce and recipes of the area. Savigno is famous for its truffles, so mushrooms, but it also boasts one of the most remarkable selections of cured meats (the long-cured prosciutto is exceptional), obviously a variety of fresh pasta dishes, ranging from tortellini in old hen’s stock to tagliatelle with ragù, as well as tigelle, with the main courses consisting chiefly of meat and a range of delicious desserts.

Name: Tre Olivi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: At the Savoy Hotel & Spa, in the heart of Cilento, a culinary experience is taking shape that combines contemporary elegance with a deep connection to the local area. The offering comprises tasting menus and a menu that showcases local specialities, many of which come from the establishment’s own farm. The ingredients, flavours and traditions of the Cilento region and the Mediterranean diet are reinterpreted with a modern sensitivity, giving rise to well-balanced dishes that are simple in appearance yet rich in character. One of the most interesting new features is a sophisticated room with its own kitchen, designed for private events and bespoke dinners. In the dining room, attentive and professional service enhances the experience with discretion and care, helping to create a warm and relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Umberto a Mare
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In a spectacular setting beneath the Church of Soccorso, with breathtaking sunset views over the sea, Umberto rises to match such natural beauty with elegant, contemporary Campanian cuisine. The tasting menu Sogno di una Notte di Mezza Estate (A Midsummer Night’s Dream) dazzles with the signature Gioco di Mare dish, while the dessert selection is equally memorable. Don’t miss the grouper tortelli or the daily catch, prepared with modern techniques. The visitable wine cellar houses over 1,500 labels, featuring exceptional Champagnes, great French classics, and outstanding German Rieslings. Special praise goes to the young sommelier-owner, whose passionate and precise recommendations enhance the entire experience.

Name: Un Piano nel Cielo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: An atmospheric panoramic lift leads from the Casa Angelina hotel to the restaurant: in good weather you can dine on a terrace, by candlelight and with a breathtaking view of the Coast. Leopoldo Elefante's cuisine is Mediterranean and largely dedicated to the sea, although there is never a shortage of excellent meat specialities. Not to be missed is his “soufflé alla pastiera”, a signature dish that combines an international dessert with typically Neapolitan flavours. Great care is given to presentation and the lighting uses various colours to accompany the guest through the different courses, changing in tone and intensity throughout the meal. The chef is well supported by the service, precise and friendly, and an important wine list. The wine cellar is around 1500 labels, with an incredible availability of large formats for connoisseurs.

Name: Une
Description: Situated in a hamlet of Foligno criss-crossed by springs and streams (UNE is the word for water in the old language of Umbria), this restaurant occupies a 17C mill. The dining room has retained all the rural and romantic charm of the original building, which was once used for the milling of cereals and later for the production of olive oil. Today, young chef Giulio Gigli brings a touch of modernity to the restaurant. Having gained experience working in Italy and abroad, he creates elaborate and personalised dishes from local produce, most of which is grown and raised within a 20km radius of the restaurant, as well as occasionally more exotic ingredients, showcasing his dishes on two tasting menus. The wine list follows the same philosophy as the cuisine, featuring local labels alongside bottles from elsewhere in Italy and further afield which are sourced from small wineries with a focus on organic, biodynamic and natural wines.

Name: Vecchia Malcesine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Situated at the entrance to the old town, the restaurant is fronted by a small but delightful garden of olive trees, from which you enter the dining room, which overlooks the rooftops of Malcesine, the lake and the opposite shore – an enchanting view. In the kitchen, Leandro Luppi creates delicious, flavourful dishes, with a range of options centred on freshwater fish – but that’s not all. Some are particularly creative – his ‘carbonara di lago’ is famous – while the presentation is sure to be remembered for its attention to detail and elegance.

Name: Vecchio Ristoro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre, this charming 17th-century former mill welcomes guests into an atmosphere that evokes the essence of the most authentic mountain life. The original features, such as the millstone and the old wheel, blend elegantly with the refined surroundings and attentive service, orchestrated by Paolo Bariani, a partner in the establishment and a passionate wine connoisseur. With a range of over 300 wines, many of which are also available by the glass, the wine cellar offers a well-balanced selection that combines renowned wines with interesting niche productions. In the kitchen, from spring 2026, Tommaso Lupo will be taking over the reins under the supervision of Filippo Oggioni, who will continue to oversee the project while embarking on a new professional venture in Lombardy. The culinary offering remains firmly rooted in the flavours of the Aosta Valley, reinterpreted with a contemporary sensitivity and enriched by elegant nods to the neighbouring French tradition. There is no shortage of original combinations of land and sea, such as free-range chicken and blue lobster in a fricassee. The dishes are available as part of various tasting menus, including a vegetarian option, or à la carte, depending on inspiration and the quality of the day’s market produce.

Name: Venissa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Far away from the tourist hordes, Venissa is situated in a small walled vineyard dating back to the Middle Ages – complete with 14C belltower – on the small island of Mazzorbo, a magical setting which is perfect for a short stroll before settling down to eat. In addition to the Dorona di Venezia vineyard, the restaurant also has a kitchen garden which provides most of its vegetables, including unusual varieties such as “castraure”, a type of local artichoke. Once out of the garden, you come to a small wooden bridge which links Mazzorbo to neighbouring Burano, where you can complete your visit to the lagoon by exploring the lacemakers’ shops and admiring the colourful local houses. The main focus here, however, is the cuisine – and excellent cuisine it is too! Chefs Chiara Pavan and Francesco Brutto describe their dishes as “ambientale” (environmental) because of the close connection between the lagoon and the Upper Adriatic: the menu features plenty of fish and vegetables and almost no meat. Guests choose their number of courses and the dishes come as a surprise, accompanied by organic wine pairings. At the Osteria Contemporanea next door the dishes are simpler but still full of flavour.

Name: Veritas
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: At the first terrace leading up to Vomero, with the comfort of paid parking just steps away, an intimate, captivating venue awaits, where warm décor meets impeccable dining room service. The sommelier, with grace and discretion, guides guests through intriguing labels, unveiling small regional producers and sparking curiosity with every recommendation. In the kitchen, the approach turns refined: several tasting menus or the option to order à la carte from the Essenziale and Autentico offerings. Particularly appealing is the Formula Funky, three surprise courses from the chef reserved for under-35s, an invitation to discovery. Marco Caputi interprets the territory with elegance, exalting Campanian flavors and beyond in delicate, chromatically perfect compositions. Among the creations that leave their mark: spaghetti with smoked butter, clams, pine nuts, and lemon: a bold balance of sweet and savory, and the amberjack with celeriac, bay leaf, and helichrysum, releasing intense aromas and vegetal notes.

Name: Vescovado
Description: For many years, the Ricchebuono family has been a leading name in hospitality and catering in the area, thanks to its high-quality cuisine and a warm welcome where each detail is taken care of. Today, this tradition is being carried on thanks to the contribution of the new generation: their children, Martina and Elia, work alongside their parents, both driven by a deep passion for the trade. At the heart of the experience is Giuseppe Ricchebuono, a chef of proven sensitivity and technical rigour, who is able to showcase the very best of the area’s produce through simple yet elegant dishes. Great attention is paid to seafood from Noli, which is also listed on the menu by its dialect names: ‘cicetta’, for example, refers to monkfish. In the dining room, alongside her mother, Martina expertly manages an extensive wine list divided into three sections dedicated respectively to Liguria, international wines and wines by the glass. Elia, on the other hand, guides guests through the cheese trolley, which is dedicated to regional produce. During the summer months, service moves to the picturesque terrace overlooking the small bay of Noli, offering a truly enchanting view. Set against a backdrop of extraordinary beauty, nestled between the sea and the Mediterranean scrub, the Bishop’s Palace stands as an important testament to the local historical and architectural heritage. Rounding off the property’s facilities is L’Orto del Vescovado, an outdoor area surrounded by greenery which, during the milder months, welcomes guests for aperitifs and moments of relaxation in the open air.

Name: Vespasia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just a short walk from the Basilica of San Benedetto, which was rebuilt after the earthquake, the restaurant is situated within the elegant Palazzo Seneca hotel. A series of dining rooms leads to the elegant Vespasia dining room, where chef Fabio Cappiello makes use of Umbrian culinary specialities – olive oil, cured meats, lentils, Cannara onions, river prawns and fish, lamb from the Sibillini Mountains and, of course, the finest black truffles (extraordinary with umbricelli) – to create innovative and enticing dishes. At least twenty-four hours before your meal, you choose what you’d like to eat from the à la carte dishes or the tasting menus (Vespasia, Terra, Acqua, Orto), before indulging in a superb dinner in the heart of this gem of a town.

Name: Vignamare
Address: Strada Castello, 20 - Colla Micheri, Andora, 17051, Italy
Description: At Vignamare, a new chapter unfolds: two chefs at the helm, a clearly recognisable local identity and a cuisine that weaves together agricultural production and contemporary sensitivity. From Andora, the road climbs the hill through a series of hairpin bends leading to the car park; from there, a few steps on foot bring guests to the restaurant entrance, while the landscape already sets the tone for the experience: vineyards overlooking the sea, olive groves and maritime pines sketch one of Liguria’s most luxuriant views. The project was born from the restoration of a 1970s cistern, unused for decades and now transformed into a fine-dining venue. When the weather allows, the panoramic terrace becomes the true stage; otherwise, a modern wood-clad dining room welcomes guests in a warm, contemporary atmosphere. The gastronomic offering is structured around two tasting menus, of seven and nine courses respectively, alongside an entirely “green” menu. The technique is clear and well defined, with a language rooted in the Mediterranean and showcasing regional produce of excellent quality, much of it from the gardens and livestock of PEQ Agri, the agricultural enterprise underpinning the project. On the upper levels there is also a more informal offering, ideal for a cocktail or a light stop, with an incomparable view and a particularly pleasant atmosphere on warm summer days.

Name: Villa Maiella
Address: Via Sette Dolori 30, Località Villa Maiella, Guardiagrele, 66016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Since 1966, the Tinari family has been showcasing Abruzzo through its cuisine. Situated at the foot of Mount Maiella, the restaurant is now run by two generations: mum Angela and her son Arcangelo in the kitchen, and Peppino and his son Pascal in the dining room. The menu features the finest produce of the area, selected in keeping with the time of year, with a special focus on the black pigs reared on the family farm and the cured meats made from them. The region’s culinary traditions and the wealth of knowledge passed down by their parents form the basis of a cuisine that the Tinari brothers continue to develop with sensitivity and personality. The wine cellar is also impressive, housing over a thousand wines and offering a wide selection by the glass. Finally, in the warmer months, guests can take a seat on the magnificent panoramic terrace overlooking the stunning hills, where the charm of the landscape blends harmoniously with elegant and captivating cuisine.

Name: Villa Naj
Description: Now housed within Tenuta Riccagioia (the region’s agricultural research facility), two elegant and modern dining rooms with large windows overlook the internal courtyard directly. The chef’s cuisine aims to be territorial, though it willingly wanders along the peninsula with excellent lamb culurgiones. Additionally, there’s Sicilian extra virgin olive oil from Castelvetrano, outstanding bread service, and intriguing desserts. Among the must-tries is certainly the local duck, flavored with rhubarb, wild garlic cream, and coffee jus, prepared in traditional fashion. Wine is a beautiful chapter unto itself, with Oltrepò Pavese standing out in both quality and quantity, while the rest of Italy and international selections are carefully balanced to complement the cuisine. The evening atmosphere is relaxing with soft lighting and excellent service.

Name: Vineria Modì
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Hidden down a quiet lane in the historic centre, this restaurant offers an intimate and romantic atmosphere. The modern and pared-back interiors are complemented by a handful of outdoor tables set along an evocative alleyway, lit by soft lighting. At the stove is Dalila Grillo who, after significant professional experience elsewhere, has returned to her homeland to run the family restaurant alongside her brother. Her cuisine is distinguished by a remarkable attention to detail and a refined aesthetic sensitivity, as demonstrated by the antipasto dedicated to red prawn, in which elegance of presentation and balance of flavours merge harmoniously. The offering comprises two six-course tasting menus – Ease and Creativity, dedicated to seasonality, and Timeless, which gathers the chef's signature dishes – alongside the option of choosing à la carte. Born as a pub and wine bar, the restaurant has kept its vocation for wine intact: the list, with over 1,600 carefully selected labels, is brought to life by the expertise of the front-of-house team. Given the limited number of covers and the success of the restaurant, booking is essential.

Name: Vintage 1997
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: A classic of the Turin dining scene for nearly thirty years, this venue continues to stand out for its rare consistency, unmoved by passing trends. The interiors, intentionally somewhat old-fashioned – though recently refreshed and perfectly in keeping with the Vintage name – frame the welcome of owner Umberto Chiodi Latini, a maître d’ of great personality and old-school charm. In the kitchen, the offerings have expanded over the years without ever compromising on ingredient quality: notable, for instance, is the attention devoted to vegetables, honored with an entire tasting menu. Alongside indispensable Piedmontese classics – from vitello tonnato in its traditional version, roasted and without mayonnaise, to tajarin – well-crafted vegetarian dishes find their place, such as Sinestesia, a medley of vegetables with citronette and acacia honey, as well as an ever-expanding selection of seafood. The wine list, finally, features compelling verticals from various Langhe producers and beyond, confirming a solid, knowledgeable approach.

Name: Vitantonio Lombardo
Address: Via Madonna delle Virtù 13/14, Matera, 75100, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: The story of this restaurant captures the most authentic essence of the spirit of Matera: an ancient abandoned grotto has been transformed, through a demanding work of restoration, into an elegant dining room that today stands as one of the city’s foremost gastronomic venues. We find ourselves in the very heart of Sassi, and it is practically obligatory to take the time for a stroll through the alleyways of one of the most evocative historic centres in Italy, above all after dinner on an evening visit, when the night lighting gives it all an intense and deeply moving atmosphere, particularly from the belvedere of Piazza Duomo. In the kitchen, the chef demonstrates a profound bond with the territory, frequently drawing upon Lucanian recipes and ingredients that are nevertheless reinterpreted with great expressive freedom, giving rise to results that are both personal and creative. The gastronomic offering is broad and articulated: alongside the most established dishes, new creations find their place, allowing the guest to compose their own tasting journey freely across five, seven or ten courses. The experience may be further enriched by a carefully considered wine pairing, chosen with expertise and sensitivity by the accomplished and professional maître sommelier Donato.

Name: Volta del Fuenti by Michele De Blasio
Address: SS 163 Amalfitana km 47,300, Vietri sul Mare, 84019, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Once past Vietri sul Mare on the way to the Amalfi Coast, the Giardini del Fuenti overlook the sea from a spectacular vantage point, stretching between the beach, terraced gardens and the Riva Restaurant, which is open just for lunch and often hosts events dedicated to food and wine. The dining room, featuring large windows that frame one of the coast’s most picturesque landscapes, offers the ideal setting for a culinary experience that draws on the traditions of Campania with a contemporary twist. The kitchen reinterprets local recipes and flavours through carefully crafted, simple dishes, with a particular focus on the quality of the ingredients. The experience can be tailored through a range of tasting itineraries, including a more comprehensive, themed one. Among the highlights of the meal were the sumptuous welcome canapés – with a special mention for the now-famous ‘asinello vietrese’ – and dishes of great balance, such as the veal sweetbreads with citrus fruits, walnuts and rocket.

Name: Votavota
Address: Lungomare Andrea Doria 48, Marina di Ragusa, 97010, Italy
Description: A painting for sea lovers, admired in all its splendour through the dining room’s floor-to-ceiling windows. Behind guests, the open kitchen hosts two chefs – Giuseppe Causarano and Antonio Colombo – who create dishes of surprising quality and creativity, where fresh catch naturally takes center stage. Among the standouts that won us over: smoked spaghetti with butter and anchovies, a dish of exceptional creaminess, aromatics, and intensity. Seemingly simple, it demonstrates excellent technique and is worth the journey alone! On the wine front, let Benito, the sommelier, be your guide on a journey through Sicilian labels – from Etna to the smaller islands – as well as the rest of Italy and beyond, with excellent selections and some fine by-the-glass options.

Name: Wistèria
Address: Fondamenta del Forner, Sestiere San Polo 2908, Venice, 30125, Italy
Description: Nestled along the Rio de la Frescada, one of the numerous tranquil lateral canals, the modest entrance of Wisteria opens directly onto the outdoor area, enlivened by the eponymous wisteria under whose shade several tables are arranged when the season permits. Wisteria delights guests with dishes attuned to the seasonality of ingredients and the diverse offerings of the region: contemporary Venice’s gastronomic landscape through six or eight-course tasting menus. Highly recommended is the dessert with pumpkin, licorice, and almonds.

Name: Wood
Address: Via Guido Rey 26, Breuil Cervinia, 11021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: PLEASE NOTE: temporarily closedThe talented chef Amanda Eriksson, in the centre of Breuil-Cervinia, at an altitude of two thousand metres, pursues her vision of cuisine – which blends Swedish and Italian influences – with conviction and style. Hailing from northern Sweden, she captivates with a menu featuring creative recipes that alternate – and sometimes combine – ingredients from both countries: elk tartare wrapped in beetroot ravioli with horseradish sauce, alongside cauliflower cooked in butter like an escalope and topped with smoked fontina. The wine list, on the other hand, curated by partner Cristian Scalco, features excellent wines, including some rare vintages, and offers a good selection by the glass.

Name: Zash
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Once through the entrance gate, make your way through an orchard planted with citrus trees to get to this restaurant occupying a charming, carefully restored 19C “palmento” (a building once used for fermenting wine) that has retained its magical and romantic atmosphere. Here, Giuseppe Raciti’s top-quality cuisine is showcased on themed tasting menus from which dishes can also be chosen à la carte. His dishes put Sicily centre stage, as does the excellent wine list, with specialities which the chef reinterprets in impressive, modern style. For us, the charcoal-grilled tuna ventresca with smoked aubergines, grapefruit, red onion and teriyaki sauce was particularly memorable.

Name: Zass
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: The legendary San Pietro hotel is one of the world's most celebrated, the jewel of Positano and the Amalfi Coast. Within its illustrious walls lies this restaurant whose tremendous success (book considerably in advance is advised), aside from its undoubtedly enchanting location, owes much to the expertise of Belgian Chef Alois Vanlangenaeker, who has been here for over 20 years. His cuisine harmoniously and elegantly narrates the strength, fragrances, and flavours of the Mediterranean, primarily using the Campanian language that remains pure in tradition as the meal begins with a freshly baked Margherita pizza, gradually enriched by pleasant creative notes within the dishes. The property's organic garden is increasingly making its presence felt in a menu of both land and, predominantly, sea-focused options. The emblematic San Pietro dish is a masterpiece, lemon scented and accompanied by buffalo yogurt potato puree, seasonal vegetables, and the house’s renowned Champagne and truffle sauce. Opting not to take the lift to the main hall is recommended—instead, treat yourself to a spectacular descent through gardens, statues, and mesmerizing vistas of one of Italy’s most famous hotels.

Name: Zia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: A young chef of undisputed talent is the driving force behind this discreet restaurant, hidden away behind the busier, more touristy streets of Trastevere. We are speaking of Antonio Ziantoni and his cuisine: creative, yet always governed by rigour and restraint, and built on solid classic foundations. Through precise and delicate technical steps, ingredients of outstanding quality are transformed into dishes that are generous and well balanced, capable of delivering full, rounded and deeply satisfying flavours. A telling example? Quail with sage and carnation flowers. The cellar is equally accomplished, presented with passion, as is the service: knowledgeable and cordial, completing an experience of rare charm.

Name: Zunica 1880 a Villa Corallo
Description: The historic Zunica 1880 – and the numbers don’t lie – is reborn within Villa Corallo, an imposing resort and landed estate. Guest rooms are in the main villa, while the restaurant occupies what was once the farm equipment building. Two vegetable gardens, crop cultivation, raising of calves and pigs, plus a new garden and pool, primarily used for weddings and events. The cuisine of Gianni Dezio, an Abruzzo native from Atri and student of Niko Romito, already operates at a high level through two tasting menus – at the chef’s discretion – or à la carte. His stylistic signature is a judicious, targeted use of a few ingredients, many of them estate‑produced, each with its own value and precise effect. The result: dishes that are aesthetically refined – now essential at this level – but above all designed to deliver flavor and pleasure, drawing inspiration from both local traditions and the chef’s imagination. Overseeing it all is the discreet, understated presence of owner Daniele, a charismatic figure in Abruzzo dining.

Name: Zur Rose
Address: Via Josef Innerhofer 2, San Michele, 39057, Italy
Description: A gourmet landmark along the romantic South Tyrolean Wine Road, Zur Rose leaves a lasting impression. In this historic house, chef Herbert Hintner, who has been working here side by side with his son Daniel for over five years, offers his idea of contemporary creativity with a strong Alto Adige regional identity. Daniel offers a seven‑course seasonal menu that deftly balances the restaurant’s long‑standing traditions with a fresh look at local cuisine. In the elegant 14th‑century dining space, where the name “La Rosa” has been associated with the restaurant since 1585, the offerings change with the seasons, and a vegetarian menu is also available. On the crest of the wave for decades, the cooking here has lost none of its appeal, continuing to make this an unmissable gastronomic stop.

Name: sui generis.
Description: A modern dining-room with an open-view kitchen where young Alfio Nicolosi can be observed at work, ably assisted by friendly and attentive staff front of house. When you book, you’ll be asked if you have any food allergies or intolerances, or any ingredients that you don’t like, as there is just one surprise tasting menu served here. The truly extraordinary dishes are inspired by the chef’s remarkable knowledge of culinary traditions from Italy and further afield (strong Asian and South American influences are obvious), resulting in highly personalised dishes. Nicolosi is one of the most interesting young chefs in Italy at the moment and his exciting cuisine is full of intense flavours, including grilled dishes with a hint of street food and other influences apparent throughout.

Name: 13 Comuni
Address: Piazza della Vittoria 31, Velo Veronese, 37030, Italy
Description: Situated in a pretty village square, this restaurant is reached by driving along picturesque mountain roads. Guests come to 13 Comuni to taste typical dishes from the Lessinia region, including lamb and Brogna mutton, as well as chicken, cheese and other delicious local specialities, all of which are rich and full of flavour.

Name: 53 Untitled
Address: Via del Monte della Farina 53, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: In the heart of historic Rome, just steps from Piazza Navona, this intimate establishment with its relaxed atmosphere offers cuisine of remarkable character. Seating is limited – reservations are recommended – and the menu alternates between Roman inspirations, such as dumplings filled with oxtail alla vaccinara, and more contemporary creations with Asian touches and global influences, including the standout Yucca Mooncake. New to the lineup are “morsi e morsetti” (bites and nibbles): small tapas-style portions conceived as appetizers or mini main courses, complemented by an offering of pastas, cured meats, cheeses, and desserts.

Name: Agritur El Mas
Address: Strada de Saslonch 176, località Col de Soldai, Moena, 38035, Italy
Description: Located above the village, this guesthouse is part of a real working farm with cows, horses and pigs, producing meat, charcuterie and cheese, not to mention seasonal vegetables from the kitchen garden. It goes without saying that the menu offers hearty mountain cuisine: the cheese dumplings with “crudo di Moena” cheese and spinach are excellent, as are the slow-cooked stews and braised dishes made with the farm’s own meat. Other local delicacies are also available, including Val di Fiemme char served with beetroot, chanterelle mushrooms and Trentodoc beurre blanc. The restaurant welcomes you into a delightful cosy, rustic setting, featuring antique wood furnishings and a brazier in the middle of the room. Built in compliance with the principles of “green” construction, the premises also offer comfortable guest rooms.

Name: Ahimè
Description: Situated near the Mercato delle Erbe (well worth a visit either before or after your meal), this restaurant changes its menu regularly, sometimes even daily, in order to guarantee the freshness of its farm-to-table ingredients. The simple cuisine features some delicious vegetarian dishes, including stand-out recipes such as fennel with coconut and green pepper sauce. Don’t miss the home-made bread, which is baked daily with great technical skill.

Name: Ai Burattini
Address: Via Madaschi 45, Adrara San Martino, 24060, Italy
Description: In the heart of town, yet with no parking difficulties, and slightly elevated above the lake – just a few kilometers away – stands one of the most reliable venues for exploring the local gastronomic tradition, both lake and land. The menu is an irresistible invitation, difficult to exhaust in a single sitting: from Bergamo’s giant sheep to delicate lake trout meatballs, from house-made casoncelli pasta to excellent roast rabbit, served with Rovetta polenta that pairs beautifully with a classic such as beef braised in olive oil. Alongside traditional desserts, a carefully curated selection of Bergamasque cheeses provides an ideal finale. Wine may be selected directly from the generous display of bottles or chosen with guidance from the owner, ever-present in the dining room with both expertise and warmth.

Name: Al Becco della Civetta
Description: In the pedestrian heart of this enchanting village, embraced by the Lucanian Dolomites, the kitchen here is run entirely by women and now in its third generation. Antonietta preserves the local recipes with passion: from peperoni cruschi to cavatelli with pezzente sausage, from local lamb to prized Podolica beef, as well as wild herbs, authentic cheeses, and cured meats. All in a softly lit dining room with large windows to enjoy the surrounding panorama.

Name: Al Bersagliere
Description: A classic, historic restaurant to which one returns time and again with great pleasure. No contrived or artificial creativity here, just traditional cooking that is reassuring and substantial. Among the must-try dishes: creamy whipped baccalà, pasta e fagioli, pastissada de caval, and, among the desserts, the diplomatico (prepared with pandoro and caramel).

Name: Al Borgo
Description: Housed within an 18C villa in a small traditional hamlet, this restaurant with a warm rustic ambience serves regional cuisine. The Gioie del Borgo (home produced salami and sausages), barley and bean soup, and homemade ice cream are all highly recommended.

Name: Al Cambio
Description: Situated off the usual tourist trail, Al Cambio serves authentic Bolognese cuisine (as well as other dishes) with a focus on traditional, seasonal meat and fish dishes. So if you’re looking for a genuinely local culinary experience, leave the city centre and allow chef Matteo Poggi to delight you with his cuisine. Don’t miss the guinea fowl breast with truffle-flavoured potatoes. The restaurant is often full, even at lunchtime, so booking ahead is highly recommended.

Name: Al Convento - Casa Torrente
Description: Following renovation work, the frescoed dining room at this restaurant now has the feel of a contemporary osteria, while its attractive terrace boasts tables overlooking the picturesque village’s small square. The menu focuses mainly on fish and seafood (although a few meat options such as tomahawk ribeye and steak also feature), including raw fish, tartares, fried anchovies stuffed with smoked provolone cheese, grilled dishes and pasta, including spaghetti with the local anchovy sauce. If you choose fish from the dry-ageing cabinet, you’ll add a little extra to your bill. The desserts are also excellent – don’t miss the shortcrust pastry tartlet with lemon cream, basil and soft meringue.

Name: Al Monastero
Address: Via Ristori 9, Cividale del Friuli, 33043, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In the heart of the old town, rustically charming dining rooms of varying sizes welcome guests with authentic warmth. Try booking the most intimate room, where the Friulian fogolar fireplace crackles and spreads the scent of embers, creating a homely atmosphere. On sunny days, the inner courtyard of the historic building becomes a pleasant refuge, bathed in soft light and silence interrupted only by the clinking of glasses. The all-female waiting staff are quick but attentive, with discreet smiles accompanying every course. The food reflects regional tradition with simplicity: classic cooking methods that bring out the best in the meat, intense aromas reminiscent of goose, a staple ingredient in authentic, comforting dishes.

Name: Al Palazzon
Address: Via Ca' Onorai 2, Loc. Mottinello Nuovo, Galliera Veneta, 35015, Italy
Description: Housed in an early 20C farmhouse, this restaurant boasts the typical ambience of a traditional multi-generational trattoria, while the cuisine focuses on classic dishes that are typical of the Veneto. Highlights include bigoli pasta, bean soup, Vicenza-style baccalà cod and mallard duck.

Name: Al Piave
Address: Via Cormons 6 - Fraz. Corona, Mariano del Friuli, 34070, Italy
Description: In a little village in the Friuli countryside, a family-run trattoria welcomes guests into two cosy dining rooms, connected by a charming stone fireplace that spreads warmth and the scent of wood. In summer, service moves outdoors, to a well-tended garden, where the murmur of the leaves accompanies the friendly atmosphere. The menu follows the seasons, bringing the region's authentic flavours to the table: succulent meats, aromas reminiscent of charcoal and, among the main courses, irresistible grilled dishes such as golden, fragrant lamb chops that convey all the flavour of tradition.

Name: Alla Pace
Address: Via Sauris di Sotto 38, Sauris, 33020, Italy
Description: Not the easiest place to reach unless you are already in the area, Sauris di Sotto is a picturesque mountain village, with houses that seem lifted from a fairytale. Here you’ll also find this restaurant, with its characteristically Alpine interior. The menu naturally celebrates the local territory, beginning with the area’s famous cured meats, an excellent frico of cheese and potatoes with polenta, and, of course, plenty of meat.

Name: Altavilla
Description: Situated in the upper part of town, surrounded by woods and vineyards, this simple, family-run restaurant is highly inviting. Salumi, meat and cheeses make a frequent appearance on the menu, together with dishes inspired by old regional recipes, such as chisciöi, sciatt and taroz. In summer, make the most of the beautiful panoramic terrace.

Name: Andrea
Address: Via Padre Giacinto 20, Palazzolo Acreide, 96010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A new venue, still in the historic centre of Palazzolo Acreide, but with the same philosophy as before for this restaurant, where chef Andrea Alì continues to serve cuisine deeply rooted in the Iblean region, accompanied by a warm and friendly welcome. The stars of the show are the produce of the Sicilian hinterland, showcased in harmony with the changing seasons: bread, homemade pasta and cakes, Palazzolo sausage, black truffles from the Iblei mountains, trout, black suckling pig and excellent local cheeses. A cuisine that blends tradition with a contemporary sensitivity, in the heart of a town renowned for its splendid Baroque architecture and the nearby Greek theatre.

Name: Angiolina
Address: Via Passariello 2, Località Marina di Pisciotta, Pisciotta, 84066, Italy
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the sea, at the far end of Marina di Pisciotta, this establishment, which has been in business since the late 1950s, welcomes guests to its pleasant, tree-lined outdoor terrace during the warmer months. The cuisine reflects the Cilento region’s seafaring tradition, showcasing the day’s catch through dishes that respect the time of year and the flavours of the region. The undisputed stars of the show are the Menaica anchovies, caught using an ancient selective technique and served in a variety of ways, from the classic ‘mbuttunate’ anchovies, stuffed with ricotta, to those prepared ‘alla scapece’. There is no shortage of other seafood specialities and dishes that combine produce from the coast with that from the hinterland.

Name: Antica Filanda
Address: SS 157, contrada Raviola, Capri Leone, 98070, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: Although the view from this restaurant takes in the sea and the mountains alike, it’s the latter that inspires the menu. It features inland specialities cooked with the best local ingredients. Suckling pig is a particular favourite, appearing in a number of different guises, including cured ham and meat sauces. The restaurant also offers new, welcoming guestrooms.

Name: Antica Locanda di Sesto
Address: Via Ludovica 1660, Loc. Sesto di Moriano, Ponte a Moriano, 55100, Italy
Description: Rooted firmly in history, this restaurant dates back to the end of the 14th century and is an authentic jewel, listed among Italy's “Historic Restaurants”. It still retains its vitality today, with cuisine honouring Tuscan peasant traditions, supported by a genuine philosophy: the owners also run an organic farm, producing wine, extra virgin olive oil and excellent vinegar. Specialities include “peposo” (stewed pork shin) with cannellini beans, while grilled meats are the undisputed stars when it comes to main courses. To fully experience the peaceful charm of the village, book one of the few outdoor tables well in advance: an experience that is well worth waiting for.

Name: Antica Osteria
Description: Situated in the centre of a beautiful little village in the Val di Sole, at the mouth of the Val di Peio and the foot of the Presanella mountains, this pleasant restaurant is divided into three small dining rooms with a charming mountain feel, plus a veranda with modern floor-to-ceiling windows. Every year, the food at this restaurant, prepared by one of the members of the family, improves in quality while retaining its focus on the region – the char (marinated in miso) and the venison loin are particularly good. The menu includes traditional recipes alongside more personalised dishes.

Name: Antica Trattoria Cattivelli
Address: Via Chiesa di Isola Serafini 2, Monticelli d'Ongina, 29010, Italy
Description: Antica Trattoria Cattivelli remains a safe haven for those who want to savour authentic Piacenza cuisine. Traditional aromas fill the dining room, inviting guests to taste dishes that tell local stories: pisarei e fasò, , soft pasta smothered in rich sauce, and suckling pork fillet, glazed with honey and mustard, which releases a perfect balance of sweet and spicy notes. Authentic flavours that alone are worth the trip!

Name: Antica Trattoria Gianna
Description: This delightful, long-established family trattoria, in business for over a century, has the motto “Chi mangium nustran” (“here we eat local”) in a demonstration of its commitment to cuisine from the Lower Po valley, although other Italian dishes also feature on the menu. At midday, choose from a selection of simple, delicious and reasonably priced homemade dishes, while in the evening just one single tasting menu, concluding with the dessert trolley, is served.

Name: Antica Trattoria La Toppa
Address: Via del Giglio 43, San Donato in Poggio, 50028, Italy
Description: A family-run trattoria, simple and unswayed by fashion, in the heart of a small medieval village of genuine charm. On the main street, in the warmer months, service moves outdoors to a convivial and informal setting. The culinary offering is rigorously Tuscan and land-based: the mixed crostini, ribollita, pici all’aglione and braised beef with vegetables are unmissable. At certain times of year, game also makes an appearance, with a wild boar stew not to be missed. To close, a caramel panna cotta that ranks among the finest in the area.

Name: Antica Trattoria da Miculan
Description: Behind the small building that houses the bustling village bar, popular with locals, lies the true soul of the restaurant: a dining room with classic charm, featuring a fireplace that spreads warmth and the scent of wood in winter. The chef-owner carefully selects Friulian and seasonal ingredients, turning them into dishes that showcase the local area. The menu alternates between fish dishes and authentic flavours like those that characterise rich and comforting tagliatelle with duck ragout or golden “frico” served with steaming polenta. Snails à la bourguignonne are always on the menu, releasing intense and inviting aromas and completing an experience that tastes of tradition and good company.

Name: Antica Trattoria la Grotta dal 1918
Address: Via Tignano 3, Loc. Mongardino Grotta, Sasso Marconi, 40037, Italy
Description: It takes a while to get here, along a road which wends its way through the hills, but the cuisine more than compensates for the journey. The food here is based on a careful choice of ingredients (including produce from the restaurant’s own farm) from as far away as the Apennines, with a few ingredients from elsewhere in Italy, with a focus on traditional recipes. Don’t miss the tortellini in brodo, or the game and truffles available in season.

Name: Antiche Sere
Description: This renowned osteria situated in a district off the tourist trail is run by attentive and friendly female staff. Its dishes have a regional focus – vitello tonnato, agnolotti and tajarin pasta, caponèt (stuffed cabbage rolls), bonet dessert etc – and are served in three small, simple and traditional dining rooms, one of which shares space with the bar. There’s also pleasant outdoor dining in the garden to the rear in summer. Due to its popularity, booking ahead is highly recommended!

Name: Antichi Sapori
Description: An extraordinary representation of rural Apulia, here you will find one of the region's gastronomic excellences.
