The array of mainly vegetable starters, the fresh pastas combined with extraordinary ragùs, the fabulous meats (especially the capocollo and sausage) and the desserts (especially the “quasi cassata”) live up to the name the restaurant has built up since opening in 1993. Often sold out, we recommend making a reservation, even well in advance.

Name: Apollonia
Address: Via Sant'Apollonia 3, Località Sirmiano Sopra, Nals, 39010, Italy
Description: Following a road that twists and turns uphill, surrounded at first by vineyards and fruit trees and then by woodland, you climb to an altitude of 900m to reach this restaurant run by the Geiser family, who have been serving simple yet delicious regional (and Italian) cuisine here for three generations. With a focus on seasonal ingredients from the Alto Adige, the menus feature specialities such as potato rosti with beetroot, baked pumpkin, broccoli and porcini mushroom cream, as well as home-made tarts and sorbets. The beautiful views take in Terlano in the middle of the valley and the majestic Dolomites (including Sciliar, Catinaccio and Latemar) in the distance.

Name: Azzighe • Osteria a metà
Description: Situated near the canals of Livorno’s historic centre, this restaurant has just one convivial and informal dining room. Here, the focus is on meat and fish dishes influenced by Livorno and further afield in Tuscany, as well as a few more creative options. The “cacciucchino” cappelletti pasta dish is inspired by the famous local fish soup, while the beef “francesina” main course is worth a special mention.

Name: Battaglino
Description: This restaurant run by an enthusiastic and friendly family (now joined by the fourth generation) has been serving traditional Piedmontese cuisine since 1919. The outdoor dining space is particularly charming when the wisteria is in bloom.

Name: Bistrot di Pescheria
Description: This attractive, contemporary-style bistro is the “low-cost” sibling of the Pescheria restaurant situated in a more upmarket location on Salerno’s seafront. Run by the same management, the bistro aims to serve simpler dishes at more modest prices yet with the same focus on freshness and attention to detail evident in its sister-restaurant. As a result, you’ll find options such as oily fish and local white prawns on the menu rather than oysters and caviar. Don’t miss the squid soup with nduja sausage, potato mousse and crispy bread.

Name: Boivin
Description: A traditional trattoria in the picturesque historic centre, with a pleasantly familiar and informal atmosphere. Many dishes on the menu reflect the traditions of Trentino, including freshwater fish. Among the most accomplished offerings: the alpine grey tongue pastrami with borlotti beans and sauerkraut, and the Mòchena spotted kid terrine with fermented giardiniera.

Name: Borgo Poscolle
Description: This small family-run trattoria is nestled in the heart of Carnia and is an excellent example of mountain hospitality. Most of the ingredients used in the kitchen are sourced locally and are complemented by vegetables from their own organic garden. The chefs are passionate about tradition, which they present to guests with a delightful personal touch, as in the case of their cjarsons, the area's famous ravioli, the filling of which changes with the seasons.Those with a sweet tooth really must try the chocolate trilogy, one of the restaurant’s most successful and popular desserts.

Name: Brisla Trattoria
Address: Strada Luigi Carlo Farini 41/a, Parma, 43121, Italy
Description: A contemporary trattoria where you can enjoy some of the region’s delicious specialities, all of which are faithfully reproduced with maybe just a hint of modern flavour – this is one of the most interesting restaurants in central Parma! We particularly enjoyed the bomba di riso (stuffed rice pie) with pigeon ragù, as well as the fresh pastas and the roast meat stuffed with roast potatoes.

Name: Bros' Trattoria
Address: SS172, zona G 61, Martina Franca, 74015, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Sharing its entrance with the Relais Villa San Martino, the car park leads to a cluster of romantic trulli surrounded by a small vineyard. The kitchen is entrusted to the Pellegrino-Potì duo from the nearby gourmet restaurant, yet here it is tradition that holds sway: dishes rich in flavour, often cooked in the wood-fired oven, with a menu that changes frequently to follow the freshness of the season and the market. A straightforward and satisfying offering that honours ancient techniques and the produce of the territory within a setting of great rural charm.

Name: Bruxaboschi
Address: Via Francesco Mignone 8, San Desiderio, 16133, Italy
Description: Anticipate a little time and patience tackling a winding progressively less urban road to reach, inland, San Desiderio, where Bruxaboschi has been delighting clients since 1862 under the same familial management. It will be worth it. Rightly renowned, the cuisine pays homage to local traditions (nearly exclusively meat), commencing with an excellent Genoese cima, picagge and pansotti among pastas, and fried rabbit. In season, obligingly, is the unmissable fungi engagement.

Name: Buatta Cucina Popolana
Description: This simple yet lively and dynamic restaurant occupying the beautiful, historic rooms of an old shop is always busy with locals and tourists, so booking ahead is highly recommended. Dishes are traditionally Sicilian, such as the “sarde a scottadito” (sardines) and change regularly in line with the seasons. Meat, fish, offal and vegetarian options all feature on the menu.

Name: Burro & Alici
Description: Separated from the beach by the seafront promenade, this restaurant, with its simple, informal atmosphere, evokes the feel of Marotta’s traditional seaside trattorias. In summer, one of the rooms opens out onto the outside, almost becoming a terrace overlooking the sea. What sets it apart is its high-quality cuisine, centred on fish from the Adriatic and characterised by generous dishes, rich in colour and flavour. The menu ranges from the great classics of the tradition to more personal creations, enhanced by the chef’s imaginative touches, not to mention a small selection of meat dishes. The gourmet pizzas are also worth a look, with fresh fish taking centre stage once again.

Name: Buscone
Description: The difficulty, which perhaps you may encounter when trying to reach this trattoria, is compensated by the very pleasant family atmosphere and genuine home - made cooking.

Name: CASAeBOTTEGA
Description: An attractive restaurant situated on the charming main square of the village of Dolceacqua, with a beautiful outdoor space and views of the old Doria castle. Inside, the dining room is decorated in “shabby chic” style which gives it a friendly, welcoming and colourful atmosphere. The regional, seasonal cuisine includes standout dishes such as “brandacujun mantecato alla ponentina” (creamed salted cod), “coniglio al rossese” (rabbit in red wine) and delicious desserts.

Name: CUCINA.eat
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: One of Cagliari’s most appealing spots in terms of value for money, this restaurant wins you over with its informal and friendly atmosphere, which makes you feel right at home straight away, whether you’re sitting at a table or at the lively bar. A great deal of attention is also paid to wine, with bottles displayed on the shelves and staff on hand to help guests choose. The cuisine strikes a fine balance between references to Sardinian tradition, more classic dishes and creative offerings designed for those who love to experiment with new flavour combinations. At lunchtime, the selection is more limited, but remains true to the same philosophy: high-quality ingredients, meticulous preparation and a strong focus on flavour.

Name: Ca' d' Frara Trattoria Moderna
Description: In a quiet corner of the center, a small, discreet door opens onto two interconnected dining rooms: modern yet simply elegant. The air is fragrant with Romagna: hand-rolled fresh pasta, tender Swiss chard and ricotta tortelli cloaked in melted butter and Parmigiano, golden oven-baked lasagne, rustic tagliatelle bathed in a richly flavored prosciutto ragù. The main courses are a triumph of taste: tender tongue and succulent cotechino paired with velvety purée and creamy sauces. The finale is sweet and enveloping, with the moist-hearted tenerina accompanied by a small glass brimming with soft, fragrant mascarpone cream.

Name: Cacciatori
Description: You pass through beautiful hilly scenery to get to Cartosio, where you’ll find this typical country house specialising in local cuisine. Although it’s been in business for several decades, during which nine different generations have been at the helm, the formula has (fortunately!) hardly changed, with a focus on Piedmontese dishes made from top-quality local and seasonal ingredients, with the main courses still cooked on the wood-fired stove. The wine list includes some excellent vertical labels, especially from the main wineries in the Langhe. Simple yet attractive guestrooms are also available.

Name: Caffè Grande
Description: Housed in a charming palazzo with an Art Nouveau façade overlooking the main square of the village, this restaurant has an unexpectedly modern and minimalist-style interior. The menu features an impressive selection of fine local charcuterie (including coppa, pancetta and salami), as well as anolini pasta in broth and ricotta and spinach tortelli. The quality of the meat is outstanding.

Name: Caffè La Crepa
Description: Overlooking the picturesque Piazza Matteotti, a Renaissance gem in the heart of Isola Dovarese, this historic venue retains the charm of an old-fashioned café and the warmth of a timeless trattoria. The history of the venue dates back to the 19th century, but it has been linked to the Malinverno family since 1969. Set against a backdrop that evokes the Risorgimento and Art Nouveau influences, the cuisine celebrates the Po Valley through dishes deeply rooted in the region and family traditions: marubini with three broths, cured meats, the traditional mixed boiled meats served with homemade mostarda, river fish and produce from the vegetable garden. The experience is rounded off by the shop, which specialises in a carefully curated selection of wines and gourmet specialities.

Name: Camiano Piccolo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Housed in a 16C farmhouse with and outdoor swimming pool, the Camiano Piccolo agriturismo stands on a hill overlooking the Umbrian countryside, 10 minutes’ drive from Montefalco. Here, chef Giuseppe Fabrizi brings the best of the region’s ingredients to the table, from vegetables grown in the restaurant’s own kitchen garden to local wines and olive oils, delicious meat and black truffles in season.

Name: Cantina dei Cacciatori
Address: Località Villa Superiore 59, Monteu Roero, 12040, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: The original painted sign on the façade recalls with quiet pride the century-long history of the establishment. Born from the restoration of an old trattoria set apart from the village centre, immersed among chestnut trees and outcroppings of tufa, the restaurant remains faithful to the Piedmontese tradition, presenting a cuisine that is forthright and firmly rooted in the territory. The menu focuses on simple yet carefully considered dishes, among them the old-fashioned Russian salad, prepared according to the custom that calls for the use of giardiniera, responsible for its pleasingly characteristic ‘slightly acidic’ note. In the warmer months, the enchanting terrace affords moments of genuine relaxation, while the early twentieth-century underground cellar, open to visitors, adds charm and depth to the experience. In the colder months, a modern fireplace warms the dining room, helping to create a welcoming and intimate atmosphere perfectly suited to savouring the cooking of another age, reinterpreted with measured restraint.

Name: Casa del Vino della Vallagarina
Description: The flavors, aromas, and wines of Vallagarina take center stage at this delightfully situated venue within the seventeenth-century walls of Palazzo de Probizer, offering stunning mountain views (weather permitting). The cellar features virtually every wine producer in the area (available by the glass as well!) while the kitchen relies on a well-proven formula: a single tasting menu that changes daily, with the option to select just a few dishes. The creations draw inspiration from the seasons, the territory, and Italian tradition, as well as from the fragrant bounty of the restaurant’s own garden. The inspector recommends: raviolo with alpine ricotta, Jerusalem artichoke, and Trentingrana cheese. A varied selection of desserts, listed on a separate menu, rounds out the experience.

Name: Castagneto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: On the lower slopes above Lake Maggiore, this rustic building offers particularly panoramic views of the verdant landscape, enjoyed both from the terrace and most indoor tables. The atmosphere is homey with a sense of long-standing tradition, and it couldn’t be otherwise since the restaurant has been operating for over 50 years (since 1969). The cuisine ranges across the entire Italian peninsula (including seafood), following the rhythm of the seasons, though the standout dishes remain predominantly local and regional. In addition to the wine selection, there's also a carefully curated offering of spirits.

Name: Cibus
Address: Via Chianche di Scarano 7, Ceglie Messapica, 72013, Italy
Description: In the narrow streets of the historic center, once you cross the threshold the atmosphere could not be more authentic: dining rooms with barrel-vaulted ceilings and an evocative inner courtyard, where tables find their place beneath ancient porticoes. The kitchen pursues a passionate exploration of Apulian products and recipes, interpreted with care and authenticity. Among the dishes not to be missed, the marretto di agnello stands out, prepared with offal and served with roast potatoes, but the entire menu is so inviting that choosing becomes a pleasant dilemma. Whether you are a local or visiting the region, a stop at Cibus is warmly recommended – better still with a reservation in advance, given the popularity of the house.

Name: Cile's Bistrot
Description: A restaurant not to be missed if you are in the area. The moment you walk through the door, the rooms overflowing with decorations will surprise you, but then it will be time to sample the cuisine. The chef puts his own personal stamp on some of the classics of local and national seafood tradition. One dish after another, you won’t ever want to stop eating!

Name: Clemente
Description: Situated in the charming centre of Sulmona, Clemente has for many years offered guests a simple, welcoming ambience in the restored stables of a palazzo dating from the early 19C. The menu has an exclusive focus on ingredients from the Abruzzi, including home-made pasta “alla chitarra” and the use of saffron from Aquila. The main courses are all meat-based, while among the desserts the Pan dell'Orsosemifreddo is particularly delicious. Although the portions are generous, most of the dishes are also available in half-portions. Aperitifs are served in the bistro-style room.

Name: Condividere
Description: A small and impeccably tended bistrot in the heart of Arona’s historic centre, a few steps from the lakeside promenade, this venue distinguishes itself through a gastronomic proposal that is both personal and firmly rooted in the territory. In the kitchen, the chef and owner leads a seasonal menu that is lively and refined, bringing genuine sensitivity to the finest local produce.Among the dishes not to be missed, the “Condividere” antipasto, a sequence of small tastes recalling the Italian tradition of the shared starter: burrata with crunchy puntarelle and anchovies, a tartlet of Russian salad and lake bottarga, alongside other preparations designed to be enjoyed in good company. Front of house is today entrusted to Mattia Trentani, a professional of solid experience, who accompanies the balanced and contemporary experience with attentiveness and expertise.

Name: Consorzio
Address: Via Monte di Pietà 23, Turin, 10122, Italy
Description: Casual and relaxed, simple and authentic: at the Consorzio you’ll find one of the finest examples of traditional Piedmontese cuisine. A feast of meat and fresh pasta, then: from the classic agnolotti gobbi to braised Piedmontese Fassona beef, there’s also room for offal dishes, such as ravioli di finanziera and tagliatelle with heart ragù. The desserts are not to be missed, from panna cotta to hazelnut cake and zabaglione.

Name: Contesto Alimentare
Description: Small, essential and free from affectation, this is a true declaration of love for Piedmont, interpreted with authenticity and excellent quality. The closely set tables, overlooking the central Via Accademia Albertina, create a lively and informal atmosphere, ideal for savouring regional specialities, with the occasional interesting foray beyond the region. Such is the case, for example, with the fresh chitarra pasta with cream of tomato, pecorino, pepper and crispy guanciale, sampled during the warmer season. Among the main courses, meat predominates – well represented and of quality – while the cheese selection proves solid and well considered. To close, the desserts offer a sweet and characterful finale: from the classic panna cotta to the bonet, through to more original variations such as the mountain lavender panna cotta, wryly renamed “lavanda gastrica”.

Name: Coquus
Description: Just eight tables, set beneath a vaulted brick ceiling, define this small restaurant in the historic centre of Lucera, housed within the former 18th-century bishop’s palace and, in fine weather, also offering pleasant outdoor service. Chef-patron Mirko Esposito stands out for joyful, sun-filled cooking built around Apulian ingredients from both land and sea. Particularly playful is his reinterpretation of the “prawn cocktail”: the shellfish are arranged individually on the plate, each covered with perfect alternating stripes of cocktail sauce and squid-ink cream.

Name: Coxinendi
Address: Viale del Golfo di Quartu 25, Quartu sant'Elena, 09045, Italy
Description: Coxinendi — meaning ‘cooking’ in Sardinian — is the restaurant created by Davide Atzeni, a chef with a wealth of experience, who chose to leave the inland areas to set up shop right on the sandy shores of Poetto. Here, along this famous stretch of coastline beloved by the people of Cagliari and visitors to the city, the restaurant takes on a new dimension, bathed in the light and the breath of the sea.The stylistic signature remains as stated at the start of the menu: a cuisine that is “Sardinian, creative, free-spirited and unhurried”, capable of combining identity with creative freedom. To round off the experience, the spacious outdoor area invites you to enjoy your meal while gazing out towards Capo Sant’Elia.

Name: Da Alighiero
Description: Nestled amid the cobbled streets of Anghiari, one of Italy’s most beautiful villages, this rustic-style restaurant is hidden behind a wooden door with glass panes and curtains. With its brick-vaulted ceiling, old cupboards, art on the walls and bottles everywhere, Da Alighiero has a warm, authentic ambience. The cuisine celebrates Tuscany’s classic favourites (don’t miss the tripe served in a spicy red sauce), while enthusiastic host Gianni is on hand with recommendations for the perfect wine.

Name: Da Burde
Description: A celebrated food shop with an adjoining trattoria, situated just beyond the western edge of the city, boasting over 125 years of history and a loyal following that ensures it is constantly frequented: booking is recommended. The surroundings are simple and rustic, with the option of sitting at the small tables near the entrance, beside the counters displaying charcuterie and cheeses, the protagonists – alongside crostini – of the starters. The cooking, entirely consistently, is traditional and Tuscan, with particular emphasis on meats, offered both braised and grilled (the bistecca fiorentina is, of course, a constant). Noteworthy, finally, is the wine selection: broad, well structured and curated directly by the owner Andrea, who regularly organises themed tasting evenings.

Name: Da Fausto
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: With Fausto front of house, his wife Rosella at the helm in the kitchen and daughter Gaia who not only works in the dining room but is also responsible for the desserts, this restaurant celebrates Piedmontese cuisine on a menu that changes weekly in order to ensure that ingredients are fresh and seasonal. Meat takes centre stage, alongside excellent fresh pasta dishes (such as the famous agnolotti) and delicious desserts including fiordilatte ice-cream. The wine cellar is well stocked, thanks to the restaurant’s own production of Pinot Nero (dry and sparkling labels), while for anyone wanting to prolong their stay, attractive guestrooms are available at the Borgo del Gallo.

Name: Da Felice
Description: On the beautiful coast road, just a short walk from the seafront, you’ll find a place that exudes tradition and hospitality. A family-run eatery where time seems to move slowly and Ligurian seafood cuisine takes centre stage. Every dish tells a story of authentic flavours, lovingly prepared and served alfresco in summer, inviting guests to enjoy the sea breeze and the pleasure of good company. The inspector recommends: “brandacujun” (made with dried cod and potatoes) or calamari on the “ciappa” (a stone slab), served with potatoes and “preboggion” (cooked wild herbs).

Name: Da Flavio e Fabrizio "Al Teatro"
Description: Situated next to the cinema-theatre, in an area a little off the beaten track but well worth exploring, this gem of a restaurant specialises in fish and seafood from the Veneto, serving its fish (fresh off the boat) in traditional home-made dishes which are timeless and comforting. Each dish introduces diners to the authentic flavours of the lagoon, in carefully prepared recipes that fully respect the top-quality ingredients. To finish your meal, don’t miss the pannacotta with fresh strawberry sauce – a classic favourite that is truly delicious! There’s a carefully thought-out selection of wines by the glass, offering the perfect pairing for each course.

Name: Da Giannino - L'Angolo d'Abruzzo
Description: A simple and informal urban trattoria with a friendly atmosphere, tables arranged close together and typical red-and-white check tablecloths. The Abruzzo takes centre stage in the delicious cuisine served here – we particularly recommend the sagne (a type of pasta) and beans, the maccheroni alla chitarra, the roast lamb and the arrosticini (skewers of mutton).

Name: Da Giocondo
Description: A simple, rustic trattoria, perched among the narrow streets of the upper part of the village. The owners themselves attend to both dining room and kitchen, ensuring that homestyle yet flavorful Abruzzese dishes reach the table, sometimes announced verbally to complement a menu featuring cheeses, cured meats, and grilled fare (yes, there are arrosticini!). The specialties not to be missed are certainly the traditional handmade pastas, each bearing its own distinctive name, and the indulgent desserts (the seasonal fruit crostatas are excellent). Also noteworthy is the small wine list showcasing the region above all, with cellars represented from each of its provinces. Reservations are always advisable.

Name: Da Gregorio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A few kilometers from Orvieto, after a series of winding roads in the village of Morrano Nuovo, an old 1980s sign will guide you to the restaurant Da Gregorio. A stop here is a must: straightforward, local cuisine with homegrown vegetables and cured meats, and a wine list celebrating small winemakers and native grape varieties. The grilled pork with maple syrup is a must-try – a true surprise on the plate.

Name: Da Marchesi
Description: In a hamlet of Novafeltria, lthe road that winds upward through the Apennines between Romagna and the Marche is home to this modest gem, where the Romagnan tradition is savoured in all its simplicity and goodness: handmade sfoglia for the pasta, main courses featuring local meats, and daily specials that follow the seasons. Not to be missed are the fried porcini mushrooms and the tortelloni of green pasta filled with ricotta and spinach, dressed with butter and truffle.

Name: Da Pode
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In a skilfully refurbished farmhouse nestled in the hills surrounding San Gimignano, Da Pode restaurant welcomes guests into cosy dining rooms featuring stone and wood, and onto a large terrace where, when the weather is warm, diners can enjoy their meal as they admire the Tuscan countryside. The cuisine is authentic and deeply rooted in tradition, with recipes handed down through four generations. Fresh pasta is prepared daily on the premises, the meat is of the highest quality, and the desserts are worthy of attention too: the soft, light apple cake with custard is a delicious finale that sums up all the authenticity of the place.

Name: Da Sapì
Description: In this hotel-restaurant’s modern dining rooms, you’ll enjoy some of the most interesting cuisine in the region, where the top-quality ingredients and skilful preparation will impress in equal measure. Not wishing to ignore any of the dishes on offer, we particularly enjoyed the braised snails, with a herb and cavolo nero soup and sweet garlic cream; the game tortelli; the charcoal-grilled char; and the rose cake served with zabaglione.

Name: Dalla Libera
Address: Via Farra 52, Sernaglia della Battaglia, 31020, Italy
Description: At this restaurant, an American-style barbecue garden (in summer) and a smart, rustic dining room provide the backdrop for carefully prepared local cuisine with a personalised, gourmet twist, such as the home-made gnocchi served with three different types of tomato. The wine list features top-quality labels from Italy and further afield, including a few vintages that will delight wine-enthusiasts.

Name: Dalla Rosa Alda
Address: Strada Garibaldi 4, San Giorgio di Valpolicella, 37015, Italy
Description: In one of the five villages of the Valpolicella Classica region, as you drive up roads flanked by enchanting scenery, you come to this charming hamlet with its many stone houses. The restaurant has been run by the same family since 1853; it goes without saying that it remains true to the region’s traditional dishes, ranging from fresh pasta to meat dishes. Of course, the local wines are a must, and there’s a good selection available by the glass too.

Name: Dei Cantoni
Description: Situated in a picturesque historic hamlet with a castle once inhabited by the Malatesta dynasty, this restaurant boasts a charming and traditional dining room. The delicious cuisine is the star of the show here, featuring imaginative dishes showcasing ingredients from the Romagna region, as well as more classic recipes such as pasta with carbonara and amatriciana sauces. All the fresh pasta is home made.

Name: Del Belbo - Da Bardon
Address: Valle Asinari 25, San Marzano Oliveto, 14050, Italy
Description: The tradition of the Monferrato region has been told for generations through simple local cuisine. Indeed, there is an inviting list on the menu in which none of the great classics are missing: peppers with bagna cauda, vitello tonnato, tagliolini with Cervere leek sauce, stewed tripe, braised veal stew with Barbera d'Asti, the sweet "mattone monferrino" and so on. Straightforward flavours to pair easily with an endless wine list for true fans of Langhe, Asti, all of Italy and France. All "seasoned" with proper customer care and pleasant outdoor service for the warm weather. Basically, the restaurant you want near home!

Name: Dell'Alba
Description: In business since 1850 and now run by the sixth generation, this simple and authentic family trattoria is a mecca for fans of Bassa Padana cuisine. The menu boasts an extraordinary combination of specialities from Cremona and Mantova, including local cured meats, pumpkin tortelli with sweet tomato sauté, “porc-tonné” (meat with tuna) from an original recipe by Pellegrino Artusi, and sbrisolona cake with warm zabaglione. Although you will be offered a menu, we highly recommend chatting with the exuberant chef, who will be happy to guide you in your choice of food and wine.

Name: Domenico dal 1968
Description: Far from the tourist crowds, this is an authentic neighborhood restaurant, beloved by Romans and regulars alike. The menu arrives verbally, as tradition dictates, and alongside a few fish offerings it is impossible to resist the most forthright repertoire of Roman cuisine: carciofi alla romana and alla giudia, eggplant polpette, tripe, sweetbreads, coratella. An irresistible parade of genuine flavors, served in small, simple, and welcoming dining rooms with a familial feel. Tables are few: reservations are strongly recommended.

Name: Dongiò
Description: A true benchmark in the city’s dining scene, winning over palates since 1987 with its Calabrian cuisine, rich in intense aromas and generous flavors. A convivial, genuine venue where recipes speak of tradition and passion: from the robust, comforting tagliatelle with donkey ragù to the celebrated sirloin meatballs bathed in a rich, fragrant sauce.

Name: Durnwald
Address: Via Nikolaus Amhof 6, località Durna in Selva, Gsies, 39030, Italy
Description: A delicious plate of Schlutzkrapfen (ravioli stuffed with spinach and ricotta) is just what’s needed after a good day’s skiing or a hike through the woods. And that’s not all – Durnwald celebrates the Alto Adige in all its glory, both in terms of its landscapes, which can be admired from the dining room windows, and its cuisine, which keeps alive the region’s authentic traditions. The owner himself is at the helm front of house – a perfect host who guides guests in their choice of food and wine.

Name: Edelweiss
Description: A real bastion of local cuisine for over 60 years thanks to the hard work of an entire family. The menu features mountain-style cuisine, including game dishes, a small selection of local cheeses (we highly recommend the Bettelmatt) and home-made ice cream. Relaxed and informal ambience.

Name: Enoteca San Nicola
Address: Contrada di San Nicola 11/a, Bobbio, 29022, Italy
Description: In the historic heart of Bobbio, on the first floor of a former 17th-century convent, three intimate, well-appointed rooms welcome you with lively paintings and vintage objects. The menu is lean yet rich, offering four options for each course, blending tradition with playful flavors. The wine list is like a small encyclopedia, featuring a thousand labels from around the world, with vertical selections for connoisseurs. Don't miss the ricotta pearls with sun-dried tomatoes, black olives, and Parmesan.

Name: Estrò
Description: A lively bistro with a youthful feel, set in the heart of the town centre and featuring a pleasant outdoor terrace overlooking the square. In the kitchen, chef-owner Della Croce presents a menu that strikes a pleasing balance between meat and fish, always guided by careful respect for the seasons. Among the dishes most appreciated by the Inspector is the excellent octopus alla marinara: expertly cooked in two stages and full of flavour, it is served with cherry tomatoes, garlic, olives and capers, bringing out the character of the ingredient with both simplicity and skill.

Name: Forentum
Description: In the heart of the historic center, this charming restaurant welcomes guests between a cool outdoor terrace and an evocative dining room created in a natural cave. The cuisine celebrates local traditions, with occasional forays into seafood. In the evening, the offering also includes pizzas, made with three different doughs: the classic Neapolitan, the thin and crispy “Papà Luigi”, and the one with vegetable charcoal. Surrounding the restaurant, simply furnished yet well-maintained guest rooms in the style of a scattered hotel complete the experience.

Name: Foresta
Address: Strada de la Comunità de Fiem 42, Moena, 38035, Italy
Description: Situated in front of a dense fir wood, this restaurant comes as something of a surprise. The dishes are prepared with genuine local ingredients, resulting in food that is full of flavour. Don’t get up from the table without having tasted the pappardelle pasta with mushrooms and speck ham or the fillet of venison with a redcurrant sauce.

Name: Forma
Description: Not by the sea, but at the foot of a medieval quarter, the dining room is an elegant blend of old and new; you can’t go wrong with the cuisine: Gianluca Formichella is a truly talented chef who puts a modern spin on Italian classics with creative touches. The ingredients are at the heart of the dining experience, in both meat and fish dishes. Among the best are those cooked on the barbecue.

Name: Fracia
Description: After leaving your car in the car park and walking up a short slope through the terraced vineyards, you reach this charming restaurant, housed in an old stone building once used for wine-growing. The rooms retain the charm of old Valtellina, with a pleasantly rustic and romantic atmosphere, while in the warmer months the arbour offers a splendid view over the valley. The cuisine draws on local traditions to create a menu that combines classic recipes with contemporary interpretations: there is no shortage of bresaola, pizzoccheri and meat dishes, alongside more creative dishes that follow the rhythm of the seasons. The wine cellar is particularly interesting, showcasing the finest wines of Valtellina, with a selection of wines from the historic Nino Negri winery, which owns the vineyards of the same name, among which the restaurant is situated.

Name: Fratelli Bruzzone
Description: Great credit is due to the Bruzzone brothers, who have transformed the very premises where they once operated as a simple delicatessen into an authentic temple of Piedmontese cooking. Today, across two small dining rooms of homey character – where a reservation is indispensable, even at lunch – a sequence of dishes takes shape that pays homage to tradition with rigour and passion. The offering is a celebration of timeless flavours: acciughe al verde, onion with vermouth and Blu del Moncenisio fonduta, agnolotti of impeccable pastry, rabbit al civet, guinea fowl, through to the classic desserts such as bonet and vanilla panna cotta. Course after course, the cooking wins one over through its forthright honesty and depth, making departure a reluctant affair: this is one of those places from which one rises from the table already longing to return.

Name: Futura Osteria
Address: Largo Garfonda 10, località Abbadia Isola, Monteriggioni, 53035, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Along the Via Francigena, just a few steps from Monteriggioni, stands the small medieval hamlet of Abbadia Isola, with its splendid Romanesque church and ancient buildings that once formed the monastery and its dependencies. Futura Osteria occupies the rooms that were once the monks’ cellars, where they stored their wines: here you can enjoy flavourful, Tuscan-inspired cuisine, simple and profoundly seasonal. The format offers three fixed-price tasting menus, with portions that are always generous; many of the vegetables come from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden. In addition to the menus, there is always Florentine steak cooked over the embers, as well as the option of ordering the selection of cured meats made by hand in the osteria and cheeses matured in-house. Completing the picture are a refined wine selection, friendly service and a secluded, atmospheric terrace.

Name: Gabbiano 1983
Address: Piazza Vittorio Veneto 10, Corte de' Cortesi, 26020, Italy
Description: Having successfully been in business for over 40 years, this restaurant continues to shine for its top-quality traditional cuisine, priding itself, as it has always done, on its love for local specialities. Goose dishes take centre stage on the menu (the area is famous for its goose), alongside an excellent selection of traditional boiled meats all of which are sourced locally. There’s also a good choice of wine, which is skilfully displayed and served from a trolley in the dining room from which wines are served by the glass.

Name: Gassenwirt
Description: Situated next to the village church, this restaurant has been serving excellent South Tyrolean cuisine since as far back as 1602. House specialities include canederli pressati (dumplings) and Buchteln (a type of sweet bun).

Name: Granaro del Monte
Description: A return home for Granaro del Monte to the center of Norcia and inside Casa Bianconi, a charming hotel, overlooking the town’s main street. A series of intimate dining rooms includes one adorned with frescoes, originally part of the old local granaries. The cuisine is traditional and offers the classic cured meats, featuring a truly excellent 24‑month prosciutto, as well as traditional recipes revisited by the owners, such as the outstanding tagliatelle with ricotta and sausage. The grill is always fired up, turning out beef, lamb, and other specialties. With excellent value for money and service available every day, this address is truly unmissable!

Name: Green T.
Address: Via del Piè di Marmo 28, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: This restaurant situated behind Piazza San Ignazio and not far from the Pantheon has been renowned for its Chinese food for the past 20 years. The small dining rooms here are arranged on different levels and decorated with beautiful original objects, including a fine collection of teapots. The menu naturally features Chinese dishes, which range from classic favourites to street food-style options and more contemporary fare. The dim sum, freshly made on the day, are excellent, as are the stir-fry dishes which include a delicious tuna, vegetable and Szechuan pepper recipe.

Name: Hostaria Viola
Address: Via Verdi 32, Castiglione delle Stiviere, 46043, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A rustic building welcomes guests into a warm and authentic setting, where the family atmosphere is made even more pleasant by the warm welcome extended by the owners, who know just how to put guests at ease within minutes. The kitchen serves contemporary dishes, prepared with simplicity and taste. According to the Inspector, the most tempting of the desserts is the “meringata a cucchiaio”, a meringue dessert served with ice cream, whipped cream and a crunchy crumble of amaretti biscuits and chocolate: an irresistible finale.

Name: Hosteria Grappolo d'Oro
Description: Situated near Piazza Navona and Campo de' Fiori, this long-established restaurant has been run by five local business partners (one of whom is the chef) since 2000. Top-quality, classic and generous Roman cuisine is to the fore here, served in a simple, rustic-style dining room which is always busy (hardly surprising, given the location!). Dishes include pasta with the famous sauces of Rome (amatriciana, carbonara and cacio e pepe), as well as meatballs, puntarelle, and maritozzo with cream. We highly recommend the “Percorso Romano” tasting menu which includes four small courses for just over 30 euros.

Name: I Tri Siochètt
Description: At the edge of the city, just off the ring road, this quintessential trattoria features spacious dining rooms where a familial, informal atmosphere prevails, while from the kitchen arrive the pillars of Parmesan tradition, executed at an excellent level: flavorful dishes crafted from predominantly local products. Among the unmissable offerings, the anolini in capon broth, savory and satisfying, as well as the pork cheeks in lemon cremolade with cream of garbanzo beans.

Name: Il Cardinale Vino e Cucina
Description: This pleasant restaurant is situated within the traffic-restricted area of Sarzana, just a few steps from the beautiful central piazza of this small town (which is in Liguria, although the dialect spoken here has a Tuscan influence). With a new name and a new team at the helm, the restaurant serves delicious, colourful cuisine that follows the seasons, with a balance of reasonably priced meat and fish dishes on the menu. A spacious outdoor summer-dining space shaded by parasols, plus courteous, efficient female staff complete the picture.

Name: Il Casolare dei Segreti
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: A family - run restaurant with young, enthusiastic staff. Four rustic dining rooms provide the setting to enjoy delicious regional dishes, such as the ever - popular Marchigiana veal steak.

Name: Il Cedro
Description: At the entrance of the village of Moggiona, along the road connecting Camaldoli to Poppi, Il Cedro welcomes you with homely aromas and genuine flavors. Mariangela and Cristina – one in the dining room, the other in the kitchen – share the Tuscan tradition with enthusiasm and warmth, offering rustic dishes, sincere smiles, and a family-like atmosphere.

Name: Il Ciabot
Description: Warmed by an open fire in winter, this welcoming family-run restaurant celebrates the cuisine of Piedmont, although a few fish dishes also feature on the menu. Traditional, time-honoured and overlooked dishes take pride of place, such as boiled meat terrine with a salsa verde, Fassone beef in a crust, plus an excellent giandujotto chocolate mousse. Booking ahead is recommended.

Name: Il Conte Matto
Description: The 14th-century home of the castle gamekeeper has been transformed into a showcase of regional products with a terrace overlooking the hills and, from the rooms, glimpses of the surrounding countryside. Chef Chiara's cooking is easy to read: Tuscan and local, with an emphasis on seasonal produce from the garden and nearby farmers. The triptych of hams is already a good reason to sit at the table, delicate and firm at the same time, with perfect seasoning! Among the starters, indulge in an artichoke flan; among the main courses, the classic Florentine steak or pigeon, served whole and flavoured with vin santo.

Name: Il Fiorile
Address: Via XXV Aprile 6, frazione Castel Ratti, Borghetto di Borbera, 15060, Italy
Description: Almost as if on a postcard, the warmth of an old barn set in verdant silence, on the border between Piedmont and Liguria, inspires a cuisine based on seasonal and local raw materials, in which there is a fine commitment to the search for 0 km products. The management is obviously direct and family-run, and the recipes aim to give you a taste of the simple but exquisite flavours of the Val Borbera.

Name: Il Latini
Address: Via dei Palchetti 6 r, Florence, 50123, Italy
Description: Faithful to itself over time, Latini is a true Florentine institution where tradition finds expression through an authentic uncompromising Tuscan character. The simple, intimate rooms retain a marked rustic character, with hams hanging from the ceiling and shelves lined with bottles, retrieved with the characteristic long tongs that slide above the tables. The gastronomic offering remains anchored to the great classics of local cooking, executed with rigour and respect: from crostini and ribollita to peposo, through to cantucci served with vinsanto. The bistecca fiorentina dominates the scene, though guests should be prepared for a bill commensurate with the experience. The generations pass, but this venue preserves intact its convivial spirit: welcoming, animated at precisely the right level and perfect for any informal occasion.

Name: Il Moro
Description: Occupying a 17C palazzo in the village centre, this restaurant showcases regional cuisine in all its glory. Specialities include agnolotti (stuffed pasta) served in three traditional ways (plain, cooked in wine, or with a meat sauce), boiled tongue, and local hazelnut semifreddo with chocolate fondant, all accompanied by wines chosen from an extensive wine list. Added attractions are the open fire in winter, an attractive outdoor space for summer dining, and a few comfortable guestrooms to the rear.

Name: Il Ritrovo d'Abruzzo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Getting there may require some patience, but it's eased by the journey through one of the most enchanting parts of rural, hilly Abruzzo. This family-run restaurant, managed by the Di Tillio brothers (one in the dining room and the other in the kitchen, united by a passion for their work) offers a pleasant outdoor service in summer and takes guests on a journey through the region's culinary traditions. The dishes are often enhanced with produce from the family garden or fresh pasta made with their own wheat flour, with creative touches here and there.

Name: Il Sogno
Description: Situated in the green heart of the Mirano countryside, this restaurant serves simple yet substantial cuisine. Authentic traditional cuisine is to the fore here, with a focus on top-quality ingredients and reasonable prices. The ambience is warm and welcoming, evoking the feel of a country house, while the serving staff – always available with a smile – add a friendly touch that makes every meal a special occasion. The perfect address for anyone looking for authenticity, flavour and a family-style welcome.

Name: Il Sottomarino
Description: A lively restaurant on the seafront, featuring a pleasant terrace with panoramic views, which is highly sought after during the season – so it's best to book it as early as possible. For over twenty years, the solid family management has focused on excellent seafood cuisine, mostly classic, with some personal touches, especially in the desserts. Be sure to try the dark chocolate and crunchy cannoli, served vertically and filled with gianduja semifreddo, topped and plated with a cold Moscato d’Asti zabaglione.

Name: Il Turacciolo
Address: Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II 4, Andria, 76123, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: A characteristic and pleasant atmosphere reminiscent of an enoteca wine bar introduces one of the most intriguing culinary offerings in the area. If seeking the most typical Apulian products, this is your address!

Name: Impero
Description: A culinary landmark in the Novara province, this restaurant has been run for decades by the enthusiastic Naggi sisters, whose family have owned the premises since 1934. The secret to their success lies in the warm welcome and the delicious traditional cuisine, which includes fresh homemade pasta, an extraordinary paniscia (a type of risotto), and stuffed boiled chicken served with various sauces and chutneys displayed on a trolley. All the dishes are full of flavour and made from seasonal ingredients. You’ll have no problem finding a good wine to accompany your meal from the impressive wine list that includes plenty of local labels.

Name: In Cucina dai Pennisi
Description: The Pennisi family business started in this butcher’s shop, which over time has expanded to include a restaurant serving excellent cuisine to guests who sit at small tables facing a counter where a fine selection of meat, salumi and cheeses is displayed. The menu features grilled meat options alongside filled rolls and hamburgers, as well as delicious cooked dishes that are both generous and substantial. We suggest asking staff for recommendations, as we did – we were not disappointed!

Name: Italia
Description: Operating since 1971 and still under the same family management, they are a reliable address, a great classic if you are in the area. The ambience is well cared for, while the cuisine is solid. Alongside some local cues (battuta di fassona with fresh cheese or agnolotti with butter and sage), there are also seafood dishes (tuna tataki with coconut and soy sauce) and, in general, some contemporary touches, very evident in the pleasing presentations.

Name: Kanton Restaurant
Address: Via Antonio Gramsci 17, Capriate San Gervasio, 24042, Italy
Description: In an unremarkable district of Capriate lies one of the most interesting expressions of Chinese cuisine in Lombardy. Do not be misled by the surroundings: once through the door, the atmosphere is pleasant and welcoming and, above all, Mr Zhu Weikun’s cooking is truly accomplished, with an excellent quality-price ratio. The menu is refreshingly concise rather than overwhelming, focusing on a well-judged selection of fragrant dishes that clearly express the flavours and techniques of the great Chinese gastronomic tradition. Desserts, by contrast, follow a decidedly European approach and are not listed on a menu as such: instead, they are presented on a tray, inviting a final choice. Completing the experience is a carefully curated and extensive selection of teas, ideal for accompanying or concluding the meal.

Name: Krone
Description: The past retains its fascinating appeal in this traditional restaurant situated in a small mountain village, where modern trends are ignored in favour of authentic dishes from the South Tyrol. Originally opened as an inn, the restaurant still offers a few simple and discreet rooms furnished in traditional style, as well as a new and modern sauna.

Name: L'800
Description: Period furniture, regional cuisine and a cheerful ambience are some of the characteristics of this old farmhouse which is named after the 1800s when it was built. Some of the ingredients used, such as snails and frogs’ legs, may come as a surprise: the restaurant specialises in these unusual delicacies, even offering a tasting menu totally dedicated to snails.

Name: L'Acino
Description: In the heart of the Quadrilatero Romano, just a stone’s throw from the bustling Porta Palazzo market, this small, family-run restaurant embodies the very essence of Piedmontese culinary tradition. The simple, welcoming atmosphere provides the ideal setting for cuisine that is rich in flavour and generous in portion size, deeply rooted in the local area and traditional recipes. The menu, often enhanced by the day’s specials announced verbally, invites you on a journey through the great regional classics: from traditional starters to fresh stuffed pasta, right through to the slow-cooked dishes that are a hallmark of Savoyard cuisine. To round off the meal, there are some unmissable desserts such as bonet and hazelnut cake, served with zabajone. There are just a few tables and they’re in high demand: booking in advance is strongly recommended.

Name: L'Acquario
Address: Via Vittorio Emanuele 69, Castiglione del Lago, 06061, Italy
Description: In the historic center of this charming village above the lake, this spot is a great place to explore Umbrian cuisine, particularly traditional dishes featuring freshwater fish. For example? The oven-roasted medallion of porchetta-style carp, which offers a rich and succulent flavor!

Name: L'Ortone
Description: A bistro with a Tuscan soul overlooking the Sant’Ambrogio market: pared-back in décor and equally forthright in its culinary approach, alongside tributes to the territory, the cuisine focuses on imaginative preparations inspired by the great themes of Italian cuisine. Emblematic is the work with squab, interpreted according to the season, as in the agnolotti, a dish that speaks to technique and contemporary sensitivity. The wine list offers a focused selection of regional bottles at every price point, while a small terrace provides a handful of pleasant tables on milder days.

Name: L'Oste Dispensa
Description: Along one of the two strips of land that join the mainland to the Argentario is this contemporary osteria, minimal but comfortable and equipped with a pleasant veranda that opens in summer, always projecting toward a splendid view of the sea (don't miss the sunset if you can). The cuisine is based on local products, especially sustainably caught fish: not surprisingly, in keeping with this, the wine list features several organic labels. Highly recommended tasting menus that can range from 35 to 45 Euro. Better make reservations because they are extremely popular!

Name: L'Osteria della Trippa
Description: In the heart of Trastevere, a recent interior refurbishment has given the Osteria della Trippa a new look, while retaining its rustic, homely character. The cuisine passionately celebrates the traditions of Rome and the Lazio region, offering generous, meticulously prepared dishes, with a particular focus on offal. The undisputed star of the show is, of course, tripe, served in a variety of ways and featuring as the centrepiece of a dedicated tasting menu; another menu, meanwhile, pays tribute to the cuisine of Viterbo. There’s no shortage of the great classics, from artichokes alla giudia to coratella, right through to pasta dishes with the most famous sauces: amatriciana, carbonara, cacio e pepe and pajata. Rounding off the experience is the warm welcome from Alessandra Ruggeri, the heart and soul of the dining room, and a wine list with a focus on wines from Lazio and across Italy.

Name: L'Ostreria Fratelli Pavesi
Description: The menu is a journey through flavours that weave the traditions of Piacenza together with influences from other Italian regions. One of the highlights is their take on a Ligurian dish: Cappon magro di fiume, which combines sturgeon and trout with seasonal vegetables and salsa verde, creating fresh and lively contrasts. But the dish that won us over today is the charcoal-grilled pigeon: juicy meat, velvety liver pâté, a rich gravy and vegetables from the garden, in a perfect balance between technique and taste. The experience doesn't stop here: the wine list offers a wealth of rare and intriguing labels, ready to complete the delightful dining experience.

Name: La Baita
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre, this establishment seamlessly combines a trattoria and a delicatessen, embodying a time-honoured tradition that has been skilfully brought to life. At the entrance, the counter is striking for its size and quality, with a selection of cured meats and cheeses that effectively forms a menu in its own right, complemented by the restaurant’s menu, which is based on the flavours of Romagna and updated regularly to reflect the seasons. Historically also a wine shop, the venue boasts a wine cellar containing over a thousand labels, displayed throughout the premises and a testament to the owner’s great passion, all offered at a decidedly attractive value for money.

Name: La Brinca
Address: Via Campo di Ne 58, Ne, 16040, Italy
Description: Since 1987, this trattoria, regarded as one of the finest in Italy, has been the domain of the Circella family. Guests come here to savour local cuisine and authentic hospitality. The menu is a journey through local flavours and recipes, with generous and fragrant dishes, enriched by the “dishes of the year” introduced from 2010 onwards. Dishes not to be missed include the ravioli with herbs and Sarazzu with aged cow's milk ricotta from Val d'Aveto, enveloped in a sauce made from local hazelnuts, and the slow-cooked suckling pig with bay leaves and chestnuts. Downstairs, an excellent wine cellar is home to over 1,000 labels, absolute treasures that earned sommelier Matteo the wine service award in 2021.

Name: La Bucaccia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: One of the best places to discover Tuscan cuisine, and that of Arezzo in particular, this restaurant serves exquisite dishes full of flavour. Just a few tables are laid out along the main street in the historic centre, while the two interior dining rooms are rustic and romantic in feel. Friendly and exuberant owner Romano merits a particular mention, providing guaranteed entertainment in between courses.

Name: La Campanara
Description: In a charming hamlet just outside Galeata, the entrance opens onto a small, pretty courtyard that in summer leads to outdoor tables beside the church, shaded by trees and facing the hills: a truly idyllic setting. The cuisine is rooted in the local territory, which here means not only Romagna but also echoes of the neighboring Marche and, above all, Tuscany – as in a memorable lampredotto with porcini mushrooms, tasted on our most recent late‑summer visit. In the adjoining shop, guests can purchase products prepared in the restaurant’s own workshop, while a few guest rooms are also available.

Name: La Chioccia d'Oro
Address: Via Novi 2, loc. Pietra dei Correnti, bivio Novi Velia, Vallo della Lucania, 84078, Italy
Description: For over 40 years, La Chioccia d'Oro has been renowned for its delicious, bountiful cuisine inspired by the Cilento region, including excellent pasta dishes (fresh and dried pasta served with tasty sauces) and equally delicious meat-based main courses. The ambience is decidedly unpretentious and the prices are some of the most reasonable you’ll find in Italy!

Name: La Civetta
Description: Deep in the Apennines, at the heart of a tiny village, you’ll find a cozy osteria run with passion by a young couple. The cuisine draws on Ligurian and Piedmontese traditions, honoring seasonality with both land and sea dishes: from fragrant fried anchovies with basil-lime mayonnaise to house-made ravioli filled with sea bream alla ligure. Lunch features a simple daily menu, but on request, an à la carte service is available by reservation.

Name: La Cuccagna Giro di Vite
Description: Founded in 1969 by Martino Marsella, the restaurant has its roots in the tradition of the Apulian butcher’s shop with grill, of which it became a natural gastronomic extension. To this day the management remains firmly in family hands and meat continues to occupy a central role on the menu, as the excellent breaded capocollo readily attests. Alongside these, freshly harvested vegetables, drawn in part from the family’s own kitchen gardens, find their place, together with a generous procession of antipasti and first courses frequently entrusted to fresh pasta, such as the riccioli sampled during our most recent visit. Considerable attention is also dedicated to wine, with a cellar of over 300 labels. For those wishing to prolong the pleasure of their stay, the family offers a bed and breakfast adjacent to the restaurant, the perfect conclusion to a generous dinner.

Name: La Cucoma
Description: In the heart of the Ravenna hinterland, this timeless and family-spirited venue is one of the most convincing expressions of Romagnan seafood cooking. A place one arrives at with pleasure and returns to willingly, not least thanks to a particularly attractive quality-to-price ratio. The menu pays homage to the flavours of the northern Adriatic through traditional recipes executed with care and the freshest of fish: from mantis shrimp to steamed skate wings, from marinated oily fish to raw seafood, through to crispy fried dishes and the ever-present spaghetti with "poverazze" – the typical Adriatic clams. Generous wood-fired grills are not lacking either, an authentic symbol of local maritime conviviality. A sincere, flavourful cuisine deeply rooted in its local area.

Name: La Dispensa di Armatore
Description: A very small, atypical restaurant, almost a bistro with only tables outside, at the counter with stools overlooking the sea or in the more classic dehors. The menu lists several fish recipes! You will find bluefin tuna, anchovies, squid... after all, the owners have been involved in fishing for four generations. Those with a sweet tooth should know that there is only one dessert on offer, the spumone, made for them by a nearby artisan ice-cream parlour. The dish that won the inspector over: octopus tentacles with chickpea hummus and anchovy colatura, simple but very tasty!

Name: La Fratanza
Description: Follow your satnav and you’ll easily find this private residence situated just outside the village. The restaurant is family run and furnished in classic style, with an attractive veranda room overlooking the garden. The friendly owner serves regional cuisine, all carefully prepared using top-quality local ingredients, some of which (such as the delicious lemons and excellent San Marzano tomatoes that appear in a number of dishes) are grown in the restaurant’s own orchard and kitchen garden. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the ravioli di genovese served with onions and pecorino cheese.

Name: La Gioconda
Description: In the evocative 17th-century cellars of Palazzo Brancuti – a historic noble residence in the centre of Fossombrone, characterised by its charming vaulted ceilings – chef and owner Giacomucci has been serving cuisine deeply rooted in the Marche hinterland for over twenty years. His menu alternates between traditional recipes, reimagined with a contemporary twist, and creations that showcase the region’s finest produce and his own creative flair. Examples include Furlo snails with a courgette and pea purée, or the surprising crema catalana flavoured with Marsala. During the season, black truffles, mushrooms and, above all, the prized white truffle take centre stage on a dedicated menu. There is also a strong focus on wine, showcased through a selection of around 500 wines that reflects a genuine passion for the world of wine.

Name: La Locanda Gesù Vecchio
Description: In the picturesque alleyways of Spaccanapoli, an authentic trattoria unfolds across two spaces – at different street numbers (the other at number 4) – yet sharing the same soul: closely set tables in simple rooms, a lively and informal atmosphere, and young, smiling service. The cuisine is a hymn to Neapolitan tradition, with dishes that evoke the aromas of home: pasta mista with potatoes and smoked provola, crispy fried salt cod on escarole cream, and the lemon caprese, fresh and fragrant, perhaps enjoyed with a small glass of artisanal limoncello. Reservations and punctuality are essential, even at lunch, to secure this genuine experience.

Name: La Locanda del Falco
Description: This is the sort of small family-run restaurant that everyone would like to have as their local, where courteous and friendly service go hand-in-hand with good traditional cuisine. Dishes such as ravioli del plin, vitello tonnato, beef tartare and veal tongue are some of the daily specials marked up on the blackboard here. The wine list comes as a pleasant surprise, with its excellent selection of labels from Piedmont and further afield.

Name: La Pignata
Address: Viale Dei Tigli 7, Ariano Irpino, 83031, Italy
Description: For over 40 years the Ventre family have been championing the flavours of Irpinia, seeking out the region’s best seasonal ingredients. These are then used in traditional dishes such as soups, as well as in more personal reinterpretations of local specialities (their “post-modern” arancino is now renowned in the region) that nonetheless retain all their original flavour with influences from both Campania and Puglia. The pizza here is excellent and there’s also a good selection of wine.

Name: La Pineta
Description: Patience and perseverance are required to navigate the winding mountain roads through forests and hills to reach La Pineta, but the cuisine makes the journey worthwhile. The menu focuses on a tasting format that can be customized with fewer courses, and has always featured the restaurant’s iconic dish: fritto misto alla piemontese – a Piedmontese mixed fry. The appetizers are equally impressive, offering generous portions with an array of delightful small tastings.

Name: La Taverna delle Follie
Description: This restaurant with a discreet sign is situated in a small village overlooked by a splendid Norman castle. Meals are served either in the simple yet comfortable dining room or in the charming outdoor space in fine weather. The reasonably priced cuisine celebrates the sea in its many varied fish and seafood dishes, which range from pasta with shellfish or seafood to fish guazzetto (a tomato-based stew) with green vegetables and even raw fish options. Among the desserts, we particularly recommend the babà.

Name: La Torre One Fire
Description: Before reaching the restaurant, housed within an ancient tower that played a significant role during the Napoleonic era in Naples and under Joachim Murat, it is well worth taking a stroll to the nearby viewpoint overlooking Capri. An evocative prelude to a culinary experience that celebrates the most authentic traditions of Campania. In a cosy, family-friendly atmosphere, the kitchen serves up local dishes prepared with care and without any frills: highlights include the excellent ravioli alla caprese, aubergine parmigiana, potato gâteau and a particularly delicious selection of fried seafood. To round off the picture, there is the warm hospitality of the Mazzola family, who welcome guests with genuine friendliness.

Name: La Villa
Address: Contrada Cavallerizza, SS 303 verso Rocchetta Sant'Antonio, Melfi, 85025, Italy
Description: This country restaurant owes its welcoming atmosphere to the special attentions of the family management. The menus are based on traditional recipes that do full justice to the local produce.

Name: Laghetto
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the delightful village of Brusson at an altitude of 1 300m in the verdant Val d'Ayas, this restaurant is part of the hotel of the same. In a dining room decorated in typical mountain style, enjoy well-prepared dishes made from regional ingredients. The delicious specialities include light Aosta Valley pancakes (made from rice flour), local cheeses, cured meats, plenty of meat options and fish such as trout and char.

Name: Le Antiche Sere
Description: A small restaurant overlooking the brackish waters of Lake Lesina, where everything revolves around the professionalism and experience of chef-owner Biscotti, assisted by his two sons. The menu celebrates the flavours of Daunia, with particular emphasis on both sea fish and lake fish, cooked in classic tradition yet presented with a pleasingly modern and colourful touch. Among the most representative creations is their original dessert – now a true signature – “rigatoni al pomodoro”: puffed-pasta rigatoni filled with whipped ricotta, tomato jam and shavings of white chocolate.

Name: Le Due Lanterne
Description: A young, dynamic couple of professionals has revitalized this historic restaurant in the heart of town, facing the lively main square and beloved by neighborhood regulars. The menu celebrates Piedmontese tradition – think carne battuta, plin, braised Fassona beef, and bonet – elevated with the chef’s creative touches, such as onion stuffed with sausage and Castelmagno cream – a dish that alone is worth the visit! The hospitality is spontaneous and kind. Reservations? Highly recommended: the venue’s reputation is once again at its peak.

Name: Le Miniere
Description: Situated on the main square of a charming village, this hotel-restaurant dates back to the late 19C and is run by the friendly Arsini family. The setting here is truly picturesque, thanks to the village’s location on a green and sunny ridge in the Val Chiusella, surrounded by cyclamen bushes and majestic birch and chestnut trees. Meanwhile, the Piedmontese dishes offer excellent value for money, with a focus on local ingredients and produce from the wider region. If you’re a fan of traditional cuisine, don’t miss the tripe alla campagnola with polenta taragna whipped with butter, while in season the roast cardo gobbo served with a delicious bagna cauda and truffle is a must. A stroll around the small village offers the perfect conclusion to your meal.

Name: Lerchner's In Runggen
Description: This establishment is dedicated to traditional South Tyrolean cuisine, alongside its own farm with beef cattle. Great attention is paid to both the details and the ambiance, and the dishes – always generous, with many available as small tastings called “Tyrolean tapas” – celebrate the finest ingredients and most delightful regional recipes. The specialties follow the seasons: Gröstl (a roast of beef and pork with potatoes, onion, and speck), Tirtlan (rye fritters), and the essential apple strudel, along with homemade bread and breadsticks, are also available for takeaway. The wine list fully embraces the essence of South Tyrol.

Name: Li Somari
Description: Situated at the entrance to the historic centre, this restaurant is an unmissable stop for anyone wishing to discover authentic Lazio meat dishes, characterised by intense, authentic flavours deeply rooted in tradition. Alongside the region’s great classics, there is no shortage of interesting culinary references to neighbouring regions and a carefully selected range of fish dishes. In the kitchen led by Adriano Baldassarre, a special place is reserved for offal, prepared with skill and flair: among the most popular dishes are the pan-fried chicken giblets – a symbol of Roman tradition – and grilled marrow served with beef tartare and truffle potatoes. The dessert menu is also very well put together, offering a wide range of choices including seasonal fruit, timeless classics and house specialities.

Name: Lo Stuzzichino
Address: Via Deserto 1/a, Sant'Agata sui Due Golfi, 80061, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In the heart of Sant’Agata sui Due Golfi, this cosy, family-run restaurant charms guests with its authentic atmosphere, featuring traditional ceramics, thoughtful details and an open kitchen that makes the experience all the more engaging. Guests are welcomed by a charismatic host, who is deeply knowledgeable about the finest produce from Campania and is on hand to help them choose their dishes and explain their origins and characteristics. The cuisine celebrates the region’s culinary heritage with simplicity and flavour, making the most of seasonal ingredients and local produce. The focus is very much on produce, with many vegetables sourced directly from the family vegetable garden, lending a sense of freshness and authenticity to the dishes. A sincere and generous meal that makes you want to come back again and again.

Name: Locanda Cacciatori
Address: Località Mistadello di Castione, Ponte dell'Olio, 29028, Italy
Description: Locanda Cacciatori, housed in a former carpenter’s workshop, lies in the quiet heart of Val Nure, amid the scent of wood and country air. The restaurant celebrates Piacenza cuisine with dishes that revive the authentic flavors of times past, elevated by skilled hands. In winter, the warmth of broth envelops handmade meat anolini, small parcels of flavor steeped in tradition. In fine weather, an inviting terrace beckons guests outdoors, amid rustling leaves and gentle sunshine, for an experience that speaks of home and memory.

Name: Locanda Mariella
Description: Reservations must be made at least 24 hours in advance by email, choosing from three menus: tradition, land, or fish. The rest is history, if not legend, for what has been one of the best trattorias in the province (we’d venture to say the region) since the 1960s. In a corner of the Parmesan Apennines, Mariella continues to delight guests with the same family management, enhanced by a Japanese cook who adds a slightly more modern touch to select recipes. Recently, a comfortable lounge area with good background music has been added.

Name: Locanda Pincelli
Description: Named after the village’s former postman, an important and charismatic character in this small community, this former workers’ club is housed in a rustic restaurant with a beautiful porch where you sit in summer beneath cooling fans. The cuisine steps away from local tradition to offer creative yet never overly fanciful dishes which are always generous and beautifully presented. We particularly enjoyed the mezze maniche pasta with stewed white onion, sour butter and burnt lemon, as well as the leg of guinea fowl browned with paprika, its own juices and horseradish mayonnaise. When choosing your wine, you might like to ask owner Danilo for his recommendations from a list which is not extensive but is certainly interesting and carefully chosen.

Name: Locanda al Cervo - zum Hirschen
Address: Via Schrann 9/c, San Genesio Atesino, 39050, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in a pleasant location on the Altopiano del Salto plateau just a few kilometres from Bolzano, this restaurant has been run by five generations of women, all of whom enshrine a strong connection with the local land through their top-quality cuisine. The menu here showcases delicious, generously portioned cuisine from the South Tyrol (the veal cheek fondant, taragna polenta mousse, cocoa shavings and sour radishes is superb) which is prepared for the most part from home-produced ingredients and served in typical, modernised dining rooms or on the bright, airy panoramic terrace. To enjoy the relaxing atmosphere of San Genesio to the full, we recommend booking one of the rooms in the inn and maybe even taking one of their Haflinger horses out for a ride.

Name: Locanda da Condo
Address: Via Fontana 134, Col San Martino, 31010, Italy
Description: Immersed in the wine-growing landscape of Prosecco, among orderly hills and rows of vines that define the territory, Condo is a historical family-run trattoria, the custodian across several generations of the Venetian gastronomic tradition. The interiors, warm and full of character, speak of the simple charm of the old country table; in summer, a pleasant veranda enveloped in climbing plants offers outdoor dining of genuine and unhurried character, perfectly suited to savouring the tranquillity of the surroundings. The cooking faithfully follows the rhythms of the territory, with dishes that are intense and substantial, in which meat occupies a central role: the roast goose leg is excellent, rich and succulent; the rabbit in the pan is traditional and reassuring, while the braised pork cheek wins one over through its tenderness and depth of flavour. Completing the offering, a selection of produce – mushrooms, radicchio and other regional excellences – that enters the menu in keeping with the natural course of the seasons.

Name: Locanda del Barone
Address: Località San Vittorino, Caramanico Terme, 65023, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in a district of Caramanico, this typical stone house is home to an attractive restaurant that is the perfect choice for anyone keen on typical Abruzzo specialities. Prepared from regional ingredients, the dishes are delicious and substantial.

Name: Locanda delle Grazie
Address: Via San Pio X 2, Grazie, 46010, Italy
Description: A long-established family-run concern, opened many years ago and today a cornerstone of traditional Mantuan cooking: forthright, generous and of consistent quality, in the heart of the small and evocative village of Curtatone. Here the classic repertoire is never found wanting: tortelli di zucca, local cured meats, pike in salsa verde, long-braised meats, sbrisolona, zabaione... simple and fragrant dishes of genuine homely character, served in abundant portions at prices that are more than reasonable.

Name: Lokanda Devetak
Address: Via Brezici 22, località San Michele del Carso, Savogna d'Isonzo, 34070, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A historic and rightly famous restaurant. The same family – now in its sixth generation – has been celebrating the flavours of the region since 1870, just a stone's throw from the Slovenian border, where traditions and aromas blend seamlessly together. Authentic emotions are brought to the table: Palatschinke lasagne with mushrooms and pumpkin béchamel sauce, veal tripe à la Carsolina flavoured with bay leaves and pecorino cheese, and the traditional “Kraško pecivo”, a soft cake with raisins and walnuts, accompanied by cinnamon ice cream. The wine cellar, lovingly curated by the owner, boasts 1,000 labels and a rich selection of wines by the glass, with local wines taking centre stage.

Name: Luna Rossa
Address: Via Marconi 18, Terranova di Pollino, 85030, Italy
Description: Nestled in the heart of the Pollino National Park, Luna Rossa is an authentic local trattoria that makes tradition its hallmark. The cuisine is based on traditional recipes handed down from generation to generation, prepared with meticulous care and enhanced by carefully selected local ingredients. From charcoal-grilled carchiola to strascinati made with local flours, each dish reflects the traditions, flavours and culture of these mountains. The experience is made even more engaging by the presence of the owner, a passionate storyteller who knows the local area and its culinary traditions inside out.

Name: Magazzino 52
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: The dining room, defined by characteristic brick ceilings, retains the memory of its warehouse origins, while the numerous labels displayed on shelves – available for retail purchase at a modest discount – attest to a broad and carefully curated selection, justifying the establishment’s self-description as “wine and dishes.” The kitchen presents a concise yet thoughtfully composed menu built on the quality of its ingredients: nods to Piedmontese tradition, select seafood offerings, and creative touches in the accompaniments, all designed to showcase the principal components. Dishes may be ordered individually or as part of generous and flexible mini-tastings, customizable to the guest’s preference. An excellent address in one of the city’s most elegant neighborhoods.

Name: Magnagallo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just a minute’s drive from the Campogalliano motorway exit, this ultra-classic restaurant has made a name for itself over the years thanks to its excellent price-quality ratio, which has remained surprisingly stable even at times when inflation has been high. The menu features numerous traditional Emilian dishes — gnocco fritto, tortellini, and Emilian-style “fritto misto” — alongside some of the great classics of Italian cuisine.
