The finale is left to the cake counter, situated right at the entrance to the restaurant: a riot of homemade desserts that invites you to choose whatever takes your fancy, following the inspiration of the moment and ending your meal on a truly indulgent note.

Name: Maso Palù
Description: Along the road that climbs towards Monte Baldo, and in business since 1984, this venue is a maso in name and spirit alike (they cultivate apples), and its atmosphere reflects this. The cuisine naturally celebrates the Trentino local area: local charcuterie and cheeses, orzotto, canederli, game, polenta and strudel. Open seven days a week in summer, and from Friday to Sunday in the rest of the year.

Name: Me Cumpari Turiddu
Description: With its old chandeliers, chairs and tables, this original and attractive restaurant offers its guests a feel of traditional Sicily. The cuisine focuses on typical Sicilian specialities, as well as offering a simpler, less expensive bistro menu. There’s also a shop selling food produce and a cocktail bar, which is open non-stop from 11. 30am until the early hours of the morning.

Name: Mezzolitro Vini e Cucina
Description: In the heart of Rho old town, among the quiet lanes of the restricted traffic zone, lies a corner of Abruzzo that exudes authenticity. A tempting, family-run refuge where a simple atmosphere meets refined, welcoming details. Tradition takes shape in dishes that tell stories of genuine flavours: such as the famous “chitarra alla teramana”, fresh pasta covered in a rich and enveloping sauce, with little meatballs and the bold touch of pecorino cheese. An invitation to sit down, indulge and feel right at home.

Name: Mingone
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In addition to the usual dishes from Lazio, this restaurant which has been renowned for its local cuisine for over a century also serves a few seafood and freshwater fish specialities, as well as its famous meat and fish dishes cooked over the barbecue grill. The many rooms include a classic-style dining room decorated with frescoes, while the wine list includes some rare labels and interesting vertical options.

Name: Molin Vecio
Description: In the idyllic setting of a 16C mill with a garden and small lake, this restaurant boasts an equally magical dining room with a warm, friendly and traditional feel. Top-quality dishes from the Veneto include a delicious sopressa(the region’s cured ham), Vicenza-style baccalà (cod) with Marano polenta and a soft guancetta served with a superb pendolòn (potato polenta).

Name: Namo Ristobottega
Address: Via Giovan Battista Marzi 1, Tarquinia, 01016, Italy
Description: Namo is renowned for the excellent cuisine conjured up by its chef Tiziana Favi, who creates unmissable dishes such as paccheri pasta with tomato and stracciatella cheese served with a bread crumble – you’ll want to mop up every crumb! Make sure you also ask the enthusiastic owner for her food and wine recommendations. Seasonal ingredients from the Viterbo region take centre stage here, while the chef’s green philosophy is clearly explained on the first page of the menu. Book in advance if you want to enjoy the views from the beautiful outdoor space, as there are only a few tables here.

Name: Nangalarruni
Description: This restaurant, named after the ancient Sicilian musical mouth instrument similar to a small flute and used in folk music, is located in the heart of the historic center. It features a spacious outdoor area for the summertime and interior spaces that predominantly use materials such as wood and stone. The cuisine pays homage to traditional local dishes, expertly crafted and "revitalized," using ingredients that mostly come from the Madonie Park where the location is situated. The mushroom specialties are not to be missed, and the wine selection is also excellent.

Name: Nerina
Address: Via De Gasperi 31, località Malgolo, Romeno, 38010, Italy
Description: In business since 1969, you’ll find it set among the picturesque landscapes of the Val di Non, with its apple orchards and charming villages. The culinary offering is centred on local produce or, more broadly, Alpine specialities: cured meats from Nones, Valsugana ‘spin’ maize gnocchi with mortandela and casolét fondue, as well as canederli with Moena ‘puzzone’ fondue are just a few examples of the most delicious dishes.

Name: Nida
Description: Just a short walk from the old town, enjoy a stroll along the ancient walls: a delightful itinerary that sets the scene for the experience ahead. The cosy and welcoming restaurant boasts a vibrant interior where you can choose to sit at the counter, facing the chef, or at tables with comfortable sofas. The menu is a journey through Japanese tradition, interwoven with the chef's childhood memories: fresh sashimi, impeccable nigiri, the famous gyoza and ramen with rich broth, just like in Southern Japan. At lunchtime, don't miss the teishoku: choose your main course and the chef will complete the dish with a refined selection of Japanese appetisers.

Name: Oishi
Description: Located in the heart of the city center, Oishi offers a comprehensive tribute to Japan in an intimate, minimalist yet colorful dining room that has been recently renovated. This homage to Japan is evident both in the interior design and – above all – in the numerous and ongoing classic Japanese references throughout the menu. Sometimes reimagined with local ingredients and flavors, the dishes range from crudo and marinated preparations to sashimi and nigiri, rolls, some tempura, and more. The wine selection is respectable, featuring Italian craft beers with flavors consistently oriented toward the East.

Name: Old Friend
Address: Via Giuseppe Cesare Abba 51, Cagliari, 09126, Italy
Description: Tucked away a little off the beaten track from the main shopping streets, this restaurant charms diners with its contemporary, relaxed atmosphere, featuring stylish design touches, good background music and attentive, professional service. The cuisine strictly follows the rhythm of the seasons, creating original dishes that are deeply rooted in local identity, such as the delicious spiced aubergine with almonds and fig leaves. Beyond individual creations, the common thread is the pursuit of flavour and balance. As well as the à la carte menu, guests can choose from three different tasting menus, which also include dishes created specifically for these menus.

Name: Ostaria Pignatelli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: A stone's throw from the neoclassical Villa Pignatelli, with the municipal gardens in front and the sea just beyond, lies a haven of authentic charm: you can sit outside or inside, where the décor is reminiscent of an elegant tavern. “You only live once, so eat well” is the motto here, and when you see the dishes arriving at your table, you can't help but agree. Neapolitan classics executed to perfection and served in generous portions: from “mozzarella in carrozza” (fried mozzarella sandwiches) to cuoppo of fried anchovies, from mixed pasta with potatoes and provola cheese to “candele alla Genovese” (pasta with beef ragout), Neapolitan-style cod and “Pastiera”, all of which are truly unmissable. Reservations? Absolutely! Even for lunch.

Name: Ostaria Tyrol
Description: In the heart of this picturesque mountain resort, this contemporary restaurant is situated on the ground floor of the Post Hotel, within the restricted traffic zone. The simple, cosy interiors offer a contemporary take on traditional mountain taverns, featuring extensive use of wood and understated elegance. The cuisine follows the same philosophy: straightforward, authentic and deeply rooted in the region, with a strong focus on meats, cured meats and cheeses. Standout specialities include beef tartare with brioche and cranberries, canederli, polenta with venison goulash and the unmissable strudel served with whipped cream, as well as our own homemade ice cream. Please note that the venue does not accept bookings, but its particularly long opening hours make it easy to visit.

Name: Osteria Bar Sport
Address: Strada Alessandria in San Germano 85, Casale Monferrato, 15033, Italy
Description: In what was once a typical sports bar, the friendly owner-chef serves home-style cuisine featuring traditional dishes from Monferrato and further afield. Don’t miss his plin pasta served with a roast meat sauce and a delicate cream of leeks, cotechino sausage and raw Mazara prawns. The atmosphere here is pleasantly informal and relaxed.

Name: Osteria Bartolini
Address: Via A. Boito 26, Milano Marittima, 48015, Italy
Description: Having already proved a success at its Cesenatico and Bologna branches, this modern seafood restaurant has found a particularly picturesque location here, on the ground floor of a building situated between the beach and the small harbour. The cuisine pays homage to Adriatic tradition through simple, comforting dishes, ranging from sardines sautéed in oil and lemon to tomato risotto enriched with fish, served ‘the old-fashioned way’, as the menu puts it. A great deal of attention is paid to fried dishes, the restaurant’s true speciality, while the daily specials are determined by what’s available at the Cesenatico fish market, ensuring freshness and seasonal variety. Rounding off the range are desserts, ice creams and baked goods made in our own bakery, further evidence of our commitment to quality and craftsmanship.

Name: Osteria Bartolini
Description: The sister restaurant of the Bologna and Milano Marittima restaurants of the same name, this osteria serves fresh fish with an excellent choice of delicious and generously portioned dishes. As the restaurant doesn’t take bookings, make sure you get here early in high season or during busy periods.

Name: Osteria Bartolini
Description: Under the majestic vaulted ceiling of Palazzo Dondini Ghiselli and in the shade of an old plane tree, this restaurant combines a simple ambience with an innovative concept. Here, guests can enjoy typical seafood dishes from Romagna – don’t miss the delicious sardines sautéed in oil and lemon, which are a real treat!

Name: Osteria Borsò Gambrinus
Address: Via Capitello, 20, San Polo di Piave, 31020, Italy
Description: Casual and relaxed, the atmosphere is just like that of a typically traditional tavern, consisting of a series of pleasant little dining rooms, while the menu combines local specialities with fresh seafood dishes.

Name: Osteria Didù
Description: A small establishment in the heart of the historic centre, where simple and genuine cooking pays homage to the flavours of the sea and the Ligurian tradition. Quality ingredients, dishes executed with care and a decidedly competitive bill make it an ideal port of call for those in search of authenticity without affectation. Among the most accomplished offerings, the stoccafisso accomodato alla ligure stands out, a great classic interpreted with respect and taste.

Name: Osteria Expanificio
Description: Situated in the historic centre between the Pirandello theatre and the belvedere, this former bakery has been transformed into a modern, welcoming restaurant that has recently been expanded to include an evening cocktail bar (the Buvette del Panificio). The menu features a superb selection of some of the island’s most famous dishes, including stuffed sardines, Robiola goat’s cheese, Palermo-style sword fish and ricotta cassata.

Name: Osteria La Pimpinella
Description: Situated in the historic centre but near a square with a car park, this modern inn serves Piedmontese cuisine which is contemporary in style yet still firmly anchored in local traditions. The generously portioned, well-presented dishes on the menu include vitello tonnato (excellent – we tried it!), tajarin pasta, Bra sausage and casseroles (the soft suckling pig cheek was delicious), all of which are as much a feast for the eyes as for the palate. The restaurant is run by an enthusiastic couple, aided by proficient and courteous staff with a feminine touch.

Name: Osteria La Solita Zuppa
Description: In the heart of the historic centre of Chiusi, the authentic spirit of a true Tuscan trattoria pervades the air, between evocative barrel-vaulted ceilings and a cool terrace that invites one to linger. Here a love of regional cooking finds expression in the revival of ancient recipes, presented with the generous richness of flavour that characterises the local tradition. Among the dishes recommended by our Inspector, the fragrant artichoke and mint soup and the refined rabbit with ginger, inspired by an ancient medieval preparation, stand out.

Name: Osteria La Torre
Description: To get to this welcoming restaurant, it’s best to leave the car in one of the convenient car parks just outside the town walls a short walk from Cherasco’s quiet, picturesque historic centre with its two perpendicular streets. At Osteria La Torre, the friendly female staff will happily guide you through the menu, which features traditional dishes prepared in contemporary style – we particularly enjoyed the egg, cardoon and fondue dish, followed by breaded veal rump as our main course. If you’re a fan of snails, you really must try them here as Cherasco is renowned for this speciality. The extensive wine list demonstrates the same high quality as the cuisine.

Name: Osteria Le Panzanelle
Description: Just outside Radda, in a small hamlet, a rustic little house welcomes guests with a territorial cuisine that is solid and full of flavour. Handmade fresh pasta, seasonal produce and a well-considered wine list – anything but predictable, and firmly rooted in the local area – contribute to an authentic and satisfying experience. Much appreciated by both tourists and local regulars alike, the restaurant is often full: booking is therefore strongly recommended.

Name: Osteria Madonnetta
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the square with its famous chessboard, this authentic trattoria boasts a warm, inviting dining room and an outdoor space shaded by wisteria. Run by the same family for 120 years, the restaurant serves regional specialities such as tripe soup, bigoli pasta with various sauces, Vicenzo-style bacalà (salted cod), Venetian liver and desserts such as zaeti biscuits and macafame bread pudding. As there are just a few tables and the restaurant is very popular, booking ahead is recommended.

Name: Osteria Magona
Address: Località Vallone dei Messi 199, SP 16/b km 2,400, Bolgheri, 57020, Italy
Description: Amidst vineyards and the renowned cypress avenue, Osteria Magona is a must-visit for meat enthusiasts and Tuscan regional cuisine aficionados. Impeccable are the famous soups, from ribollita to pappa al pomodoro, alongside gnudi and fresh pastas. The wine list offers ample room to various Bolgheri labels.

Name: Osteria Mondo d'Oro
Description: The osteria as envisioned by celebrated three-Michelin-starred chef Giancarlo Perbellini: a place, indeed, a “world,” where guests can savor fragrant Italian classics and vegetarian options in a relaxed atmosphere at remarkably honest prices, complemented by an excellent selection of wines by the glass. The inspector enjoyed: pasta reale in capon broth, Amarone-braised beef cheek with potato purée and fried leek. Right in the city center, tucked along a side street off Via Mazzini, diners may choose between the intimate indoor dining room and the alfresco terrace (weather permitting!).

Name: Osteria Numero 2
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: La Fefa is the perfect place for lovers of authentic flavours from the Emilia region. The Inspector sums it up like this: “Flicking through the menu you want to try everything!” - and this really is the case. Start your meal off with a selection of the finest charcuterie, in which an outstanding Culatello di Zibello, accompanied by a “Gnocco Fritto” not to be missed reigns supreme. Continue with excellent homemade, fresh-egg pasta followed by main courses made up exclusively of meat, in keeping with local tradition. The dessert page is deliciously tempting, offering an extensive selection of sweet treats: trifle, biscuits served with warm zabaione, “taccolenta degli Estensi” cake and lots of other specialities that evoke memories of the region’s cuisine. Fragrant and generous flavours, served in a simple but charming dining room featuring a splendid wooden ceiling recovered from an old country haybarn.Great attention is also paid to the winelist, which boasts impressive vintages and a meticulously curated selection, skilfully put together by talented sommelier Edoardo, that completes a rich, sincere and profoundly Emilian gastronomic experience.

Name: Osteria Ophis
Description: Situated in the beautiful historic pedestrianised centre of Offida, this restaurant with a brick-vaulted ceiling is housed in the former stables of an old palazzo with a modern, inviting and intimate feel. Here, owner-chef Daniele Citeroni Maurizi skilfully reinterprets regional cuisine to create precise, imaginative dishes that are full of flavour. The stuffed cannelloni cooked on the barbecue grill are delicious, as is the veal tartare served with a warm meat, herb and vegetable jus on the side. We should also highlight the “low cost” tasting menu available for guests aged under 25.

Name: Osteria Piazzetta Cattedrale
Description: Just a stone’s throw from Ostuni’s 15th-century co-cathedral, dedicated to Santa Maria dell’Assunzione, a husband and wife passionately run this refined and cosy gourmet gem. The interiors, adorned with mirrors and ceramics on the walls, evoke the atmosphere of an elegant private drawing room, enhanced by floors and chandeliers of remarkable quality. In the kitchen, Mrs Marilea offers a selection of regional recipes featuring both land and sea fare – simple yet prepared with great care. There is also a significant range of artisanal produce, including fresh pasta, bread, baked goods, cakes and ice cream. Among these, the ricotta ice cream with fig compote and toasted almonds, served on a sponge cake as a unique take on the zuccotto, is particularly worth mentioning. As well as the menu, the excellent value for money of the small traditional tasting menu is a real draw. Given the limited number of seats, particularly during busy periods, it is advisable to book in advance.

Name: Osteria Platzegg
Description: This comfortable and informal “Gasthaus” with a simple yet welcoming and contemporary feel is run by talented chef Herbert Hintner, the undisputed master of Alto Adige cuisine. Housed within a historic building in the town’s pedestrianised centre, the restaurant serves simple cuisine with a focus on regional recipes and ingredients (such as potato ravioli filled with speck ham and spleen crostini in broth) alongside a few Mediterranean-influenced dishes such as arancini in a gorgonzola sauce. The wine list, on the other hand, focuses uniquely on the Alto Adige.

Name: Osteria San Giulio
Address: Via Dulzago, Badia di Dulzago, 28043, Italy
Description: A timeless atmosphere lingers in this hamlet, a former rural abbey that speaks to the region’s deep ties with agriculture and its enduring traditions. Those same roots are reflected in the menu of this humble, almost austere osteria: agnolotti with roast meat sauce, local cured meats and cheeses, panissa, and bunet. Prices are very fair, especially with the Menù dell’Oste (under €40).

Name: Osteria Veglio
Description: With a convenient reserved parking space and an expansive terrace overlooking the Langhe panorama, the 1920s-built house greets guests with stylistic minimalism but gastronomic enthusiasm in its sincere regional cuisine proposal. The minimum selection à la carte comprises two courses excluding desserts.

Name: Osteria Zanchetti
Description: In the heart of Fossombrone’s charming historic centre, at the top of a picturesque narrow street, this superb contemporary osteria makes a striking first impression: as soon as you step inside, the medieval charm of the village gives way to interiors inspired by the elegance of the Roaring Twenties. Here, head chef and owner Luca Zanchetti draws on the experience he has gained in prestigious restaurants – many of which have been awarded Michelin stars – to create his own personal and creative take on regional cuisine. His dishes range from traditional classics, such as vanilla ice cream ‘drowned’ in Fano’s Moretta coffee, to original creations crafted from the excellent produce of the surrounding valleys. An authentic, contemporary dining experience that wins you over with its balance, character and warmth: the sort of trattoria that, as the inspectors agree, everyone would love to have on their doorstep.

Name: Osteria dal Moro
Description: A lively fish and seafood restaurant on the seafront, which is always busy thanks to its excellent value for money – booking ahead is highly recommended! Fish-based dishes only, all of which are announced at your table and which change regularly depending on market availability. The dishes are simple, rustic but full of flavour, which is why it’s easy to forgive the rather restricted choice of wine.

Name: Osteria de Börg
Description: In the characteristic Borgo San Giuliano so dear to Federico Fellini, with its narrow streets and colourful houses that were once home to the local fishermen, this excellent osteria celebrates the most typical Romagna cuisine, including the finest charcuterie, fresh homemade pasta (the traditional cappelletti in chicken broth are excellent) and meats, including Mora Romagnola pork, which is used in a variety of dishes. Inside, you'll find a setting that you would traditionally associate with a trattoria, complete with check cotton tablecloths and bottles on display.

Name: Osteria dei Maltagliati
Address: Via Regina Margherita 37, Torano Nuovo, 64010, Italy
Description: Run by Maicol and Federica, this cosy, rustic-style restaurant wins you over with its cuisine, which has its roots in tradition and is enhanced by the use of a wood-fired oven and a grill fuelled by its own embers. The cooking methods evoke authentic flavours and time-honoured traditions, reinterpreted with a contemporary sensitivity and a focus on the ingredients. In the warmer months, the wooden tables on the small, cool outdoor terrace offer a pleasant spot to relax, while the rooms above the restaurant allow you to extend your stay and enjoy the very best of Abruzzo’s authentic hospitality. Among the specialities not to be missed are the hand-rolled pasta dishes, prepared with artisan care, including the flavourful wild boar cappelletti with olives and sage, a true expression of the local area.

Name: Osteria dei Segreti
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Situated amid hills in a secluded and panoramic location, this farmhouse offers guestrooms, a spa and a restaurant, where meat (often cooked over the grill) takes pride of place on the menu, alongside various local specialities such as stuffed pigeon, roast goose and “coniglio in porchetta” (stuffed rabbit).

Name: Osteria del Boccondivino
Description: Access is via the inner courtyard of an elegant period building, where, on sunny days, the outdoor tables buzz with conversation and delicious smells. Upstairs, there is a large, bright dining room flanked by two cosy side rooms that are perfect for conversing. In the main room, a climate-controlled wooden display case catches the eye: inside are precious bottles, from the intense reds of Langa and Roero to wines that tell stories from every corner of the world. The menu is a journey through the flavours of Piedmont: dishes that exude tradition, such as “Gobbi di Nizza Monferrato” (cardoons drenched in velvety bagna cauda), or persimmon mousse paired with sweet chestnut cream. Every mouthful is a memorable encounter of textures and aromas. We recommend booking ahead, even for lunch!

Name: Osteria del Gallo e della Volpe
Address: Piazza Umberto I 14, Ospedaletto d'Alpinolo, 83014, Italy
Description: This restaurant in the centre of this small town is run by the Silvestro family (father and son). In summer, book one of the tables in the charming outdoor space overlooking the square. The menu focuses on local traditional cuisine with the occasional personalised twist, such as the pork-belly kebab with a papacelle reduction (short, pulpy peppers with a sweet flavour) and stracciata sauce, while the wine list features labels from the Irpinia region (and elsewhere) with a good choice of vertical wines and top-quality names such as Aglianico and Taurasi.

Name: Osteria del Mare già il "Votapentole"
Address: Via IV Novembre 15, Castiglione della Pescaia, 58043, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the city center, there's a small but lively restaurant with cheerful colors and a charming outdoor area on the pedestrian street. The atmosphere is always relaxed, even in summer when dining is only in the evening and tables are in high demand (reservations are essential). The menu is a journey through the sea: always featuring raw seafood, tuna amatriciana, cacciucco, and other classic dishes with imaginative touches.

Name: Osteria del Miglio 2.10
Address: Via Patrioti 2, Pieve San Giacomo, 26035, Italy
Description: A pleasant (and excellent) provincial restaurant with a modern feel and a traditional brick-vaulted ceiling, where owner-chef Samuele Miglioli pays tribute to local traditions in his cuisine (don’t miss the marubini pasta in three broths and the famous pumpkin tortelli). The dishes here focus on seasonal ingredients which are carefully transformed into generous dishes full of flavour, as demonstrated by the rice timbale served on a delicious beef ragù and topped with beef carpaccio. There’s also an excellent selection of wines, with a particular focus on sparkling wines.

Name: Osteria dell'Accademia
Description: Within an evocative medieval hamlet dating to the thirteenth century, with breathtaking views extending to the sea, this is an authentic osteria where the pleasures of local and regional home cooking may be savoured: the cappelletti with cream sauce and Grana are not to be missed, nor are the excellent gelati among the desserts. For a particularly memorable visit, reserve a table on the welcoming summer terrace, which enjoys wide-ranging views over the surrounding hills.

Name: Osteria della Villetta
Description: A bastion of tradition for over a hundred years, Art Nouveau furnishings and a retro atmosphere are the accompaniment to Brescian classics and familiar recipes: always based on seasonal ingredients, as in the case of the many vegetables from their own garden, from which the Evo oil also comes. The wine list offers a wide selection of labels from Franciacorta, Barolo and Barbaresco: true passion of the owner Massimo!

Name: Osteria la Fefa
Address: Via Trento e Trieste 9/c, Finale Emilia, 41034, Italy
Description: A beautiful farmhouse not far from the town, with a friendly, welcoming and colourful feel, where the menu features Italian dishes alongside a few local specialities, such as an excellent "bagna caoda". Special mention goes to the superb selection of beers chosen by owner Moreno, which ranges from local craft beers to labels from across the globe. There’s even a beer-themed dessert, the Birramisù. Offering excellent value for money, it is extremely popular, so booking ahead is recommended.

Name: Palazzaccio
Description: Following its recent relocation, this charming restaurant has found a new home in the heart of the historic centre, within an ancient building that still retains the charm of its origins, with its striking exposed stone walls left visible during the restoration. The interiors, now characterised by a contemporary bistro-inspired style, combine elegance and informality, while the selection of wines on display in the dining room reflects a particular focus on wine. Among the must-try dishes, the six-course starter menu stands out – a culinary journey that celebrates tradition and seasonal produce through locally sourced vegetables, cheeses and meats. Mushrooms are a must, especially in season, and take centre stage in dishes that authentically reflect the local cuisine.

Name: Palmerino - Il Bacalà a Sandrigo
Description: If you like cod, you’ll be in your element in this restaurant which serves this versatile fish in many different ways, from plain to salted (baccalà) and dried ((stoccafisso). The house speciality is the most famous dish of nearby Vicenza, namely bacalà alla vicentina (written with just one ‘l’ in this region and featuring dried rather than salted cod, despite the name). In addition to cod, the menu also includes other classic fish and seafood options as well as a few meat dishes.

Name: Perbacco - Vini e Cucina
Description: This quiet and elegant restaurant in a small street in the village of Cannara has a stylish yet friendly ambience and serves traditional, local cuisine where onion is a star ingredient in many of the dishes – don’t miss the delicious onion soup with gruyère cheese. If you’re choosing a wine to accompany your meal, we suggest asking enthusiastic owner Ernesto for his astute recommendations.

Name: Podere San Faustino
Address: Via San Faustino 33 (SS Emilia Nord), Fidenza, 43036, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Notable sake list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the beautiful countryside outside Cerreto Guidi, Villa Petriolo is a magnificent Medici residence offering luxurious rooms in a setting of outstanding charm. In addition to the beauty of the villa and its garden, overlooked by the restaurant’s terrace, the location benefits from the property’s delicious home-produced ingredients, such as extra-virgin olive oil, wine, Cinta Senese pork, meat and chicken, produce from the kitchen garden and ancient grains. The kitchen reinterprets these rich ingredients with a modern twist, offering two tasting menus — one of which for vegetarians — with dishes also available à la carte. Alternatively, Osteria di Golpaja offers authentic and intense flavours, those that have made Tuscany a renowned destination for lovers of fine dining.

Name: QuarantunoDodici
Description: 4112 are the naval coordinates of the location, and the choice is no coincidence: we are in the vicinity of a shipyard, just a few metres from the Tiber, looking out onto the moored vessels. Chef Lele Usai (the same hand behind the starred Il Tino on the floor above) prepares here simpler and more traditional cooking, with seafood classics such as spaghetti alle vongole lupini and grilled fish, yet always with the same exacting attention to the quality of the catch, in an informal and relaxed setting of an almost holiday atmosphere, particularly at the outdoor tables.

Name: Raieü
Address: Via Milite Ignoto 23, Cavi di Lavagna, 16033, Italy
Description: After over 60 years in business, this trattoria, which started out in a warehouse that was once used to store fishing nets, is still a reliable choice in terms of quality and price. Located in the centre of the little village, simple and old-fashioned, with outdoor seating overlooking the characteristic narrow street, it still serves the same deliciously tasty and generous Ligurian seafood cuisine it did when it first opened. The fish soup is a great classic, but is rivalled by some delicious versions of fish tartare.

Name: Rimulas
Description: This small restaurant in the historic centre of Voghera boasts a minimalist and contemporary-style decor in a quiet dining room from where you can observe the chef at work in the kitchen. The cuisine is local with personalised twists added by the chef, which make his dishes interesting and exciting. We particularly enjoyed the tagliolini with a heart ragù and Parmesan cheese cream, which is full of strong yet delicious flavours. The dining experience is enhanced by the warm welcome offered by the female owner, who is happy to recommend wines from the excellent selection from the Oltrepò Pavese and Alessandrino regions. Dishes are also available in half portions for guests with a smaller appetite.

Name: Roma
Description: Over a century of history and several generations of the family make this restaurant a solid institution in inland Liguria. Generous seasonal cuisine linked to the local area and the produce of the family's vegetable garden and orchards is served in the airy, classically styled dining room. Homemade pesto, mushrooms and truffles, excellent meat tartare and steak, not to mention a section dedicated to fish. Highlights include chestnut lasagnette on a fondue made with local cheese, and the quintessential Ligurian vegetable soup. In addition to the menu, tempting specials arrive daily from the market. But the secret to this restaurant's enduring success is also its warm, family-style welcome, making it an essential stop when travelling through the Apennines.

Name: Romani
Address: Via dei Ronchi 2, Vicomero di Torrile, 43056, Italy
Description: Traditional in atmosphere, starting from the rooms covered with decorations, to the cuisine, obviously from the area: this is the restaurant for those who do not like revisitations and exotic searches, but prefer to be reconfirmed in the classic Parmesan flavours: cured meats, fresh pastas, roasts and grilled meats, in a typical country farmhouse with a large garden and a store selling typical local food products.

Name: Romanè
Description: A lively trattoria just a stone’s throw from the Vatican, simple to the point of austerity, open continuously from midday until late in the evening and well known for its generous portions and the most unvarnished of Lazio cooking. Here the offal takes centre stage – from fried brain to trippa alla romana – alongside the classic pasta dishes of amatriciana and carbonara, served in a substantial format of a full 130 grams, saltimbocca alla romana, pollo alla cacciatora and the traditional ricotta and sour cherry tart. Directly opposite, the offering multiplies with Armare, an almost twin trattoria presenting the same menu enriched by seafood dishes, and with Arbanco, a neighbourhood rosticceria. Taken together, a true landmark of the Trionfale quarter, frequented by local residents and passing visitors alike in search of authentic flavours.

Name: Ronchi Rò
Address: Località Cime di Dolegna 12, Dolegna del Collio, 34070, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Ronchi Rò is an estate and agriturismo immersed in greenery, among the rolling hills of Collio and its lush woodlands: a borderland of captivating and almost fairy-tale character, celebrated for its extraordinary wines, the only ones to appear on the small dedicated list. The cooking of chef Fares Issa is flavoursome and forthright, vivid in colour and deeply seasonal. Drawing on a fine selection of local produce – salami, prosciutto, goose speck, cheeses – it also offers dishes of a more contemporary profile in which his imagination comes to the fore: excellent, for instance, the raviolacci filled with smoked potato and dressed with a sauce of marcundela, an ancient and increasingly rare local cured meat made from pork offal. The atmosphere is intimate: just six tables in a pleasingly modern dining room. Booking is advised.

Name: Rosselli 77
Description: A series of warm and cosy dining rooms, adorned with antique furniture – much of which is also for sale – leads into this simple, family-run restaurant situated on the outskirts of the village. Here, we rely on the chef’s recommendations, as he presents the available dishes each day. The menu changes frequently, but remains true to Piedmontese produce and traditions: from homemade green macaroni with sausage ragù to a cream of roasted chestnuts and mushrooms, right through to the excellent snails. An honest, authentic cuisine that celebrates the region with comforting, skilfully prepared dishes.

Name: Salotto sul Mare
Description: Steep steps lead up to the first floor of this building, which is home to owner-chef Giuseppe Costa’s main restaurant, Il Bavaglino. Here, the veranda-style dining room boasts spectacular views with the azure sea extending in all directions. The good, honest cuisine is full of flavour and simply prepared from top-quality ingredients, all showcased on an à la carte and three tasting-style menus that are perfect for sharing. In addition to an interesting wine selection, there’s also a choice of cocktails which offer a perfect alternative, even at lunchtime.

Name: Scannabue Caffè Restaurant
Description: This local restaurant is decorated in vintage style with books, furnishings and decor all evoking the early 20C. The cuisine is regional in flavour and includes some surprising technical touches – the “vasocottura” rabbit tuna (cooked in a jar) is superb, while the beef cheek with mashed potato is served with an intensely flavoured gravy. Top-quality, authentic cuisine.

Name: Sot'Ajarchi
Description: A typical seafood trattoria, this is the place to go if you love the traditional flavours of a cuisine that showcases excellent produce, starting with the famous moscioli (wild mussels) from the Conero. Pasta dishes with a variety of seafood sauces; as for main courses, in addition to the catch of the day, the squid skewers and the fish stew are particularly popular (the latter is available by prior booking and for a minimum of two people). A pleasantly informal and relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Stella
Description: Dining options at this restaurant include an attractive outdoor terrace with views of the surrounding area (in summer) and a friendly bistro-style dining room. We particularly enjoyed the linguine with carp roe, as well as the stuffed pigeon.

Name: Su Gologone
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: For many decades, the restaurant and hotel of the same name have represented one of the most beautiful photographs of the Sardinian hinterland. You can sit on the terrace with a breathtaking view of vineyards and olive groves or in one of the beautiful, rustic dining rooms decorated with Sardinian handicrafts, including one with a huge fireplace where you can watch the cooking of the famous porceddu. In fact, only traditional inland Sardinian cuisine is served, of which the suckling pig on the spit is certainly the most famous dish. Not to be outdone, however, are the dishes taken from the menu: the antipasto misto with cured meats and cheeses, and curious samplings of offal, pane frattau, kid with fennel, and various ice creams.

Name: Taverna 58
Description: In the heart of Old Pescara, on the very street where Gabriele D’Annunzio and Ennio Flaiano were born, Taverna 58 has been preserving the flavours of Abruzzo’s culinary traditions since 1980. The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, in keeping with the restaurant’s authentic, generous cuisine, which is deeply tied to the region. The table is laden with the ever-present arrosticini, the famous, sublime omelette with vegetables and goat’s cheese, and a host of meat specialities, ranging from lamb to pork, and from rabbit to wild boar. A single concession to the sea: salted cod (baccalà), served either raw (cured) or en papillote with onion marmalade. To round off, the distinctive white nougat from Abruzzo, renamed here ‘Oh pe’ la Maiella’. The wine cellar is also well worth a visit, as it houses artefacts from the Roman and medieval periods.

Name: Taverna Kerkira
Address: Corso Vittorio Emanuele 217, Bagnara Calabra, 89011, Italy
Description: This simple restaurant with a friendly atmosphere has been in business for 40 years, and is now one of the most popular eateries in this seaside town where singer Mia Martini was born. Situated near the centre and the sea, Taverna Kerkira serves Calabrian and Mediterranean dishes with influences from Greek cuisine (part of the family comes from Greece and the restaurant takes its name from the Greek word for Corfu), including excellent moussaka and farfalle pasta with Greek yoghurt.

Name: Taverna dei Caldora
Description: In the maze of alleys and narrow streets of Pacentro, one of Italy’s most beautiful villages, the Taverna de li Caldora is housed in a historic building overlooking the main square. Since 1978, the Cercone family has been serving cuisine firmly rooted in the traditions of Abruzzo, with a particular focus on the region’s ingredients. Specialities include maccheroni alla chitarra with saffron from L’Aquila and truffles, goat’s milk ricotta ravioli, and the unmissable grilled meats, particularly lamb chops and arrosticini. To round off the experience, there is a panoramic terrace offering a splendid view of the Peligna Valley.

Name: Taverna del Grappolo Blu
Address: Scale di via Moglio 1, Montalcino, 53024, Italy
Description: In the heart of Montalcino, this rustic and welcoming tavern offers authentic cuisine, built on tradition, simplicity and ingredients selected and prepared with passion. The most impressive dishes include homemade pici with meat sauce: an authentic, unpretentious version that captures the true flavour of the local cuisine. The wine list also deserves a mention, featuring a wealth of old vintages and characterised by a wide selection of local wines, to create the perfect pairing for every course.

Name: Terme
Description: Not far from the picturesque village of Pigna, this family-run hotel and restaurant embodies the simple charm of the cuisine of the Ligurian hinterland. The classic, timeless surroundings provide an ideal backdrop for a culinary experience centred on traditional recipes, authentic flavours and dishes with local roots. The house specialities include the great local classics and hearty dishes that reflect the valley’s culinary culture. The menu is regularly updated with daily specials, often featuring seasonal and locally sourced produce, such as the much-loved tortelli with porcini mushrooms. In the warmer months, the lovely outdoor seating area, shaded by a pergola, offers a picturesque view of the village, making the experience even more relaxing and authentic.

Name: Tipico Osteria dei Sensi
Description: The Locanda del Capitano and the Tipico offer menus showcasing traditional Umbrian dishes (the former serves gourmet cuisine, while the latter offers a simpler menu). The wine list boasts over 400 labels, while the olive oil selection includes the best oils from the region. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the “maritozzo di mazzafegato” (a type of sausage bun) with escarole, caramelised onions and olives.

Name: Trattoria Ai Due Platani
Description: One of the most celebrated venues in the province, this restaurant set in a tranquil country hamlet just outside the city requires reservations well in advance. The cuisine is firmly rooted in the land, yet never shies from a creative impulse, which emerges in both flavor and contemporary plating. Among the more contemporary offerings, the tender Apennine gray rabbit stands out: presented as an elegant terrine, accompanied by olive crumble, potato millefeuille, and peppers. A harmonious, delightful dish!

Name: Trattoria Antichi Sapori
Description: Just a few kilometres from the city, already enveloped in the tranquillity of the Parma countryside, this trattoria embodies to perfection the spirit of local cooking: a simple yet warm atmosphere, a homey welcome, and dishes that speak of the territory with forthright honesty. The menu revolves around the specialities of Parma, prepared with quality produce and a homely touch that wins one over from the very first mouthful. The tortelli alle erbette, made with an excellent locally sourced fresh ricotta, are not to be missed, a true emblem of the tradition. For those with a sweet tooth, the meal must conclude with the freshly churned mascarpone and praline ice cream: a delight for the unashamed gourmand. Patron Davide Censi is frequently to be found in the dining room: an opportunity not to be passed up, whether for a recommendation on the dishes of the day or for guidance towards a pairing that will do full justice to one’s choice.

Name: Trattoria Cibrèo - Il Cibrèino
Address: Via dei Macci 122 r, Florence, 50122, Italy
Description: A simple, authentic trattoria – not to be confused with the more elegant Ristorante Cibrèo next door, but rather similar to the nearby Caffè Cibrèo, of which it is an even more informal version – this historic Florentine establishment has for years remained a go-to spot for those seeking tasty, traditional cuisine without breaking the bank. The menu features dishes that have now become true house classics: tripe salad, vegetable minestrone with red rice, braised lampredotto, roast pork loin with mashed potatoes and, to finish, a caramel panna cotta that evokes memories. As the Inspector summarises: ‘It’s the restaurant I’d go to for a meal if I were on holiday in the city.’ A reassuring and distinctive establishment, true to its culinary philosophy and still much loved today by both Florentines and tourists.

Name: Trattoria Dentella
Description: Set against the picturesque backdrop of the Val Serina, this venue preserves the timeless charm of genuine family management, reflected in a warm and welcoming atmosphere. The deliberately concise menu pays tribute to local tradition through dishes of genuine character: from carpaccio of Orobica bresaola accompanied by a broccoli timbale and pecorino fondue, to the classic casoncelli with butter and pancetta. In season, mushrooms and truffles take centre stage – among them the prized black truffle of Bracca – while polenta, offered in several variations (Bergamasca or taragna, plain or enriched with strachitunt or a fried egg), remains the undisputed star. In fine weather, a panoramic terrace invites guests to enjoy the surrounding landscape. Front of house is managed entirely by women, attentive and smiling; at the stove, the man of the house tends faithfully to flavours and traditions.

Name: Trattoria Lanzagallo
Description: The spaces have been refreshed – simple yet more contemporary – without losing the venue’s authentic soul. The kitchen remains faithful to seafood traditions, offering a sound quality-to-price ratio, now elevated by a more polished presentation. Not to be missed are the raw scampi, delicately marinated with fine shavings of lemon zest, and the turbot baked in a potato crust, an enduring house classic. To finish, fragrant puff-pastry biscuits, served warm with confectioner’s custard. Long a fixture, and still today, a true reference point in the Ferrara area.

Name: Trattoria Losanna
Description: This little bastion of traditional Monferrato cuisine is situated in a rustic building on the side of a road outside Masio. Most of the dishes here are local in flavour (as is the wine), including specialities such as Russian salad, veal tongue in green sauce, braised beef marinated in Barbera wine and semifreddo al torrone dessert. The classic, comfortable dining rooms have a welcoming feel.

Name: Trattoria Pennestri
Address: Via Giovanni Da Empoli 5, Rome, 00154, Italy
Description: An authentic neighbourhood trattoria, were it not for the fact that its quality has by now carried its reputation well beyond the streets of Ostiense: the restaurant is often full and booking – by telephone only – is essential. The setting is simple and informal, yet has an immediate charm, entirely in keeping with the popular soul of the district. The kitchen focuses on the great Roman classics: carbonara, cacio e pepe, amatriciana and gricia open the dance of true flavours, accompanied by a few more creative proposals that add verve without distorting the identity of the house. Efficient and always smiling service completes the experience with courtesy and good advice, perfectly embodying the genuine spirit of the Roman trattoria of old.

Name: Trattoria Porteri
Description: Situated outside the centre in the equally typical and historic Borgo Trento district, this restaurant has all the warm ambience and character that you would expect of a traditional trattoria. The regional cuisine includes a remarkable array of charcuterie, as well as dishes such as tripe in Brescia-style broth, beef in olive oil and the typical local bocciolo di rosa dessert with zabaglione ice-cream.

Name: Trattoria Rosmarino
Description: Just a few steps from the central Piazza De Ferrari, this authentic trattoria – a point of reference for Ligurian cooking for fifteen years – continues to delight its guests with dishes prepared according to tradition. Its popularity is such that booking well in advance is almost always essential. Beyond the unmissable brandacujun and the classic trofie al pesto alla genovese, the accomplished chef Alessandro Massone also puts his name to a wealth of other specialities, born of passion, experience and a sincere devotion to the regional kitchen. A straightforward and generous table, one that tells the story of Liguria in all its nuances.

Name: Trattoria Via Vai
Description: A pleasant rural trattoria with a charming summer dining space overlooking the garden, just five minutes’ drive from Crema. In this simple, informal setting which is both well-kept and welcoming, guests dine either in the classic-style room with green wood-panelling or in the veranda-style dining room. Wherever you eat, you’ll enjoy regional specialities such as local hams and poultry, and Crema’s famous sweet tortelli. Foie gras also features very regularly on the menu.

Name: Trattoria al Parco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the small, bespoke dining rooms – our favourite is the more traditional one, where the warmth of the fogolar fireplace and the crackling of the embers accompany the owner's interactions with guests – this charming stone and brick house, surrounded by a wooded park, tells the story of the local area through its aromas and flavours. Charcoal grilling is the beating heart of the kitchen, releasing intense aromas that waft through the air; the creamy, comforting risottos are surprisingly well-balanced, an excellent example being that with clams, saffron and courgette flowers. The experience is completed by cosy guest rooms and a cellar where the house wine is made, with the family's own labels forming the basis of the wine list, reflecting an authentic bond with the land.

Name: Trattoria alla Ruota
Address: Via Proale 6, località Mazzano, Negrar, 37024, Italy
Description: Nestled among the Valpolicella hills, guests may settle into the cozy dining room with its fireplace, the charming veranda, or in fine weather the outdoor terrace. The warm hospitality ushers diners into the world of chef Renza Peretti, who celebrates local traditions while embracing modern inspiration. Noteworthy dishes include the Amarone-braised meat tortelli, duck terrine with puff pastry, and the passion fruit soufflé with vanilla ice cream. The wine list devotes many pages to the Verona region, with an impressively broad selection available by the glass.

Name: Trattoria da Fagiolino
Description: An authentic family-run trattoria, the sort you’d love to have just round the corner, with simple and typically rustic dining rooms and a friendly atmosphere. The menu is firmly rooted in Tuscan tradition, featuring fragrant, unpretentious dishes served with no frills, made with the finest ingredients: from Florentine-style tripe to a wide selection of fresh, homemade pasta, not to mention a huge choice of meats. The restaurant’s specialities include mushrooms, which are featured in a number of dishes. The Inspector particularly enjoyed the apple and puff pastry rose with cinnamon ice cream, which provided a delicate and fragrant finale. A stroll through the small but pretty village where the restaurant is located is also highly recommended.

Name: Trattoria da Paeto
Description: You follow narrow roads flanked by canals and surrounded by countryside to get to this warm and friendly restaurant with modern, comfortable dining rooms. The menu here always features a daily special of raw fish or seafood, served with creative seasoning, and sarde in saor (sardines). However, the true star of the show is cod (baccalà) – we recommend the triptych of baccalà which showcases the different traditional recipes of this fish to the full.

Name: Trattoria da Probo
Address: Via Provinciale Nord 13, Bagnolo in Piano, 42011, Italy
Description: A bulwark of traditional local cuisine, this trattoria serves antipasti such as erbazzone (a savoury pie), fried gnocchi and charcuterie, followed by fresh pasta (the cappelletti in broth are excellent), a choice of boiled and roast meat dishes, plus a selection of desserts. Chalked up on a blackboard by the entrance, the daily specials are also classic in style and vary depending on whatever is available in the market that day. Booking ahead is recommended!

Name: Trattoria da Zamboni
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the Berici hills, this restaurant run by a friendly and welcoming family boasts views of the surrounding greenery from its first-floor dining rooms. Although the cuisine focuses on local ingredients (in other words, mainly meat), the menu also includes a particularly delicious baccalà alla vicentina (salted cod).

Name: Trattoria della Fortuna
Description: An unassuming location, admittedly, close to a road junction, leading eventually to a simple dining room with a few outdoor tables. The cooking, however, is rather more interesting, ranging from the classics of Lazio (beginning with the pasta dishes featuring guanciale, namely gricia, amatriciana and carbonara) to recipes from other regions.

Name: Trattoria di Via Serra
Description: It’s well worth heading off the traditional tourist trail to experience this simple and informal trattoria in Bolognina, the city’s historic working-class district which now has a very multicultural feel. Run by a friendly owner, with his talented business partner at the helm in the kitchen, the restaurant boasts a welcoming and friendly ambience that has made it popular, so booking ahead is recommended, even at lunchtime. Top-quality regional cuisine is celebrated here, from fresh pasta (excellent tortellini in broth) to zuppa inglese (a type of trifle).

Name: Tre Noghere
Description: Situated in a peaceful location amid fields and vineyards, this attractive country restaurant run by the same family since 1965 boasts an outdoor space where three walnut trees (“tre noghere”) provide shade in summer, plus a neat and simple dining room. Traditional cuisine, including home-made pastas, are to the fore here – we particularly enjoyed the rabbit cooked in the oven which is served with a delicious potato millefeuille.

Name: Trippa
Description: Simple, informal and with a slightly retro feel, this restaurant serves a range of dishes from all over Italy, including the tripe which gives the restaurant its name. Unfussy and uncomplicated, the cuisine prepared by the skilful young chef using top-quality ingredients makes this one of the best trattorias in Italy. House specialities include Milanese risotto with grilled marrow, vitello tonnato and, of course, the ever-present tripe!

Name: TuMa
Description: Once home to the I Pupi restaurant, and run by the same team, this “new generation” osteria takes its name from chef Lo Coco’s children, Turi and Emma. The cuisine here is in the hands of the sous-chef, who pays tribute to Sicily and its glorious, colourful culinary traditions: caponata, aubergine balls, swordfish rolls and the catch of the day all feature on the menu. In summer, tables are laid out in the quiet alleyway behind the restaurant.

Name: Upepidde
Address: Vico Sant'Agnese 2, angolo corso Cavour, Ruvo di Puglia, 70037, Italy
Description: Quintessentially Apulian restaurant, beginning with its ambiance: a sequence of rooms excavated within the rock of ancient Aragonese walls. The cuisine is equally inspired by local traditions, encompassing cardoncelli mushrooms, burnt wheat orecchiette, and cheeses from the Murgia hills, to name a few, with almost exclusively meat dishes along with vegetarian options and delightful sweets.

Name: Vascello d'Oro
Description: The Vascello d'Oro, located in the heart of the village linked to the fat ox – the star attraction from November to Easter – has been welcoming guests to its cosy rooms steeped in history since 1887. If you are in company, ask if you can go down to the cellar: here, in the charming “Crota dl'amicissia”, a round table for ten people invites you to share bagna cauda in a warm and authentic atmosphere. The menu reflects Piedmontese tradition with skilfully prepared iconic dishes: creamy Russian salad, meat and vegetable ravioli, “finanziera”, crispy fried delicacies and the inevitable selection of boiled meats. To finish on a sweet note, hazelnut cake and velvety “bonet”. Just a stone's throw away there are cosy guest rooms, some with kitchenettes.

Name: Vecchia Lama
Address: Via XXIV Maggio 24, Lama Mocogno, 41023, Italy
Description: A simple yet welcoming refuge in the woodlands of the Modenese Apennines, where the scent of truffle in season mingles with the aromas of Emilian and mountain specialties. In the dining room, Sara Ori greets guests with warmth and genuine smiles, while her parents orchestrate flavors in the kitchen: father at the helm of juicy, steaming meats, mother crafting hand-rolled pastas and fragrant desserts, among them a standout zuppa inglese, creamy and comforting. For those who relish the open road and sweeping vistas, the drive along the SP3 from Modena is well worth it: an hour of winding curves through verdant valleys and breathtaking scenery.

Name: Vecchia Marina
Address: Lungomare Trento 37, Roseto degli Abruzzi, 64026, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: A favourite with a loyal clientele, La Vecchia Marina has built its reputation on exceptional value for money and seafood cuisine that focuses on the freshness of the catch. Just a stone’s throw from the beach, in a simple, family-friendly setting, it serves up traditional dishes without unnecessary fuss, showcasing the authentic flavour of the ingredients. Among the most iconic dishes, the ‘mezzi paccheri’ with sole, scampi and fresh cherry tomatoes stand out – full of flavour and balanced. The tasting menu is also very interesting and is offered at a particularly competitive price. Given the venue’s popularity, booking is strongly recommended.

Name: Vecchio Porto
Address: Lungomare Cenide 55, Villa San Giovanni, 89018, Italy
Description: Although travellers may know Villa San Giovanni for its ferry port to Sicily, fans of gourmet cuisine are familiar with the port as the home of the “Vecchio Porto”, one of the best restaurants in the region and one which boasts spectacular views of the Straits of Messina from its second-floor terrace. The menu features classic dishes including fish cooked on the grill and more imaginative options such as the raw antipasti (snapper flavoured with sea-urchin sauce, lumpfish roe, onion and diced cucumber). The remarkable quality of the fish is a constant theme here.

Name: Veneziano
Address: Contrada Arena, SS 120 km 187, Randazzo, 95036, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated just outside Randazzo, one of the villages with typical lava-stone buildings dotted around Mt Etna, this restaurant serves excellent local cuisine. Recipes featuring mushrooms and meat take pride of place on the menu, from antipasti such as the excellent mixed mushrooms to first courses of mushroom soup and mains that include a highly recommended “asado” (mixed grill) and an unmissable Nero dei Nebrodi capocollo ham.

Name: Vez
Address: Via Addolorata 7/9, San Marzano di San Giuseppe, 74020, Italy
Location: San Marzano di San Giuseppe, Italy
Description: In a small village in the province of Taranto, in the shadow of the church of San Carlo Borromeo, a contemporary culinary experience deeply rooted in the region is taking shape. The head chef uses ingredients produced nearby, enhanced by aromatic herbs grown in the restaurant’s own kitchen garden, to create elegant, creative dishes brimming with character. The menu, which is deliberately simple and updated roughly every two months, follows the rhythm of the seasons and showcases the very best of Apulian produce, with fruit and vegetables taking centre stage. Among the must-try specialities, the homemade fresh stuffed pasta stands out, a tribute to the chef’s formative years in Bologna. A place that is certainly well worth a visit.

Name: Violetta
Address: Via Valle San Giovanni 1, Calamandrana, 14042, Italy
Description: At this family restaurant, the daughter is now at the helm in the kitchen, having taken over from her grandmother a few years ago, while her parents oversee the dining room where the rather old-fashioned 1960s decor is brightened by their attentive service. The menu continues to focus on traditional Piedmontese dishes (especially from Monferrato) cooked in a simple, almost homely style, including specialities such as veal with a tuna sauce (usually known as vitello tonnato), agnolotti monferrini (a type of ravioli), tajarin with porcini mushrooms, finanziera stew, and torroncino parfait. The wine list has the same regional focus as the menu.

Name: Vögele
Description: This restaurant is a Bolzano institution. It is a typical inn whose origins are lost in the mists of time, and is still furnished in traditional Biedermeier - style. The menu focuses on regional cuisine, with an occasional hint of the Mediterranean.

Name: Zeb
Description: In the San Niccolò district, in the heart of Oltrarno, there is a decidedly unusual restaurant. You won't find yourself occupying the usual kind of seating here, as most guests dine on tall stools at a long counter, rather like in a sushi bar. The atmosphere evokes the Far East but the recipes here are typically Tuscan: simple, well-executed dishes, listed on a blackboard that changes with the seasons and according to the chef's inspiration. The menu ranges from oven-baked courgettes stuffed with meat to pici pasta with ricotta and fresh tomato pesto, from “ribollita” to “peposo”, and stuffed guinea fowl; to finish, an apple cake with almonds, pine nuts and cinnamon. Practical note: the restaurant does not take reservations at lunchtime.

Name: /gu.stà.re/ oltrecucina
Description: A fine contemporary restaurant in the heart of town, combining colourful, minimalist tones with a few vintage touches – such as the striking old petrol pump in the dining room. The cuisine draws inspiration from Piedmontese regional tradition – the pink-cooked veal eye round with hazelnut mayonnaise and caper powder inevitably recalls vitello tonnato – yet goes well beyond mere homage. The young and talented chef Valentina Maioni brings passion and quality ingredients to the table, reworking recipes with personal, imaginative touches. Equally at ease with meat and fish, she creates dishes of remarkable balance, such as the exquisite eel with potato foam, pak choi, cocoa nibs and bay leaf powder, while also offering interesting vegetarian options, among which the beetroot tartare with chickpea hummus, puntarelle salad, leek oil and puffed buckwheat stands out. In the dining room, Manuel’s professionalism and expertise complete a carefully crafted and convincing experience.

Name: 1224 Restaurant Cortina
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: In the sumptuous surroundings of the Grand Hotel Savoia, the name pays homage to Cortina’s altitude, but one cannot help but suspect that chef Federico Rovacchi will also take your taste buds to new heights. With two tasting menus (one featuring the classics, the other dedicated to the latest creations) and à la carte options, the cuisine here is of an extraordinary standard. It ranges from mountainous landscapes to international influences, including those from Asia, all presented with good taste, style and elegance. A number of ingredients are cooked over charcoal to superb effect, with the flavours and ingredients really coming into their own.

Name: 177 toledo
Description: At Via Toledo 177, on the fifth floor of an elegant building in the heart of Naples, one of the most fascinating expressions of the culinary world of Giuseppe Iannotti – the two-Michelin-starred chef at Krèsios – is taking shape. The experience begins as soon as you walk through the door, amid contemporary artworks and references to Campania’s craftsmanship, which are also reflected in the details of the menu – printed on handmade paper from Amalfi and featuring a design inspired by the tradition of Tombola. In the kitchen, head chef Antonio Grazioli puts a contemporary spin on the great Neapolitan classics, creating a menu that is both creative and distinctive. A prime example of this is the reinterpretation of ‘puveriello’-style spaghetti, enhanced by the aroma of truffle.

The name of this restaurant refers to the year in which the hotel in which it is located (the Park Hotel Holzner) was opened, while the design is a nod to the Liberty style of the period. Despite this, both the ambience and the cuisine bear the modern and imaginative hallmark of Stephan Zippl. Paying careful attention to sustainability, this chef selects the best regional produce for his dishes – even the Wagyu beef is raised in the chef’s native Renon region. This strong connection with the Alto Adige is also evident on the excellent wine list, which features almost 400 labels from the region and provides perfect pairings for the chef’s tasting menu. Other options include non-alcoholic drinks such as apple juice and alcohol-free cocktails.

Name: 20Tre
Address: Via David Chiossone 20 r, Genoa, 16123, Italy
Description: Run by three partners, this contemporary-style restaurant is situated in the heart of Genova’s historic centre. The cuisine here is prepared using the best seasonal ingredients, all presented in an array of modern dishes. Meat and fish feature on the menu, with a focus on regional recipes and the occasional Asian twist (for example, the amberjack and ponzu bonbon).

Name: 28 Posti
Description: The main focus of 28 Posti is its ethical stance, with seasonal ingredients sourced from small producers and an emphasis on making the most of each and every ingredient in order to keep food waste to a minimum – a philosophy that has been important to the restaurant for many years now. New chefs Franco Salvatore and Andrea Zazzara, both from the Abruzzi, have brought their own personal touches to cuisine which has its roots in the rich gastronomic traditions of central Italy and their native region.

Name: 3.0 Ciro Cascella
Description: Fans of Neapolitan pizza will be in their element at this restaurant, where the pizzas are light, with a larger and softer crust, thanks to the long fermentation and leavening process – some people come here simply to eat the crust, it’s so good. There’s also a wide choice of excellent toppings, including top-quality ingredients from Campania. Gluten-free options and dough made from different flours are also available.

Name: 4 Ciance
Description: Two bright rooms in the heart of the old town welcome guests with warmth and professionalism, courtesy of the all-female staff. A refined atmosphere, the scent of wood and meticulous attention to detail create the backdrop for the dishes created by the two chefs, conceived to delight both the eyes and the palate. The menu is based on solid traditional foundations, but with contemporary and creative touches. Choose from two tasting menus and an à la carte menu, featuring dishes made with seasonal ingredients. The focus is on meat, as is traditional in Piedmont, but there are also refined seafood alternatives for those looking for different flavours.

Name: 50 Kalò
Description: In the Neapolitan tradition of interpreting dreams, 50 means bread (dough), while the word “kalò” has Greek origins and means good – the name “good dough” explains the secret behind the pizzas made by Ciro Salvo, one of the most famous master pizza chefs in Naples. This chef makes traditional Neapolitan pizzas, which are very large and made with a soft dough. The restaurant doesn’t take reservations – if it’s busy you just leave your name and wait to be called. However, if you prefer not to wait, there’s a second restaurant at 2, Piazza della Repubblica where you can book in advance.

Name: 85 Bistrot
Address: Piazza Martiri di Via Fani 85, Sesto San Giovanni, 20099, Italy
Description: This simple, modern, family-run trattoria with a welcoming ambience is the kind of restaurant that everyone would love to have as their local. The owner-chef, who has plenty of experience working in Milanese restaurants, is a real culinary expert who creates traditional dishes from Milan but also from further afield. Here, the popular breaded cutlet is served thick so that the delicate flavour of the veal can be enjoyed to the full.

Name: A Mangiare
Address: Viale Monte Grappa 3, Reggio Emilia, 42121, Italy
Description: Situated at the entrance to the historic centre, this restaurant now has a new owner, who is nonetheless assisted by the old management team front of house. The cuisine here includes traditional and creative fare, both on the tasting menu and the à la carte, in dishes that are generously portioned and beautifully presented – you’ll also find a few fish options. Care and simplicity are the principles that guide the young female chef who arrived here with the new owners.

Name: A Spurcacciun-a
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Always a good choice for gourmet cuisine, this lovely restaurant within the Hotel Mare boasts a fine location with a garden for summer dining overlooking the beach and the sea. Whether you’re soaking up the views outside or sitting comfortably in the attractive contemporary-style dining room, it’s Simone Perata’s cuisine that will convince you that you’ve chosen the best place in town. The menu is teeming with delicious dishes made from top-quality ingredients (especially fish, such as the delicious whitebait with grilled artichokes and green curry sauce), all prepared with a modern twist and beautifully presented. The excellent wine list (including a few vintage labels) provides the perfect accompaniment to your dining experience.

Name: A' Cuncuma
Description: In 2022, young sous-chef Gianfilippo Gatto became the owner-chef of this simple and intimate restaurant situated in Palermo’s historic centre. The key attraction here is the quality of the cuisine, which features colourful dishes and modern interpretations of Sicilian recipes (meat and fish alike). Examples include arancina stuffed with young caciocavallo cheese and cooked in the oven, then topped with orange prawn tartare and served on a prawn bisque. The excellent wine list is completely Sicilian, with separate sections dedicated to the Etna wines produced in different parts of the region, many of which are young, promising and highly recommended!

Name: A' Paranza
Description: For more than 30 years, this restaurant run by the Proto brothers has been a popular choice for visitors to the beautiful Atrani valley. Simple cuisine served in a simple and informal setting (dishes are nearly always announced at your table rather than listed on a menu), with a focus on Mediterranean and Campanian dishes.

Name: AB Osteria Contemporanea
Description: A small village just a few kilometres from Udine provides the backdrop for modern, regionally influenced cuisine with plenty of character. The renovated dining rooms have two distinct styles: the one near the entrance is friendly and relaxed; the other has a much more formal ambience. The large outdoor space is perfect for summer dining.

Name: AVUS
Description: In the heart of Marino’s historic centre, this venue distinguishes itself through a simple, modern, and minimalist aesthetic, accompanied by a gastronomic proposal that is almost entirely vegetarian. The menu, concise and carefully composed, offers a select number of dishes from which to choose freely, all built around plant-based ingredients.The young chef, talented and creative, works with precision on vegetables, pulses, and fruit, combining them in preparations of bold and at times complex flavour, capable of winning over even the most traditional of palates. The commitment to quality is absolute: only fresh produce is used, selected and prepared daily according to the number of guests, in a spirit of rigour and respect for the raw material. For this reason, the restaurant operates exclusively by reservation, guaranteeing a bespoke experience without compromise.

Name: Abbamele Osteria
Address: Corso Vittorio Emanuele III 59, Mamoiada, 08024, Italy
Description: In the heart of Barbagia, in the centre of Mamoiada, Maura Ladu’s restaurant showcases the region with authenticity and a contemporary sensitivity. The chef and owner, a local, welcomes guests into an intimate dining room with a minimalist feel, where the stone walls provide a backdrop to photographs and masks of the mamuthones – the iconic figures of the famous local carnival – which help to forge a strong connection with the local culture. The culinary offering reinterprets Sardinian tradition with elegance and precision, through an affordable multi-course tasting menu complemented by an à la carte selection. The stars of the show are high-quality local ingredients, used in dishes that play with textures and subtle contrasts: from courgettes given a new twist with an egg cooked at 65 degrees Celsius to the pairing of suckling pig with whole aubergines, enhanced by a delicate touch of candied lemon. The experience is rounded off by a carefully curated wine list, featuring around 130 wines, and the rare and welcome opportunity to sample most of them by the glass.

Name: Acaja
Description: Central, elegant and modern, the cuisine of Acaja winds along two lines: the traditional regional one, with ravioli del plin, cardi gobbi, Piedmont veal and hazelnuts to mention just a few that cannot be missed, but also various fish dishes that are truly remarkable, with a touch of contemporaneity, starting with excellent raw materials.

Name: Acanto
Description: At Acanto, the young new chef at the helm, Matteo Gabrielli, who has experience of working abroad, focuses firmly on traditional cuisine – the risotto alla Milanese remains one of the highlights here! In a classic-style dining room inside the Principe di Savoia hotel, enjoy Italian meat and fish dishes prepared using modern techniques that allow the quality of the ingredients to shine through. Attentive, professional service adds to the appeal.

Name: Accademia Ristorante
Description: Over the years, the gastronomic quality of this excellent restaurant has been confirmed and even increased. The cuisine is basic Piedmontese (the ravioli del plin are excellent), with the addition of a few seafood dishes and some more technical courses (such as rabbit à la royale). In fact, solidity and growth are mainly due to the passion of the histrionic owner, Nicola Mecca, who is polite and passionate and also adept at providing pertinent suggestions on Monferrato wines and his beloved Champagnes. Naturally, we would also highlight the location itself, which offers some very fascinating insights: inside a late 18th-century aristocratic palace, you enter the first floor by climbing an imposing staircase, while with your nose to the sky you enjoy the all-Italian beauty of the frescoed ceilings.

Name: Aciniello
Description: A family-run trattoria since 1948, it has now been completely refurbished thanks to a recent renovation that has enhanced its interior, featuring exposed stonework and contemporary touches. The atmosphere remains that of a cosy, informal, authentic tavern, where the cuisine celebrates tradition through dishes that are simple in appearance, but rich in flavour and substance. The star of the menu is meat, served in a variety of dishes, with one notable exception: salted cod, a long-standing and much-loved feature of the menu.

Name: Acqua & Sale
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: The enthusiastic owners of Acqua & Sale have transformed what was originally a simple fishmonger’s into a restaurant with the addition of an informal, well-appointed dining room on the side. Here, guests enjoy unfussy fresh fish dishes, including an array of raw options and Mediterranean recipes with the occasional personal touch. Recipes include grilled octopus with black broccoli and wine-fermented plums, and porchetta-style tuna with a green sauce, fried new potatoes and sweet and sour peppers. The perfect choice for fish-lovers!

Name: Acqua Pazza
Description: Although this restaurant is not in the centre, if you’re looking for excellent fish (mostly from the Mediterranean) personally selected by the owner - chef, then it’s well worth the few minutes it takes to find a parking space here. Beautifully cooked food, which is simply prepared using top - quality produce.

Name: Adelaide
Description: From the outside, it could easily go unnoticed, but beyond the threshold of Hotel Vilòn unfolds a world of refined spaces, rich with significant decorative details that never veer into excess: a discreet enchantment of great charm. In the kitchen, Gabriele Muro presents a high-caliber offering that weaves together Campanian memories and contemporary creativity, reinterpreting Mediterranean flavors with modern sensitivity and polished presentations. The menu also features timeless Roman first courses – carbonara, cacio e pepe, amatriciana – executed with precision. When weather permits, the small interior courtyard offers a secluded and pleasant spot for dining.

Name: Agorà
Description: In Rende, this restaurant is a go-to destination for lovers of contemporary seafood cuisine. The menu centres on high-quality fish and seafood, brought to the fore by meticulous preparation and a style of cooking that combines technical skill with a sense of spontaneity. Guests can choose between two tasting menus or select freely from the extensive à la carte selection. The modern and elegant setting is characterised by its spacious interior, enhanced by striking display cabinets dedicated to wine, while in the warmer months a lovely outdoor seating area surrounded by planters offers a pleasant alternative al fresco. A well-curated selection of wines rounds off the experience.

Name: Agriturismo Ferdy
Address: Località Fienili, fraz. Scalvino, Lenna, 24010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Once you’ve left your car in the car park and crossed the River Brembo, you enter a landscape with an almost fairy-tale charm, among meadows, horses and views stretching out to the peaks of the Orobie Alps.
