It is from these mountains that the restaurant draws its inspiration, creating a cuisine deeply rooted in the region, characterised by substance, innovation and authentic flavours. Meat, dairy products and other produce of the region take centre stage in hearty dishes full of character, while the famous cheese trolley is an unmissable highlight of the dining experience. The wine list is also interesting, with a particular focus on the region’s wines and natural wines. In the warmer months, the outdoor tables, in the shade of the large trees and surrounded by immaculate lawns, make the experience even more memorable.

Name: Agriturismo Il Cavallino
Address: SP 55 Saturnia-Semproniano, località Fibbianello, Semproniano, 58055, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: A property located in a very peaceful setting within an organic farm stay. The management is driven by great passion: he works in the kitchen, carrying forward the family business tradition; she manages the dining room with grace and attention. The recipes offered are tied to the territory, with dishes that are generous, flavorful, and colorful, showing particular attention to the lightness of the preparations. The quality of their organic extra virgin olive oil is particularly noteworthy.

Name: Ai Cadelach
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Enjoy local cuisine in a rustic - style dining room or alongside the swimming pool in summer. The menu focuses on meat dishes (especially grilled meat), such as traditional Fiorentina steak and Alpago lamb. Wine lovers will appreciate the excellent wine cellar kept by Ezio, one of the restaurant owners.

Name: Ai Campi di Marcello
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This restaurant is situated just a stone’s throw from the shipyards in the historic working-class Panzano district, a rare example of a neighbourhood built specifically to house shipyard workers, complete with residences for unmarried men and women. A long-established, family-run restaurant, Ai Campi di Marcello has a simple atmosphere and serves classic, generously portioned fish and seafood dishes. Food can also be ordered to take away, plus there’s a video which explains how to make seafood risotto.

Name: Ai Do Campanili
Address: Via Marco Polo 2, Località Treporti, Cavallino, 30013, Italy
Description: Both the building in which it is housed and the dining room of this restaurant are on the small side, but the quality of the food more than compensates for the lack of space. Run by young and enthusiastic staff, the restaurant specialises in fish and seafood with raw options and modern dishes featuring on the menu. Excellent selection of wine, also available to take away.

Name: Ai Gondolieri
Address: Fondamenta de l'Ospedaleto, sestiere Dorsoduro 366, Venice, 30123, Italy
Description: Situated behind the Guggenheim museum, this rustic restaurant with wood panelling on the walls offers a meat-based menu that focuses on traditional, regional cuisine (the braised rack of lamb with spinach tortino with butter and parmesan cheese is superb). The well-stocked wine cellar is home to a huge selection of white, red and sparkling wines, plus there’s an extensive choice of cocktails. At Ai Gondolieri, enjoy a good glass of wine accompanied by typical Venetian fare such as cured hams and sweet-and-sour vegetables.

Name: Ai Mercanti
Address: Corte Coppo, Sestiere San Marco 4346/a, Venice, 30124, Italy
Description: A family-run “gastrosteria” hidden in a small Venetian courtyard, with a modern and elegant decor dominated by beige and black tones. Full of exciting and imaginative flavours, the modern meat and fish dishes prepared by promising young chef Nadia Locatello make a change from the typical specialities of the region.

Name: Ai Porteghi Bistrot
Description: Situated under the picturesque arcades on Via Cesare Battisti, this restaurant is home to a young chef whose cuisine is inspired by traditional and well-known recipes which he reinterprets with his own personal touch to create highly interesting dishes. Simpler and more reasonably priced options are also available at lunchtime.

Name: Ai Torchi
Description: Occupying a 17C olive oil press in the heart of a charming medieval village, this restaurant has retained its old stone mill and wooden press in its vaulted dining room, which provides the backdrop for imaginative fish and seafood dishes prepared using top-quality local ingredients. The delicious Italian-style ceviche is made from the catch of the day, while the Mare Mare mixed fish dish is baked in a casserole with cherry tomatoes, courgettes and bay leaves. If you’re looking for a simpler option, try the I Torchiettibistro on the corner of the same street.

Name: Aimo e Nadia BistRo
Description: A small jewel of elegance and refinement, where the celebrated starred establishment has chosen to offer a simpler, more relaxed cuisine without sacrificing precision or identity. The menu gathers national classics reinterpreted through a contemporary lens – the signature saffron risotto with ossobuco reduction and warm zabaione served with cinnamon ladyfinger cookies are both essential – alongside a tempting selection of shareable dishes. Among these, the gnocco fritto with Colonnata lard and the celebrated mondeghili meatballs stand out, perfect for pairing with one of the cocktails from a list crafted specifically to complement the kitchen’s offerings.

Name: Akira Back
Description: A new city opening that marks the arrival in Italy of Akira Back, internationally renowned chef-entrepreneur and purveyor of fusion cookery that weaves together Japan and Korea through a distinctly American lens. Situated on the ground floor of the W Florence, the establishment immediately pulses with vibrant, fashionable energy, aided by decisively pitched music and a metropolitan atmosphere. The kitchen moves with freedom and playfulness, offering comfortable and cosmopolitan dishes animated by a pop verve that renders them instantly recognisable. Among the most sought-after specialities are the crisp American tacos filled with Korean-style beef bulgogi and finished with a “Japanese-style” ponzu sauce, alongside the miso caramel ice cream encased in a mock cigar of crisp chocolate. A wine list is present, though the ideal pairing remains with cocktails: beyond the house signatures, the great international classics are well represented.

Name: Akoya
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Notable sake list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: At Spazio Musa, a contemporary art gallery in the heart of Turin’s Quadrilatero district, a project is taking shape that brings together culture, design and haute cuisine. Amid striking exposed brick vaults and spaces furnished with elegant simplicity, Christian Mandura and Alessandro Daddea have created a dining experience centred on omakase, the Japanese concept whereby the chef curates the tasting menu. Seated at the counter, guests watch the dishes being prepared first-hand, appreciating the precision of the cuts, the quality of the ingredients and the attention to detail in the presentation. The experience takes place in a dynamic, multifunctional setting: aperitifs and the end of the meal are enjoyed in the elegant adjoining sitting rooms, which are integrated with a lounge bar that rounds off the experience. Alongside the selection of wines, the extensive sake list is also well worth a look; it has been curated for enthusiasts and those simply curious to explore Japanese culinary culture in greater depth.

Name: Al 588
Address: Via Roma 588, Bagno a Ripoli, 50012, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: “Al 588” is the restaurant at Borgo I Vicelli – a ‘rural chic’ agritourism property set in a secluded 16th-century hamlet surrounded by greenery – which overlooks the swimming pool and opens at sunset. Here, chef Andrea Perini showcases local and seasonal ingredients through contemporary cuisine that is meticulously presented, simply constructed and a delight to the palate, while one of the highlights is the “Brace del Borgo”, a selection of premium, dry-aged meats sourced from small Tuscan farmers and butchers named on the menu, grilled to bring out their authenticity and character. The same commitment to the local area guides the wine cellar, which favours Tuscan wines while making room for a few Champagnes, and finds its full expression in the extra virgin olive oil produced from the estate’s centuries-old olive trees – authentic ‘green gold’ that tells the story and identity of the place.

Name: Al Baccanale
Description: In the heart of the historic centre, just a short walk from Piombino Castle and the ancient Medici Fortress, this cosy restaurant welcomes guests into charming surroundings, with exposed stone walls, vaulted ceilings and just a few tables, all of which help to create an intimate and refined atmosphere. The menu reinterprets tradition through a contemporary lens, creating dishes that are deeply rooted in the region’s cuisine but are reimagined with character, a modern sensitivity and solid culinary technique.

Name: Al Camin
Description: On the road to Misurina lake, this friendly restaurant with a modern Alpine style offers dishes of the regional tradition with imaginative touches and modern technique. So a great deal of practicality, then, as in the beef tenderloin wrapped in speck dry-cured pork with cep mushrooms and Ampezzo-style potatoes. The chef and sommelier Fabio Pompanin manages a wine list with approximately 200 labels. In the warmer season, take advantage of the open-air service.

Name: Al Capitan della Cittadella
Description: Bearing the signature of three-starred Perbellini (his celebrated millefeuille features among the desserts), but with the talented Andrea Manzoli at the stoves, this is the quintessential venue for lovers of traditional seafood cuisine; here and there a creative touch, with the exceptional quality of the catch always center stage.

Name: Al Carroponte
Address: Via Edmondo De Amicis 4, Bergamo, 24127, Italy
Description: This restaurant is renowned in Bergamo for its good choice of varied cuisine, as well as its lively, buzzing atmosphere. The excellent, tasty cuisine is typically Italian and contemporary in style, and includes luxury ingredients such as lobster and caviar, while the “classic” à la carte is enhanced by a selection of cured hams, cheeses and finger food. But the Carroponte’s beating heart is owner Oscar Mazzoleni’s passion for the world of wine, with an incredible selection of over 2 000 labels that puts many more famous Michelin-starred restaurants in the shade.

Name: Al Cavallino Bianco
Description: Situated near the banks of the River Po, this century - old, family - run restaurant serves regional specialities, such as the famous culatello ham. You will find reasonably priced local dishes at the ‘Tipico di Casa Spigaroli’ at lunchtime during the week, and themed menus at the weekend.

Name: Al Cjasal
Address: Via Nazionale 30, Località San Giorgio al Tagliamento, San Michele al Tagliamento, 30028, Italy
Description: A new generation is now at the helm in this warm and elegant restaurant decorated with a profusion of wood, adding a more modern touch to the cuisine while maintaining its regional character and excellent local ingredients. The menu has its own unique flavour thanks to the option of numerous cicchetti (tapas-style snacks) options available, either in half- or full portions, enabling guests to create their own menu.

Name: Al Covo
Address: Campiello della Pescaria, Sestiere Castello 3968, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: Authentic family hospitality for this renowned restaurant, which makes niche products - mainly seafood - its flagship, even if some land specialties are always present on the menu. Almost all of the vegetables come from the Osti in Orto property garden on the island of Sant'Erasmo.

Name: Al Dragone
Description: Occupying a natural cave, this typical restaurant serves traditional regional dishes prepared with care and imagination. House specialities include scampi in an almond crust.

Name: Al Fogher
Address: Strada Statale 117 bis, Piazza Armerina, 94015, Italy
Description: This small, rustic-style restaurant just outside the centre of Piazza Armerina serves personalised cuisine in which local ingredients take pride of place. Influences from elsewhere in Italy are also evident, with dishes such as artichoke pansotti (stuffed pasta) with local tuma cheese and black truffles on the menu.

Name: Al Gatto Nero
Description: Family - run, informal service, care in the choice of raw materials in a typical welcoming trattoria with Venetian and seafood cuisine; delightful outside area in the summer.

Name: Al Grop
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Beneath the bell tower of a pretty village, Al Grop welcomes guests into a classic setting brightened by original touches and the warmth of a crackling fireplace. The menu reflects the local flavours, with grilled meats, and asparagus in season, taking centre stage. There's a grand finale for those with a sweet tooth: the dessert trolley. And for those who want to stay a little longer, the guesthouse offers cosy, well-appointed rooms.

Name: Al Moro
Address: Via Pietri 1277, Marina Di Campo, 57034, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Situated away from the main tourist area, in a rustic building that is striking for its attractive outdoor space shaded by a wooden gazebo, this restaurant boasts an informal and relaxing atmosphere. The Mediterranean cuisine is full of character and prepared with top-quality ingredients, including a small selection of oysters.

Name: Al Palazzo
Description: Al Palazzo is the renowned restaurant at the Palazzo Murat hotel which is run by the Attanasio family. Dine alfresco in the restaurant’s beautiful botanical garden with its tiny vegetable patch, apart from on rare days of bad weather, when guests are served indoors in its small, elegant dining rooms. The Mediterranean cuisine includes meat and fish dishes alike, with slightly different menus at lunchtime (simpler options) and in the evening. Le Petit Murat bar is still open, offering an interesting selection of cocktails to supplement its excellent wine list.

Name: Al Paradiso
Address: Via Sant'Ermacora 1, Paradiso di Pocenia, 33050, Italy
Description: A little gem housed in an old farmhouse, along the avenue leading to the splendid Villa Caratti-Fraccaroli. The interiors, which are both romantic and authentically rustic, captivate with their soaring ceilings, exposed brick arches, period décor and copper pots hanging on the walls. Building on a long family tradition, the restaurant continues to showcase the local area with passion and an increasing focus on research into ingredients and traditional recipes. The menu focuses on meat and game, accompanied by excellent cured meats and cheeses, traditional cjalsons and tempting grilled dishes prepared in the large fireplace in the main dining room. It’s worth saving a bit of room for dessert: the desserts are, in fact, one of the restaurant’s specialities, as demonstrated by the delicious mille-feuille and the impeccable crêpes Suzette.

Name: Al Persef
Description: In the small, contemporary dining room of Hotel Sporting Family Hospitality, overlooking the Alps, diners can watch the kitchen staff as they work, creatively and paying close attention to locally sourced ingredients. Excellent wine list.

Name: Al Petes
Description: Situated amid the alleyways of the historic centre, Al Petes has a pleasant contemporary feel and is run by young, welcoming and friendly owners. Marko’s menu demonstrates an obvious preference for seafood, most of which comes from the Adriatic, and which is served with Mediterranean and even occasional Asian influences. The surprise tasting menu is highly recommended. Just around the corner, the restaurant’s small hotel (James Joyce) is the ideal choice for overnight accommodation.

Name: Al Pilèr
Description: Situated in the town centre, this restaurant can be accessed by car despite its location perched above the town. It takes its name from an old boundary stone that is still partially visible and which once separated the Arab and Norman sections of town (the word comes from the curious Gallo-Italian dialect spoken in parts of Sicily, which has more in common with the Lombardy dialect than those of the island itself). Meat takes centre stage, including the aged meats on display, although the menu also features generous, colourful classic dishes with a creative twist. There’s also an outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Al Pozzo
Description: The cuisine at this restaurant is almost exclusively based on fish and seafood, with three main points of focus – an extensive array of raw dishes; ageing of almost all the fish to accentuate flavour and texture (as well as making the skin pleasantly crispy); and the grilling of some courses. Top-quality ingredients and delicious desserts complete the picture.

Name: Al Segnavento
Address: Via Gatta 76/c, Località Santa Lucia di Tarù, Zelarino, 30174, Italy
Description: An elegant restaurant run by an entire family, whose philosophy could be summed up in the phrase “from farm to fork”. Fruit, vegetables, mutton, lamb, pork, plus a delicious breed of duck are all showcased in this zero-kilometre restaurant. If you’re looking for simpler fare and wine by the carafe, the restaurant also has a more informal bistro nearby. Charming guestrooms also available for visitors wanting to prolong their stay.

Name: Al Tonno di Corsa
Description: Not only the restaurant, but a large part of the tantalising menu as well is based on the tuna caught in the nets. Open kitchen; two small dining rooms and two pleasant little terraces.

Name: Al Vecchio Convento
Description: At the gates of the city, within a building steeped in history and featuring convenient private parking, this restaurant welcomes guests with classic elegance from the entrance, where artisanal cantucci and ricciarelli are displayed for sale. The dining room echoes the same refined atmosphere, with attentive, punctual service. In the kitchen, Tuscan tradition reigns: meat dishes take center stage, with few concessions to seafood, and fresh pastas prepared according to time-honored methods. An offering built on the strength of regional flavors and authenticity. No frills, but careful attention to detail.

Name: Al Vedel
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A temple for the production of culatello ham, which features in the dishes served and is also matured on the premises for 16, 26 and 38 months (the maturing rooms are well worth a visit), Al Vedel also serves other regional specialities, as well as more imaginative fare. The menu features dishes such as gran lesso(boiled beef and chicken), delicious Bourguignon-style snails, tortel dols (tortelli pasta with a hint of sweetness), and specialities enhanced by the addition of Parmesan cheese and red butter. The wine list, which will delight Lambrusco enthusiasts, boasts a selection of French wines including newer wine-producing regions, while the cheese trolley offers a selection of regional and Italian cheeses, plus a few options from further afield such as the famous Brillat-Savarin with its natural, bloomy rind.

Name: Al Volt
Address: Via Fiume 73, Riva del Garda, 38066, Italy
Description: As you explore the narrow streets which lead from the commercial port to the centre, you’ll come across this restaurant comprising several inter - connected dining rooms with low ceilings and antique furniture. The menu focuses on regional cuisine, albeit with the occasional creative twist.

Name: Alajmo Cortina
Description: Situated in the restored premises of the historic El Toulà restaurant, Alajmo Cortina is home to a bar on the ground floor, with the restaurant occupying the two upper floors (no lift). Although traditional in feel with a profusion of wood, the restaurant is run by a young and enthusiastic team. The cuisine focuses mainly on the region, although the menu also features fish and other imaginative options on tasting menus and an à la carte.

Name: Albergaccio di Castellina
Address: Via Fiorentina 63, Castellina in Chianti, 53011, Italy
Description: In the heart of one of Italy’s most iconic landscapes, Chianti Classico, with its harmonious hills and vineyards tracing picture-perfect panoramas, Albergaccio, considered Tuscany’s oldest historic restaurant, welcomes guests with a perfect balance of past and present. The interiors preserve the authentic charm of the setting, while the kitchen reinterprets traditional dishes with a contemporary touch, never betraying their essence. In the dining room, Francesco greets guests with grace and professionalism, guiding them in selecting the wine best suited to enhance the gastronomic experience. An establishment that celebrates history, terroir, and a timeless vision of hospitality.

Name: Alessandro Borghese - Il lusso della semplicità
Address: Calle Seconda del Cristo 2040, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description: This restaurant is situated in the Casinò di Venezia, or to be more precise, Palazzo Ca’ Vendramin Calergi, a 16C building overlooking the Grand Canal which boasts a beautiful garden in which meals are served on warm summer evenings. Chef Alessandro Borghese serves modern and attractive cuisine which is full of enticing flavours. There are two tasting menus available, with the option of adding the chef’s signature dishes to either of these.

Name: Alessandro Feo
Address: Via Angelo Lista 24, Marina di Casal Velino, 84040, Italy
Description: In a beautiful stone-vaulted building (an old 17C monastery) on the town’s seafront promenade, young owner-chef Alessandro Feo has made his mark in this region that perhaps has fewer gourmet restaurants than many places elsewhere. Here, he creates dishes that combine traditional influences and classic favourites from Campania with his own individual flair and creativity. His focus is on local, seasonal ingredients, including produce from his two kitchen gardens and fish sourced from local fishermen as well as from his own ventures out to sea.

Name: Alessandro Mecca al Castello di Grinzane Cavour
Description: There’s no shortage of classic Piedmontese ingredients (such as anchovies, peppers and veal) on the menu at this restaurant, where traditional recipes are reinterpreted with a personalised and contemporary touch. Dishes from outside the region, including various fish-based options, also feature, while the restaurant aims to avoid food waste by using every single part of its ingredients where possible. The location in a splendid castle with 11C origins, once the home of Camillo Benso, count of Cavour, adds to the appeal.

Name: Alex
Address: Via Versilia 157/159, Marina di Pietrasanta, 55045, Italy
Description: This elegant yet relaxed restaurant does not overlook the sea directly, but is situated on a trendy roadside, adorned with tribal motifs, wicker chairs and dark wood marquetry tables. Here, guests can enjoy a menu predominantly based on seafood, featuring modern touches and imaginative interpretations that make the most of the ingredients without compromising their identity. The menu also features some of the restaurant’s great classics, such as the unmissable steamed langoustines and prawns, served with crisp vegetables and mayonnaise in a perfect example of flavour, balance and technique.A high-quality wine cellar completes the experience with a wide and international selection of wines, perfect for accompanying dishes that, while Mediterranean in style, offer a broader, more cosmopolitan perspective.

Name: All'Olivo
Description: In one of the characteristic squares of the beautiful old town, four dining rooms, the central one lined with bottles of wine, while the others are embellished with numerous drawings by artists who have taken part in the legendary Lucca Comics festival. The menu is of regional inspiration, offering both meat and fish dishes. Be sure to try the traditional Lucca tortelli served with meat sauce. The extensive wine list also offers a good selection of wines by the glass. Delightful alfresco service in summer.

Name: All'Osteria Bottega
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Beneath the porticoes of a somewhat hidden side street in the city centre lies a trattoria that celebrates authentic Emilian cooking, prepared according to tradition, without diversions or reinterpretations, but showcased in its most typical recipes. From the exceptional selection of cured meats and cheeses to the fresh pasta dishes, from the meat dishes to the wines – largely local – everything speaks the forthright and comforting language of this land. It is worth, therefore, leaving a little room for the zuppa inglese, served with alchermes ring cake and chocolate shavings: a great classic that concludes the meal in the most indulgent fashion. The setting is small and welcoming, and it comes as no surprise that the restaurant is fully booked every day: reserving a table is strongly advised.

Name: Alla Corte Lombarda
Description: Housed in a restored hay barn on the edge of the village, this charming rustic restaurant offers traditional cuisine with a modern twist, a good selection of wine and an excellent choice of beer. Every week, the menu features five records which played a major role in the history of music or which represent an important moment in time for the restaurant owner.

Name: Alla Fassa
Address: Via Nascimbeni 11, Castelletto di Brenzone, 37010, Italy
Description: Although the beautiful views of the lake (with only a cycle path between the restaurant and the water) and mountains on the opposite shore can be admired from the dining room, in fine weather it’s a race for the outdoor tables just a few metres from the water. The cuisine is as impressive as the setting, with a fine balance of classic and modern dishes featuring fish from the lake (such as the “il lago in un piatto” – the lake in a dish – starter) and the sea. A few guestrooms with views of the lake are also available.

Name: Alla Laguna - Vedova Raddi
Description: In this charming little town criss-crossed by canals, a restaurant with a homely, old-world charm has, over the years, built its reputation on seafood dishes that remain true to tradition. The dishes, simple and free from unnecessary frills, allow the quality of the ingredients to shine through – they are the undisputed stars of the menu. From the catch of the day, grilled to perfection, to the most classic seafood dishes, each dish showcases the freshness, seasonality and authenticity of the flavours to the full.

Name: Alla Lanterna
Description: On the Adriatic coast road south of Fano, run by the same family since 1976, the year it opened, this restaurant is a must for seafood lovers. The dishes are essentially inspired by the seafaring traditions of the Marche region.

Name: Alla Locanda
Description: A colourful, contemporary-style restaurant within the Locanda degli Artisti Art Hotel, a new address that is striking for its large art collection displayed throughout its various rooms. The cuisine here focuses on seasonal ingredients which are used to create personalised and imaginative dishes showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte. Interesting wine list, with a special emphasis on labels from the Trentino-Alto Adige region.

Name: Alle Ciaspole
Address: Località Plazze 4, Frazione Tret, Fondo, 38013, Italy
Description: This beautiful Alpine house surrounded by the low mountains of the Val di Non is home to husband-and-wife team Ivano and Antonella, who have run this restaurant with enthusiasm and professionalism for many years. She offers a warm welcome front of house, while he is at the helm in the kitchen, where he prepares dishes from top-quality ingredients (mostly local, such as the Alpine beef, char, cheese and game) with skill and precision. A few seasonal ingredients from outside the region also make it on to the menu, as do a couple of fish-based dishes.

Name: Alle Codole
Address: Via XX Agosto 27, Canale d'Agordo, 32020, Italy
Description: For over half a century, the family has successfully run this establishment, combining the restaurant business with a small hospitality facility offering around ten rooms. In the kitchen, chef Oscar Tibolla interprets the region through a menu that is rich in flavour and rooted in tradition, while incorporating more creative and contemporary influences, expressed with his own personal touch. In the dining room and the wine cellar, his brother Diego looks after guests with professionalism and passion, suggesting spot-on wine pairings that bring out the very best in the dishes. A solid and welcoming family-run business that continues to evolve while remaining true to its roots.

Name: Alle Corone
Address: Campo della Fava, Sestiere Castello 5527, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: Modern Mediterranean and Venetian cuisine served in three elegant dining rooms or – on request – in the wine bar surrounded by bottles of wine. Through the windows, enjoy the spectacle of gondolas passing by along the small canal outside.

Name: Alloro
Description: In the baroque heart of the city, this small restaurant – comprising two dining rooms, one overlooking the bell tower of the Basilica Collegiata dei Santi Apostoli Pietro e Paolo, the other more intimate – welcomes guests with a contemporary style and cozy atmosphere. The cooking takes a modern and bold approach, offered either à la carte or through two tasting menus that trace journeys of travel and inspiration by way of forthright and intriguing flavours. To then end the meal with a touch of lightness thanks to the playful ‘tiratisù’. Here, you are not simply clients, but guests.

Name: Almondo Trattoria
Address: Piazza Gran Madre di Dio 2/l, Turin, 10131, Italy
Description: This simple yet charming restaurant located just a few metres from the Gran Madre church serves a fine array of regional Italian dishes. Although specialities from Piedmont understandably take pride of place, the menu takes guests on a culinary journey throughout Italy and the changing seasons, featuring dishes such as scialatielli pasta with seafood, Puglian stuffed meat rolls, and zabaglione with traditional hazelnut cake from the Langhe. There’s also a good selection of gluten-free options.

Name: Alpenrose
Address: Via delle Sette Chiese 1, Loc. Pinzago, Brixen, 39042, Italy
Description: Situated in a beautiful panoramic location a few kilometres outside Bressanone, this restaurant combines regional traditions with a modern approach thanks to its classic techniques and the use of Mediterranean ingredients in some dishes. There are also elegant apartments available, plus a private wellness space, for anyone wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Alpes
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A warm and welcoming setting, where hospitality stands out for its authenticity and attention to detail. The kitchen, under the direction of chef Matthias Kirchler, presents creative, refined dishes designed for those who love to experiment and be surprised. The gastronomic offering has been recently refreshed and now unfolds in two distinct journeys: “Alpes 1988” and “Alpes – Locanda” for culinary experiences that narrate the territory with contemporary flair.

Name: AlpiNN by Norbert Niederkofler
Address: Plan de Corones, alt. 2275, Brunico, 39031, Italy
Description: Situated at an altitude of 2 000m in the Plan de Corones ski area, this restaurant is accessed via the cable-car from Riscone and then, in winter, by walking (or skiing) for around 150m through the snow. This impressive project by famous chef Norbert Niederkofler showcases his “Cook the Mountain” philosophy, where a modern approach and Alpine traditions combine to create perfect dishes full of flavour, all inspired by the seasons with a focus on using the whole ingredient with no food waste. The five tables with the best views are reserved for guests who choose the tasting menu, which has to be booked ahead of time. NB: the last cable-car leaves at 5pm!

Name: Altatto
Description: A taste of the big city in Milan’s southwest inner periphery: Altatto brings a fully vegetarian cuisine built on contemporary ideas, modern techniques, and flavors that alternate between bright citrus accents and softer, more captivating tones. A prime example is the mascarpone risotto with celeriac base and walnuts, intense and perfectly balanced. The space, minimal and clean-lined, finds warmth in an informal, jovial service that makes the overall experience all the more welcoming.

Name: Altriménti
Description: A bistro with a contemporary soul, where the informal atmosphere mingles with a subtle elegance that captivates without ostentation. The scents that waft out from the kitchen reveal the seasonality of the ingredients: fresh, carefully selected from small producers, transformed into dishes that speak Italian, with a harmony between sea and land. Every course is an invitation to discover something new, every detail a sign of attention. When it comes to wine, let the owner guide you: his enthusiasm will steer you towards pairings that enhance every nuance of flavour.

Name: Amandus
Address: Via Statale 125, Mandello del Lario, 23826, Italy
Description: Situated in the Villa Lario Resort, this restaurant directly overlooks the lake and boasts fine views which extend as far as the promontory of Bellagio. The excellent cuisine features a few freshwater fish dishes, as well as plenty of meat and seafood options, on a menu that combines classic recipes with a few more creative specialities.

Name: Amanõ
Description: Born in Campania but Sardinian by choice, Vincenzo Sorvillo tells the story of his journey through the very name of his restaurant, where a tilde over the ‘o’ symbolically evokes the sea that links the two lands. The atmosphere is intimate, with just a few tables and an open kitchen, which takes centre stage in the dining room alongside the numerous handcrafted decorations, in keeping with the restaurant’s identity. The culinary offering takes the form of 5- or 9-course tasting menus, in which Sardinian produce, flavours and traditions are reinterpreted with creativity and a contemporary sensitivity. The result is a range of original dishes brimming with character, capable of incorporating even the most unexpected influences, as demonstrated by the excellent gyoza filled with duck, Parmesan and green apple. A cuisine that manages to be at once unique, distinctive and, above all, extremely compelling.

Name: Amo Bistrot
Description: Traditional features such as exposed stone walls and wooden ceilings provide a pleasant contrast to the contemporary-style furnishings at this restaurant housed in the charming Palazzo Forti, while the attractive cloister with its old walls and soft lighting is highly recommended in the hot summer months. The cuisine combines traditional meat and fish dishes with Asian fare, including the option of sharing small dishes such as tapas or bao (steamed buns). There’s also an excellent brunch on Sundays.

Name: Anastasia
Description: This cocktail bar on the seafront is also a restaurant specialising in fresh fish served in a selection of classic dishes (such as tartare) and more elaborate recipes. The dining room is modern and spacious, plus there’s an outdoor terrace for alfresco dining in fine weather. Guestrooms and luxury apartments are also available (swimming pool on the roof).

Name: Angiò-Macelleria di Mare
Description: With a range of fish cured products and processes reminiscent of meat ageing, one can appreciate the essence of a true ‘seafood butcher’s’. The restaurant continues to evolve in the way it welcomes guests: today, guests order directly at their table, choosing either a single tasting menu or from a well-established à la carte selection.The cuisine, designed for sharing, invites guests to enjoy a wide-ranging and comprehensive tasting experience, while the dining room – minimalist yet attractive, with an open kitchen – also opens onto a cool, covered outdoor area, framed by small plants. Our advice remains to put yourself in the chef’s hands. Among the must-try dishes are the red prawns with panelle and finger lime; for more discerning palates, the sea liver pâté with Marsala and pistachios is particularly intriguing.

Name: Ansitz Romani
Address: Via Andreas Hofer 23, Termeno sulla Strada del Vino, 39040, Italy
Location: Termeno sulla Strada del Vino, Italy
Description: An attractive, well-kept restaurant in a historic building with a romantic, rural feel, especially in the beautiful garden. Although the menu is not that extensive, the chef is highly skilled, and it doesn’t feel as though anything is missing here. The dishes reflect the flavours of the region, making use of local ingredients such as venison and asparagus from Termeno accompanied by home-produced speck ham. The menu also features a couple of fish-based recipes and all dishes are modern and imaginative in style. Beautiful guestrooms are also available.

Name: Ansitz Steinbock
Description: Further renovations and the arrival of a new, young chef have transformed the offerings at this beautiful castle in the center of the small town. The à la carte selection, which is more tied to the local area, remains available at Stain, a classic Tyrolean stube that also offers outdoor service in the beautiful season. Meanwhile, "La Lumosa," a small and romantic setting with four tables, offers a more contemporary cuisine with a tasting menu that can be configured into five or six courses. There are twelve elegant suites for those wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Antica Cucina 1983
Description: Overlooking a square in the city centre, customers are welcomed into elegant surroundings, where almost exclusively fish dishes are served, in classic and tasty preparations, without too many complications to enhance the catch.

Name: Antica Farmacia
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant was used as a pharmacy until the late 1970s. In 2010, it was taken over by owner-chef Juri who now runs his own restaurant here, serving Tuscan-inspired cuisine made using local ingredients and recipes which he reinterprets with a light touch. Full of flavour, dishes include highlights such as baked marrow and Tuscan Chianti beef stew.

Name: Antica Locanda
Address: Piazza della Seta, Località San Leucio, Caserta, 81100, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This establishment is practically a trattoria; one can dine in either of two characteristic rooms separated by a brick archway. The cuisine is typical of the Naples area and rice dishes are the specialty.

Name: Antica Locanda dell'Orco
Description: Fans of Piedmontese cuisine will find one of its best exponents in this restaurant located at the end of a beautiful porticoed street in the historic centre. Savour some of Italy’s most exciting regional cooking, such as snails, bagna caoda, agnolotti pasta, a few (mainly freshwater) fish dishes, braised and boiled meats, “finanziera” stew and some extraordinary desserts – all prepared in magnificent style.

Name: Antica Osteria Al Forno
Description: A place that stirs the imagination the moment you spot the sign from the street: history lives on in this tavern, dating back to the early 19th century, in atmospheric rooms adorned with a wealth of decorations. The dishes, chosen from a shortlist, are part of the culinary tradition of home-style, family cooking, without any unnecessary complexity. They are full of flavours and memories; they delight the palate just as much as they warm the heart.

Name: Antica Osteria Il Monte Rosso
Description: Situated on the lakeside in the residential district of Verbania, this small, Old England - style restaurant serves a selection of freshwater and saltwater fish specialities. If the weather allows, ask for one of the few tables on the panoramic terrace.

Name: Antica Osteria La Rampina
Address: Via Emilia Fraz. Rampina 3, ang. via Rocca Brivio, San Giuliano Milanese, 20098, Italy
Description: It is said that General Radetzky, fleeing from the city during the Five Days of Milan rebellion, camped his troops right in front of La Rampina’s courtyard. Surrounded by nature and full of fascinating history, the restaurant now makes an ideal spot in which to enjoy the various culinary options served by Lino and his young son Luca, which offer a careful balance of local traditional flavour and skilful innovation.

Name: Antica Osteria Magenes
Description: This fascinating restaurant occupying an old house renovated in modern style comes as a surprise given its location in a small village deep in the countryside. Enjoy traditional cuisine reinterpreted in a playful and original way in the well-tended garden, where six exclusive tables provide the perfect setting for an intimate and romantic alfresco dinner.

Name: Antica Osteria Moirago
Description: This old monastery in Moirago, overlooking the Naviglio Pavese canal, was founded in 1250 and converted into an inn as early as 1478. Centuries may have passed, but the tradition of hospitality continues in the building’s enclosed painted portico, as well as in its two warm and atmospheric dining rooms. The chef’s Puglian origins explain the abundant use of vegetables and raw fish dishes, while in winter the cuisine takes on a more northern Italian flavour. Good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Antica Osteria da Penacio
Description: A family - run restaurant in a villa on the edge of a wood: inside two refined dining rooms and a small, but well stocked, wine bar; traditional cuisine.

Name: Antica Osteria dei Camelì
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within a sixteenth-century farmhouse of intact charm, where historic rooftops now coexist with modern solar panels in a clear gesture of sustainability, this establishment represents a successful encounter between classic elegance and contemporary design. The kitchen follows the same philosophy: tradition and innovation converse naturally in dishes that place great emphasis on nutritional balance and wholesome pairings, thanks in part to ingredients sourced from trusted local farmers. In the dining room, service maintains the professionalism and courtesy it has always been known for, affirming an approach that has lost neither rigor nor warmth over time.

Name: Antica Osteria del Mare
Description: Situated on the Naviglio away from Milan’s bustling nightlife, this rustic-style restaurant is decorated with a profusion of wood. As the name suggests, fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu, with a good choice of antipasti to whet the appetite, as well as inviting trays of raw fish dishes (shared by the whole table), followed by delicious traditional pasta and grilled options.

Name: Antica Osteria del Mirasole
Address: Via Matteotti 17/a, San Giovanni in Persiceto, 40017, Italy
Description: A place with soul, where every corner tells a story and the cuisine elegantly celebrates Emilian traditions – and more besides. The grill dominates among the main courses, while everything originates from the family’s farm and dairy, whose products are available in the shop and online. In addition to the à la carte menu, there are two tasting options: the great classics of the past and the Mirasole signatures. A dish worth the journey? The tortellini with cream skimmed from the top of the milk... simply unforgettable!

Name: Antica Osteria del Ponte
Address: Piazza Gaetano Negri 9, Cassinetta di Lugagnano, 20081, Italy
Description: This renowned restaurant in Lombardy has made its mark on the history of Italian cuisine and now has a new young couple at the helm and a new classic-contemporary menu. There’s also an interesting and reasonably priced three-dish menu at lunchtime, as well as the option of ordering an informal gastronomic picnic box. The beautiful natural setting of Cassinetta di Lugagnano and its canal completes the picture.

Name: Antica Osteria il Ronchettino
Description: An authentic Milanese trattoria in operation since the late 17th century as a post station, while the apartment buildings of Gratosoglio rose up all around it in the 1960s, the interiors still preserve their historic charm. The cuisine fortunately remains faithful to the spirit of the place, offering some Milanese classics, such as mondeghili (meatballs), risotto alla milanese (with or without ossobuco), and the “elephant ear” cutlet.

Name: Antica Pesa
Description: Typical Roman dishes made from carefully selected ingredients grace the menu of this restaurant, which is housed in a grain storehouse that once belonged to the neighbouring Papal State. Large paintings by contemporary artists hang on the walls and there is a small lounge with a fireplace near the entrance.

Name: Antica Trattoria Cirio
Description: A trattoria refreshed in its management yet firmly anchored to authentic Piedmontese tradition, which remains the cornerstone of its offering: from vitello tonnato to raw beef tartare, through to the inevitable agnolotti. Alongside these great regional classics sit iconic preparations from “bourgeois” cuisine, not solely Italian, such as onion soup or lamb stew enveloped in puff pastry crust, dishes particularly dear to proprietor Federico, who brings significant kitchen experience garnered in Italy and abroad. During the Sundays of the colder months, at both lunch and dinner, the trolley of boiled meats is not to be missed, presented in its complete formula with dessert and house wine included.

Name: Antica Trattoria Giovanelli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In an enchanting bucolic setting at the foot of the hills, this family-run trattoria – established in 1939 and now in its third generation – offers a cuisine deeply rooted in its territory.The menu celebrates the great classics of the tradition, from charcuterie to roasts and boiled meats, but it is above all the handmade fresh pasta and the almond cake served with zabaione that merit particular attention.In fine weather, the outdoor veranda provides a pleasant open-air space. For those wishing to extend the experience, the trattoria’s own-produced charcuterie is available to purchase.

Name: Antica Trattoria al Gallo 1909
Description: It is an unavoidable reference point in the gastronomic panorama of Ravenna and, as a matter of fact, it is almost always full! An "Historical Establishment of Italy", and rightly so considering that it has been run by the same family for over 100 years, this restaurant is a trattoria only in its name, given the blaze of art nouveau decorations inside. As regards the cuisine, you can expect regional dishes: truffles, succulent meats and local fish. In the dining room everyone is involved, while the young owner will illustrate the wine selection with the typically delightful congeniality of Romagna.

Name: Antica Trattoria del Gallo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A splendid example of a country trattoria, which has been delighting its guests with typical dishes from Lombardy for over a century. Meals are served either in the attractive vintage-style dining room or, in fine weather, outdoors under the Virginia creeper and mature wisteria. Truly enchanting!

Name: Antiche Carampane
Address: Rio Terà delle Carampane, Sestiere San Polo 1911, Venice, 30125, Italy
Description: From the typical floors to the wall decorations, everything here speaks to the heart to tell you about a historic trattoria where people joyfully return each time to enjoy local seafood specialities. Sarde in saor, baccalà mantecato, fried moeche (spring and autumn), cuttlefish in nero to name but a few. The recipes are crafted with skill and fidelity to tradition. In addition to the dishes listed on the menu, each day you will be verbally presented with off-menu specials. An excellent wine selection ranging from Italian to French labels with good value for money.

Name: Antico Albergo
Description: With its exposed bricks and beams, this restaurant housed in an 18C building has a historic feel. Delightful wisteria-shaded summer terrace, plus a menu featuring fish dishes and more creative options alongside traditional specialities from Lombardy.

Name: Antico Morer
Description: In a charming area of Treviso's historic centre, the Morer restaurant offers fresh seafood dishes, homemade pastas and desserts. Not to be missed are the lemon noodles and the scallop with its coral and pepper. Not far from the Cathedral, this historic venue is named after a mulberry tree – morer, in the local dialect – once located in front of the entrance, but which is now gone!

Name: Antico Ristorante Forassiepi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This restaurant is renowned in the province of Lucca, thanks to the reliable owners who have been at the helm here (the restaurant’s history goes back to the early 20C) since 2004. With its elegant decor and courteous and attentive service, the restaurant has a charming ambience in summer when meals are served alfresco with stunning views of the typical Tuscan hills, valleys and villages all around. The restaurant also owes its success to its cuisine, which focuses on regional specialities (both meat and fish) reinterpreted with a modern twist.

Name: Antico Ristorante Pagnanelli
Description: In business since 1882, yet constantly evolving, this restaurant boasts a superb location overlooking the lake. The menu features meat and fish dishes, enhanced by wild herbs. The extensive wine selection is presented on two wine lists. Don’t miss the famous wine cellars built into the rock, plus the small wine museum.

Name: Anticofurlo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Along the road that passes through Furlo (a hamlet of Acqualagna, one of the truffle capitals of Italy) this family trattoria (already an inn in the nineteenth century) offers the prestigious tuber in various dishes, subject to seasonal availability. The atmosphere is simple and informal, and the cooking firmly rooted in the territory; the handmade egg pasta is particularly good, as is the guinea fowl in a bread crust among the main courses.

Name: Anto e Robi
Description: Situated in the heart of a small town surrounded by rice fields, this restaurant has a charming and personalised feel. The cuisine is often (but not always) based around fish, which is showcased in dishes inspired by regional traditions. While Robi oversees the front of house with skill and expertise, offering recommendations on wine (over 300 labels, including many by the glass) and rum (his particular passion), Anto prepares a host of delicious recipes in the kitchen.

Name: Ape Vino e Cucina
Description: This attractive restaurant in the heart of Alba, the gastronomic capital of the Langhe, is home to chef Damiano Nigro who has previous experience in Michelin-starred restaurants in the area. The restaurant serves aperitif snacks, tapas and top-quality cocktails alongside its delicious, generously portioned meals which, as you might expect in Piedmont, have a traditional flavour. The pasta, bread, desserts and ice-cream are all homemade, while on our last visit in the summer we particularly enjoyed the maccheroncini with scampi and peppers, and the exquisite Fassona beef with a red-wine sauce and seasonal vegetables. Booked ahead is recommended.

Name: Apollinare
Description: In the heart of medieval Spoleto, nestled within the ancient walls of the Sant’Apollinare convent, this restaurant offers an intimate and romantic retreat. Exposed beams and stone, understated elegance, and a kitchen that celebrates seasonality and terroir, reinterpreting tradition with contemporary sensibility. The menu embraces meat, seafood, and vegetarian offerings. On summer days, a delightful outdoor terrace completes the experience.

Name: Aprudia
Description: A restaurant tucked into an intimate corner of the historic center, with spaces characterized by brick vaulting that creates a pleasant contrast with some modern touches in the furnishings. Here, Enzo Di Pasquale – through a tasting format where diners freely choose dishes and quantities – celebrates the seasonality of mostly plant-based and local products, sometimes sourced directly from his own garden. The dishes are absolutely original (like the restaurant’s name: if you're curious, ask for an explanation from the staff) and always very colorful. The philosophical thread is a commendable “no waste” approach.

Name: Aqua
Description: The most attractive space in this restaurant is its contemporary, almost Milanese-style veranda-dining room which boasts relaxing views of Lake Garda, with sailboats bobbing on the water ruffled by the famous Ora wind, and the peaks of Trentino in the distance. The Italian cuisine served here is prepared simply, allowing the quality of the ingredients (many of which are sourced locally) to shine through. Fish from the lake takes pride of place, although saltwater fish also features. There’s also a good selection of wine.

Name: Aquadulcis
Address: Contrada Tenda, Vallo della Lucania, 84078, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Created from the restoration of an old water-powered oil mill, the restaurant retains all the charm of its history: the kitchen is on the ground floor, while the dining room occupies the upper level in a charming glass-enclosed gallery with just a few tables overlooking the large wheel that once drove the millstone for olives and cereals. The dining experience unfolds across three tasting menus – vegetarian, land-based and seafood – designed to showcase the region in all its nuances. At the helm of the kitchen is Luigi Coppola, originally from nearby Paestum, who interprets the flavours and traditions of Cilento with a contemporary sensitivity, making judicious use of fermentation to add depth and complexity to the dishes without compromising the identity of the excellent local ingredients.

Name: Aquanova Hosteria
Description: Housed in an old “water house” with origins dating back to the 17C and a large water wheel still visible in the dining room, this restaurant is home to a chef with Albanian origins (who grew up in Italy) who creates fresh, imaginative and seasonal cuisine in colourful dishes that are full of flavour. Sicilian traditions (inland as well as coastal) with a highly personalised twist take centre stage on the à la carte and tasting menus. There’s also a firm focus on vegetables thanks to the restaurant’s own on-site kitchen garden, which is well worth a visit. Also not to be missed is a visit to the delightful wine cellar – a real treasure trove which is home to more than 1 700 labels from across the globe.

Name: Aquariva
Address: Via Marconi 57, Padenghe sul Garda, 25080, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Renowned for its fish, this restaurant offers a good choice of raw fish and a delicious plateau royale. The elegant, spacious dining room boasts a restful colour scheme and views of the lake through its picture windows.

Name: Arca
Address: Viale Rinascimento 143, San Benedetto del Tronto, 63074, Italy
Description: After years of serving fine cuisine in Alba Adriatica, chef Massimiliano Capretta has moved around 15km away to the Hotel Smeraldo. Here, he pays careful attention to the use of organic produce, creating meat and fish dishes that are inspired by local traditions and prepared in a style that is a combination of classic and modern influences. Desserts remain in the capable hands of his sister Dalila, whose millefeuille is one of her standout dishes.

Name: Aria
Description: The Villa Riviera resort home to this restaurant is situated slightly inland and uphill from the sea in a tranquil oasis of greenery. The modern, minimalist veranda-style dining room is welcoming and elegant, while the summer terrace has a romantic ambience with superb views of the coast, especially at sunset. The menu features modern, occasionally creative cuisine with Ligurian influences evident in dishes such as the “La mia Liguria” dessert which combines ingredients such as basil and olives with white chocolate, pine nuts and fiordilatte ice cream.

Name: Armando al Pantheon
Description: This small restaurant just a few metres from the Pantheon has been run by the Gargioli family since 1961, with the third generation now at the helm. Popular with locals and visitors alike for its traditional cuisine, which includes Roman and Lazian dishes, meat and fish options, and specialities such as offal, veal intestines, spring lamb, fresh anchovies, and sour-cherry tart.

Name: Armani/Ristorante
Description: Elegant and carefully prepared contemporary cuisine served on the seventh floor of a palazzo which is totally dedicated to the world of Armani. Superb views of Milan combine with a decor of black marble and backlit onyx to create an exclusive and fashionable ambience.

Name: Arnaldo - Clinica Gastronomica
Description: Crossing the threshold of this fifteenth-century palace next to Hotel Aquila d’Oro is like stepping into an Emilian tale of aromas, flavors, and memory. Rolling carts take center stage: antipasti featuring hand-carved prosciutto and erbazzone, desserts with zabaione to pour over pears in red wine, and the essential parade of roasts and boiled meats. The sfogline (pasta makers) prepare fresh pasta each morning, served in broth or with rich sauces. Arnaldo is a hymn to tradition: no frills, just authentic taste!

Name: Aroma
Description: Aroma occupies the historic spaces of Matera’s first pharmacy and overlooks, mere steps from Piazzetta G. Pascoli, a scenic vista of the Sasso Barisano: an ideal setting for a quality gourmet pause. The cuisine is characterised by measured creativity, never gratuitous, consistently attentive to balance and flavour. The dishes, expressive and inviting, bear the mark of a confident and distinctive hand. The menu offers a generous à la carte selection, complemented by two tasting menus conceived for those who wish to entrust themselves to the chef and be guided through the experience.

Name: Artifex
Description: This restaurant is situated within the Feuerstein Nature Family Resort, a 5-star property which continues to expand and which nestles in the verdant Val di Fleres, not far from Vipiteno and even closer to the Austrian border. In the small, elegant dining room here, the focus is on creative, regional cuisine, with dishes often accompanied by herbs and vegetables sourced from the property’s own kitchen garden where they are grown without the use of chemicals. Top-quality seasonal ingredients take pride of place in the cuisine here, while the well-stocked wine cellar features a good selection of labels decanted in the dining room by the talented sommelier.

Name: Arva
Address: Calle Tiepolo, Sestiere San Polo 1364, Venice, 30124, Italy
Description: Located in a 16th-century building, inside the Aman Venice hotel overlooking the Grand Canal, Arva is the ideal place to enjoy modern cuisine that celebrates the sea, the land and the finest seasonal ingredients, sourced from the Rialto market and the islands of the Venetian lagoon. The restaurant's dining rooms are opulent and overflowing with decorations in the most classic Venetian style, perfect for celebrating your stay in the Serenissima in style.

Name: Asina Luna
Address: Via della Resistenza 23, Peschiera Borromeo, 20068, Italy
Description: A restaurant with an attractive atmosphere, thanks to its profusion of wood, soft lighting and contemporary colour scheme. Meat aged for different periods takes pride of place on the menu. Sourced from different countries, it includes sweet Piedmontese Vicciola beef fed on hazelnuts and tender and delicately marbled Australian Scottona beef. Good selection of strongly flavoured and aged meat options.

Name: Atempo
Description: Situated on the outskirts of Martina Franca’s charming historic centre, this up-and-coming restaurant, led by chef Giovanni and maître d’ Martino, has quickly carved out a prominent place for itself on the local culinary scene. The cosy and elegant dining areas provide the perfect setting for a contemporary menu that thoughtfully showcases seasonal produce from Puglia. The cuisine reflects a measured and refined touch, skilfully balancing both fish and meat, while paying great attention to the presentation of the dishes. Among the most impressive dishes, the dessert-style reinterpretation of the famous Lecce coffee stands out: a coffee namelaka resting on a buttery crumble, enveloped in a light almond mousse and finished with fresh mint drops.

Name: Attico sul Mare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the second and top floor (don’t worry, there’s a lift!) of the historic Kursaal building, this panoramic penthouse-style restaurant has recently been given a new contemporary design after nearly 20 years in business. The same modern feel is evident in the cuisine, which focuses (but not exclusively) on fish and seafood on its inviting menu. Classic local recipes such as seafood salad (with ingredients skilfully cooked in front of guests in the dining room) feature alongside the chef’s more creative options, such as turbot, in which nearly all parts of the fish are served – fillets, cheeks and even the “crackling”. For dessert, we recommend the alkermes cake with Italian pastry cream and chocolate, which is finished directly in front of guests in the dining room.

Name: Aubergine
Description: Situated in a town famous for its thermal baths, this classically elegant restaurant serves meat and fish cuisine including specialities from the Veneto such as Berico ham, bigoli pasta with sardines, and veal liver with onions.

Name: Augurio
Address: Via Dietro le Mura B 16, Trento, 38122, Italy
Description: Opened by three brothers (Augurio is the family name), this restaurant in the city centre successfully combines the traditional and the modern in both its cuisine and its decor. The dining room, with an open-view kitchen on the ground floor, boasts an old, vaulted ceiling, while its wood furniture adds a contemporary look. The menu features local and Italian dishes reinterpreted with flavour and style. Lighter options are available at lunchtime; the grande carte needs to be ordered ahead of time.

Name: Aurea Osteria Contemporanea
Description: A new and decidedly original restaurant, run by a young, all-female team that has created a truly unique culinary experience. At the heart of the research lie the combinations of seafood and vegetables, a focus on minimising waste, and a marked preference for freshness and well-balanced acidity. The atmosphere is intimate and centres around the open-plan kitchen situated in the middle of the dining room: just a few tables and some seats at the counter allow guests to watch the kitchen team at work and see the dishes take shape. The cuisine stands out for its character, technique and creativity, with dishes that are hard to replicate elsewhere. Examples include white fish balls with medlar ketchup and spring onion, or line-caught fish served with a broth made from fish bones and wild herbs, lentils and juniper oil. An experience that breaks the mould and is definitely worth a visit.

Name: Aurora
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the Concattedrale di San Pietro Apostolo, Aurora boasts a cheerful and contemporary-style dining room with colourful furnishings, soft lighting and plenty of wine bottles on display. The carefully prepared cuisine includes Italian and regional meat and fish specialities with a light, modern twist.

Name: Ausa
Description: In the heart of Isernia, a young couple of chefs trained at Niko Romito’s school have launched a culinary venture that is breathing new life into the city’s food scene. Anisia Cafiero and Pasquale De Biase create a cuisine that is predominantly plant-based, characterised by solid technique, well-defined ideas and a remarkable lightness of touch. The artichoke is a standout dish: cooked twice and enhanced by a cream made from its own trimmings, it is served on a velvety potato purée and finished with a sauce of aromatic herbs, including wild mint. Great attention is also paid to bread, which takes centre stage in a dedicated selection that invites you to enjoy it with whipped butter or a selection of fine extra virgin olive oils.

Name: Autem*
Description: The entrance opens directly onto the open-plan kitchen, where Luca Natalini welcomes guests with his infectious energy and a spontaneous manner that you’ll also experience throughout the meal. The menu centres on a carefully curated selection of dishes, handwritten and updated daily depending on the day’s deliveries and the availability of the finest ingredients. In the elegant dining rooms, bathed in soft, subdued lighting, a culinary experience of the highest calibre takes shape, characterised by technical skill, sensitivity and a focus on the finest ingredients. Among the most convincing dishes are the plin ravioli filled with duck and tomato seeds, Italian-style sauce and pepper leaf, as well as the grilled milk-fed lamb accompanied by bitter herbs and chanterelles. At lunchtime, alongside the evening menu, the more informal ‘Convivium’ menu is also available: a set-price menu which, based on a single daily selection of ingredients, offers a succession of different tasting portions served in the centre of the table and designed to encourage sharing and conviviality.

Name: Azotea
Description: In the very heart of the city, with a small terrace that sets the mood, the interior reveals deliberately aged walls in soft shades of green, enriched by climbing plants that evoke a corner of South American jungle. It is the ideal setting for Nikkei cooking that looks directly to Peru, the chef’s native land, and expresses itself through a range of beautifully fresh offerings available both à la carte and within carefully considered tasting menus. The philosophy is clear: to celebrate one of the most vibrant and contemporary gastronomic traditions, with a hand attuned to contrasts and the clarity of flavours. Among the distinctive features of the house, which also operates as a well-stocked cocktail bar, the sip pairing stands out: a sequence of small cocktail tastings crafted with ingredients typical of Nikkei cuisine, conceived to accompany the dishes without overpowering them. Not to be missed is the yuzu Americano, pleasingly citrus-forward, with a hint of sharpness that invites the next sip.

Name: Ba Restaurant
Description: This restaurant combines Chinese traditions with contemporary, fashionable design in a dining room where large red lamps and small lanterns on the tables create an intimate and relaxing feel, accompanied by lounge music as a backdrop. The modern twist added to the classic Chinese dishes gives the cuisine an interesting flavour, from the carefully chosen ingredients and quality of their Dim Sum to our inspector’s favourite dish, namely the scallops with XO sauce, asparagus, foie gras salsa and cured ham chips.

Name: Babette
Description: Situated just beyond the centre of Albenga in a beautiful location right on the beach (with only a small private beach club separating it from the sea), this restaurant has been in business for over 20 years (10 years on this site, and 10 in the town centre before that). It is renowned for its excellent, modern cuisine that focuses on top-quality, fresh and seasonal fish. A lighter (yet equally excellent) menu is also available at lunchtime.

Name: Baccanti
Description: Facing Matera’s picturesque cave churches in one of the most charming parts of the old town, this restaurant is housed in a complex of old caves. Despite being inspired by local traditions, the cuisine is modern and creative in style and always of the highest quality.

Name: Bacchus
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A hotel restaurant with solid management, cheerful and welcoming. While lunch offers a very simple selection (including club sandwiches and hamburgers), as well as service, it’s in the evening that a beautiful menu based on Sardinian and Mediterranean cuisine is presented, with land-based dishes and especially seafood. When the weather permits, choose a table on the veranda overlooking the pool.

Name: Bacco
Description: Nestled within the historic centre, you’ll find classic and charming Apulian stone environments of a fourteenth-century building, while the kitchen sends forth predominantly fish dishes, along with some meat offerings, in classic Italian tradition recipes with a few modern twists.

Name: Bacucco d'Oro
Description: From the coast, you take a winding road uphill to this family-run trattoria which boasts sea views from its terrace. Apart from the salted cod, the menu only features meat dishes, with a focus on simple, traditional Abruzzo specialties. These include arrosticini (skewered grilled meat), fragrant mushrooms, barbecued meat and delicious “pizza dogge”, the latter a type of layered dessert with sponge cake, custard, confectioner’s cream and Alkermes liqueur. The concise wine list also focuses on the Abruzzo.

Name: Badalamenti Cucina e Bottega
Description: A historic address, established in the 1950s as a delicatessen selling charcuterie, cheeses and wines, it is now in its third generation and has been given a contemporary makeover. It is still “the shop” where you can buy local delicacies, but it also offers a restaurant service: traditional dishes from land and sea, revisited with taste and personality. The inspector's favourite dish? Cuttlefish ink arancina with red prawn tartare, pea cream and cheese fondue.

Name: Badessa
Description: This restaurant has a surprising location in a 19C cheese factory which once produced parmesan. Although the purpose of the building has changed, the love of the region remains the same – the chef goes out of his way to source local ingredients and search out old recipes, serving traditional Emilian dishes often with a modern twist. The fresh pasta and other ingredients are produced by the restaurant, while the carefully chosen wine list focuses on natural labels in particular.

Name: Bagatto
Description: Hidden down an alleyway in the town centre, this friendly trattoria boasts an attractive ceiling with exposed brickwork. An excellent address for fans of Ligurian cuisine, fish and seafood. House desserts include sour orange semifreddo.

Name: Baia del Silenzio
Description: In a beautiful position inside the bay, the restaurant serves dishes with a contemporary twist that enhance the local products and the good ingredients. The offer is divided between the bistrot for lunch, the gourmet dinner and the wine bar. In summer you can dine alfresco on the outdoor terrace or directly on the beach.

Name: Baita Fraina
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Warm little bar rooms, reminiscent of the German wine bars or "Stube", a summer terrace and well - prepared regional dishes: for those who want to escape the mundane life of Cortina for the silence of an isolated "baita" [mountain hut]. Delightful rooms, colourfully furnished in warm tones so you can better enjoy the silence and scents of the mountains.

Name: Baldo Vino
Address: Via Curtatone e Montanara 51, Pistoia, 51100, Italy
Description: In the historic centre of Pistoia, within the elegant Palazzo Ganucci Cancellieri, a charming 17th-century residence, chef Marco Cahssai and head of dining Martina Mattioli have embarked on a new chapter in their professional careers following their successful stint at the helm of Atman in Vinci. Joining them is Francesco Balloni, the restaurant’s owner and a great wine enthusiast, who offers guests an extraordinary wine cellar containing around 3,000 bottles, with a particular fondness for Champagne. In the kitchen, Cahssai demonstrates his talent through dishes that combine technique, creativity and restraint, characterised by refined presentation and consistently balanced flavours. Alongside the tasting menus, there is also an à la carte selection, while for those looking for a more informal experience, there is Bibendum, the restaurant’s bistro-style section, offering a selection of delicious and mouth-watering dishes.

Name: Balin Sestri Levante
Description: An intimate restaurant on the seafront with a tiny dining room and small veranda, and a young, contemporary ambience. The Mediterranean-style cuisine is modern and creative with a focus on Ligurian ingredients to which the chef adds the occasional Asian twist, often in the sauces. Booking ahead is recommended given the limited number of tables here!

Name: Balzi Rossi
Description: Still within Italy but just a stone’s throw from the French border, with a spectacular terrace overlooking the Côte d’Azur: from here the gaze takes in the historic centre of Menton as far as Cap Martin. In high season, reserving one of the most coveted outdoor tables well in advance is an absolute necessity; alternatively, the welcoming interior dining room offers an elegant and relaxing setting. The cooking follows a modern and fresh line, with seafood dishes that impress through their lightness and balance. Among the standout preparations, the shi drum wrapped in vine leaves with chargrilled tomato and onion: a combination of clean and harmonious flavours, played with purity and precision.

Name: Bar à Fromage
Description: A cosy, elegant Stube-style restaurant where the staff wear typical Aosta Valley costume and the menu features dishes with a particular focus on cheese (including an excellent fondue!) alongside traditional regional fare. Typical decor with refined, personalised furnishings and a profusion of wood.

Name: Baracca - Storica Hostaria
Description: A classic, attractively elegant restaurant which boasts an extensive choice of dishes on its menu. The varied options here range from meat to fish dishes, often prepared in regional recipes such as tagliatelle with duck ragù and toasted hazelnuts, chicken liver risotto, Vicenza-style baccalà and meat casserole.

Name: Barbagianni
Address: Via Gracco del Secco 86, Colle di Val d'Elsa, 53034, Italy
Description: Housed within an elegant stone building along the road leading into the heart of Colle, Barbagianni welcomes its guests into a warm and evocative setting: at the centre of the dining room stands a magnificent stabilised oak tree, illuminated by small lights that heighten its spectacular presence. Youthful and playful in its approach, the cuisine aims for a delightful balance between technique and flavour, featuring dishes that blend creativity with a sense of familiarity. The menu offers two tasting menus, alongside an à la carte option that encompasses meat, seafood and plant-based dishes, all designed to showcase the seasonality and quality of the ingredients. Completing the experience, a dynamic and good-humoured front-of-house team, attentive to the needs of each guest and always on hand to recommend the most fitting wine to accompany every creation.

Name: Barbieri
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just a few minutes’ drive from the charming medieval village of Altomonte, which we recommend you visit before sitting down to eat, is the Hotel Ristorante Barbieri. For almost sixty years, the Barbieri family has been welcoming guests with great warmth, serving cuisine that showcases regional ingredients and their own wines. On summer evenings, it’s well worth having dinner on the terrace, where a pleasant breeze makes the atmosphere even more enjoyable. Among the dishes not to be missed, the gnocchi with ‘nduja and salted ricotta stand out.

Name: Baretto di San Vigilio
Address: Via al Castello 1, San Vigilio, Bergamo, 24129, Italy
Description: In the small piazza that welcomes the funicular’s arrival station – with a small public parking area right at the top of the climb – lies a venue of retro charm, with Anglo-Saxon touches and an authentic soul. It serves as both bar and restaurant, where tradition meets modern accents in generous, thoughtfully composed dishes. The undisputed stars are the meats, accompanied by bread and desserts made strictly in-house. In warmer months, service moves to the panoramic terrace, offering enchanting views over the city (and, for the more intrepid, even in winter when the sun permits). Inside, two rustic-elegant dining rooms are warmed by cordial, convivial service that completes the experience.

Name: Barlèsh
Description: In the heart of Montevarchi, as cozy as a dining room at home, Barlèsh restaurant offers what the chef likes to call "spontaneous cuisine." This unconventional place will delight you with both traditional and contemporary recipes: a six-course tasting menu and an à la carte menu featuring shareable bites, main courses, and desserts.

Name: Battipalo
Description: An intimate and atmospheric venue, ideal for a romantic lakeside stop, where you can enjoy a relaxing break thanks to Italian and lake cuisine, sometimes reinterpreted with a more contemporary approach, but with little affectation and, instead, excellent substance. Enthusiasts will appreciate the snails with bread, butter, and parsley, accompanied by a garlic cream and seasonal mushrooms. Above all, the use of quality raw materials is fundamental.

Name: Bebop
Description: Just a few steps from the Politeama theatre, this small and elegant contemporary jewel box welcomes guests into a romantic, relaxed atmosphere. In the kitchen, a young talent proposes a personal and modern cuisine, rooted in regional tradition and underpinned by a careful selection of excellent local ingredients. Not to be missed is the BBQ poussin with sweet-and-sour vegetables, a well-balanced dish rich in nuance, as are the delicious tagliolini with shellfish, scented with cumin and lemon, an original and highly successful combination.

Name: Beccaccino
Description: Situated within a nature reserve, this recently renovated restaurant makes the most of its natural materials and bright, airy feel. The menu focuses on fish dishes made from freshwater and saltwater fish alike.

Name: Bel Ami
