Description: This 19C palazzo renovated in modern style serves fish and seafood, including raw dishes, with fish displayed in a cabinet in the dining room. Among the desserts, the vanilla ice-cream is a classic favourite!

Name: Bella Italia Pesce
Address: Via Sebino 29, Peschiera del Garda, 37019, Italy
Description: Not far from the centre of Peschiera, yet with a car park for those arriving by car, the restaurant is an excellent choice for anyone looking for top-quality seafood, with dishes that often have a Mediterranean flavour. The dishes served are often elaborate and technically sophisticated, yet without compromising on the quality of the fish, which is paired with intense and flavourful tastes. You should also try the desserts.

Name: Belle Parti
Description: In a charming arcaded alley in the pedestrian centre, on the first floor of the historic Palazzo Prosdocimi, the warm and welcoming romance of the room will convince you that you are in the right place. Paintings, mirrors, and woodwork rival the beautiful ceiling of exposed beams, while the à la carte proposal is in tune with the seasons, offering a review of tasty and classic mostly seafood dishes (but some customisation is there, as in the case of Belle Parti's spaghetti alla chitarra, a cacio e pepe embellished with scampi), mostly regionally sourced, with good meat alternatives. Reception and service genteelly tuned to the feminine.

Name: Belvedere
Address: Via Monti di Mola 39, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
Description: Over the years, this family restaurant has become one of the most popular along this coastline. An informal dining room provides the backdrop for the decidedly Mediterranean cuisine served here, where the focus is the fish display cabinet that changes daily and from which guests can make their choice. The friendly and professional approach of the two brothers that run the restaurant has contributed to its success, while the brand-new terrace-lounge, with its stunning view, is the perfect spot for an aperitif or after-dinner drink.

Name: Belé
Description: The name says it all – in Milanese dialect, “belé” means beautiful and the word is an apt description of this restaurant. Belé is charmingly lit by an old-fashioned chandelier on which the pieces of crystal create a play of light resembling an intricate and shifting lace-like pattern. The dining rooms are decorated in attractive contemporary colours, with comfortable armchairs and acoustics perfect for conversation, while the cuisine is Italian with a modern twist.

Name: Benedikto
Address: Via Eremo delle Carceri 1/a, Assisi, 06081, Italy
Description: On the edge of Assisi’s historic centre, within the refined setting of the Nun hotel, Benedikto offers a selection of classic Umbrian products, but the gastronomic proposal is principally creative and of a high order. In fine weather, dining on the terrace with its view over the Rocca di Assisi takes on a particularly romantic quality.

Name: Benso
Description: Situated in a small garden in the historic centre, this modern bistro has a light, airy feel thanks to its large windows and its outdoor tables perfect for alfresco dining in summer. The menu features contemporary-style, personalised meat and fish dishes which are full of flavour, while at lunchtime, the lighter “Pranzetto” menu is a good option. The restaurant also offers an excellent selection of cocktails for an evening aperitif, plus an impressive choice of digestifs to enjoy after your dinner.

Name: Bentōteca
Description: Top-quality Japanese cuisine with heavy Mediterranean influences takes pride of place at this restaurant, where talented chef Toku Yoji Tokuyoshi creates dishes such as horsemeat tataki with a pizzaiola sauce, and barbecued fish neck with friggitello pepper. If you opt for a seat on the large bench facing the kitchen, you’ll be able to watch the chefs at work and admire the precision required to prepare different types of sushi. Modern, understated decor.

Name: Between
Description: This top-quality restaurant occupies just one simple, minimalist-style dining room, where the young female chef serves a happy combination of Piedmontese ingredients and more creative dishes acquired during her time working abroad.

Name: Bianca sul Lago
Description: Overlooking the evocative Lake Annone, the restaurant at Bianca Relais captivates from the very first glance thanks to its expansive panoramic windows, which frame sunsets of rare beauty as the sun slips slowly behind the gentle outline of the surrounding hills. An elegant and refined setting, ideal for an emotionally resonant gastronomic experience. At the helm of the kitchen is chef Filippo Oggioni, previously awarded a Michelin Star at Vecchio Ristoro in Aosta, who presents a creative and refined proposal articulated across three “blind” tasting menus: one dedicated to the plant world, one centred on freshwater fish, and a third that follows the inspiration and seasonality of the market. Completing the journey is a young, well-trained and attentive front-of-house team. For a more informal approach, the Drop Restaurant & Lounge Bar offers a versatile and contemporary alternative, with an all-day menu served continuously from midday to ten in the evening, perfect for any moment of the day.

Name: Bino
Description: In the heart of the historic centre, next to the Ceramics Museum – some of whose works also adorn the restaurant’s dining areas – this venue welcomes guests into its elegant dining rooms and a pleasant outdoor terrace overlooking a charming little square. The culinary concept is the brainchild of Giuseppe Ricchebuono, a Michelin-starred chef from Noli, who showcases the local area through a cuisine that blends ingredients from both land and sea, while incorporating a touch of creativity. The dishes showcase traditional Ligurian ingredients and flavours with a sense of balance and character; the potato gnocchi with homemade pesto and fresh pine nuts are particularly successful, a dish that captures the simplicity and richness of the region’s cuisine.

Name: Bis Osteria Italiana Contemporanea
Address: Via 20 Settembre 50, Colle di Val d'Elsa, 53034, Italy
Description: In the glorious premises of the old Arnolfo restaurant in the old town, this restaurant is run by the same management as previously, although with a new young chef at the helm in the kitchen. The delicious yet concise menu features “Italian specialities” (the name given to all the main courses) with a focus on meat and fish, accompanied by excellent bread options (you can even order “scarpetta” dipping bread for mopping up the remains of a Cinta Senese pork sauce). The house speciality is a delicious pigeon dish. In fine weather, guests can dine on the beautiful, tranquil terrace.

Name: Bislakko
Address: Via Thaon de Revel 87, Vercelli, 13100, Italy
Description: They’ve played with words here, because “bislacco” (quirky) applies only to the name. This restaurant will win you over with its cuisine: meat dishes, fish, and vegetarian options coexist harmoniously, without forgetting the ever‑present risottos, available à la carte or in tasting menus. Among these, Chocolate Passion stands out, where chocolate – expertly dosed – appears in every course. After all, they call themselves a “cioccoristoreria” (a playful portmanteau of chocolate and restaurant).

Name: Bistrot
Description: Anyone who loves traditional recipes – whether meat or fish dishes – and a wide choice will find this restaurant the ideal place to dine. Overlooking a small square in the historic centre where, weather permitting, a few tables are set up for al fresco dining (others are on a covered veranda and, finally, in the dining rooms inside), it is a cosy restaurant serving excellent dishes.

Name: Bistrot 64
Description: The classic-style dining room in this restaurant situated in the Flaminio district belies the gourmet discoveries that await here, with echoes of traditions from Lazio that act as inspiration for creative, top-quality dishes with the occasional Asian twist.

Name: Bistrot Donatella
Description: This restaurant in a small village dominated by a bell tower boasts a charming inner courtyard which provides a romantic setting for a meal in fine weather. The Piedmontese cuisine served here is prepared using top-quality ingredients. A friendly welcome completes the picture, making this an enjoyable dining experience.

Name: Bistrot La Perla
Address: Strada Col Alt 105, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: The venue unfolds around a large wooden bar, where the bartenders are constantly at work making excellent cocktails that complement an impressive wine list. We are in the bistro of the famous La Perla hotel: a tribute to mountain life, expressed through charming and cheerful décor that creates a lively and welcoming atmosphere. The menu invites you to indulge in mouth-watering dishes inspired by the classic flavours of Italian tradition, while live music plays in the background.The venue is open practically all day: a café in the morning, a bistro at lunchtime, a more informal menu from 2 pm to 4 pm, and then it’s time for aperitifs, with cocktails and snacks, before moving on to dinner.

Name: Bistrot Royal
Description: Inside the refined Grand Hotel Royal e Golf, the Bistrot offers the opportunity to savor the delicious flavors of Valle d’Aosta in a refined and lighter interpretation. In recipes where the quality of the raw ingredients takes center stage, you’ll be pampered by excellent service while comfortably seated in spaces that interpret Alpine style with personal touches.

Name: Bistrot de Venise
Address: Calle dei Fabbri 4685, Sestiere San Marco, Venice, 30124, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In the heart of the city, just a few steps from St. Mark's Square and Rialto, the fine restaurant Bistrot de Venise will surprise you with Venetian cuisine that combines tradition and innovation. Both past and current dishes are reinterpreted with a contemporary twist, offering a unique dining experience. Wine lovers will be delighted by the selection of Italian rarities, perfect to accompany each course.

Name: Bites
Description: The cuisine at this tiny, simply furnished restaurant includes barbecued dishes and fermented ingredients, all of which feature on a tasting menu. Guests can also choose à la carte: the small portions (as the restaurant name suggests) make it possible to taste several dishes at a reasonable cost. Booking is essential in the evening and also advisable at lunchtime.

Name: Blanco Osteria da Fabio
Description: Just steps from the waterfront, yet conveniently close to the city center, this venue captivates with its warm, welcoming atmosphere. The front-of-house is gracious and smiling, while the kitchen delivers a menu steeped in the sea and tradition: concise, yet brimming with authentic flavors. Our advice? Don’t miss the housemade fresh pasta: the scialatielli with shrimp and stracciatella is a celebration of indulgence, while the maccheroncini showcase simplicity elevated to excellence. Completing the experience, fragrant bread served with a light and rustic artisanal oil that speaks of authenticity.

Name: Blaue Traube
Description: Young yet already remarkably mature, Christoph Huber brings fresh energy to the Blue Grape (Blaue Traube), a historic establishment with roots reaching back to the seventeenth century. His is a contemporary cuisine that engages with South Tyrolean tradition without nostalgia, but with an informed and cultured perspective: rigorously selected local products, techniques such as fermentation to lend depth, and a precise vision that weaves together terroir and modern sensitivity. Hospitality is calibrated with, never excessive, care in perfect harmony with a setting that preserves the charm of history without forsaking present-day comfort. In the evening, the gastronomic experience unfolds through a shared tasting menu, conceived as a singular narrative. At lunch, the approach becomes more nimble and informal, while maintaining the same dedication to flavour and ingredient quality.

Name: Blum
Description: A magnificent location directly in a gazebo where you can count the waves breaking on the beach, but in case of bad weather, there’s also an equally intimate and elegant indoor dining room available. Pampered by attentive and exceptionally kind service, follow the chef’s creations along tasting journeys, including vegetarian options, or à la carte dishes from both land and sea, always served with great aesthetic taste, often built on local products crafted with contemporary and colorful sensibility. In short, enjoy the complete experience that two hours in this exclusive corner of Sicily will offer you!

Name: Bluu il Mare Dentro
Address: Piazza Luigi Guerritore 11, Nocera Inferiore, 84014, Italy
Description: The double “u” in this restaurant’s name is not a mistake but was added with the intention of evoking the flow and sound of water that can heard from afar. Here, chef Angelo Borghese demonstrates his passion for the sea through his delicious, precise and personalised recipes in which the highest quality fish takes centre stage. The escarole and anchovy pizza with colatura mayonnaise is excellent, as is the selection of raw and marinated fish dishes.

Name: Boccadoro
Description: Situated on the outskirts of Padova, this classically elegant restaurant is very popular with locals – and for good reason! The menu includes skilfully prepared dishes influenced by the traditions of the Veneto (from bigoli pasta to dried cod and liver Venetian-style) as well as a selection of grilled options.

Name: Boccon DiVino
Address: Via Traversa dei Monti 201, località Colombaio Tozzi, Montalcino, 53024, Italy
Description: At the edge of the town, a skilfully restored farmhouse welcomes guests into an atmosphere of refined simplicity: from the carefully appointed rustic dining room to the bright glazed terrace, pleasant even in winter.The kitchen celebrates the flavours of the territory, reinterpreted in a measured contemporary key, without forgoing certain great classics such as peposo and onion soup.The wine list favours the local reds, with particular attention to Brunello and to labels of mature vintages. In the dining room, a warm welcome and assured knowledge of wine contribute to making the experience all the more rewarding.

Name: Bolle
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: We are in the Agnelli showroom, a well-known manufacturer of cookware for professional kitchens. The modern shop is located on the ground floor, while the first floor hosts the restaurant with its elegant tables in a refined minimalist and contemporary environment. On the menu, dishes with an impressive balance of ingredients, including occasionally exotic choices.

Name: Bon Wei
Description: China on a plate! This attractive restaurant with an intriguing decor combining elegance, modern style and Asian influences serves a wide selection of Chinese specialities. Dishes include appetisers, dumplings, noodles and meat options, as well as a huge array of specialities from eight different regions, from the spicy dishes of Szechuan to the delicate flavours of Zhejiang.

Name: Borgo Cala Creta-Giardino Arabo
Description: In the elegant resort of Dammusi di Borgo Cala Creta, surrounded by lush Mediterranean scrub, the “Giardino Arabo” is their beautiful restaurant, with tables elegantly arranged around a spectacular olive tree. Outdoors, you can enjoy a rich seafood cuisine with a modern and imaginative touch, featuring traditional recipes, including an unmissable “Seafood Caponata” enriched with unsweetened cocoa and pistachio.

Name: Bottega Aleotti
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the splendid Santa Croce church, this charming restaurant should not be missed. The cuisine combines Emilian traditions with fresh, local ingredients, and includes dishes with a more contemporary touch. The excellent bread and home-made pastries add to the overall dining experience.

Name: Bottega Culinaria
Address: Contrada Pontoni 72, San Vito Chietino, 66038, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled amid a charming landscape of olive groves, this restaurant is not particularly easy to find, so make sure that you use a satnav or ask for directions when booking. A simple, minimalist-style dining room provides the backdrop for imaginative cuisine which includes plenty of vegetables and is full of contrasting flavours and reinterpreted regional influences.

Name: Bottega Lucia
Description: A charming bistro-style establishment, with exposed wood and brick creating a warm, informal atmosphere, offering immediate and flavorful Italian cuisine – the spaghetti alla chitarra cacio e pepe with black truffle is emblematic – alongside forays into the nearby Iberian Peninsula and playful international influences. Among these, the steamed bao with pulled pork and coleslaw and the celebrated Milanese-style gyoza stand out, the latter filled with ossobuco and served with saffron cream. Meat and fish appear in equal measure, in a menu designed to satisfy diverse tastes without losing coherence. Just steps away is Casa Lucia, a more informal iteration of the same establishment, ideal for simple dishes and good pizza.

Name: Bottega del Re
Address: Via Francesco Domenico Guerrazzi 66r, Genoa, 16146, Italy
Description: In the tranquil heart of Albaro’s residential quarter, a cool summer courtyard welcomes guests with the scent of flowers and the gentle rustle of leaves. Inside, warm spaces blend rustic charm with elegant touches, creating a comforting, refined atmosphere. The cuisine is a journey between land and sea, where tradition meets seasonality: each dish reveals the authentic flavors of ingredients carefully sourced by young, talented Chef Orlandi. Not to be missed: the “quaglia della bottega,” quail stuffed with a giardiniera of crunchy, aromatic vegetables, releasing intense aromas with every bite. Our advice: save room for dessert, true masterpieces of sweetness that bring the meal to a close with velvety, surprising notes.

Name: Bramea
Address: Viale Villa d'Errico 10, Palazzo San Gervasio, 85026, Italy
Description: Bramea, whose name is inspired by a rare butterfly native to the Vulture area, comes to life within a skilfully restored ancient ruin. The restaurant, characterised by a modern and contemporary style, presents a cuisine that expresses itself through several tasting menus, set alongside a concise and well-calibrated à la carte menu. Lucanian ingredients form the point of departure for every journey and make their impression from the very first amuse-bouches: the fried lampascione and the taste of gnummareddo both stand out as particularly accomplished, immediately arousing the curiosity of the palate.

Name: Brezza fish and chill
Description: An alternative eatery amid the Abruzzo dining options, situated on the beautiful seafront promenade at Soverato. The idea is simple: fish takes centre stage, served in rolls, on "broast" and “friselle” bread, as well as raw or fried, although generous salads and delicious desserts are also available. The ingredients, full of flavour and always simply prepared, result in copious and colourful dishes. Good quality wine is available by the glass, plus a fine choice of cocktails which is enhanced in the evening by the addition of creative home-made options. Friendly female staff, plus excellent background music. A pleasant address serving quality food at very reasonable prices!

Name: Brindo
Description: The service is characterized by a cohesive and friendly team in welcoming guests to their small home. Brindo is an informal reality, where the cuisine is fun, engaging and more than simply territorial: raw foods, tartar and fish of the day are at the top!

Name: Bros'
Address: SS172, zona G, 59, Martina Franca, 74015, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Floriano Pellegrino and Isabella Potì have transferred their gastronomic project into the Relais Villa San Martino, just a few kilometres from Martina Franca, in a setting of classic elegance with a slightly retro appeal. There is no à la carte menu: the dining experience consists of surprise tasting menus – the ‘trajectories’ – which must be selected at the time of booking. The cuisine continues to follow the path that made Bros’ famous, taking its inspiration from Apulian ingredients and traditions and reinterpreting them using contemporary techniques, with a growing focus on the use of the whole ingredient. Alongside the usual creative drive, we are now seeing a renewed engagement with classical traditions, well exemplified by dishes such as the pasta and duck timbale, where tradition and innovation strike a compelling balance. The service, expertly managed by Ruben, guides guests through a carefully orchestrated experience that begins the moment they arrive.

Name: Bruna Bistrò
Description: Set in a corner building on the Senigallia seafront, this restaurant offers the very best of traditional Marche seafood cuisine, combined with friendly, informal service. Timeless dishes, such as monkfish tripe in potacchio and handmade spaghetti with Ragusa-style porchetta sauce, while among the main courses, the extraordinary Senigallia-style brodetto (a red fish soup) is a feast for the eyes as well as the palate.

Name: Buca di Sant'Antonio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Just a stone’s throw from Piazza San Michele, in the heart of the beautiful historic centre of Lucca, the Buca di Sant'Antonio dates back over 200 years and is one of the city’s oldest restaurants. Here, the old copper pots and pans that hang from the ceiling add to the warm, romantic atmosphere, while the cuisine unsurprisingly showcases traditional Tuscan specialities including meat dishes and home-made pasta.

Name: Buriani dal 1967
Address: Via Matteotti 66, Pieve di Cento, 40066, Italy
Description: A family-run restaurant in the province of Bologna with an excellent reputation for good food. Whether you choose one of the fish-based recipes or meat dishes, you’ll enjoy cuisine with a balance of classic flavours and modern influences, including a few regional specialities.

Name: Bàtu
Description: Housed within a splendid historic villa that has been restored to its former glory, this restaurant marks a significant milestone in Sicily’s tradition of exceptional hospitality, as it forms part of the first Relais & Châteaux property in Taormina and on the island. A meticulous restoration project has been carried out across the estate, creating elegant, contemporary spaces that blend seamlessly with the property’s original charm. One of the most evocative venues is La Rotonda sul Mare, an iconic viewpoint overlooking the coast which provides a setting for private events and special occasions. In the kitchen, chef Luca Miuccio creates a menu that is closely tied to the seasons and the world of vegetables, showcasing local ingredients through refined and creative dishes. Guests can choose between two eight-course tasting menus: one that is vegetarian, elegantly celebrating the richness of the plant kingdom, and a second menu that combines produce from the vegetable garden with a selection of fine fish and meat. The experience is rounded off by the work of bar manager Marco, who guides guests in choosing the best pairings with personalised advice and original cocktail pairing itineraries, tailor-made to bring out each nuance of the menu.

Name: CR21
Description: In the heart of the old town, among narrow streets steeped in history, lies a modern bistro that exudes energy with its bright colours and open kitchen. Here, chef Di Bartolo creates contemporary dishes that evoke Mediterranean flavours, interpreted with skill and imagination. Every creation is an invitation to discover authentic flavours with an innovative twist, in an atmosphere that combines elegance and friendliness. Highlights include the crispy cannolo, red prawns and burrata with red fruit coulis, as well as chive mayonnaise.

Name: Ca' 7
Address: Via Cunizza da Romano 4, Bassano del Grappa, 36061, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a charming 18C villa, this elegant restaurant overlooks its attractive garden in a magical setting which is typical of the Veneto. The cuisine also has a regional focus, with classic recipes featuring on the menu alongside more creative dishes (fish appears more often than meat).

Name: Ca' Apollonio Gourmet
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: Ca’ Apollonio Gourmet offers a contemporary cuisine deeply rooted in the territory of the Venetian foothills, where nature, seasonality, and research coexist in refined equilibrium. Within a historic villa set in the landscape of Monte Grappa, executive chef Alessio Longhini constructs tasting menus that celebrate local and organic ingredients sourced from a carefully selected short supply chain, many of them grown in the property’s own kitchen gardens according to principles of regenerative agriculture.The proposal develops through menus that weave together gastronomic memory, technique, and contemporary sensitivity, following the rhythm of the seasons and offering an evolving reading of the territory. Completing the experience is a cellar of over a thousand labels – spanning small producers and great houses – with a particular focus on PIWI grape varieties, curated by sommelier Michele Griggio. In an intimate and elegant setting, animated by the masterful front-of-house direction of maître Lorenzo Palma, every detail is considered with a view to creating an experience that is harmonious and immersive.

Name: Ca' Mia
Description: This welcoming restaurant in the hills surrounding Lake Alserio makes guests feel completely at home. The two young chefs with plenty of experience behind them create modern dishes with a preference for quick cooking methods and a focus on a wood-fired oven and barbecue, as well as fermented ingredients.

Name: Ca' del Profeta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in a beautiful location in the Asti countryside overlooking rolling hills and the estate’s own vineyards, Ca' del Profeta lies just a few kilometres from the provincial capital. A modern dining room and panoramic terrace provide the backdrop for decidedly innovative Piedmontese cuisine, which is inspired by traditional recipes and seasonal ingredients and then transformed by the chef into personalised dishes. Ingredients from further afield, such as root vegetables (black salsify, celeriac and beetroot) also make an appearance in three creative recipes inspired by the Orient. The service is friendly yet professional, plus a few modern guestrooms are also available. A panoramic swimming pool completes the picture.

Name: Cacciani
Description: Run by the Cacciani family for over 100 years, this is one of the most famous restaurants in the Castelli Romani region. Demonstrating a real passion for regional traditions and eschewing modern trends, the menu continues to offer a tempting selection of delicious classic dishes from Lazio, including a couple of fish and seafood options. The focaccia, which is served with the bread, is superb and well worth a mention. The dining room evokes the long history of the restaurant, while the panoramic terrace is a firm favourite with guests.

Name: Caffè Grande - Osteria del Centro
Description: Almost all the main dishes at this restaurant are grilled (mostly meat but there are also fish options), plus there’s a good choice of appetisers, including substantial options such as tripe and sweetbreads, with tasting menus that combine starters and main courses. The à la carte features a generous selection of classic, well-prepared dishes made from top-quality ingredients. The restaurant occupies the premises of a historic café that has experienced closures and problems in the past but has now been courageously reopened by three young business partners.

Name: Caffè Meletti
Address: via del Trivio 56 (piazza del Popolo), Ascoli Piceno, 63100, Italy
Description: Housed on the first floor of the historic café where the aniseed liqueur of the same name was created, this restaurant serves simple yet creative, regional and maritime - inspired cuisine. Don’t miss the terrace with views of Piazza del Popolo. Faster options available at lunchtime.

Name: Caffè delle Rose Bistrot
Description: Occupying an early 20C building in the heart of Pallanza’s picturesque historic centre, this authentic bistro now has a young and contemporary feel. Run by Massimiliano Celeste, a talented chef who is very well known in the region, the restaurant specialises in Mediterranean cuisine prepared with a touch of imagination. There’s a small chef’s table in front of the kitchen, plus an old ice-house (now a small wine cellar housing some excellent wines) which is well worth visiting.

Name: Café Carducci
Description: Those with a passion for retro and nostalgic atmospheres will find inspiration in this establishment opened in 1928. Since then, generations have succeeded one another, but always within the same family. Today, you enter through the bar before passing into the dining room, a space so enchanting with its books, paintings, and bottles that you’ll never want to leave. Alongside a vast selection of cured meats and cheeses (predominantly French), exquisite meat and fish dishes await, complemented by a legendary cellar boasting some two thousand labels.

Name: Café Cracco
Address: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, Milan, 20121, Italy
Description: This café run by the famous chef of the same name (his gourmet restaurant is on the first floor of the same building) is the bar-pasticceria par excellence in Milan. It is also a good place to eat, with a menu that moves easily from Milanese specialities reinterpreted with a modern twist to international dishes, including pizza. The café offers tables arranged outdoors in the extraordinary Galleria and is open seven days a week but does not take bookings.

Name: Café Les Paillotes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This old acquaintance of the Michelin Guide now has a new chef at the helm! Although the decor and furnishings remain the same with a slightly old-fashioned feel, the cuisine is modern yet with no unnecessary frills and has a fresh and generous flavour. Highlights on the menu include the new raw fish options, which have an entire tasting menu to themselves. The well-stocked wine cellar is home to around 500 labels which offer good value for money.

Name: Café Quinson
Description: The Café Quinson has reopened! In this rustic yet elegant “mountain restaurant”, the whole family makes guests feel welcome, serving a selection of regional dishes with an imaginative and contemporary touch. Excellent choice of wines, almost all of which are available by the glass.

Name: Cala Luna
Address: Via Angela di Francesca 1, Cefalu, 90015, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Refined fine dining at the boutique hotel "Le Calette." In the summertime, Cala Luna is hosted in a splendid garden surrounded by plants and flowers, with breathtaking views of the bay, the Caldura sea stacks, and the Rocca. The dishes are a technical and creative expression of Chef Dario Pandolfo’s experiences, who applies what he has learned working in prestigious restaurants in Italy and abroad to Sicilian ingredients and traditions. The result is a vibrant and colorful cuisine, sometimes with strong flavors, always creative and deeply Mediterranean. "Green" notes are evident not only in the "Fiori di Luna" menu, dedicated to Sicilian vegetables, herbs, and flowers, but also in the sustainable approach to using raw materials, enhancing every part of them, and focusing on reducing waste without ever compromising quality.

Name: Camana Veglia
Description: Situated on the first floor of the hotel of the same name, this restaurant is run by professional and welcoming staff who immediately make you feel pleasantly at home in the warm, Stube-style dining room. The menu features local specialties alongside more creative options for guests keen for a change from traditional cuisine.

Name: Campamac
Description: A real gourmet inn which serves traditional Piedmontese dishes made from excellent ingredients alongside top-quality meats cooked on the barbecue grill. An elegant ambience with a deliberately retro feel, which is beautifully maintained and has plenty of charm.

Name: Campiello
Address: Via Nazionale 46, San Giovanni al Natisone, 33048, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Fish and wine are the soul of this historic restaurant, where the scent of the sea meets the fragrance of the vineyards. The catch, which is among the finest on the market, yields the most delicious dishes: the fish soup with shellfish, enveloped in a Buzara jus that releases intense flavours, is an absolute must. The wine cellar, with a selection of 25,000 bottles, takes you on a journey through the Collio and Colli Orientali hills, enriched by great Italian and international labels and big bottles for real winelovers. A destination to add to your diary if you love authentic and memorable experiences.

Name: Campo Cedro
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the centre yet away from the tourist crowds, this restaurant is well worth the effort needed to find it! Here, Japanese chef Sugihara, who has more than 20 years’ experience working in Italy, creates modern and skilfully prepared Italian meat and fish dishes which are fresh and elaborate. You’ll nearly always find seafood risotto on the menu, which is made with fish, mussels and finely chopped shrimps all cooked together with rice and then sprinkled with crumbled seaweed and dotted with tomato paste. Excellent value for money!

Name: Campocori
Address: Via di Santa Maria de' Calderari 49, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: Housed within the Chapter Hotel and designed by South African designer Tristan Du Plessis, this restaurant is conceived as a nighttime place with a dark atmosphere, “ferrying” into the capital a contemporary, cosmopolitan take on fine dining, blending Roman, Italian, and international references.

Name: Canapone
Description: In classic settings embellished with many plants and customised by the porphyry floor, while in warm weather we move to the outdoor area overlooking the splendid Piazza Dante, in any case they serve Maremma cuisine of excellent fragrance and based on impeccable raw material, both fish (our suggestion goes for the steamed catch of the day with vegetables and freshly made mayonnaise) and meat. Next door, Osteria Canapino offers a more streamlined and informal cuisine.

Name: Capriccio
Description: Young chef Graziano Accolla has returned to his native city where he serves creative cuisine of the highest quality, while at the same time raising Augusta’s gastronomic profile. Thanks to his experience in Michelin-starred restaurants, he offers highly interesting dishes which focus on the use of top-quality ingredients.

Name: Capuccina
Address: Via Novara 19/b, località Capuccina, Cureggio, 28060, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A new chef brings fresh energy and ideas to this excellent restaurant housed within a 16C farmhouse that is surrounded by countryside and which has been restored in elegant style. The chef focuses on top-quality ingredients (including vegetables from his own kitchen garden) and contemporary recipes with a classic flavour, as well as personalised recipes created with just a few ingredients for which he uses a mix of classic methods (“express” cooking) and modern techniques (such as whipping siphons) in order to achieve comforting, classic flavours. With the exception of a few champagnes, the wine selection showcases the region, especially the areas closest to Upper Piedmont, such as Ghemme, Gattinara, Boca and Sizzano – plus, of course, the wines produced on the restaurant’s own estate!

Name: Carlo Magno
Description: This restaurant housed in a country house dating from the 19C offers elegant period dining rooms and a menu featuring Mediterranean-style meat and fish dishes.

Name: Carlo e Camillo
Description: The Grand Hotel Sitea’s second restaurant is an intimate and elegant bistrot, a true jewel box in which to savour an Italian cuisine that particularly celebrates the Piedmontese tradition, complemented by some regional offerings from the Peninsula. The offering is completed by off-menu dishes that follow the seasonality and inspiration of the kitchen, contributing to an experience that is dynamic and always current.

Name: Carne & Spirito
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the outskirts of the city, meat lovers will find their paradise: the kitchen selects some of the finest breeds from around the world (almost exclusively beef), offered in a variety of cuts and cooked over a Josper charcoal oven: an authentic delight. Cured meats also feature among the starters, alongside fresh pasta and excellent desserts. The wine selection is equally noteworthy, as is the selection by the glass.

Name: Carter Oblio
Address: Via Giuseppe Gioachino Belli 21, Rome, 00193, Italy
Description: Although the rooms at this restaurant are simple and minimalist in style, the cuisine, skilfully prepared by chef Ciro Alberto Cucciniello, is bursting with colour and flavour. The dishes are inspired by different culinary traditions from all over Italy and then reinterpreted with a personal touch by the chef with pleasing and occasionally exciting results.

Name: Caruso Roof Garden
Description: In a city already rich with rooftop restaurants, this address stands out as one of the most prestigious, both for its clientele and for its panoramic views: Castel dell’Ovo, Capri, the Sorrento Coast, and Vesuvius. Besides the sea! Chef Petrosino loves to express himself through several tasting menus; for those who prefer it, à la carte options are also available. Whatever the choice, Campanian products take center stage: abundant seafood, vegetables, and even some meat, all accompanied by the professionalism of excellent service and the breathtaking beauty of the Gulf of Naples as a backdrop.

Name: Carusu
Description: Along the road through the archaeological park, two small rooms on different floors host an elegant and refined restaurant, born from the Mangione family's passion – nomen omen. In the kitchen, young Alen, after significant experiences in renowned restaurants, offers his reinterpretation of Sicilian cuisine, with a strong focus on vegetables, many of which are grown on the farm tended by his uncle. At the entrance, you'll find father Francesco, while in the dining room, his equally young brother Dominique is available for conversations about wine.

Name: Casa Camperio
Description: Under the careful direction of Roberto Conti, here in the role of executive chef, this intimate address in the basement of an elegant central building, predominantly used for offices, presents cooking that reinterprets Milanese tradition with contemporary sensibility. The dishes speak a modern language, punctuated by refined Japanese influences that emerge decisively in the sharing snacks, raw dishes and sushi rolls. The establishment also functions as a cocktail bar, thanks to a list of twelve original drinks, created in-house and united by a constant Japanese-inspired thread.

Name: Casa Celesia
Address: Piazza Martiri della Libertà, 31, Oleggio, 28047, Italy
Description: Nestled in the heart of Oleggio, beneath the portico that opens onto the charming main square with its historic bell tower, Chef Corrado Lombardo showcases his extensive expertise. The restaurant offers an understated entrance and a warm, inviting dining space, complete with intimate tables and a delightful ambiance. The menu masterfully blends culinary skill with traditional flavours, paying homage to seasonal produce and highlighting the finest ingredients with well-judged seasoning and subtle contrasts of aroma. This is all paired with impeccable yet approachable service, creating a refined and thoroughly enjoyable dining experience.

Name: Casa Coppelle
Description: Situated in the heart of the city, this delightfully intimate restaurant offers a number of different dining rooms, from the “gallery” of portraits to the more British-style library rooms and the “herbier” with themed paintings on the walls. The Mediterranean cuisine is contemporary in style and succeeds in the difficult task of combining two leading food cultures (Italian and French) in an interesting and attractive way – the foie gras with apples and brioche is a good example. Impeccable service and an impressive wine selection complete the picture.

Name: Casa D'Angelo
Address: Via San Nicola 5, Fara Filiorum Petri, 66010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Housed in what was once an old family home, this elegant restaurant serves delicious regional cuisine. The menu includes dishes that have been skilfully and imaginatively enhanced by the chef, such as warm pheasant terrine with apple, alongside more traditional fare, from cured ham to charcoal-grilled local lamb and potato gnocchi with a duck sauce. The restaurant’s own extra-virgin olive oil often adds further flavour to the dishes. The 4-course tasting menu deserves a special mention for its excellent value for money.

Name: Casa Fantini/Lake Time
Description: Situated on the shores of Lake Orta, this elegant property is the result of the restoration of a historic building, reinterpreted in a contemporary style, with welcoming spaces and a cohesive, refined design down to the last detail. At the restaurant, where a lighter set menu is offered at lunchtime, the new chef presents a cuisine that draws on ingredients from the land, the lake and the sea, brought to the fore through seasonal pairings, carefully balanced colours and particular attention to presentation, with a distinctly contemporary flair. The lounge, garden, swimming pool and 11 rooms all contribute to the overall experience, ensuring a stay characterised by relaxation and charming hospitality.

Name: Casa Federici
Description: The area around Montoro, famous for its cipolla ramata (copper onion), is now also home to a gourmet restaurant thanks to young chef Francesco Cerrato, whose cuisine is inspired by locally sourced ingredients from this inland region as well as fish and seafood from the coast. The menu also features creative, carefully prepared dishes served by the attentive young staff. Minimalist-style ambience.

Name: Casa Format
Description: An eco-friendly establishment with its own vegetable garden, a modern kitchen and a tangible passion are the hallmarks of this restaurant with a strong sense of character. The architecture is contemporary and the building is completely self-sufficient in terms of energy, making use of large windows that capture the natural light and optimise it fully. The menu features delicious, authentic cuisine, enriched by original ideas and carefully chosen ingredients. Alongside the regular menu, there are several ‘special dishes’ that stand out, such as the winter offerings featuring “bue grasso” (fat ox), sourced from animals selected specifically for the restaurant by a well-known butcher: a tribute to tradition interpreted with expertise and contemporary sensitivity.

Name: Casa Gasperoni
Address: Via Castello di Montebello 6, località Montebello, Poggio Torriana, 47824, Italy
Description: At Montebello, near Poggio Torriana, in the hills of the Rimini hinterland, a small medieval village is home to the kitchen of a highly accomplished chef from the Romagna region, Gasperoni. Contemporary regional cuisine, without excessive reinterpretation, that aims squarely at flavour and the satisfaction of the palate: an excellent experience!

Name: Casa Klopè by Luigi Lepore
Description: Nestled among the lush olive groves and citrus orchards that characterise the countryside around Francavilla Angitola, Luigi Lepore’s restaurant is situated within the Klopè complex, in an elegant and contemporary setting. The bright dining room, dominated by a large open-plan kitchen, is striking for the presence of two centuries-old olive trees housed within a glass structure – a distinctive feature that lends the space a strong sense of character. The culinary offering is structured around three tasting menus – Origins, Inspirations and Signature – comprising 5, 7 and 9 courses respectively, and designed to showcase the chef’s culinary vision. The experience is rounded off by an informal yet attentive service that combines professionalism, friendliness and a focus on the guest.

Name: Casa Perrotta Restaurant
Description: This small, welcoming restaurant with a hint of minimalism and just a few tables serves personalised meat and fish dishes which aim to offer something a little different, with a choice of three tasting menus and an à la carte. Having previously gained experience outside the area, the young family team from Campania runs the restaurant with enthusiasm and a real love for the region’s cuisine.

Name: Casa Rapisarda
Description: In an intimate setting reminiscent of the living room of a private residence, set along the picturesque Costarella staircase, Chef Rapisarda presents a creative yet refined cuisine, characterised by elegant nuances and a deep respect for the ingredients. The focus is on fish, showcasing its freshness, often accompanied by vegetables and herbs from the restaurant’s own garden, while still making the occasional foray into the world of meat.The menu is divided into three tasting menus – Classic, Purity and Indulgence with Balance – alongside an à la carte menu featuring a selection of the restaurant’s most representative dishes. Among the most impressive dishes, a refined seafood salad ‘sur les herbes’ and tagliolini with sea vegetables and clams, served with a beurre blanc flavoured with Timut pepper and sumac, stand out as a successful example of the balance between technique and character.During the summer season, booking is strongly recommended, particularly to secure one of the two tables on the small, romantic terrace, while other tables are set out along the picturesque staircase. Finally, please bear in mind that the car park is not immediately nearby.

Name: Casa Rispoli
Address: Piazza San Francesco 7, Cava de' Tirreni, 84013, Italy
Description: The charming historic centre, with its arcades, is well worth a visit; it leads to a square where you’ll find Casa Rispoli. The heart and soul of the restaurant is its friendly owner, who is a true connoisseur of the catering trade; do ask him for recommendations while you’re in the dining room. Although there are a few meat dishes, there is a wider selection of fish dishes, all of which are of excellent quality.

Name: Casa Romano
Description: A long-standing family establishment overlooking the main square for over sixty years, and for much of its history devoted to banqueting, it has been redesigned by the younger generation – brothers and cousins – in a contemporary and elegant key. Today it presents itself as a bright and panoramic space, thanks to generous picture windows opening onto the surrounding landscape, where the kitchen is in the hands of Luca Adobati, a thirty-year-old with significant experience abroad. His proposal, vivid in colour and precise in flavour, follows the seasonality of the raw materials with rigour, and is articulated across a concise à la carte menu and a seven-course surprise tasting menu. Among the most convincing dishes, the amberjack accompanied by an aromatic mushroom trilogy, and the closing dessert: layered apple millefeuille, hay ice cream, and zabaione. At lunch during the week, a leaner business formula is also available. Summer evenings are further enhanced by a spectacular panoramic terrace from which the view stretches without limit.

Name: Casa Rusticale dei Cavalieri Templari
Description: This building, home to the San Bartolo Knights Templar “hospital” until the 13C, now houses an attractive restaurant which continues this old tradition of hospitality. Here, a friendly dining room with a pleasantly rustic yet elegant feel serves as a backdrop for generous, substantial cuisine with a hint of creativity. An outdoor space shaded by a vine-planted pergola completes the picture.

Name: Casa Scarica Cucina Da Vivere
Description: It all began with a cookery school and one of its most passionate students, today at the helm of this new and lively venue in the heart of the world capital of pasta. During the week, at lunchtime, the offering focuses on sweets and dishes dedicated to local tradition: generous preparations, rooted in classic canons yet at times reinterpreted with more personal and creative touches. On Thursday to Saturday evenings, the menu expands to make way for a more varied selection, still inspired by the region’s culinary heritage.The restaurant retains its educational ethos, strengthening its ties with the local area through cookery classes and authentic ‘pasta tours’ – experiences designed to engage guests and showcase the local culinary culture in a direct and exciting way.

Name: Casa Serafini
Description: The restaurant takes its name from its owner, a gifted young chef in his early thirties who, after honing his craft in several starred kitchens, chose to create his own culinary space here. The setting is modern and carefully appointed, divided into two dining rooms; the most desirable seats are the three tables directly overlooking the kitchen, with a wood fire glowing in the hearth behind. The cuisine looks firmly to the contemporary with a confident hand, and among the most representative dishes are the cappelletti with bitter herbs, cardoncelli mushrooms, acidulated butter and almond, an example of balance and aromatic depth. There are three menu options: La vostra mano libera, Ricerca and the vegetarian Natura, each conceived to convey a personal style of cooking in constant evolution.

Name: Casa Vicina
Description: After more than twenty years in Turin, the Vicina family has returned to its origins, to the very place where it all began with father Roberto, a true master of cooking over the grill. A signature dish on the menu is dedicated to him: the Fassone Piemontese rib, subjected to a long period of dry-ageing that brings out its succulence and depth of character. The guiding thread of the offering, which the family themselves describe as ‘contemporary tradition’, is firmly rooted in the Piedmontese kitchen, enriched however by the experience and sensitivity accumulated over the years. The restaurant is situated within a new hotel in a semi-central position, where during the week a simpler and more straightforward lunch formula is also available.

Name: Casa Vissani
Address: S.S. 448 Km 6,600, vocabolo Cannitello, Baschi, 05023, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Upon arrival, welcomed by son Luca, weather permitting, treat yourself to a pause on the lawn facing the lake before entering and immersing yourself in the elegance of the dining rooms. You’ll begin in the rock room for the welcome, aperitif, and dish selection, then move to the refined service room, a masterful mix of diverse elements combined with open kitchens framed like paintings. Recently, a new à la carte selection method was introduced, allowing each diner to choose at least two dishes from the Departures and Arrivals sections (excluding Sweet Stops). Alternatively, you can opt for one of two tasting menus proposed by the chef: Volare in Piccolo (Flying Small), featuring 4 courses, or Volare in Grande (Flying Grand), with 7 courses. “TerritOri” is instead the new pop restaurant that, in another room of the same structure, complements Casa Vissani. More inclusive, this concept traces its storied past, offering cuisine that celebrates Italian territorial traditions with a more accessible and familiar formula.

Name: Casa del Nonno 13
Address: Via Caracciolo 13, loc. Sant'Eustachio, Mercato San Severino, 84085, Italy
Description: Recently re-opened under new management, this charming restaurant winds its way from room to room until you finally arrive at the palazzo’s old cellars, the jewel in its crown. The cuisine here has quickly made a name for itself, focusing on strong links with regional traditions and showcasing local favourites on a menu full of tempting options, including salumi, local vegetables, pasta dishes, grilled meat options and typical local ingredients such as San Marzano tomatoes. The delicious cuisine pays tribute to the fine culinary traditions of Campania.

Name: Casa della Rocca
Description: Situated in picturesque Dolcedo, this restaurant occupies an early 20C mill complete with millstone and press. The cuisine focuses on an interesting selection of traditional Ligurian dishes with a satisfying balance of meat and fish (occasionally on the same plate), plus creative touches and hints of the Piedmont, all of which combine to make a trip to this inland restaurant well worth while!

Name: Casamare
Description: In a particularly lovely location just a stone’s throw from the Lungomare Trieste, the restaurant welcomes guests via a gourmet boutique dedicated to the finest produce from Campania – the ideal introduction to a setting of refined charm. The long dining room, characterised by a successful balance between period details and contemporary design, features an open-plan kitchen and a well-stocked fish counter that sets the tone for the restaurant’s central theme. The colourful ceramics from Vietri help to define the restaurant’s identity, while the cuisine celebrates the sea through a wide selection of fish and seafood, prepared in a variety of ways inspired by the traditions of Campania. There is also plenty of space set aside for raw dishes.

Name: Casanova
Address: Piazza San Benedetto 5, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the heart of Polignano’s historic centre, the journey towards a gastronomic experience begins as soon as you head up to the first floor of the Palazzo del Suono del Mare. Here, amid sparkling Venetian chandeliers, elegant mosaic floors in shades of blue and large windows overlooking the coast, the atmosphere is that of a sophisticated seaside residence. On milder days, the panoramic terrace adds a touch of magic, offering a spectacular view of the Adriatic.In the kitchen, chef Michele Panzarini reinterprets the culinary heritage of Puglia and Italy with a contemporary sensitivity, while preserving its essence. The dishes, prepared to order, showcase the quality of the ingredients and the value of tradition. A standout dish is the seafood soup, enriched with scallops and shellfish, followed by a pasta dish served in the rich, flavourful broth from the soup. The finale is a tribute to classic haute cuisine: a light soufflé finished at the table with flambéed Grand Marnier and served with a velvety quenelle of vanilla ice cream. A dessert that on its own is worth the journey.

Name: Cascina Moro
Address: Strada Provinciale 8, Frazione Moro, Locate di Triulzi, 20085, Italy
Description: This skilfully restored 18C farmhouse has all the authentic charm of the Milanese lowland region, with each corner telling a story, from the intimate lounges to the delightful room with a large stone fireplace. There’s also a bright, welcoming veranda-style space which is perfect at any time of year. The menu features an array of meat and fish dishes, including dishes that celebrate Mediterranean cuisine and Milanese traditions alike. The well-stocked wine cellar (which can be visited) will delight wine-enthusiasts thanks to its excellent selection of interesting labels.

Name: Cascina Vittoria
Description: Situated in a rural setting surrounded by rice fields outside Milan, this restaurant specialises in home-made pasta and breads, vegetables grown in its own garden, and Piedmontese meat cooked in traditional fashion over a barbecue grill. Takeaway produce is also available for purchase.

Name: Castel Toblino
Address: Località Castel Toblino 1, Castel Toblino, 38076, Italy
Description: Situated in a bucolic location in the Trentino where the excellent Vino Santo is produced (we recommend rounding off your meal with a glass of the equally superb grappa), this restaurant and adjacent bar occupy a fascinating medieval castle (tours of which can be arranged) jutting out into the lake of the same name. The generous, modern meat and fish dishes are featured on various tasting menus, along with an extensive à la carte. In summer, make sure you book a table on the charming terrace overlooking the lake.

Name: Castello
Address: via Cagna 4, Santa Vittoria d'Alba, 12069, Italy
Description: Located beside the ancient castle walls, the restaurant welcomes guests with a veranda overlooking the Langhe and an intimate dining room where the atmosphere turns hushed and inviting. The cuisine looks to local tradition, yet embraces well-calibrated seafood forays, such as octopus with black-eyed peas, as well as contemporary interpretations, including standout tajarin with shredded ossobuco and fragrant gremolata.

Name: Casu Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Situated on Giarre’s main street, this small, simple restaurant has just a few tables and an informal atmosphere. The menu offers a small selection of reasonably priced dishes with a focus on Sicilian cuisine made from top-quality ingredients that guarantee delicious flavours.

Name: Cavallini
Address: Viale Bigioli 47, San Severino Marche, 62027, Italy
Description: Situated on the main street passing through the town, this bright, relaxing and well-soundproofed restaurant on the first floor is run by two brothers – one at the helm in the kitchen and the other front of house. While continuing the family tradition, the brothers also serve the type of cuisine that they prefer, namely fish and seafood in dishes that are both classically prepared and substantial. The menu also offers good alternatives for meat-lovers.

Name: Cavalluccio Marino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Imaginative cuisine in a long - established family restaurant, which is constantly updated by each generation. Situated away from the town centre, yet easily accessible, the restaurant boasts an enviable seafront location. Excellent selection of local and international wines.

Name: Cavour
Description: Cavour serves top-quality cuisine rooted in regional traditions, making it the type of restaurant that everyone would like as their local. Daily specials with a seasonal focus, such as the ultra-fresh puntarelle chicory salad with anchovies and Parmesan cheese, are also available.

Name: Ceresio 7
Description: For over a decade now a fixture among Milan’s coolest venues, capable of uniting glamour and elegance in a single, successful formula: pool bar, restaurant and swimming pool on the fourth floor of Via Ceresio 7. The interior design seduces with a refined balance of brass, marble and wood, in a harmonious play of enveloping tones and vintage touches, while the view opens out from the two ever-accessible terraces, offering captivating glimpses of the skyscrapers of Porta Garibaldi. On the table, an Italian cuisine reinterpreted with lightness and contemporary flair, celebrating seasonal ingredients with freshness and precision. If mixology is one of its defining traits, with cocktails that have by now become city icons, the well structured wine list is no less impressive with a clear predilection for Champagne. A number of convenient parking spaces are also available by reservation, at an additional cost.

Name: Cestello Firenze
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: On the spectacular piazza dominated by the historic church of San Frediano in Cestello, this atmospheric restaurant distinguishes itself through a relaxed elegance, complemented by an excellent bar where a carefully considered cocktail offering is accompanied by refined tapas pairings. The cooking is entirely dedicated to fish and seafood: generous space is given to raw preparations from the sea, also available through a dedicated tasting menu, while the heart of the carte explores modern and creative compositions. For those who favour a more classic approach, it is possible to approach the fish counter and select the catch of the day. The wine list is solid and well-structured, enriched by significant Italian verticals, among which Masseto and Ornellaia stand out.

Name: Chalet Gerard
Address: Via Plan de Gralba 37, Selva di Val Gardena, 39048, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In a breathtakingly beautiful natural setting between the Sassolungo peak and the majestic Sella mountains, this restaurant serves simple mountain fare alongside a few more modern dishes, all of which are prepared from typical ingredients from the Alto Adige. Although you can’t book at lunchtime, bookings are required in the evening. Beautiful guestrooms are also available.

Name: Charleston by Giovanni Solofra
Address: Piazzetta Salvatore Fausto Flaccovio 6, Palermo, 90141, Italy
Description: The celebrated Charleston returns to the heart of Palermo, precisely where it was born before becoming an icon of Mondello, occupying the former Mazzara bar premises. On the ground floor are the café, cocktail bar and bistrot; on the first floor, reachable by lift, an elegant salon in contemporary Sicilian style, with a refined terrace devoted to after-dinner.The kitchen is in the hands of chefs Giovanni Solofra and Roberta Merolli, whose creative dishes unite regional tradition with reinterpretations of Charleston classics. Not to be missed are the iconic fillet "alla lampada", infused with whisky, and the historic "Coppa Charleston" with vanilla and mandarin orange. The wine list is enhanced by the recommendations of sommelier Michela Vitale.

Name: Chat Qui Rit
Address: Calle Tron, Sestiere San Marco 1131, Venice, 30124, Italy
Description: “Lagoon fusion” cuisine awaits you at this historic restaurant just a short walk from St. Mark's Square: generous, colourful dishes prepared with meticulous attention to detail and love for the local area, but without neglecting a few forays into the Orient, a passion of one of the two Venetian chefs. The menu features mainly seafood and, depending on the season, some really interesting locally caught fish with lots of personality. The excellent wine list includes some rare vintage and collectible wines.

Name: ChiaroScuro
Address: Corso Vittorio Emanuele II 380, Cagliari, 09123, Italy
Description: In this small neighbourhood restaurant, chef Marina pays homage to the iconic dishes of her island, such as Su Filindeu, a type of pasta in broth formed by very thin threads (the name means “threads of God”), stacked in three criss-crossed layers: it is a complex preparation that requires great skill. Originally from the Nuoro area, this talented cook's menu focuses mainly on inland dishes; nevertheless, two or three fish specialities are always on the menu.

Name: Chicco di Grano
Address: Viale dei Caduti del Lavoro 5, Castel Mella, 25030, Italy
Description: This rustic, welcoming restaurant (two dining rooms with exposed beams) acts as the backdrop for traditional cuisine featuring meat and fish dishes alike, often cooked on the barbecue grill. The Fiorentina steaks and chops are well aged and cooked to perfection, resulting in extraordinary flavours that will satisfy even the most demanding of palates.

Name: Chichibio
Description: This restaurant stands out for its high-quality cuisine, served in an intimate and cosy setting in the heart of the village. The restaurant has just a few tables, so it’s advisable to book in advance. The menu places particular emphasis on ingredients produced nearby, while still making the occasional foray into the world of seafood, interpreted with a contemporary sensitivity and a measured touch of creativity. A restaurant that’s definitely worth a visit.

Name: Chimera di Bacco
Description: Just moments from the magnificent Piazza Unità d’Italia, this venue welcomes guests into a warm and distinguished environment, classically toned and carefully finished in every detail. In the kitchen, a chef of long experience offers a solid interpretation of maritime tradition, bringing contemporary sensitivity to the local catch. The well-constructed and balanced dishes are distinguished by a personal touch that brings the recipes up to date without compromising their identity. In fine weather, the outdoor terrace provides a pleasant open-air setting, while the cellar, boasting over 700 labels, completes a gastronomic experience of assured quality.

Name: Christian & Manuel
Description: This restaurant features sophisticated, creative cooking and top quality ingredients, without forgetting the culinary traditions of the area and region. Therefore, don't be surprised by the special attention reserved for rice: the menu offers a selection of twenty risottos, but also a lot of delicious land and sea specialities.

Name: CiPASSO
Description: A small restaurant which combines a contemporary feel with a hint of vintage style in its decor. The menu is inspired by Roman and regional traditions, with the occasional imaginative twist and other more Mediterranean-inspired dishes, all showing a strong focus on seasonal ingredients. The impressive wine list includes an excellent selection of regional wines, with a particular focus on wines by the glass. Friendly yet professional service from the young team completes the picture.

Name: Ciambra
Description: At the gates of the town and a few steps from the magnificent Cathedral of Monreale, this rustic yet elegant venue proves to be an intriguing destination for those wishing to explore refined seafood cookery, reinterpreted with a modern touch while never betraying the authenticity of the flavours. The Tonnarello fresco cacio e pepe con quenelle di gambero rosso (fresh tonnarello cacio e pepe with a red prawn quenelle) is a delightful pasta dish that well represents the chef’s hand, as do the impeccably fresh and expertly executed seafood crudo. Finally, the house desserts are not to be missed: the true stars of the end of the meal, leaving a deliciously lingering memory.

Name: Cibrèo
Address: Via A. Del Verrocchio 8r, Florence, 50122, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A historic city institution and essential stop for anyone arriving in Florence, this establishment welcomes guests into an elegant dining room reminiscent of a private salon, where cordial, graciously measured service frames a cuisine of bold flavors. The menu features dishes that have become true house classics, capable of narrating the territory through recipes that time has rendered iconic: pork liver with lemon, tortellini timbale, squab stuffed with mostarda, rabbit roulade with sweet-and-sour borettane onions, and, to close, a cheese tart accompanied by marmalade.

Name: Ciccio Bistrot
Description: In the evocative vaulted dining room that once housed the celebrated Cavallino, Ciccio Bistrot now brings to the table a forthright, deeply local cuisine, faithful to tradition and free of unnecessary digressions – except in the playful titles that punctuate the menu. Among the offerings, the whimsically named “no name” deserves a taste: agnolotti del plin served with the sauce of your choosing, a small ritual of personalization that wins over regulars. Each day brings a few off-menu delicacies, while wine maintains the role tradition assigns it: a discreet yet essential companion, supported by a well-curated selection and the expert guidance of the owner, always ready to steer guests toward the most fitting pairing.

Name: Cielo
Description: In the white city of limestone stairways, at the highest point of the village, a skillfully restored ancient residence houses a splendid relais that – fittingly – bears the name La Sommità. The gourmet restaurant Cielo welcomes guests with romantic summer dinners among the citrus trees of the small inner courtyard, or in the barrel-vaulted dining room, where the atmosphere is intimate and evocative. The menu offers a modern reinterpretation of Apulian cuisine: not to be missed are the stewed catalogna with grilled lamb offal and sweet-and-sour lampascioni, or the pasta cooked in spicy tomato water, served with raw red mullet and chervil. At aperitivo hour, it is worth ascending to the splendid terrace to take in the sunset, while at lunch the offering becomes simpler, designed for a lighter yet always refined experience.

Name: Cinque Foglie
Address: Via SS 18 Tirrenia Inferiore, 54, Battipaglia, 84091, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Within the Hotel Commercio, Cinque Foglie offers a gastronomic experience, where each detail has been thoughtfully considered. The experience begins with a visit to the recently renovated cellar and a small photographic gallery dedicated to the history of Battipaglia, before continuing into a bright contemporary dining room overlooking the open kitchen. Chef Roberto Allocca interprets the local area through a technical and creative cuisine, founded on quality ingredients sourced also from the property's own kitchen garden and farm at Piana del Sele. The offering comprises the tasting menus Nostos and the vegetarian L'Orto di Francesca, alongside a generous à la carte selection. Among the most accomplished dishes, Il Canto del Mare stands out: a fillet of John Dory cooked in buffalo butter, accompanied by courgettes in two textures – gratin and carpaccio – and a bottarga emulsion.

Name: Cip's Club
Description: This is the most informal and intimate restaurant of the Hotel Cipriani and comes with a coveted panoramic terrace which looks out over the Giudecca Canal, St. Mark's Square and the Doge's Palace. It's a true institution in the city and the seasonal menu of Venetian dishes includes a whole page dedicated to its signature classics.

Name: Clandestino Susci Bar
Description: After driving along the scenic hairpin bends of the Conero Park, you leave your car in the public car park and a short walk takes you to a charming little beach, nestled among the Conero cliffs. A little corner of paradise, home to Il Clandestino, the brainchild of two-Michelin-starred chef Moreno Cedroni from Senigallia. In the evenings, just a tasting menu is available; at lunchtime, there is also an à la carte menu. The dishes are creative and innovative, combining classic, must-try dishes with the latest creations and culinary journeys. A place close to our hearts that we’ll remember for a long time to come.

Name: Claudio Ristorante
Description: In the heart of the lower Padana valley, in the open countryside and in a lovely, specially restored farmhouse, Claudio prepares almost exclusively seafood cuisine of excellent quality, with a few southern accents, particularly from Puglia, his homeland. In summer, it is pleasant to sit at outdoor tables under the modern portico. The indoor dining room on the first floor has a contemporary feel.

Name: Club Morera
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Nestled in Mediterranean scrub just beyond the hills overlooking the coast, this rustic farmhouse welcomes guests amid centuries-old olive trees and restorative quiet. Inside, exposed stone and beams frame a relaxed yet elegant setting, with a small garden terrace perfect for summer evenings. Chef-owner Vincenzo has realized his dream here: to offer genuine hospitality and regional cooking revisited with a contemporary taste. Among the dishes not to be missed are the tagliatelle with seafood, salsa verde and basil, and the amberjack in a courgette flower crust, with potage parmantier and liquorice. The cellar stocks 300-plus labels to pair thoughtfully with each dish.

Name: Cocchi
Description: This restaurant adjoining the Daniel hotel is the town’s pride and joy. Here, two quiet, rustic-style dining rooms provide the backdrop for typical Parma specialities that change with the passing seasons – the “tortelli alle erbette” (tortelli pasta with herbs) with parmesan and melted butter is particularly delicious – all accompanied by an excellent choice of wines. Booking in advance is highly recommended as the restaurant is extremely popular with visitors and locals alike.

Name: Cocun Cellar Restaurant
Address: Strada Prè de Vì 31, San Cassiano, 39036, Italy
Description: In the cellars of the Ciasa Salares hotel, you dine surrounded by bottles – after all, cocun in Ladin means cork, and not by chance the wine selection is vast. The chef creates dishes with ingredients and influences from every corner of the world and makes frequent use of the grill.

Name: Coeur de Bois
Description: The name of this elegant restaurant was inspired by its wooden ceiling. Surrounded by spruce decor dating from the 18C, antique furniture and paintings, enjoy interesting traditional cuisine in this excellent gourmet restaurant, which is all the more attractive thanks to its location in the Gran Paradiso national park.

Name: Colle Serrano
Address: Contrada Colle di Guardia 18, Ripatransone, 63065, Italy
Description: Set within an elegant, modern country house on a 70-hectare estate stretching across the foothills just a few kilometres from the sea, this restaurant enjoys a truly charming setting, surrounded by vineyards and olive groves as far as the eye can see. The estate, which will soon also be home to a horse farm, is complemented by wine and olive oil production, which strengthen its ties to the region. In the kitchen, Chef Ficcadenti brings a creative and contemporary sensitivity to a culinary heritage rich in traditions and ingredients of the highest quality. The best way to experience his vision is through the ‘Voyage’ tasting menu, comprising seven courses and embodying his culinary philosophy. At lunchtime, however, the menu takes on a lighter, more informal feel, without compromising on quality or character.

Name: Collina
Address: Via Ca' Paler 5, Almenno San Bartolomeo, 24030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Along the road leading to Roncola, a spacious and elegant restaurant whose main dining room opens – through a large glazed wall – onto an evocative Lombard panorama embracing the hills of Bergamo, seen from an unusual perspective. The cuisine of the chef-patron stands out for its solidity and imagination, with dishes built, wherever possible, from local ingredients and in strict respect of seasonality. Particular attention is devoted to freshwater fish, a true passion of the house, to which an entire tasting menu is dedicated, available on request.

Name: Colline Emiliane
Description: A taste of the Emilia region in Rome. Ever since the 1960s, this friendly restaurant has been serving typical Emilian specialities such as delicious salumi, fresh homemade pasta made in the small kitchen visible near the entrance (tagliatelle with ragù, tagliolini with culatello ham, sometimes a superb green lasagne), and superbly cooked meat dishes, while the desserts are displayed in a large fridge to the rear. An extraordinary gastronomic voyage to a different Italian region while remaining in the country’s beautiful capital city.

Name: Coltivare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The organic soul of the Brandini estate, which houses the restaurant, makes itself felt immediately upon arrival: from the vineyards managed with great respect for the environment to the small herb and spice garden, an invaluable support to the work of chef Zecchin in his continuous pursuit of new aromatic equilibria. A focused experimentation, serving to refine dishes of deeply Langhe character, underpinned by a solid grounding in the territory. Alongside the principal offering, a vegetarian menu is available for devotees of the kitchen garden, while from the carte particular attention is merited by the eel with an intense cream of pil and roasted lettuce, as well as the Fassona chuck, rendered all the more tender and harmonious by Pink Lady apple and a deep brown maize jus. The wine list reflects the same strong bond with Piedmont, without overlooking a carefully considered selection of Champagnes. By day, the spacious dining room affords a splendid view through the large windows that surround it, enriched by the dramatic presence of an imposing fireplace.

Name: Come in Corte Aurora
Description: At this restaurant, the two brothers (the owners) who work together front of house come from a family of farmers whose meat features on the menu, while two other brothers, originally from Rome but settled in the Veneto for many years, are at the helm in the kitchen. The original and colourful cuisine aims to please both the eyes and the palate, with dishes showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte – the quail served with a caponata of apricots, yucca and porcini mushroom mayonnaise was particularly memorable. Housed in the Villa Lussana, with its seven Art Nouveau-style guestrooms, the restaurant has been completely renovated by the new young owners. In summer, meals are served outdoors with views of the surrounding hills.

Name: Comi 107
Description: Situated near the lake at the entrance to a narrow street dotted with various shops, this small contemporary-style restaurant boasts an equally tiny outdoor space for summer dining and is run with skill and professionalism by a young couple. The friendly, welcoming wife oversees the front of house, while her husband creates dishes full of character in the kitchen.

Name: ConTatto
Description: In a small town just a few kilometres from the capital, two passionate young chefs serve dishes inspired by the region with a contemporary twist, such as cave mushrooms, seaweed and pecorino, or charcoal-grilled tripe with mint and sour cherry balsamic vinegar. The tour of the tuff cellars, where the chef experiments with traditional preservation methods and unique flavourings, is well worth a visit.
