Furthermore, each year, the premises are ‘lent’ to a modern art gallery owner for exhibitions.

Name: Concezione Restaurant
Description: In a minimalist, contemporary setting, enhanced by the vaults of the historic building and a refurbished reception area, takes shape the culinary project of Manuel Tropea, one of the most exciting talents on the Catania scene. In recent years, the restaurant has undergone a profound transformation, affecting the team, the wine cellar and the culinary offering, which is now increasingly distinct and personal. Sicily remains at the heart of it all, particularly eastern Sicily, reinterpreted with a contemporary sensitivity while respecting its roots and culinary heritage. There are just six tables: reservations are strongly recommended.

Name: Contrasto
Description: Lucio Testa, chef-patron, has returned to his native village perched at an altitude of 937 metres, opening this restaurant in a former sheepfold on the outskirts of the village. The perfectly preserved stone façade, several small rooms spread over several levels, exposed beams and contemporary lamps give the ambience a modern touch. His is a creative cuisine, in which traditional Molise recipes are revisited, combining local and seasonal products (often from his own garden) with sauces, dressings and emulsions, learnt from working with French chefs; mulard duck is a favourite, several tasting menus guide the discovery of the territory, and finally, for those who prefer, a la carte choices. Among the wines, we suggest tasting a Tintillia del Molise Rutilia 2019 from Cantine Salvatore.

Name: Convivial
Address: Via Torre di Lavello 7, Tuscania, 01017, Italy
Description: In the picturesque medieval historic centre, the kitchen is in the hands of a young and talented cook, Andrea Astolfi, who celebrates the local area with passion, pairing more traditional offerings with some creative dishes. Among the most accomplished: the almond granita with Argentario pink prawns, peas and elderflower; the orzotto with artichoke cream, egg yolk and black garlic; and the lombrichelli with butter, anchovies and truffle.

Name: Coppola Rossa
Description: In the historic centre, a short distance from the sea, you’ll find this characterful, no-frills restaurant, with vaulted ceilings and brick walls that create a genuinely homely atmosphere, starting with the informal service where the catch of the day and the wines are described to you in person. Since 1983, it has been a go-to destination for those seeking traditional seafood cuisine served in generous portions: the meal begins with raw seafood and soups, followed by pasta dishes and classic specialities – from grilled and fried dishes to those cooked in salt and in the oven. Choosing locally caught fish may, of course, affect the bill, but it assures an even more authentic experience.

Name: Corbezzoli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the Relais Bellaria hotel, the Corbezzoli restaurant takes its name from the magnificent garden visible through its large picture windows. The cuisine, which is both creative and full of flavour, includes a wide array of dishes that range from vegetarian to meat and fish options, with the possibility of choosing from three tasting menus and an à la carte. Make sure you leave room for one of the delicious desserts, which include an unmissable Neapolitan-style baba with pastry cream and sour cherries.

Name: Coro
Description: In the centre of Orvieto, Coro is set in the captivating deconsecrated church of San Giuseppe. The modern, refined style provides the backdrop for chef Ronald Bukri’s cuisine, which weaves together memory, innovation, and global influences into dishes with a distinctly contemporary character.

Name: Corsaro Nero
Address: Località Portu Maga, Marina di Arbus, 09031, Italy
Description: A wide choice of fresh fish and a menu with a firm focus on fish and seafood served in a large dining room offering views of the spectacular sunsets.

Name: Corte Federiciana
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The dining room at this restaurant housed in the Palazzo Baronale’s old outbuildings in the historic centre of Apricena boasts an attractive brick-vaulted ceiling. The cuisine, which focuses mainly on fish and seafood (raw, cooked, baked in the oven or served with pasta), effortlessly combines traditional and modern flavours. A delightful welcome and friendly service complete the picture.

Name: Corte Matilde
Address: Via Pelate 38, Pieve di Coriano, 46036, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: Set within a charming, renovated farmhouse on the outskirts of the village, surrounded by the greenery and tranquillity of the countryside, is an establishment run as a solid family business. In the kitchen, head chef and owner Marco Fincatti creates a delicious and well-defined menu, striking a balance between Venetian tradition and Lombard influences, while showcasing high-quality local and seasonal produce. Among the most successful dishes are the “duck cappelletti with brown butter, rosemary, green peppercorns and 36-month-aged Parmigiano”, a fine example of balance and depth of flavour. To make the most of your stay, we recommend choosing the bright, enclosed veranda, which overlooks a well-tended garden.

Name: Corte Sconta
Address: Calle del Pestrin, Sestiere Castello 3886, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: From its flooring to its tables, this restaurant has the charming, nostalgic feel of a typical trattoria in its simple dining room, while the outdoor space in an inner courtyard under a vine-shaded arbour is a charming place to eat in fine weather – a real gem right in the centre of Venice. The cuisine is as simple in style as the decor, with traditional Venetian fish and seafood dishes taking pride of place on the menu.

Name: Corte Visconti
Description: A classical, rustic style environment with walls in stone and brick vaulted or wood and stone ceilings. The cuisine is authentically local but with a pleasant touch of creativity.

Name: Cortile Arabo
Description: In one of Sicily’s most iconic fortified villages which once prospered as a tuna fishery and is now a popular tourist attraction, Cortile Arabo serves carefully prepared and occasionally elaborate dishes of the highest quality, with a focus on fish (the menu also features a few meat dishes). The terrace on the rocks overlooking the sea, where the sound of the waves provides a soothing backdrop, is one of the highlights here.

Name: Cortile Pepe
Description: Nestled among the narrow streets of the historic centre, situated between the Cathedral and the sea, this charming establishment welcomes guests beneath ancient stone arches or in its cosy inner courtyard, which is particularly atmospheric on summer evenings. In the kitchen, local culinary traditions are reimagined using contemporary techniques and creative flair, resulting in dishes with distinct flavours and a presentation that is elegant and vibrant without being over the top. The experience is rounded off by attentive and friendly service, characterised by a genuine culture of hospitality.

Name: Cosmo Restaurant
Description: Although the menu here and there includes references to Campanian gastronomy and produce, Cosmo stands out as an excellent gastronomic destination for those seeking more elaborate and creative cuisine, the work of a young chef who produces complex dishes of a very high standard.

Name: Cravero - Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Warm colours such as teal and ochre give this restaurant a cosy and welcoming ambience. The cuisine here is authentic and traditional in style, with dishes based on top-quality local ingredients accompanied by a choice of regional wines. There’s also an outdoor area for summer dining.

Name: Crotasc
Address: Via Don Primo Lucchinetti 63, Mese, 23020, Italy
Description: Here one can choose between a smaller, typically mountain style dining room with stone paving and open fireplace and a larger room in contemporary rustic style. In summer one can dine on the terrace.

Name: Crotto Valtellina
Address: Via Fiume 11, Località Valle, Malnate, 21046, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: For over half a century, the Valbuzzi family has preserved the spirit of this charming traditional restaurant, now in its third generation. The setting retains the warmth of tradition, with wooden tables, elegant furnishings and details that evoke the history of the place, while the summer veranda opens out onto a cool garden dominated by a striking sandstone wall. In the kitchen, the connection with the local area is reflected in a constantly evolving menu, which is updated several times a year to reflect the seasons and the availability of the finest local specialities. Alongside the great classics of the Valtellina tradition, such as the unmissable pizzoccheri, there is also room for more contemporary dishes, all of which are characterised by the high quality of their ingredients.

Name: Cucina
Address: Via Giano della Bella 3r, Florence, 50124, Italy
Description: At this restaurant, local ingredients (mainly from the market) take pride of place on the daily menu which changes in accordance with whatever produce is available at the time. The rustic-style dishes are full of intense flavours, with meat and vegetables often cooked in the wood-fired oven. The pleasantly informal dining room with its many cookery books dotted here and there was designed by the owner-architects themselves.

Name: Cucina Bacilieri
Description: A small restaurant in the heart of the city, refined and romantic, where soft spotlights cast a gentle glow over the tables, creating an intimate, comforting atmosphere. The flavors are entrusted to chef-owner Bacilieri, who crafts modern, harmonious dishes rooted in seasonality and the freshness of ingredients, spanning both meat and fish. Not to be missed: the dessert course, here it is a true indulgence for the palate. Service, led by a young, passionate team, attends to every detail of the experience with warmth and care.

Name: Cucina Rambaldi
Description: Regional dishes and produce are reinterpreted with a personal and measured style, maintaining a constant equilibrium between territorial roots and creative impulse. Technique – from the precise control of temperatures to the accuracy of the knife work, through to the care taken in the selection and keeping of ingredients – is always placed at the service of flavour, and the result is one of great coherence and pleasure. Particularly tempting is the section dedicated to the ‘Lenitivi’: small tasting morsels conceived also for pairing with aperitifs, gathered in an introductory list that rewards careful exploration. For those seeking an even more tailored experience, there is the option of the social table, accommodating up to six guests. The service is professional and cordial, accompanying the meal with attentiveness and measure.

Name: Cucina di Sintesi
Description: On the first floor of the historic 18C palazzo that today houses the Hotel De Ville, overlooking the ancient port, stands a restaurant that reveals from the outset a personal and imaginative cuisine. The offering, Ligurian in character yet sustained by a contemporary technique honed through years of experience in fine dining establishments, unfolds across three tasting menus. Among the most representative dishes, mention must be made of “La Basse-Coeur”: a harmonious composition of guinea fowl, onions, burnt lime, marjoram and chargrilled artichoke, a balance of contrasts that articulates the philosophy of the house.

Name: Cucine Nervi
Description: Inside the Cantine Nervi, a contemporary restaurant where the kitchen is totally open, you can choose to eat on the large counter or at more classic tables. The young chef Matteo Piana delights in a contemporary and creative style. If it seems obvious that there is no lack of meat dishes, you will be pleasantly surprised by the presence of some incursions from the sea (try the raw tuna to dip in different tasty sauces, some of oriental inspiration). There is a good wine selection, naturally the house wines are the most represented: many also served by the glass.

Name: Cuculia
Description: An establishment of measured elegance, with refined interiors that evoke the atmosphere of a contemporary French bistrot, enhanced by a small library displaying culinary volumes and beyond. Chef Oliver Betancourt, originally from Venezuela, built his training through notable kitchens in France, Spain, and Italy: a journey that today translates into a gastronomic approach rich in nuance, nourished by diverse traditions and constructed around seasonal local products, alongside more exotic ingredients such as kombu, soy sauce, and koji. Vegetarian options are clearly marked on the menu, together with several dishes suitable for vegans as well.

Name: Cuoco di Bordo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: An attractively furnished restaurant on the seafront with a small dining room and a veranda offering partial views of the sea. Fish takes pride of place on the menu, which focuses on raw fish dishes and classic recipes. The wine list is excellent, especially the whites (although the reds also include some impressive options) with many different vintages of the same wine available.

Name: Cura Cucina Contemporanea
Address: Via Risorgimento 6/8, Marina di Davoli, 88060, Italy
Description: A single tasting menu invites guests to explore the culinary vision of Chef Massimo: a journey through authentic flavors of land and sea, enhanced by creative, personal touches. Delightful contrasts unfold around the onion, enveloped in a velvety cheese cream, while the “sottobosco” dish evokes autumn with the earthy aroma of porcini and tart hints of red berries. All this is embraced by the warm atmosphere of a converted former stable, where dry stone walls whisper tales of times past.

Name: Cut
Description: Situated right in the heart of the Bergamo plain in the small town of Caravaggio, famous for the painter of the same name and for a much-visited pilgrim shrine, this welcoming restaurant boasts a modern decor and vintage furnishings. At lunchtime, it serves a good, competitively priced business menu, while in the evening the more elaborate à la carte features contemporary-style meat and fish dishes (mostly the latter).

Name: DA MÓ
Description: This new, restored restaurant in the upper part of the Sassi (yet still near the centre of Matera and its car parks) has a warm friendly ambience and boasts a small, charming outdoor space. Here, an entire family (father in the kitchen, mother and daughter front of house), who moved to Matera from Venosa (home of the Latin poet Horatio), serves regional cuisine with a contemporary twist and no little skill and professionalism. Various tasting menus are available, as well as an à la carte. An interesting wine list completes the picture.

Name: DEG Ristorante
Address: Via Gioacchino Rossini 29, Busto Arsizio, 21052, Italy
Description: In a tranquil quarter of the city, where parking presents no challenge, a self-taught chef of considerable experience has taken the helm of an intimate and thoughtfully appointed establishment. The contemporary interiors, enlivened by delicate pastel tones, help create an atmosphere that is both intimate and refreshingly informal in spirit. Here, cookery is a convivial gesture: the chef does not remain hidden behind the stoves, but often comes out into the dining room to speak with passion about his dishes, born of contemporary techniques and personal sensitivity. His signature lies in well-calibrated sapidity, achieved through targeted fermentations, measured touches of acidity and a selection of quality ingredients that converse with Oriental influences while never losing their connection to Italian roots. The emblematic example is his tuna osso buco with yuzu potato cream, tuna jus and sun-dried tomato garum: a successful crossover in which tradition and Asian influences interweave with natural ease.The gastronomic offering is both broad and structured: several tasting menus allow one to explore the chef’s philosophy with coherence, including a Chef’s Table experience that must be booked in advance, designed to experience the service at even closer quarters, almost overlooking his work. There is also a generous carte, conceived for those who prefer to construct their own flavour journey whilst maintaining complete freedom of choice.

Name: Da Annetta
Description: In an 18th Century building, a rustic yet elegant atmosphere with a particular attentiveness at the tables and in the cuisine, which has a traditional base, but also knows how to add imaginative variations.

Name: Da Aurelio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Within La Posta Vecchia – one of the most exclusive and luxurious hotels on the Lazio coast – dining on the terrace directly in front of the sea, whenever the weather allows, is enchanting. A classic cuisine with several seafood dishes as well as meat options; in the evening, some of the offerings are somewhat more elaborate than those served at lunch.

Name: Da Bibe
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: At the gates of Florence, at the precise point where the city dissolves into the green of the countryside, Bibe welcomes guests beneath the leafy canopy of its summer terrace and within the warm interiors of a trattoria safeguarding over one hundred and fifty years of history, now in the hands of the sixth generation. Here, Tuscan cuisine remains the absolute protagonist: artisanal cured meats, traditional crostini, pici al ragù, and iconic dishes such as beef peposo. Not to be missed are the fried or grilled chicken and, for devotees, a fiorentina that interprets the classic canons in the most authentic manner.

Name: Da Bob Cook Fish
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Working in close collaboration with the adjacent fishmonger’s, from which fresh fish and seafood are delivered daily straight to the kitchen, this restaurant has found a home in a charming building that once served as an orange store and boasts over four centuries of history. Although there is a menu, the best way to enjoy the experience is to let the staff guide you through the day’s fresh arrivals, perhaps while taking a look at the fish counter as well. The cuisine favours dishes that bring out the best in the ingredients, with recipes inspired by tradition but not without a touch of creativity. One example is the squid stuffed with aubergine parmigiana, served with a fried aubergine cube, datterino tomato tartare and basil oil.

Name: Da Carla
Address: Via Necchi 3/5, fraz. Molino Isella, Gambolò, 27025, Italy
Description: Once a mill, this restaurant still stands next to its old canal which lends the setting a delightful bucolic ambience echoed in the warm, welcoming dining room. Highlights on the menu include risottos, frog’s legs, snails and goose - based dishes, as well as cured meats. Inviting guestrooms complete this delightfully rustic picture.

Name: Da Cecco
Address: piazza Belvedere Puccini 10/12, Torre del Lago Puccini, 55049, Italy
Description: A cosylittle restaurant at the beginning of the lakefront. Mainly seafood dishes, though in the winter there is also game. Rustic atmosphere.

Name: Da Cesare
Description: A restaurant with an ultra-classic character, founded as far back as 1921, offering a menu with the flavour of another era: one of those very long lists, rich in choice and able to range naturally between meat and seafood. The section devoted to grilled meats is extensive, as is that reserved for raw fish, which is always much in demand. In the evening, the offer widens further with the addition of the pizzeria.

Name: Da Ciacco
Address: Via Dante Alighieri 30/a, San Quirico d'Orcia, 53027, Italy
Description: In the heart of the pedestrian historic center, this venue offers a warm welcome in a rustic dining room or at a few tables overlooking the paseo. Family-run, it serves authentic Tuscan flavors prepared traditionally. The handmade pici with cherry tomatoes, olives, and slightly spicy anchovies are an unmissable summer delight!

Name: Da Concettina ai Tre Santi
Address: Via Arena alla Sanità 7 bis, Naples, 80137, Italy
Description: In the heart of the Sanità district: ancient, lively, popular, often chaotic. The Oliva family has managed this excellent venue for over 60 years, successfully updating it with a tasteful renovation while maintaining its traditional roots. Today, it also offers more imaginative and modern pizzas, like the Sott e’ Ngopp (“under and over,” describing the concept of the dish), along with fried items and a tasting menu. Shaded terrace available.

Name: Da Ercole
Description: On the seafront in Crotone, Da Ercole has been a favourite haunt for lovers of seafood for almost forty years. The welcoming atmosphere and family-run management provide an ideal setting for a dining experience that authentically celebrates the flavours of the Ionian Sea, through an extensive and generous menu centred on the freshness of the catch. To really capture the spirit of the restaurant, we recommend following the advice of Ercole Villirillo, the warm and hospitable host, who loves to guide guests on a culinary journey that often begins with some excellent raw seafood.

Name: Da Fausto
Description: Situated in these premises since 2015, Fausto has become a local favourite thanks to the quality and style of its cuisine which combines classic flavours and regional influences. Two of the chef’s great passions (chocolate and ice cream) always feature on the dessert menu, while the cool outdoor space near the entrance adds to the appeal.

Name: Da Gelsomina
Description: Reached on foot or (with a prior telephone call) by shuttle, this is an authentic family-run trattoria; just a few metres from the restaurant are the breathtaking views of the Philosophers’ Park. Among the most popular dishes are the Caprese ravioli and the chicken cooked under a brick in the wood-fired oven.

Name: Da Giacomo
Description: Within the charming centre of a beautiful locality divided by the Adda River and encircled by ancient walls, is a venue merging rustic notes with contemporary elements, featuring a delightful outdoor area beneath the portico. They present regional cuisine (for instance, nougat espuma with melted chocolate) and Italian dishes (glazed suckling pig loin with Sicilian orange blossom honey), modernised and lightened. The fine selection of wines is constructed over the years with care and passion by the owner.

Name: Da Gianfranco
Address: Via delle Orchidee 5, Alba Adriatica, 64011, Italy
Description: Gianfranco Verdecchia, restaurateur and heir to a family of butchers, has always cooked the food that sustained his people. After running a restaurant in Sant’Omero – a hill town known for its festival dedicated to baccalà (salt cod), a staple in the area’s cuisine – he returned to his hometown of Giulianova. Here, in a stylish, secluded space away from the sea, he has kept baccalà as the sole seafood option, devoting an entire menu to it alongside a wide selection of dishes highlighting his first love: meat.

Name: Da Gigetto
Description: A long-established restaurant with a renowned reputation thanks to the enthusiasm of the family at the helm and the excellent cuisine on offer. The carefully designed menu focuses mainly on classic regional dishes, yet also includes more contemporary options and even a few fish-based specialities, while the impressive wine list features more than 1 000 different labels, including some surprising names and various vertical wine-tasting options.

Name: Da Giovanni
Description: The 18C ceramic stove, bright, colourful decor (both period and vintage), long family tradition and excellent cuisine all contribute to making this restaurant which opened half a century ago a bastion of fine cuisine in Piacenza and the wider Po valley. Meat and fish both feature on the menu, although it is the latter that has become renowned as the restaurant’s speciality over the years. The excellent service is friendly and informal yet highly professional, while the extensive wine list also includes a good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Da Guido
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The story of this restaurant began in 1967, when Guido and Giovanna Fasan, both of whom still work front of house, met in Germany. They then moved back to Italy, where they opened Da Guido in the early 1990s. White dominates in the elegant, contemporary-style dining room, while the cuisine features delicious seafood dishes with a focus on grilled specialities. In summer, there’s a welcoming bar in the garden, which boasts a romantic atmosphere. Together with other restaurant-owners from Venice, the Fasan family also have a kitchen garden on the Venetian island of Sant’Erasmo, where they focus on sustainable growing methods.

Name: Da Lorenzo – Al Giardino Segreto
Address: Fondamenta Madona de l'Orto, 3500, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description: Hidden within the elegant walls of the NH Collection Palazzo dei Dogi, far from the bustling tourist crowds, Da Lorenzo – Al Giardino Segreto is an oasis of taste created by Paulo Airaudo, a multi-starred Spanish chef, who is assisted in the kitchen by the young Salvatore Paladino. Every dish at this restaurant is a refined combination of culinary technique, elegance and local flavours, enhanced by sophisticated Japanese accents. To immerse themselves in his gastronomic vision, guests can choose between two evocative tasting menus: Emozioni and Sensazioni – two experiences that convey the soul of this restaurant with style.

Name: Da Luciano
Address: Via Nazionale 11, Passignano sul Trasimeno, 06065, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Enjoy beautiful views of Lake Trasimeno from the outdoor terrace of this restaurant, where the menu focuses mainly on fish, alongside original ingredients such as beans and Umbrian truffles which are used in typical specialities such as tegamaccio (fish stew).

Name: Da Manuela
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: To step inside Da Manuela is to gift oneself a moment of genuine conviviality, especially precious on the grayest winter days, when the warm welcome and proudly regional cuisine have a way of lifting the spirits. At the entrance, Berkel slicers take pride of place, devoted to showcasing local cured meats of great character, while the table receives freshwater fish prepared with skill – as in the charcoal tagliatelle with coarse perch ragù and Arctic char roe – alongside game preparations. Not to be missed are the fried frogs’ legs, snails offered in multiple versions, and the risottos of the day. Reasons abound, in short, to discover this storied corner. Need more convincing? The truly abundant cheese trolley and a cellar attentive to small local producers, yet open to new horizons and Europe’s principal wine regions, will win over the undecided.

Name: Da Miky
Address: Via Fegina 104, Monterosso al Mare, 19016, Italy
Description: Situated right on the seafront, Miky is one of the best restaurants for fish (including the famous Monterosso anchovies) in the region, serving cuisine which is more and more exciting and individual every year. There’s also a small shop selling local produce.

Name: Da Miro alla Lanterna
Description: Buoyed by a long tradition that has made it a true institution of the city over the years, this historic venue overlooking the tourist harbour continues to stand as a point of reference for seafood cookery. Today the selection of fish no longer takes place at a display buffet, yet the menu – broad and well-constructed – speaks with precision to the quality of the produce and the variety of what is on offer. Crustaceans, deep-water fish and catch of varying size are handled with respect and expertise, giving rise to dishes capable of conveying genuine Mediterranean emotion. Among the preparations not to be missed are the spaghetti alla Trabaccolara, a historic recipe of the Viareggio tradition, based on tomato and fish, here interpreted in faithful keeping with local memory. The setting is that of a classic and elegant dining room, with professional and attentive service, accompanied by a wine list that is both broad and well-judged in its value for money. A reassuring constant since 1954.

Name: Da Nando
Description: Proud champion of local cuisine, along with more classic dishes, with a unique touch: the menu is written in Friulian dialect as well as Italian. Aromas of the woods and sea hover around the tables, with succulent meats – including game – and the freshest fish. Don't miss the cjarsons ravioli, delicious little morsels available in both sweet and savoury versions. The restaurant boasts an extensive wine cellar, and the scent of truffles reigns supreme on a dedicated menu in season.

Name: Da Nicolo
Description: Situated in a prime location along the seafront promenade, this historic restaurant carries on a long-standing family tradition, as evidenced by signature dishes such as Linguine alla Nicolo, which have featured on the menu since 1973. Today, the restaurant continues to stand out above all for the quality of its cuisine, created by the Pomata family, where fresh fish takes centre stage in generous dishes that are beautifully presented and rich in vibrant colour contrasts. The recipes draw on the traditions of Carloforte, reinterpreting them with a contemporary sensitivity while remaining true to their identity. Don’t miss the tuna – a true local treasure and a signature ingredient of the menu. Next to the restaurant, the Bistrot offers a more informal atmosphere, with traditional cuisine that also includes meat dishes and a selection of pizzas.

Name: Da Niko
Address: Via Privata Fratelli Gabba 7/b, Milan, 20121, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Inside the Bulgari Hotel, the exclusive location and the elegant, trendy atmosphere combine with a menu curated by Niko Romito – holder of three Michelin stars for his restaurant in Abruzzo – to celebrate a range of Italian culinary classics, on a gastronomic journey across the peninsula from north to south, brimming with delicacies and accompanied by his famous, superb bread.

Name: Da Nilo
Description: In the heart of Cetona's square, a well-tended outdoor area among hedges welcomes guests with warmth and smiles. The cuisine is authentically Tuscan and well-crafted. Don’t miss the selection of local cured meats and the classic pici all’aglione, a true must-try!

Name: Da Noemi
Description: The mother of the current owner opened this busy restaurant in a medieval alleyway in the historic centre, giving it her own name. The historic dishes here reflect the culinary traditions of Ferrara, with specialities such as salama da sugo (pork sausage) and pasticcio di maccheroni (a baked pasta dish) on the menu. A must for anyone looking to sample local dishes already famous during the time of the Este family.

Name: Da Nonna Sceppa
Description: Founded in the 1960s by Grandma Giuseppa, the inn has today become a restaurant. The management has stayed within the hands of the same family: nephews and great - nephews are spread over dining room and kitchen. Local recipes on the menu, which changes daily.

Name: Da Odino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant has stood on this square for many years, having been built as a “casone” and previously used as a dance hall. Despite its large size, the atmosphere is pleasant and convivial, helped by the staff here who are friendly yet professional. Situated just a stone’s throw from the Park Hotel Junior, a modern hotel under the same ownership, the restaurant specialises in fish and seafood, although you’ll also find meat and vegetarian options on the menu.

Name: Da Orlando
Description: Simply arriving in Cusago near Milan, where the imposing castle dominates the attractive centre, puts you in a good mood. At Da Orlando, the menu is equally balanced between top-quality fish dishes such as the “bollita di mare” and meat-based dishes that will delight food-lovers, such as snails with trumpet mushrooms and duck breast with ginger. Two elegant dining rooms are the perfect setting for a romantic evening, while the attractive outdoor space comes into its own in summer. A good restaurant with over 40 years of history.

Name: Da Oscar
Description: Standing on the hills overlooking Lake Garda, this attractive, spacious restaurant has an elegant atmosphere. There is a delightful terrace for alfresco dining in summer.

Name: Da Peppe
Description: Situated in the historic centre of a small village in the Parco del Pollino, this long-established restaurant serves traditional and copious local dishes that are always expertly prepared. Guestrooms are also available in the family B&B of the same name.

Name: Da Poli alla Stazione
Address: Viale della Repubblica 10, Castelnovo di Sotto, 42024, Italy
Description: In the centre of a town known for its carnival and many allegorical floats, this family-run restaurant housed in an old railway station dating from the early 20C serves traditional regional dishes. The house speciality is charcoal-grilled cuisine, with an equal emphasis on meat and fish options.

Name: Da Politano
Description: Just outside Cuneo, at Boves, Da Poliziano is a family-run establishment that combines the hospitality of a hotel with a table attended to in every detail. The kitchen follows a tightly focused menu built around seasonality, enriched by a contemporary touch from young Luca, who draws on experience gained beyond these walls. In winter – particularly between December and January – the Helix pomatia snail ravioli with its own ragù is a must-order: a signature dish of rare finesse, worth the trip on its own.

Name: Da Rinuccio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the slopes of "a muntagna," one of the respectful nicknames for the volcano in the area, just outside the town with ample private parking, you'll find a family-oriented setting offering predominantly meat dishes, fresh pasta, and mushrooms. The dishes are carefully prepared, with generous portions, and meals are always enjoyed in a lovely glass-enclosed veranda. The wine list focuses mainly on Sicilian and particularly Catanese selections.

Name: Da Severino il Vecchio - Di Luciano
Address: Largo Abruzzi 2, ang. via Piemonte 23, Senorbì, 09040, Italy
Description: This historic restaurant now has new premises with a classic yet modern feel. Mediterranean cuisine with a traditional and regional influence.

Name: Da Tonino
Description: The chef at this restaurant serves decidedly contemporary cuisine with its roots in traditional recipes. His creative flair results in modern dishes in which each detail is carefully curated, with bold combinations that come as a surprise yet always feature a perfect balance of flavours and textures. The restaurant, situated in a quiet residential area away from the hustle and bustle of the small town, is the perfect choice for anyone looking for a relaxed and yet elegant dining experience.

Name: Da Tuccino
Address: Via Santa Caterina 69/F, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
Description: Overlooking the town square since 1968, this venue is now under new management, which has refreshed its direction while remaining faithful to its original character. The offering remains steadfastly anchored to a classic, clear and fragrant seafood cuisine, built upon superior-quality ingredients – with especial attention to raw preparations – and executed with meticulous care and precision. The experience is enhanced by several distinct advantages: private parking, a prime location just beyond the bustling town centre yet directly by the sea, a charming front garden and a spacious veranda-style dining room, fully openable and roof-retractable in fine weather. Throughout, one theme prevails: the constant call of the sea salt air.

Name: Da Vincenzo
Description: It's never easy to find the right balance between quality and quantity, especially in a town that is very much on the tourist trail. However, Da Vincenzo has succeeded in doing just this for years, ever since it was first opened by the family’s grandfather Vincenzo in 1958. Today, the founder’s grandson (who shares his grandfather’s name) is at the helm here, creating dishes which focus mainly on fish. Pleasant atmosphere, with a few small tables on the pavement of the street that runs through the centre of Positano. A choice of cocktails supplements the wine selection from lunchtime onwards.

Name: Da iumén
Address: Via Vittorio Emanuele II 26, Castelnuovo Belbo, 14043, Italy
Description: Since 1869, five generations have reinterpreted Piedmontese tradition through a modern lens. In an elegant, intimate setting, the restaurant serves dishes that fuse history and innovation – don’t miss the potato-and-hazelnut gnocchi with robiola cream. In the warmer months, reserve a table on the panoramic terrace: the view of the town hall and the hills of Castelnuovo Belbo is pure poetry.

Name: Da ö Vittorio
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Reassuring Ligurian cuisine in a classic interpretation and in a “Historical Restaurant of Italy”, where the same family always keeps up with the times, served in two separate rooms: one with a traditional tone, the other more modern. It is interesting to browse through the menu and wine list with historical notes and useful information on grape varieties. The many seafood dishes are accompanied by timeless local specialities, such as cima alla genovese. The focaccia with cheese is proverbial!

Name: DaV Mare
Description: The classic, wrought-iron outdoor dining space at this restaurant overlooks one of the most romantic little squares in Italy, while the view takes in the promontory dominated by its castle – a picture-postcard view that is famous around the world. The experienced Cerea family from the famous three-starred Michelin Da Vittoria restaurant in Bergamo are at the helm, serving consistently top-quality cuisine whether you’re here for a quick lunch or a gourmet dinner. It’s best to book ahead as the few tables are much in demand!

Name: DaV by Da Vittorio Louis Vuitton
Description: Situated in the heart of the central fashion district at the beginning of Via Montenapoleone, this new restaurant is the result of a collaboration between the renowned Cerea family and the equally prestigious fashion house Louis Vuitton, one of whose Milanese stores is located right behind it. The cuisine here is Italian to its core, albeit with a focus on dishes reinterpreted in a contemporary style that blends perfectly with the setting and the expectations of its guests. The decor is that of an elegant bistro, with the very busy dining room immediately after the entrance and reception, and a more intimate mezzanine accessible via stairs or a lift. The staff will quickly put you at ease and are on hand to offer recommendations from the à la carte or the chef’s tasting menu.

Name: Dabbanna
Address: Piazza Principe di Napoli 8/9, Modica, 97015, Italy
Description: It all began with the Cabbanna rotisserie, opened by grandfather Carmelo in 1971 and still going strong today, on his return from a time spent living in Venezuela. Fifty years later, his grandchildren are running a restaurant right opposite, in the central area of lower Modica, in a charming establishment with tasteful, welcoming interiors and several outdoor tables used in the summer. The menu is based on the island's ingredients and recipes, but also includes exotic influences — such as ceviche, known locally as “Ciauru ri mari” — reinterpreted with a contemporary twist. This results in colourful, beautifully presented dishes, excellent ingredients and delicate, attentive service provided by a female team.

Name: Dal Pittore
Address: Via Edmondo De Magistris 5, Cagliari, 09123, Italy
Description: In a quiet residential area a short distance from the Teatro Massimo, Renato Bacchetta, together with his family, has created a cosy restaurant with an intimate atmosphere, drawing on the experience gained during a long career that has also seen him play a leading role in Arona. His is a form of ‘artistic cuisine’ that remains true to a classical vision of gastronomy, based on a careful selection of ingredients and preparation methods designed to bring out their best qualities and flavours. The result is generous, colourful and satisfying dishes that combine elegance and flavour with a pleasant sense of familiarity. In the dining room, the service is provided by a professional and friendly team, who look after guests with expertise and genuine hospitality, helping to make the experience particularly enjoyable.

Name: Dallo Zio
Description: Just a short stroll from the Arch of Augustus, Dallo Zio is a restaurant that manages to be appealing without becoming luxurious, with a convivial and pleasantly informal atmosphere. The cuisine follows the same spirit: traditional recipes, generally not overly elaborate and largely seafood-based, with cooking methods that respect the catch, whether grilled over embers or baked, alongside the ever-tempting fried specialities.

Name: Dama
Address: Via Mulino 2, località San Gaudenzio, Cervesina, 27050, Italy
Description: Situated just a few kilometres from Voghera in the Bassa Lomellina area, this gourmet restaurant run by a young chef occupies the old stables of the Castello di San Gaudenzio. Alongside local specialities such as baked onion and 24-month-old Grana Padano cheese, the menu also features more creative dishes based around authentic recipes. The wine list includes some particularly interesting labels from the Oltrepò region.

Name: Dama Restaurant
Description: The cuisine served at this restaurant comes from a deep knowledge of the region, is inspired by tradition and yet constantly evolving. At Dama , guests will find creative cuisine with an equal balance of meat and fish dishes. Housed within Ca’ Bonfadini, the restaurant boasts an outstanding location overlooking Cannaregio canal, while the attractive dining room has just three elegant wooden tables that encourage sharing and can accommodate up to 10 guests.

Name: DanielCanzian
Description: In the heart of Brera, this restaurant showcases Italy’s high‑craft spirit, and its custom‑made furnishings echo Chef Canzian’s culinary philosophy. Lovers of classic Italian fare with a dash of whimsy will be delighted: the John Dory with autumn vegetables and Marsala sauce is superb. Naturally, the chef’s Veneto roots shine through in a dedicated tasting menu that can be enjoyed in 4, 5 or 6 courses.

Name: Daniela
Address: Piazza Matteotti 6, San Casciano dei Bagni, 53040, Italy
Description: Having arrived in the picturesque village of San Casciano, we recommend a charming walk through the cobbled streets to admire its perfect preservation. Next, in the main square, take a seat at Daniela's. The Tuscan menu offers homemade pastas and a small wine list that celebrates Tuscany, with an international twist such as Greystone's 2016 Thomas Brother Pinot Noir. Among the delicacies on offer, you will find pici all'aglione, pappardelle al cinghiale, porchettato rabbit and grilled veal tenderloin: in short, a choice for all tastes! The cosy rooms are carved out of old stone spaces, and the outdoor terrace offers partial views of the bucolic landscape surrounding the village.

Name: Darmagi
Description: ‘Darmagi’ in dialect means ‘what a shame’, and it would indeed be a shame not to cross the threshold of this secluded little villa, enveloped in a warm and genuinely homey atmosphere, particularly evocative in the handsome dining room with its fireplace. The cooking celebrates with conviction the traditions of Piedmont and Canavese; on winter weekends, the fritto misto and bagna caoda are simply not to be foregone. In the warmer months, a pleasant terrace immersed in greenery, complemented by the convenience of ample parking.

Name: Darì
Address: Vicolo Cieco San Pietro Incarnario 5, Verona, 37121, Italy
Description: Overflowing with stuccoes, mirrors, ceramics, and Murano chandeliers, guests take their place in one of five dining rooms, each more refined and distinctive than the last, for an evening befitting a grand occasion. Everything draws inspiration from opulence within this sumptuous fifteenth-century palazzo, while the cuisine ranges from local to international, from creative to traditional. In fine weather, service moves to an enchanting garden, a rarity in the heart of Verona.

Name: De Gustibus
Address: Via Martiri della Libertà 9, Chieri, 10023, Italy
Description: Enjoy modern, Mediterranean-influenced cuisine in an elegant restaurant with an attractive vintage-style ambience, where the excellent menu is announced at your table and varies according to daily availability. Very friendly and attentive service.

Name: De Gustibus - Maurizio
Description: Simple, modern fish dishes full of flavour take centre stage at this family-run restaurant in the charming historic centre of Palmi. The raw fish dishes served here include a delicious carpaccio made with the catch of the day and seasoned with a delicate home-made vinaigrette and cherry tomatoes, while the “Intrusi” menu offers three or four meat options for non-fish eaters. Desserts are announced at your table and always include a delicious cannolo. The wine list features mainly Italian labels, as well as a choice of champagnes. An intimate and warmly recommended restaurant.

Name: De' Minimi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed
Description: Situated within the beautiful Villa Paola hotel just outside Tropea, this gourmet restaurant is named after the Frati Minimi (Order of Minims) who once occupied this old monastery. The modern and occasionally creative cuisine here is showcased on 4-, 5-, 7- and 9-course tasting menus (San Tommaso, Miserie e Nobiltà, Di Necessità Virtù, La Novena ), all of which are prepared from the best Calabrian ingredients including many vegetables and citrus fruit grown on the property. The small wine list also has a regional focus and is complemented by a choice of cocktails served at the bar.

Name: Degli Angeli
Address: Località Madonna degli Angeli, Magliano Sabina, 02046, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: In the hamlet of Madonna degli Angeli, the dining room looks out over a breathtaking landscape embracing the hills and the Tiber valley. In business since 1820 and now in its seventh generation, devotees of traditional Lazio cuisine will find their refuge here. Among the offerings: lamb coratella, hand-rolled fettuccine, salt cod and various grilled meats. A generous selection of exceptional olive oils (also available for purchase) and an extensive wine list.

Name: Degusteria Italiana
Description: Tucked away among the narrow streets of the historic centre, in a strategic position between the Galleria degli Uffizi and the timeless Ponte Vecchio, this small restaurant wins one over through its intimate, considered and naturally chic atmosphere. True to its name, the cooking celebrates Italian ingredients through contemporary recipes that are spare and never overwrought, conceived more to comfort than to astonish. Completing the experience, a carefully curated selection of cheeses and cured meats, and a broad and well-constructed wine list dedicated entirely to Italy, with the region taking pride of place and the Supertuscans prominently featured.

Name: Degusteria del Gigante
Address: Via degli Anelli 19, San Benedetto del Tronto, 63074, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Situated in the charming historic centre of the upper part of the town, right behind the Torre dei Gualtieri, this restaurant occupies a 19C building with 15C foundations. Regional cuisine skilfully reinterpreted with a modern twist takes pride of place on the menu, where the focus is on flavour and seasonal ingredients rather than a vast selection of dishes. House specialities include options such as boned caramelised rabbit served with its own jus (inspired by the better-known traditional Marche dish), while daily visits to the market usually result in one or two fish-based recipes.

Name: Del Fagioli
Description: A historic city landmark, this rustic and sincere trattoria welcomes guests with a simple, warm atmosphere, where the open kitchen at the entrance serves as an immediate calling card. The distinctly familial ambiance makes it beloved by many, so much so that reservations well in advance are required. The table sees straightforward, fragrant recipes: excellent Florentine steaks, pici with aglione sauce, pappa al pomodoro, twice-cooked beef with sautéed green beans, and to finish, house-made cantucci. A stop that celebrates the most authentic Tuscan tradition with genuine spirit.

Name: Delicato
Description: Set among the narrow streets of a picturesque medieval village perched on a hill, whose history is reflected in the distinctive dining rooms nestled within its stone walls, chef Carlotta Delicato aims to showcase local produce to its best advantage, without unnecessary frills or complications, so that the flavours of the ingredients take centre stage on the plate. However, it does not overlook international influences – particularly those from Spain and South America – which appear here and there on the menu, adding a touch of the exotic. In any case, it’s an excellent restaurant – definitely not to be missed!

Name: Der Unterwirt
Description: Occupying a private house, this restaurant boasts a couple of charming Stube-style dining rooms, one of which is highly romantic and dates back to the 13C – although the vintage wood looks as though it may have come from elsewhere, it has in fact been here for centuries. Owner-chef Thomas Haselwanter creates carefully thought-out dishes which combine precision and classic comfort with the occasional modern touch, harmoniously combining the flavours of the Alto Adige with Mediterranean influences, with a particular focus on fish. A welcoming outdoor terrace for summer dining and seven modern guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Derby Grill
Description: Facing the Villa Reale, the dining room envelops guests in classic elegance with British undertones, reflecting the Hotel de la Ville that houses it, while select tables overlook a luminous, refined veranda. From the kitchen emerge two tasting journeys: Viaggio alle origini, which tells the story of the chef’s native Campania through Mediterranean aromas, and Il territorio… secondo me, where Lombard tradition meets creative touches. Dishes, which may be selected freely, showcase seasonal ingredients and fresh vegetables harvested from the restaurant’s own organic garden.

Name: Deschevaliers
Description: Under the guidance of multi-starred chef Nino Di Costanzo, a fine dining destination takes shape along one of Italy’s most celebrated gourmet streets, set within the elegant spaces of an international hotel showcasing its most exclusive brand. The atmosphere exudes refined contemporary flair: soft lighting, minimalist décor, and works by local artists that engage with the space. At the table, Neapolitan identity is expressed through dishes bearing dialect names, dressed in a modern aesthetic: creations that evoke tradition yet come alive with contemporary details, in a harmony of colors and textures. The service, attentive and professional, discreetly guides an experience that bridges heritage and innovation, weaving together authentic flavors and signature inspirations.

Name: Deste
Description: Set back slightly from the port, this restaurant boasts stunning views from its terrace which is highly recommended in fine weather. The culinary focus here is on modern dishes with an interesting choice of meat and fish options. Tea and kombucha offer an alternative to wine, while the home-produced gin is definitely worth sampling.

Name: Di Martino Sea Front Pasta Bar
Description: Situated opposite the Maschio Angioino (Castel Nuovo) in Naples, this restaurant was opened by a pasta producer from nearby Gragnano, making it the perfect choice for pasta-lovers. Sitting at a sushi bar-style counter, you can watch the chefs at work and choose from a menu that is dedicated entirely to pasta dishes (as well as desserts of course): 126 varieties, unusual combinations and almost endless possibilities, without, however, neglecting tradition and the great classics. When ordered à la carte, the dishes are generously portioned; however, for a more complete overview, opt for the tasting menu which includes more courses but in smaller quantities.

Name: Diana's Place
Description: Facing the square in front of Termini station, this wine bar-cum-restaurant is striking for its fresh and creative approach to cuisine. Nearly all the top-quality ingredients are local and can be purchased from the food counter. The excellent staff are happy to help with your choice of wine, which is also available by the glass.

Name: Dieci
Description: In the historic centre of Nepi, young chef Jordan Giusti expresses his personal vision of Tuscia cooking. Starting out from local ingredients, at times humble and popular in origin, yet full of flavour and loaded with memories, he produces excellent dishes, applying modern techniques and a contemporary outlook to the gastronomic heritage of the area.

Name: Dim Sum
Description: This restaurant with a partially open kitchen introduces its guests to the delicious specialities of Guangzhou and Southern China in rooms full of decorative details. The small dishes which characterise the culinary traditions of these regions have been refined with just a hint of contemporary flavour. A truly authentic Chinese dining experience.

Name: Dimora Ulmo
Description: Three tasting journeys are on offer – Contaminazioni, Dimora Ulmo and A Mano Libera – conceived to accompany the guest in a continuous dialogue between modern cooking and local traditions; individual courses may also be selected à la carte from within the menus. All of this takes shape within an ancient palazzo sensitively restored, enriched by a summer terrace with a striking outlook over Sassi. Among the dishes tasted, the porchetta-style rabbit with Ligurian gravy and roasted pepper merits particular mention, a successful expression of technique and personality. The service, attentive and engaged, conveys both expertise and genuine passion, while the well-constructed wine selection does justice to the territory without forgoing an openness to the rest of Italy and to some interesting international labels.

Name: Dina
Description: A large wooden door dating from the late 19C leads into this restaurant, which makes a striking impression from the moment you step over the threshold. You come first of all into a dark-coloured reception area, which then leads into three dining rooms decorated with antique furniture, most of which dates from the 1950s. Two tasting menus are served here (one classic in style, the other more creative), showcasing chef Alberto Gipponi’s culinary skills to the full – one of the most interesting options is the guinea fowl with lemon and gentian, which has a perfect balance of softness and delicate acidity. Ask the talented sommelier for his wine recommendations – we particularly enjoyed an excellent Riesling from the nearby Val Brembana.

Name: Dispensa Franciacorta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The decor at this restaurant features bottles of wine on the walls (there are around 700 labels on the wine list, with an unsurprising focus on sparkling wines from the local Franciacorta region), while the menu celebrates some of Italy’s best produce, as well as ingredients from further afield, with a focus on Mediterranean flavours. There’s also an excellent cheese selection which will delight cheese-lovers.

Name: Doc
Address: Via Vittorio Veneto 1, Borgio Verezzi, 17022, Italy
Description: Quiet, well - kept restaurant located in an aristocratic, early twentieth - century villa surrounded by a pretty garden.

Name: Dodici Fontane
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The scenery that you drive through to get to this restaurant on the slopes of Mt Etna is as breathtaking and impressive as the charming luxury Villa Neri hotel in which it is housed. In the modern dining room, the chef serves personalised cuisine with a focus on Sicilian ingredients, resulting in occasionally complex dishes (meat and fish) which are showcased on his tasting menus. Guests can also choose dishes à la carte style, while the wine list includes an excellent and highly recommended selection of local Etna labels, including the property’s own wine (they also produce their own extra-virgin olive oil).

Name: Dogma
Description: A small restaurant run by two young and passionate spouses, drawing on considerable previous experience: she in the dining room, he at the stove. Their cooking has a strongly defined personality and focuses above all on the sea, with dishes in which cooking over charcoal – or at least certain fundamental stages of it – takes centre stage, extending even into the desserts. The flavours are intense and convincing, with occasional foreign inflections, as in the Talo, a kind of Basque flatbread, made with white maize flour and filled with anchovies, broccoli and stracciatella: a preparation that showcases their mastery of this type of cooking. The setting is intimate and welcoming; booking is advisable, particularly in the evening, given the growing popularity of the venue.

Name: Dolia Gaeta
Description: This brand-new restaurant boasts an elegant, chic decor and a relaxed and informal ambience. The very young team here is overseen by a talented chef who prepares modern and creative dishes with a focus on fish from the local gulf, as well as elsewhere. The wine list is also particularly interesting, featuring a remarkable choice of champagnes and a special emphasis on labels from Lazio.

Name: Don Camillo
Description: A long-established restaurant, active since 1985, that continues to win over the palate with a cuisine inspired by Sicilian tradition, reinterpreted with a modern and personal touch by chef-patron Giovanni Guarnieri. In the heart of Ortigia, steps from the Metropolitan Cathedral of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, the surroundings express an equally timeless elegance: fifteenth-century tufa stone walls, period wooden furnishings and evocative wrought-iron candelabras contribute to a warm and refined atmosphere. Our Inspector recommends saving room at the end of the meal for their excellent desserts.

Name: Don Carlo
Address: Strada Comunale Su Guventeddu, Pula, 09050, Italy
Description: Located within the Sant’Efis Hotel, the restaurant enjoys a prime location right on the beach, with a splendid view of the sea and the island of Coltellazzo in the background. The menu celebrates the flavours of Sardinia through a selection of local ingredients and recipes that showcase the region, alongside dishes inspired by seasonal produce and market trends. The relaxed and light-filled setting invites you to enjoy an authentic Mediterranean experience, especially at lunchtime, when the scent of the sea accompanies your meal just a stone’s throw from the water. Given the popularity of this venue, it is advisable to book in advance, particularly for those not staying at the hotel.

Name: Don Carlos
Description: The tribute that the Grand Hotel dedicates to Giuseppe Verdi is accompanied, in the small historic rooms of the Don Carlos, by a tribute to Milanese and Italian cuisine, perhaps with a Mediterranean nuance introduced by multi-star Gennaro Esposito, here as a consultant, and carefully executed. In a succession of sketches, pictures and paintings dedicated to the world of opera, for music lovers the restaurant is a must-visit. Caruso Nuovo, on the other hand, with its bistro formula, can be an always inviting and less demanding alternative.

Name: Don Ciccio
Description: Overlooking the seafront, it is the classic seaside restaurant that you’d hope to find in a holiday resort. The atmosphere is lively and bright, with a pleasant veranda opening onto the promenade, while the catch of the day is prominently displayed at the entrance. From sashimi and seafood pasta dishes to grilled specialities, the choice is wide and tempting, characterised by freshness and simplicity executed to perfection. When booking, it’s worth asking for one of the front-row tables on the terrace, so you can make the most of the sea view.

Name: Doppio Gusto
Description: A short distance from the city centre and the embarkation points for the Aeolian Islands, the broad and carefully kept terrace – between outdoor seating and open-air spaces – invites guests to take a break dedicated to taste. On the table, a fragrant and contemporary Sicilian seafood cuisine, built on seafood of great quality and interpreted with a contemporary touch. The wine offering is also well structured, with interesting labels available by the glass.

Name: Dry Aged
Address: Via Cesare Da Sesto 1/A, Milan, 20123, Italy
Description: An evocative name, ‘Dry Aged’ immediately evokes the technique of dry ageing and clearly hints at the restaurant’s speciality. In a young, informal setting with a New York-inspired industrial charm, meat is indeed the star of the culinary offering. The menu devotes considerable space to dishes such as tartare, hand-chopped steak and raw sausage, but the real highlight of the menu is the selection of ribeye steaks and prime cuts from various breeds of cattle, ranging from Chianina to Bavarian Simmental and the renowned Prussian Manzetta. An ideal destination for meat lovers, where the meat is served with expertise and a focus on quality ingredients.

Name: Duanima
Description: In a narrow and elongated dining room, amidst subdued lighting and modern furnishings, Chef Patron Luca Floris champions a truly convincing culinary line. Whether dealing with meat or fish, his recipes reflect contemporary trends whereby the harmonious blend of ingredients is easily and delightfully discernible. Occasionally, the touch is more creative, such as with raw tuna carpaccio drizzled with the renowned Japanese teriyaki sauce, wherein soya’s savoury essence shines, enhanced by sweet chutney of Sardinian camoni tomatoes; at times it’s more classic, as with the Saint-Pierre scalopp atop varying vegetable textures.

Name: Due Pini
Address: Via Spinale 37/bis, Madonna di Campiglio, 38086, Italy
Description: Although recently restored, this restaurant has retained its strong Alpine character. The cuisine is regional in style and reinterpreted with an imaginative and contemporary twist.

Name: Dulchemente
Description: A contemporary-style restaurant which serves modern dishes alongside simpler, more classic options, with a notable focus on fish. A splendid outdoor terrace for alfresco dining and friendly, professional staff complete the picture.

Name: Duo
Address: Via Cavour 7, San Felice del Benaco, 25010, Italy
Description: Situated in the historic centre of the charming small village of San Felice del Benaco, Duo is the project of chefs Daniele Ghedini and Federico Pelizzari (the latter also oversees the front of house). Their personalised, modern cuisine is Mediterranean in style and features meat-based dishes, vegetarian options and fish recipes (salt- and freshwater), with a focus on matured fish which also has its own dedicated tasting menu. This colourful restaurant also boasts an outdoor space shaded by a pergola and surrounded by walnut trees.

Name: Duo
Description: In this restaurant housed in a historic palazzo in the centre of Chiavari, the owners have used the structural beauty of the building to showcase the skills of local artisans, resulting in a very attractive ambience. The modern cuisine is simple in style, allowing all the flavour of the ingredients to shine through.

Name: Duo Ristorante
Description: This elegant, intimate restaurant with subdued lighting is the perfect choice for a romantic gourmet dinner. Showcased on tasting menus and a concise à la carte, the excellent cuisine focuses on typical recipes and specialities from Puglia, often with an added personalised and creative twist.

Name: Duomo
Description: Bright and inviting is the dining room of this small resource aspiring towards contemporary culinary offerings—grounded in seasonal products—and numerous homemade preparations. The two siblings at the helm also unveil intriguing regional recipes with apt personal touches. For the wine lovers, an appropriate label awaits every need, whilst the setting further enhances the enjoyment: located in the town’s alleyways, just steps from the Cathedral.

Name: ES Cantina&Ristorante
Description: Inside Gianfranco Fino’s winery, a charming tuff-stone building houses a light-filled restaurant on the first floor, featuring large windows overlooking the vineyards and a spacious terrace set among the surrounding countryside. The culinary offering interprets ingredients from land and sea with a contemporary sensitivity, striking a balance between tradition and creativity. At dinner, the experience takes the form of a tasting menu, while at lunch, on days when the restaurant is open, a more concise and informal menu is available. The selection of wines showcases the winery’s entire range, offering a comprehensive overview of the estate’s various vintages.

Name: Eea
Description: Named after the Ancient Greek name for Ponza, this restaurant is situated above the port and boasts fine views of the island’s picturesque houses and rugged coastline from its terrace. With an almost exclusive focus on fish and seafood, the menu features a balance of creative and more traditional dishes.

Name: Eggentaler
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just three kilometers from Bolzano and equally close to the highway exit, this restaurant boasts over a century of history and has been expertly run by the Schmieder family for more than forty years. Such longevity speaks for itself: the establishment is a benchmark for enthusiasts of charcoal-grilled meats, the true specialty of the house. But the menu does not end there: alongside the carnivore mainstays, a modern Italian cuisine offering finds its place, spanning land and sea, with simple yet well-executed dishes such as prawns in spicy garlic oil served with bruschette. The wine list is equally commendable, curated directly by a family member. Completing the offering is a small hotel equipped with sauna and pool.

Name: Ego
Description: The experience begins at the moment of reservation, when guests choose the number of courses and prepare to place themselves entirely in the hands of the chef’s creativity. Ego is a reflection of the personality of Lorenzo De Lio, a young Roman talent with an international journey that emerges clearly in his dishes. His cuisine is a voyage without borders, where Mexican influences, Southeast Asian references, and unexpected inspirations coexist, constructed to stimulate the palate with spices, contrasts, and intensity. The dining room counts just five tables – to be reserved well in advance – entrusted to the gracious and knowledgeable care of Beatrice, who also curates wine pairings by the glass with great sensitivity.

Name: El Brite de Larieto
Address: Località Larieto, strada per Passo Tre Croci, Cortina d'Ampezzo, 32043, Italy
Description: A charming spot for mountain lovers, starting with the road leading there, which winds through a larch forest, the oldest room inside (a 15th-century stube, though the newer room on the upper floor is also charming) and, of course, the cuisine. Some of the ingredients come from the animals on the neighbouring farm (it’s a farm holiday accommodation). Excellent mountain dishes are served, under the direction of Riccardo Gaspari of the SanBrite restaurant – which has one Michelin star – also in Cortina.

Name: El Filò
Address: Strada Dolomites 103, Pozza di Fassa, 38036, Italy
Description: Following recent refurbishment, El Filò is now even more comfortable than ever, boasting an Alpine-influenced decor that is striking for its contemporary style. The Dolomites and Ladin culinary traditions are still very much to the fore in the cuisine, which is prepared by the excellent owner-chef, although modern touches and influences from outside the region also feature. The wine list offers a fine selection of options from the region.

Name: El Gato
Description: Chioggia is famous as one of the more active fishing ports in the region and this restaurant takes full of advantage of the local catch. Situated on the central promenade of this picturesque town, the restaurant serves fish of truly exceptional quality served in traditional recipes from the Adriatic.

Name: El Magazen osteria contemporanea
Address: Calle Larga Giacinto Gallina 5402, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description: With its exposed brick walls and large wooden shelves brimming with bottles and Venetian Carnival masks, this small restaurant overlooking a quiet canal retains the city’s authentic charm and the cosy atmosphere of a family-run establishment. At the helm is Yasmiin, the owner and chef, supported by her husband Nino, the sommelier, while the service is handled by the chef’s sisters. The concept, which allows guests to pop in even just for a glass of wine and a few dishes, thoughtfully interprets Venetian tradition while introducing contemporary touches. Among the most popular dishes are the classic Sardinian ‘sarde in saor’, here given a new twist with a crispy panko coating, caramelised onions with a delightful sweet-and-sour balance, snow peas and a delicate wasabi sauce – a successful fusion of lagoon-inspired flavours and Japanese influences.

Name: El Primero
Description: Situated in a building with a striking appearance (the Uruguay Pavilion at Expo 2015), this restaurant boasts stunning views of the mountains in the distance. Inside, the large dining room acts as a backdrop for South American cuisine with a focus on grilled meat dishes and a barbecue grill in full view of guests. Sourced from recognised and certified Uruguayan farms, the meat here is subject to rigorous controls throughout the supply chain. The “parillero”, the chef at the barbecue grill, uses all his skills to enhance the flavours of the top-quality meat and maintain its tender texture. The wine cellar is dominated by Uruguayan and Italian wines, as well as beers and typical liqueurs, offering the perfect accompaniment for every dish.

Name: Elementi
Description: In this intimate, pared-back venue, with wooden tables and soft lighting, warmth and fine cookery reign supreme. Gentle chamber music sets the tone for a journey through the cuisine of Valentina and Saverio, whose cooking bears a distinctly personal stamp. The menu alternates between land and sea: house-marinated anchovies, caserecci from Abruzzo prepared in the classic cacio e pepe style with pink prawns, and an impeccably rendered duck breast among the main courses. A venue that will satisfy even the most discerning of palates: a truly gourmand experience.

Name: Elephant
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the famous Elephant hotel (with which it shares a name), this restaurant has a unique, historic ambience thanks to its decor of antique wood panelling. The cuisine here is regional with a modern twist, featuring dishes such as char with cream of celery and green apple on a bed of fragrant elderflowers. The interesting wine list boasts a selection of almost a thousand different labels.

Name: Emilio
Address: via Girardi 1, loc. Casabianca, Fermo, 63900, Italy
Description: With 60 years of history behind it, Emilio can definitely be described as a leading light on the region’s restaurant scene. The restaurant is renowned for its excellent fish, which is usually cooked in classic style (fish stew and mixed steamed fish served on steamed vegetables are prime examples) and often announced at your table, although a concise menu is also available. The elegant dining room is enhanced by a collection of striking works of art.

Name: Enigma Restaurant
Address: Viale Leopoldo Nobili 2/c, Reggio Emilia, 42121, Italy
Description: Housed within a hotel in a centrally located park, this attractive restaurant with its own private entrance boasts fine views of the surrounding greenery through its large windows. The cuisine is both regional and imaginative, often combining influences from Emilia and Campania (chef Ciro Sieno’s native region), as demonstrated by the tortello pasta filled with a Neapolitan ragù and the cappelletti filled with minestra maritata. Vegetarian options also feature alongside the meat and fish dishes on the menu.

Name: Enoclub
Description: Under the arcades of a piazza named after Michele Ferrero, this restaurant has a simple, modern ambience with walls covered with wine bottles, as well as friendly, efficient female staff. The beautifully prepared Piedmontese cuisine is showcased on an à la carte and a tasting menu, accompanied by an impressive selection of quality wine.

Name: Enotavola Pino
Description: The entrance to this restaurant through a wine-bar can be misleading, as you are eventually led to simpler – yet still attractive – dining rooms. In this wine-themed setting, enjoy delicious fish and seafood dishes with the occasional creative twist, accompanied by a particularly extensive selection of wines by the glass. A highly recommended address for fish lovers, situated right in the historic centre of Padova.

Name: Enoteca Cavour 313
Description: Reborn in late 2024 thanks to the enthusiasm of a young Frenchwoman raised among vineyard rows and harvests, this historic establishment has found new life without losing its soul as a rustic, welcoming wine shop. Just beyond the entrance, guests pause for an easy lunch, guided by a nimble offering written on the blackboard and enriched by a daily special – irresistible, during our visit, the saffron risoni with mantis shrimp. In the evening (reservations recommended), one moves into the more intimate spaces that open beyond the visible kitchen, where the young Roman chef, trained at the ALMA school, presents seasonal dishes interpreted with technique and creativity. The wine list is excellent, harmoniously divided between Italian labels and those from across the Alps.

Name: Enoteca Del Duca
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Despite the change of ownership at this centrally located restaurant right behind the castle and the main square, there’s a certain continuity to the cuisine which remains focused on classic dishes with a regional flavour (with the option of steak on the menu). The dining room features old stone walls, plus there’s also an attractive outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Enoteca L'Armadillo
Description: Situated in the district of La Palud at the foot of Mont Blanc, this small wine bar serves interesting cuisine created by a talented Japanese chef who adds his own personal twist to the valley’s top-quality ingredients. Dishes include the occasional fusion option, such as capon salad with yuzu, puntarelle and black garlic, while wine is chosen directly from the shelves in the intimate dining room. Booking is recommended, especially in high season.

Name: Enoteca Meucci
Description: Occupying a restored farmhouse at the foot of Cortona, this restaurant has two different dining areas: a wine bar on the ground floor where you can enjoy excellent aperitifs or buy local food produce, and a restaurant on the first floor that serves a traditional yet constantly evolving menu with a focus on seasonal ingredients. There’s also a beautiful outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Enoteca di Buttrio
Description: Housed in a beautiful historic building, this business, originally a wine bar (hence the name “enoteca”), gradually developed into a restaurant over the years. The menu focuses uniquely on fish, almost all of which comes from the Adriatic, showcased in traditional dishes enhanced with a creative twist.

Name: Enoteca di Canelli - Casa Crippa
Description: Occupying a late-19C palazzo, in what was a historic wine cellar right up to the late 1960s, this family-run restaurant serves carefully presented, regional cuisine with a lightly creative and contemporary twist. A good example is the “carne cruda alla monferrina” (a kind of beef tartare) served with a Parmesan cream and hazelnuts.

Name: Ensama Pesce
Address: Via Aristide Dondarini 4, Sala Bolognese, 40010, Italy
Description: A menu which focuses only on fish (from the daily market) which is prepared with a hint of Puglia, the chef’s native region. As soon as guests are seated at their table, they are brought a selection of homemade breads, including taralli bread rings and focaccia. Owner-chef Sabino is the heart and soul of this restaurant, where guests can be sure of a memorable culinary experience!

Name: Entroterra Trattoria Sostenibile
Description: In the heart of the historic centre, a short distance from the Romanesque Cathedral dedicated to Santa Maria Assunta, stands this intriguing gastronomic address run by three passionate young restaurateurs: Jacopo and Paride at the stove, engaged in Abruzzese regional cuisine enriched by a contemporary touch, and Luca front of house, dedicated to hospitality and wine service. Among the most successful offerings stands out calf’s tongue with roasted squash, salsa verde, anchovy mayonnaise and rice crisps, a balanced dish full of nuance. The desserts are equally unmissable, such as vanilla and chamomile panna cotta accompanied by frozen blueberries, sauce and cocoa crumble: a finale that captivates through contrast, freshness and precision.

Name: Entrà
Address: Via Salde Entrà 60, località Entrà, Finale Emilia, 41034, Italy
Description: Siblings Antonio and Elvira uphold a family tradition which, since the 1960s, has been part of a much longer history, that of the simple wine shop which occupied these premises immediately after the Great War.
