For generations, the Previdi family has been a benchmark for authentic, fragrant and delicious Emilian cuisine, prepared — as they like to recall — “without revisiting it, whenever possible”.Fresh, homemade pasta is a real highlight, starting with the legendary pumpkin tortelli – made famous in part by the restaurant’s proximity to the province of Mantua – served with a savoury meat sauce. The signature dish, however, is roast guinea fowl, served on a bed of seasonal salad and accompanied by tender roast potatoes, in the truest family tradition.The wine selection is also of the highest standard, comprising around 400 labels and reflecting a carefully considered choice that complements the dishes on the menu.

Name: Erbaluigia
Description: This attractive restaurant with a simple, minimalist decor stands almost opposite the thousand-year-old church of San Frediano. The inviting menu here focuses on regional dishes with a successful combination of traditional and modern styles, including a section dedicated to barbecue options. Meat takes pride of place, although offal, cheese and a few vegetarian options also feature.

Name: Essencia Restaurant
Address: Piazza Santa Maria la Nova 9, Naples, 80134, Italy
Description: Having spent many years living in Spain, the young chef at this quiet, elegant restaurant offers an appealing combination of Spanish and Italian dishes, resulting in his own interesting interpretations of Mediterranean cuisine. Situated in the heart of the historic centre, the restaurant has an open-view kitchen and chef’s table for four guests near the entrance, while the main dining room is on the first floor.

Name: Essentia
Address: Piazza San Nicolò 2, Castrocaro Terme, 47011, Italy
Description: Situated at the foot of the fortress in the historic centre of Castrocaro, this restaurant has an interesting young chef at the helm, Andrea Giacchini. The cuisine often (but not always) has a local influence and demonstrates remarkable technical expertise that is neither overly ostentatious nor an end in itself, but rather a way of skilfully showcasing the top-quality ingredients used.

Name: Essenza
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Essenza is housed within the Borghi dell'Eremo resort in a stunning setting surrounded by beautiful and tranquil natural landscapes. The spacious dining room, which is flooded with natural light thanks to the picture windows that look out at the Umbrian hills, provides the backdrop for a culinary experience that focuses on traditional cuisine. Our inspector particularly recommends the exquisite Borghi saffron tagliatelle served with a rabbit ragù (the rabbits are raised on the estate’s own farm).

Name: Essenza Bistrot
Description: A cosy bistro-restaurant in the heart of the historic centre, characterised by intimate, tastefully decorated spaces, with stone walls that reflect the architecture and character of the local area. In the kitchen is chef Massimiliano Villani, who reinterprets contemporary cuisine using mainly regional ingredients and a menu that follows the rhythm of the seasons. To mark its tenth anniversary, the restaurant also celebrated its history with a tasting menu featuring the most iconic and beloved dishes from its history. The wine list is interesting, and the outdoor seating area is lovely in fine weather.

Name: Estro Vino e Cucina
Address: Calle Crosera, sestiere Dorsoduro 3778, Venice, 30123, Italy
Description: Located in the slightly more secret part of Venice, this is a place we can highly recommend. It has a relaxed and informal atmosphere reminiscent of a wine bar, and the food is excellent, whether you choose meat or fish, with many dishes that will be remembered for a long time, thanks also to an excellent selection of around 700 ecologically sustainable wines.

Name: Etra
Description: Within the Palazzo Doria De Fornari, overlooking the celebrated piazza De Ferrari, one need only cross the threshold and venture into the heart of the building to discover Etra’s discreet entrance: a name that is an anagram of arte (art), evoked by the constantly evolving gallery that adorns the walls of the restaurant, enveloped in dark tones and studied minimalism. The cooking is distinguished by curiosity, verve and technical precision, structured around three tasting menus. Among the most accomplished offerings are the ray bottoni with red prawn tartare and a green vegetable jus, a dish that surprises with its freshness, aromatic character and refinement of execution.

Name: Evo Ristorante
Description: This restaurant at the entrance to the historic centre boasts a delightful garden which leads to a porch where tables are set out in summer – an enchanting setting that feels as though you’re eating in the countryside despite the village location. The chefs’ imagination knows no bounds in complex and elaborate dishes that focus on ingredients from Puglia and are grouped into themed tasting menus.

Name: Exforo
Description: Occupying old stables in the square where the town’s livestock market was once held, this restaurant boasts charming views of the Prato della Valle gardens. Also home to a bistro serving aperitif snacks and a cocktail bar for post-dinner drinks, the main restaurant is very much the focal point here, with its dark-coloured, contemporary decor and colourful, modern cuisine. In summer, don’t miss the summer terrace with its fine views.

Name: Extra
Description: Situated slightly inland behind Marina di Carrara, Extra (the name refers to the quality of the region’s world-famous marble) is a bright, modern restaurant with a menu inspired by the area’s fish and seafood culinary traditions. The menu is slightly more elaborate and the ambience more elegant in the evening and on Saturday lunchtimes.

Name: Exé Restaurant
Address: Via Circondariale San Francesco 2, Fiorano Modenese, 41042, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The ground floor of the Executive Spa Hotel is home to a contemporary, elegant and bright restaurant. The spacious rooms invite you to soak up the relaxed atmosphere, while the aromas from the kitchen tantalise your senses: from the enveloping notes of ragout on handmade tagliatelle to the rustic scent of guinea fowl cooking slowly in the wood-fired oven. The sea comes to the table with fresh fish dishes, while the heat of the grill enhances fine meats, carefully aged until they are irresistibly tender. The wine list is a journey through the finest wines, and the sommelier, with confident gestures and discreet smiles, will guide you in your choice, serving even the most sought-after labels by the glass.

Name: Faletta 1881
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled among the hills of Monferrato and surrounded by its vineyards, this lovingly restored historic farmhouse offers an authentic welcome. The kitchen is dominated by Piedmontese tradition, with some modern touches and national flourishes. Be sure to try the trio of antipasti. The wine list is entirely house‑selected, featuring a Grignolino that deserves attention. Cozy rooms and a salt‑water pool complete the experience.

Name: Fana Ladina
Address: Via Plan de Corones 10, San Vigilio di Marebbe, 39030, Italy
Description: The three small dining rooms at this restaurant include a bright and airy room overlooking the village and a historic Stube with a romantic feel. The cuisine here is typically Ladin in flavour, with the option of daily specials and an à la carte, while the efficient service comes courtesy of staff in local costume. Owner-chef Alma Willet’s friendly welcome and a charming outdoor space for summer dining complete the picture.

Name: Faraglioni Restaurant
Address: Lungomare dei Ciclopi 115, loc. Aci Trezza, Aci Castello, 95021, Italy
Description: Situated next to the hotel of the same name (a reference to the Faraglioni islands just off the coast here) but with its own entrance, this restaurant overlooks the beautiful Riviera dei Ciclopi. Sicilian ingredients take pride of place here in traditional and creative dishes with a focus on fish and seafood (vegetarian options are also available).

Name: Farmacia dei Sani
Description: Occupying a corner of the central Piazza del Popolo in the delightful historic centre of Ruffano, this family restaurant (also a liqueur-maker) is surrounded by old palazzi which add to the charm of its setting. The Puglian cuisine served here has a modern twist while remaining unfussy in style and firmly anchored in the region. The service is quick, and each guest is greeted with a smile by the Rizzo family.

Name: Fattoria delle Torri
Description: A slice of paradise in Modica’s historic center: delightful terrace service among the lemon trees and a professional legacy carried on by chef-patron Peppe Barone's daughters – Carla in the dining room and Francesca in the kitchen – who, with youthful energy, champion a highly original gastronomic offering that balances innovation with tradition. They draw freely from the island’s culinary history, enriching it with exotic touches often characterized by gently spiced flavors. The wine program is equally impressive: guests can confidently rely on their recommendations to discover something special from an excellent wine list.

Name: Federico II
Description: Offering classic seafood cuisine, this restaurant serves the most well-known and loved dishes, from raw seafood to pasta and gnocchi with various sauces, and main dishes such as baked fish, fish stew, and salt-crusted fish. Of course, there are also fried dishes and fish soup (available by reservation). Everything is served in a lovely dining room with brick arches or, when the weather is nice, along the pedestrian street of the picturesque historic center.

Name: Feel Como
Description: Wild regional produce, game and freshwater fish take pride of place on the menu at this elegant restaurant which celebrates nature in all its glory, despite its town-centre location. The dishes prepared by chef Federico Beretta have a contemporary feel, while the tasting menu is dedicated to wild ingredients foraged from the woods.

Name: Felter alle Rose
Address: Via Gasparo Da Salò 33, Salò, 25087, Italy
Description: A trattoria that tells stories of family and tradition, renewed under the guidance of those who have made hospitality and quality their vocation. The spaces open up into different atmospheres: the authentic warmth of the dining room, the closed veranda that filters the soft light of the seasons, and the cellar, where the scent of wine accompanies tastings and aperitifs. The kitchen serves Italian dishes, prepared with simplicity and good taste, using fresh, seasonal ingredients: genuine flavours intertwined with the pleasure of feeling at home.

Name: Feria
Description: A modern restaurant with an Indonesian-style decor, plus an attractive open-view kitchen which creates a warm and welcoming ambience. Here, Marco Feltrin, an Italian chef with experience in Indonesian cuisine, serves typical dishes from this country with a contemporary twist. We particularly enjoyed the noodles, squid and leeks, and the charcoal-grilled snapper. The wine list includes a good selection of organic and biodynamic labels which are the perfect accompaniment to the Asian food served here. Feria has two distinct spaces – the bistro-cum-bar which serves cocktails and some street-food snacks and the gourmet restaurant.

Name: Feva
Description: In the historic centre of Castelfranco Veneto, while the courtyard is period, the restaurant’s style is inspired by a contemporary, intimate and elegant minimalism, with the dining room on the first floor featuring original wooden beams. Nicola Dinato’s cuisine is showcased through two tasting menus, Anima and Corpo. The first offers a selection of the chef’s new dishes, reflecting his continually evolving spirit… The second, on the other hand, draws on classic signature dishes (the scampi risotto alla busara is not to be missed). As well as an interesting selection of French wines, the wine list also impresses with some Italian gems, such as the 1999 Brunello di Montalcino from Case Basse Soldera.

Name: Fiamma Cremisi
Address: Via De Gasperi 37, località Viadana, Calvisano, 25012, Italy
Description: Italian cuisine that strikes a balance on several fronts: while the chef’s dishes include nods to Brescia’s culinary tradition, they are also enlivened with creative touches. In summer, service extends outdoors beneath a gazebo; in the colder months, the main dining room is warmed by a fireplace. At lunchtime the menu is shorter, more affordable, and there is a business menu.

Name: Filia Ristorante
Description: In Borgo Trento, an elegant residential quarter just steps from the historic center, Filia plays the card of a modern, minimalist setting, where just five tables find their place. Tasting menus are served, with dishes also available à la carte. The cuisine is modern and creative, at times revisiting classics of the Italian tradition.

Name: Filippino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Opened in 1910, this historic restaurant with an attractive shaded outdoor pergola serves an extensive array of delicious local fish prepared in traditional recipes. Enjoy a selection of typical Sicilian specialities prepared by the Bernardi family, including the highly recommended “Nonno Filippino” fish soup.

Name: Filippo
Description: In this modern and elegant restaurant, Filippo chooses three products every day and creates a surprise meal for guests with these ingredients. An original idea which is certainly worth a try, but for less adventurous diners there is also a small menu.

Name: Filo
Description: From the splendid lakeside position, the view extends to the opposite shore, Comacina Island, and Villa Balbianello. An enchanting terrace overlooking Lake Como, surrounded by greenery with hills as a backdrop like a painting, is where you can savor Mediterranean-flavored dishes. Choose from three tasting menus ("Freestyle," "Classics," and "Vegetarian"). Or opt for the à la carte menu, with offerings such as purple prawns with goat cheese cream, berries, and bisque: an explosion of flavors!

Name: Finger's Garden
Description: Firmly aimed at a trendier crowd, this restaurant has soft lighting and an Oriental feel. The chef here skilfully creates a range of dishes, including raw fish options and original fusion cuisine with a hint of Brazilian flavour. Gourmet diners will be happy to give full rein to the chef on his surprise menu.

Name: Fiorfiore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Set in a panoramic location overlooking the rolling hills of Umbria and the skyline of Todi, this elegant residence combines hospitality and fine dining in a setting of great charm. The cuisine offers a contemporary take on regional traditions, showcasing the finest local produce, starting with extra virgin olive oil and a selection of wines produced on the estate. Also worthy of note are the carefully curated selection of Champagnes and dishes that blend culinary technique with gastronomic heritage, such as oxtail ‘bottoni’ alla vaccinara served with a pecorino fondue, pepper and cocoa beans. Comfortable, quiet rooms round off an experience centred on relaxation and fine dining.

Name: Flurin
Description: Flurin occupies an old medieval tower in Glorenza, a small hamlet in the Val Venosta which is surrounded by walls that also date back to the Middle Ages. Furnished in a modern style that contrasts with its old, vaulted ceiling, the restaurant serves contemporary cuisine that enthusiastic owner-chef Thomas Ortler prepares from carefully selected seasonal ingredients from the region. His creative and imaginative recipes include dishes such as duo of Wagyu beef (raised on the property) served with polenta, carrots and spring onions. There’s also a charming small outdoor space which must be booked well in advance in summer.

Name: Foresta
Address: Via Litoranea 2, Marina di Pisa, 56128, Italy
Description: Overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea, all the tables at this restaurant offer sea views, whether you’re sitting in the winter dining room or on the outdoor summer terrace. The menu here focuses on top-quality fish dishes, which are classic in style, as is the background music and wine list, although the desserts have a more imaginative flavour.

Name: Forme Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Forme Restaurant is a modern, ever-evolving venue located outside the city center within the Atena educational complex, which also houses the Sottoforme bistrot. At the helm is Abruzzese chef Arianna Gatti: her cooking is a contemporary narrative, vivid in color and bold in flavor, rooted in Italian tradition yet reimagined with restraint and sensitivity. Her dishes evoke the comforts of home: the spice-scented ventricina, Navelli saffron butter that gently caresses the palate, and artisanal Abruzzese spaghettone celebrating authentic simplicity.

Name: Forte del 48
Address: Via Carlo Vizzotto 1, San Donà di Piave, 30027, Italy
Description: This pleasant restaurant started life in 1848 as a bastion used by the Habsburg army and was later transformed into an inn. Recognised as a “Locale Storico Veneto”, it’s now run by the third generation of the De Faveri family who serve traditional meat and fish dishes here. Comfortable guestrooms are also available for guests wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Frades La Terrazza
Address: SP94 - Località Abbiadori, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Situated in a panoramic location on Cala di Volpe bay, this trendy restaurant serves excellent cuisine with a focus on Sardinian specialities and other Mediterranean dishes. There’s a beautiful terrace for an aperitif, plus tapas options to share and a good selection of sparkling wines. Young and enthusiastic staff.

Name: Frades Porto Cervo
Description: This new Milan venture is the brainchild of three brothers who already run a restaurant and delicatessen in Porto Cervo. Elegant and extremely contemporary in style, the restaurant serves modern Sardinian cuisine, while a corner reminiscent of their delicatessen allows guests to taste the island’s hams and cheeses by the slice.

Name: Franceschetta 58
Description: Intimate and vibrant settings, where the smell of warm bread and the clinking of glasses convey the simple philosophy with which Massimo Bottura renews his love for Modena and Emilia. The menu, which includes both classic dishes and tasting menus, starts from the roots: the intense flavour of 36-month aged pancetta caressed by the sweetness of Campanina apple “mostarda”, or the velvety creaminess of “zuppa inglese”. Then the journey opens up to creativity, with unexpected touches such as grey mullet “alla cacciatora”, which releases aromas of herbs and the sea. The tortellini, made by the patient hands of Tortellante, where fresh pasta becomes both a therapeutic gesture and shared art, are an absolute must. The wine list is short, with carefully selected wines, while Lambrusco, in all its nuances, occupies a whole page, celebrating the deep-rooted connection with the region.

Name: Franchino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Situated within the Onda Verda hotel on the road down to the delightful seaside town of Conca dei Marini, this attractive restaurant boasts a terrace overlooking the sea that is hard to resist. The menu here adds to the appeal, featuring traditional fresh fish dishes and local seafood recipes which combine to make this an exquisitely romantic experience. When you book, ask for one of the tables on the terrace or on the pedestrianised promenade.

Name: Frosch Restaurant
Address: Via Santi Pietro e Paolo 1, Varena, 38030, Italy
Description: Situated in the centre of the small village of Varena (just outside the more famous Cavalese), this romantic and intimate restaurant with modern comforts and a mountain ambience is home to a talented female chef. Her contemporary recipes focus on local produce combined with Mediterranean flavours in some of the fish dishes and international ingredients such as foie gras.

Name: Frosio
Description: Housed in a 18C villa which was once a family inn, this restaurant is run by the dynamic and professional Frosio family who have over 30 years’ experience in the restaurant business. There’s nothing improvised about Frosio, where Camillo guarantees impeccable service front of house and Paolo is at the helm in the kitchen, creating carefully prepared dishes with a classic-modern feel and an equal emphasis on meat and fish, often made from traditionally “gourmet” ingredients such as scampi, lobster, foie gras, pigeon and caviar. The wine list continues to offer an excellent selection, with one section dedicated to Italy and another to the rest of the world. Decorated with austere elegance, the wine cellar in the 13C tower is home to more than 1,000 different labels. Attractive outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Fuori Rotta
Description: In the "upper" part of the town, just steps from the public parking and already in the pedestrian area, the cuisine leans more towards Ligurian traditions than seafood. We enjoyed the "Scherpada": a savory vegetable tart with melted cheese, prepared and served by a young team passionate also about wine, as evidenced by the excellent wine list and recommendations from the owner-sommelier. Reservations are essential, especially for those wishing to sit at the panoramic outdoor tables.

Name: Futura
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre overlooking the monumental Piazza San Giustino, this restaurant has a traditional feel in keeping with its location, enhanced by typical brick walls in dining rooms arranged on two floors. In contrast, the predominantly meat-based cuisine is contemporary in style, with some interesting technical and creative twists.

Name: FØRMA contemporary restaurant
Description: Situated in a secluded residential district that is part of L’Aquila’s historic centre, this intimate restaurant with an elegantly minimalist ambience is home to skilful owner-chef Simone Ciuffetelli. Having gained experience working abroad, Ciuffetelli showcases local ingredients in his creative, contemporary dishes, with the occasional use of fermented products and a frequent focus on just three ingredients. A good example is his dessert featuring cream and crunchy toasted hazelnuts generously coated with a white-chocolate mousse that is “disguised” as an Italian-style meringue thanks to a sprinkling of liquorice powder.

Name: Fàula
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Fàula – “fairytale” in Piedmontese – represents the gourmet offering of Casa Langa, a property that opens like an elegant amphitheatre overlooking the valley. In the kitchen, Francesco Clerico presents a cuisine that weaves Piedmontese tradition and modern interpretations with natural ease, always with a personal touch. The tasting menu dedicated to vegetables from the estate garden speaks to a sincere attention to product, while the à la carte selection moves with balance among meat dishes, fish, and vegetable offerings. A well-curated wine selection and the gracious professionalism of the service complete a harmonious, thoughtfully constructed experience.

Name: Gagini
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the vibrant heart of the city, between the Vucciria market and the Cala harbor, modern design and vivid colours bring a contemporary touch to the timeless charm of the ancient walls that house it: those of the 16th-century workshop of sculptor Antonello Gagini. In the kitchen, a new chef of Piedmontese origin weaves together the recipes of his native region and northern Italy with the freshness of the sea and the rich pleasures of Trinacria, drawing out their quality through original and well-considered pairings. Among the standout dishes are barbecued mussels with ‘nduja salmoriglio, Vietnamese bisque and crispy rapini, or tagliatelle made with 30 egg yolks, served with artichokes, citron and tuna bottarga: dishes that speak of a vibrant and contemporary gastronomic encounter.

Name: Gainn
Description: A change of management in January 2026 brought with it a new hand in the kitchen, without however altering the identity of Gainn, open since 2007 and a long-standing and dependable ambassador of Korean gastronomic culture. The cooking is lively and flavoursome, composed of colourful dishes revolving around rice, restorative soups, meat and fish, with generous space given to vegetables, soya and a well-judged balance between sweet-sour and spicy notes. The approach is avowedly convivial: generous portions and preparations conceived to be shared at the centre of the table. A single dessert features on the menu: those with a sweet tooth would do well to bear this in mind.

Name: Galileo
Address: Viale IV Novembre conc. 25, Civitanova Marche, 62012, Italy
Description: Boasting a dining room overlooking the beach, Galileo is a typical Adriatic restaurant serving fish and seafood dishes that are popular with many Italians. Options include seafood salad, a selection of antipasti, fish and seafood pastas, assorted small fried fish, and grilled recipes. In other words, delicious, traditional and unfussy cuisine in which fish takes centre stage.

Name: Gallery Bistrot Contemporaneo
Description: Modern cuisine, prepared with meticulous attention and enriched with carefully selected seasonal products. Tradition meets originality, as in the surprising risotto with clams, cauliflower and a dash of cocoa. Only twenty places in a spectacularly designed dining room: walls and ceilings clad in undulating light wood panels that weave together in a dynamic arch, creating an impression of movement that envelops the dining experience.

Name: Gallo Nero
Description: Just a short distance from Campo, at the boundary of the Leocorno contrada, the restaurant settles at the foot of a medieval tower: a thirteenth-century structure that once served as an armoury and which today, following a careful restoration, receives its guests in surroundings enriched by design furnishings from the 1950s and 1970s. It is here that the gastronomic offering of the Gallo Nero takes shape, with a cuisine that celebrates the Sienese tradition through meat dishes firmly rooted in the territory, set alongside vegetable creations and forays towards the sea. The cellar, nestled within an evocative Etruscan grotto carved from tufa, holds some 300 labels: a treasure conceived to accompany the journey through flavour.

Name: Gardenia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Even if you’re not a local, you’ll feel at home in this old property which offers a glimpse of the Piedmont of old. In this 19C building, with a typical balcony running along the inner courtyard, the atmosphere continues into the dining room and, of course, via the dishes on the menu. Here, regional cuisine is celebrated to the full, so you’ll find lots of meat (although some fish options are also available), accompanied by a carefully selected choice of vegetables, some grown in the restaurant’s own garden.

Name: Gasthaus Lamm
Address: Via del Villaggio 36, Saint Martin in Passeier, 39010, Italy
Description: In the historic center of this small yet charming village, you’ll find a trattoria that has been in operation since 1777. Today, under the current family management, the wood-paneled dining rooms evoke the warm, traditional Tyrolean atmosphere, mirrored by a kitchen that turns out an enticing lineup of local specialties. Lamb, an homage to the restaurant’s name, goat, trout from Val Passiria, beef from Val Sarentino, and of course speck, strudel, and more, all executed at a high level.

Name: Gasthofstube Stafler
Description: This restaurant situated in the splendid Stafler hotel on the road to Austria is perfect for a romantic dinner, with a comfortable Stube-style dining room and an internal garden for fine weather. Friendly and welcoming staff and traditional Tyrolean cuisine with a focus on ingredients from the Isarco valley, plus interesting personal twists added by the chef.

Name: Gatto Rosso
Description: A small and dependable institution of the city, consolidated over decades of family management that have brought the establishment to its third generation. Fish has always been the speciality, prepared along classical lines and served in comforting recipes such as the seafood salad, various raw preparations, and dishes cooked in the pan or over the grill. Dishes that are only apparently simple, drawing out to the full the freshness and quality of the catch from the Ionian Sea.

Name: Gennaro Amitrano
Description: The large picture windows at this restaurant offer fine views of the Tyrrhenian sea, where the blue of the sea blends with the elegance of the dining room. The view of the bay is truly spectacular, providing the perfect backdrop for a dining experience that is both traditional and innovative. The chef here serves classic dishes alongside Italian specialities reinterpreted with a modern twist, surprising guests with combinations that are bold yet always balanced. A good example is his elegant lemon tartlet served with a caper and pepper powder.

Name: Gennaro Di Pace
Address: Vicolo della Chiesa 8, loc. Perno, Monforte d'Alba, 12065, Italy
Description: The owner-chef’s Calabrian origins are evident on a menu that combines Mediterranean cuisine (including fish and seafood) with Piedmontese specialities and showcases beautifully presented dishes prepared using contemporary techniques. This small modern restaurant situated near Perno castle is also open at lunchtime (by prior reservation only).

Name: Giano
Description: Enjoying a privileged location close to via Vittorio Veneto and in a quiet corner within the modern W hotel – with which it shares a welcoming cocktail bar and well-tended garden – Giano offers a contemporary concept: informal at lunch, with simple, straightforward dishes, and more gourmet in the evening, when the offering broadens and becomes more refined. The cooking, led by the chef with the support of Ciccio Sultano’s experience (two-starred Duomo in Ragusa), reflects a clear Mediterranean and island identity, with echoes of Sicilian traditions reinterpreted in a modern key. Among the recommended specialities are the iconic spaghetti taratatà (tuna and bottarga), caponata and carpacci, expression of a cuisine with clean, satisfying flavours. The desserts also deserve attention: the classic ricotta cannolo refreshed with a prickly pear consommé and the more creative Banana Mirage reveal accomplished and indulgent pastry work. A contemporary homage to Sicily, completed by attentive and professional service that contributes to making the experience harmonious from start to finish.

Name: Giardinetto
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Set on the shores of the lake within the elegant hotel of the same name – now approaching its centenary after careful renovations – this restaurant boasts splendid views that extend as far as the Island of San Giulio. The cuisine is Mediterranean (try the beef bavette with red and yellow pepper sauce), with the occasional imaginative flourish (such as Carnaroli risotto with basil, black lemon, and purple shrimp). For an aperitif or after-dinner drink, a stop at the Roof Top Bar is recommended. In addition to cocktails, the wine cellar is also well stocked.

Name: Giardino di Mari
Description: Among the finest seafood restaurants in the area, it enjoys a privileged position directly on the Viareggio promenade, a few steps from the sea, with an outdoor terrace particularly pleasant to enjoy during the warmer months. In the kitchen is a chef of undoubted talent, capable of ensuring raw materials of exceptional quality combined with sound, personal technique. Among the signature dishes stand out the octopus alla plancia with panissa and tomato chutney, as well as the salt cod in breadstick crust accompanied by chickpea cream and sautéed cavolo nero. In the dining room, courtesy and professionalism are very much in evidence, supported by an extensive and well-chosen wine list, rich in interesting labels.

Name: Gibas
Description: Still within the municipality of Pesaro, yet perched on a headland immersed in greenery and close to the sea, all the more appealing when dining outdoors, with beach umbrellas providing shade and a breathtaking view as the backdrop. The menu offers a range of classic Adriatic seafood dishes for a thoroughly appetising experience in an enchanting setting.

Name: Giglio
Description: Housed in a beautiful 18C palazzo, Giglio boasts a superb location in one of the many squares in Lucca’s charming historic centre, as well as a delightful outdoor space. The meat and fish dishes on the menu here are inspired by traditional Italian recipes and reinterpreted with a light modern touch – a good example is the siphoned potato which is sprinkled with bottarga and served with a squid sauce, chanterelle mushrooms and spicy parsley cream. The bread is always excellent.

Name: Gimmi Restaurant
Address: Via San Pietro in Lama 23, Lecce, 73100, Italy
Description: The building is a former Dominican monastery dating back to 1442, which also houses a boutique hotel. The restaurant, on the other hand, is decidedly modern and furnished in a minimalist style: light-coloured floors, mighty stone columns, vaulted ceilings and a room with a view of the wine cabinet. The service is very efficient, attentive and friendly, and the cuisine reaches high levels. Among the most recommended specialities are palamita with fennel tarallo, burrata, salad, bell pepper extract, tarragon oil, and among the main courses the grilled snapper, its extract with saffron pistils, artichoke and provolone mousse.

Name: Gina casa con cucina
Address: Via Croce di Città 25, Aosta, 11100, Italy
Description: This restaurant in the old town has a simple and informal feel, with two rooms in the basement built between the Roman walls of Aosta. The quality of the cuisine here is remarkable – the menu features dishes inspired by local traditions, alongside a selection of modern and personalised Italian dishes (including meat options).

Name: Ginevra
Address: Rupi di via XXIX Settembre 12, Ancona, 60122, Italy
Description: Situated on the fourth floor of the Seeport hotel, this restaurant boasts a summer roof garden offering stunning sea views. The chef, a native of Ancona who trained with Gualtiero Marchesi, serves traditional local dishes prepared using ingredients from the region, as well as remaining open to the rest of the world (just like his town and its port). Lighter fare is available at the Seeport Bistrò.

Name: Gino Sorbillo
Description: In the heart of Spaccanapoli, on the famous “via della pizza”, an institution with an international feel welcomes guests into simple, rustic surroundings steeped in authentic Neapolitan energy. The choice of pizzas, enriched with excellent P.D.O. ingredients, is endless. You'll need to be patient during peak hours and, if you happen to find yourself sharing a table, embrace the magic of Neapolitan friendliness!

Name: GioEle
Description: In the heart of the town, guests are received with professionalism and gracious warmth in a lively setting, carefully considered in its details and characterised by a measured elegance. The gastronomic offering moves within the tradition, reinterpreted with a contemporary sensitivity, alternating between dishes from the land and the sea. With the arrival of the warmer months, the experience is further enriched by tables set out in the pleasant internal courtyard or on the terrace, ideal for savouring the atmosphere to the full.

Name: Già Sotto l'Arco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: A historic gourmet restaurant, with an equally historic setting on the first floor of a Baroque palazzo fronting an elegant piazza. A fine staircase leads up to the simple yet stylish dining room, which is skilfully run by a father and his offspring. In the kitchen, his wife Teresa prepares creative, regional cuisine, which is showcased on a surprise menu of four, six or eight courses and which features locally sourced meat and fish. If you’d like to book the delightful table on the small terrace for just two fortunate guests, make sure you do so well in advance!

Name: Gnocchetto
Description: This long-established family-run restaurant (opened in 1926) with an updated contemporary decor continues to serve cuisine that is classic and generous in style yet adapted to modern tastes. Individual dishes take pride of place on the menu at lunchtime, although you can also order from the À la carte if you wish. There’s also an outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Gong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: East meets West in a harmonious fusion of flavours at this restaurant, which takes its name from the imposing gongs dotted around the modern, elegant dining room. The attentive and thoughtful staff are always on hand to explain the different dishes, which are influenced by Chinese traditions yet often have an innovative feel. Beautiful presentation and carefully chosen ingredients typify the contemporary international flavour of this type of cuisine, with an extensive and varied selection of dishes on the à la carte and various tasting menus. One of the latter is dedicated to Peking duck, the restaurant’s signature dish.

Name: Granoturco Bistrot
Description: Although the external façade of this restaurant recalls its former life as a pub, the building is now home to a restaurant run by a young chef whose experience working abroad has done nothing to dim his love of the Piedmont. Here, he serves some of the best regional cuisine in the area, with a few more creative options also featuring on the menu.

Name: Gries 13
Description: Just outside the historic centre, in a quiet residential area, this modern bistro with the feel of a wine bar is definitely worth a detour. In a welcoming and informal setting, a versatile culinary offering takes shape, moving effortlessly between dishes from the sea and the land: from gnocchetti with veal ragù and chanterelle mushrooms to Gargano oysters, right through to carpaccio of salted beef with burrata and melon. An eclectic and skilfully executed cuisine, complemented by a carefully curated selection of wines and service characterised by great warmth. In the warmer months, the lovely outdoor seating area with views of the mountains adds further charm to the experience.

Name: Gunè San Frediano
Address: Via del Drago d'Oro 1r, Florence, 50124, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: It takes its name from the ancient Greek word for ‘woman’ and pays tribute to the feminine world, which is also evoked by the portraits of icons such as Sophia Loren and Amy Winehouse that adorn the walls. In the heart of San Frediano, the owner – originally from Basilicata but now a Tuscan by adoption – works alongside his team to offer a refined, contemporary cuisine, inspired by Mediterranean tradition and centred on ingredients from land and sea, with frequent forays into the world of vegetables. To round off the experience, there is a carefully curated selection of wines and a range of cocktails that benefits from the synergy with the adjacent Next Door, a cocktail bar and bistro under the same ownership.

Name: Gustificio
Address: Via Guglielmo Marconi 52, Carmignano di Brenta, 35010, Italy
Description: An inn fragrant with freshly baked pastries, but above all a restaurant brimming with energy, where the glow of the charcoal grill caresses prime cuts of meat, the undisputed stars of the kitchen. Andrea Poli, chef-owner, celebrates product and season with playful dishes and authentic flavors, while embracing contemporary forays such as the irresistible “grilled radicchio gnocchetti, draped in béchamel, red wine sauce, and crispy hazelnuts.” On Wednesdays, a small selection of gourmet pizzas adds an unexpected twist to the experience.

Name: Gustoo
Description: Located in the heart of the town, this long-established venue has been reinterpreted with a contemporary touch in its hospitality and service spaces. The kitchen presents a rich selection of raw seafood preparations, complemented by abundant and vibrant dishes, where the interplay of multiple ingredients gives rise to consistently aromatic and seductive preparations. At lunch, the Menu of the Day simplifies selection without compromising on quality, while the service – entirely female – accompanies the experience with attentiveness, grace and proven professionalism.

Name: Hanswirt
Description: Occupying a former post-house, this restaurant boasts dining rooms decorated in Tyrolean style, as well as a large veranda-style room. Although the focus here is on local ingredients (especially vegetables and meat such as goat kid and lamb raised on the restaurant’s own farm in the Senales valley) and freshwater fish, the menu also features the occasional Mediterranean speciality, such as the excellent braised aubergine tartare with burrata, focaccia and basil-flavoured olive oil. There’s also a hotel of the same name, which is housed in an attractive old building to the rear of the restaurant.

Name: Hazama
Description: Japanese cuisine in a small restaurant with a minimalist mood echoed in its cooking. Here, young chef Satoshi Hazama offers – in addition to the à la carte menu – a 7‑course Kaiseki journey or a 4‑course tasting menu. Kaiseki cuisine employs five fundamental techniques applied to seasonal ingredients: raw, grilled, fried, boiled, and steamed, in a crescendo of intensity that showcases Japanese haute cuisine (advance reservation required).

Name: Henri Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Having returned to his native Viareggio in 2021, Henri Prosperi, a gracious maître in the old-school tradition, will guide you with style and professionalism in choosing dishes that blend classic and modern approaches, with a penchant for some French influences. The menu, divided between meat and fish, always focuses on premium ingredients, the same character that distinguishes the wine cellar, rich with great national and international labels, from Sassicaia to Petrus, including the finest Italian and French sparkling wines. An open kitchen and outdoor seating!

Name: Hidalgo
Description: Although fish dishes also feature on the menu, Hidalgo has long enjoyed a reputation for its excellent meat options thanks to its different cuts of steak and beef sourced from all around the world and cooked mainly (but not exclusively) on the barbecue grill. In a separate room(Aomi, a kind of restaurant within the restaurant), guests can choose from a menu dedicated uniquely (from antipasti to main courses) to Japanese Wagyubeef.

Name: Hostaria Baccofurore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Patience is needed to get to this restaurant from the coast, as a result of the winding road which makes its way through small villages, but once here the view of the sea is breathtaking. The village of Furore is built alongside the road and is famous for the Marisa Cuomo winery situated opposite the restaurant. The cuisine is as impressive as the vista, with its focus on different local ingredients cooked with a mix of traditional influence and imagination. Comfortable guestrooms are also available, almost all of which have been recently renovated and boast impressive views.

Name: Hostaria alla Tavernetta
Address: Via Artico di Prampero 2, Udine, 33100, Italy
Description: A venue that welcomes warmly, thanks to a lively, family atmosphere. A lit fireplace fills the air with the scent of burning wood, while wooden furnishings and linen runners blend with background music to create a relaxing setting. At the table, authentic flavors: from Friulian frico with Montasio and potatoes to plum gnocchi cloaked in clarified butter and cinnamon, to succulent goose leg. Mediterranean forays also appear, such as the tuna tataki with anchovy sauce and bottarga. For those who wish, a carefully crafted vegan menu is also available.

Name: Hostaria da Franz
Address: Salizada Sant'Antonin, sestiere Castello 3499, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: Founded in a different venue by an Austrian soldier in the late 19C, this historic Venetian restaurant is now run by owner Maurizio, who oversees the front of house in a courteous yet friendly manner. He introduces guests to its variety of dishes, which aim to please rather than surprise. Fish specialities are to the fore here.

Name: Hostaria dai Musi
Description: Offering a limited à la carte that includes fish dishes (including raw options) which vary according to market availability, this restaurant serves what it describes as “typically modern cuisine”. The breaded and fried anchovies with a typical saor sauce and lemon gel are particularly good, plus the menu features a selection of typical regional specialities. The pleasant setting is enhanced by the backdrop of the large central square in a pedestrianised area on the edge of the old town. The drinks menu includes an excellent selection of wines, plus a good choice of local beers.

Name: Hostaria del Pavone
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: A small gem for fish enthusiasts, this delightful restaurant situated amid the alleyways of the historic centre (just 2 minutes’ walk away) boasts a quiet ambience with a white colour scheme and minimalist decor chosen by the exuberant owner. Although the menu focuses on fish and seafood (the raw fish dishes are superb), the pasta dishes and main courses are also excellent. To round off a delightful dining experience, the wine list includes some surprising top-quality labels. A must!

Name: Hostaria del Teatro
Address: Via Ordanino 5b, Castiglione delle Stiviere, 46043, Italy
Description: In the heart of the small town, within a rustic building enriched by refined interiors and an atmosphere that is at once warm and homey, the cooking distinguishes itself through a carefully considered and territorially inspired offering, with one dish that is most certainly worth tasting: the unmissable duck agnolini with their jus and black truffle, an authentic signature of the house.

Name: Hostaria del Vicolo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in a central yet secluded location, this intimate and elegant restaurant serves typical Sicilian cuisine with a focus on fish, vegetables from the kitchen garden and delicious cheeses. A good wine selection completes the picture.

Name: Hosteria Giusti
Description: Hidden away in the back room of the historic Giusti delicatessen, which has been famous for over four centuries, is a small dining room with just four tables. Simple and pleasantly retro, this is th perfct place to soak up the authentic spirit of Modena’s culinary tradition. The menu is a sincere tribute to Emilian cuisine: it begins with charcuterie, mostly from Mora Romagnola pigs reared in the wild, accompanied by the ever-present gnocco fritto and fragrant pasta fritters.This is followed by fresh pasta, the star of iconic dishes such as tortellini in capon broth and tagliolini with cheese and walnuts, before moving on to slow-cooked meats, including the outstanding beef stew with mashed potatoes and the traditional recipe for fried cotechino with Sorbara zabaione, a precious tribute from the Morandi family. The desserts are simple yet delicious and include panna cotta with saba (grape syrup), a perfect blend of tradition and simplicity.All that’s left is to wish you “buon appetito”.

Name: Hosteria La Cave Cantù
Description: Situated within the 18C Cantù monastery, now also home to a museum and library, this modern restaurant with a friendly ambience in its dining rooms and wine cellar also boasts an attractive outdoor space and a convenient car park. The menu features personalised cuisine with the occasional exotic influence prepared by the owner-chef (his wife, who works front of house and oversees the excellent wine list, is from Ecuador). The result is colourful, generous and beautifully presented cuisine which is full of flavour.

Name: Hosteria Toblino
Address: Via Garda 3, Sarche di Madruzzo, 38070, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The most welcoming section of the extensive Cantina Toblino complex is home to the large, contemporary and minimalist-style Hosteria. Here, a young chef serves simple reinterpretations of regional dishes with a focus on zero-mile produce with the occasional yet astute use of ingredients from further afield.

Name: Hosteria del Platano
Description: Situated on the main road overlooking the lake, this pleasant family-run restaurant serves excellent traditional cuisine with a focus on local fish. Atmospheric dining room with stone walls and vaulted ceilings, plus an attractive outdoor space, and friendly, attentive owners.

Name: Hydra
Description: Situated in the picturesque historic centre of Salerno, this is one of the city’s best restaurants. The dining room here is almost minimalist in style, yet thanks to the soft lighting and beautiful background music it has a pleasing atmosphere; in fine weather, tables are set out in a charming inner courtyard. The cuisine is Mediterranean and contemporary, with a selection of light and creative meat, fish and vegetable dishes featuring on the menu.

Name: I 5 Campanili
Address: Via Luigi Maino 18, Busto Arsizio, 21052, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Contemporary cooking with an emphasis on Mediterranean fare in tune with the seasons is to the fore in this elegant restaurant occupying a 20C building with an attractive veranda to the rear. Fish takes pride of place on the menu, with a particular focus on raw dishes and shellfish, but the splendid desserts are also worthy of note, such as cherries in sour cherry juice with fior di latte ice cream.

Name: I 5 Sensi
Description: The whole family (mother and four children) is involved in the running of this restaurant, both front of house and in the kitchen. If you’re looking for top-quality cuisine which focuses on local ingredients yet is also creative and innovative, then this is the place for you! Classic-style dining room with the occasional modern decorative touch, plus a well-stocked wine cellar offering a selection of 700 labels.

Name: I Banchi
Description: Housed in a palazzo full of history – the building was a synagogue before the 1693 earthquake and has retained its ritual bath in its charming room of mirrors – this restaurant bears the imprint of renowned chef Ciccio Sultano, holder of two Michelin stars at the nearby Duomo restaurant. The cuisine is eclectic yet with a Sicilian focus, plus the wine list is complemented by a choice of interesting cocktails.

Name: I Carracci
Description: Within the luxurious Grand Hotel Majestic, though with its own independent entrance, the restaurant welcomes guests into a dining room of great impact, presided over by a spectacular ceiling frescoed in the seventeenth century by the school of the Carracci. An ideal setting for special occasions, which finds further expression in the cuisine of chef Agostino Schettino. Originally from Castellammare di Stabia, the chef weaves Emilian and Neapolitan influences into his offering: emblematic in this regard is the tasting menu “La Dotta, La Grassa, La Rossa”, an homage to Bolognese tradition. More generally, his is a contemporary Mediterranean cuisine, balanced with confidence between sea – as in the sea bass with charred lettuce, almond, oyster and caviar – and land, with dishes such as the lamb accompanied by scorzonera and marinated red onion. For the pairings, alongside the expertise of the sommelier, a well-considered cocktail offering distinguishes itself as an original complement to the wine list.

Name: I Due Cippi dal 1976
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Upon entering, guests are welcomed by an evocative crackling fireplace, beside which aged meat is cooked to perfection. The varieties offered come from the world’s finest regions and sustainable farms, including prized wagyu. Chianina naturally takes center stage, but the menu extends to game as well, offering a wide range of authentic flavors. The elegant dining rooms, which have gained charm and refinement over the years, are the result of management that began in the 1970s and is now more vibrant than ever. A warm atmosphere, attentive service, and a selection of prestigious labels complete the gastronomic experience. During the warmer months, outdoor seating is also available.

Name: I Giardini dei Rodo
Address: Via Bonomo Alto - Scauri, Pantelleria, 91017, Italy
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant’s guests can enjoy their meal surrounded by verdant gardens, which are planted with palms, flowers and citrus trees. Regional flavours take centre-stage in the modern dishes in this romantic and original setting.

Name: I Mori
Description: This is the classic spot to recommend to anyone who wants fish prepared simply and traditionally, with no frills, just top-quality seafood that the friendly owner personally sources. The menu is supplemented by spoken specials based on that day’s fish-market finds, but among the mains we suggest you don’t miss the charcoal-grilled dishes.

Name: I Pifferi
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This restaurant occupying an old post house that dates back to the time of Marie Louise, Duchess of Parma, lies amid the verdant landscapes of the Parco Regionale dei Boschi di Carrega, just a kilometre outside the village of Sala Baganza. This stunning setting is the backdrop for typical dishes from Parma, such as Nonna Lina’s herb tortelli served with melted butter and parmesan cheese. In summer, dine alfresco in the cool, shady garden.

Name: I Rodella
Address: strada esterna vicinale della Rocca 2, Deruta, 06053, Italy
Description: Housed in an early 17th-century building that once served as a coaching inn for travellers bound for Rome, this elegant relais also comprises six rooms and two superior rooms with a mezzanine. At the helm of the establishment is a family originally from Veneto: the twin brothers Stefano and Andrea run the kitchen, while Samuele professionally oversees the hospitality and wine service. The culinary offering unfolds through two tasting menus: Elemento, closely linked to the local area and the seasons, and Identità, the embodiment of the chefs’ creative vision. The result is a contemporary and personal style of cooking, based on local produce, aromatic herbs and solid technical expertise.

Name: I Salotti
Address: Località Querce al Pino, SS 146, Chiusi, 53043, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In summer, the outdoor spaces at this restaurant, such as the garden gazebo, are the perfect setting for a candlelit dinner in total harmony with nature, while in winter, the elegant dining room with just a few tables (book well in advance) really comes into its own. Creative cuisine prepared using produce from the restaurant’s own farm, plus a long-established wine cellar that has been extended over the years so that it now boasts over two thousand different labels from the region and elsewhere in Italy, many of them of the highest quality.

Name: I Savi
Address: Via Spangaro 6, località Peseggia di Scorzè, Scorzè, 30037, Italy
Description: Situated in a small rural hamlet, this restaurant is one of the best in the Venetian hinterland for top-quality fish. Served in welcoming dining rooms, the fish and seafood dishes here are traditional and unfussy in style, and full of natural flavour.

Name: I Sette Consoli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In this simple restaurant boasting an attractive outdoor summer garden and splendid views of the Duomo, chef Anna Rita focuses on carefully selected ingredients from the region and beyond. Highlights include soft egg, pan-fried courgettes and spring onions, and pecorino crumble, as well as soft veal rump, Jerusalem artichoke sauce and home-made pickled vegetables. The wine and spirits selection is particularly appealing – as an example, the Orvieto Classico Superiore Doc “Vendemmia Tardiva” is the perfect pairing for your dessert.

Name: I Tigli
Description: An iconic pizzeria which has brought Italy’s favourite street-food snack right up to date! With almost 30 years’ experience behind him, Simone Padoan knows how to make difficult things easy: he uses a mix of wholemeal flours and pays meticulous attention to natural leavening processes to create a dough which has a crispy crust yet soft interior. He also focuses on different types of toppings, including fish, meat and vegetables – whether your preference is for traditional or more imaginative pizzas, every option is of the highest quality. A choice of excellent desserts provides the perfect conclusion to your meal!

Name: Ichikawa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: Ichikawa is one of the culinary masters who played a part in introducing Japanese cuisine to Italy. After decades in the country working in various restaurants, this chef has finally opened his own eatery, where he serves top-quality Japanese cuisine ranging from familiar favourites such as sushi and sashimi to other less-known family dishes and street food from the land of the Rising Sun. A good place to discover the joys of Japanese cuisine!

Name: Il Baretto
Description: Il Baretto on the outskirts of Padova is a must for anyone who loves classic, traditional fish and seafood, thanks to its menu which includes a number of typical Venetian dishes. The top-quality fish is skilfully prepared to bring out its full flavour and distinctive characteristics, providing a real treat for the tastebuds in this inland temple to the sea.

Name: Il Barolino
Description: The Emilian authenticity of the Barolo brothers and their team fills the air with smiles and warmth, making every visit to this simple and welcoming restaurant a pleasure, the perfect place to enjoy the company of friends or colleagues. The menu is steeped in tradition: it is impossible to resist their pasta dishes, such as the creamy and satisfying “gramigna sporcafaccia” or tortellini covered in a velvety smooth Parmesan cream sauce. Desserts include a crunchy “sbrisolona” cake served with zabaglione made with passito wine, while the “zuppa inglese” trifle releases deliciously smooth notes to end the meal on a sweet note.

Name: Il Basilisco
Description: A simple, cosy restaurant with a single dining room and just a few tables, situated on the outskirts of Treviso, whose main attraction lies in its cuisine. The menu strikes a fine balance between meat and fish, blending contemporary flavours with nods to the culinary traditions of the Veneto region. An authentic and well-executed menu, offering a delightful gourmet experience off the beaten track.

Name: Il Bikini
Address: SS 145 Sorrentina km 13,900, Vico Equense, 80069, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: For over 70 years, the elegant Il Bikini restaurant has been soaking up the sun in this superb location facing the spectacular Bay of Naples. Now home to a new and exuberant chef, the restaurant serves classic fish cuisine with a contemporary twist at lunchtime under the name Locanda di Mare, while in the evening the restaurant transforms into L’Atollo, a more elegant, fine-dining venue. Ever since the restaurant was opened in 1952, the panoramic terrace here has been one of the best places in the region in which to enjoy good food and spectacular sea views.

Name: Il Cairoli
Description: As is suggested by the use of the definite article before its name, Il Cairoli is a modern hotel restaurant with its own entrance. The menu here features classic Milanese specialities such as mondeghili meatballs, ossobucco risotto and veal cutlets, as well as other delicious and colourful dishes that are contemporary in style and based on the use of seasonal ingredients. There are also a few vegetarian options, as well as daily specials at midday, when a quicker and cheaper lunch option is available. An attractive dining room with large picture windows boasting views (albeit partial) of the Sforza castle adds to the appeal.

Name: Il Calandrino
Address: Via Liguria 1, loc. Sarmeola, Rubano, 35030, Italy
Description: Situated next to the three-Michelin-starred Le Calandre (and run by the same family), Il Calandrino is an elegant and eclectic restaurant which includes a bar-cum-pasticceria that is well worth visiting at any time of day. The cuisine here ranges from creative dishes such as scallops with toasted leek cream, sea urchins and cima di rapa, to classic house favourites such as Erminio’s legendary beef tartare with toasted bread and salad greens, and Rita’s pazientina (chocolate layer cake) served with zabaglione.

Name: Il Capestrano
Address: Via Gian Francesco Pizzi 14, Milan, 20141, Italy
Description: This restaurant takes its name from the warrior statue dating back to the 6C BC which was discovered in Capestrano (Aquila province) in 1934. The statue, carved from a single block of local stone, is one of the most mysterious finds in history. No such mystery surrounds the dishes served in this restaurant, which focuses on cuisine from the Abruzzo, including top-quality hams and cheeses produced by small-scale producers, as well as mutton, lamb, beef, barbecued lamb kebabs and other culinary delights.

Name: Il Capriolino
Address: Via Nazionale 108, Vodo di Cadore, 32040, Italy
Description: This elegant restaurant has been run by the same family for years and has a history dating back over two centuries. It serves regional yet creative cuisine and has a distinctly Middle European ambience with its hunting trophies, clocks and frescoes.

Name: Il Carpaccio
Description: This traditional family restaurant has been recently renovated to include an attractive veranda - style dining room overlooking the valley. Typical dishes from Calabria, fish specialities by prior arrangement, and a good wine list all add to the appeal.

Name: Il Cascinalenuovo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Having been under the watchful eye of chef Walter Ferretto for decades, Il Cascinalenuovo serves classic, seasonal cuisine which celebrates local traditions in a glorious array of Piedmontese dishes, such as the region’s famous plin (filled pasta) served in a napkin or with a roast meat sauce, tongue millefeuille and pigeon. The menu also includes more contemporary-style recipes such as the “artichoke and artichoke” dish or the lightly fried catch of the day, while the extensive and carefully curated wine list focuses largely on Piedmont. In fine weather, book a table in the attractive outdoor space overlooking the garden and swimming pool. The restaurant also offers romantic guestrooms, which are ideal for a relaxing stay.

Name: Il Cavallo Scosso
Description: A young and modern restaurant situated in a residential area about 2km from the centre, where owner-chef Enrico Pivieri offers a menu that is equally divided between traditional meat-based dishes from Piedmont (some, such as the plin pasta, are very traditional in style while others have a more reinterpreted feel) and more creative fish-based options. The chef gives full rein to his creativity in dishes such as the Mediterranean fish ceviche with avocado, passion fruit gel and sea-urchin mayonnaise.

Name: Il Chiosco di Bacco
Description: This restaurant boasts a rural location in the Montefeltro region, to which half the menu is dedicated (fresh home-made pastas, salumi, porchetta-style rabbit etc). The other half focuses on meat dishes, with an interesting selection of steaks and ribs from Italian and Scottish breeds (including more expensive beef that has been left to age for a month). You’ll find the perfect wine pairing on the excellent wine list.

Name: Il Cigno
Description: Adjacent to the historic center, this elegant and refined restaurant occupies an evocative sixteenth-century building that preserves a timeless charm. The talented and creative chef presents a contemporary cuisine that alternates meat and fish dishes with balance, playing with modern techniques and touches of imagination. The “amberjack sashimi with almond cream, raspberry, and puffed quinoa” is a small opening of pure finesse, while concluding with their excellent desserts is nearly obligatory. In fine weather, it is worth reserving a table on the evocative terrace, arranged around a captivating fifteenth-century well.

Name: Il Cipresso - Da Cioni
Address: Via Alcide De Gasperi 28, Loro Ciuffenna, 52024, Italy
Description: Standing on a round terrace, this restaurant with a fairly plain interior serves dishes made from some of the best produce of the region – cured hams, bread, pasta and famous Tuscan meats. The restaurant also offers simple, rustic - style guestrooms.

Name: Il Colmetto
Description: A true gourmet agriturismo, Il Colmetto changes its menu almost week by week in line with the changing seasons. Full of flavour, the ingredients here (many of which are produced on the property, while others are sourced locally) are cooked with precision, avoiding overly fussy and complicated techniques. Instead, the focus is on good, honest cuisine with its roots in peasant traditions, in which the aim is to create comforting dishes that will appeal to the palate. The barbecued specialities, such as the sweetbreads and the excellent Jerusalem artichokes, are particularly delicious, while the superb goats’ milk butter, served soft and fluffy as a cloud with bread and focaccia, is truly delicious – its only drawback is that it can be addictive!

Name: Il Convito della Venaria
Address: Via Andrea Mensa 37/g, Venaria Reale, 10078, Italy
Description: This restaurant is run by an enthusiastic couple, with Lucia front of house in the classic and welcoming dining room and Christian at the helm in the kitchen. The menu is lighter (and less expensive) at lunchtime with a wider choice of regional and Italian fare in the evening, plus a few more creative options, including fish dishes. Comfortable guestrooms are also available, two of which have views of the royal palace.

Name: Il Cortiletto
Description: Standing on the Lake Garda road, this small, simple, yet far from ordinary restaurant serves Mediterranean dishes with the occasional inventive twist. Two words of advice – opt for alfresco dining in fine weather, and don’t miss the maccheroncini served with perch and lemon pesto sauce.

Name: Il Credenziere
Address: Via Quattro Strade 12, Annone Veneto, 30020, Italy
Description: A restaurant with a pleasant, contemporary atmosphere; although it does offer a few meat dishes, its reputation – which is certainly well-deserved – is based on its fish. Excellent dishes – hearty and full of flavour – often with a Mediterranean twist.

Name: Il Cugnolo
Address: Contrada Cugnolo 19, Torre di Palme, 63900, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This gourmet restaurant housed in a restored period residence that once belonged to the counts of Adami is surrounded by the green maquis and hills of the Marche, with the sea visible in the distance just a few miles away. Here, the young Neapolitan chef creates cuisine that is surprising for its attractive, clean lines, providing a real explosion of flavours and a tribute to the region and the Mediterranean in general. The restaurant also owns a nearby agricultural estate which provides many of the wines and olive oils served during tastings.

Name: Il Doretto
Description: Housed in an attractive farmhouse, this restaurant serves seasonal cuisine that includes delicious fish and seafood (raw dishes as well as more elaborate options), alongside meat dishes, including some delicious game recipes.

Name: Il Faggio
Description: In the building that once housed the Workers’ Mutual Aid Society, there now unfolds an elegant dining room, with large windows and classic furnishings, wrapped in a comfortable atmosphere that feels almost suspended in time. While the setting evokes an elegance of another era, the kitchen moves along calmly modern lines, with a clearly recognisable Mediterranean imprint. The menu alternates with balance between seafood dishes – such as amberjack marinated with curry, coconut and beetroot – and meat-based proposals, among which the partridge cooked on the bone with smoked parsnip, a date stuffed with its livers and mustard sauce stands out: careful, readable preparations with real personality. Completing the experience is a particularly extensive wine list, with a solid Piedmontese presence alongside labels from across the Italian peninsula, as well as France and other interesting international forays.

Name: Il Favri
Address: Via Borgo Meduna 12, San Giorgio della Richinvelda, 33095, Italy
Description: Warm and welcoming, with an atmosphere that evokes the most authentic Friulian tradition, this historic tavern has been a favourite haunt for lovers of good food for over a century and a half. The current management is carrying on an important legacy, which is enhanced during the warmer months by a lovely garden. The kitchen features authentic, skilfully prepared dishes that showcase the region through great classics such as prosciutto crudo, frico with polenta and orzotto, while also including some timeless favourites from Italian tradition. Meat remains the star of the show, but it is the full range of regional specialities that gives the experience its character.

Name: Il Fico trentacareghe
Description: Along one of the region's most scenic coastal routes, fronted by a charming olive garden, and within a petite hotel yet operating independently, the vista stands as a restaurant's focal strength, appreciated from some dining area tables and further still from the summer terrace. The cuisine, however, doesn’t fall short: two tasting menus and a seafood-focused menu rooted in local traditions with a flourish of creativity bear the kitchen’s signature.

Name: Il Focarile
Address: Via Pontina al km 46,5, Aprilia, 04011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The sumptuous entrance gives an elegant tone to a large bright dining room with well spaced out tables; a touch of Tuscany with a cuisine rich in tradition and also imagination. Now offers new, elegant rooms.

Name: Il Frantoio
Address: Via del Castello 40, Colle di Val d'Elsa, 53034, Italy
Description: The 19C millstone, press and cisterns can still be seen in the dining room at this restaurant, bearing witness to its past as an olive oil mill. Situated in spectacular Colle di Val d’Elsa, Il Frantoio boasts old stone and brick walls and vaulted ceilings, as well as tables set out in the piazza for summer dining. Although the setting suggests simple and rustic cuisine, the chef surprises guests with top-quality dishes which are technical and often highly creative, such as liver with sour cherries and pistachios, and smoked spaghetti with an anchovy sauce, capers and black garlic cream.

Name: Il Frate
Description: In 2025, this restaurant celebrates a century of existence, as a veritable treasure trove of history that has preserved its family soul intact. Today, the kitchen is run by Lorenza, heir to a tradition that smells of Emilia and Piacenza, the same tradition lovingly preserved by her mother. The dishes arrive at the table generous and steaming, with classic flavours that seduce the eye and the palate. The wine list, which is now digital, boasts around 350 labels: the treasures of Northern Italy prevail, but there are also international notes. For the perfect pairing, let yourself be guided by Giorgio, the fourth generation of the family in the dining room. With grace and expertise, he will transform every sip into a harmonious accompaniment to your dish.

Name: Il Funghetto
Address: Strada Litoranea 11412, località Borgo Grappa, Latina, 04010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu at this restaurant just a few minutes’ drive from the beach. The owner-chef (the second generation since 1973) is happy to advise guests on food and wine choices alike, offering a wide choice of wines from all over Italy and around the world. Welcoming dining room and shady arbour. Gluten-free options available.

Name: Il Galeone
Description: In a bright, elegant and modern dining room inside the Elisabeth Due hotel, Galeone is one of the city's finest gastronomic destinations. The menu focuses on fish, with dishes that draw on local traditions, such as “brodetto alla fanese” fish soup (available by advance order), alongside more creative offerings.

Name: Il Giardinetto
Address: Piazza Giuseppe Garibaldi 10, Mandello del Lario, 23826, Italy
Description: Looking out over the calm blue water, this classic restaurant serves traditional cuisine with the occasional imaginative twist. Fish from the lake feature on the menu, as do meat and seafood options with something for everyone. There’s also a small outdoor terrace where guests can enjoy a pre- or post-dinner drink.

Name: Il Giardino "Da Felicin"
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: A bastion of the most authentic Piedmontese tradition, the restaurant is located in a refined period building, enhanced by a panoramic terrace and a romantic garden that invites guests to dine al fresco in the summer months. The dining rooms reflect the same vocation for traditional, rich and welcoming elegance, which reaches its fullest expression in the dishes: impeccable interpretations of the region’s finest cuisine. The restaurant’s signature dish is the famous Tajarin di Felicin, handmade tagliatelle cut into very fine strands and served with a delicate Fassona beef sauce, a true declaration of love for local gastronomy. The property also comprises a scattered hotel, with rooms located both in the main building and in other parts of the village, including the charming Palazzo Boeri, which has a small spa accessible by reservation. The owners know the area intimately and are delighted to accompany guests on guided tours of the Langhe, organised by themselves or by local experts, making the stay a complete experience encompassing cuisine, hospitality and local culture.

Name: Il Giardino del Gusto
Description: In the most evocative heart of Ventimiglia, the restaurant looks out over a graceful pedestrian square where, in the warmer months, a small outdoor area welcomes guests to the slow rhythm of the old town. Inside, the intimate dining room, with its classic décor, exudes a discreet warmth, made up of traditional details and an atmosphere that invites guests to linger. The kitchen gives pride of place to the sea, interpreting local produce with respect and creativity, the undisputed star of the menu. Yet there is also a tasting menu dedicated to the vegetable garden, designed to showcase the freshness of Ligurian land, as well as a number of carefully prepared meat dishes that complete a balanced and contemporary gastronomic offering.

Name: Il Giardino delle Esperidi
Description: Whether you choose to dine al fresco in the bustling centre of Bardolino or opt for the more intimate atmosphere of the dining room, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone who appreciates cuisine that prioritises the quality of its ingredients. The menu, available both as a tasting menu and as a concise, well-balanced à la carte selection, focuses primarily on fish from the lake, complemented by a number of interesting meat dishes. Carefully prepared dishes, distinct flavours and a style of cooking that focuses on the essentials without compromising on character.

Name: Il Ginkgo
Description: A restaurant with modern, minimalist dining rooms that houses the creative and gourmet cuisine of young chef Lorenzo Barbieri. A native of Cremona, he serves in his splendid city elaborate and contemporary dishes, both of meat and fish, with few references to local traditions, yet these will appeal to those seeking novelty, echoes of international cuisine and occasionally unexpected flavour pairings.

Name: Il Giurista
Description: This restaurant is named after Bartolo da Sassoferrato (as is the street on which it stands), a distinguished 14C jurist. From the street, you head down a few steps to the welcoming dining rooms with their historic ambience and brick-vaulted ceilings that keep the temperature pleasantly cool. The cuisine, which focuses exclusively on meat, is traditional and regional in flavour – an entire section of the menu is dedicated to black truffles in season. Friendly and attentive service.

Name: Il Grano di Pepe
Description: While you’re trying to decide between the tasting menu and the à la carte at this restaurant, you can tuck into its excellent bread, including the “sfincione” – a type of tomato-flavoured focaccia from Palermo which makes the journey here worthwhile on its own! If fish is your preference, we recommend the “Palermo and Marseille” fish stew, an intense dish full of bold and delicious flavours. Minimalist decor and a friendly welcome from chef Rino Duca complete the picture.

Name: Il Grifone
Address: Via Ca' Masino 611/a - loc. Varignana, Castel San Pietro Terme, 40024, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This fine-dining restaurant housed in the 18C Palazzo Bentivoglio Bargellini is part of the luxurious Palazzo di Varignana resort (with which it shares the Il Grifone symbol), the latter also home to a farm producing olive oil, wine and fruit.
