In the evening, choose between two tasting menus and an à la carte offering a selection of meat and fish dishes on which the modern recipes feature a careful balance of colours and flavours.

Name: Il Grottino
Address: Piazza Beato Ugolino 5, Gualdo Cattaneo, 06035, Italy
Description: Situated in the old medieval village of Gualdo Cattaneo, amid the gentle valleys not far from Foligno, Il Grottino is the perfect choice for anyone keen to sample the authentic flavours of Umbrian cuisine. Here, truffles and zero-km produce take pride of place on the menu, with a particular focus on meat which is carefully cooked on the open-view barbecue grill. Alongside locally sourced produce, you’ll also find a choice of carefully selected Prussian beef. Comfortable and welcoming guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Il Gusto
Description: In the central area, chef Alessio Boldrin has reinvented the Venetian bàcaro tradition. Classic cicchetti here become samples served on one large plate, entertaining the palate. Not to be outdone is the à la carte menu, which offers a wide selection of mouth-watering and satisfying dishes, such as tagliolini cacio, pepe and scampi. The wine list features a good selection of Italian and French bubbly.

Name: Il Gusto di Xinge
Description: The dining room plays on warm brown tones reminiscent of a teapot, enlivened by touches of brilliant blue and modern leather chairs that lend a contemporary edge to the space. The Chinese chef presents authentic cuisine from her homeland – dim sum included – while drawing inspiration from Italian and French culinary traditions, all infused with a decidedly “pop” creative flair. To best begin the experience, consider an artisanal cocktail at nearby DrinX, the perfect prelude to dinner.

Name: Il Labirinto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the outskirts of Brescia, this long-established restaurant has an elegant retro atmosphere. The cuisine is varied with a balance of fish and meat dishes, as well as some excellent home-made salumi.

Name: Il Liberty
Description: Nestled in an Art Nouveau palazzo just a short walk from the dynamic Porta Nuova district, the restaurant offers a warm and refined setting, comprising a bright main dining room, a romantic balcony, a small room with an open‑view kitchen and a convivial social table. Inspired by Mediterranean tradition, the menu weaves together seafood and meat dishes with fine balance: from the “cotto-crudo” veal and mortadella mondeghili with soft potato, light salsa verde and hazelnuts, to the sumptuous thick-cut veal cutlet Milanese, served with fresh potato crisps, homemade ketchup and a delicate honey mustard.

Name: Il Marchese - Osteria Mercato Liquori
Description: Boasting a sumptuous Art Deco setting that contrasts pleasingly with the traditional cuisine served here, this restaurant is the Milanese sibling of Il Marchese in Rome which pays tribute to the famous Italian film “Il Marchese del Grillo” starring Alberto Sordi (it is also the first bar in Europe to offer more than 600 “amaro” liqueurs). The culinary philosophy here is based on traditional Roman cuisine with a contemporary flavour, including delicious specialities such as pasta with carbonara, matriciana and gricia sauces, veal saltimbocca, pork belly and much more besides!

Name: Il Marchese - Osteria Mercato Liquori
Description: Convivial and informal with a touch of elegance, this restaurant is perfect for a night out with friends – and indeed for anyone in the mood for delicious cuisine brimming with flavours which are predominantly Roman in style. The carbonara and amatriciana are superb, while the antipasti (especially the croquettes and artichoke in season) should not be missed. An impressive selection of cocktails completes the picture. Booking is recommended, as it’s often full!

Name: Il Mecenate
Description: Occupying the premises of a historic local laundry along the city “moat”, this authentic trattoria has a friendly, convivial ambience. The menu showcases local dishes to the full, including specialities such as “tordelli lucchesi” (ravioli stuffed with different meats, thyme and nutmeg and always served with a meat ragù), tripe and bread pudding, the original recipe of which dates back to the 18C. A picturesque outdoor terrace facing San Francesco church and an excellent wine selection complete the picture.

Name: Il Melograno
Description: In the village centre and therefore not right by the sea, this successful, well - established restaurant is decorated in elegant contemporary style. The menu focuses on fish dishes reinterpreted with a touch of imagination.

Name: Il Merlo
Address: Viale Sergio Bernardini 660, Lido di Camaiore, 55041, Italy
Description: Situated right on the beach, Il Merlo boasts a welcoming dining room decorated in elegant, contemporary style. The owner is at the helm in the kitchen, where he creates dishes with a focus on fish and seafood, such as the raw seafood platter and the salt-baked catch of the day. A few delicious meat options, such as plin pasta and pigeon, are also available.

Name: Il Michelaccio
Description: A modern bistro in the heart of the city, just a short walk from the famous Via XX Settembre. Here, the chef and owner interprets fragrant, market-fresh cuisine that pays tribute to Ligurian tradition – such as potato cream with Genoese-style sea snails – and embraces Italian flavours, such as pappa al pomodoro with burratina. In addition to the menu, delicious dishes inspired by the market surprise guests every day. Don't miss the “Minestrone alla ligure” soup, served in a small pot: pure goodness! The warm and informal welcome makes everything special.

Name: Il Mirto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: On arriving at the luxurious Hotel Botania, guests are accompanied to the restaurant through a park of over three hectares immersed in the most luxuriant Mediterranean vegetation: the finest possible introduction to the cuisine that awaits at Il Mirto. Here the experience unfolds across two extended tasting menus – with the option of reducing either to four freely chosen courses – one vegetarian and one vegan, with almost all the vegetables sourced from the property’s own kitchen gardens or from cultivation elsewhere on the island. Among the most representative dishes, the signature “Ris8” stands out, interpreting technique and creativity in a contemporary key. The service, too, is excellent – young and spontaneous – contributing to an evening that is a fully immersive experience in nature.

Name: Il Molo
Address: Via Falcone Borsellino 2, San Leone, 92100, Italy
Description: Situated on the seafront facing the small tourist harbour of San Leone, this elegant restaurant boasts an attractive summer terrace with a relaxed ambience. Here you can savour a selection of regional fish and meat dishes prepared by the owner-chef with ingredients of the highest quality.

Name: Il Molo
Address: Via Aganor Pompili 9, Passignano sul Trasimeno, 06065, Italy
Description: Situated in the historic centre of Passignano, where the village seems to jut out into Lake Trasimeno (some tables in the main dining room boast views of the lake – make sure you book in advance), Il Molo has been run by the Pellegrini family since 1978. The restaurant has become a popular choice for guests keen to try top-quality fish from the lake as well as excellent poultry dishes, with dishes showcased on an à la carte and three tasting menus. We highly recommend the herb bottoni pasta with sunfish and saffron butter. There’s also a good choice of sparkling wines and champagnes.

Name: Il Narciso
Description: Housed in the Polda baths near the marina, this recently opened small restaurant on the beach serves cuisine with a contemporary yet classic flavour. The restaurant boasts excellent bread, home-made pasta, traditionally cooked dishes such as chicken casserole and creative desserts. Highly recommended, especially the terrace with its fine sea views.

Name: Il Paguro
Address: Via Cala Capra, Capo d'Orso, Palau, 07020, Italy
Description: The small bay of Cala Capra is truly romantic and exclusive. Advance reservations are advised; without one, the barrier at the top of the road down to the marina won’t be raised. Hotel Capo d’Orso, which houses the Paguro restaurant, shares the same atmosphere: with a gorgeous Mediterranean-style terrace overlooking this little slice of paradise. The food suits the setting: classic, straightforward cooking built mostly around excellent local catch. A place that’s genuinely hard to leave.

Name: Il Pavone
Description: Situated in the heart of Alghero and with a beautiful veranda overlooking the sea, this restaurant has been in business for almost 50 years. Fish and seafood take centre stage here, served in classic dishes which are full of flavour and prepared using top-quality local ingredients. Specialities include fresh pan-fried and grilled fish, delicious bavettine pasta with scampi and fried mussels, and the island’s famous “seadas” served with Sardinian eucalyptus honey or home-made ice-cream.

Name: Il Pescatore
Address: Via Acqua Dolce 7, Cala Gonone, 08022, Italy
Description: This Mediterranean-style restaurant has the evocative feel of a seaside village with its beautiful photos of the coast on the walls. It’s best to book ahead if you want one of the tables on the small terrace overlooking the sea. To avoid confusion, note that the Il Pescatore that we recommend is situated at 7, via Acqua Dolce.

Name: Il Piraña
Description: A classic fish restaurant that opts for simply prepared dishes rather than fussy, inventive avant - garde cuisine. The perfect address for those in search of traditional fare.

Name: Il Poggio
Description: This simple yet welcoming family-run restaurant is situated on the wine route that wends its way through the hills behind Sondrio, less than 5km away. The dining room boasts a cheerful open fireplace (also used as a grill), while an attractive outdoor terrace offers fine views of the valley. The cuisine focuses mainly on local recipes and ingredients, with some main courses cooked over the grill.

Name: Il Portico
Description: Chef Lopriore returns to his native region with this new restaurant which offers an original format – the lunchtime menu focuses on single course options, while in the evening the tasting menus comprise an interesting combination of imaginative fish, meat and vegetable dishes which can be combined as you wish. Cuisine with an emphasis on seasonal market ingredients where locally sourced produce takes pride of place.

Name: Il Portolano
Address: Via Molara 11, Porto San Paolo, 07020, Italy
Description: Right on the seafront in front of Tavolara Island, a simple restaurant run by an experienced couple. The kitchen exalts the best fish in the area with a modern taste, offered with a wide selection including some raw (such as red tuna tartare with cucumber and raspberries) and the catch of the day grilled, baked or in salt. In the summer, reservations are highly recommended because the scenic outdoor seating area, although large, is extremely popular!

Name: Il Posticino
Description: A tiny gem in the historic center, just steps from the San Michele towers. A very intimate setting, with a refined yet informal atmosphere. The cuisine? Seafood with a seasonal twist, including standouts such as the surprising Brandapolenta: creamy baccala, crispy polenta, taggiasca olive pâté. Reserving a table – especially for outdoor seating – is a must!

Name: Il Pozzo
Description: This restaurant is housed in a historic palazzo. It has a traditional dining room, as well as an area that was once home to a wine bar (vaulted ceilings and more convivial atmosphere). A full range of Italian specialities are served.

Name: Il Presidente
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: In the heart of the historic centre, just a short distance from the Cathedral of Lucera, this restaurant lies in an ancient alleyway where the stables of a noble palazzo once stood. Today the dining room is arranged across several interconnecting spaces, framed by elegant stone vaulting; at its centre, two glass panels allow a glimpse of the cellar, which houses over 300 labels. The cooking is Mediterranean, modern and vivid in colour: among the dishes, octopus with almonds, fusillone with pumpkin cream and scampi, and a fillet of fish – sea bream, sea bass or dentex according to the market – accompanied by seasonal vegetables, to give some sense of the style. The focaccia di mare is not to be missed. This is not so much cooking of technical virtuosity as a homage to the ingredient itself: flavour, here, remains the true protagonist.

Name: Il Principe
Address: Via Colle San Bartolomeo 4, Pompei, 80045, Italy
Description: This restaurant focuses on a skilful and creative reinterpretation of Campanian specialities, serving the type of cuisine that you’d be happy to eat every day. Although the dishes are inspired by the chef’s childhood memories and his grandmother’s cooking, he adds his own contemporary touch and careful presentation. Both meat and fish feature, showcasing all the colour and imagination of the best regional cuisine.

Name: Il Riccio
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Situated just a few metres from the Blue Grotto and perched right above the water, Il Riccio is the quintessential Mediterranean fine-dining restaurant thanks to its tasteful and elegant decor. Undoubtedly one of Capri’s iconic addresses, it focuses uniquely on fish and seafood dishes. Whether you have a sweet tooth or not, a visit to the tempting dessert buffet to admire its array of delicacies is a must!

Name: Il Ridotto
Address: Campo S.S. Filippo e Giacomo, sestiere Castello 4509, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: Just a few steps from St. Mark's Square and the Bridge of Sighs, in a small square, Il Ridotto welcomes you with a colourful and warm atmosphere. The cuisine, based on territoriality and seasonality of products, will win you over. Not to be missed is the mouthwatering and fresh white chocolate dessert of bergamot, citrus and grapefruit.

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Description: Situated on the fifth floor of the Hotel Bulgari with views of the Mausoleum of Augustus, this restaurant boasts a spacious terrace and an elegant, welcoming dining room with mahogany walls adorned with works of art. To reach the dining room, you pass through the lively bar, where we recommend starting your evening with an aperitif. Once at your table, the menu offers a concrete expression of three-Michelin-star chef Niko Romito’s culinary approach which focuses on lighter, elegant versions of traditional Italian dishes in a sequence of courses that take guests on a culinary tour around Italy. Spaghetti in tomato sauce, artichoke soup, saffron risotto and Piedmontese “bonet” dessert all feature on the menu.

Name: Il Ristorante Alain Ducasse Roma
Description: A few steps from Piazza del Popolo, a 17th-century palazzo houses the ROMEO Roma hotel and, within it, the restaurant bearing the name of the world’s most-starred chef. The dining room – like the hotel, designed by Zaha Hadid – is a triumph of precious materials: ebony on the walls, marble for the open kitchen, an aesthetic that unites luxury, exclusivity and futuristic lines in each detail. This restaurant is a tribute to great Italian cuisine, reinterpreted through French techniques and Alain Ducasse’s ‘Cuisine de la Naturalité’ philosophy. A contemporary cuisine that draws inspiration from nature and its surroundings, featuring carefully selected, high-quality ingredients and delicate, understated flavours that bring out the purity of local produce. Fresh, seasonal vegetables take centre stage on the menu, while technical precision, balance and a Mediterranean sensitivity bring to life elegant, straightforward dishes that are in tune with the stunning surroundings.

Name: Il Rivale al Lago
Address: Via Marconi 93, Padenghe sul Garda, 25080, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the lake, this multi-faceted restaurant serves classic Italian dishes, often with a creative twist, alongside top-quality international ingredients such as Cantabrian anchovies and Japanese Wagyu beef. Grilled meats and vegetable dishes also make an appearance on the menu.

Name: Il Rivale in Città
Description: Situated in a beautiful 18C palazzo right in the centre of Brescia, this elegant restaurant consists of several small dining rooms of different colours, fabrics and furnishings yet all with the same historic atmosphere – the room with just one table is truly intimate! The cuisine features substantial recipes with a contemporary Italian flavour including top-quality options such as potato puff pastry, scampi, caviar and hazelnut cream, while one of the highlights of the new formula is the wooden dessert trolley on which a selection of tempting home-made delicacies is presented. The wine list (easily consulted on a tablet) is also impressive, with a particular focus on labels from nearby Franciacorta.

Name: Il Salotto Atelier Gourmet
Description: The small, classic Rosabianca hotel on the seafront in Rapallo has begun to improve its facilities, starting with its restaurant where large windows (which can be opened in summer) overlook the promenade, and its intimate, elegant interior with subtle lighting and a relaxing ambience. The cuisine focuses on fish and seafood which are skilfully prepared so that the quality of the superb ingredients shines through, while the service ensures that guests are looked after with discretion and professionalism.

Name: Il Sanlorenzo
Description: A historic palazzo built over the foundations of the Teatro Pompeo is home to this atmospheric restaurant, which brings together history and contemporary art. However, the real star is the fish on the menu, most of which comes from the island of Ponza, and is served either raw or cooked very simply in a modern style.

Name: Il Santo Bevitore
Address: Via Santo Spirito 64/66 r, Florence, 50125, Italy
Description: The atmosphere is simple and convivial, with the authentic feel of a typical Tuscan trattoria. It is from this tradition that the cooking takes its cue, offering a number of regional classics: from the selection of cured meats to ribollita, from roast pigeon served with fettunta and zolfini beans to cantucci with Vin Santo. There are also occasional seafood dishes, such as cuttlefish and artichoke stew. These are generous, full-flavoured dishes, faithful to a style of cooking that expresses Tuscan identity to the full, sometimes refreshed through more contemporary interpretations, yet always recognisable and reassuring.

Name: Il Saturnino
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: It was a love story between an American and a local girl from Forio that led, in 1949, to the opening of this restaurant overlooking the port, with its attractive veranda boasting fine sea views. The current management team have made this one of the most interesting restaurants in the region for anyone keen to sample traditional cuisine from Ischia and Campania. Don’t miss the pasta served with local (and very rare) zampognaro beans, mussels and squid, or the Ischian-style rabbit presented in an attractive terracotta dish. A good choice of fish dishes is also available.

Name: Il Sole di Ranco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: An elegant residence with gardens sloping down to the lake. The charming terrace, where meals are served in summer, offers superb views of the lake, while the cuisine combines the traditional and the modern, including imaginative flavours with a focus on locally sourced ingredients.

Name: Il Sommelier
Description: This small, intimate restaurant next to the elegant Palazzo Roccabruna in the historic centre is slightly off the beaten track despite its central location. Recently opened by the Poletti brothers (one in the kitchen, the other front of house), with an attractive dining room designed by the owners’ father, the restaurant serves top-quality ingredients (especially fish and seafood) in dishes which include modern influences (the mango cheesecake is delicious) and a pleasing classic appeal (raw fish dishes).

Name: Il Tartufo
Description: Housed in a small villa in the residential area of the village, this intimate and secluded restaurant serves delicious cuisine with distinctly regional roots. In season, locally sourced truffles take centre stage, while fish and seafood dominate the menu at other times of year.

Name: Il Trillo
Description: On the hills overlooking the town, an ancient residence transformed into a refined hospitality venue – and today home also to the estate’s own winery – receives its guests in surroundings of considerable elegance. A charm that reaches its apogee in the warmer months, when dinner is served in the evocative limonaia: a romantic panoramic terrace bathed in soft light and surrounded by lemon, orange, bergamot and mandarin trees. The kitchen engages in a dialogue with the territory, weaving together ingredients from sea and land along classical lines enriched by touches of imagination and careful presentation. Among the dishes that drew particular appreciation from our Inspector, the tortellini filled with pear and pecorino in a saffron and pistachio sauce, and the duck breast with mandarin accompanied by a celeriac tartlet.

Name: Il Verso del Ghiottone
Description: This restaurant housed in an 18C building has a warm, rustic feel with terracotta, stone and brick decor and black tables with American-style place mats, resulting in a vibrant yet elegant atmosphere where the service is informal and yet also highly professional. The cuisine is inspired by regional recipes which are reinterpreted and given a lighter flavour. There’s no shortage of interesting fish dishes, including the exquisite red shrimp, which is half-cooked, half-raw and served with passion-fruit caramel.

Name: Impronta
Description: An elegant restaurant that has the feel of a private home, with its beautiful light-wood tables. The Sicilian origins of talented chef Andrea Colombara are reflected in his dishes, which have a strong Mediterranean flavour. Highlights on the menu include delicious mullet with caponata which is served with onions, pine nuts, capers and small vegetables in a sweet and sour sauce.

Name: In Riva a Numana
Description: Riva is the Hotel Vista’s fine-dining restaurant, situated just behind Numana’s beach with fine panoramic views. The restaurant serves top-quality ingredients from the Adriatic and surrounding countryside in creative dishes full of flavour which are showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte.

Name: InAlto Alfio Ghezzi Dolomites
Address: Passo San Pellegrino 32, stazione a monte della funivia Col Margherita, Moena, 38035, Italy
Description: At Col Margherita, perched at 2,550 meters and accessible by cable car in winter (departing from Moena via Passo San Pellegrino), a new ski bar bears the signature of Alfio Ghezzi. The menu favors Alpine traditions, though a more elaborate, creative selection showcases several not-to-be-missed dishes from the chef. In warmer months, the venue is also reachable on foot or − for the more athletic − by bicycle (two charging stations available for e-bikes).

Name: InGalera
Description: Thanks to its location inside Bollate prison, InGalera offers a unique dining experience. Here, guests eat in a room within the prison itself, while dishes – of equal quality to other restaurants in the area – are prepared with the contribution of prison inmates. In this subdued ambience, choose from meat and fish dishes, with a restricted choice at lunchtime and the option of ordering a single dish.

Name: Incàlmo
Description: “Clean”, almost naive dishes full of clear and defined flavours take centre-stage at Incàlmo, where the cuisine is distinctly unfussy with no unnecessary frills. As a result, ingredients are clearly recognisable (as is the way they are prepared), allowing guests to focus on their contrasting textures and flavours. In the chef’s view, “if one element does stand out, it’s probably the bitter flavours that we enjoy playing with,” says the chef, “while at the same time balancing this with other elements. We also prioritise the use of vegetables.”

Name: Indigeno
Address: Via di Villa Bianca 15, Montepulciano, 53045, Italy
Description: Boasting an unusually beautiful setting within the Salcheto Organic Winery amid the rolling hills around Montepulciano, this 13C farmhouse has been converted into a wine estate that also includes a restaurant. Simple, home-style cooking with a focus on local traditions takes pride of place here, with dishes made from ingredients either produced on the estate itself or sourced from small-scale local producers. Guests sit at large shared tables made from Amiata oak, or outdoors in summer, where they can enjoy home-made bread and numerous other specialities, including bread gnocchetti with creamed broad beans and bitter herbs, and roast goose leg.

Name: Indiniò
Description: Located in a charming little village, Indiniò is an extraordinary place to discover Carnic cuisine. The ingredients tell the story of the local area, but chef Gloria Clama transforms them into refined creations that are sometimes bold and surprising. The dining rooms, furnished with wood and modern details, evoke tradition in an elegant way, creating a warm and romantic atmosphere.

Name: Inka
Description: The name was not chosen at random: in the heart of the old town, you will find an excellent selection of Peruvian cuisine, rich in spices, colours and a variety of ingredients combined in often complex dishes. The chef is of Peruvian origin and, in addition to classic ceviche, he likes to add a Japanese touch to some dishes, creating Nikkei cuisine, the result of emigration to Peru by Japanese people who brought their own culinary traditions with them and blended them with the local cuisine.

Name: Innesti
Address: Via San Pietro 8, Pergine Valsugana, 38057, Italy
Description: Daniele and Elisa are a couple of young restaurateurs who are familiar to us from their time at Blumenstube in Sant'Orsola. Having moved on, they have now opened their own restaurant in Pergine, where both the decor and the cuisine are contemporary-Alpine in style. As in currently in vogue, their dishes are showcased on three tasting menus (short, medium and long) from which dishes can also be chosen à la carte style. All the recipes have a creative feel, demonstrating the chef’s playful approach to his contemporary ingredients.

Name: Innocenti Wine Experiences
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Innocenti Wine is a venue with a dual identity: on one side, a wine shop boasting an ever-evolving collection of over 1,200 labels spanning Italy’s finest wine regions and international terroirs; on the other, a restaurant where contemporary cuisine finds expression through three tasting menus or à la carte selections. A place designed for those who approach wine as exploration and the table as its natural complement.

Name: Insieme
Description: On a quiet, tucked-away street far from the well-trodden paths, a small neighborhood restaurant tells the story of a couple who, after experiences abroad, chose to return and put down roots here. The result is a venue of authentic character, where a familial warmth is immediately palpable and becomes an integral part of the experience. The nimble, ever-evolving menu reflects a cuisine that approaches flavors with contemporary sensitivity: from gentler notes, such as roasted squash with Parmigiano foam and almond crumble, to bolder tones, exemplified by an excellent Carnaroli saffron risotto enriched with tongue and a vibrant parsley sauce. Whatever the guest’s mood, simply trust the suggestions of owner Federica: young and knowledgeable, she guides with ease toward the ideal glass, in perfect harmony with chef Alessandro’s cuisine.

Name: Insieme Dal Clandestino
Description: A chef of Albanian origin, who in his restaurant’s name proudly acknowledges the complex journey that brought him to Italy, delivers a cuisine that seamlessly blends memory and modernity. Experience gained both in the region and in the city has shaped dishes that are anything but contrived, reinterpreting solid Piedmontese traditions through a contemporary lens, while making generous use of the territory’s iconic ingredients, from fresh pasta to chocolate, hazelnuts to truffles. The value is equally compelling: at lunch, a lighter selection is available from the menu, while the kitchen often extends the option to explore the more elaborate evening offerings as well.

Name: Io Osteria Personale
Description: Well past its tenth year of operation, this contemporary bistrot has by now established itself as a solid point of reference in the San Frediano quarter – and more broadly across the city. The setting, spare yet considered, plays upon exposed beams, brick walls and a handful of wooden tables left deliberately in their natural state, arranged in two rows: a simplicity that is only apparent, behind which is felt a carefully attuned minimal sensitivity. The same attention is to be found in the kitchen, where a creative and personal offering takes shape, moving with balance between meat, fish and vegetarian options. Among the dishes tasted by our Inspector, the ravioli with peas and asparagus, accompanied by a camomile and pollen goat’s cheese foam, are particularly convincing: an original recipe, chromatically elegant and decidedly accomplished.

Name: Io e Luna
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This classic-style restaurant serving updated regional cuisine offers views of the surrounding hills from its attractive outdoor terrace.

Name: Ippogrifo
Description: This elegant restaurant with a smart, classic feel is situated in the Expo Fiera area not far from the city centre. Ever since it opened in 1982, this restaurant has been a reliable choice for top-quality fish (although meat also features on the menu), which is prepared using classic techniques and recipes. Highlights include dishes such as tuna and amberjack carpaccio, warm seafood salad, grilled fish, fish cooked in typical Ligurian style with potatoes and Taggiasche olives, and fish soup with croutons.

Name: Isi Ivano Ricchebono Chef
Description: In the heart of the Carignano quarter, the restaurant conceals itself along a quiet side street, revealing an atmosphere that is both intimate and elegant. Three tasting menus – Tradition and Innovation, Classic, and Vegetarian – guide the guest through a gastronomic journey rich in identity, with the option of dining à la carte should one prefer. The cooking unites boldness with refinement, interweaving classic references and modern impulses in dishes that impress through their balance and personality; the trofie al pesto genovese, presented here in a reinterpretation of decided character, are not to be missed. The business lunch proves a most welcome discovery: broad choice, excellent quality, and a value for money that is genuinely winning. The wine list is generous and well-structured, with a particularly interesting focus on Ligurian labels, while the competent and professional service contributes to making the experience pleasingly relaxed within surroundings that are both considered and comfortable.

Name: Izu
Description: Recent refurbishment at this long-standing restaurant on the city’s main square has given it the feel of an elegant bistro. Although the owners and managers here are Chinese, the cuisine focuses on Japan and includes all the usual classic options (sushi, uramaki, sashimi etc), as well as a series of “Izu special creations” and various dishes influenced by Asia and the Mediterranean alike. There’s also a good wine list (including, as you might expect, a few sakes) overseen by an experienced and knowledgeable sommelier.

Name: J Contemporary Japanese Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Arranged over several floors and in different dining rooms, this smart, elegant restaurant offers excellent service. In this modern setting with subtle lighting, enjoy typical Japanese specialities (almost exclusively fish dishes) which are showcased on an extensive menu.

Name: Jamantè
Address: Via San Vito 97, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
Description: Located not far from the historic centre and the picturesque Lama Monachile beach, Jamantè is an elegant restaurant with well-spaced-out tables perfect for a stylish night out. As is traditional in Puglia, there’s a wide selection of raw options to start, followed by dishes with a focus on fish and seafood. Elaborate and creative cuisine is to the fore here.

Name: Januarius
Description: Dedicated to San Gennaro, whose relics are kept in the nearby Duomo, this address pays homage not only to the city’s patron saint but also to the most authentic traditions of Campanian gastronomy. The table presents a procession of the specialities that have shaped the culinary history of Naples: from polpo alla Luciana to broken ziti with traditional ragù, through to the classic baccalà accompanied by Neapolitan-style escarole. Alongside these icons sit more contemporary offerings, described as ‘non-traditional special dishes’, born of the house’s own creative spirit. Guests are welcomed at the entrance by a well-stocked shop of excellent produce – salumi and cheeses above all – while to either side open two characterful dining rooms, authentic and full of personality.

Name: Joca
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Wheelchair access
Description: A contemporary, on-trend atmosphere in one of the liveliest pedestrian areas, just steps from the elegant Riviera di Chiaia. Here, chef Gianluca D’Agostino, with solid experience both in the city and beyond, presents gourmet cuisine that plays on creativity and Campanian influences. Alongside the main menu, a dedicated tapas section: not Spanish-inspired, but rather reinterpretations of Italian and local classics in a smaller format. Among the most compelling offerings on the gastronomic journey are the sweetbreads with puntarelle, lupin bean mayonnaise, and mullet bottarga, while the main courses alternate between refined meat and fish preparations. The wine list is in the capable hands of Alfredo, who offers thoughtful recommendations and also curates the soundtrack, making for a complete and harmonious experience.

Name: Josef Stube
Address: Località Certosa 29, Madonna di Senales, 39020, Italy
Description: Run with passion by the two owners who continue the long family tradition in this hotel-restaurant is one of the most picturesque sights in the Val Senales. Its beautifully kept dining room is romantic and typical of the region, providing a backdrop for just a few dishes which are prepared by the chef with a focus on local ingredients. A hint of Mediterranean influence adds to the appeal.

Name: Josto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: One of Cagliari’s most interesting venues, comprising two small rooms, each with its own distinctive character, where contemporary design blends harmoniously with nods to local tradition. In the entrance hall, the open-plan kitchen showcases a culinary offering deeply rooted in Sardinian tradition, reinterpreted with a contemporary sensitivity and remarkable precision. Among the most characteristic dishes are Sardinian-breed pork ham, fregula, mullet and a dessert based on saba (an iconic ingredient of the island, made by slowly cooking grape must). The atmosphere is made even more pleasant by the selection of music played on vinyl at a moderate volume, while the wine list focuses on Sardinia and Burgundy without neglecting interesting Italian and international wines.

Name: Josè - Tenuta Villa Guerra
Address: Via Nazionale 414, Torre del Greco, 80059, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: 2025 has seen a change at the helm in the kitchen at this restaurant, in line with the new approach introduced by its enthusiastic owners. The full focus now is on the flavours of Campania, served in lighter versions and reinterpretations of traditional recipes. This is the case with the legendary Santa Rosa dessert, which has been transformed into a millefeuille made with the same ingredients as the original dish, namely crispy puff pastry, custard and sour cherries in syrup. Situated in one of the extraordinary villas on Herculaneum’s “Golden Mile”, the restaurant boasts an elegant dining room within this 18C building, as well as a room overlooking the villa gardens where pizzas are served from mid spring to late summer. Wine-enthusiasts will be pleased to hear that the wine cellar continues to offer an extensive selection of superb labels.

Name: KELINA Fine Dine
Address: Strada Lech de Boà s.n., Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: Open at lunchtime, Kelina represents the most refined gastronomic offering of the Piz Boè Alpine Lounge. Easily reached from Corvara via the modern Boè cable car – or directly on skis – it surprises on arrival with its gourmet spirit at altitude. The essential and elegant interiors have been conceived to celebrate the true star of the experience: the extraordinary panorama over the peaks of Sassongher, Santa Croce and Varella, admired through broad picture windows. In the kitchen, a focused and well-defined offering centres on clean and immediate flavours, with dishes that privilege taste and substance; among them, the cacio e pepe risotto with sausage is particularly appreciated. A carefully curated wine list, rich in Italian labels and prestigious French references, completes the experience.

Name: Kandoo Nippon Restaurant
Description: Contemporary spaces spread across two floors, plus a veranda terrace, make this solid restaurant a great choice for lovers of Japanese specialties – both cooked and raw preparations of meat and fish – executed with a light touch and clean, distinct flavors. At lunch (weekdays only), the kitchen also offers rice bowls and noodle dishes accompanied by various sides. Wine enthusiasts will appreciate the dedicated Champagne section on the wine list.

Name: Kircherhof
Description: A 17th-century farmstead run by the same family for four generations, initially as a produce farm (fruit and vegetables) before the younger generation expanded into dining in the early 2000s. The offering, based entirely on organic, sustainably sourced ingredients, is compelling, particularly delicious, and rooted in local traditions while casting a savvy, curious eye toward the present. Dishes are colorful and very generous; the all-female service team is warm and happy to explain the house philosophy. There’s also a shop where you can stock up on treats before you leave.

Name: Kirchsteiger
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This restaurant has long been one of the most interesting in the area. It has a pleasing combination of traditional and modern cuisine created by the expert chef. The dining rooms have the same blend of old and new with an elegant use of local materials in the decor. Ask for one of the newer guestrooms.

Name: Kisté - Easy Gourmet
Address: Via Santa Maria de' Greci 2, Taormina, 98039, Italy
Description: Housed in the 15C Casa Cipolla, with a romantic terrace for summer dining, Kistè is a treasure trove of gourmet Sicilian cuisine prepared in contemporary style.

Name: Kleine Flamme
Description: In his small open-view kitchen situated in the centre of this restaurant, chef Bacher Burkhard develops his vision of fusion cuisine with energy and precision, combining flavours from Italy and the Alto Adige with Asian spices and techniques to create delicious and imaginative dishes. His tuna tataki is superb, seasoned with salty lemon oil and accompanied by intriguing bitter herbs that (as Professor Montanari has noted in a recent book) are particularly popular with Italians. The chef’s wife Annelies works front of house, where she looks after guests in a friendly and professional manner.

Name: Kohaku
Description: On a street running parallel to the celebrated Via Vittorio Veneto, Kohaku brings the elegance of Japanese kaiseki cuisine – the country’s haute gastronomy – to the capital. The menu offers a broad range of classic and traditional dishes, with quality at its heart: impeccable ingredients, precise knife work and carefully composed presentations. The freshness of the fish is evident in the many raw dishes, among which – according to the Inspector – the scallop and amberjack tartare stands out, mixed with cubes of avocado and dressed with a delicious ponzu sauce and sesame oil. The meats, too, are of notable quality. Depending on personal taste, guests may choose the celebrated gyoza dumplings, tempura, noodles or the many charcoal-grilled preparations, to name only part of the offering. For those seeking total immersion, the “Kohaku kaiseki” tasting menu is also available at dinner: an eight-course itinerary dedicated to lovers of great Japanese cuisine.

Name: Koinè
Description: Whether you dine in the modern dining room at this centrally located palazzo or in the small courtyard in fine weather, Alberto Buratti offers a choice of tasting menus (including the vegetarian “1MQ d’orto”), alongside a concise à la carte. His cuisine includes a combination of local dishes (from classic risottos to breaded veal) and more creative fare.

Name: Konnubio
Address: Via dei Conti 8 r, Florence, 50123, Italy
Description: In an informal yet meticulously designed setting, the kitchen takes diners on a journey through the great flavours of Italy, reimagined with a contemporary twist. Among the most interesting dishes, the spaghetti with garlic, olive oil, sea urchins, caramelised cream and barley bread crumble stands out, while for meat lovers, the grilled Fiorentina steak is a must. The wine list is well-curated, complemented by a selection of cocktails prepared with great care. The romantic table on the steps is highly sought-after, so it’s best to book well in advance. At lunchtime, however, the menu features a selection of simpler, more straightforward dishes.

Name: Kosmo Taste the Mountain
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the centre and also accessible from the ski slopes in winter, this contemporary, Alpine-style restaurant boasts a spacious dining room and large picture windows. The cuisine reflects the traditions of the Valtellina mountains, with a dedicated space for the charcoal grill and an excellent selection of cheeses. The extensive wine list pays particular attention to mountain wines produced by wineries with a sustainable focus.

Name: Kro
Address: Via Tollarini 70/c, località Pontagna di Temù, Ponte di Legno, 25050, Italy
Description: Old stables have been converted into this restaurant, which boasts a stylish decor of wood and stone and the sort of romantic atmosphere that you would expect from the mountains. Although a few fish options are included on the menu, the cuisine focuses mainly on Alpine cuisine, featuring ingredients such as mushrooms, meat and game.

Name: Kürbishof
Description: This romantic inn with guestrooms occupies an old farm with a hay barn. In two typical Stube-style rooms, one of which offers views of the Cembra valley, enjoy cuisine prepared by a mother-and-son team. They work side by side, preparing dishes from mainly regional ingredients (the menu often includes the names of producers) each in their own individual way, which is highlighted on the menu: to the left, you’ll find the traditional dishes made by the mother, Sara, while on the right you can choose from a selection of modern, creative options prepared by young chef Mathias. Our inspectors were delighted with their combination of choices from both lists!

Name: L'A Gourmet L'Accademia
Address: Via Largo C. Colombo 6, Reggio Calabria, 89125, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: From the restaurant on the first floor (no lift) of this early 20C building, you’ll enjoy fine views of the sea and the Strait of Messina. Here, skilled chef Filippo Cogliardo prepares fish-based dishes which include classic recipes (raw seafood) as well as more modern options (amberjack, red turnip with honey, fennel mayonnaise and lime gel). A few meat dishes also feature on the menu.

Name: L'Accanto
Address: Via Santa Maria Vecchia 2, loc. Seiano, Vico Equense, 80066, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Leaving behind the traffic of the Amalfi Coast, one enters the quiet and elegant enclave of the Hotel Angiolieri, where the experience of its most exclusive restaurant takes shape. The interiors are distinguished by a classical and understated elegance, but it is outdoors that the restaurant truly comes into its own: as soon as the season permits, dinner is served on one of the most scenic terraces in the area, suspended between the Bay of Naples and sunsets of extraordinary beauty. The cuisine draws on the great riches of Campanian tradition, reworked with inventiveness and contemporary sensitivity. The dishes, marked by a creativity that never tips into excess, find expression in two tasting menus that strike a confident balance between land and sea, in a coherent and harmonious gastronomic narrative.

Name: L'Acchiatura
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Delicious cuisine from Puglia, including excellent orecchiette pasta with clams and chickpeas, served in a delightful ambience with a number of different rooms and internal patios. The same traditional atmosphere is evident in the attractive, well - equipped guestrooms, as well as in the picturesque swimming pool housed in a grotto.

Name: L'Acciuga
Description: A reliable city destination for seafood, the venue welcomes guests in nautical-themed surroundings that evoke the interiors of vintage ships. The ingredients are fresh and fragrant, interpreted through tradition and then elevated in personal recipes: raw scallops with cannellini beans, onion, and rosemary; anchovy spaghetti with crispy bread and lemon; monkfish ossobuco. The wine list is complemented by a playful selection of cocktails and kombucha offered at the Bar counter. A maritime atmosphere and warm Romagnolo hospitality round out an experience that delivers on every front.

Name: L'Acqua Bulle
Description: Divided into several dining rooms with elegant tables enhanced by the absence of tablecloths, the chef proposes an intelligent and flavourful interpretation of the typical produce of Castelli Romani, beginning with freshwater fish such as perch, whitefish, eel and pike, as well as various meats, for instance lamb. Technique and terroir are at an excellent level, imaginative yet without excess, making this an outstanding choice for those in the area.

Name: L'Agave
Description: Be cautious not to be misled by any potential misdirections from satellite navigation systems. Head directly to the tourist marina of the quaint locality overlooking the sea—a place offering one of the most striking vistas in the area. Here, dishes crafted by a young chef and wines selected from remarkable regional highlights boldly declare a love for Liguria. From Albenga’s artichokes and asparagus to Pigna beans, pine nuts, 'prebugiun', olives, and of course, seafood—all elements here speak of this land. The concept encompasses tasting menus, with dishes available à la carte.

Name: L'Aia dei Cappellani
Description: In the dining room there are old photos and equipment from country life, from the terrace the entire valley. Among widespread grasslands and olive trees enjoy fresh produce and home - cooked local dishes. In the dining room there are old photos and equipment from country life, from the terrace the entire valley. Among widespread grasslands and olive trees enjoy fresh produce and home - cooked local dishes.

Name: L'Ambasciata
Address: Piazzetta Ambasciatori del Gusto 1, Quistello, 46026, Italy
Description: This has long been one of those restaurants in Italy where the opulent interior decor has no equal – at Christmas, the mirrors, rugs, silverware, chandeliers and piles of books are joined by the largest and most ornate Christmas tree that you’ll ever see in a restaurant. The cuisine created by owner-chef Matteo Ugolotti is inspired by Mantuan traditions and the restaurant’s previous famous owners, occasionally going all the way back to the Renaissance. Special mention should be made of the extraordinary chocolate salami – a dessert coated with a delicious, frothy, warm zabaglione poured from a copper pan at your table. The menu also features more modern recipes and tasting menus.

Name: L'Ancora della Tortuga
Address: Salita Cappuccini 4, Monterosso al Mare, 19016, Italy
Description: Just a few minutes' walk from the centre, slightly uphill, and from the indispensable public car park, we are in a restaurant in full marine style, literally clinging to the cliff, with a wall carved out of the living rock. From the upper terrace (reservation strongly recommended!) the view is breathtaking, while the cuisine, very generous and rich in ingredients, honours the sea without forgetting the land, as in the best Ligurian tradition. The dishes on the menu are updated daily with alternatives by voice or blackboard.

Name: L'Angolino da Filippo
Address: Via Sangritana 1, Marina di San Vito, 66038, Italy
Description: A red door just a few metres from the sea marks the entrance to this long-established restaurant (a family-run business for over a century), which boasts two small dining rooms with brick-vaulted ceilings and a lively atmosphere. Unsurprisingly, the menu focuses on fish and seafood specialities, which showcase a combination of delicious modern and traditional flavours.

Name: L'Angolo d'Abruzzo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: For almost 40 years, the Angolo d’Abruzzo restaurant has been home to the Centofanti family, who act as excellent ambassadors for the region by offering the best local, seasonal ingredients (for this reason, there’s no fish on the menu) in a host of traditional, regional recipes. Specialities such as cured meats, local ham, bruschetta and fresh home-made pasta (including “chitarra” spaghetti) take centre stage, while main courses include grilled dishes (porcini mushrooms in season, cuts of beef and veal at any time of year) and stews (mutton etc). When it comes to dessert, make sure you try the crème caramel with Navelli saffron. A misleading sign saying “sagrestia” (sacristy) actually indicates the well-stocked wine cellar.

Name: L'Antico Giardino
Description: A menu steeped in Ferrarese tradition, served in a welcoming and comfortable setting, energised by the friendly charm of the owner, who offers valuable advice on the best wine and food pairings. The menu features flavours that seduce the senses: passatelli drenched in a velvety cheese fondue, enriched with morel mushrooms and the intense aroma of autumn black truffle ; soft and juicy larded pheasant breast accompanied by a Castelmagno custard that caresses the palate; and to finish, a soft cheesecake with double white chocolate and pistachio mousse, topped with a blackberry sauce. And, season permitting, the king of the table: the white truffle, ready to enhance every dish.

Name: L'Arcangelo
Address: Via Giuseppe Gioacchino Belli 59, Rome, 00193, Italy
Description: Simple and austere: the rightfully earned fame of this restaurant is due to the search for the best regional (but not only) products. A real passion of the owner who, like an archangel, will guide you to the paradise of the palate and gastronomic niches.

Name: L'Archivolto - Osteria Nostrale
Description: Situated on Ovada’s main square, this restaurant has the pleasant friendly ambience of an attractive trattoria, while its menu takes guests on a delicious culinary journey through the Piedmont region, including local specialities such as home-made tajarin pasta, braised beef in Ovada wine with mashed potato, and the local bunet dessert (finanziera stew also makes an occasional appearance). The restaurant is also a wine bar/boutique offering a selection of wines, including different Barolo labels (presented area by area) and aperitifs served both at lunchtime and dinner.

Name: L'Argaj
Description: In the Piedmontese dialect, “Argaj” translates as “satisfaction” and never has a restaurant name seemed more appropriate! In a simple, colourful and welcoming dining room with windows looking out at the hills, all the attention is on cuisine which is skilfully balanced between classic local dishes and more creative options. Choose between the à la carte and tasting menus, all accompanied by an excellent array of wines.

Name: L'Aurum
Description: At L’Albereta, one of Franciacorta’s most prestigious destinations, an elegant and intimate setting, characterised by delicate colours and a refined atmosphere, provides the backdrop for a distinctly contemporary cuisine. The menu reinterprets Italian tradition with a modern sensitivity, often favouring local and seasonal ingredients. Amid the kitchen’s details, references to the teachings of Gualtiero Marchesi emerge with understated elegance; his influence continues to inspire this place. The result is a dish of great balance and character, an expression of contemporary and accomplished Italian haute cuisine.

Name: L'Imbuto
Address: Via della Pieve Santo Stefano, 967/c, Lucca, 55100, Italy
Description: Having found a home just outside the city in a hillside farmhouse with extensive outdoor summer service, Cristiano Tomei continues to offer his original flavors – with a beloved focus on bitter notes and Parmigiano Reggiano cheese, often combined – through a format based on choosing the number of courses blind (though in reality, diners tend to lose count thanks to the kitchen’s generous spirit). His perhaps most signature dish remains: the Bistecca Primitiva. The dining room provides warm service, with staff well-inclined to offer the necessary explanations.

Name: L'Officina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Tradition and a cosmopolitan spirit combine in this highly original and exciting restaurant which serves spectacular and unusual dishes such as cuttlefish ink tagliolino with a perch ragù. An ideal setting, either for dinner with friends or a business lunch (the menu for the latter is displayed on a blackboard).

Name: L'Oste Scuro
Description: Within an eighteenth-century palazzo, L’Oste Scuro boasts a centuries-old tradition, with the current management at the helm since 1998. A favored destination for seafood enthusiasts, preparations are decidedly classic and traditional, built on excellent-quality ingredients. Weather permitting, guests may dine in the palazzo’s enchanting inner courtyard. An extensive wine selection offers approximately 1,150 labels, with a particularly impressive range of Champagnes and Burgundies.

Name: L'Oste e il Sacrestano
Description: In the historic center, this cozy restaurant boasts a "Sicilian designation of origin" and is adorned with intriguing and rare memorabilia on the walls. Chiara warmly welcomes guests, while Peppe is in the kitchen, offering two "surprise" tasting menus. The meals are characterized by generous portions and excellent market cuisine, primarily focusing on fish and vegetables.

Name: L'Osteria H20
Address: Via Pergola 10, Moniga del Garda, 25080, Italy
Description: In a slightly elevated position overlooking the lake, on a clear day the view stretches from the tip of Sirmione to Mount Baldo. This is an excellent place to stop for a bite to eat. While the menu also includes meat dishes, most people come here for the fish, and with good reason: the ingredients are of the highest quality and the recipes are mostly classic.

Name: L'Osteria del Castellazzo
Address: via Borgo Castellazzo 40, Salsomaggiore Terme, 43039, Italy
Description: The determined and enthusiastic young owner of this restaurant graduated with a literature degree before giving in to her passion for food. She swapped her pen for a ladle and now creates delicious local specialities such as braised veal cheeks, alongside dishes from Pïacenza and Mantua, such as pisarei (a type of gnocchi) and sbrisolona cake.

Name: L'Osteria dell'Orologio
Address: Via di Torre Clementina 114, Fiumicino, 00054, Italy
Description: Along the road that runs beside the Tiber canal, restaurants abound both before and after L’Osteria dell’Orologio, but do not miss this one, which stands out for the remarkable quality of its fish and shellfish. Dishes from the seafaring tradition are sometimes presented in their familiar form, sometimes in the more personal interpretations of the talented Marco Claroni.

Name: L'Osteria di Santa Marina
Address: Campo Santa Marina, sestiere di Castello 5911, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: This classy inn is managed by young professionals who serve seafood and traditional dishes, but they also offer some interesting culinary innovations.

Name: L'Ostì
Address: Strada Sassongher 2, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: A minimalist-style restaurant featuring a wood decor, an extensive display of bottles, and some windows boasting partial yet splendid views of the Dolomites. The chef here prepares creative cuisine using local ingredients alongside produce sourced from other regions. The wine list includes a wide selection of natural wines.

Name: L'Ottava Nota
Description: In the bustling heart of Kalsa, just a stone's throw from the marina, this restaurant offers guests an elegant welcome without sacrificing its warm, informal atmosphere. In the kitchen, chef-patron Vladimiro Farina combines the flavours of Sicily and Spain, his homeland. One of the highlights is “Salmorejo”: a fresh Spanish soup revisited with date tomatoes, watermelon, peaches, basil, vinegar, croutons and cheese.

Name: L'Uva e il Malto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Welcoming and informal, this is a restaurant in the historic centre with a well-stocked cellar, the bottles are also for sale. A generous à la carte selection of both fish and meat, the dishes are predominantly traditional, Maremman, Tuscan, and some from further afield.

Name: L'antica Pizzeria da Michele
Description: You can really sense the history of Naples in this pizzeria, which was founded in 1870 and boasts a lively, convivial atmosphere – if you sit alone, you’re sure to find yourself sharing travellers’ tales with fellow diners by the end of your meal! Note that the restaurant only serves two types of pizza – Margherita (tomato and mozzarella) and Marinara (tomato, oregano and garlic). Numbered tickets are issued to diners, who then take a seat and are called in turn (open all day). A second restaurant has recently been opened nearby.

Name: La Barca
Address: Litoranea Salentina, Marina di Pulsano, 74026, Italy
Description: Nestled among magnificent beaches and bays, the sea reigns supreme: it dominates the horizon and returns to the plate in its most authentic expression. Patron Saverio Galeone is the guiding presence of the house, and the cooking follows a classic approach in both its techniques and pairings, so as to draw the very best from the quality of the catch. The finest cuts are generally cooked over the grill, while molluscs and crustaceans are presented in preparations that are spare and respectful of the ingredient. A table that speaks the language of the sea with frankness, precision and clean flavours.

Name: La Botte
Description: A modern and welcoming contemporary bistro situated in the heart of Stresa’s historic centre. Run by an entire family, the restaurant serves modern and imaginative fish and meat dishes where the focus is always on seasonal ingredients. The interesting wine list also includes a selection of wines by the glass.

Name: La Bottega del 30
Address: Via Santa Caterina 2, località Villa a Sesta, Castelnuovo Berardenga, 53019, Italy
Description: There’s a story behind the name of this restaurant: on the 30th day of every month a travelling salesman used to stop in this small, delightful village. In the meantime, a young French chef, Hélène, arrived here and fell in love with Chianti and its cuisine. She named her restaurant after the travelling salesman and the name has been kept in his memory. In a typical setting of stone walls and old rural objects from bygone days, Hélène is now front-of-house taking care of guests, while Nadia Mongiat has replaced her in the kitchen, where she continues with the restaurant’s tradition of creating simple Tuscan cuisine. The focus here is on preparing ingredients in traditional ways, such as pork liver (the thinnest part of the liver is used) cooked at a low temperature and then stored in lard with fennel for a few days before being re-heated sous-vide in a bain-marie. As a result, the liver (served lukewarm on a bed of Tuscan green beans) is soft and delicious.

Name: La Braja
Address: Via San Giovanni Bosco 11, Montemagno, 14030, Italy
Description: A traditional Piedmontese restaurant, where owner Giuseppe Palermino welcomes guests to his elegant dining room with consummate style. Although the specialities here have a regional focus (such as the hand-made agnolotti pasta with three types of meat), fish and seafood also make an appearance, broadening the appeal of the menu. The cheese trolley is superb, while white truffles always take centre stage in season.

Name: La Braseria
Description: This restaurant offers a culinary experience dedicated exclusively to Italian meats, sourced primarily from free-range, organic farms. Its philosophy is rooted in sustainability and respect for ingredients, with a whole-animal approach that reduces waste and highlights each individual cut. The goal is to enhance the quality of the product through simplicity, precise technique, and creativity, resulting in authentic flavors deeply tied to Italian gastronomic tradition. Dining at La Braseria is a sensory journey through territory, seasonality, and sustainability.

Name: La Brughiera
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This old farmhouse in the Groane Regional Park has never lost its warm family atmosphere. The interior is spacious and attractive and the menus are based on traditional and national specialities.

Name: La Bul
Description: Here, in one of Bari’s most interesting restaurants, chef Antonio Scalera serves top-quality cuisine accompanied by intelligently chosen wines with fascinating stories behind them. The dishes often feature traditional recipes and ingredients from Puglia yet are creative and of the highest quality.

Name: La Bursch
Description: In the Valle Cervo lies a romantic retreat: La Bursch, a wonderful hamlet restored with great taste through the passion of an entire family and a vision of sustainable hospitality. Within it, the eponymous restaurant stands apart, among furnishings and fabrics gathered by the owners over a lifetime, soft lighting and a service of the warmest character, an atmosphere that is almost magical pervades the space. The dishes showcase the territory’s finest ingredients, enhanced in carefully prepared presentations (the precision of the beef Wellington is emblematic), well presented and lifted by a delicate contemporary touch.

Name: La Cantina di Manuela
Description: The dining room in this young, dynamic restaurant is surrounded by bottles of wine. Elaborate dishes feature on the menu, with antipasti available in the evening. At lunchtime these are replaced by various salads aimed at a business clientele in a hurry. Milanese-style cutlets are the house speciality.

Name: La Cantinella
Description: Nestling in the hills, this small country restaurant delights guests with its relaxed atmosphere and Tuscan cuisine reinterpreted with a light, contemporary flavour. The paccheri pasta with a sausage ragù and celeriac cream is particularly delicious. The warm welcome offered by the owner, who always greets guests with a smile, adds to the appeal.

Name: La Capanna di Eraclio
Address: Località per Le Venezie 21, Codigoro, 44021, Italy
Description: Whenever we cross the threshold of Capanna di Eraclio, we are embraced by a rare and wonderful feeling, as if we were coming home. Opened in 1922 and now run by the fourth generation of the Soncini family, time seems to have stood still inn this restaurant, which offers the same authenticity that once transformed the inn into a kitchen. The atmosphere is nostalgic and familiar, understated but enhanced with touches of refined elegance. The aromas of the Po delta inspire a repertoire that celebrates water and land: delicate Goro sole, steamed and served with fresh mayonnaise; maltagliati pasta that captures the flavour of clams and savoy cabbage; and the obligatory “arost in umad” eel, golden and succulent, served with white polenta. A unique detail: the dining room is seven metres below sea level, offering guests a truly unique experience.

Name: La Casa degli Spiriti
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The Chignola family has been welcoming guests in this beautiful, restored farmhouse – a luxurious residence with one of the best views of Lake Garda – for almost 30 years. The ground-floor restaurant occupies a veranda surrounded by greenery facing the lake, where young chef Filippo (following in his father’s footsteps), together with his brother, sommelier Lorenzo, offers his guests an enjoyable dining experience with its roots in the cuisine of the region. The first-floor terrace is home to the Osteria Spiritino, which is more informal in both its cuisine and atmosphere. The remarkable wine cellar is housed in a room adorned with 18C frescoes and boasts more than 1 300 labels, with a particular focus on champagnes.

Name: La Cascina 1899
Description: Situated on the main road running alongside the sea, this pleasant restaurant with a large car park occupies a late-19C building that has been transformed into an attractive, rustic-style eatery with plenty of outdoor areas and air-conditioned rooms with exposed-stone walls and wooden ceilings that provide welcome respite from the heat of summer. It’s no surprise that fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu, although meat dishes also feature. The shop next door sells regional specialities, some produced by the restaurant itself, including the famous local bergamot citrus fruit.

Name: La Casina
Description: This large farmhouse with attractively renovated rooms overlooks the verdant landscapes of the Sarca valley from its wisteria-shaded summer pergola. Young chef Giada Miori prepares regional ingredients with skill and precision, serving specialities such as traditional potato fritters and “carne salada” (salted meat) preserved by the restaurant itself, as well as char, meat from the Trentino region and mushrooms. The Miori family also grow their own red berries, which often make an appearance in their desserts, along with their own sweet chestnuts.

Name: La Chiocciola
Address: via Runco 94/f, Quartiere di Portomaggiore, 44015, Italy
Description: A restaurant and an inn in a small country village, it’s the right place if you’re looking for hospitality and you appreciate the regional cuisine, made of snails and frogs, but also fish from the nearby sea. Something for every palate.

Name: La Ciambella
Address: Via dell'Arco della Ciambella 20, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: Originally from Testaccio, the district of Rome that is historically associated with butcher’s shops, chef Francesca Ciucci serves some of the best meat dishes in the Italian capital, including offal such as sweetbreads, a delicious Roman-style tripe dish and her own reinterpretation of “coda in carrozza” (an oxtail recipe). Meat dishes, often with a creative twist, take centre stage here, offering a delightful gastronomic experience that is not to be missed. There’s a large Travertine marble counter near the entrance, while the dining room is arranged around an open-view kitchen under a large skylight that bathes the entire room in natural light.

Name: La Ciotola
Description: A fresh, dynamic venue along the road to Pordenone, thoughtfully run by the Cover brothers. The kitchen tells tales of both land and sea: earthy, satisfying dishes such as the juicy young heifer entrecôte wrapped in golden potatoes with mustard dressing, and tempting seafood offerings such as the fragrant, comforting linguine with scampi alla busara. Quality ingredients take center stage! At lunch, the menu streamlines and service quickens, with lighter prices to match; come evening, the carte expands and the experience becomes complete and gratifying.

Name: La Coccinella
Description: This warm and welcoming establishment evokes the reassuring atmosphere of a country house. The menu, a single offering, presents a well-judged balance between meat and fish dishes, complemented by the daily specials presented verbally at the table, a detail that underlines a direct and convivial rapport with the guest. The wine list is well-constructed, with a predominantly local selection enriched by some interesting forays into older vintages, and prices marked by a most pleasing honesty.

Name: La Collina dei Ciliegi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated within the La Collina dei Ciliegi wine estate amid the verdant Valpantena hills, this first-floor restaurant (lift available) is home to two chefs – he is from Calabria, while she is from Puglia. Together they create exciting, modern Mediterranean cuisine using ingredients from their native regions, including their signature dish – homemade spaghetti served with a delicious, well-balanced 'nduja, smoked ricotta and tomato ristretto sauce. Top-quality local ingredients take pride of place, as demonstrated by the Brogna mutton, which is raised on site, barbecued and served with an exquisite caper sauce and seasonal mushroom pie. The concise wine list features labels from the Veneto alongside a few French options.

Name: La Conchiglia
Description: This small restaurant with a vaulted ceiling provides the setting for dishes that have by now become classics thanks to their focus on top-quality ingredients. The cuisine is light and simple rather than bold and elaborate, with a focus on bringing out the full flavour of the fish (a few meat dishes are also available). If you’re keen to learn more about Ligurian gastronomic specialities, take time between courses to chat with the friendly owner, who has an impressive knowledge of the region.

Name: La Conchiglia d'Oro
Address: Via Nazionale Adriatica nord, Pineto, 64025, Italy
Description: The rather anonymous location does not in any way detract from the quality of this historic restaurant, which is renowned for its excellent fish and seafood. The menu showcases fish from the Adriatic cooked using classical techniques with the occasional modern twist, such as in the tuna tartare seasoned with caramelised onions and citrus powder-flavoured mayonnaise. Considering the quality of the fish here, the prices are very reasonable. The beautifully presented desserts are an added bonus.

Name: La Corniola
Address: Via dei Mastri Lombardi 24, Pescocostanzo, 67033, Italy
Description: Known throughout Italy for its pillow lace, the small town of Pescocostanzo in the Parco della Maiella is one of the most beautiful in Italy. It is also home to the Relais Ducale hotel and its La Corniola restaurant, which is renowned for its excellent modern Abruzzo cuisine, including delicious, seasonal dishes made from different vegetables, potatoes and onions grown in the hotel’s own kitchen gardens. Simple yet elegant dining room.

Name: La Corte
Description: At the luxurious Villa Abbazia hotel, the sumptuous rooms, adorned with fireplaces, frescoes and period décor, and the equally elegant al fresco dining area for the warmer months provide the ideal setting for the cuisine of Giuseppe Francica, a young chef who was practically brought up in the family. His culinary offering ranges from tasting menus to à la carte options, featuring Venetian specialities – both from the sea and the land – alongside some more creative dishes and vegetarian options. A wide selection of wines, including by the glass. At lunchtime, there’s a bistro for a more informal meal.

Name: La Corte
Address: Via San Pancrazio 41, Palazzolo sull'Oglio, 25036, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in a tranquil street that leads to the centre of Palazzolo sull’Oglio, this stylish restaurant in a 16C palazzo boasts classic elegance and authentic cuisine which is delicious and full of flavour. Here, Aldo and his wife offer guests a warm and informal welcome, always with a smile on their lips.

Name: La Corte degli Dei
Description: Relax amid the greenery on the patio terrace at this restaurant, which is housed in an old palazzo full of timeless charm and history. The interior is as charming as the exterior, boasting delightful dining rooms teeming with character. The cuisine skilfully encompasses traditional classic favourites alongside more innovative dishes, offering guests a culinary journey that combines past and present with elegance and flavour.

Name: La Corte del Noce
Address: Via Alfredo Biffi 8, Villa d'Adda, 24030, Italy
Description: Housed within an 18C rural complex, a carefully appointed and welcoming dining room is graced by a striking fireplace. Outside, although the majestic walnut tree that long defined the identity of the house is no longer there, the memory of its shade still lingers over summer service. The kitchen pursues two distinctly separate paths: on the one hand, the signature dishes of "Radici", an expression of established classicism refined over more than forty years under the same stewardship; on the other, the "Visioni" offerings, more contemporary in character, exploring modern techniques such as fermentation and unexpected flavour combinations. A strong wine selection rounds off the experience, with equal care dedicated to the by-the-glass offering.

Name: La Cucina de' Mibabbo
Description: Exposed brickwork and lots of wood create a rustic, refined and welcoming atmosphere. Tuscan cuisine takes centre stage here, from the excellent charcuterie selection to the famous Florentine T-bone steak. When the weather warms up, a small covered terrace on the pavement offers the pleasure of al fresco dining.

Name: La Cucina dei Frigoriferi Milanesi
Description: An interesting location in the artistic-cultural setting of the Frigoriferi Milanesi industrial complex for this restaurant with a modern feel both in its decor and its market cuisine.

Name: La Cucina di Donna Carmela
Address: Contrada Grotte 7, località Carruba di Riposto, Riposto, 95018, Italy
Description: Generous Sicilian specialities reinterpreted with imagination and prepared using top-quality produce from the hotel’s orchards and vegetable garden, all beautifully presented in contemporary style, take centre stage here. There’s an extensive choice of meat and fish dishes showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte, which can be enjoyed either in the elegant dining room or on the attractive outdoor terrace shaded by palm trees. Courteous and professional service completes the picture.

Name: La Fermata
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the countryside around Alessandria, this 18C farmhouse has a modern, minimalist decor which serves as a backdrop for traditional Piedmontese cuisine with a clever modern twist. The chef offers just the right amount of creativity, with a focus on meat dishes and satisfying, memorable flavours that appeal to the emotions as well as the palate. Adding to the appeal, the elegant and exclusive ambience is the result of careful refurbishment, which has transformed the dining room into a triumph of art and design.

Name: La Ferrata
Description: The walls tell stories through photographs of locomotives and the warm glow of copper pots and lids at this century-old osteria. Rustic charm and conviviality define this welcoming venue, nestled in the picturesque historic center of Pordenone. Generous portions steeped in tradition emerge from the kitchen: cured meats, hearty cuts, and local cheeses share the stage with simple, authentic dishes such as beef cheek braised in Refosco wine, served alongside creamy polenta, a rustic, flavor-rich experience.

Name: La Fiaschetteria
Description: Set in an elegant 18th-century farmhouse nestled in the heart of Verdi’s homeland, this wine bar combines the charm of rural tradition with a contemporary, refined style. The cuisine focuses on fresh, homemade pasta and carefully selected seasonal ingredients, brought to the fore by simple yet delicious dishes, such as the unmissable fried porcini mushrooms when they are in season. Rounding off the experience is the passion of Vittorio, a true connoisseur of wine, who guides guests in choosing wines and, often, takes them on a tour of the cellar, enthusiastically sharing his knowledge of this world.

Name: La Filanda
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre, this restaurant occupies an old spinning mill ("filanda") that has been completely restored without losing any of its original charm. Here, self-taught chef Barbara serves traditional dishes reinterpreted with real flair, such as the involtino di ciaffagnone filled with Maremma beef on a bed of melted pecorino cheese and crispy leek. The chef’s husband oversees the wine list, which includes a selection of Tuscan labels.

Name: La Filanda
Description: Housed on the first floor of an old silkworm factory, with a contemporary-style dining room that opens out on to a beautiful terrace in fine weather, this restaurant is one of the few in the province to serve top-quality fish and seafood, including a good selection of raw options. The cooked dishes on offer demonstrate a light modern touch and are prepared whenever possible using vegetables from the restaurant’s own garden.

Name: La Foresteria
Address: Contrada Passo di Gurra SP 79 km 91, Menfi, 92013, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
