Description: Planeta’s elegance is reflected in this property nestled among Sicilian vineyards. The rooms bear the signature of the celebrated winery, while the restaurant offers modern Sicilian cuisine, with an à la carte menu and two tasting journeys. Don’t miss “Casa Planeta”: five iconic courses inspired by the monsù, the chefs of ancient noble residences.

Name: La Fortuna
Address: Via Ponte Rino 6, Campagnola Cremasca, 26010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated less than five minutes’ drive from the centre of Crema, this delightful contemporary-style trattoria boasts a modern dining room with a minimalist decor brightened by splashes of colour. The equally attractive cuisine is inspired mainly by Italian traditions, especially at lunchtime during the week (when the prices are very competitive), while in the evenings (at the weekend) dishes are enhanced by additional contemporary touches. The wine list is divided between Italian and French labels, including an excellent selection of champagnes.

Name: La Fossa del Grano
Description: A must for anyone looking for traditional home cooking and authentic cuisine from Puglia. Make sure you try the antipasti, and then move on to a first or main course.

Name: La Fugascina Ristorante
Description: Situated on a small square with an attractive outdoor space, this restaurant offers a menu which features fish from the lake and other seasonal produce prepared with both modern and traditional techniques, but always with a contemporary flair. The focus is on locally sourced (zero-mile, wherever possible) produce.

Name: La Gallina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Villa Sparina is an elegant rural resort named after its winery. The Orangerie hosts guests, whereas fine dining unfolds at La Gallina restaurant: amid rustic and elegant settings, contemporary cuisine is presented, drawing ample inspiration from Piedmont, as well as nearby Liguria (the dessert "Good Morning Genoa" playfully mimics breakfast with cappuccino and focaccia), though Campania references, the chef's homeland, never falter. Personalised wine selection: exclusively Champagne, abundant Piedmont choices, with particular emphasis on Barbaresco and Barolo.

Name: La Gritta
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Two of your senses will experience powerful marine sensations in this place. Your sight will be delighted with the enchanting view, especially from the terrace, and your taste will be tantalised by the imaginative, top - quality cuisine.

Name: La Kuccagna
Address: Via Milano 14, località Barbuzzera, Dovera, 26010, Italy
Description: La Kuccagna's fresh, quality offerings are bolstered by management that is always full of energy; menus range between land (tripe with legumes, squash and mushrooms) and sea (amberjack with coconut sauce, sea urchin and herbs), while the grill is always ready to accommodate the most suitable cuts of meat. A fine selection of wines starting with labels from beyond the Alps. The location is exquisitely bucolic, while the interior is modern and comfortable.

Name: La Kucina
Address: via Giulio De Petra 67, Foggia, 71121, Italy
Description: Welcoming and a short distance from the centre, the restaurant distinguishes itself through an architectural character of clear contemporary orientation and an equally modern gastronomic offering. The cooking ranges with balance between fish and meat dishes, interpreted through modern recipes and contemporary cooking techniques, among which the use of the Josper oven stands out, reserved in particular for selected meats left to mature in the dedicated dry-ageing unit. Among these, prized Iberian cuts feature prominently on the evening menu. At lunch, the offering broadens to include more immediate and accessible proposals, conceived to meet different tastes and budgets without any compromise on quality.

Name: La Leggenda dei Frati
Description: After an uphill approach if you’re arriving here on foot, you come into the Villa Bardini museum complex and from there into this elegant and welcoming restaurant which provides the setting for delicious, creative and modern cuisine. Here, chef Filippo Saporito, never one to rest on his laurels, continues to experiment and perfect his cuisine, which focuses mainly on Italian culinary traditions and a scrupulous selection of top-quality ingredients, preferably from sustainable supply chains (various types of meat, bread and pasta), all showcased on different menus, including a vegetarian option. In summer, enjoy your meal on the romantic terrace surrounded by greenery and the scents of herbs, with a glimpse of Santa Croce church as a backdrop. Although the centre of Florence is not far away, it seems as though you’re already in the Tuscan hills, even with the occasional sound of cicadas in the background.

Name: La Limonaia
Description: Away from the centre, nestled within a residential neighbourhood of quiet apartment buildings, this address surprises from the very first glance: the interior calls to mind a large veranda, furnished with an original and harmonious mix of objects and decorative pieces chosen with great taste – among them a piano that catches the eye – and looking out onto an intimate yet splendid terrace where, in the warmer months, dinner is taken in the shade of lemon trees. The cooking favours fire and the grill, from which generous, personal and intriguing dishes emerge, not always bound to tradition, but built around the finest the market has to offer. Worthy of particular note, for instance, is the ‘grilled fish collar finished all’acquapazza’, based on grouper, sampled during our most recent visit. The service, entrusted to a courteous and attentive all-female team, moves with natural ease, while the excellent background music contributes to an atmosphere of pleasingly elegant relaxation.

Name: La Locanda dei Beccaria
Description: Housed in the village’s historic wine cellar, this well - kept, rustic - style restaurant with typical wooden ceilings serves traditional, regional cuisine.

Name: La Locanda del Cardinale
Description: Situated right in the centre of Assisi, La Locanda del Cardinale occupies an old palazzo that is home to the perfectly preserved remains of a Roman villa dating back to 70 BC in a fascinating setting full of history. The menu features simple recipes such as crispy organic egg with asparagus and marjoram, as well as more elaborate, modern dishes including quail and Danubio brioche with barbecued artichoke. It’s not surprising that this delightful restaurant also boasts a superb wine cellar with an array of carefully chosen labels that will delight wine-enthusiasts.

Name: La Locanda di Fabio e Vale
Description: Young, informal and friendly owners Fabio and Vale welcome guests to their restaurant in Offanengo, just a few kilometres from Crema. A good choice for anyone looking for a change from traditional cuisine, the restaurant serves moderately creative dishes including a good selection of fish options (the Mazara del Vallo red prawns served with green gazpacho, caviar and lemon are particularly delicious).

Name: La Locanda di Piero
Address: Via Roma 34, strada per Dueville, Montecchio Precalcino, 36030, Italy
Description: Housed in a small country villa with the ambience of a private residence, this restaurant boasts a dining room with a welcoming fireplace in winter and a veranda full of natural light, giving it a classic feel that makes it perfect for an elegant and romantic dinner. The cuisine is distinctive and full of substance, featuring a selection of meat and fish dishes that includes classic and creative options alike.

Name: La Locanda di Pietracupa
Address: Via Madonna di Pietracupa 31, San Donato in Poggio, 50028, Italy
Description: The gastronomic dream of every traveler in Tuscany takes shape at this restaurant, housed in a quintessential Chianti farmhouse with a shaded terrace dedicated to summer service. The menu presents a notable procession of regional flavors guided by the seasons: pici with salt cod, three peppers, and pistachio pesto; squab with truffle vinaigrette; ricotta and citrus cake with ginger sauce… culminating in the unmissable Fiorentina, the territory’s timeless icon.

Name: La Locandiera
Description: At the bottom of a steep valley, a rustic restaurant that offers fine cuisine, much appreciated in the area, with a great preference for local products. Old traditional recipes are revisited with a personal touch.

Name: La Loggia Bistrò
Description: Tucked into a slightly secluded courtyard yet still in the heart of the city, this venue offers alfresco service of discreet charm during the summer months. The interiors surprise with dramatic hot-air balloons descending from the ceiling, design details that help create a distinctive and welcoming atmosphere. The culinary offering moves between dishes rooted in local tradition and more creative forays, including some appealing fish options.

Name: La Luge
Address: Perreres, loc. Varvoyes, Breuil Cervinia, 11021, Italy
Description: Situated in a tranquil, panoramic location on the road to Breuil-Cervinia (less than 4km away), this old farm has been transformed over the past decade into an intimate little hotel with a good restaurant decorated in attractive mountain style and enhanced by a fireplace that is always lit in winter. Here, you can enjoy simple, authentic cuisine prepared from top-quality ingredients with careful attention paid to seasonality. The owner himself oversees the well-stocked wine cellar.

Name: La Lumira
Description: In a town synonymous with tortellini, Lumira offers an authentically regional experience with a touch of modernity; contemporary interiors and warm service ensure a memorable visit. The menu draws on the generosity of Emilian and Romagnolo cuisines, a natural expression of the chef-owner, born right here. The house-made fresh pastas are essential: from tortellini in capon broth to pumpkin tortelli dressed with garlic, olive oil, chili, and broccoli. Special praise goes to the bollito misto, served with excellently crafted sauces.

Name: La Madia
Description: This authentic rural trattoria overlooking the valley and Franciacorta specialises in regional produce and typical Italian cuisine. Each dish on the menu lists the origin of the ingredients used, plus the name and address of the producer. Specialities include tagliolini pasta sautéed in a walnut sauce with tuna. Top quality cuisine offering excellent value for money.

Name: La Maison Delfino
Address: Via Lagrange 4, borgo Mercato, Moncalieri, 10024, Italy
Description: This small, elegant restaurant outside the centre is enthusiastically run by two brothers: round tables and well - kept dining room for savoring seafood specialities.

Name: La Maison de Filip
Description: Situated at the entrance to the pedestrian section of the beautiful city of Trento, this intimate restaurant has a modern, minimalist and vaguely Nordic style, with just a few solid wood tables and stools of different sizes. The menu features a concise selection of carefully thought-out dishes, with starters, first and main courses (meat, fish or vegetarian) that are elegant, well prepared and contemporary in style. Beautiful presentation completes the picture.

Name: La Marianna
Description: A historic seafood trattoria of Rimini near the Tiberius Bridge, various managements have succeeded one another since 1908, yet the current proprietor remains true to the spirit of the place: almost exclusively seafood dishes, prepared simply and straightforwardly to showcase the freshness of the ingredients, served in modest yet atmospheric dining rooms with a convivial and informal ambiance.

Name: La Martinatica
Description: Housed in an old mill, this restaurant boasts a warm and welcoming dining room crowned by wood beams and elegant furnishings. The menu offers a selection of meat and fish dishes, although the latter are the main speciality of the owner-chef, who can usually be seen taking orders in the dining room. The raw seafood option demonstrates the skill and imagination of the chef, with its array of small bites which are both creative and delicious. The attractive outdoor space is perfect for summer dining.

Name: La Masseria
Address: Via Chiesa 61, località Marzaglia, Modena, 41123, Italy
Description: A corner of Puglia at Modena’s doorstep: not a masseria, but an old mill that welcomes with the aromas and flavors of the heel of Italy. Vegetables reign supreme – stuffed peppers, eggplant parmigiana, fava purée with chicory – while, despite being in egg-pasta territory, fresh Mediterranean interpretations shine. Among the entrées, ample space is given to meats cooked over live embers, the authentic heart of Puglian tradition. To close, desserts arrive in a large basket: small delights, often featuring dried fruit and chocolate, celebrating a simple and genuine indulgence.

Name: La Meridiana
Description: In business for over 50 years, this long-established, centrally located restaurant has changed its look over the years and is now a modern bistro with an attractive outdoor summer space overlooking the magical town centre. Here, the owner-chef serves fish prepared in two different ways, either in typical Italian tradition or in a style inspired by his native Spain – his paella is definitely worth sampling! The front of house is overseen by the owner’s friendly wife, who is also at hand to help with your wine choices.

Name: La Nicchia
Description: This tastefully decorated restaurant is housed in a late - 18C building, which is marked on an old map from the Napoleonic era. Here the best local ingredients are selected to create regional dishes with the occasional contemporary twist.

Name: La Nigra
Description: Located in the old port, it is a restaurant with tasteful and very pleasant interiors, where chef-patron Gaetano, together with his wife Sonia, welcomes guests first thing in the morning for breakfast and a wide selection of homemade pastries. The kitchen offers a wide selection of traditional island and Sicilian dishes, prepared with the day's catch, such as the delicious “Paccheri alla carbonara di mare”, made with swordfish, raw prawns, amberjack roe and mullet bottarga. It is, of course, essential to save room for their delicious desserts, including a signature deconstructed cannolo.

Name: La Notizia 53
Description: Although situated away from the tourist centre, Enzo Coccia’s pizzeria continues to be considered one of the best places for pizza in Campania. Featuring classic Neapolitan pizzas with soft, stringy dough, the menu offers traditional and creative toppings alike. The “'mpustarella”, a five-grain and wholemeal flour roll with different fillings, more than compensates for the lack of “fritti” on the menu. The first historic restaurant at number 53 has now been joined by a second address at number 94/a nearby.

Name: La Nunziadêina
Description: A landmark occasion: in 2026, the fourth generation celebrated one hundred years of history of this establishment, also with its inclusion in the Guide. The venture was first set in motion by Annunciata in Cittanova, before closing in 2002 and reopening four years later at its present address, directly opposite the magnificent Abbey of Nonantola, taking on the name that had long served as its founder’s nickname: Nunziadêina. Since then, the common thread has remained the same: the delicacies and indulgent treats of Emilia-Romagna.The dining rooms are homely, yet attentive to detail; fresh flowers on every table lend a pleasing touch, while a fire crackling at the back of the room offers a foretaste of one of the house’s specialities, charcoal grilled meat. Alongside this, there is always fresh pasta, outstanding charcuterie and a wealth of traditional recipes, all rounded off by the customary irresistible dessert trolley. An impressive wine list completes the offering. A truly deserving venue!

Name: La Palomba
Description: Boasting the attractive ambience of a typical Italian trattoria, La Palomba has been run by the Cinti family since 1965 and is now in the hands of the third generation. The menu features Umbrian specialities including delicious home-made umbrichelli pasta served with various sauces.

Name: La Passion
Address: Via San Nicolò 5/b, Vandoies di Sopra, Vintl, 39030, Italy
Description: A small, cosy, completely wood - panelled stube has been set up in this residential building. The menus are traditional but inventive.

Name: La Perla
Description: Housed in a historic palazzo on the charming Piazza della Motta in the town centre, this restaurant is one you will immediately want to share with family and friends thanks to its delicious cuisine. The menu focuses mainly on fish and seafood (including impressive raw fish dishes) although a few meat options are also available. Good choice of wines and spirits.

Name: La Piazzetta Lake Como
Description: Tucked among the picturesque streets of Cernobbio, this modern, inviting bistro blends retro charm with contemporary furnishings and personalized touches. At the entrance, a cozy lounge with a bar counter beckons guests to linger over aperitifs and signature cocktails, while in summer the outdoor terrace offers moments of pleasure amid the lake breeze. In the kitchen, a young, dynamic team reinterprets Mediterranean flavors through contemporary recipes that are both authentic and aromatic. Not to be missed: “Pappa e Gambero,” crusted shrimp atop tomato and basil pappa, and “Tagliolino ai tre pomodori,” a tribute to refined simplicity.

Name: La Piemontese
Address: Via San Martino 48, Mariano Comense, 22066, Italy
Description: The focus at La Piemontese, a simple yet modern restaurant with a convenient car park, is mainly on meat dishes, although game and fresh truffles also feature in season, plus there’s a generous business menu at lunchtime. An enjoyable dining experience that offers good value for money.

Name: La Pineta
Address: Via Gualco 82, località Struppa, Genoa, 16165, Italy
Description: Now a gastronomic institution in the city, in a secluded setting immersed in nature, La Pineta occupies the ground floor of a nondescript building in which the simple, “dated” yet comfortable decor provides the backdrop. Although there is a menu (but no wine list), the dishes are usually announced in person at your table by the owners. Simple, traditional and abundant cuisine which is mainly cooked on the open grill in the centre of the room, including meat (its signature speciality) and fish.

Name: La Pista
Address: Centro Commerciale Lingotto - via Nizza 262, Turin, 10126, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The top floor of the Lingotto shopping center – a quintessential Turin landmark, once a Fiat factory whose rooftop test track has been transformed into a visitable botanical garden – is the site of an easily reached restaurant thanks to clear signage at the entrance. Once seated, guests may choose from four tasting menus (all available à la carte): the Piedmontese tradition of Radici, the contemporary restraint of Gli Essenziali, the vegetarian Botanic World and the creative Zero/100 km/h, as well as Trust, a ‘blind’ journey guided by the kitchen’s sensitivity. Whichever the choice, the experience turns out to be convincing: solid, harmonious dishes with clear, perfectly-calibrated flavors.

Name: La Porta Antica
Address: Via Quarto dei Mille 16, Brescia, 25128, Italy
Description: Contemporary interiors and a prime location in a quiet residential neighborhood provide the backdrop for a seafood-focused kitchen that balances measured creativity with precise flavors. The shellfish selection excels: from prized Sicilian red prawns to steamed jumbo shrimp, refined and elevated by a soft bean purée with crispy guanciale.

Name: La Porta Restaurant
Address: Piazza Vieira de Mello 4, Bologna, 40128, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a futuristic building which extends like a bridge across Via Stalingrado, La Porta Restaurant is a highly versatile establishment. Set within a futuristic building that spans Via Stalingrado like a bridge, La Porta Restaurant is a versatile venue: the garage provides access to the café’s delicacies and, at lunchtime, the bistro opens with simple dishes, while gourmet diners can enjoy the evening menu in the restaurant with its elegant wooden decor. The menu features an array of fish, meat and vegetable options, while service comes courtesy of a mainly female team, all of whom are extremely friendly and welcoming. With some references to the culinary traditions of Emilia, the kitchen serves dishes featuring ingredients (both meat and fish) and recipes from various regions, complemented by the chef's creative touch.

Name: La Péniche
Address: Via Lungo Brugiano 3, Marina di Massa, 54100, Italy
Description: A corner of France along the Brugiano Canal. We eat in a stilt house with original and romantic settings that marry colonial style and Parisian model with a very warm and romantic result. Vast à la carte choices, there is something for everyone, from a list devoted entirely to oysters to some of Spain's most famous products, such as pata negra and anchovies from the Cantabrian Sea, as well as, of course, many more elaborate meat and fish dishes. In summer, tables on the raft are coveted, recalling the péniches on the Seine even more. Best to make reservations well in advance.

Name: La Quartina
Description: Outdoor service in the summer on the terrace with an exceptional view of the lake. Original furnishings and extremely well kept rooms. Menu including lake specialities. The rooms are simple, comfortable and always neat and tidy.

Name: La Refezione
Description: An imaginative cuisine for the elegant "club - house" located inside a sports centre; managed by two great enthusiasts of the culinary art. You will receive a hearty welcome.

Name: La RiMa
Description: This restaurant in the heart of the town serves excellent contemporary cuisine (meat and fish, plus a few vegetarian options). The menu features dishes such as fregola sarda (a type of couscous) with tomato, buffalo mozzarella, friggitelli peppers and fried capers, with a personalised twist added by talented owner-chef Matteo Ridoni.

Name: La Ripa
Description: Housed within a striking complex carved out of the rock – which in the 15th century was home to a convent – La Ripa takes its name from the spectacular panoramic cliff over which it looks out. The atmosphere still retains the timeless charm of an ancient cave, while in the milder months the tables are set out among the characteristic alleyways of the historic centre, offering guests an experience immersed in the beauty of the village. In the kitchen, the chef, with a contemporary sensitivity, carries on the culinary journey begun decades ago by his mother, offering an elegant and refined cuisine that reinterprets local traditions with modern touches. The menu, offering a balance of seafood and meat dishes, showcases local produce through carefully prepared dishes and authentic flavours.

Name: La Ripadoro
Description: Tucked away in the small medieval village of Rivalto, with stunning views of the surrounding Tuscan hills, the Ripadoro agriturismo is home to this rustic yet elegant farm-restaurant serving traditional Tuscan dishes made from produce grown on the property. There’s an authentic charcoal grill which is used to cook classic ribeye steak, as well as the superb “girarrosto” – boned pigeon and quail served with potato rosti, yellow carrots with ginger and Jerusalem artichokes in foil. Make sure you save space for one of the delicious desserts! In summer, it’s well worth booking one of the outdoor tables under the shade of large lime trees.

Name: La Risacca Blu
Address: Viale Tunisia, angolo via Tadino, Milan, 20124, Italy
Description: The first thing you see when you enter this restaurant near the central railway station is its large display of fresh fish, all delivered daily. The menu features a selection of classic and authentic fish and seafood options, with pride of place given to its raw fish dishes.

Name: La Ristobottega
Address: Via Vittorio Veneto 46A, Reggio Calabria, 89121, Italy
Description: As the name suggests, this restaurant is divided into two sections: a shop on one side, which sells local products such as tempting salumi and cheeses (they also serve informal lunches at midday); and on the other, in the evening, an attractive bistro with wooden tables and soft lighting, where you can enjoy delicious cuisine. Among the fish dishes (aged on site), we particularly recommend the grouper fillet with vegetable caponatina and raw scampi on a bed of mashed potato, while the meat options include top-quality cuts such as Wagyu beef. A small outdoor space on the pavement completes the picture.

Name: La Rosa dei Venti
Address: Via Piero della Francesca 34, Milan, 20154, Italy
Description: Simple, authentic seafood cuisine anchored in tradition: the roasted turbot is emblematic, served in season with porcini mushrooms and potatoes, a testament to a philosophy built entirely on freshness and clean flavors. The recipes draw on Sardinia and, more broadly, Italian cuisine, free of pretense or unnecessary flourishes. The recommendation is to trust the owner and be guided through the day’s off-menu offerings, often tied to what has just arrived from the market and perfectly capturing the soul of the place.

Name: La Rosina
Description: With over 100 years of history behind it, La Rosina is still looking good, thanks to renovation work carried out a few years ago which has given the restaurant a new look. Situated in an attractive location in the hills around Marostica, this excellent restaurant is a sound choice for good food in the province of Vicenza, serving modern regional and Italian dishes which are full of flavour. Enjoy beautiful views of the surrounding hills from the guestrooms.

Name: La Saletta
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the seafront promenade in the historic centre of Alghero, this small gem run by Gian Luca Chessa offers the best of Sardinia. The cuisine is showcased on different tasting menus, including Rivoluzione (creative yet with a regional focus); Radici (vegetables take centre stage); Riviera (local fish); and Cortile (traditionally inspired dishes). We particularly enjoyed the gnocchi stuffed with sheep’s ricotta cheese, beetroot sauce and Sardinian scorzone truffle – a real treat! All the wines are available by the glass, so don’t hesitate to ask the sommelier for recommendations.

Name: La Sbornia a Verduno
Description: This building, almost cube-like in shape with large floor-to-ceiling windows that offer breathtaking views of the beautiful surrounding countryside, is striking for its modern, contemporary design, with a delightful outdoor space that is perfect for alfresco dining. Originally from Puglia, talented owner-chef Carmela Straniero fell in love with the Langhe having spent time working in England and Italy. Her refined and highly personalised cuisine fully respects culinary traditions and is prepared using top-quality local ingredients.

Name: La Serra
Address: Via Marconi 169, località Belvedere Fornillo, Positano, 84017, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Slightly removed from the lively centre of Positano, the restaurant of Hotel Le Agavi enjoys a privileged position, with a panoramic terrace from which the gaze sweeps across Positano, Praiano and the Amalfi coastline, particularly evocative at sunset. The interior dining room, with its broad picture windows, extends the dialogue with the landscape even on cooler evenings. Chef Alberto Annarumma interprets Mediterranean cuisine through the concept of "tradition in evolution", reinterpreting the great flavours of Campania with contemporary technique and elegant presentation, without losing sight of the authenticity of the raw material. The lemon of the Amalfi Coast recurs as a guiding thread throughout the menu, alongside carefully selected local ingredients. The offering comprises three tasting menus – seafood, meat, and vegetable – alongside the à la carte. Among the most interesting dishes, the handmade prawn ravioli stand out: a delicate fresh pasta casing enclosing a refined crustacean mousse, served with Jerusalem artichoke cream, prawn bisque and parsley: a polished preparation that enhances the flavour of the sea with balance and technical precision.

Name: La Società Milano
Description: Situated near Porta Venezia and its lush gardens, Giulia and Andrea’s restaurant boasts a warm and original ambience. Three dining rooms adorned with tapestries and an entrance with a fine white marble fireplace act as the setting for Mediterranean cuisine with the occasional exotic twist. Don’t miss the amberjack caponata in which the ceviche flavours contrast with the sweetness of the fried breaded aubergine.

Name: La Sosta di Ottone III
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Ask for directions to this restaurant when you make your booking, as you’ll need to leave your vehicle in a private car park at the entrance to the village and then make your way uphill on foot. Situated in one of Liguria’s most typical and picturesque inland villages with views of the sea in the distance, the restaurant offers outdoor dining under a wisteria in fine weather. The menu features a small choice of regional dishes, with the same focus on Liguria evident on the wine list.

Name: La Spigola
Address: Via Cristoforo Colombo 19, Golfo Aranci, 07020, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Set on a beautiful beach of fine white sand, where there is also a small beach club, this restaurant wins you over at first glance with its relaxed and authentically Mediterranean atmosphere. The sea view, the undisputed highlight of the experience, complements the cuisine created by Roberto Pisano, whose dishes are characterised by their freshness and lightness. The menu takes the form of a single tasting menu comprising five or seven courses – a true declaration of love for the sea and its bounty, interpreted with a contemporary sensitivity and a strong commitment to environmental responsibility. A focus on the conservation of marine resources, the use of each part of the fish, and the use of vegetables from the restaurant’s own vegetable garden are, in fact, the cornerstones of the restaurant’s philosophy. One of the most interesting dishes is the squid marinated in shio koji with an onion emulsion, rich in umami notes and great elegance. Also worth noting is the wine list, which, alongside an already extensive and carefully curated selection, features a section dedicated to ‘Orfanelli’ containing prestigious wines from all over the world, including historic vintages from the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s. At lunchtime, the menu takes on a more informal feel, while those looking for a different experience might want to head to the Bistrot di Mare, which offers a more relaxed and convivial atmosphere.

Name: La Sponda
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: From the elegant dining room at Le Sirenuse – one of the most iconic and charming venues on the Amalfi Coast – as soon as the weather permits, guests move out onto the splendid panoramic terrace, which overlooks the spectacular cascade of houses in Positano and is lit up in the evening by hundreds of candles. In the kitchen, Gennaro Russo presents a menu that celebrates the flavours of the South through vibrant, fresh and well-balanced dishes, inspired by Mediterranean and Campania traditions but given a contemporary twist. The result is an elegant and harmonious culinary journey that authentically captures the many nuances of southern Italy.

Name: La Taverna del Leone
Description: Situated three kilometres east of Positano, this family-run restaurant has been in business for almost 60 years and is one of the most popular in the region – and for good reason. The classic-style dining room with a striking open-view kitchen adorned with local blue-and-white ceramics provides the setting for meat and fish dishes (mainly local) prepared from top-quality ingredients with the occasional personal touch.

Name: La Taverna di Bacco
Description: A small restaurant just a stone’s throw from the sea which is memorable for its chic decor and intimate ambience. The cuisine combines traditional influences with an innovative approach resulting in ambitious, creative and modern dishes. The wine list is particularly worthy of note.

Name: La Taverna di Fra' Fiusch
Description: Nestling in a charming hill town, this restaurant will delight visitors looking for traditional cuisine with an updated, contemporary flavour. Specialities include agnolotti (a type of ravioli) and Piedmontese fritto misto (fried seafood and vegetables).

Name: La Tavola
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: The restaurant at the Il Porticciolo hotel is sure to delight lake lovers: once you’ve left your car in the car park, take the lift down to the dining room, where the windows look out over the water and offer views of the opposite shore of Lake Maggiore. There is a choice of three blind tasting menus comprising four, five or six courses, inspired respectively by the chef’s classic dishes, the local region and, more generally, Italian cuisine. If, on the other hand, you’d prefer to choose your own dishes (at least three), there’s also a short menu.

Name: La Terrazza
Description: Overlooking the Torbole lakefront, just steps from the center, this small restaurant with a panoramic veranda is a tribute to the flavors of the lake. The cuisine is meticulous in its details, with dishes that tell the story of the territory through refined presentations. The tasting menu celebrates lake products, while the à la carte selection strikes a balance between lake, land, and garden. Don’t miss the “Del Leone” spaghetti: freshwater prawns, ginger, and lime in a fresh and spicy embrace.

Name: La Terrazza
Description: A salon en plein air overlooking Asolo’s historical center, this charming spot offers attentive service and Italian cuisine presented with a modern touch. The menu spans land and sea, with vegetarian options as well. A classic and welcoming atmosphere makes it an ideal setting for a romantic dinner.

Name: La Torre
Description: Situated on the ground floor of Spilimbergo’s beautiful medieval castle, this restaurant has equally beautiful interiors which welcome guests into a romantic atmosphere, steeped in history but accompanied by every contemporary comfort. For a really special dinner for two, we highly recommend booking the intimate alcove table. The cuisine is modern and beautifully presented with a special focus on meat, although the fish dishes are every bit as delicious.

Name: La Torre
Description: Overlooked by a medieval tower in the main town square, this restaurant is perfect for anyone keen on classic, traditional cuisine. House specialities include dishes cooked over the barbecue grill.

Name: La Tradizione - Cucina Casalinga
Description: A corner of traditional Apulia to be experienced in a trattoria in the centre, in a typical and pleasantly homely atmosphere. The dishes are listed verbatim, not to be missed are the series of starters, but also the characteristic fresh pastas.

Name: La Veranda
Description: Situated a few metres from the lake in the centre of the village, this welcoming and long-established family restaurant boasts a dining room that transforms into a veranda with outdoor dining in summer. The cuisine here is traditional, with generous portions of fish from the lake and sea.

Name: La Veranda
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: In summer, the terrace by the lake offers a splendid view and is the perfect setting for dishes that highlight Italian tradition but also satisfy the most cosmopolitan palates. The foie gras escalope served with parsnips, apple compote and pink grapefruit, for example, is excellent. If the weather's not so great, you'll be just as comfortable in the elegant indoor dining room overlooking the lake (the most popular) or the garden. The evening dress code is elegant (we are, after all, inside the luxurious Villa d'Este hotel).

Name: La Veranda del Color
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the luxurious setting of the Color Hotel, guests can take a seat at the tables on a glass-enclosed veranda (which opens out in fine weather) facing the swimming pool. The cuisine is technical, refined and creative; the menu features both meat and fish dishes, with few references to local lake produce but rather Mediterranean influences, making for a sophisticated and elegant evening.

Name: Ladinia
Address: Strada Pedercorvara 10, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: Both the Berghotel Ladinia and its restaurant of the same name boast a warm, vintage Alpine-style ambience, with wood decor that tells the story of this business which opened as a simple inn back in 1930. Little has changed since then and guests return here time after time thanks to the warm welcome and attention to detail offered by the Costa family. The traditional cuisine has the occasional modern twist, while the few Ladin-style guestrooms are decorated with a profusion of wood.

Name: Lalibera
Description: In the heart of Alba, just a stone's throw from the cathedral, this refined and elegant restaurant offers guests a warm and simple welcome. The aromas of Langhe cuisine combine with the chefs' creativity to deliver dishes that reflect the region's flavours with taste and harmony. The wine list, lovingly curated by Flavia, offers a wide variety of labels, with Piedmontese wines taking centre stage.

Name: Lampl Stube
Description: In the elegant setting of the Lamm boutique hotel, in the heart of the historic centre, Marc Oberhofer has created a culinary experience that offers a contemporary take on mountain cuisine. A self-taught chef with great sensitivity, he crafts his tasting menus by weaving together technique, local produce and personal memories. The set menus, named after his parents Hanni and Leo and available as five- or ten-course options, pay tribute to his family roots and the passion for cooking he has nurtured since childhood. His dishes impress with their elegant presentation, characterised by a careful choice of colours, but above all by the balance of flavours. Among the most impressive dishes, the wild spinach tortelli with a morel emulsion stand out – delicate yet full of character. The experience takes place in an intimate dining room with just three tables, which must be booked well in advance, where an alpine atmosphere blends with a minimalist, contemporary design. In the dining room, Gianluca Rovai attends to guests with professionalism and discretion, guiding them through the wine pairings and expertly explaining the chef’s culinary philosophy.

Name: Langosteria
Description: This is an establishment of soft lighting and music, a highly fashionable address and among the best known in the city. The elegant atmosphere provides the setting for a culinary offering entirely dedicated to seafood, interpreted through classic preparations that are never banal, enriched by indulgent, personal touches. The selection of raw fish is extensive and carefully curated, closely tied to the daily market arrivals. Also of note is the wine list, comprehensive and well constructed, featuring important and prestigious labels.

Name: Langosteria Paraggi
Address: Via Paraggi a Mare 1, Paraggi, 16038, Italy
Description: The elegant Milanese style of the famous Langosteria restaurant has been given a maritime and holiday feel in its seasonal sibling which is housed within the Bagni Fiore overlooking the small yet stunning Paraggi bay. Langosteria Paraggi boasts a vintage decor which is at the same time glamorous and up-to-date, views of the beach and the sea, and a menu focusing on delicious fresh fish and seafood such as oysters and shellfish.

Name: Lanzani Bottega & Bistrot
Address: Via Albertano da Brescia 41, Brescia, 25127, Italy
Description: This modern restaurant (open from 7am to 11pm), once the family butcher’s, is also a delicatessen and wine boutique. It serves top-quality produce such as Pata Negra and other hams, anchovies from the Cantabrian sea, an excellent selection of cheeses and more elaborate dishes. At mealtimes, the venue transforms into a proper restaurant, with a smaller menu available at lunchtime.

Name: Lapprodo
Address: Via Roma 22, Vibo Valentia Marina, 89900, Italy
Description: This restaurant close to the port of Vino Marina is a long-established favourite in the area and is renowned for its seafood cuisine which showcases traditional recipes made using the best-quality fish. In summer, make the most of the dining space on the delightful outdoor veranda.

Name: Laurin
Description: In the magnificent setting of the exclusive Parkhotel Laurin, this restaurant is one of the best in Bolzano, boasting a Liberty-style dining room and tree-shaded tables in the garden for summer dining. The traditional cuisine also includes a few modern touches with ingredients and techniques from all over Italy and beyond, such as the grilled trout and leek terrine wrapped in nori algae in the shape of a flower. The menu features meat and fish dishes, with a small section dedicated to traditional local specialities.

Name: Lazaroun
Address: Via Del Platano 21, Santarcangelo di Romagna, 47822, Italy
Description: The prototype of a typical Romagna restaurant, run by an efficient and friendly family team. Excellent choice of high - quality first and second courses, including fresh pasta, hams and salamis, meat options and grilled dishes. An interesting feature of the restaurant is the presence of ancient tufa caves in the basement. Created around 400 AD and part of an intricate network of underground passages, they were later used by the Malatesta family as an escape route and are now open to the public.

Name: Le Baccanti
Description: Simple premises with two large windows overlooking its kitchens. It serves imaginative dishes where tradition and creativity become one. Informal service.

Name: Le Beccherie
Description: In the heart of Treviso, what was once a stronghold of traditional cuisine is now a restaurant with contemporary appeal, where a carefully curated atmosphere is matched by sophisticated design; the most coveted tables overlook the canal, providing a particularly atmospheric setting. The gastronomic proposal combines fantasy and references to the territory; in addition to the à la carte, two tasting menus are available: "We" brings together a selection of the most representative dishes of chefs Beatrice Simonetti and Manuel Gobbo, while "Beccherie 1962" pays homage to the sign's historic cuisine, reinterpreted with a modern twist. Among the most interesting creations is Risotto alla Cima, the restaurant's iconic dish, as well as Tiramisù.

Name: Le Cantine
Address: Via cantine cattaneo 1, Sestri Levante, 16039, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A few management changes, but they are still in charge: Enrico in the kitchen and Nadia in the dining room. Already in a bucolic setting, but just a few steps from the centre and the sea, preceded by its own vegetable gardens, you dine within the restored 1590 walls of a former oil cellar, in a pleasantly rustic and romantic atmosphere overflowing with decorations. But the best comes with the cuisine, with no fish menu at all, with a strong focus on self-produced vegetables and succulent meat dishes, mostly barbecued with olive wood, along with a good selection of wines, mostly regional and high-quality.

Name: Le Case della Saracca
Description: Situated in the delightful Saracca district (Monforte’s old historic centre), this restaurant occupies an old, restored house with a glass and steel decor that provides a harmonious contrast with the building’s original features. Tables are arranged on different levels connected by a series of vertiginous staircases. Quiet and intimate, the restaurant serves a dual purpose: there’s a wine bar for aperitifs, while the dining room provides the backdrop for dishes from the region and further afield. Superb wine list with various labels available by the glass, plus guestrooms that offer the chance to spend the night in this unique setting.

Name: Le Cedrare
Description: You head through a delightful garden to get to this restaurant housed in a room once used as a conservatory for citrus trees in the 18C Villa Perez-Pompei-Sagramoso. Here, the owner-chef serves delicious regional cuisine which he prepares with particular attention to beautiful presentation. He also makes use of extra-virgin olive oil produced in the countryside around Illasi, with a small selection of oils available for tasting, including the restaurant’s own.

Name: Le Cementine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This rustic, vintage-style country restaurant run by the Alajmo brothers stands on the banks of the Sile river, just a few minutes from the Venetian lagoon, and overlooks a vegetable garden, vineyard and beautiful green meadows. The cuisine demonstrates a strong focus on seasonal, regional ingredients, featuring meat and fish alike, with vegetables taking centre stage in many of the dishes.

Name: Le Chiavi d'Oro
Description: Situated in Arezzo’s historic centre, this restaurant boasts an original, minimalist ambience with an elegant wood decor. The main focus here is on the cuisine, which is among the best not only in the city but also in the region. Skilful interpretations of traditional dishes, with a focus on Tuscany, where the gastronomic pleasure increases with each course.

Name: Le Cicale
Description: A grandparents’ home has evolved into a charming bistro-like restaurant, while outdoors, the owner-curated garden beckons a peek. The cuisine is simple and classic, comforting, with certain regional dishes alongside fish courses, while an entire menu page is dedicated to risottos.

Name: Le Cicale in Città
Description: A classic-style dining room adorned with mirrors and silverware acts as the backdrop for fish and seafood dishes at this restaurant. The raw fish is particularly excellent, as are the mupa (a little-known fish that lives in the deep waters of the Mediterranean), prawns (in season) and home-made primi served with delicious sauces, such as the chicken plin with brown gravy. For special occasions, we recommend the table to the rear of the room near the arte povera-style dresser. Cheerful, friendly service adds to the appeal.

Name: Le Colonne
Address: Via Benefattori 7, Santa Maria Maggiore, 28857, Italy
Description: In the small historic center of town, a couple with comprehensive management experience operates this well maintained, modest restaurant offering eclectic cuisine.

Name: Le Colonne
Description: In a dining room with marble columns and flooring and enhanced by a beautiful grand piano, Rossana Marziale serves Mediterranean dishes that showcase the ingredients of Caserta and the Campania with a perfect balance of comforting classic flavours and creative modern ideas. Buffalo mozzarella takes pride of place here, presented in many different ways, including in some of the desserts.

Name: Le Fucine Gourmet
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The modern Le Fucine hotel is home to two restaurants with almost identical names: Le Fucine Brasserie and, of course, Le Fucine Gourmet. The latter welcomes guests into an elegant dining room featuring contemporary, minimalist design: clean lines and spotlights that caress the tables, creating an intimate atmosphere. In the centre, like a live stage, is the open kitchen, where chef Andrea Fantini, from Friuli, moves with confident gestures amidst steam and aromas, sharing the experiences he has accumulated over time with every dish. Two tasting menus invite you on a sensory journey: the first reinvents local traditions, while the second is inspired by the chef's memories of his travels. For those who love balance, there is also a third, shorter menu that combines elements of both. To complete the experience, sommelier Nicholas Chiarossi will guide you through the wine cellar's labels, skilfully selecting the perfect wine pairing for each dish.

Name: Le Grenier
Description: Situated in the heart of Saint Vincent, this restaurant has the feel of an old granary (“grenier” in the Aosta valley dialect) with an open fireplace, sheaves of wheat hanging from the ceiling, and old tools on the walls. In this surprising setting, the Mazzotti brothers’ cuisine delights guests with carefully prepared and unexpectedly modern dishes, including home-made bread, specialities from the Aosta Valley and traditional Italian dishes (a few fish options also feature on the menu). The extensive wine list showcases a selection of carefully chosen labels from the region.

Name: Le Lampare al Fortino
Address: Via Tiepolo, molo Sant'Antonio, Trani, 76125, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Depending on the season, you can take a seat in two completely different but equally breathtaking settings: inside, in a former 14th century church, in the milder climate on the covered terrace overlooking the Trani harbour basin. The cuisine includes dishes with a predominantly Mediterranean character with more fish, but also some meat dishes.

Name: Le Logge del Vignola
Description: This small establishment is a good spot in the old town centre. Its tables are a bit cramped but they have smart table settings and well - prepared, regional ingredients are served.

Name: Le Macine
Address: Via Lino Carlo del Favero 11, Vittorio Veneto, 31029, Italy
Description: Housed in a recently renovated 18C mill on the banks of the Meschio river, this restaurant is run by brothers Giuseppe (front of house) and Adriano (in the kitchen), who serve top-quality cuisine with its roots in local traditions and the occasional imaginative twist with warmth and professionalism. It is even more appealing in summer, when meals are served on the beautiful outdoor terrace.

Name: Le Nove Scodelle
Description: Now available everywhere in Italy, ethnic cuisine is gradually becoming more specialised, as is the case in this restaurant serving specialities from the province of Szechuan in south-west China. Exciting and original cuisine full of spicy flavours.

Name: Le Rune
Description: Various small dining rooms, including one directly above the kitchen, create a simple yet welcoming ambience at this restaurant. The food is regional and seasonal, with a focus on fish and seafood. Specialities include “brandacujun” stockfish; burrata panna cotta with baby spinach, porcini mushrooms and toasted pine nuts; squid stuffed with prawns and courgettes in an aioli sauce; and corn linguine with fresh tuna, red onions and olives on a pepper sauce.

Name: Le Tre Colombe
Description: This intimate and romantic restaurant occupies an old 19C farmhouse situated in a tiny hamlet in the Cembra valley. In the softly-lit dining rooms, chef Mara Fronza serves just one tasting menu which changes every month (guests have the choice of the main menu or a shorter version if they prefer) and showcases Italian dishes with obvious regional influences, especially in the seasonal ingredients used, all prepared with a modern twist. The famous carbonara is reinterpreted with the addition of anchovies and Crusco peppers, while the dark chocolate dessert with cherries in rum and cardamom-infused cream is truly delicious. Highly recommended!

Name: Le Vele
Address: Via Litoranea Sud 71, Bagni 70, Misano Adriatico, 47843, Italy
Description: This modern, minimalist - style restaurant is practically on the beach and almost within touching distance of the sea. It specialises in fish dishes with a contemporary flavour.

Name: Le Vie del Borgo
Description: In a renovated building in the historic center of the picturesque village of Toceno, in Val Vigezzo, a young couple passionately presents recipes from the region and beyond: dishes showcasing modern technique, excellent seasonal products, and an interesting wine list. The restaurant comprises several intimate dining rooms in Alpine style. In summer, the pleasant outdoor terrace with limited seating must be reserved well in advance.

Name: Le Viste
Address: Via del Falcone (spiaggia delle Viste), Portoferraio, 57037, Italy
Description: Leaving the port area, you climb toward the historic area of the Medici fortresses and then descend again along the opposite side until you reach a small beach. Here you’ll find the restaurant, charmingly and characteristically simple, right in front of the water’s edge. The cuisine is pleasantly traditional and essentially offers classic Italian seafood dishes.

Name: LeBolle
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The ‘bubbles’ that give the restaurant its name are charming private dining areas surrounded by greenery, designed to offer an intimate and secluded experience; however, the pleasant outdoor seating area overlooking the garden and the elegant dining room, with its contemporary design, also ensure a high level of comfort. After all, the restaurant is part of the elegant Boutique Hotel Stresa, and shares its commitment to hospitality and quality. The culinary offering focuses on Mediterranean cuisine with a modern twist, characterised by meticulous preparation, well-executed techniques and a particular emphasis on plant-based ingredients, which are also showcased through a dedicated five-course tasting menu. The dishes are characterised by their balance, lightness and harmonious presentation. Rounding off the offering, the rooftop bistro – open for lunch and boasting a stunning panoramic view of the lake – serves up a more straightforward and informal menu to be enjoyed in a relaxed and convivial atmosphere.

Name: Lemelae
Description: After a path that has taken him through various national and international experiences, including time in starred kitchens, the chef returns to the Asiago plateau to realise a stripped-back project in which everything revolves around his own gastronomic vision. The setting reflects this approach: unadorned, sincere, and driven by a concrete passion for cooking. The menu is concise but well-defined, with creative dishes that assert a strong connection to the territory. Fermentation and raw material preservation techniques occupy a prominent place, while with the arrival of warmer weather lighter, fresher preparations come to the fore. The grill, however, remains central: a preferred cooking method that brings out the best in characterful meats such as the Foza sheep.

Name: Leone Felice
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: The new chef at this restaurant focuses on highlighting produce grown in the property’s own kitchen garden, as well as meat from the farm in the Grosseto area that is also run by the Andana estate. The classic-style cuisine on the à la carte features occasional personalised touches (for example, aubergines baked in fig leaf with oregano, and perch or sea bass fillet served with coloured beets and soft potato), while in the evening a tasting menu is served in a dedicated part of the restaurant. The expertly explained wine list focuses on the estate’s own labels and the Franciacorta region in general, yet at the same time includes a selection of wines from elsewhere in Italy and further afield.

Name: Li Jalantuùmene
Address: Piazza de Galganis 9, Monte Sant'Angelo, 71037, Italy
Description: Chef Gegè Mangano’s infectious passion – combined with his great charm – guides guests on a journey of discovery through the authentic flavours of Puglia, in an intimate restaurant overlooking a charming little square in the historic centre. The menu, which is deliberately limited, changes frequently to reflect the seasons and ensure the utmost freshness of the ingredients, while the recipes focus on simplicity, using just a few ingredients to clearly bring out their flavours. The dishes are so tasty, light and straightforward, leaving a vivid and clean impression on the palate. The couple’s aim is clear: to make each guest feel at home, offering not just a dinner, but an experience that leaves them with a smile.

Name: Li Lioni
Address: SS 131 km 244,400 - regione Li Lioni, Porto Torres, 07046, Italy
Description: The highlights of this restaurant just outside the tourist centre of Porto Torres are its informal atmosphere and spacious garden. The cuisine here focuses on meat, with a superb selection (most of which is from grass-grazed animals) and carefully aged options. If you want to taste the restaurant’s legendary porceddu (suckling pig), you’ll need to order this ahead of time when you book. When it comes to choosing wine, we recommend the well-structured and intense house red.

Name: Lillotatini
Description: Situated in the heart of a small medieval castle-hamlet, this traditional-style restaurant with an attractive terrace on the historic square provides the setting for local specialities such as freshwater fish and truffles in season. There’s also a wine boutique on the same piazza (reached as soon as you come into the historic centre), which sells typical local produce and a good selection of wine. The latter also features on the restaurant’s wine list, with the family on hand to offer recommendations.

Name: Lineadombra
Address: Ponte dell'Umiltà, sestiere Dorsoduro 19, Venice, 30123, Italy
Description: Boasting a splendid location with an outdoor dining space on a kind of raft-cum-platform, this restaurant boasts one of the most delightful views in Venice, with the Giudecca on the opposite side of the canal. Contemporary cuisine with a focus on fish and the occasional creative twist.

Name: Ling's Ravioleria Migrante
Description: Tucked away in a quiet residential neighbourhood is a tiny restaurant which, thanks to the success it has enjoyed over the years, usually requires a booking. Around twenty seats inside and a few tables outside during the warmer months provide the setting for an original and ever-evolving culinary offering. The starting point is Chinese ravioli, but the cuisine extends far beyond this, following the concept of a ‘migrant’ gastronomy that blends Asian, Mediterranean, French and Italian influences, while maintaining strong ties to the Emilia-Romagna region. Examples of this include dishes such as Mora Romagnola pork in Peking-style or pink Adriatic prawns marinated in mirin and soy sauce. The menu changes daily, depending on market availability, the season and the chefs’ inspiration. To be enjoyed with tea, craft beers or a small but carefully curated selection of wines.

Name: Lino Bistrot
Description: In the heart of Pavia’s old pedestrian centre, precisely in the piazza where linen was once traded, this new restaurant shares its entrance with its more distinguished “elder brother”, the fine dining restaurant Lino. In fact, although now the younger sibling, it was the first step of the project, which subsequently evolved into the fine dining establishment. The spaces, which once housed a bank and later a bookshop, have been transformed into a welcoming venue where honest and immediate cuisine is proposed, carefully presented and faithful to pleasing simplicity. The menu features dishes of clear flavour and sound construction, such as house-made gnocchi with Nerano sauce and shavings of Provolone del Monaco, cod with creamed rapini and Taggiasca olives, or an indulgent tiramisù with cream, salted cocoa crumble, coffee-soaked savoiardi and chocolate sauce.

Name: Lio Pellegrini
Description: Refined interiors, attentive to the smallest detail and enriched by a generous selection of quality objects – also available through a dedicated catalogue – define the style of this venue in the heart of the city, just steps from the Accademia Carrara. Completing the experience is an elegant outdoor terrace, a genuine oasis of calm, ideal for dining al fresco. The cuisine moves between Mediterranean suggestions of land and sea, striking a balance between tradition and contemporary touches: on one side more classic dishes, on the other offerings enriched with creative flourishes. A gastronomic journey that looks to the local area without forgoing occasional forays into Tuscan culture, the owner’s homeland. A spacious and elegant room, designed for boutique hospitality, completes the offering.

Name: Lisander
Description: A Sicilian chef proposes a cuisine that straddles tradition and modernity, with a broad and generous offering of several tasting menus and an à la carte selection encompassing both land and sea, sweet and savoury, with occasional gastronomic echoes of his native region. All this is served in the elegant dining room carved from the common spaces of the Hotel Promessi Sposi, overlooking the lakefront.

Name: Livello 1
Address: Via Duccio di Buoninsegna 25, Rome, 00142, Italy
Description: Situated in the suburbs off the main tourist trail, this fish restaurant also has a fishmonger’s next door. The fish and seafood cuisine served here is highly interesting, featuring modern recipes made from top-quality ingredients. There’s also a small lounge in which to enjoy a cocktail, plus a selection of good wines. The open-view kitchen allows guests to observe the skilful chef at work.

Name: Lo Scalco Grasso
Description: In a cosy dining room with an informal atmosphere – simple yet full of character – the head chef oversees the kitchen and welcomes guests, maintaining a constant presence in the dining room as well. The menu stands out for its generosity and authenticity, alternating classic Mantua specialities – such as the unmissable pumpkin tortelli, served with melted butter or the classic festive sauce – with more contemporary creations. The result is a straightforward and satisfying cuisine that celebrates the local area without sacrificing a touch of creativity.

Name: Lo Scopiccio
Description: Run by the owner-chef and her husband, Locanda Lo Scopiccio is a charming restaurant where careful attention is paid to every detail so that guests feel totally pampered. The cuisine is regional with the occasional hint of creativity, with a choice of two surprise menus or à la carte dining. There’s also a winter garden with a bright yet romantic feel.

Name: Lo Scudiero
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Young, enthusiastic chef Daniele Patti is at the helm at this restaurant housed in the delightful stables of a restored 16C palazzo. Here, he serves a selection of creative dishes, including two tasting menus – the intriguing Vieni in Sicilia con me (inspired by his native Sicily) and the Adriatico - and an à la carte which focuses on the local region’s abundance of fine ingredients. Wine-enthusiasts can ask to visit the impressive cellar, which also offers a good choice of wines by the glass.

Name: Lo Squalo
Description: With a long history, this restaurant has a contemporary vibe, where expert management offers exclusively seafood dishes, with well executed classic preparations, elevated by careful plating and lively pairings, often featuring fresh vegetables. Both the menu and the wine list are still handwritten, but the overall quality is thoroughly modern.

Name: Lo Stornello
Description: Offering quality and professionalism in a tourist setting, this small restaurant is popular with locals as well as visitors. The menu focuses on imaginatively presented Mediterranean cuisine.

Name: Locale Firenze
Description: Within a palazzo steeped in history, spanning from its medieval underground cellars to the Renaissance piano nobile housing the restaurant, guests enter through the ancient courtyard, now a refined lounge bar with a large counter dedicated to mixology and small tapas-style bites. From here you reach the splendid interior dining rooms, the ideal backdrop for an avowedly creative cuisine shaped by the chef’s international experiences across Australia, Japan, and France. The evocative medieval cellars also house “Labo-ttega,” an exclusive experience combining avant-garde cuisine and mixology, available by reservation for up to four guests. A vibrant destination brimming with energy and quality, interpreting contemporary gastronomy with distinct personality.

Name: Locanda '800
Description: Whether you dine indoors, on the bright veranda or in the wine cellar with its barrels and wines produced by the estate, you’ll enjoy cuisine at this family-run restaurant which has gained a reputation in the region for its balance of meat and fish dishes. Excellent service and a pleasant setting in a rustic building surrounded by greenery.

Name: Locanda 4 Cuochi
Description: A simple, albeit pleasant and lively, restaurant just behind the famous Arena, well run by two good students of chef Perbellini. You can sit at classic tables or sit on stools at the small counter facing the kitchen. In any case, full speed ahead with a contemporary Italian line, with dishes such as "Mozzarella & Carrozza," spaghetti aglio olio peperoncino and raperonzoli with shrimp and lime... to finish – perhaps – with a good tiramisù.

Name: Locanda 53 Supper Club
Description: Stepping inside feels almost like entering the home of Evelyn and Carlo, on the first floor of a building in the historic centre of Arco: just three tables and eight covers in total, spread across two floors. The dishes reveal the couple's love of travel, a passion that inspires the two tasting menus (one meat-based, one fish-based), which combine ingredients from Trentino, including from the lake, with more exotic produce.

Name: Locanda Alpina
Description: Along the enchanting Val di Non, amid rows of apple orchards and the silhouettes of ancient castles, this building of nineteenth-century origin is home to a dependable family-run establishment, in operation for nearly a century, since 1933 to be precise. The cooking interprets the flavours of the territory with quiet competence, drawing out its seasonal excellences – such as white asparagus and venison preparations – while not shying away from occasional forays into broader national influences. Emblematic in this regard is the excellent pistachio ice cream, singled out by our Inspectors as not to be missed.

Name: Locanda Altobelli
Description: A pleasant little restaurant that differs from the many fish options in town with its traditional regional meat-based cuisine. There’s a real alchemy here between the young owner who is passionate about wine and the talented chef who boasts an impressive CV. Carefully chosen ingredients sourced directly from small local producers are the basis for its exciting, delicious dishes, while the wine list features some interesting organic wines. Small outdoor space for alfresco dining.

Name: Locanda Baggio
Address: Via Bassane 1, località Casonetto, Asolo, 31011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A warm and welcoming dining room, together with professional yet pleasantly friendly and informal service, provide the perfect complement to the extraordinary cuisine: hearty, full of flavour, unsullied by unnecessary artifice. The pasta tubes with a rich sauce of baby cuttlefish, dried seaweed and sea urchins are unforgettable, as is the grilled fish with a sauce made from clams, leeks and seaweed oil.

Name: Locanda Belvedere
Address: Via San Giuseppe 736, frazione San Rocco, Saludecio, 47835, Italy
Description: Reached by climbing panoramic hill roads, one eventually finds the restaurant that is an excellent example of the quest for and celebration of local produce, beginning with their outstanding olive oil. One may choose between two tasting menus, the longer of which expands upon the shorter one with the addition of other dishes, dining in the tranquillity of a terrace that in summer opens on one side onto the greenery surrounding the restaurant.

Name: Locanda Gulfi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: In an isolated but well‑marked location that doesn’t escape the notice of oil and wine enthusiasts, Locanda Gulfi produces both, as you can tell from the view of the wine cellar visible from the dining room. The cuisine offers revisited Sicilian dishes, with the possibility of overnight accommodation and, naturally, tastings of the estate’s products, accompanied by dedicated menus or simple snacks specially designed for the occasion.

Name: Locanda La Posta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A traditional setting reflecting the style of the early 20th century, with photos and documents telling the restaurant’s story, and numerous small dining rooms characterised by wooden ceilings. The restaurant’s traditional-style cuisine features excellent home-made pastas and a typical boiled meat trolley (“carrello dei bolliti”). One of the signature dishes here is rabbit stew served with a generous portion of Carmagnola peppers. In the summer, guests can sit in a welcoming outdoor area adorned with green plants and flowers.

Name: Locanda La Raia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The magnificent biodynamic La Raia farm, an enchanting 180-hectare oasis between Novi Ligure and Gavi, is home to a contemporary art foundation, the Rossi Cairo family winery, a Steiner school for employees’ children, guest accommodation, and this restaurant which benefits from a fertile ecosystem that provides much of its zero-mile produce. The cuisine is rooted in local traditions which have been reinterpreted in contemporary style. In the evening (and at lunchtime at weekends), choose between an à la carte, a tasting menu inspired by wines from the property’s estates between Gavi and Langhe, and a delicious “Sei mezze” menu featuring small samples of the restaurant’s most iconic dishes.

Name: Locanda Le Logge
Description: Occupying a period building in the heart of this beautiful village, with an outdoor dining space laid out under the portico in summer, this restaurant serves typical cuisine from the Marche on its various tasting menus and à la carte supplemented by daily specials. Boasting a rustic and pleasantly informal atmosphere, the restaurant also offers six romantic guestrooms with wrought-iron beds, including a four-poster bed in the Sogno room.

Name: Locanda Marchesani
Description: In addition to specialities such as oysters and caviar, this restaurant serves sophisticated classic, traditional cuisine reinterpreted with a modern twist. Choose between à la carte options or tasting menus prepared with refined ingredients of the highest quality.

Name: Locanda Martinelli
Description: It’s well worth leaving the coast and climbing into the foothills to get to this small restaurant serving excellent cuisine. Housed in a rustic-style house with individual furnishings, in what could be the sitting room of a private house, the restaurant serves meat and fish specialities prepared with imagination from local produce and ingredients from further afield. As well as being a wine expert, the female owner gathers herbs, flowers and berries to flavour her recipes.

Name: Locanda Nelli
Address: Via Vittorio Veneto 15, Pietra Ligure, 17027, Italy
Description: A friendly and welcoming little restaurant in the heart of the town’s historic centre. It’s no surprise that the specialities here focus mainly on fish and seafood, with an emphasis on Mediterranean cuisine, homemade pasta and the use of extremely fresh ingredients – the menu changes daily depending on market availability. The charming outdoor space boasts tables set out along the small pedestrianised street.

Name: Locanda Perbellini
Description: Highly renowned in his native Verona, Michelin - starred chef Giancarlo Perbellini has now opened a restaurant in Milan, where he continues to offer traditional Italian cuisine from the north and south of the country, with a nod to new techniques and contemporary trends. Situated in the central Brera district, his warm and welcoming restaurant is small, discreet and, of course, highly elegant.

Name: Locanda Perbellini - Ai Beati
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the first hills behind Garda, the view from the terrace surrounded by greenery is an enchantment, embracing the southern part of the lake, while the interior rooms have been carved out of an old mill with stone walls, now comfortable, "light" and cosy spaces. Here chef Perbellini has set up a cuisine that starting from the territory, from freshwater fish in particular, opens up to proposals of sea and land with Mediterranean and contemporary taste, the steamed seafood salad topped with a wasabi mayonnaise is really delicate and fragrant. Do not miss one of the signature dishes of the famous chef, his legendary mille-feuille.

Name: Locanda Perbellini al Mare
Description: The flavors of Sicily – and not just seafood – are reimagined in a modern way, with personal touches (such as the tuna cutlet cooked and raw with soy mayonnaise and mashed potatoes), as well as vegetarian recipes inspired by the multi-starred chef Perbellini, executed with good technique and a dedication to taste. This all takes place in a modern beach establishment, complete with loungers and umbrellas. In the summertime, the windows open, and you practically all dine on the terrace, surrounded by the scent of the sea.

Name: Locanda Radici
Address: SP 21, contrada San Vincenzo, Melizzano, 82030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: A rustic restaurant with contemporary Mediterranean-style decor surrounded by the greenery of the Sannio region, which can be admired through the large windows. Modern cuisine made from locally sourced ingredients by the owner-chef, who has vast experience working in top restaurants, both in Italy and abroad.

Name: Locanda San Martino
Address: Via Don Ermolao Barattin 23, Chies d'Alpago, 32010, Italy
Description: Founded in 1952, this inn has been run by the same family – and especially its female members – ever since. It now boasts the presence of a chef whose many years of experience are evident in his dishes. Much of the meat (especially lamb) is raised in the restaurant’s own farm nearby, while the dishes on the menu are seasonal and classic in style yet with a hint of modern flavour. When the weather allows, make the most of the large terrace boasting fine views of the sunset over the surrounding Alpago region.

Name: Locanda San Michele
Address: SS 491 3, Contrada Camerale di Tossiccia, Montorio al Vomano, 64046, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Practically on the slopes of Gran Sasso with views of the verdant landscapes of the Abruzzo, this restaurant is home to a local chef who has returned to his roots having spent time away gaining experience in Michelin-starred restaurants. Here, he serves regional cuisine with a modern, contemporary twist and a focus on meat and fish alike (examples include tuna tartare with strawberries finished in the dining room with lemon “snow”) in generous portions that are typical of the Abruzzo.

Name: Locanda Sant'Agata
Address: Via del Brennero, SS 12 km 5,812, San Giuliano Terme, 55016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Not far from the village, this pleasant boutique hotel is home to a friendly, well-kept restaurant surrounded by a relaxing garden where guests can enjoy alfresco dining in summer. The menu features traditional meat and fish dishes with the occasional modern, personalised twist, such as “calamarotto” – squid (calamaro) stuffed with seafood pancotto, vegetables in dry vermouth and confit plum tomatoes.

Name: Locanda Sensi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A country retreat that captivates with simplicity and passion: modern, comfortable rooms open onto a landscape that embraces the hills of Piacenza, while outdoor dining offers glimpses of light and nature. The menu invites guests to enjoy a tasting menu in which the grill releases intense aromas, or à la carte dishes that range from land to sea to garden, in a balance of scents and colours. Two cosy suites, a holistic wellness centre scented with natural essences and, in fine weather, a Zen garden that invites you to relax, complete the experience.

Name: Locanda Solagna
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Although this restaurant has been in business since the 1950s, it feels much more modern thanks to its updated appearance. Renowned for its excellent regional cuisine served in the evening, the restaurant pays careful attention to seasonal ingredients. At lunchtime, the ”osteria”-style menu is much simpler. Excellent wine selection.

Name: Locanda Stella d'Oro
Description: The original flavour and magic of a trattoria can still be found in this establishment. The cuisine is traditional with a personal touch.

Name: Locanda Toscano
Description: The central location, overlooking the rocky shore just steps away, makes this venue an ideal stop for those seeking straightforward, no-frills Mediterranean cuisine. The menu favors the sea, with an excellent raw trio and a series of well-executed pastas, among which the ricotta and red prawn tortello stands out, elevated by a touch of black garlic. The welcome is warm and attention to guests evident in every detail. In short, an excellent gourmet stop.

Name: Locanda Viola
Description: A refined restaurant where the design plays with tables and seating of varied, original craftsmanship, yet it is the cuisine that captures attention, thanks to the talent of Filippo Moriggi. The starters are the calling card: an exotic-tinged journey that surprises with the fish bao, a soft steamed bun also available with BBQ sauce, or with the empanadas chilena, filled with white Sorrento scamorza, shrimp, and coriander-cumin mayonnaise.
