The journey continues toward more familiar flavors: well-executed pastas and risottos, fish dishes, and Bergamo lamb, leading to desserts that play on the freshness of gelato, served simply or affogato-style, for a light, flavorful finish.

Name: Locanda dei Salinari
Description: A cosy, welcoming venue, situated in the historic village of Salinari, comprising a couple of intimate dining rooms and a small outdoor seating area. In the kitchen, head chef and owner Gianni Berti offers a subtly contemporary take on cuisine, carefully preparing the finest produce from the land and sea of Romagna. The dishes retain a classic, robust and distinctive character, with nods to local tradition, such as passatelli given a new twist with shellfish and mushrooms.

Name: Locanda del Falco
Address: Castello di Rivalta 4, Rivalta Trebbia, 29010, Italy
Description: In the heart of a medieval village, an inn of authentic charm welcomes guests with the captivating aromas of Piacenza cuisine and imaginative creations that surprise the palate, accompanied by local wines and distinguished labels from beyond the region. Heritage dishes speak of time-honored flavors, revisited with modern touches, while the inspector’s favorite remains the grilled cardoncelli mushrooms: intense aroma and pure taste. In the dining room, Sabrina radiates energy and smiles, presenting each dish with infectious passion. On winter evenings, crackling fireplaces warm the atmosphere; in summer, a centuries-old wisteria drapes the courtyard tables in fragrant, romantic shade.

Name: Locanda del Feudo
Address: Via Trasversale 2, Castelvetro di Modena, 41014, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the upper and most ancient part of the picturesque village, this romantic retreat – which also offers six elegant suites – offers genuine and deeply satisfying cooking. The menu is split between dishes from the land, with numerous recipes that evoke the Emilian tradition, such as hand-rolled tagliatelle with ragù, tortelli in capon broth, or a selection of the finest local cured meats, and seafood offerings distinguished by a modern and lighter touch. In the warmer months, guests may take their place on the small and charming terrace overlooking the main street, ideally suited to savouring the village in its most relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Locanda del Marinaio
Description: Delicious cuisine full of the flavours of the Mediterranean (prepared by the German owner - chef! ) in a delightful little restaurant in the bustling centre of Cefalù. Simple surroundings but excellent food!

Name: Locanda del Molino
Description: This rustic yet charming restaurant occupies an old family mill. It has attractive guestrooms that reflect the elegant simplicity of the Tuscan countryside. In the kitchen, the female chef creates traditional specialities such as fried rabbit and nettle with ricotta cheese gnudi (ravioli filling without the pasta) in a fresh tomato sauce.

Name: Locanda del Villoresi
Description: What was once a post station is now a renowned restaurant overlooking the Villoresi canal. Although the attractive dining room has retained some of its historical features, the decor here is more contemporary in feel. The Mediterranean-style cuisine focuses mainly on fish and is beautifully presented, with dishes such as fried artichokes with red prawns and bottarga on the menu in season. Raw fish dishes are also occasionally available.

Name: Locanda dell'Angelo
Description: This stylish, elegant restaurant occupying a historic 17C building in an attractive medieval village serves contemporary cuisine which is influenced by recipes and ingredients from Liguria and Piedmont alike. Dishes include Ligurian-style rabbit terrine with a pine nut and gravy sauce, and Piedmontese white suckling pig tomahawk on sauerkraut with a spicy, sour apple sauce.

Name: Locanda dell'Arcimboldo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At the town gates, a friendly inn with a family atmosphere in a fine building, with a pleasant veranda. Fish dishes prevail on the menu, featuring an interesting selection of oysters. At midday there is also an easier set menu.

Name: Locanda della Luna
Address: Via delle Oche 7, San Giorgio del Sannio, 82018, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In a remote location in the Sannio, this authentic inn offers fine views from its well-kept dining room-cum-veranda and outdoor terrace. The owner-chef creates dishes with a regional flavour using produce from his own garden, without straying too far from local traditions.

Name: Locanda delle Tre Chiavi
Description: This restaurant housed in an 18C building is run by its talented and enthusiastic owners Sergio (front of house) and Annarita (in the kitchen), who do their utmost to provide guests with the best seasonal, regional ingredients prepared in classic dishes full of flavour. The wine list focuses on good-quality labels from the region.

Name: Locanda di Nonna Ida
Address: Località Pontarola 12, Marano di Valpolicella, 37020, Italy
Description: A welcoming inn nestled amid the last vineyards of Valpolicella and the first pasturelands of the lower Lessinia region, where a young chef serves cuisine with a focus on local ingredients and classic Italian recipes with a modern twist. In summer, the terrace offers a fresh, cool setting with extensive views. The barbecued meat is superb.

Name: Loewengrube
Description: This building has been home to a restaurant since the 16C, making it one of the oldest in Bolzano. Today, it houses an elegant restaurant that serves a combination of traditional Alpine cuisine and classic Italian dishes with a contemporary twist, such as carbonara tortelloni filled with parmesan cream and crispy bacon. The attractive wine cellar boasts a selection of approximately 1 000 wines from the region and elsewhere in Italy, as well as a choice of labels from further afield.

Name: Lofficina
Description: This building with a minimalist, contemporary design is situated on the edge of the historic centre at the Sant'Erasmo belvedere, from where, in summer, panoramic views extend over Monte Conero and the sea (booking ahead is recommended). In the kitchen, owner-chef Davide Breccia conjures up creative dishes featuring original combinations and mainly inspired by the sea. There are two tasting menus, Iconico and Idee, for guests who like to be guided, plus an à la carte for those who prefer to choose their own courses.

Name: Lord Nelson
Description: Set right on the seafront, with a delightful outdoor seating area, this historic restaurant – opened in 1969 and dedicated to the famous English admiral – boasts classic elegance with mahogany furnishings and light-coloured curtains reminiscent of unfurled sails. Mediterranean-inspired cuisine plays with modern and creative touches, such as slow-cooked amberjack served with baby spinach, pine nuts, marjoram and date tomato sauce.

Name: Lorenzo Ruta
Address: C.da Zimmardo SP45 km5, RG, Modica, 97015, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Situated in a new, low-rise resort in a secluded location, this attractive, contemporary-style restaurant is run by a local chef with plenty of experience behind him, together with the women of his family, namely his wife and sommelier sister-in-law. The extensive selection here includes various tasting menus plus an à la carte, all of which showcase meat and fish dishes featuring imaginative combinations. The impressive wine list includes labels from outside Sicily and Italy, with a strong focus on French wines and champagnes in particular.

Name: Lou Ressignon
Description: Founded in 1966 and now run by the fifth generation, the Lou Ressignon family trattoria (in local dialect the name translates as “the night snack”) serves authentic cuisine full of character which showcases the produce and traditions of the Aosta Valley. The dishes include a delicious Valpellinese soup and excellent tripe with borlotti beans and polentina. In addition to the first-floor dining room, there’s also a historic taverna, while four welcoming guestrooms are available for anyone wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Lu Pisantinu
Address: Viale Giovanni Maria Orecchioni snc, loc. Liscia di Vacca, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: A terrace framed by granite columns overlooks the coast, the sea, and Porto Cervo (about 2 km away): both the culinary style and the overall décor of the welcoming spaces are classic. The menu features primarily seafood, though there are also dishes and flavors from the inland area, with nods to Gallura traditions, such as the strictly handmade chijusoni gnocchetti. Welcoming you is a local family that has been operating here for over 40 years.

Name: Lucenti
Description: A family-run restaurant with classic charm, decorated in warm pastel shades, where the region’s culinary traditions meet contemporary presentation and sophisticated flavour combinations. Among the most iconic dishes are the porcini mushroom frittata, ricotta and herb tortelli with black truffle, pan-fried rabbit fillet with olives, cherry tomatoes and potatoes, and, to round off the meal on a sweet note, the chocolate tart with orange cream. A genuine and carefully crafted selection that showcases the flavours of the region.

Name: Lucia
Description: In business since 1971, the restaurant and hotel of the same name remain one of the most trusted establishments on the Abruzzo coast to this day. Here, the sea takes centre stage, without compromise: the cuisine is dedicated to seafood, and the wine list – in harmony with the menu – clearly favours white wines. Great care is taken in selecting the raw ingredients, which come largely from the Adriatic Sea and are served in dishes that combine respect for tradition with a contemporary sensitivity. Examples include the impressive local scampi, cooked and served in a pan with oil, wine, garlic and rosemary, alongside more original dishes such as crispy red mullet served with the famous Abruzzese ventricina. For lovers of the freshest seafood, the tasting menu – dedicated to raw seafood, comprising six courses and designed to showcase the full quality of the produce – is well worth a mention.

Name: Luciano Cucina Italiana
Address: Piazza del Teatro di Pompeo 18, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: It is said that one of the capital’s finest carbonaras is served here, and we can only agree: no small feat, given the dish’s sacred status in Rome. But the experience at Luciano Monosilio extends far beyond his famous signature; the menu offers other equally compelling preparations that strike a balance between deep Lazio roots and flashes of measured creativity, always delivering intense, well-defined flavors. In the basement, adjacent to the pasta laboratory, Veleno provides the ideal setting for an aperitivo or intriguing cocktail pairings. A new lounge area now also welcomes guests on the upper floor, rounding out a dining and mixology program designed for a fully immersive experience.

Name: Luigi Pomata
Description: This famous classic restaurant in Cagliari serves top-quality cuisine in its modern dining rooms and on an outdoor terrace. The menu features interesting reinterpretations of Sardinian dishes among other options, including their own tuna (the house speciality), which is also available in tins to take away.

Name: Luminist Cafè Bistrot
Description: On the ground floor of the historic Palazzo del Banco di Napoli, which also houses the Gallerie d’Italia, this elegant venue opens onto a sophisticated space dedicated to coffee and pastries. In the background, the open-plan kitchen presents a straightforward and accessible offering, built around high-quality ingredients prepared with skill and precision. Among the dishes that best represent the restaurant, highlights include a delicious aubergine parmigiana, rolled rabbit and a delicate crème caramel to round off the meal. To round off the experience, there’s excellent value for money and a prime location on the lively Via Toledo, ideal for continuing your day with a spot of shopping and a stroll around the city.

Name: Lupaia
Address: Località Lupaia 74, Torrita di Siena, 53049, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: An enchanting setting, a Tuscan hamlet nestled among the hills between Montepulciano and Montefollonico, from which breathtaking sunsets may be enjoyed; tables in the open air during the warmer months, while in the cooler season the dining room looks out onto a splendid open kitchen. The gastronomic offering is determined daily by the chef, whose tasting menu draws above all upon the produce of the estate. Booking is essential for those not staying in the hamlet, and the journey to reach it is thoroughly bucolic.

Name: L’Alchimia
Description: The parquet floor, wood-beamed ceiling and exposed brickwork lend a warm ambience to this restaurant, which is bright and airy during the day and romantic in the evening thanks to its soft lighting. With Giuseppe Postorino at the helm, the cuisine here includes classic recipes alongside more personalised dishes all prepared using top-quality ingredients that are typical of Italian cuisine. Additional features include a small, beautiful brick-vaulted wine cellar (open to visitors), plus an adjacent bar-bistro which serves quick lunches and excellent aperitifs.

Name: L’Oca Bonda
Address: Via Imprunetana per Pozzolatico 154, Impruneta, 50023, Italy
Description: A little over fifteen minutes from Florence, three young chefs give shape to a fresh and contemporary proposal centred predominantly on fish, without neglecting certain meat options. The project comes to life within the space of a former grocer’s shop, today transformed into a small restaurant with a somewhat vintage character: mismatched chairs and china of a former era, recovered with care, provide the counterpoint to a current and well-calibrated cuisine. The light and immediate dishes focus on quality produce, handled with simplicity and restraint, always to convincing effect. Among the highlights, the tuna tartare with chives, candied lemon zest and a touch of caviar stands out, while the dessert plays on freshness and contrast with marinated strawberries, mascarpone foam and meringue chips. All of this offered at decidedly attractive prices.

Name: MARE Bistrot
Address: Via della Torre Clementina 126, Fiumicino, 00054, Italy
Description: Among the many restaurants lining the right bank of the Tiber canal, this is undoubtedly one of the finest: presiding over the kitchen is Pascucci, chef of the eponymous starred restaurant nearby, who here presents a simpler seafood cuisine and traditional recipes in an informal and convivial atmosphere.

Name: MARdiVINO
Description: Inside a recently renovated 1800s farmhouse, MARdiVINO's kitchen offers fresh seafood specialities inspired by Apulian tradition. Do not hesitate to try the barbecued rock octopus, marinated in scapece, accompanied by potato and speck mille-feuille.

Name: MOI Omakase
Description: Situated in the centre of Prato, with views of the Castello dell’Imperatore, this restaurant takes guests on a culinary voyage to Japan without leaving Italy! All guests eat the same single menu, starting at 9pm, as part of which the chef prepares his selection of sushi and sashimi directly in front of them in the dining room. Omakase means “I trust you” – an act of trust that you certainly won’t regret. Our inspector recommends the miso and monkfish soup with kelp and green onions.

Name: MU Dimsum
Description: Already visible from the pavement outside this restaurant, the large kitchen where its staff can be observed busy at work is testament to its success. Inside, the dining room is modern and elegant, with careful lighting effects creating a muted ambience in the evening. The extensive menu features classic Chinese dishes – in addition to different types of delicious dim sum, Peking duck also takes pride of place among the main courses.

Name: Ma.Ri.Na.
Address: Piazza San Gregorio 11, Olgiate Olona, 21057, Italy
Description: The classic and timelessly elegant Ma.Ri.Na restaurant has been a bastion for fish and seafood enthusiasts for decades. The menu features classic Italian specialities alongside more creative options, including a good selection of raw dishes as well as delicious seafood pastas and risottos. The wine list is also impressive and includes an array of wines by the glass.

Name: MaMe Restaurant
Description: Situated in central Viareggio near the town’s shipyards, MaMe occupies a long, narrow space that is reminiscent of Oriental restaurants with its long bench running alongside one wall and small bistro-style tables. This informal yet beautifully kept dining room is the backdrop for cuisine with interesting technical details such as the home-made mayonnaise served with the highly recommended steamed fish dish, and the delicious sourdough loaf which is freshly baked and served warm.

Name: Macelleria Motta
Address: Strada Padana Superiore 90, Bellinzago Lombardo, 20060, Italy
Description: Motta has established a reputation for quality, especially for its meat which is carefully sourced from farms in the Piedmont region. Some of the excellent options on the menu are aged in a large fridge near the entrance, along with different types of delicious salumi which are produced and cured by the restaurant. Various types of meat feature here – these are cured or cooked using classic methods with the occasional modern touch. Piedmontese beef is one of the highlights, with different cuts grilled on the barbecue or served boiled. Make sure you try the 300g hamburger with Aosta valley Toma cheese, BBQ sauce and caramelised onions served in a sesame-seed bun. Enjoy alfresco dining in a typical Lombardy courtyard in summer.

Name: Machettö
Address: Via Vittorio Veneto 23, Pietra Ligure, 17027, Italy
Description: Situated amid the picturesque alleyways of the historic centre, this beautiful restaurant boasts an elegant decor and a warm, friendly welcome. Here, the young, talented chef (originally from Campania but now settled in Liguria) serves Mediterranean cuisine with a traditional regional influence cleverly added to each dish. Our favourite dishes included the excellent trenette pasta with octopus ragù and 24-month-aged parmesan fondue, and the timeless “brandacujun”, which is freshly prepared and served at your table by the chef himself.

Name: Madama Piola
Description: The aptly named Madama Piola (in Piedmontese dialect, “piola” is a village inn) has a simple yet attractive and friendly ambience that serves as a backdrop for typical Piedmontese dishes. Highlights include the memorable stuffed onion, as well as tonnato, braised cheeks and hot zabaglione. Regional wines take pride of place on the wine list, which includes a good selection by the glass.

Name: Madama Vigna
Description: This restuarant has a good wine list with a focus on local labels, as well as an excellent selection of regional specialities on the menu. Dishes include agnolotti (a type of stuffed pasta) with fondue, Piedmontese beef, Villanova chicken and the inevitable bunet dessert.

Name: Madre
Description: A winning venture by a very young couple, who have transformed the premises of a former restaurant into a venue with an intimate and contemporary feel. In the kitchen, a chef with a wealth of experience despite his young age; in the dining room, a warm and genuine welcome. The menu follows the rhythm of the seasons and is characterised by a subtle creativity that brings out the best in the ingredients, with distinct flavours and beautifully presented dishes. A limited à la carte menu, a range of tasting menus and a cuisine that moves effortlessly between seafood and meat dishes. While waiting for the dishes to arrive, a little brainteaser also helps to make the experience even more personal and enjoyable.

Name: Magiargè Osteria Contemporanea
Description: The dining rooms in this lively, typical restaurant in the upper, historic part of Bordighera appear to be almost dug out of the rock. Here, a local chef with plenty of experience behind him creates predominantly Ligurian cuisine (and not just fish and seafood), accompanied by an excellent and extensive wine list, including labels from outside Italy and a good selection of champagnes. Attentive service completes the picture here.

Name: Makorè
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Makorè today tells the story of over a decade of evolution, a journey born in close partnership with the neighbouring fishmonger’s and always deeply connected to the sea. Over time, the experience has been refined with consistency, supported by a thoughtful kitchen and an ongoing exploration of seafood as its central ingredient. In the elegant dining room, with views onto the brigade at work, the experience is divided between an à la carte offering – devoted entirely to fish, shellfish and vegetables – and a six-course tasting menu, the current synthesis of the restaurant’s philosophy. The cuisine speaks a contemporary language of balance and restraint, with light, well-judged forays towards the East: from the sashimi and marinated fish platters to fresh pasta buttons with katsuobushi, through to marinated sturgeon with an Asian-style sauce and black sesame mayonnaise. The pairings are devised with rigour, always in service of the essential purity of flavour. Before the sweet finale, room is made for a selection of Italian and international cheeses, both fresh and aged, adding a further gourmet note to the journey. The service stands out for its precision and attentiveness, with a special mention for sommelier Isacco Giuliani.

Name: Malenco
Address: Via Funivia 22, Chiesa in Valmalenco, 23023, Italy
Description: This typical family-run restaurant serves typical mountain cuisine, although a few fish dishes also feature on the menu. Highlights include game, cheese and the delicious homemade pizzoccheri pasta. Ask the young son for recommendations from the wine list, which includes labels from Valtellina.

Name: Malga Roncac
Description: In a former Alpine dairy on the slopes overlooking Moena, romance continues in the wood-clad dining room complete with fireplace, complemented by a small panoramic veranda. Yet the cuisine here is no mere afterthought: hearty, predominantly mountain fare, almost exclusively meat, is of excellent quality. With limited seating, reservations are recommended.

Name: Mamesa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Mamesa is the gastronomic restaurant of the Weisses Kreuz, an elegant adults-only hotel created within an ancient barn and today comprising 37 suites. The intimate dining room accommodates just six tables set before broad picture windows that frame the alpine landscape, allowing guests to follow the slow shifting of light on the mountains as evening falls. Here chef Marc Bernhart gives shape to his vision of "Glocal" cuisine, expressed through a single tasting menu that weaves together local produce, contemporary sensitivity and Mediterranean and international influences. The result is dishes that are creative, vivid in colour and well-defined in flavour. In the dining room, Jennifer accompanies guests with expertise and natural warmth, suggesting the most fitting pairings to bring out the best of each course.

Name: Mamma Orso
Description: Situated in the lively Nomentano quarter, to the north-east of the city and behind Piazza Bologna — not a tourist area, but rather one of Rome’s student districts — this youthful operation offers fragrant and unfussy Italian regional cookery, reinterpreted with evident passion. The recipes traverse the Italian peninsula from north to south, before being reinterpreted with a personal touch: the traditional Mantuan pumpkin tortello, for example, becomes a slice of roasted pumpkin with sour butter, curry sauce, licorice, and amaretti.While many dishes retain an almost home-cooked feel, there is no shortage of imagination: the barley crème caramel, served with crushed salted peanuts, is excellent. All of this unfolds within a single, intimate and welcoming dining room, possessed of a charming vintage spirit.

Name: Mamma Rosa
Address: Via XXIV Maggio 1, San Polo d'Enza, 42020, Italy
Description: On the outskirts of town in a verdant area near a sports center, with convenient parking, warm hospitality, and family management, this restaurant focuses all its efforts on delivering seafood cuisine based on excellent market selections. Dishes are often paired with vegetables, some grown in their own garden, following the most authentic Mediterranean style.

Name: Mammaròssa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At this restaurant, owner-chef Franco Franciosi focuses on the Abruzzo in dishes which are both traditional and modern. The cuisine showcases the best ingredients from the region, including home-grown vegetables from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden and excellent bread made with solina wheat (typical of the Apennines), amid a decor that focuses on sustainability. Daniela looks after guests front of house, offering recommendations from the short yet carefully chosen wine list.

Name: Mammà Isola di Capri
Description: Situated within the multi-functional Sondo building (also home to a museum, offices and exhibition spaces), this large restaurant decorated in contemporary, post-industrial style provides the backdrop for chef Raffaele Amitrano’s Mediterranean cuisine which is strongly influenced by the flavours of Campania. His plin pasta dish pays tribute to the region and is particularly interesting thanks to ingredients such as cacio cheese, pepper and raw prawns. Make sure you arrive early if you want to visit the building and maybe even take advantage of the large sharing table.

Name: Mangiare Bere Uomo Donna
Description: She’s from Hong Kong, while he’s from Suzzara – together this couple run this welcoming restaurant where their international focus extends from the dishes which feature on the menu to the wine selection and the couple’s love for applied arts. Once seated, you can either choose traditional fare, including a few delicious fish dishes, or you can be tempted by the decidedly Asian options. Whatever you decide, one thing’s for sure – authenticity and seasonal, locally sourced ingredients are guaranteed.

Name: Manna
Description: Hidden away in a quiet district, this semi-pedestrianised area comes to life in the evening thanks to the restaurants nearby. The bar at Manna serves excellent cocktails, with a few tables outside on the street, while inside the new, elegant and minimalist-style dining room you’ll enjoy personalised cuisine that skilfully combines tradition and creativity. Perfect for a romantic dinner or a business lunch, with a faster menu available for the latter. Among the desserts, we highly recommend the delicious and not-to-be-missed Tarte Tatin.

Name: Manuelina
Description: Very few restaurants in Liguria can compete with the long gastronomic tradition of this restaurant, which was named after its original owner back in 1885! It was Manuelina herself who made the typical focaccia of Recco famous, offering it as a dish in her tavern. The fourth generation of the family now runs the business with the same passion and enthusiasm – part of the building houses the typical Focacceria, where family traditions are kept alive, while the other is home to the restaurant itself (even here the legendary and highly recommended focaccia is on the menu) with its round tables. The cuisine is traditional yet with modern touches and based on Ligurian ingredients with a focus on fish (although meat also features).

Name: Maragoncello
Address: Via San Giovanni 1, località Vighizzolo, Montichiari, 25018, Italy
Description: An elegant, modern restaurant where excellent cuisine is served, with a strong emphasis on seafood. In the dishes of the Neapolitan-born chef, the vibrant colors and flavors of his native culinary tradition sometimes make a welcome appearance, alongside a few offerings inspired by the north.

Name: Marc Lanteri
Description: Situated right next to the Fratelli Massucco winery, with which it shares its comfortable outdoor spaces as well as stunning views of the surrounding hills and vineyards, this restaurant is run by Marc Lanteri and Amy Bellotti, partners in life and work, who have chosen this setting for their new Piedmontese adventure. Their cuisine is full of individual character, with three tasting menus (including a vegetarian option featuring produce grown in their own garden) and dishes also available à la carte style. Local ingredients and recipes naturally take centre stage, always enhanced by small touches of colour and imagination. The wine list showcases the property’s own wines, as well as offering a choice of labels from elsewhere in Italy and further afield.

Name: Marcelin
Address: Piazzetta della Vecchia Segheria 1, Montà, 12046, Italy
Description: The dishes on the menu are often creative but usually maintain a link with the local area, its products and its recipes, imaginatively reinterpreted by the chef.

Name: Marchese
Description: Located in a still-central area of the city, this restaurant is not a new opening but has recently reinvented its identity by entrusting the kitchen to a Roman chef with a solid background. The culinary offering maintains a classic structure, with a choice between a “surprise” tasting menu and an extensive à la carte selection. In the kitchen, local and national traditions intertwine, enriched by an international touch that translates into visually striking, colorful creations that above all deliver on the palate. The dishes, both meat and fish, follow the seasonality of ingredients, with particular attention to vegetable pairings. Among the standout offerings: the pumpkin risotto with blue prawn, red berry umami, and Caesar salad crisp, a successful balance of technique, flavor, and creativity.

Name: Marconi
Description: In the heart of the picturesque town that serves as a gateway to Val Formazza stands a welcoming establishment where familial warmth blends with a touch of contemporaneity. In the kitchen Denis, joined in the dining room by his wife Sabrina, knows how to pamper guests with a series of dishes that evoke tradition while being reinterpreted with imagination and modern sensitivity. Not to be missed is their signature “Walser Beef Filet,” a true house specialty, though the “venison ossobuco with cream of potato and blueberry compote” also merits a taste.

Name: Marechiaro
Description: A refined and elegant atmosphere that takes on a decidedly romantic character in the evening: for over twenty years this has been the venue of choice in Bolzano for those wishing to enjoy fish prepared according to the most classic recipes of the Italian maritime tradition, founded upon the quality of the catch – sourced predominantly from the Mediterranean – and upon clean flavours. At the helm are two brothers of Neapolitan origin, a detail that accounts for certain Campanian echoes among the offerings and for the presence of pizza, available in the evening only and baked in a wood-fired oven. Not to be missed is the generous daily selection of raw fish, the true calling card of the house.

Name: Marelet
Description: The name of this restaurant discreetly hidden away in an alleyway on the edge of the town centre is a dialect word meaning “old bachelor”. Small tables set close together give the ambience of a French brasserie and provide the setting for modern, Mediterranean-inspired cuisine. There’s a simpler menu at lunchtime, including salads, tapas and sandwiches, while more choice is available in the evening. Lively atmosphere.

Name: Marina Grande
Description: Situated directly on the beach, this pleasant restaurant with a contemporary decor boasts splendid sea views and a small private beach club. Although the setting obviously has a tourist feel, the traditional cuisine served here is full of flavour. We particularly recommend the “gamberi in carrozza” (shrimp) with fior di latte and a variation on puttanesca sauce.

Name: Marina del Nettuno
Address: Viale della Libertà-Batteria Masotto, Messina, 98121, Italy
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant and lounge bar is situated right on the jetty of the Yachting Club Messina. Elegant and minimalist - style decor, as well as creative cuisine with a focus on fish dishes.

Name: Marino
Description: As you drive along the scenic road from Pesaro, the sunset appears to the west, emerging from the greenery, while to the east the sea appears and disappears, finally settling as the backdrop to the pleasant outdoor area of this restaurant. This is the creation of the chef-owner, who, after traveling the world and working in Michelin-starred kitchens, has returned "home." He incorporates everything he has learned into modern and sometimes creative recipes, occasionally adding a light fusion touch, such as using fruit in dishes such as spaghetti with mussels and sea urchins enhanced by two well-balanced textures of peach.

Name: Marino e Silvana
Address: Via San Salvatore da Horta 7, Cagliari, 09124, Italy
Description: Situated on the edge of the pedestrianised area near the Bastione di Saint Remy, this restaurant is named after its charismatic owner Marino, who helps guests with their choice of menu and is happy to tell them all about the history of the restaurant (the street in front of the restaurant, for example, has not always been there). At the helm in the kitchen, his wife Silvana prepares Mediterranean dishes with a Sardinian flavour – the fish and seafood options are particularly delicious.

Name: Marixx
Description: Located well away from the busy city centre and overlooking the luxury yachts and boats moored in the harbour, this restaurant opened in the summer of 2021, at the same time as the modern Cala del Forte marina in which it is situated (the name of the marina comes from the Forte dell'Annunziata, the ruins of which are visible from the side facing the sea). Fish and seafood take pride of place here (especially raw fish dishes), served with classic, seasonal accompaniments, as well as snacks, while an oyster bar is an added attraction. Although the best tables are in the glass-fronted veranda overlooking the pedestrian promenade, the contemporary-style dining room is also attractive. The owner-chef has plenty of experience behind him, especially working in the region.

Name: Marsupino 1901
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Once the village bakery and now a landmark for those in search of authentic cooking, the trattoria Marsupino 1901 tells a family story spanning four generations. Here, tradition remains the anchor: solid, reassuring and sincere cuisine, yet capable of revisiting familiar flavours with contemporary sensitivity and a measured hand. Emblematic of this approach is the hazelnut semifreddo with Marsala zabaglione cooked in a bain-marie, an indulgent, beautifully judged dessert that brings the meal to an elegant close. In the dining room, the welcome finds its ideal interpreter in Luca: professional, warm and animated by a genuine passion for wine, he accompanies guests with competence and ease. His carefully chosen selection of labels, and his ability to describe them with clarity and engagement, enrich the experience, transforming the gastronomic journey into a harmonious voyage through memory, territory and conviviality.

Name: Maré
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An unexpected gourmet restaurant in a typical private beach club on the Romagna coast, with a dining room that opens on to the beach with its long line of beach umbrellas. The dishes here are carefully prepared and occasionally creative, and all of good quality. We particularly recommend the monfettini (fresh egg pasta) mantecati with cuttlefish, clams, mantis shrimp and ink, which looks like a risotto and is absolutely delicious. The restaurant also boasts a good wine list with an excellent choice of champagnes.

Name: Maso Burba
Address: Via Pietro Bernardelli 32, località Piano, Commezzadura, 38020, Italy
Description: Housed in a traditional maso of wood and stone, the quintessential mountain atmosphere continues inside through warm, timber-clad interiors and a classic ceramic stove that heats one of the first-floor dining rooms. The cuisine, with occasional seafood exceptions, fully embraces the Trentino terroir.

Name: Maso Runch-Hof
Description: Surrounded by woods, a trip to this restaurant housed in an 18C farmhouse is like taking a journey back in time. Take a seat in one of the wood-adorned Stube-style rooms and enjoy generous portions of delicious home-cooked Ladin specialities featured on a single tasting menu, including cajinci t’ega (spinach-filled ravioli), excellent pork ribs with polenta, and apple strudel. The small wine list has the same local focus, featuring labels from the Alto Adige region. A recent addition, the restaurant also now has a few spacious, welcoming chalets available for guests.

Name: Masseria Moroseta
Description: Chef Giorgia Eugenia Goggi offers a unique and authentic gastronomic experience that focuses on fresh ingredients (mostly vegetables), many of which are sourced from small organic gardens. The 90€ menu celebrates Mediterranean cuisine to the full, with colourful dishes that are full of flavour and in which the freshness of the ingredients is allowed to shine through. The beautifully kept, rustic dining room provides an ideal setting for an unforgettable dinner, while the selection of natural Italian wines offers the perfect accompaniment to the chef’s dishes, further enhancing your dining experience. There are six comfortable guestrooms available should you wish to extend your stay and immerse yourself in these peaceful rural surroundings. Booking in advance is highly recommended given the restaurant’s popularity and unique appeal.

Name: Mater
Description: Mater is a "retreat" where time seems to stand still and silence reigns supreme. The surrounding nature provides the perfect backdrop for a culinary offering that harmonizes beautifully with the environment. The dining room, welcoming and elegant, features an open kitchen on one side and large French doors on the other, flooding the space with natural light and offering a stunning view. The offerings range from the “Madre” menu to a lighter option called “In libertà”: 3 courses of your choice, plus 1 dessert (the same for the entire table). We recommend the sweetbreads, delicate and tender, flavored with an excellent Casentino gray pork jus. Alternatively, try the grilled guinea fowl among the mains for a dish with traditional tones and a bold flavor.

Name: Mater Bistrot
Description: A small bistro situated in a street just behind Piazza Cinque Giornate, with a few tables and small lights that give the setting a cosy feel. The dining room is minimalist in style, with just a few tables and a counter where you can sit and watch chef Alex (Alessandro) at work in the kitchen. Guests have the option of two tasting menus or a selection of smaller dishes to share. A choice of natural wines accompanies the chef’s imaginative dishes.

Name: Mater Terrae
Description: Situated on the top floor of the Raphaël hotel just behind Piazza Navona, this restaurant serves some of the best vegetarian cuisine in Rome. Each of the elaborate dishes boasts numerous ingredients and every single course is a delightful surprise. Equally stunning is the panoramic terrace overlooking the city’s rooftops, where meals are served in fine weather.

Name: Materia Prima
Address: Località Piana Santa Liberata, Castel di Sangro, 67031, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A pleasant and intimate terrace overlooks the shores of an artificial lake dedicated to sports activities. The glass windows provide the same view from the modern, sleek, and minimalist interior rooms, just like the dishes: creative, yet reminiscent of local cuisine, such as the simple but tasty Pallotta Cacio e Ova, offered among the welcome bites. There are also various daily specials according to the market. The service is friendly and attentive, with a young and motivated team overall.

Name: Materia | Spazio Cucina
Description: One has the impression of crossing the threshold of the chef’s own home, through a door of pleasantly domestic character; inside, a welcoming dining room opens up, with shared tables and a striking wall entirely lined with jars filled with nuts, pumpkin seeds, red lentils and other ingredients. The cuisine, classic in inspiration yet open to contemporary technique and the use of the grill, offers land and sea in a Sicilian key, with close attention to seasonality. Our Inspector recommends beginning with the convincing “piatti del contadino”, a vegetable selection in which the “Onion on the BBQ with dry-cured black olives, tuma persa cream and parsley oil” stands out, alongside the delicate “Salt Cod Salad”, cooked with oregano oil and served with a sauce of almonds, olives, capers and orange zest.

Name: Matteo Ristorante
Description: In elegant and intimate spaces with soft, muted tones, guests enjoy the contemporary cuisine of Matteo Marra. Meat and fish feature equally on the menu, with a constant emphasis on meticulously crafted and spectacular presentations of dishes. A small outdoor area sits under a portico, with tables that must be reserved well in advance during the warmer months. Coffee and aperitif service is also available at the adjacent Laboratorio, at No. 10.

Name: Maxi
Address: Via Luigi Serio 8, SS 145 Sorrentina km 14,500, Vico Equense, 80069, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Once you’ve arrived at the Capo La Gala hotel and left your car in the car park, you can head down to the restaurant by lift or, better still, on foot, taking in the extraordinary view of the Gulf of Naples and Vico Equense as it unfolds before you step by step. Just a few metres from the sea, among the rocks and boulders lapped by the water, the focus then turns to the dishes of Emmanuel Scotti, a chef from Campania who brings his homeland to life with energy, colour and authentic flavours. All this is accompanied by a particularly extensive wine list, with a wide selection also available by the glass. The experience is made even more memorable by the picturesque sunset over the sea and the impeccable service led by Giulia Tavolaro.

Name: Meltemi
Description: This small restaurant boasts an enviable location on a small square, with an outdoor terrace which is perfect for summer evenings. Here, the talented chef focuses on fish in all its guises, including raw options and tartares, all served with delicious accompaniments that bring out the full flavour of the fish. Homemade pasta also features, such as pappardelle with raw and cooked prawns, as well as burrata, plus main courses that include a superb, delicate mullet dish. A choice of excellent Italian sparkling wines and champagnes, also available by the glass, completes the picture.

Name: Menabò Vino e Cucina
Address: Via delle Palme 44 d/e, Rome, 00171, Italy
Description: Two brothers have brought fresh life to this exciting bistro in the heart of the Prenestino-Centocelle district, where the delicious cuisine is prepared by Paolo and the wine selection overseen by Daniele. The menu features a good balance of meat, fish and vegetarian dishes with a focus on seasonal ingredients and the best market produce. Very popular, so booking is recommended!

Name: Menarosti
Description: Dating back to 1903, this historic restaurant has a warm, welcoming feel. Excellent fish and seafood prepared using top - quality ingredients, where simple preparation allows the flavours to shine through.

Name: Menegaldo
Address: Via Pralongo 216, Monastier di Treviso, 31050, Italy
Description: Menegaldo is a long-established favourite for anyone who loves authentic fish dishes made from top-quality ingredients. Although it feels as though time has stood still in the pleasantly old-fashioned dining room, with its outmoded decor and furnishings, the service here is attentive and enthusiastic. The dishes are traditional and typical of the area, making this an excellent choice for delicious seafood cuisine that is elaborate without being overly fussy.

Name: Menzaghi
Address: Via San Giovanni 74, Fagnano Olona, 21054, Italy
Description: In a small dining room decorated in traditional style, the Menzaghi Restaurant is now run by the fourth generation of the family, who passionately carry on its long-standing traditions. The owner is a great wine enthusiast, and the informal but professional service helps create a pleasant and welcoming atmosphere. The cuisine is hearty, with a strong focus on seasonal and locally sourced ingredients. It is also worth taking a look at the daily specials, which are often particularly interesting.

Name: Meraviglioso
Address: Largo Gelso 16, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the statue of Domenico Modugno and one of Polignano a Mare’s most iconic viewpoints, Meraviglioso boasts a location that alone makes it well worth a visit, with spectacular views of the Adriatic Sea and the characteristic houses perched on the cliffs. But it is at the table that the restaurant truly reveals its identity. Here, chef Andrea Vicario – originally from Lucera and with a wealth of experience gained in Italy and abroad – presents a cuisine that celebrates the Apulian region through a contemporary sensitivity and impeccable technique, with a focus on flavour. The sea takes centre stage in a refined yet understated menu, as demonstrated by the langoustine tartare served on a crispy pancotto patty with Swiss chard and finished with a delicate shellfish beurre blanc – a harmonious blend of coastal traditions and flavours from the hinterland. Among the main courses, the dishes cooked on the Josper charcoal grill stand out, as they showcase the quality of the ingredients. The meal concludes with a dessert that plays on citrus fruits and textures: creamy sorbet made from charcoal-grilled mandarins, coconut crumble, thin wafers filled with mandarin mousse, crema catalana made with local cheese, and a citrus sauce. An elegant, fresh and deeply Mediterranean finish.

Name: Mesadoria Restaurant
Address: Piazza De Honestis Cavallino, Sassari, 07100, Italy
Description: This reliable restaurant has moved from the coast to simple, modern premises in the town of Sassari, where it has a new look and new chefs at the helm. The cuisine is as good as ever, with a focus on fish and seafood yet also including a few meat options, in dishes that are classic with a modern twist and cooked using predominantly Sardinian ingredients.

Name: Meta Ristorante
Address: Via Generale Pescetto 5, Celle Ligure, 17015, Italy
Description: Situated in the picturesque historic centre of Celle, this old boathouse with a typical brick ceiling is now home to an excellent gourmet restaurant, where a young chef creates some of the most interesting dishes in the region.

Name: Metis
Description: A small establishment in the residential neighbourhood of Mezzocammino, the restaurant distinguishes itself through modern, carefully appointed interiors, enriched by contemporary art touches that define its stylish identity. The cuisine is of solid quality, guided by a creative hand that alternates personal touches with more traditional executions, consistently well-controlled. The dining room exudes an informal and cordial atmosphere, while the wine list offers a balanced and well-considered selection. Among the most successful dishes, the bronze-cut spaghettone with butter and yeast stands out, essential and convincing. For those seeking a more immersive experience, four counter seats facing the kitchen are available, in direct contact with the chef.

Name: Mia Ristorante
Address: Via Borgotufi, Castel del Giudice, 86080, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: If you're not already in the area, plan some time to get there, traveling through a green, hilly landscape to reach Borgotufi, a "diffused hotel" spread among stone houses. In the former stables transformed into a restaurant, Marco Pasquarelli, a talented young chef, offers a modern take on various local ingredients, with a few seafood dishes as well.

Name: Michelasso
Description: Situated in the city centre, this refined restaurant with an elegantly classic decor is perfect for a romantic, intimate dinner. The menu features meat and fish, with traditional dishes reinterpreted thanks to the chef’s expertise and proven experience. In summer, choose a table on the pleasant outdoor space overlooking the lively Via Santa Brigida.

Name: Miil
Description: Housed in a converted 15C mill on the Kränzelhof wine estate, this smart, elegant restaurant provides the backdrop for excellent, contemporary-style cuisine prepared wherever possible using locally sourced (and always top-quality) ingredients.

Name: MikEle
Description: An elegantly contemporary dining room punctuated by large portholes seems to herald the menu’s seafood focus: fish dishes arrive at the table, moderately creative yet firmly anchored to prime ingredients. The “nudo e crudo” is the essential selection of the day’s catch served simply, typically featuring at least six different varieties, while the tagliolini with langoustine is elevated with caviar and a creamy white cabbage purée finished with Martini. The heart of the experience, however, remains the quality of the ingredients, the absolute and memorable stars.

Name: Milano
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This is a historic establishment, the guardian of a family tradition stretching back almost a century – celebrated in its iconic dessert, zabaione. The elegant setting draws its charm from a veranda overlooking the lake, further enhanced by a private jetty. The cuisine interprets contemporary tastes without compromising on classic favourites, supported by excellent ingredients sourced from the land, freshwater and sea. A prime example are the refined ravioli del plin with 100% langoustines.

Name: Mildas
Address: Via Rosmini 7, località Vadaione, Giustino, 38086, Italy
Description: Housed in what was once the chapel of a medieval monastery, Mildas serves classic specialities from Trento alongside a selection of dishes created by Mirko, the late founder of the restaurant, which is now run by his son. The wine list features illustrations and descriptions.

Name: Millo Ristorante
Address: Via Garibaldi 4, Santa Teresa Gallura, 07028, Italy
Description: A charming restaurant with fair prices, Millo offers dishes infused with the flavors of the sea, sometimes with a creative twist (such as spaghetti with a garlic, oil, and chili emulsion, red prawn carpaccio, and a crispy bread crust), other times inspired by tradition (such as the seafood soup cooked in a jar). There are also a few meat options available. The lovely summer terrace is perfect for taking in the lively local scene.

Name: Mirabelle
Address: Via di Porta Pinciana 14, Rome, 00187, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: From the penultimate floor of the Hotel Splendide Royal, guests enjoy an extraordinary view, among the most breathtaking in the capital at sunset, sweeping across Villa Medici, Trinità dei Monti, St. Peter’s, and the Janiculum Hill. For an even more dramatic setting, simply ascend one level to Adèle, a lounge bar welcoming guests for aperitifs and atmospheric after-dinner drinks. In the kitchen, a modern approach built on solid classical foundations, generous in its combinations and attuned to the seasons, with both meat and seafood offerings. A venue that has become iconic in Roman fine dining – in every sense of the word.

Name: Miranda
Address: Via Cornello 8, Riva di Solto, 24060, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in a superb location overlooking Lake Isea, this restaurant boasts superb views of the lake and Monte Isola from its outdoor terrace and dining room alike. The menu features fish (mainly from the sea) and meat dishes with a creative twist.

Name: Mirepuà Food Lab
Description: Situated in a picturesque medieval village in the Monferrato hills, this restaurant serves classic Piedmontese cuisine with plenty of meat options, alongside a few specialties from the chef’s native Liguria, including fish and seafood dishes.

Name: Mirko's
Address: discesa Annunziata 1, Castellammare del Golfo, 91014, Italy
Description: This small restaurant, located near the steps to Cala Piccola, is run by an entire family and is beginning to earn an excellent local reputation. The son is at the helm in the kitchen. Having gained experience elsewhere for many years, he decided to start his own venture, which shows every sign of having paid off. Enjoy excellent fish and seafood specialities cooked in Mediterranean and Sicilian style in a quiet, beautifully kept dining room.

Name: Miseria e Nobiltà
Description: The name of this restaurant occupying a late-18C palazzo with attractive flooring and Murano glass chandeliers alludes to the peasant traditions that influence its cuisine (miseria) and the creative, elegant dishes served here (nobiltà). The menu features excellent home-made pastas, vegetables and meat dishes, including boned rabbit with leeks and Annurca apples and white and black truffles from the Molise in season.

Name: Mistral
Description: Situated at the tip of Bellagio’s promontory where the two branches of the lake meet, this villa occupies a superb panoramic location, with its restaurant housed in a covered veranda boasting delightful views of the opposite shore, its little villages and exclusive residences. The atmosphere here is reminiscent of a grand hotel, with background piano music in the evening and guests from all around the world. The moderately creative cuisine offers a choice of Italian dishes alongside more international options.

Name: Mizuna Japanese Restaurant
Description: Just outside the charming village center of San Pantaleo, this is easily one of Sardinia’s best Japanese restaurants. It’s the realized dream of an Italian chef who learned the craft while working around the world and who, in a minimalist, welcoming setting, deftly prepares an array of sushi and gyoza, plus mushi-pan (steamed cakes), soups, and more. Pristine flavors are assured by the kitchen’s reliance on mostly fresh Sardinian fish. To finish, creative Italian-inspired desserts appear alongside classic oriental mochi.

Name: Modì
Description: This restaurant has moved from its previous location in central Torregrotta to a more secluded setting slightly above the town centre, where it aims to offer its guests an even better dining experience. The owner-chef has more than achieved this, serving excellent Sicilian dishes reinterpreted with careful precision and a contemporary twist. A good wine list completes the picture.

Name: Mogano
Address: via del Praticello Alto 7, Formello, 00060, Italy
Description: Aiming to promote craft beers as a worthy pairing for gourmet cuisine, the Faenza family opened Mogano – a modern, elegant restaurant with a wood-inspired decor, soft lighting and just five tables, right next to their Ritual Lab brewery. One of the sons (Matteo, the chef here) greets guests before dinner with an aperitif served in the kitchen. With plenty of international culinary experience behind him, he combines Italian flavours with influences from all around the world. Despite the focus on beer, a wine list is also available.

Name: Moi
Description: It's worth heading off the tourist trail and making your way to the north of the city to find this small restaurant with its friendly staff and delicious cuisine. The chef here is Thomas Moi, whose dishes are influenced by various gastronomic traditions (including from outside Italy) and are definitely worth trying! Booking ahead is recommended.

Name: Momento al 25
Description: A late 19th century building houses this simple but welcoming restaurant, which moves its service outdoors during the summer months, creating a pleasant and informal atmosphere. The menu alternates traditional local specialities with Italian dishes, featuring a significant selection of seafood options. Raw seafood is always on the menu: served plain or in slightly more elaborate versions, it is one of the most popular choices among diners.

Name: Mondschein
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Nestled within the picturesque Dolomite landscape of Sappada, the Mondschein is now one of the most interesting dining destinations in the area. For several years now, with the arrival of the new generation of the Kratter family, the restaurant has been undergoing a significant process of evolution: Federico heads up the kitchen, Stefano oversees the wine list and Sofia welcomes guests in the dining room, all helping to shape a contemporary venture with a strong sense of identity. The cuisine follows a single gastronomic philosophy, focused on research, showcasing the produce of the region and of the time of year, with menus that are constantly adapted according to the availability of the finest ingredients. Rounding off the experience is a significantly expanded wine list, featuring a wide selection of wines by the glass and enhanced by the KAVEAU, the restaurant’s charming wine cellar, a space dedicated to wine tastings and in-depth explorations of wine. The rooms, which have been refurbished as part of a major renovation project, combine contemporary elegance with an alpine atmosphere, offering a setting that is in keeping with the hotel’s current philosophy.

Name: Morelli
Description: Within a refined design hotel, the chef’s gourmet offering is served exclusively at dinner, either in the elegant dining room with soft lighting or at the friends’ table in the kitchen. The culinary direction is firmly Italian, showcasing the country’s iconic products: from land-based dishes – such as lamb with escarole, anchovies, and licorice – to seafood preparations, including a standout Carnaroli Gran Riserva risotto finished with smoked buffalo ricotta and topped with red shrimp tartare, black truffle, and anchovy essence. Equally indulgent is the dessert chapter, with offerings such as pears poached in Sauternes, accompanied by almond gelato and salted caramel cream. From 6 p.m., guests may begin the evening at Bulk, the hotel’s mixology and food bar, which extends outdoors in warmer months, a perfect prelude to dinner.

Name: Moscatello Muliner
Description: Situated in a rural setting on a huge agricultural property, this attractive restaurant is dominated by an early 20C millstone. The menu combines traditional Italian fare with regional specialities, all at reasonable prices.

Name: Motelombroso
Description: An old, carefully restored road worker’s house on the Alzaia Naviglio Pavese canal is the setting for this modern, stylish restaurant where Alessandra and Matteo welcome guests in a graceful, elegant and yet informal manner. The menu features contemporary meat and fish dishes accompanied by a good choice of wines. If you’re curious about the restaurant’s name, ask the owners for an explanation: could it be something to do with the private dining room perhaps?

Name: Muraglia - Conchiglia d'Oro
Description: Here, choose between the simply furnished, bright dining room with a proudly vintage feel that dates back to its opening in the 1970s and a tiny yet attractive terrace with sea views (there are just a few tables, so it’s best to book in advance). Fish has always been – and still is – the house speciality, with fresh, top-quality dishes simply prepared according to classic methods such as the barbecue grill visible in the dining room. The fish is so fresh that the handwritten menu changes daily.

Name: Musciora
Description: Run with passion by a close-knit family duo – father in the kitchen and son in the dining room, overseeing the cellar – this restaurant distinguishes itself through a total commitment that finds further expression in the new space recently created alongside the original one. Here, the open kitchen looks directly into the dining room, creating a continuous dialogue between the brigade and the guests. The gastronomic offering is structured across three tasting menus: one dedicated to the sea, one focused on the produce of the hinterland and meats, and a “Vera Esperienza Musciora”, a harmonious encapsulation of both souls. The dishes begin with island ingredients, celebrated through an essential approach and contemporary intuitions that bring out their authenticity and flavour. The wine list reflects the same attention to the local area, favouring Sardinian labels – often from small artisan producers – alongside a selection from beyond the region, oriented predominantly towards natural wines.

Name: Ménage
Description: Situated in the heart of the city near the Teatro Bellini and Piazza Università, this restaurant occupies an Art Nouveau-style building. Here, a trio of experienced young chefs from Catania have brought new life to the old “Da Turi Finocchiaro” restaurant, which has always been very popular with the city’s high society. Offering a small outdoor space near the entrance, the quiet, intimate dining room on the ground floor provides the backdrop for reinterpreted, contemporary Sicilian cuisine with an exclusive focus on meat (especially barbecued dishes which are the restaurant’s trademark), while the first floor is home to a cocktail bar run with passion by one of the partners. Two frescoes painted by Giuseppe Barone in 1930 add to the appeal.

Name: N'uovo Vino e Cucina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled in the refined Antico Borgo di Sutri resort, in the heart of the lush Tuscia Viterbese, this restaurant offers an intimate and modern atmosphere, characterised by soft lighting and large windows overlooking the surrounding greenery. The talented young chef Lezzerini offers cuisine inspired by the local area, revisiting traditional regional recipes with modern techniques and the finest local produce. Countless offerings have made a lasting impression, from the starter that echoes the restaurant’s name, N’uovo alla brace, to the quality of the fresh pasta and the meat main courses, such as the dry-aged wild boar served in the manner of roast beef.

Name: NUH Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Situated in Tivoli’s historic centre, this restaurant has a young chef at the helm who skilfully pays tribute to the region’s gastronomic traditions. Although the menu also features a few fish dishes and the occasional ingredient from outside Lazio, it is the dishes made from local produce with their intense, delicious flavours that will linger long in the memory.

Name: Nannini
Description: This restaurant run by the young Nannini brothers (one front of house, the other in the kitchen) occupies one of Livorno’s most interesting buildings, situated in the district of Antignano with its period houses and typical atmosphere. The focus here is almost exclusively on fish, in dishes which are original yet at the same time respectful of their ingredients – matured fish is one of the specialities. A top-quality dining experience.

Name: Nello
Address: Via IV Novembre 66, San Casciano in Val di Pesa, 50026, Italy
Location: San Casciano in Val di Pesa, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Federico at the stove and Chiara, pastry chef and the soul of the welcome, have brought new life to a long-established local restaurant, transforming it into a modern expression of Tuscan cooking. The menu, varied and stimulating, features dishes such as the raviolo filled with Parmigiano cream from Red Cows, served with chanterelles and onions – intense and technically accomplished – as well as their intriguing take on tiramisù, given an added dimension by a secret touch of tobacco. Over the years, the wine list has grown considerably, reflecting the deep passion of both proprietors; the bottles are kept in a captivating sixteenth-century space that is most certainly worth a look.

Name: Nero&Oro
Address: Via del Parco Regina Margherita 45, Naples, 80121, Italy
Description: The dream of a young Neapolitan chef comes to life in an intimate, refined hideaway, tucked among the elegant streets connecting Vomero to the Chiaia waterfront. Here, dishes burst with vivid colors and Mediterranean aromas, accented by contemporary touches that reveal personality and culinary exploration. Two blind tasting menus invite discovery, or guests may opt for a well-balanced à la carte selection of land and sea, where each ingredient shines with clarity, lifted by subtle exotic nuances that awaken the senses. The wine cellar, dominated by Campanian labels, exudes tradition, yet upon request opens to selected wines by the glass, completing an experience that plays on harmony and curiosity.

Name: Next2
Description: Along the street that runs through the heart of Positano, a well-maintained outdoor terrace surrounded by greenery welcomes guests into a relaxed and elegant atmosphere. The kitchen, which is contemporary and brimming with creative ideas, offers dishes featuring both seafood and meat, as well as an intriguing tasting menu. Standout dishes include the steamed bao with lobster, marinated onion, tomato and guacamole, and seared tuna with wakame seaweed, a soy sauce and honey reduction. The experience is rounded off by attentive, professional service from the waiting staff, who are on hand to ensure each guest feels to be the centre of attention.

Name: Nicolin
Address: Via Paisiello 4, località Maggianico, Lecco, 23900, Italy
Description: Restaurant-hotel not far from the centre, but in a quiet, residential area, this is where you can find some of the best cuisine in town. The cook revisits some national dishes in a personal way, with a few seafood offerings as well.

Name: Nido del Picchio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This restaurant with a low-key, hushed atmosphere has the feel of a tastefully furnished private home, with an open fire to warm cold winter evenings while a cool, welcoming outdoor terrace becomes the ideal spot for al fresco dining in summer. The dining experience comprises four tasting menus and an extensive à la carte menu, offering a generous variety of dishes designed to delight every palate. The recipes range naturally between meat, fish and vegetarian options, offering a wide and well-balanced array of flavours. The desserts are all well worth trying and our favourites include Tribute to Gauguin, a tonka bean blancmange with passion fruit, mango, papaya and coconut ice cream for an exotic and refined finish. The chef’s wife, Lucy, manages the dining room service with the utmost courtesy and professionalism, contributing to a thoroughly enjoyable overall experience. The wine cellar is home to more than 700 of finest best Italian and international wines, with a curious and interesting emphasis on labels from cooler climes.

Name: Nives
Address: Via Nives 4, Selva di Val Gardena, 39048, Italy
Description: Since December 2023, there has been a new chef at Nives who appeared on Masterchef and has left his work as a project manager to follow his passion for cooking. His cuisine is generous both in the choice of dishes offered (including a few fish options) and in portion sizes. The house specialities include convivial fondues (either Chinese style or made with local cheese) and premium local beef (Tomahawk, T-bone, ribeye, sliced etc). There’s also an interesting choice of wine by the glass.

Name: Nni Lausta
Address: Via Risorgimento 188, Santa Marina Salina, 98050, Italy
Description: Fish plays the starring role here, where the authentic traditional flavours and ingredients of Aeolian cuisine are skilfully interpreted with a touch of imaginative flair. If it’s not too hot to sit outside, ask for a table on the pleasant, shaded terrace on the first floor.

Name: Nobuya
Description: Nobuya boasts a minimalist elegance that is typical of Japanese restaurants, with brown tables, dark wooden beams on the ceiling, attractive subdued lighting, plus an illuminated wine cabinet to add a touch of colour. Here, the talented Japanese chef creates top-quality cuisine using the freshest ingredients. At lunchtime, there’s also a lighter “Bento box” and an omakase tasting menu (“Mi affido a te”) which is completely vegetarian.

Name: Nomos Ante
Address: Via di San Paolo alla Regola, 3, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: Within a newly opened hotel of clean, luxurious lines, a contemporary restaurant of well-defined personality takes shape, guided by a young and cosmopolitan chef. Deeply connected to the gastronomic culture of France, where he spent many formative years, yet also influenced by experiences in Japan and England, he delivers a refined and dynamic cuisine, capable of uniting technique with international sensitivity. The proposal moves along a modern line in which precision and immediacy of flavour are accompanied by careful attention to balance. The dishes tell a story that alternates elegance and character, never redundant, always centred on the essential quality of the ingredient. Among the most successful creations are the citrus spaghetti, conceived for those who appreciate fresh and vibrant profiles, and the charcoal-grilled lamb, elevated by a delicate accompaniment of rhubarb that adds a refined acidic note to the whole.

Name: Novanta
Description: Situated in the Bassa Pavese region and easily accessible via the A21, Novanta is a classic, rustic-style restaurant with a warm and authentic feel. At lunchtime, the menu offers simple, genuine dishes, while in the evening and at the weekend the cuisine takes on a more gourmet and regional flavour. Duck takes pride of place on the menu, featuring in numerous dishes, and is an important ingredient in the delicious ragù served with fusilloni pasta. The extensive wine list features local and international labels, including an interesting 2012 Wollenweider Riesling Renano from Germany’s Moselle region. The lunchtime menu offers unbeatable value for money!

Name: Novo Osteria
Address: Piazza De Cristoforis 30, Borgonovo Val Tidone, 29011, Italy
Description: Originally a monastery, this building dating back to the 11C was later transformed into an inn. Having closed at the beginning of this century, the building has now been fully renovated and restored to its original function, while retaining much of its original architecture. In addition to the restaurant, which serves traditional local cuisine with a modern focus and plenty of flavour (we particularly enjoyed the savoury zabaglione gnocchi with porcini mushrooms, Jerusalem artichokes and currants), there are also seven guestrooms available in the adjoining Locanda Borgo Impero.

Name: Nugolo
Description: A restaurant with a convivial atmosphere, enlivened by chic, colourful furnishings, provides the setting for an open kitchen where a young and talented chef stages a contemporary, creative and deeply seasonal offering. The dishes reveal imagination and precision: seared octopus with mussels, potatoes, buffalo-milk panna cotta and parsley; duck breast with a red-fruit jus, chard, bao and shredded duck leg; Sorrento lemon sorbet with herb crumble and candied lemon. Completing the experience is cheerful, attentive service from a motivated and well-coordinated front-of-house team.

Name: Nunù Trattoria Moderna
Address: Corso Giuseppe Garibaldi 32, Torre del Greco, 80059, Italy
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the seafront promenade, this friendly, colourful restaurant serves delicious, carefully prepared fish and meat dishes inspired by the traditions of Campania yet reinterpreted with a touch of imagination and character by skilful owner-chef Nunzio Spagnuolo. Our inspector’s favourite dish was the ravioli alla caprese with three types of tomato, provolone del Monaco cheese and basil-infused olive oil.

Name: ORIGINI
Description: In the heart of the Sulcis region, a land deeply shaped by Sardinia’s mining history and brought to life each summer by the atmosphere of the famous Narcao Blues Festival, this lively restaurant on the high street is the showcase for Antonella Orioni’s passion for food and the warm welcome of Efisio, her life partner and the restaurant’s invaluable ambassador, who brings its philosophy to life. Here, Sardinian tradition is reimagined with a contemporary sensitivity, through creative dishes that retain their connection to local ingredients and flavours. The cuisine is remarkable for its character and authenticity, as demonstrated by the fresh pasta ‘gigli’ served with a ragù made from local guanciale, enriched with juniper berries aged for 18 months, or the quail with lentisk, stuffed with guanciale and rocket. The menu thus offers a rich journey of discovery through the finest produce of the Sulcis region, combining tradition, innovation and flavour in each course.

Name: Oasi
Description: Over the years, the beach establishment has gradually developed: the beach and bar remain, but today's pride is the restaurant. The husband and wife divide their duties between the kitchen and dining area (including wine). They've built a good reputation thanks to classic seafood cuisine, highlighted by the chef's personal creative touches. A passionate and imaginative self-taught chef, his steamed oyster seasoned with lemon zest on tomato water is a particularly tasty shot that represents their style.

Name: Oberlechner
Description: From Merano you climb to an altitude of 1 000m to this restaurant, which boasts breathtaking views of the town and surrounding mountains. The menu here focuses mainly on local ingredients which are carefully prepared without too many creative twists, resulting in delicious and generous dishes such as braised beef with a Lagrein sauce (accompanied by rice and vegetables). All the attractive guestrooms have a balcony and the same stunning view.

Name: Oberraindlhof
Description: The family that run this restaurant occupying an old farmhouse with origins dating back to the 16C has a relationship with the region that goes back decades. In later years, the farm became an inn and it has now been run by the same family for five generations, all motivated by a desire to introduce their guests to the best local recipes and ingredients. Dishes include excellent fresh ravioli stuffed with cheese produced in the nearby valley and served (in summer) with tomato and basil sauce. An excellent wine list and the hotel’s warm and friendly ambience add to the appeal.

Name: Oberwirt
Description: The various Stube-style dining rooms in the Oberwirt hotel restaurant have a typical Tyrolean ambience, while the cuisine is decidedly traditional with its focus on seasonal and regional ingredients, although a few fish options also always feature on the menu. Wine-enthusiasts will be delighted with the excellent wine selection.

Name: Olio Fishbar
Address: Via Padre Luigi Monti 4, Saronno, 21047, Italy
Description: A modern bistro in the heart of Saronno, where guests leave their cars in nearby parking areas to settle into well-appointed tables (reservations recommended, even for lunch) and savor generous dishes, primarily seafood, though not exclusively. Fresh aromas, clean flavors, an abundance of raw preparations, and a few meat options, curiously without any pasta courses. We particularly enjoyed the “fish and chips” featuring coalfish, crispy and golden, and the Sicilian cannolo “our way,” indulgent and fragrant. The wine list is concise but thoughtfully curated, while both ownership and kitchen bear the signature of the Michelin-starred restaurant Olio in Origgio.

Name: Olona - "Da Venanzio" dal 1922
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: A bastion of regional cuisine for over a century, this restaurant occupies an attractive group of buildings with a large outdoor summer area shaded by a pergola and a charming dining room with a retro feel. Traditional recipes with interesting and personalised twists take centre stage, including superb ravioli del plin with three roasts and a meat sauce – this is Lombardy, after all! Impressive wine list, including wines by the glass.

Name: Oltre Osteria
Address: Località le Macìe 45, Castellina in Chianti, 53011, Italy
Description: Set within the Rocca delle Macìe winery, in the heart of Castellina in Chianti, Oltre Osteria offers a contemporary dining experience created by Chef Bardotti, centred around three tasting menus, including a vegetarian option. The cuisine focuses on seasonality, showcasing local produce and the careful handling of ingredients, with an approach that prioritises waste reduction. The elegant, minimalist interiors reflect a refined attention to detail, enhanced by elements personally selected by the chef, a spectacular open-plan kitchen with a Chef’s Table, and large windows overlooking the picturesque Chianti hills. To round off the experience, there is a carefully curated wine list, which focuses on the finest local wines and those produced by Rocca delle Macìe itself.

Name: Oltre.
Description: This restaurant in the lively Mercato delle Erbe district has an entrance adorned with hundreds of stickers, giving it the appearance of a record shop rather than a contemporary-style eatery with a bar counter and a highly original surfboard table near the entrance. The modern cuisine has its roots in the region yet also includes skilfully prepared dishes from around the world (we highly recommend the Bolognese ramen, which includes tagliolino in a mushroom broth, with parmesan, quail eggs marinated in balsamic vinegar, and spinach). There’s also a choice of cocktails to start or round off your meal. Booking is highly recommended.

Name: Oltremare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Restaurant Oltremare was born of an ambitious project, conceived to give full expression to a coherent and contemporary gastronomic vision, capable of showcasing the talent of the chef and his brigade.
