Situated on the fifth floor of the Hotel Due Torri, the space has recently undergone a significant refurbishment that has heightened its elegance and atmosphere, making it more welcoming and visually striking than ever. Even in its name, Oltremare declares its identity: an authentic Mediterranean cuisine, expressed through seasonal, often farm-to-table, ingredients, and recipes rooted in local tradition. The result is a culinary journey capable of conveying the purity of flavour and the richness of aroma, always with an eye firmly on the contemporary. The offering is distinguished by a creative approach built on solid foundations, between nods to and reinterpretations of Campanian tradition, delivering balanced and recognisable dishes. Completing the experience, the extraordinary panoramic view over the Amalfi Coast: the broad windows frame glimpses of rare beauty, making every moment at the table all the more evocative and memorable.

Name: Onda Blu
Address: Via Orsa Minore 1, San Mauro a Mare, 47030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A spot of unexpected elegance, almost right on the beach, with a simple, light-filled dining room featuring large windows opening out onto the sea. The cuisine celebrates the Adriatic’s seafaring tradition through ingredients of exceptional freshness and quality, with a menu designed as a dynamic framework, enriched daily with the finest produce from the market. For lovers of raw fish and marinated dishes, the selection is extensive and carefully curated, reflecting careful and ongoing research. The experience is rounded off by an excellent wine list, featuring some interesting international selections, particularly from France; the few tables on the outdoor terrace are in high demand and should be booked well in advance.

Name: Opera
Address: Via Sant'Antonio da Padova 3, Turin, 10121, Italy
Description: The former nineteenth century refectory of the nearby church has become the laboratory of a chef who is as skillful as he is creative: wrapped in the warm atmosphere of the brickwork of the evocative dining room, all the dishes have fruit as a recurring ingredient, which adds a touch of acidity and flavor to dishes of creative cuisine, whether of meat or fish, further enhanced by the work of an excellent sommelier.

Name: Opera|02
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An oasis of taste to the east of Modena: here, the farm estate, also known for its production of balsamic vinegar, welcomes guests with rooms, a small spa and a restaurant immersed in the quiet of the countryside. The cooking tells the story of the Modenese territory through recipes that showcase local ingredients, alternating dishes faithful to tradition – such as tortelli in capon broth or the indulgent zuppa inglese – with others in which the chef allows himself greater creative freedom. The result is an honest yet carefully crafted offering, capable of uniting gastronomic memory with more personal interpretations, always in keeping with the seasons.

Name: Opificio
Description: A modern restaurant in the province of Padova which, over the past ten years, has grown and evolved from a gastro pub to the top-quality eatery that it is today. The cuisine is fairly eclectic, featuring meat and fish dishes alike, with the option of a lighter menu at lunchtime. The best dishes are showcased on the à la carte and are often made using luxury ingredients such as foie gras, scampi and Wagyu beef. The impressive wine list demonstrates a passion for international sparkling wines, while the excellent selection of wines by the glass is further enhanced by a choice of cocktails (also available at midday).

Name: Ora d'Aria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Behind the Uffizi, a restaurant that stands out for its originality: not so much for its impressively large open kitchen as for its deliberate desire to encourage direct interaction between guests and the kitchen team. The restaurant’s name reflects its proximity to the historic Florentine prison of Le Murate and its intention to offer customers a moment of genuine relaxation.A small but charming dining room adorned with a ceiling frescoed with gold leaf, houses Marco Stabile’s delightful restaurant, where he serves creative cuisine that is equally accomplished in both meat and fish dishes, all based on top-quality ingredients.

Name: Origini
Description: In the hills above Rimini, at the border with the Marche, lies an enchanting medieval village. Along the main street that runs through it, this charming restaurant offers intimate, atmospheric rooms on both floors. The kitchen, however, is the real surprise: in the hands of Filippo Benelli, it is creative, elaborate and of an excellent standard.

Name: Orso Grigio
Description: In the center of Cavalese, within the hotel of the same name, a young chef presents an intelligent and delicious reinterpretation of Trentino gastronomic traditions without distorting their identity. A stop not to be missed, complemented by a solid wine selection featuring several organic, biodynamic, and amphora-aged bottles. Essential is the Schüttelbrot gelato with black bilberry, wild spinach, and thyme.

Name: Orti Villadorata
Description: Set among the hills surrounding Noto, within the Country House Villadorata, lies a picturesque rural landscape where the view stretches all the way to the sea, and the on-site vegetable gardens provide a significant proportion of the vegetables used in the kitchen. Set against this backdrop of refined rural charm, the culinary offering remains firmly rooted in the produce and flavours of Sicilian tradition, reimagined with a contemporary sensitivity. The restaurant offers a single tasting menu with à la carte options, striking a successful balance between regional identity and freedom of choice.

Name: Ortica
Address: Via Giovanni Migone 4, Pieve Ligure, 16031, Italy
Description: You drive along 4.5km of winding, narrow (occasionally extremely narrow) roads to get to Ortica, the restaurant at the Tenuta Golfo Paradiso about 35min from Genoa. As is often the case, once at your destination the extensive views of the Tyrrhenian Sea from the restaurant more than compensate for the effort of getting here. Neither will you be disappointed by the cuisine, which is prepared using top-quality ingredients such as vegetables from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden, local fish and carefully selected meat. Dishes are fresh and modern, and occasionally cooked over the barbecue grill.

Name: Orto
FacilitiesAndServices: Brunch,Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed
Description: At Nina Trulli Resort, nestled in one of the most enchanting areas of the Puglian countryside, among dry stone walls and typical vegetation, you can reconnect with nature. Walking through the restaurant's gardens and orchards is an inspiring experience. The focus on plant-based elements is also reflected in the kitchen: there are two tasting menus – one entirely green, while the other, despite including animal products, also highlights vegetables as the main feature.

Name: Osaka
Description: A new home for this historic restaurant, with minimalist interiors that embrace a full‑on oriental aesthetic to showcase authentic Japanese cuisine. A set menu at lunch and à la carte at dinner from which we recommend the Makimoto rolls of amberjack with shiso leaves, sesame seeds and freshly marinated wasabi. Or the festive Sukiyaki, a Japanese take on a bourguignon where meat and vegetables are cooked in a simmering broth at the table and shared among guests. The menu is extensive and rich with other succulent offerings from the Land of the Rising Sun.

Name: Oscar
Description: Situated amid the fascinating 19C buildings in Ardenza, a district in the south of Livorno, Oscar is an excellent choice for anyone keen to enjoy simple, classic and traditional fish dishes with a focus on good quality – the sort of place where you would be more than happy to eat every day. And surely there’s no higher compliment than that!

Name: Ostaria
Address: Via Giovan Battista Perasso 10/12, Syracuse, 96100, Italy
Description: This restaurant in the centre of the modern city, yet just a stone’s throw from Ortigia, focuses exclusively on meat (local and from further afield, much of it aged on the premises), which is sourced from non-intensive farming and cooked using contemporary methods such as the Josper oven. The excellent wine list focuses mainly on Sicilian labels but also includes bottles from elsewhere in Italy, as well as from other important wine-producing countries. A typical Sicilian ambience, soft lighting in the evening and friendly yet professional service complete the picture.

Name: Oste Scuro - Finsterwirt
Description: Run by the capable Mayr family, this long-established restaurant has occupied a narrow alleyway in the centre of Bressanone (Brixen) since the late 19C. The dining rooms are decorated in historic style, plus there’s a charming terrace for alfresco dining in summer. Dishes are presented on different tasting menus with the option of choosing traditional or Mediterranean dishes à la carte style – we highly recommend the soup made with Sylvaner wine from the Isarco valley, as well as the Tirtl (fried pie) stuffed with ricotta, spinach and cinnamon. Guestrooms are available in the nearby and recently renovated Adler Historic Guesthouse, which is run by the same owners.

Name: Osteria 1126
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Il Borgo di Cianciano is much more than just an osteria: it's also a farm, wine bar, and scattered hotel. The name “Osteria 1126” refers to the year of its founding; in the kitchen, a young couple offers simple, seasonal Tuscan dishes. Don't miss the pappa al pomodoro and the Chianti Classico Riserva, which is elegant and persistent. At the entrance of the borgo, a small aging cellar offers a brief but fascinating visit.

Name: Osteria 1861
Address: Via Valentino Izzo 1, Santa Maria di Castellabate, 84048, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Accessed via a narrow alleyway behind the beach, this restaurant housed in an old warehouse once used for smoking cured meats and drying Cilento figs boasts stone-vaulted ceilings, a romantic ambience and a small terrace embellished by beautiful plants. Chef Antoni Tafuri’s cuisine features on various tasting menus (including vegetarian and vegan) and an à la carte and demonstrates careful combinations that aim to showcase his regional ingredients to the full.

Name: Osteria Al GiGianca
Description: Although the out - of - town location is a slight drawback, this restaurant passionately run has a welcoming atmosphere. Seasonal, regional cuisine, plus a good choice of wine and beers.

Name: Osteria Antico Brolo
Description: Situated in the upper part of the town near the Vittoriale estate, this rustic 18C building is the setting for regional cuisine prepared using seasonal ingredients. The charming small courtyard offers shade for summer dining, while the interior dining room also includes a single table on a small balcony which needs to be booked well in advance.

Name: Osteria Arborina
Description: Arborina Relais is a delightful retreat tucked away among Italy's most prestigious vineyards. Time here seems to slow down to make room for pleasure: a modern and refined location, where every detail speaks of passion and care. The cuisine takes you on a sensory journey, combining technique and creativity to deliver unique experiences. The “no waste” concept becomes a philosophy, turning every ingredient into a pure harmony of flavours. You will be surprised by two tasting menus, with 5 or 8 courses, designed to excite and amaze with every bite. Completing the picture is a wine list that celebrates Piedmont, ready to accompany every moment with elegance and character.

Name: Osteria Arbustico
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Set against the evocative historical backdrop on the outskirts of the Paestum Archaeological Park, Osteria Arbustico returns with renewed vigour, welcoming guests into a contemporary, minimalist and elegant dining room, where each detail is designed to complement the experience without distracting from it. Taking centre stage is the cuisine of Cristian Torsiello: aged forty, originally from Valva, a small village in the Salerno area where his culinary journey began. His cuisine is refined, built on technique, sensitivity and a deep respect for the ingredients – predominantly local – which he interprets with rigour and vision. The ‘Tanagro’ tasting menu, comprising ten courses, draws its inspiration from the local area while looking to the future, striking a balance between tradition and creative flair. The dishes showcase an authentic yet continually evolving Campania, where seasonality and precision guide each choice. At lunchtime, the menu takes on a lighter tone with a more casual bistro-style offering that remains true to the kitchen’s identity; in the evening, however, the pace changes and the experience becomes more complete, allowing the chef’s distinctive style to shine through.

Name: Osteria Ardenga
Description: An authentic trattoria which is a joy to visit, where time seems to have stood still for decades. Situated on the border between two provinces, the restaurant focuses on specialities from Parma, many of which are made from home - grown produce. Homemade pickles and chutneys are also sold here.

Name: Osteria Bellavista
Address: Via Piovega 30, località Farra, Paderno del Grappa, 31017, Italy
Description: At Osteria Bellavista, the menu is recited: Paolo and Raffaele, father and son, will guide you through the dishes of the day, prepared with excellent ingredients and authentic passion. The cuisine? A tribute to tradition, between sea and land, with a contemporary touch that surprises without betraying its roots.

Name: Osteria Bertaina
Description: Overlooking the picturesque square in the city’s oldest quarter, medieval in origin, the restaurant welcomes guests through the porticoes, leading them into two intimate dining rooms of vintage charm, with frescoed ceilings dating to the early twentieth century. The cuisine delivers on every level: Piedmontese recipes are reinterpreted with a modern, lighter touch without betraying their soul. Among the must-try dishes, our inspector highlights the gobbo cardoon prepared according to grandmother’s family recipe. And if indecision takes hold, trust the advice of the young, energetic and knowledgeable dining room manager, always ready to guide you toward the ideal path.

Name: Osteria Billis
Description: Almost ten years after it opened, this restaurant run by the Billis twins is moving towards what its owners describe as a “new tradition” – a personalised way of interpreting local traditions through the lens of global influences. While maintaining roots in solid Piedmontese traditions, the cuisine combines local ingredients with international techniques. Examples include “roasted rice”, a dish which is cooked in the oven and then flavoured according to the season and whim of the chef, and the “Carpaccio in Ramino”, beef which is lightly seared in a copper pan with rosemary, bay leaf, salt and pepper. The veranda’s retro ambience immediately catches the eye of passersby in the nearby park, adding to the appeal of this fascinating building dating from the early 20C.

Name: Osteria Boccolicchio
Description: Nestled among the narrow streets of the pedestrianised historic centre, this restaurant welcomes guests into cosy, tastefully decorated dining rooms, but really comes into its own on the terrace overlooking a small open space, where the atmosphere is even more charming. The menu focuses mainly on seafood and ranges from classic dishes to those featuring subtle creative touches, such as crispy octopus tentacles served on a potato purée enriched with the sweetness of turnip and finished with crispy peppers, which add fragrance and character. At the heart of it all is the quality of the raw ingredients, which are fresh and expertly prepared, as demonstrated by the fish and shellfish – often served directly at the table – which stand out for their flavour and impeccable freshness.

Name: Osteria Borgo Ronche
Description: With only a handful of tables – all the more reason to reserve – and a contemporary, streamlined yet welcoming setting, this intimate spot showcases the chef-owner’s resolutely seafood-focused cuisine, though a couple of meat options round out the menu. Preparations and pairings remain largely classic, as seen in the gratinéed Breton scallops, while raw seafood also makes an appearance, sometimes unexpectedly atop pasta, as in the standout spaghettoni with cacio e pepe and red prawn tartare.

Name: Osteria Casale Ferrovia
Address: Via Stazione 1, sulla SP 34, Carovigno, 72012, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in what was once the 20C dwelling of an old olive mill, this restaurant boasts elegant decor, including a few antique family pieces and Art Deco - style tables. The female owner - chef prepares light and modern dishes with a regional flavour, while the wine list also showcases the best of Puglia. As the name suggests, the railway lies to the rear of the property, although there’s very little noise and no disturbance at all.

Name: Osteria Cascina dei Fiori
Description: This restaurant’s warm, elegant and rustic atmosphere with wooden furniture and exposed beams provides the setting for its seasonally inspired, regional cuisine. The experienced owners are welcoming and attentive, while the menu features specialities such as frogs’ leg and courgette flower risotto.

Name: Osteria Dalie e Fagioli
Address: Via Campagnola 45, Manerba del Garda, 25080, Italy
Description: One of the best restaurants in the region, where you’ll enjoy eclectic cuisine full of convincing flavours which is inspired by various regional traditions (especially those from Brescia, but also from elsewhere in Italy) which always hits the mark.

Name: Osteria Dell'Unione
Description: In the heart of the Langhe del Barbaresco, this osteria preserves the convivial spirit of traditional establishments from times past. The atmosphere is warm and familial, while aromas and flavors immediately evoke the home cooking of recipes handed down through generations, and prepared to order. The menu celebrates the cornerstones of authentic tradition: from free-range chicken cacciatore to the soft, celebrated spinach frittatas, dishes deceptively simple in appearance, yet revealing a precise hand respectful of Piedmontese culinary heritage. The wine list, well-structured and fairly priced, accompanies the meal in a natural manner. In warmer months, the vine-shaded pergola becomes the ideal setting for a meal of rustic, genuine charm.

Name: Osteria Erbaluce
Description: Just steps from the Leonardo-designed canal harbor, this spot takes a bold stance: it serves only meat, with a strong focus on the grill. Quality ingredients, fresh pastas, and classic house-made spoon desserts. An excellent wine list, especially strong on reds, rounds out the offering. The dining room is bright and all white; the cool, tranquil outdoor terrace is very welcoming, ideal in the warmer months. At the helm is a young couple driven by passion and professionalism.

Name: Osteria Europa
Description: In the warmer months, the tables spill out onto the town’s main square, creating a lively and pleasantly holiday-like atmosphere; inside, however, the spaces are more intimate and evoke the warmth of the Alps. The kitchen is the setting for an intriguing blend of local tradition and more creative touches: the menu ranges from venison tartare to morro di baccalà, right through to dishes that look beyond regional boundaries, such as grilled cuttlefish served with garlic cream. To round off the experience, there is a carefully curated selection of wines and a relaxed, welcoming service, available at any time of day. A go-to spot for breakfast too.

Name: Osteria Fernanda
Address: Via Crescenzo Del Monte 18/24, Rome, 00153, Italy
Description: In the district famous for its Porta Portese market, this restaurant run by two talented business partners is definitely worth a visit. Andrea oversees the minimalist-style dining room, while Luca demonstrates real passion in his creative cuisine made from locally sourced ingredients, as well as produce from further afield. Among the desserts, we highly recommended the Porter beer ice-cream with black garlic mousse, chocolate and tuber peelings.

Name: Osteria Forno Ercole
Description: Hidden among the alleyways of Jesi, Osteria Forno Ercole is a former bakery (part of which can still be seen) which serves authentic cuisine in a warm, welcoming atmosphere. Local recipes and Mediterranean flavours come together on the traditional menu, with a focus on seasonal ingredients of the highest quality. Tagliatelle with porcini mushrooms, Marche-style fritto misto and steak with carrots, potatoes and radicchio are just some of the dishes on the menu here.

Name: Osteria FraSe
Address: Via Crociata 9, Piove di Sacco, 35028, Italy
Description: In this restaurant, husband Francesco takes care of the wine, while his wife Serena is at the helm in the open-view kitchen, creating dishes with a focus on fish and seafood (including raw options), fresh pasta dishes and classic recipes with the occasional imaginative twist or the addition of exotic fruit. This is a modern and welcoming osteria with a simple decor, where the female staff provide excellent service with a friendly smile.

Name: Osteria Frangipane
Description: New premises, though still in the heart of Trani, for siblings Ivan and Sara, who have moved their restaurant, which covers around 800 metres, closer to the harbour. Today, they welcome guests inside Palazzo Bianchi, using the elegant inner courtyard, shaded by majestic trees, as an outdoor seating area. The qualities that have been so highly regarded in the past remain unchanged: a contemporary tavern that showcases Apulian cuisine, with a particular focus on seafood specialities and the use of excellent ingredients. Among the most impressive dishes, the Mediterranean-style fish dish, prepared with potatoes, olives and tomatoes, stands out; the raw seafood platters are also worth a mention, while the traditional orecchiette is served with a tasty fish-based sauce.

Name: Osteria Giorgione da Masa
Address: Calle Larga dei Proverbi, 4582/A, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description: Just steps from Campo Santi Apostoli, Chef Masa weaves together homestyle Japanese traditions with Venetian cicchetti, transcending the classic distinction between courses: here, dishes arrive all at once, without rules. For those who prefer to be guided, there’s a tasting menu offering a wide array of bites. Desserts are a true surprise, especially the yogurt, caramel, and matcha mousse, a favorite of our inspector.

Name: Osteria Grande
Description: This restaurant overlooking the magnificent Piazza Grande and the Loggia Vasariana that takes up one whole side of the square was opened in the summer of 2022 by the enthusiastic Fatjon and Lorenzo (if you ask, they’ll happily share their knowledge of Arezzo’s history with you). The former is at the helm in the kitchen where he expresses his passion for cuisine in seasonal, contemporary-style dishes such as pigeon breast, leg and fillet (each cut is prepared in the appropriate way) served with sweet onion and cocoa nibs, while the latter oversees the wine selection and recommends suitable pairings to guests. For the chef’s pigeon speciality, he may, for example, suggest an original Maturato Tiberini 2018 (a white wine made from grapes that are left to ripen on the vine). Cocktail staff are also hand for guests keen to choose an aperitif or an after-dinner drink from the extensive cocktail list.

Name: Osteria Il Bagatto
Address: Via XX Settembre 16, Limone Piemonte, 12015, Italy
Description: Nestled amid the stone houses of Limone Piemonte, this charming gourmet restaurant is situated in a typical historic passageway. Influenced by the seasons and the chef’s creative skills, the menu includes interesting dishes such as char, gnocchi with blue goat’s cheese and delicious sweetbreads in butter with cannellini beans and cavolo nero. To accompany your meal, you might like to indulge in a bottle of vintage Barolo chosen from the concise yet carefully chosen wine list. The 2013 Michele Chiarlo Barolo Cerequio, produced in a cold and rainy year, has aged well thanks to its powerful tannins.

Name: Osteria Il Cappello
Description: The outdoor terrace at this restaurant overlooks a pleasant pedestrian piazza in the historic centre, while the welcoming dining rooms are decorated in a style typical of the Trentino. The cuisine – reliable, seasonal and full of flavour – is traditionally Italian, yet with a contemporary touch. The menu also features a few regional options as well as the occasional fish dish. The quail stuffed with acacia honey, pumpkin purée and stewed radicchio is superb.

Name: Osteria Il Granaio
Address: Via dei Monaci, Rapolano Terme, 53040, Italy
Description: In the heart of Rapolano Terme’s historic centre, in a charming building dating back to the 17th century, this elegant establishment combines the convivial atmosphere of a traditional tavern with the attention to detail and care of a fine restaurant. The dining rooms, adorned with striking brick arches, offer a menu ranging from the great classics of Tuscan cuisine – from pici served with a variety of sauces to the traditional peposo – to intriguing forays into the world of seafood. Among the dishes not to be missed are the ravioli stuffed with scallops and prawns, which are particularly flavourful and well-balanced. To round off the experience, there is the adjacent Enoteca Il Granaio, a real must-visit for wine lovers.

Name: Osteria Il Maialetto
Address: Via Della Repubblica 348, Monsummano Terme, 51015, Italy
Description: Next to the historic family butcher’s shop lies the vibrant tavern, which is approaching its 100th anniversary without losing any of its surprisingly youthful spirit. People come here to enjoy authentic, straightforward Tuscan cuisine: from bruschetta and crostini to pappa al pomodoro and ribollita, via platters of charcuterie and Florentine steak – which, naturally, will bump up the bill a little.The warm hospitality that characterises the place makes the experience even more enjoyable.

Name: Osteria Il Principe e Il Pirata
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This restaurant is housed in a typical island house with rustic furniture and a large terrace with sea views. Here, the Casano family look after guests, are responsible for the impressive wine list and, of course, prepare the cuisine that focuses on top-quality ingredients and Sicilian recipes. Specialities include couscous with fresh fish and vegetables, cuttlefish “alla fiamma” and courgettes marinated in mint, as well as typical desserts such as the “bacio pantesco”.

Name: Osteria Ime
Description: In this pretty, welcoming restaurant, the female chef from Albania, who has adopted Italian culinary traditions over her many years in the country, serves a choice of tasting menus. Her dishes have distinct geographical names and are full of colour and prepared from top-quality ingredients which change with the passing seasons. There are only a few tables available, so booking ahead is always a good idea. You’ll be warmly welcomed with a friendly smile that sets the tone for what is sure to be a highly enjoyable evening.

Name: Osteria L'Abbiccì
Address: Via Medici da Seregno 29, Seregno, 20831, Italy
Description: Situated in the centre of Seregno, this modern inn boasts a bright, spacious dining room with an ambience which is both friendly and yet respectful of guests’ privacy. The cuisine is overseen by Davide, who trained with Mauro Elli, the owner-chef of Il Cantuccio in Albavilla. Here, he creates dishes full of character, with a focus on top-quality ingredients and skilful presentation techniques. For a memorable dining experience, the chef’s surprise menu makes an excellent choice. Impressive wine selection and professional service overseen by Gabriele add to the appeal. The business lunch offers excellent value for money.

Name: Osteria L'Orciaia
Description: Osteria l’Orciaia is a little treasure trove of authentic flavors, where true Tuscan cuisine is celebrated in a rustic and well-crafted setting. In the summer, dining is outdoors with breathtaking views of the hills; in winter, guests retreat to a cozy room featuring exposed stone, wood, and artisanal details. The peposo is a must-try: intense, traditional, and irresistible!

Name: Osteria La Sangiovesa
Address: Piazza Beato Simone Balacchi 14, Santarcangelo di Romagna, 47822, Italy
Description: History pervades this eighteenth-century palazzo, but above all it is the soul of Romagna that fills the air, its friendly welcome, through rooms that overflow with warmth and atmosphere. The cooking is, naturally, of the local area, with cured meats, pasta, meat dishes and excellent desserts holding uncontested sway.

Name: Osteria Landi
Address: Via Claudio 28, Lido di Ostia, 00122, Italy
Description: Slightly tucked away yet centrally located, this bistrot welcomes guests into intimate interiors that evoke the discreet elegance of English clubs, with a small outdoor terrace completing the offer. In the kitchen, a dependable professional interprets a cuisine closely tied to the market and the nearby sea, with essential, well-balanced dishes. In the dining room, wine plays a leading role, thanks to a carefully curated, clear list rich in small niche producers. Seating is limited: booking is strongly recommended.

Name: Osteria Mercato
Description: Tucked slightly away from the city’s main tourist paths, behind the lanes of the historical center, this restaurant presents a contemporary setting with a distinctly customized décor. The cuisine moves confidently between land and sea: from ravioli filled with “farmyard” meats, nettles, and cardoncelli mushrooms to skewered octopus with mussels and a saffron broth, with room for a touch of creativity as well. Excellent attention is paid to sourcing local ingredients, and in the warmer months, the outdoor terrace is fresh and pleasant.

Name: Osteria Mercede
Description: For over ten years this welcoming trattoria has delighted its guests with a vibrant seafood cuisine steeped in Sicilian and Mediterranean character. In the dining room, a blackboard of daily specials invites guests to choose between recipes of solid local tradition and offerings that celebrate the sea with simplicity and personality. Among the house must-tries, the delicious bruschette del marinaio stand out: a trio of swordfish and aubergine caponata, marinated anchovies and amberjack carpaccio with salt and tuna bottarga, a perfect expression of the venue’s true calling. Also well worth trying is the “Caciucco Mercede”, rich and fragrant, prepared with John Dory, scorpionfish, sea bass, prawns and squid. And to close on a sweet note, room must be left for the desserts, in particular the “Scannolo”, a deconstructed and highly accomplished interpretation of the classic Sicilian cannolo.

Name: Osteria Mood
Address: Via Cesare Battisti 58, San Bartolomeo al Mare, 18016, Italy
Description: Situated just a few minutes from the seafront promenade in a quiet, residential district, this restaurant with a relaxing ambience serves delicious Ligurian cuisine with a focus on organic vegetables, fish and seafood (local whenever possible), and home-made bread, desserts and fresh pasta. In summer, meals are served by the swimming pool in the garden, while in winter, the welcoming covered veranda boasts extensive sea views.

Name: Osteria Numero Sette
Description: There’s been a recent change in management at this informal, friendly restaurant which serves generously portioned, carefully prepared dishes from the region and elsewhere in Italy, all at highly competitive prices. Although the cuisine might not be particularly modern, this is good solid cuisine served in a welcoming atmosphere.

Name: Osteria Ricanatti
Description: This cozy little restaurant, backed by attentive and impeccably polished service, reveals a regional cuisine that is both flavorful and thoughtfully reinterpreted, available through several tasting menus as well as à la carte. Ingredient sourcing is exacting, with all vegetables harvested from the family’s garden just a few kilometers away – a guarantee of freshness and seasonality. Among the most representative dishes: the pecorino and potato tartare dressed with chimichurri, Argentina’s signature green sauce, or the perfectly al dente paccheri with a two-tomato coulis, raw bluefin tuna, and fried capers – a plate that strikes an ideal balance of intensity and harmony.

Name: Osteria Saint Martin
Description: In the historic centre of Zagarolo, the simple and intimate dining room hosts an excellent cuisine that draws upon certain Lazio elements in both produce and recipes, yet also embraces deliberate influences born of the chef’s wealth of experience. This is a gastronomic destination not to be missed, particularly if one wishes to experience cookery that is less traditional and incorporates more exotic ingredients, or at least those not strictly local in character. Tables are limited, so we recommend booking ahead, while in fine weather one may take a seat on the charming terrace.

Name: Osteria Stella
Description: This osteria, just outside the town, has a long history and recently reopened its doors in 2024 thanks to a duo of young chefs who, after numerous experiences elsewhere, chose to breathe new life into it with a pleasantly contemporary atmosphere and cuisine that narrates the territory through regional recipes poised between Liguria and Piedmont, enriched by passion and modern technique. Not to be missed are the gnocco filled with pesto and pine nut sauce and the guinea fowl prepared in the Ligurian manner with triple-cooked potatoes, dishes that sincerely express their vision of updated tradition.

Name: Osteria Storica Morelli
Address: Piazza Petrini 1, località Canezza di Pergine, Pergine Valsugana, 38057, Italy
Description: In the typical mountain hamlet of Canezza di Pergine, two partners run this historic trattoria housed in a sixteenth-century building. The menu breathes a deep love of local produce and recipes, from charcuterie to handmade fresh pasta, through game and freshwater fish, as well as raw-milk cheeses. Among the desserts, the rosada is an excellent finale!

Name: Osteria Taviani
Address: Via del Monte Ovest 25, Bientina, 56031, Italy
Description: Housed in a small Art Nouveau-style villa, this restaurant boasts an elegant yet warm and friendly ambience. The cuisine here is modern and full of flavour, with a focus on meat dishes (although a few fish options also feature) with their roots firmly anchored in Tuscan traditions (such as the fried steak). During the hunting season, the contemporary-style game dishes are particularly delicious. The wine list includes a few French labels, plus there’s a small, attractive outdoor space in the courtyard to the rear which overlooks a beautiful garden.

Name: Osteria Terra Arsa
Description: The two Murani brothers offer compelling reason to venture into this unremarkable neighbourhood east of Foggia’s centre: their cooking. The fresh and colourful dining rooms anticipate a style that finds full expression on the plate, where fragrant and flavourful tastes reveal themselves. The recipes, sometimes inspired by family memories, take shape from Puglian and seasonal ingredients, further elevated by vegetables from their own garden. An exception is salt cod – to which an entire tasting menu is dedicated – yet it remains perfectly in keeping with local tradition: the oven-baked version is excellent, with savoury breadcrumbs, served on a cream of Carpino broad beans and sautéed chicory. The wine list is entirely regional, a coherent choice that completes the experience with authenticity.

Name: Osteria Vecchia Noce
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This former 18C mill, located in the centre of a tiny medieval district on the outskirts of Uliveto Terme, boasts a warm, elegant ambience full of character. Expertly run by the same family for the past 35 years, it serves honest, traditional cuisine with a focus on regional recipes and an equal balance of meat and fish.

Name: Osteria Vecchio Borgo
Description: Described as a “meeting point between Piedmont and Liguria”, this quiet, welcoming restaurant in the historic centre of Cuneo focuses on ingredients and recipes from these two regions – the family, all of whom are involved in the restaurant (the women in the kitchen and the men front of house), are from Liguria. The generous, top-quality cuisine is prepared using seasonal produce with a personalised touch and is accompanied by a good selection of wine, also available by the glass.

Name: Osteria a "Le Due Spade"
Address: Via Don Arcangelo Rizzi 11, Trento, 38122, Italy
Description: This beautiful Stube-style restaurant in the city centre has existed since the Council of Trent, with a succession of chefs and owners serving food here ever since the 16C. Still run with skill and expertise today, the restaurant boasts a small, intimate Alpine-style dining room where Trento specialities (char, apple strudel with vanilla ice cream) are served alongside typical Italian fare (risotto with mussel power and parsley pesto). All the dishes are cooked with an imaginative touch, resulting in a perfect balance of tradition and modernity!

Name: Osteria alle Testiere
Address: Calle del Mondo Novo, sestiere Castello 5801, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: This restaurant, now one of the most popular bistros in Venice, started out as a typical Venetian “bacaro”. The cuisine focuses on traditional Mediterranean and Venetian dishes, including vegetables, many of which are grown in a kitchen garden on Sant'Erasmo island (Osti in Orto) – an initiative which sees a number of small restaurants coming together to grow and share produce. The menu changes in line with market availability. With just a few tables, booking well in advance is highly recommended.

Name: Osteria da Afro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An expertly run family restaurant not far from the historic centre. Warm atmosphere in the two dining rooms (especially the one with the fireplace), where the daily specials are marked on a blackboard. A real gem of restaurant, which also has a few charming guestrooms furnished in fir and cherry wood.

Name: Osteria da Cippi
Description: A corner that is simply out of this world, tucked away in a delightful chalet with a fireplace that smells of wood and warmth. The cuisine celebrates local produce in tune with the seasons: wild herbs from Valdestali in spring, vegetables from the kitchen garden in summer, and fruits from the surrounding woods in autumn. Delicacies include lasagnetta with venison ragout and chanterelle mushrooms, cjarsons and antique apple strudel with vanilla ice cream. There is only one tasting menu, and reservations must be made at least two days in advance.

Name: Osteria da Fiore
Address: Calle del Scaleter, sestiere San Polo 2202/a, Venice, 30125, Italy
Description: Among a labyrinth of alleys and canals, stands the trattoria Da Fiore, elegant and with a family atmosphere. The main hall warmly welcomes guests, while a romantic terrace hosts a table for two by the canal. The cuisine, true to the land, will allow you to enjoy fried moleche [soft-shell crabs] (when in season): an experience not to be missed! Last but not least, there is the wine cellar, which has a fine selection of the most sought-after French and Italian wines (about 800 labels). Equally impressive is the selection of grappas, cognacs and whiskies.

Name: Osteria da Nando
Description: Operating since 1957 in the heart of the historic center, Nando is a go-to spot for those wanting to experience Valdostan cuisine: excellent cured meats (usually served with the famous fontina), polenta and fondue, fondue bourguignonne, rustic polenta tart with goat milk gelato... all prepared with top-quality ingredients and served in a simple yet atmospheric setting. The wine selection is excellent, focusing mainly on the Aosta Valley, with over 100 different labels, many of which are available by the glass. Among the desserts, the rothia is a must-try: white wine custard, spiced bread, and a sprinkle of cinnamon – intense, rich, and delicious.

Name: Osteria dai Coghi
Address: Via Alcide De Gasperi 9/13, Albarè di Costermano, 37010, Italy
Description: This well-kept, welcoming restaurant with a colourful decor and wine bottles adorning the walls serves imaginative dishes with modern combinations – our inspector particularly enjoyed the guinea fowl supreme with smoked black tea, carrots and beluga lentils. The well-chosen wine list features labels from Italy and further afield.

Name: Osteria dai Mazzeri
Description: Once the town hall of Follina, this building dating from 1704 is now home to a restaurant run by two brothers who serve delicious regional and seasonal cuisine here (in winter, don’t miss the spit-roasted chicken, veal or pork cooked according to local tradition). A beautiful mulberry tree, the old symbol of the village that was once involved in the silk industry, graces the outdoor dining space.

Name: Osteria dalla Peppa
Description: A trattoria in the old town, with rooms filled with memories and nostalgia, offering an atmosphere that makes you feel at home, just like the traditional cuisine. The fresh-egg pasta rolled out with a rolling pin (also on sale in their nearby shop) is the main attraction here, with main courses featuring various types of meat, and fish dishes on Fridays.

Name: Osteria de l'Umbreleèr
Description: Situated in Cicognolo in the Lower Po valley, where early morning mists create an evocative atmosphere in autumn, this traditional restaurant with a rustic feel serves specialities from Lombardy with a focus on delicious starters and top-quality meat. Our inspector particularly recommends the white onion gratin soup and the Burgundy-style snails. A simpler menu is available at lunchtime and there’s a small garden for alfresco dining on summer evenings.

Name: Osteria de' Mercati
Description: Slightly set back from the bustling streets of the historic centre yet still in the heart of the town, this delightful small restaurant is a recent addition to Sassari. It boasts a modern, elegant decor, friendly staff and a menu featuring carefully prepared fresh, seasonal dishes. Our inspector particularly recommends the seafood risotto. A choice of regional wines completes the picture.

Name: Osteria degli Angeli
Description: An attractive restaurant which offers a friendly and informal welcome and service, alongside an elegant, personalised yet classic decor. The cuisine is mainly Mediterranean in flavour, emphasised by the use of local and seasonal ingredients. The self-taught chef here is passionate about his cuisine.

Name: Osteria dei Vespri
Address: Piazza Croce dei Vespri 6, Palermo, 90133, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Situated in the palazzo where the famous ball scene in the “The Leopard” by Luchino Visconti was filmed, this restaurant serves cuisine that moves with the times, featuring modern dishes made from local ingredients, while a friendly welcome from the long-established owners adds to the appeal. Cocktails, tapas and simpler yet equally delicious cuisine is served in the Occhiovivo! Bistrot next door, the name of which refers to a Sicilian saying which means “Be careful!”.

Name: Osteria del 36
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The Osteria del 36 traces its roots to 1880 and owes its name to a curious tradition: wine was once sold here at 36 cents a litre. Today it presents a cuisine firmly anchored in the Emilian tradition, set alongside touches of a more contemporary flavour, as in the crispy loin of rabbit with Prosciutto di Parma, cream of onions, carrots and cardoncelli mushrooms. A deep affinity with the world of wine is reflected in a list that is well-constructed, carefully considered and of reliable quality, conceived to complement each dish to its best advantage.

Name: Osteria del Borgo
Description: Located in the heart of the historic center, this restaurant is distinguished by its warmly welcoming and attentive management. The cuisine alternates between fish and meat dishes, prepared with a personal touch yet still rooted in tradition. Among the desserts, highlights include the indulgent bunet or zabaione served with canestrelli cookies.

Name: Osteria del Borro
Address: Località Borro 52, San Giustino Valdarno, 52024, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the heart of Valdarno, Osteria del Borro is located within a thousand-hectare estate that houses an authentic medieval village. In the summer, you can dine on a terrace with breathtaking views of the countryside, while in the winter, you can settle into an elegant room with soft tones and an open kitchen. There are three tasting menus, built around local products and, most importantly, the estate's own garden.

Name: Osteria del Guà
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in the “barchessa” of a Palladian villa dating from 1541, this restaurant boasts an elegant dining room with an open fireplace. The cuisine here is creative and of excellent quality, with many of the main meat courses cooked over the barbecue grill. All in all, a romantic setting and superb food that is not to be missed.

Name: Osteria del Ponte
Address: Via Vittorio Veneto 22, Trezzano sul Naviglio, 20090, Italy
Description: Housed in a majestic historic farmhouse, this small friendly restaurant boasts intimate dining rooms and attractive “shabby-chic” style furnishings. In summer, the delightful outdoor space in the internal courtyard offers an idyllic setting. Traditional Milanese cuisine is the star of the show here, including specialities such as risotto with roasted bone-marrow, mondeghili meatballs and delicious breaded veal cutlet, also available in an “imperial” version for sharing.

Name: Osteria del Posto
Address: Via Calderini 15, loc. Chiugiana, Corciano, 06073, Italy
Description: Housed within an ancient mill in the village of Chiugiana, a small hamlet of Corciano, the osteria offers contemporary cuisine deeply rooted in the local area. Ingredients are carefully selected, and the wine list tells the stories of small producers, both local and national, with a special focus on artisanal and natural wines.

Name: Osteria del Tasso
Address: Via Bolgherese km 3,9, località San Walfredo, Bolgheri, 57022, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the famous Viale dei Cipressi avenue in one of Italy’s best-known wine-producing areas, this restaurant occupies one of the region’s most famous wineries, namely Guado al Tasso, renowned for its excellent wines. In fine weather, guests can dine in the shade of plane trees looking out over the vineyards. Simple, delicious and well-prepared cuisine, mostly traditional in style, plus specialities such as cured hams and grilled dishes.

Name: Osteria del Teatro
Description: Enjoy traditional cuisine served in an elegant 16C dining room with a fireplace or in more informal trattoria-style rooms, all of which are decorated with the same theatrical theme. The recipes here focus on local traditions and seasonal ingredients, resulting in colourful, well-balanced and beautifully presented dishes that are full of flavour. There are just a few tables on the small terrace near the entrance overlooking the pedestrianised street, so if you want to sit outdoors make sure you book well in advance.

Name: Osteria del Tempo Perso
Description: Tucked away in a corner of the historic centre, this little spot with a bistro feel wins you over with its cosy, informal atmosphere. Amid the photographs, books, bottles and wine glasses adorning the walls, there is an authentic charm to the place, enhanced by a well-curated selection of wines that looks beyond national borders to include some interesting European labels. The intimate seating arrangement, the soft lighting and the almost Parisian atmosphere make it the ideal spot for both a romantic dinner and an evening out with friends. The cuisine has a distinctly Italian character, with a menu that follows the rhythm of the seasons: focusing more on fish during the summer months and on meat during the winter. The dishes focus on classic flavours and showcasing the quality of the ingredients, as demonstrated by the delicious seafood ragù risotto.

Name: Osteria del Trentino - Da Marco
Description: A historical restaurant whose name recalls the origins of one of its earliest owners. Today this venue offers simple, traditional Piacenza cooking, where guests can enjoy excellent cured meats accompanied by vegetables from the restaurant’s own garden, fresh homemade pasta dishes, and main courses that also include offal preparations. Not to be missed are the fried veal brains: crispy on the outside, ultra soft within.

Name: Osteria dell'Arco
Description: Enjoy a warm family welcome at this centrally located restaurant with an internal courtyard, where the menu features a good choice of traditional and authentic dishes full of flavour. The restaurant is run by the same friendly managers as the renowned and popular Boccondivino in Bra, where the Slow Food concept was born. Booking ahead is always a good option.

Name: Osteria dell'Oca Bianca
Description: In the heart of a small town, right opposite the church, this typical village osteria run by a friendly family serves traditional cuisine from the Piedmont, including goose dishes. Highlights here include the rustic, welcoming ambience, an excellent wine list, a wine cellar that can be visited, and a charming glass-fronted veranda that is used throughout the year. There are also three beautiful guestrooms reserved exclusively for guests dining at the restaurant.

Name: Osteria della Chiocciola
Description: Situated in the historic centre just a stone’s throw from the elegant Via Roma, this restaurant is decorated with paintings by renowned modern artists such as Pignatelli, Andy Warhol, and Valerio Berruti. The ground floor is home to a colourful wine bar, while the first-floor restaurant serves traditional cuisine made from local ingredients with a natural focus on Piedmont. There is also a fish alternative for non-meat-eaters.

Name: Osteria della Corte
Description: This restaurant with 18C stone walls and arches boasts a small, intimate dining room and an outdoor courtyard for summer dining. The delicious yet simple cuisine focuses on fish and seafood full of rich flavours, which are a must for chef Silvia Cardelli! Just a stone’s throw from the restaurant, there’s also a champagne bar offering tastings by the glass and bottles produced by small, enthusiastic wineries – a choice of over 130 different labels in total.

Name: Osteria della Foce
Description: A lively and contemporary bistro that celebrates Mediterranean cuisine with a modern twist, offering meat and fish dishes characterised by distinct flavours and refined techniques. Highlights include yellowtail tartare with celery, rose syrup and seed crackers, and the delicious pavé of striped bass accompanied by mashed potatoes, sautéed artichokes and lemon sauce.

Name: Osteria della Tana
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Occupying the same red house as chef Alessandro Dal Degan’s gourmet restaurant, the Osteria is where this chef turns his attention to more traditional dishes (meat and fish alike), which are often typical of the Veneto. There’s one highly recommended exception, however, namely the carbonara dell’Osteria, prepared with top-quality ingredients from the region. Also popular are the baccalà alla vicentina (dried cod) and the tripe, both of which feature on a menu with a wide selection, including renowned dishes from the chef’s Michelin-starred restaurant. Full-bodied flavours that will delight the palate.

Name: Osteria dello Strecciolo
Description: Situated in the centre of the village, this popular and professionally run restaurant has an informal atmosphere. The cuisine is inspired by Mediterranean recipes and more regional traditions, with great care taken in the choice of ingredients and beautifully presented dishes. A business lunch menu is also available.

Name: Osteria di Fornio
Description: In the countryside at the border between the provinces of Parma and Piacenza, this osteria is a convincing stop for those in search of a cuisine that is understated yet rich in flavour. The offering distinguishes itself through handmade fresh pasta, meat main courses prepared from carefully selected produce, and a tempting selection of desserts. Among the recommended dishes, the chickpea fritter with Sant’Ilario shoulder lard, enhanced by drops of aged balsamic vinegar, stands out, as does the generous and satisfying zuppa inglese, a perfect conclusion to the meal.

Name: Osteria il Moro
Description: Overlooking the main thoroughfare of Trapani and enhanced by a pleasant outdoor area, Osteria Il Moro interprets Sicilian tradition with a contemporary outlook. The cooking of chef-patron Nicola Bandi draws its roots from the flavours of the island, before opening out into original and personal creations full of intensity and character. The sea is the chief protagonist, though forays into land-based cooking are not lacking: among these, the “Guancia Dolce Forte” stands out, enriched by an age-old chocolate-based sauce that elegantly enhances the meat. The wine selection is also carefully curated and of considerable interest, offering a generous showcase of regional excellence.

Name: Osteria la Fontanina
Address: Portichetti Fontanelle Santo Stefano 3, Verona, 37129, Italy
Description: Cross the Ponte Pietra and the enchantment of the picturesque streets of Veronetta (Verona’s historic quarter on the left bank of the Adige), continues inside this restaurant: a succession of intimate dining rooms brimming with eclectic décor. The ambiance delivers exactly what one hopes for in a romantic dinner setting, while the kitchen moves deftly between local specialties and ingredients and more creative preparations, offering both meat and fish dishes of excellent caliber.

Name: Osteria la Lanterna
Address: Via Finali 1, frazione Cressogno, Valsolda, 22010, Italy
Description: Situated on the road leading to Lugano in Switzerland, this charming restaurant with elegant furnishings and a rustic decor boasts bright dining rooms and a pleasant terrace for summer dining. The dishes are prepared with a focus on locally sourced, seasonal ingredients and are inspired by traditional recipes reinterpreted in contemporary style.

Name: Osteria le Logge
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Having retained its old shop counter and glass - fronted display cabinets, this former grocer’s shop is perfect for anyone in search of old - world charm. However, the cuisine is the real draw with its focus on quality of the highest level. Wine buffs can ask to visit the wine cellar nearby, housed in a tunnel of Etruscan origin. Simpler dining room on the first floor.

Name: Ottavi Mare
Description: In the picturesque medieval old town of Bevagna, just a few metres from the charming main square, you’ll find one of the most promising young chefs in the area. In a region with no coastline, Vittorio Ottavi offers three tasting menus dedicated to saltwater fish, available as full or smaller versions, but all of an exceptionally high standard.

Name: PEPE Barra Italiana
Description: In the heart of the Montenapoleone fashion district, on the fourth floor of a historic palazzo, a venue of decidedly contemporary spirit and international reach takes shape. The layout revolves around three large “barre”: solid walnut counters facing onto the kitchen, designed to transform the meal into a direct and continuous dialogue between those who cook and those who dine. On the menu, the talent at the helm of the kitchen interprets Italy in a modern and indulgent key, ranging from seafood, with elegantly prepared raw fish, to well-judged meat dishes, accompanied by a well-stocked cheese display in full view. A lively, elegantly informal and pleasingly convivial space, ideal for a relaxed evening of casual dining.

Name: PS Ristorante
Address: Via di Petriolo 7, Cerreto Guidi, 50050, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the splendid countryside of Cerreto Guidi, Villa Petriolo is a magnificent Medici residence offering luxurious rooms in a setting of great allure. Besides the beauty of the villa and its garden, onto which the restaurant’s outdoor terrace looks, the property benefits from an abundance of its own production: extra-virgin olive oil, wine, Cinta Senese pig farming, meats, poultry, a kitchen garden and ancient grain varieties. The kitchen reinterprets this exceptionally rich range of produce in a modern key, offering two tasting menus – one of them vegetarian – from which it is also possible to order à la carte. Alternatively, the Osteria di Golpaja offers genuine and intense flavours of the kind that have made Tuscany a celebrated destination for lovers of fine dining.

Name: Palazzo Branciforte
Description: Inside a late 16th-century patrician residence, which now also houses a fascinating archaeological museum, is a restaurant that is pure magic. Its elegant and secluded inner courtyard becomes the main dining room: a space that changes with the seasons thanks to its retractable roof, offering the chance to dine “en plein air” under the starry sky on the most beautiful evenings. A place where history and taste come together, creating an experience that goes beyond a simple meal.

Name: Palazzo Petrucci
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The entrance from the street still does not completely reveal the experience that awaits guests. Today, the restaurant is situated on the first floor, in a completely redesigned space where design and functionality blend in harmony. The modern, minimalist interiors showcase a brand-new, open-plan kitchen, flanked by a newly built wine cellar that enhances the dining experience. With just 36 covers, the restaurant retains an intimate atmosphere; two lucky diners can enjoy an even more immersive experience by taking a seat at the counter and letting the chef guide them through the meal. Lino Scarallo’s culinary offering continues to centre on tasting menus: from free-form menus, in which the chef gives free rein to his creativity, to itineraries dedicated to his signature dishes, featuring ingredients from the sea and the land, in a contemporary exploration of flavour, technique and innovation.

Name: Palazzo Petrucci Pizzeria
Address: Piazza San Domenico Maggiore 5-7, Naples, 80134, Italy
Description: Situated right in the city centre, this pizzeria with the same name and owners as the gourmet restaurant has a contemporary, minimalist feel, plus an attractive outdoor space on the piazza. Among the excellent pizzas made from top-quality ingredients, you’ll find a few created by the young, skilful pizza chef, as well as one by chef Scarallo. Don’t miss the desserts!

Name: Palazzo Utini
Description: A historical palazzo in the town center has been given new life after its purchase by a local entrepreneurial family, who also bestowed their name upon it. Just steps from the heart of Italy’s famed food valley, it now serves as a refined hospitality venue: the ground floor hosts a bar and bistro, while upstairs are elegant spaces devoted to gourmet cuisine. Tasting menus are available, with dishes also offered à la carte, alongside an extensive and well-curated wine list. The upper floors feature intimate, stylish guest rooms, designed in the same reassuring style that runs throughout the building.

Name: Pantagruele
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the harbour area and right in the heart of the city, this charming trattoria wins you over with its authentic atmosphere and informal service, which makes you feel right at home straight away. The interiors are simple and welcoming, while in the warmer months the outdoor tables allow you to experience all the vibrant atmosphere of the town centre. In the kitchen, a straightforward menu free from unnecessary frills pays homage to Apulian tradition, showcasing both produce from the land and, above all, seafood. Don’t miss the seafood pasta dishes, which are full of flavour and particularly popular with our customers.

Name: Paolo Teverini
Address: Via del Popolo 2, Bagno di Romagna, 47021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the charming village of Bagno di Romagna and surrounded by beautiful rolling hills, Teverini is a culinary name full of history in this area. The cuisine here demonstrates different traditions – the local region is an obvious influence (especially its mushrooms), but fish and seafood also feature along with plenty of vegetables.

Name: Papaveri e Papere
Description: Situated in the verdant setting of San Miniato, this attractive and friendly restaurant is home to chef Paolo Fraschi, who creates imaginative cuisine that is full of character with regional and Mediterranean influences (the home-made spaghettini with clams, courgettes and parmesan is particularly delicious). In season, dine alfresco in the beautiful garden.

Name: Parco Gambrinus
Address: Via Capitello 18, San Polo di Piave, 31020, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A rustic and romantic setting provides the backdrop for the traditional and creative cuisine served here. It is made from typical local produce with an emphasis on ethical and sustainably produced ingredients (vegan and gluten - free options are also available). Exotic animals inhabit the park, where a stream is home to the house specialities of crayfish, eels and sturgeon. The restaurant also offers a few comfortable guestrooms nearby.

Name: Parizzi
Description: Along a street in the city centre, a colourful and welcoming dining room provides the setting for a culinary offering that oscillates between local tradition and contemporary touches. The menu moves between local dishes and a selection divided between meat and seafood, providing a balanced and versatile choice. The dishes impress above all for the quality of the raw materials and for the precision of their cooking: exemplary in this respect is the charcoal-grilled sea bass, accompanied by roasted potatoes and cherry tomatoes, which expresses simplicity and flavour at their very best.

Name: Parma Rotta
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Here, where the Parma river once broke its banks, you’ll find an attractive trattoria with pleasant dining rooms and excellent cuisine cooked over a wood and herb fire, one of the oldest culinary techniques in the world. The main courses feature meat only, with an extensive number of dishes on the menu. Among the home-made desserts, we recommend the fior di latte ice-cream, which is served with a choice of delicious sauces.

Name: Partage
Description: In the kitchen, a young chef nurtured on home cooking and refined through significant professional experience in France now presides over an intimate and welcoming establishment in the heart of the town. At lunch, the offer is more immediate, with a streamlined formula and a decidedly appealing price-quality ratio; in the evening, meanwhile, the spotlight shifts to a broader, more personal à la carte menu, where creativity and technique find expression in dishes of land and sea. All of this is enhanced by a carefully curated selection of natural wines, well-structured and coherent. Passion, expertise and the youthful spirit of the management complete a gastronomic picture of undoubted interest.

Name: Pascalucci
Address: Via Appia 1, San Nicola Manfredi, 82010, Italy
Description: A traditional restaurant serving regional cuisine, as well as skilfully prepared fish dishes made from fresh produce. Specialities include Beneventano beef fillet and octopus in aspic jelly.

Name: Pasqualina
Address: Via Santi Filippo e Giacomo 12/14, Frascati, 00044, Italy
Description: In the historic centre of Frascati, this restaurant offers straightforward, traditional cooking, executed with considerable skill and often faithful to the region’s classics. From the excellent coratella (lamb offal) and other preparations celebrating nose-to-tail cooking through to the canonical Roman pastas (carbonara, gricia, amatriciana, cacio e pepe), it is a celebration of the rather robust and pleasingly rustic flavours of local cuisine.

Name: Patauner
Description: Despite its simple appearance, this restaurant on the side of the road dates from the 17C and has been run by the same family for the past century. Today, the third and fourth generations work side by side in the kitchen, preparing dishes with a strong regional flavour. Highlights include the white Terlano asparagus in season and offal dishes throughout the year.

Name: Patrizia
Description: Creative dynamism in the very heart of the city: this is Patrizia, a restaurant named after the chef’s mother. Here the journey is singular — available in either a complete or abbreviated form — and evolves with the turning of the seasons; alongside it, the lighting, music and dining room details transform as well, following precisely the vision of young chef Tommaso Zoboli. A continuous movement of ideas and exploration, designed to satisfy himself whilst delighting his guests.The progression of dishes reveals an exuberant kitchen, rich with references to diverse thoughts and cultures, unfettered by preconceptions in its pairings and consistently thoughtful in its presentation. The storytelling at the counter, led by the chef-patron and his young team, completes a dynamic and immersive experience.

Name: Peculiare Restaurant
Description: Just steps from the Arco dell’Annunziata, in a quiet side street off Via Roma, Peculiare is the reflection of a young chef’s talent. The menu blends creativity and tradition, with dishes such as sole Wellington, tagliolini with sea urchins, and a refined Rossini-style filet with velvety purée and foie gras. The sober, elegant setting unfolds in an 18th-century palace, where an ancient arch tells the story of the place. The warm welcome and genuine smiles round out the experience.

Name: Pellico 3
Description: This little gastronomic gem, housed within the Park Hyatt, boasts one of the most exclusive locations in Milan: it can be accessed directly from the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II or via the elegant cocktail bar with its entrance on the street. The interiors, adorned with contemporary artworks, provide the backdrop for a culinary experience that takes the form of two tasting menus: ‘My City’, a personal tribute to Milan, and a more free-flowing journey, guided by the seasons and the inspiration of the moment. The result is a contemporary cuisine that is precise and rich in flavour, successfully combining creativity and balance, as seen in the roast lobster on bone marrow with saffron sauce, served with a courgette flower stuffed with seasonal vegetables and basil. Further enhancing the experience is an exceptionally comprehensive wine list, featuring around 700 labels and a particular focus on wines available by the glass.

Name: Pentole e Provette
Description: This restaurant run by Luca Trabalzini and his partner Rossella is a real gem in the small town of Fasano. Their story, which began in Australia, adds a fascinating touch to this gastronomic project. The atmosphere here is warm and lively, making this the perfect setting in which to enjoy the chef’s innovative cuisine, which he showcases on three distinct menus dedicated to meat, fish and vegetarian dishes respectively. Luca’s cuisine is modern and elegant, with particular attention paid to flavours and textures so that each and every dish offers a fully rounded sensorial experience.

Name: Pepe Nero
Description: Overlooking the western shore of Lake Bolsena, Pepe Nero is an intimate restaurant that wins one over through its modern furnishings and a pleasing maritime character. The service, gentle and professional, discreetly accompanies a predominantly seafood gastronomic journey, conceived for an immersive and unhurried experience of flavour. Guests may opt for themed menus or entrust themselves to the carte, choosing at least two dishes. The wine list ranges across regional and national labels, while in the warmer months a small terrace at the water’s edge affords the pleasure of dining with a direct view over the lake shore.

Name: Pepenero
Address: Piazza del Duomo 4, San Miniato, 56028, Italy
Description: In its new home in Piazza del Duomo, in beautiful San Miniato, in the hands of chef Gilberto Rossi Pepenero continues to serve cuisine that showcases the best ingredients (both meat and fish) from this bountiful region, with delicacies such as excellent truffles featuring on the menu throughout the year. Prepared with a light and modern touch, meals are served in a spacious dining room where the many windows offer glimpses of the town centre.

Name: Perbacco
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A rustic restaurant offering an authentic taste of the Cilento area, both in its setting amid lush Mediterranean vegetation and in its regional cuisine. Fish and seafood dominate the antipasti selection, while the main courses focus more on meat and vegetable dishes. Good choice of regional wines, plus the option of a few pleasant guestrooms.

Name: Percorsi al Vecchio Ponte
Address: Via del Ponte Medioevale 1, Bracciano, 00062, Italy
Description: An evocative and romantic setting within the former carriage house of the castle, which can be visited just steps away, as can the picturesque village of Bracciano, well worth exploring. The cuisine in this restaurant is of an excellent standard and is not necessarily tied to the local area (save for certain ingredients), but is in general more creative and inventive, ideal for those wishing to venture beyond the classic dishes of Lazio. Full marks to young chef Luca Cecconi!

Name: Pernambucco
Description: This restaurant boasts a garden setting with a pleasant outdoor dining space, plus a long, narrow interior decorated in decidedly classic style. Fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu, with a focus on local fish, including excellent tartare (usually either seabream or tuna, depending on the catch of the day) and shellfish (cooked in salt, baked or grilled). The vegetables are sourced from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden.

Name: Persika
Description: Persika is a name that combines Italy and Sweden: in both languages, it means "peach." In the Chia district, an Italian restaurateur collaborates with a highly experienced Swedish chef to create a gastro-bistro with a relaxed and welcoming atmosphere. The surprise menu is often chosen, but there's also an interesting and accessible à la carte option. The cuisine is contemporary, with international influences and a strong focus on local ingredients.

Name: Pescarino-Sapori di Terra e di Mare
Description: Warm and inviting atmosphere with wooden walls and ceiling. The kitchen, recently renovated alongside the terrace, remains unchanged in offering: relatively simple in some concoctions, more creative in others, aiming primarily to highlight the product quality, predominantly seafood, with Ligurian nuances but extending to other regions. Considering the isolated location, seizing the opportunity to rest in the rooms may be worthwhile.

Name: Pesceria San Martino
Description: Born as a fishmonger’s and transformed over time into a small seafood delicatessen, this venue welcomes guests into a simple yet thoughtfully appointed setting, with an intimate front room and a colourful conservatory at the rear that opens to the outdoors in summer. Here Ivan manages front of house with courtesy and expertise, while in the kitchen Bartolo selects the freshest produce with great care. Among the more distinctive offerings, the original and well-executed “seafood charcuterie” stands out, alongside fried squid that is also available for takeaway. Not to be missed is the pan-cooked baby octopus, tender and flavourful, served with a datterini tomato sauce and a crispy bruschetta that practically begs you to mop up every last drop. Strong demand makes booking essential, particularly at weekends.

Name: Pescheria
Description: In the Santa Teresa neighbourhood, just a short walk from the commercial harbour and the heart of the historic centre, Pescheria is launching its new venture within the Crescent, the imposing architectural complex that overlooks Piazza della Libertà. The address has changed, but not the restaurant’s philosophy, ever based on seafood cuisine that showcases seasonal catches and locally sourced ingredients. The menu ranges from refined raw seafood dishes, featuring oysters and the day’s selection, to dishes with a more robust, Mediterranean flavour, such as the much-loved Pasta dei Pescatori, designed to appeal to more traditional palates.

Name: Phi Restaurant
Address: Località Forte Cappellini, Baia Sardinia, 07021, Italy
Description: Glamour and fashion are the hallmarks of this restaurant in Phi Beach, one of the most attractive nightclub-cum-lounge bars on the Costa Smeralda. Take a seat on the terrace right by the water and soak up the romantic sunsets and sea views as you enjoy Italian and Mediterranean dishes created by a famous chef from Lombardy who adds just the right touch of contemporary flavour. Also open for lunch, with some of the evening menu dishes available alongside an array of simpler options.

Name: Piacentino
Description: A short distance from the historic centre of the enchanting village of Bobbio, this restaurant presents a cuisine that speaks with coherence and respect of the traditions of the territory, drawing out authentic flavours and a faithful adherence to the seasonality of its produce. The menu is a homage to the local cuisine, and among its specialities stands out one of the emblematic dishes of the town: maccheroni alla bobbiese, prepared according to tradition and with consummate skill, a true expression of the gastronomic identity of the place.

Name: Piazza dei Mestieri
Description: Situated on a redeveloped industrial site and part of a training school, this restaurant offers a more concise menu at lunchtime with lower prices than the evening, but with the same high-quality cuisine. Our inspector recommends the spaghetti with spring onion and bottarga, accompanied by one of the craft beers produced on site. There’s also an attractive terrace for alfresco dining in fine weather.

Name: Piccolo Lord
Address: Corso San Maurizio 69 bis/g, Turin, 10124, Italy
Description: Professional service in a welcoming, modern restaurant run by a young couple. He works in the kitchen while she (having also worked as a chef in the past) runs the front of house. Delicious Mediterranean cuisine with a seasonal focus.

Name: Pierre - Trattoria Sartoriale
Description: On the edge of the historic center, this is a simple restaurant with just a few tables, set in modern spaces accented with 1920s-inspired touches. True to its name, the focus here is a “tailored” approach to cuisine. The menu reflects the best the market has to offer, interpreted with creativity, especially in the three tasting menus, while never going overboard and always prioritizing flavor. The restaurant is run by two passionate young professionals (the chef has gained excellent national and international experience). At lunchtime, a business menu is also available.

Name: Pierre Alexis 1877
Description: Situated in the historic heart of Courmayeur, this old house dating back over a century, once used as a stables and later as a carpenter’s workshop, is now home to a warm and welcoming restaurant. Here, traditional recipes are updated with creativity and enthusiasm, as demonstrated by the venison Rossini. The ingredients used are mainly local, including wild herbs for added flavour, while the wine list offers an impressive selection of labels.

Name: Pinocchio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This reliable restaurant is well run by a highly professional and experienced family. In the classic-style dining room, where the decor eschews fashionable trends, enjoy typical Piedmontese cuisine lightened by the occasional modern twist. The restaurant’s contemporary version of “paniscia” is a good example – a type of risotto with beans, salami and vegetables, in which the latter, instead of being cooked directly with the rice, are added on top of the mixture in the form of vegetable cream, giving the dish an attractive splash of colour. The menu always features a few fish-based recipes, including both salt- and freshwater species.

Name: Pirò
Description: Just steps from Piazza Navona, which grows quieter and even more captivating come evening. this venue is devoted to classic seafood cookery, with a generous selection of crudo and an array of cooked preparations that let each day’s catch shine. The setting is modern and intimate, service attentive without being intrusive, and the management draws on lengthy experience in the Roman dining scene. A fine recommendation for those seeking understated elegance and a kitchen that brings the authentic scent of the sea to the table.

Name: Podere 39
Description: Just beyond Porta Romana, one finds an intimate dining room with few covers – advance booking is strongly advised – where the restaurant wins one over immediately through its style: a small space of considerable personality, made all the more appealing by rustic details set off by generous and carefully tended floral arrangements. A portion of the ingredients comes directly from their own farm, Podere 39, a guarantee of freshness and identity.
