The menu alternates between meat and fish, a well-judged balance that draws out the quality of the produce and a cooking of authentic and unaffected character.

Name: Podere Belvedere Tuscany
Address: Via San Piero a Strada 23, Pontassieve, 50065, Italy
Description: A charming farmhouse with a rustic feel, decorated with meticulous attention to detail, welcomes guests with terracotta floors, exposed brick walls and shelves full of bottles that reflect the establishment’s passion. This is the ideal setting for a restaurant that offers a varied menu: from selected charcuterie to traditional meat dishes, not to mention some interesting seafood options. The wine list is equally impressive, featuring a selection of refined yet reasonably priced labels, carefully chosen to complement every dish perfectly.

Name: Podere Giglio
Address: Via Ponzano per San Donato 35, Empoli, 50053, Italy
Description: A classic nineteenth-century farmhouse nestled in the tranquil countryside at the gates of Empoli, this establishment preserves its original rural charm, enhanced by a restrained and meticulous restoration that brings out the simple yet welcoming interiors. The kitchen is entrusted to Marco Bagordo, a young chef of solid experience and interpreter of a contemporary Tuscany that marries precise technique, balanced flavours and measured presentations, always mindful not to sacrifice substance to aesthetics. The excellence of the dishes springs from the selection of local and seasonal ingredients, worked in such a way as to preserve their aromas and qualities. Among the most compelling offerings stands I 5 voli del piccione (The 5 Flights of the Pigeon), a refined variation that explores every part of the bird. The wine list, essential yet well-focused on the territory, is completed by labels produced on the estate, including a house red and the unmissable extra virgin olive oil.

Name: Poldo e Gianna Osteria
Description: A welcoming contemporary osteria just steps from Parliament – occasionally drawing a political face or two – whose name pays tribute to the current owners’ grandparents, true pioneers of the trade. The menu remains firmly anchored in Roman tradition, interpreted with seasonal ingredients of real interest, while allowing room for more inventive detours: notably the Marsala Florio tasting journey, a thoughtfully constructed pairing of each course with different expressions of the celebrated Sicilian wine. Reservations are wise, not only to secure a table on the pleasant terrace, but to guarantee a spot at a venue that marries family heritage and contemporary spirit with rare ease.

Name: Pomiroeu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant, one of the finest in the region, is run by its owner Giancarlo Morelli and celebrated its 30th anniversary in 2023. Situated in the centre of Seregno, the restaurant is intimate and welcoming with walls adorned with beautiful works of contemporary art thanks to the restaurant’s partnership with a local art gallery. The cuisine here is modern yet unfussy and the chef is equally at ease with meat, fish and vegetable dishes. One of the few restaurants around Monza to still offer a cheese course!

Name: Ponente
Address: Via Fontespino 11, Urbino PU, Urbino, 61029, Italy
Description: This restaurant is just a few kilometres from Urbino and is set within a typical stone farmhouse converted into a small hotel, the Aura Relais. Even before the food, it is the landscape that strikes: from the outdoor tables the view sweeps over enchanting hills in a panorama of breathtaking beauty. The dishes follow, drawing on local traditions yet reaching beyond them, often to great effect, for a delightful evening.

Name: Ponte Pietra
Description: Just steps from the bridge of the same name, this extraordinarily romantic restaurant brims with decorations and nostalgic charm. One dines here utterly enchanted. But that’s not all: tables are also arranged on two balconies – one enclosed for year-round use – overlooking the Adige River. The cuisine is rooted in the territory, with select seafood offerings as well.

Name: Porta di Basso
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Although the entrance is in one of the alleys of the historic center, the dining room opens entirely towards the sea, as it is perched on a cliff overlooking the water. Naturally, the most sought-after tables are on the terraces or near the windows, offering a stunning view. In Domenico Cilenti's kitchen, there's no à la carte option – only two tasting menus (one of which is vegetarian), showcasing many Gargano products from both sea and land.

Name: Portanova
Description: Here one finds one of the most innovative, accomplished and creative kitchens in Urbino, housed in a refined restaurant that unites ancient brick walls with more modern furnishings. Imaginative as they are, the dishes spring from a deep love of the territory and its excellent products. The service, too, is excellent: Portanova is a gastronomic stop not to be missed in the “ideal city”.

Name: Posillipo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Boasting a superb location above Gabicce Monte, this excellent restaurant run by the third generation of the same family offers breathtaking views of the Romagna coast. Posillipo’s superb fish dishes have made the restaurant a must in the region, with options ranging from raw fish to traditional pasta specialities and delicious main courses (fish fillets, catch of the day, fried options etc). There’s also a tempting dessert trolley and an excellent wine list.

Name: Posta
Address: Viale Vittorio Veneto 169, Sant'Omobono Terme, 24038, Italy
Description: Situated in the Imagna valley, this welcoming, family-run restaurant serves delicious regional specialities alongside traditional Italian favourites, including a few fish options. Highlights include the dried-cod cannelloni, soft braised “guancialino” and the unmissable zabaglione mousse with sbrisolona-cake crumbs and marzipan ice-cream.

Name: Posta
Description: A corner of Tuscany in Bologna, where famous soups such as ribollita and pappa col pomodoro are followed by pappardelle pasta with wild boar, tripe, beef pepper stew and, of course, Fiorentina steak, although there’s also room on the menu for local specialities such as tagliatelle and tortellini. Many of the wines served also come from Tuscany.

Name: Prato Gaio
Address: Località Versa, bivio per Volpara, Montecalvo Versiggia, 27047, Italy
Description: The restaurant trade is in the family genes: already an inn in the 19C, the Prato Gaio takes inspiration from the cuisine of the Oltrepò region. A selection of traditional specialities alongside dishes reinterpreted with flair and imagination are served. An essential stop for anyone looking for local flavour.

Name: Principe di Belludia
Description: The Principe di Belludia is the gourmet restaurant at the Il San Corrado di Noto hotel, a luxurious resort in a secluded rural location with two enormous swimming pools. The new executive chef Martin Lazarov showcases his love for Sicily, with a particular attention to vegetables dishes.

Name: Profumi di Cous Cous
Address: Via Regina Margherita 80, San Vito lo Capo, 91030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: As the name of this restaurant suggests, couscous takes pride of place on the menu, although other Sicilian specialities can also be sampled here. Delightful atmosphere, especially in summer when meals are served in the internal courtyard among the citrus trees.

Name: Punta Lena
Address: Via Monsignor Di Mattina 8, località Ficogrande, Stromboli, 98055, Italy
Description: At this restaurant, dine under a pergola with superb views of the sea and Strombolicchio – the perfect setting for any occasion. The menu focuses on fish, including raw and dry-aged fish options. The first courses have a local flavour and are particularly delicious.

Name: Q.B. bistró
Description: Q.B. Bistró is a small, welcoming venue in the heart of Cuneo’s historic centre, overlooking a quiet, secluded street. The kitchen looks to the contemporary with dishes that are essential yet thoughtful, built upon seasonal ingredients and carefully selected raw materials. The considered and well-structured wine list opens its gaze willingly to natural and organic bottles, with labels that tell stories of terroirs and independent producers. A youthful and pleasing establishment, ideal for those seeking simplicity, attention to detail and an authentic measure of passion.

Name: QUID
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The name Quid springs from a refined play on words: it combines the initial of chef Quintero with the acronym Unique Italian Dining, underlining from the outset the distinctive identity of the project. And this reference finds its fullest expression in the chef’s own personal signature, which is worth pointing out. Further enhancing the experience is the extraordinary view over St Peter’s, enjoyed from both the dining room and the terrace, a genuine highlight on fine days. Not to be overlooked is the bar, which as evening falls transforms into a lively and evocative space, perfectly expressing the exclusive character of the venue.

Name: Quadri Bistrot
Description: A modern bistrot with cocktail bar, fashionable furnishings, soft lighting and lounge music in the background, also featuring a small sidewalk terrace that requires advance booking. The cuisine, imaginative and creative, is guided by a talented chef who ensures personality and excellent seasonal products. Try the Mediterranean-style red mullet, while the tiramisu features a refined pairing with Sauternes. We also note a menu dedicated to caviar.

Name: Qualia
Description: Situated in a side street in the centre of this charming small town, this restaurant boasts a dining room with exposed brickwork and glimpses of the kitchen, plus a small outdoor space with a few tables for alfresco dining. The dishes here are full of flavour and focus on regional ingredients and fresh fish.

Name: Quartopiano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Elegant and refined, the modern atmosphere of this dining room plays host to a cuisine of both land and sea at an excellent level. The dishes draw their inspiration from the most celebrated gastronomic traditions, with occasional forays into more creative territory. The desserts are not to be missed! A quite different formula prevails at lunch, when a buffet is laid out (Sunday excepted).

Name: Quattro Sensi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Perched on a hill just a few kilometres from Torgiano, Quattro Sensi boasts a veranda with views of Perugia, which is perfect for a quick lunch, and an elegant dining room in which you can enjoy regional dishes such as pappardelle egg pasta with a Cinturello Orvietano pork ragù with orange and fennel.

Name: Quel Fantastico Giovedì
Description: After forty years of experience, their consistency and care make this one of Ferrara’s most sought-after tables (best to book well in advance!). Guests enter intimate dining rooms of welcoming warmth, where service is gracious and precise. The menu is fragrant with the sea: fish dishes prepared with classic elegance and modern touches, such as the green bean and vegetable velouté crowned with raw scampi, fresh and glistening. Meat offerings are equally rewarding, rich and flavorful, with the celebrated potato sformato and gratinéed salama da sugo releasing intense aromas from the oven.

Name: Quintilio
Description: For over a century, and from generation to generation, Quintilio has acted as a junction between two beautiful regions, Liguria and Piedmont – and not just in a geographical sense. These regions take pride of place on the wine list (overseen by the friendly and talented owner Lorena) as well as on the menu, which is created daily with dishes made from top-quality local ingredients full of flavour. Regional specialities such as plin, Ligurian-style rabbit tortelli, risottos, vitello tonnato (veal) and brain are all skilfully reinterpreted with a modern twist by owner-chef Luca Bazzano.

Name: Quintogusto
Address: Piazza Sandro Pertini 54 r, Savona, 17100, Italy
Description: Recently opened in the renovated section of Corso Italia in central Savona, Quintogusto is a small, contemporary and minimalist-style restaurant occupying one side of the former hospital. Here, the owner-chef (once sous-chef at the excellent Michelin-starred Il Vescovado in Noli) cements his reputation with Ligurian-influenced cuisine to which he adds his own modern and imaginative touches.

Name: Rada Rooftop
Description: In one of the most picturesque corners of Positano’s Spiaggia Grande, Rada brings together four different experiences in a single location: Beach Bistrot, Fly Lounge Bar, Rooftop Restaurant and the famous Music on the Rocks nightclub. The Rooftop Restaurant, overlooking a stunning panoramic terrace, serves Mediterranean cuisine centred on the catch of the day, complemented by a selection of meat dishes. The experience is rounded off by a carefully curated wine list, featuring a wide selection of Champagne, ideal for accompanying a dinner with a sea view.

Name: Radici
Address: Località Borgo La Chiaracia, Castel Giorgio, 05013, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Amid sinuous green valleys, within the luxurious Hotel Borgo La Chiaracia, in an elegant dining room or on the lovely outdoor terrace, the choice extends to three tasting menus, one of them entirely plant-based, though dishes may also be selected freely from either list. We were greatly impressed by the abilities of young chef Gabriel Collazzo: creativity combined with the local area, a chef of considerable talent!

Name: Radici Osteria Contemporanea
Description: In the heart of the pedestrian zone, yet with convenient parking close by, the restaurant also offers lighter, more affordable options at lunch. The menu takes a modern approach, with particular emphasis on meat dishes, though complemented by sound fish alternatives and vegetarian options. The recipes reveal a good degree of personalisation, without losing sight of the balance of flavours. All is served in a welcoming setting with deliberately evening tones, lit by large windows overlooking the street, creating a warm and pleasant atmosphere.

Name: Radici ristorante in vigna
Description: In a verdant setting that gives way to the property’s own vineyards, the upper part of the building houses the Relais Le Marne, while below, under a late-nineteenth-century brick vault, the restaurant’s dining room features a pleasing combination of clean-lined design furniture. The cuisine devotes itself to the flavours of the local area, refined with a very light modern touch, alongside a vegetarian tasting menu. A sound wine selection, featuring the in-house Mura Mura labels. The bistrot service is available exclusively on Mondays and Tuesdays, at both lunch and dinner.

Name: Radici – L’Osteria di Accursio
Description: Accursio Craparo has returned to his “Roots”: in two simple and elegant dining rooms, or in the spacious and enchanting outdoor summer space overlooking the historic center – weather permitting – the offering is based on traditional Sicilian cuisine, presented in consistently generous dishes, sometimes enriched with a touch of personal interpretation.

Name: Radicì
Description: The name of this restaurant alludes both to the chef’s origins in Isea (“radici” translates as “roots”) and his passion for vegetables, which make a strong appearance in his dishes. He offers three tasting menus, one dedicated to fish from the lake, a second which is more creative, and a third focusing on seasonal vegetables, with the option of choosing individual courses from each menu à la carte style. Whatever you choose, be prepared for complex, elaborate and surprising cuisine!

Name: Radimare
Address: Via Beato Piergiorgio Frassati 5/a, Monopoli, 70043, Italy
Description: There’s no tasting menu at this restaurant but instead a tempting à la carte featuring modern Mediterranean cuisine based on top-quality seasonal ingredients, with fish and seafood taking centre stage. Citrus fruit and a few spices, especially ginger, are used carefully and sparingly, as are aromatic herbs which add a touch of fresh flavour to the dishes. The contemporary decor, enhanced by plants and a profusion of wood, plus friendly service add to the appeal.

Name: Radino Wine Bistrot
Description: This restaurant occupies a captivating space at the confluence of a sixteenth-century church and an ancient wine press, whose original character has been meticulously preserved. The dining areas are arranged across two rooms: one on the first floor, where an open kitchen animates the space, and a second on a raised level; at the lower level there is also an intimate room dedicated to cigar enthusiasts. The cuisine offers straightforward, reassuring Italian fare, distinguished by its immediacy and appeal. Among the dishes, the hand-rolled cavatelli with ragù of humble Lucanian sausage and king oyster mushrooms stands out as particularly noteworthy.

Name: Ratanà
Address: Via G. de Castillia 28, Milan, 20124, Italy
Description: Rhythm and dynamism define this restaurant, housed in a renovated building that was once a cinema and later a tram depot, located across from the celebrated Bosco Verticale complex. Some seats are available directly at the counter, while the outdoor terrace overlooking the public park is another highlight. The cuisine stands out for its liveliness and creativity: premium ingredients take center stage, elevated in preparations where Italian flavor is expressed in a contemporary style, with several Milanese nods, such as the old Milan‑style risotto with gremolata and roast jus, or the cartoccio of mondeghili (traditional Milanese meatballs). At midday, a quick lunch is available, playfully called “schiscèta” (the Milanese dialect word for a packed lunch).

Name: Razzo
Description: In the heart of the city, a cozy bistrot bathed in soft light and contemporary design welcomes guests in a youthful, laid-back atmosphere. The kitchen delivers dishes with a bold identity, original interpretations of meat and fish, generously portioned and marked by well-calibrated creativity. Flavors are never predictable, elevated by the purposeful use of distinctive ingredients in each course. The intimate outdoor terrace, gently lit in pleasant half-light, sets the scene for a romantic evening.

Name: Rear Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: In a modern and elegant dining room with an entire wall given over to the open kitchen, the offering is highly varied: alongside more elaborate dishes there is also a street food menu, including fried specialities, sandwiches, Spanish ham and tacos, as well as raw seafood and dishes ranging from classic to creative, while several main courses, of both meat and fish, are destined for the grill. The wine selection is excellent, particularly where Champagne is concerned. Please note: throughout the summer season, the usual gastronomic experience offered within the restaurant gives way to a lighter and more informal format, designed to be enjoyed outdoors and in keeping with the season. The proposal will be centred on a dedicated selection of dishes, conceived for a convivial and relaxed experience, while maintaining the same attention to the quality of the ingredients and to the dynamic identity of the kitchen.

Name: Regallo
Description: An excellent restaurant situated less than five minutes from the town centre, Regallo has a contemporary decor with features that recall its former function as a factory. At the helm in the kitchen, skilful chef Claudio Ravinetto prepares dishes with an exclusive focus on fish, including interesting options such as cuttlefish tagliatelle with cream and diced winter roots such as celeriac, served at the table with an excellent hot vegetable broth.

Name: Regina Lucia
Description: Overlooking a square of monumental beauty where tables are laid out for alfresco dining in summer, Regina Lucia is well worth a visit even when it’s not fine enough to sit outside. In a dining room with plenty of historic character, enjoy classic Sicilian cuisine reinterpreted with a creative twist – and make sure you don’t miss the delicious desserts!

Name: Regio Patio
Address: Via San Francesco d'Assisi 23, Garda, 37016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the lakefront, this elegant gourmet restaurant in the Regina Adelaide hotel boasts an attractive English-style garden, as well as a beautiful outdoor patio and stylish dining room. The two tasting menus served here (one of which is vegetarian) showcase the traditions of Lake Garda and its surrounding region with a creative twist using vegetables from the property’s own kitchen garden and a focus on seasonal ingredients. There’s also an extensive wine list.

Name: Remulass
Description: They call it ‘Cucina con le radici’ (Cuisine with roots) and you only need to cross the threshold to understand why: a small, lively restaurant with warm colours, which gets very busy, especially in the evening, when booking is essential. The menu is simple, featuring just a few carefully planned dishes, mostly vegetarian, where seasonal freshness is paramount. Every recipe releases authentic aromas and genuine flavours, while leaving room for creativity: such as the variations on pumpkin, with oven-baked Mantovana and Hokkaido julienne in a sweet and sour sauce, caressed by tamarind cream and little cubes of blue goat's cheese. A combination of textures and aromas that tells the story of the land with elegance and creativity.

Name: Rendenèr Alpine Food
Description: Situated within the Lory hotel, this restaurant has a contemporary decor and wooden tables that give it an informal ambience. Here, the young talented chef creates Alpine cuisine from carefully chosen seasonal ingredients, with menus changing throughout the year. In spring, for example, ingredients include Alpine sow-thistle, Mugo pine shoots, woodruff and lichen, while in summer herbs and flowers from the restaurant’s own organic kitchen garden add extra flavour to dishes. An interesting wine list with a focus on regional labels completes the picture.

Name: Repubblica di Perno
Address: Vicolo Cavour 5, loc. Perno, Monforte d'Alba, 12065, Italy
Description: In the very heart of gastronomic Langa, where a reservation is an absolute necessity, lies a small and carefully restored restaurant brought to life by the passion of the couple who run it: she in the dining room, he at the stove. In the finest Piedmontese tradition, the entrance opens directly onto the open kitchen, a prelude to the intimate first floor, which accommodates just five tables. The offering takes the form of a daily menu that is rigorously regional, enriched by dishes that celebrate seasonality and local tradition. Among the most pleasing preparations, the cardoon tart with quail’s egg and fonduta stands out: harmonious and well-executed. The surroundings, neat and intimate, recall the atmosphere of a rustic family bistrot, where every detail contributes to a sense of warmth and authenticity. Completing the offering, three guest rooms are available, perfectly suited to those wishing to extend their stay and explore the Langa at an unhurried pace, between fine cooking, a domestic welcome and the spirit of the territory.

Name: Residenza del Lago
Description: The name pays tribute to Lake Candia, and we are in a mid-18th century farmhouse which is located within the town. You will find a pleasantly regional, family atmosphere and the restaurant’s traditional cuisine includes popular dishes such as onion cooked three different ways with a faux “bagna caoda” sauce and smoked ricotta.

Name: Resilienza
Description: Steps from the sea, just beyond the train tracks, a spot with an all-white decor welcomes guests in style, with outdoor spaces perfect for the warmer months. In the kitchen, his son reinterprets regional traditions, balancing seafood and land-based dishes, while his mother runs the dining room with warmth and professionalism. An authentic experience combining flavor, simplicity and a relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Restaurant 700
Address: Largo Michele Ayroldi Carissimo 14, Ostuni, 72017, Italy
Description: Situated at the entrance to the historic centre, within the prestigious Paragon 700 Boutique Hotel, housed in the historic Palazzo Rosso, the restaurant captivates guests with the charm of its eclectic interiors, where historical elements blend with contemporary touches and vintage accents. During the warmer months, the real highlight is the exclusive garden. At lunchtime, the restaurant offers a light and informal bistro-style menu, while in the evening the chef takes creativity to the next level with a range of dishes including fish, meat and vegetarian options. The experience is rounded off by Bar 700’s sophisticated mixology service.

Name: Retrobottega
Description: The fruit of a sweeping renovation by the celebrated architect Jean Nouvel, the building houses apartments and art galleries, while on the fifth floor the gastronomic soul comes to life: a single communal table, divided between an elegant interior dining room and a striking panoramic terrace offering uninterrupted views across the Palatine Hill. The cooking looks to the Mediterranean with particular attention to handmade pastas, the true hallmark of the offering. Among the iconic dishes, the tortelli with pork ribs, spring onion and cacao mass stand out with quiet authority. The same terrace is also home to a cocktail bar of enviable situation, ideally placed for raising a glass while contemplating the Roman sunset.

Name: Retrogusto
Description: Although this restaurant is slightly set back from the seafront, the high quality cuisine focusing on the flavours of the Salento makes the short walk well worthwhile. A classic ambience with simple yet tasteful furniture, soft background music and an informal atmosphere.

Name: Riccio Restaurant
Address: Via Molo di Baia 47, Bacoli, 80070, Italy
Description: Overlooking the port, this restaurant serves top-quality fish and seafood with interesting and personalised touches added by its young chef. We recommend starting with the excellent selection of cooked fish (although there’s also a choice of raw fish should you prefer it), following which you can choose from classic seafood dishes such as spaghetti with clams and fried fish, and a selection of original, top-quality dishes such as dry-aged, smoked and preserved fish and seafood.

Name: Rifugio Col Alt
Address: Stazione monte cabinovia col alto, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: During the day this restaurant can be reached in just a few minutes by cable car, providing you with breathtaking views of the Dolomites, while in the evening (when the service is more attentive – things are faster paced at lunchtime) you have to arrange transport via snowcat. The name “refuge” refers only to the location as the cuisine is definitely that of a restaurant: although the menu features hearty mountain fare, it also includes modern options and a few fish-based recipes, including oysters. Last but not least, there’s a good selection of wines.

Name: Rifugio Fuciade
Address: Località Fuciada - Soraga di Fassa, San Pellegrino, 38035, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: To give you an idea of the Alpine location of this restaurant framed by the Costabella mountain chain, suffice it to say that for centuries it was used for mountain pasture. There’s a breathtaking view of the Dolomites which extend into the distance as far as Pale di San Martino, while the menu here focuses on regional recipes such as canderli dumplings on a bed of cabbage, veal stew with polenta and chanterelle mushrooms, and polenta gnocchetti with herb pesto, smoked ricotta and lemon thyme. The wine cellar is home to more than 600 labels, plus accommodation is available in a choice of tranquil guestrooms.

Name: Rio Bistrot
Description: Situated on the street that heads down to the port in charming Riomaggiore, this lovely, well-kept restaurant offers a small selection of dishes split between Ligurian specialities and more creative options. Dine in the rustic, elegant dining room or on the outdoor terrace.

Name: Riso Amaro
Description: Inspired by the famous film Bitter Rice, directed by Giuseppe De Santis, who was born in Fondi, this restaurant welcomes guests into elegant dining rooms and a lush courtyard which is perfect for summer evenings. The cuisine looks to the present with a well-balanced creative flair that is evident in dishes such as the cuttlefish lasagnetta, served with an intense creamy sauce made from cuttlefish ink and offal, or the intriguing sweet “pinzimonio”, a fresh and light dessert that combines sweet-and-sour vegetables with softer notes. The concise but thoughtfully curated wine list features labels from all over Italy, whilst the central location, just a stone’s throw from the castle, adds further charm to the experience.

Name: RistoFante
Description: Run by the reliable and experienced “Titta” in the kitchen and Silvia front of house, this elegant, contemporary-style restaurant serves simple, modern dishes in which fresh, seasonal ingredients take centre stage. The focus here is on fish, with a menu that includes a fine selection of raw seafood options, as well as a simple yet tasty sea bass carpaccio which cooks quickly on a bed of hot porcini mushrooms.

Name: Ristorante 1500
Address: Via Pavicolo 43, funivia per raggiungere il ristorante in via Villa 3, San Vigilio, 39011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: If you’re not a guest at the Vigilius Mountain Resort hotel where this restaurant is situated, leave your car in Lana and take the short cable-car ride to Monte San Vigilio where you’ll find the hotel at an altitude of 1 500m (remember to check the time of the last cable-car back down the mountain!). Decorated with a profusion of wood, the dining room has the same modern feel as the creative mountain cuisine prepared by the new chef who started here in 2023.

Name: Ristorante Da Anita - Chalet Prà delle Nasse
Address: Via Cavallazza 24, Località Prà delle Nasse, San Martino di Castrozza, 38054, Italy
Description: This family-run restaurant is surrounded by views of the Dolomites that are particularly impressive from the outdoor terrace in summer. A historic culinary stalwart among San Martino di Castrozza restaurants, Prà delle Nasse focuses on regional mountain cuisine, although a few more personalised dishes also feature on the menu. The desserts include the grandmother’s traditional tarts alongside more contemporary options.

Name: Ristorante Mas-cì
Description: Now in its third generation of the same family and in business since 1927, the hotel and restaurant are a landmark of hospitality in the heart of the charming historic centre. A refined and welcoming setting, enhanced by elegant dining rooms with fireplaces, where local culinary traditions blend with the flavours of the rest of Italy and its coastlines, while respecting the ingredients. Don’t miss the renowned dishes featuring black truffles, the true highlight of the cuisine.

Name: Ristorante de LEN
Address: Via Cesare Battisti 66, Cortina d'Ampezzo, 32043, Italy
Description: Inside the hotel of the same name, traditional Alpine woodwork is given a modern, minimalist twist: blending the old with the new, the atmosphere is subtle and refined. The dishes also offer a contemporary take on the predominantly mountain-inspired cuisine, while the lunch menu is slightly more streamlined.

Name: Riva
Description: In a small village with a fascinating crenellated castle, this restaurant is run by a husband and wife team. They offer a refined cuisine that is a balanced blend of local recipes and creativity.

Name: Romolo Mare
Description: Situated in a private beach club facing the sea, this restaurant combines a relaxed atmosphere with an elegant feel thanks to its professional owners who have worked as restaurateurs for many years. Here, they serve excellent fish and seafood cuisine with a focus on raw dishes, plus a choice of daily fish specials. A selection of interesting local wines completes the picture.

Name: Roof Garden
Description: Make sure you ask for one of the tables next to the glass wall in this restaurant, which boasts romantic views of Bergamo’s Città Alta. The innovative, inventive cuisine is tempting and full of flavour.

Name: Roscioli
Description: This restaurant is part of one of the best food outlets in Rome, which offers delicacies such as typical Roman pastas, cooked and raw fish, meat, an impressive selection of cured hams and cheeses, as well as top-quality ingredients such as anchovies and mozzarella. Excellent home-baked bread and a varied wine list complete the picture. Make sure you book ahead, as it’s hard to get a table here without a reservation.

Name: Rosita
Description: Decorated in the same simple and rustic style as the Hotel Rosita in which it is housed, this restaurant boasts an attractive terrace overlooking the sea and the coast (call in advance to book one of the tables with the best view), which more than compensates for the narrow, winding road that you have to follow to get here. The delicious cuisine is regional in flavour, including seafood options such as the excellent stuffed baby squid in a sauce served with mashed potatoes, and meat dishes that include a tasty rabbit casserole.

Name: Rosso di Sera
Address: Via Pietro Nenni 2, Castelletto sopra Ticino, 28053, Italy
Description: Situated closed to the motorway exit, this restaurant’s rustic exterior belies its young, colourful and contemporary interior. The dishes are as modern as the decor, yet they have their roots in strong local traditions. The owner has a real passion for French and sparkling wines, including around 160 different champagnes and a wide selection of Burgundies, plus a good choice of wines by the glass, craft beers and cocktails.

Name: Roteo
Address: Via Vincenzo Puricelli 4, Sala Comacina, 22010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view
Description: At the Musa Hotel, the restaurant follows the slope of the building down towards the lake: the view from the windows is enchanting. Take the kitchen, for example: at the hob are two young chefs, drawing on their international experience to infuse their dishes with creativity, alongside a few local touches, starting with freshwater fish. With its sophisticated and well-thought-out technical elements, it is a first-class experience.

Name: Rotta Cucina e Ristoro
Description: Just a short walk from the seafront, it’s well worth taking a detour to visit this elegant Art Nouveau hotel from the 1920s, which is home to chef Gianluca Durillo’s new gastronomic venture. His cuisine offers a contemporary take on the identity of Abruzzo, reinterpreting tradition with a light touch, creativity and a delightful touch of originality. The dishes showcase the region through carefully balanced combinations and precise technique, while retaining a great sense of immediacy in flavour. Among the dishes that most impressed the inspector were the soy-marinated mackerel fillet with black garlic and button mushrooms, and the duck breast with cocoa and maple syrup, served with rhubarb, artichokes and coriander – a successful example of a balance between intensity, freshness and aromatic complexity.

Name: Rovello
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Although it has a new venue, this restaurant has retained its attractive friendly feel in a dining room that acts as a backdrop for substantial dishes that are full of flavour. The interesting classic menu is supplemented by a selection of daily specials, with meat, fish and vegetables (some grilled) prepared in front of guests seated at the counter. There are also traditional tables available and the lively atmosphere remains that of a friendly, welcoming bistro. Interesting wine list, including a selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Rueda Gaucha
Description: In Lignano Sabbiadoro, there is a restaurant which, over the years, has built up a solid reputation among food lovers thanks to one particular speciality: meat. The star of the show is the grill, which is on throughout service – even at lunchtime – serving up carefully selected cuts from the finest Italian and international producers. The menu is rounded off with a refined selection of high-quality cured meats, designed to showcase authentic flavours and ingredients of the highest quality. However, the menu also pays due attention to seafood, with a selection of delicious fish dishes that enrich the menu and broaden the range of choices on offer. A restaurant with a simple, friendly atmosphere, which has become a true classic of seaside dining over the years.

Name: Ruris
Address: Via Spiaggie Rosse, località Mazzotta, Isola di Capo Rizzuto, 88841, Italy
Description: A long-established restaurant specialising in seafood, nestled in the countryside around Isola di Capo Rizzuto and a short distance from Le Castella, one of Calabria’s most charming coastal villages. In the kitchen, chef Natale Pallone showcases the extraordinary bounty of the region through a menu that focuses on fresh fish and the produce of the area. Among the most successful dishes, the cuttlefish tagliatelle flavoured with bergamot, served with a creamy ’nduja sauce, stand out, striking a compelling balance between the freshness of the sea and Calabrian character.

Name: Sa Cardiga e Su Schironi
Address: Strada statale 195 rotonda per Capoterra, Capoterra, 09012, Italy
Description: Since 1967, this small restaurant has been delighting locals and visitors alike with its vast array of fish and seafood dishes, including grilled and skewered specialities. The fresh fish display cabinet at the restaurant entrance is one of the highlights here, as is the extensive selection of antipasti which includes tuna and mullet bottarga, “agliata alla bosana” (blue shark with tomatoes in a light sweet and sour sauce) and “burrida alla cagliaritana” (with dogfish). Other dishes include fresh and pasta with various seafood sauces, fried fish, soup, lobster, barbecued fish and even eel.

Name: Sa Corte
Description: The gastronomic tradition of Nuoro and Barbagia comes to life in a restaurant with rustic charm. The recipes, enriched with personal touches, preserve the authentic flavor of their origins: pasta is strictly homemade and ingredients largely come from the local territory.

Name: Sa Domu Sarda
Description: Despite being an island, Sardinia’s traditional cuisine tends to focus on meat dishes, and you’ll find some of its best-known specialities served at this restaurant, with its simple dining rooms and typical local décor. Enjoy evocatively named dishes such as “sitzigorrus cun bagna” (snails in a tomato sauce), Bue Rosso “bombas” (meat balls), delicious Sardinian pastas such as “malloreddus”, “culurgiones” and “fregula”, stews, casseroles and meat fillets, as well as the famous “sebadas” and “su pappai biancu” (a type of blancmange) desserts.

Name: Sa Mandra
Description: Located within the Sa Mandra farm holiday resort, this restaurant offers the opportunity to discover and appreciate one of the most iconic products of Sardinian culinary tradition: roast suckling pig. The single, fixed menu features it as the main course; guests are encouraged to arrive early to watch the cooking process (the owners are happy to explain each step in detail). Once seated, diners are served a succession of dishes and tastings, all prepared with ingredients grown directly on the farm. Rooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: Sa Musciara
Description: A modern, fresh restaurant situated next to the town hall, with views of the sea from the dining room. Fish and seafood carefully prepared by the owner - chef (also a sailing enthusiast) take pride of place on the menu.

Name: SaQua - Ristorante in Collina
Description: This restaurant, previously known simply as “Il Frantoio”, now has new out-of-town premises but any regret you may have at leaving the town centre will soon disappear, thanks to the wide range of modern Tuscan dishes prepared by the chefs in the new, larger kitchen. A further attraction is the outdoor space which boasts beautiful sunset views in summer.

Name: Sabaudia
Address: Viale Torino 11, loc. Stupinigi, Nichelino, 10042, Italy
Description: Within the farms that once surrounded the Hunting Lodge of Stupinigi, in spaces formerly reserved for servants, springs to life a comfortable establishment characterised by a warm atmosphere steeped in history. The kitchen follows the regional tradition with consistency, enlivening it with touches of imagination and colour that lend freshness to time-honoured recipes. As an alternative, there is no shortage of seafood dishes, to which one of the two tasting menus is also dedicated. The cellar, too, prefers to champion local talent, with suggestions by the glass and bottle that change weekly, keeping the spirit of discovery alive.

Name: Sabir
Address: Via delle Ginestre 1, Zafferana Etnea, 95019, Italy
Description: Situated on the slope of Mt Etna, Sabir takes its name from an old dialect once in use in the ports of the Mediterranean as a means of communication between sea merchants. The recipes created by chef Seby Sorbello demonstrate the same blend of influences, showcasing a fusion of flavours and aromas from the Ionic coast and sea, with a focus on seasonal ingredients and wild herbs from this volcanic region. Choose from a selection of tasting menus and à la carte options.

Name: Sakeya
Address: Via Cesare Da Sesto 1, Milan, 20123, Italy
Description: A Kyoto-born chef, a yakitori grill on full display from the entrance, and pared-back interiors evoking Japanese bistros: the tone is set before you sit down. One wall is devoted entirely to sake – over 150 labels, with new arrivals each week. The kitchen takes an unmistakably Eastern approach in both ingredients and technique, ranging from creative forays such as Gindara 2.0, cod with ginger and yuzu, to classics such as wagyu fillet, cooked tableside over charcoal by the guest. The true specialty, however, remains the kushiyaki: skewers of various cuts grilled over the open flame near the entrance. Service is gracious and well-prepared; let the sommelier guide you through the list, he’s always eager to share the stories and craft behind each sake.

Name: Salamensa
Address: Via Monsignor Oscar Romero 69, Montichiari, 25018, Italy
Description: A multi-function open space, with a bar for breakfasts and a classic restaurant serving pizzas made from naturally fermented dough. Although the ambience is modern, friendly and minimalist, the attention paid to the choice of ingredients and preparation of dishes is of the highest quality.

Name: Sale
Address: Via dell'Amore 23, Licinella-Torre di Paestum, 84047, Italy
Description: Housed within the Sogaris hotel, this restaurant boasts a spacious glass-fronted dining room overlooking a garden with swimming pool and furnished in a contemporary style that gives it an elegant yet relaxed look. The cuisine focuses on fish and seafood served in regional recipes reinterpreted with a light, modern touch. Don’t miss the daily raw seafood specials which are listed separately on the menu.

Name: Sale Grosso
Description: This restaurant describes its cuisine as Mediterranean and it’s true that fish and seafood dominate the menu. However, other dishes also feature and during our visit we particularly enjoyed the carefully prepared fried artichoke heart accompanied by a fresh white Tuscan Montecarlo wine. Friendly, informal service in a simple dining room with a distinctive bistro feel.

Name: SaleGrosso
Address: Piazza della Vittoria 14, Marciana Marina, 57033, Italy
Description: On the waterfront of Marciana Marina, just steps from Il Cotone, the old fishing village, the setting itself suggests a cuisine focused mainly on the sea, combining fish traditions with a few creative offerings. Dishes are of excellent quality, making this one of the island’s best restaurants.

Name: SaleGrosso
Address: Viale II Giugno 15, Milano Marittima, 48015, Italy
Description: For over twenty years, this restaurant has been a trusted choice for those seeking carefully prepared, reliable seafood dishes. The bright, light-coloured interiors evoke the maritime world with understated elegance, while the pleasant outdoor seating area at the entrance offers a welcoming alternative in the warmer months. Over time, it has become a real landmark in the area. The menu celebrates fish in all its forms, starting with raw seafood, which takes centre stage in a dedicated section of the menu. The recipes are deeply rooted in Adriatic tradition, enriched with well-balanced touches of creativity, as in the case of oven-baked scallops au gratin served with a mango emulsion, toasted sesame seeds and crispy ham. The pasta dishes, which are excellent, are also worth a mention, as is a selection of desserts that round off the meal on a satisfying note. Among the restaurant’s great classics, the Cervia salt-baked dishes and the grilled dishes naturally stand out, both enhanced by a careful selection of high-quality fish.

Name: Saleblu
Description: Once a Bourbon reserve dedicated to fish farming, this property is now enjoying a new chapter as a refined boutique hotel overlooking the sea. The restaurant unfolds in a light-filled waterside veranda, complemented by a shaded terrace that seems to hover directly above the blue. At lunchtime, the kitchen adopts a lighter, more Mediterranean tone under the “Peschiera Bistrot” formula, while in the evening the offer broadens through several tasting menus, with dishes also available à la carte and a decidedly more contemporary slant. Fish remains centre stage, accompanied by a number of appealing meat-based alternatives and vegetarian options.

Name: Salsedine367
Address: Via Marradi 11, Lido di Savio, 48125, Italy
Description: Overlooking the beach and forming an integral part of the beach club, this venue invites you to enjoy al fresco dining at any time of day. In the evening, the experience takes on a special charm, with the chance to dine just a stone’s throw from the sea, almost with your feet in the sand. The cuisine focuses primarily on fresh fish and the traditions of the Romagna region, reinterpreted with a contemporary twist: examples include cappellettino with cheese and pepper, served with tomato water, raw prawns and basil pesto. However, there is no shortage of references to the finest Italian traditions, such as in the tartlet with fresh apricot, biancomangiare and almond sorbet. The whole experience is enhanced by elegant international influences, including ceviche, Cantabrian anchovies, yuzu and beurre blanc. At the heart of each dish lies a rigorous selection of ingredients, which is the real strength of the cuisine. The portions are also a pleasant surprise – generous and satisfying – a detail that helps to make the experience even more rewarding.

Name: Salvo
Description: Situated opposite the Villa Comunale gardens, this restaurant serves some of the best pizzas in Naples (classic Neapolitan-style pizza which is soft and so big that it spills over the plate) as well as a selection of delicious appetisers, such as superb pasta fritters with various toppings. Welcoming ambience, with a more elegant feel than that of a typical pizzeria.

Name: Salvo Cacciatori
Description: Since 1906, when distant forebears established a simple osteria with wine counter, this establishment has travelled a remarkable path. Today it presents itself as a welcoming and well-appointed restaurant, distinguished by elegant and contemporary furnishings. The cooking offers an à la carte selection of fish and meat dishes, complemented by tasting menus that allow guests to place themselves entirely in the hands of the chef. The well-structured wine list encompasses not only Ligurian labels but also selections from other regions. The terrace overlooking the pedestrian thoroughfare is most pleasant, and should be reserved well in advance.

Name: San Baylon
Description: Just a short distance from Piazza del Popolo, within the elegant Palazzo Ripetta, San Baylon presents itself as a refined yet informal venue, perfectly at ease in the heart of Rome. The spaces marry the architectural charm of the historic building with a contemporary and measured atmosphere, giving rise to surroundings that are welcoming and equally suited to an unhurried lunch or a more elegant dinner. In the warmer months, service extends to the delightful internal garden, a kind of secluded green retreat that adds a note of tranquillity to the experience. The cooking is distinguished by precision and balance, with careful attention to seasonality and the selection of ingredients. It is the produce itself, of evident quality, that occupies centre stage, drawn out by a modern and restrained approach that keeps the flavours clean, recognisable and direct. Technique, never worn on its sleeve, and a measured creativity lend the dishes both finesse and coherence, giving shape to a style that is elegant and immediately legible. The service, attentive and discreet, accompanies the meal with natural and unhurried rhythm.

Name: San Domenico
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Perched high on the tufa cliffs overlooking the Costa degli Dei, this contemporary-style restaurant boasts superb views from its dining room and especially from its panoramic summer terrace. The cuisine served by the young owner-chef is as modern as the setting – dishes are light and almost exclusively focused on local fish.

Name: San Genesio
Address: Via Francesco Viano 1, San Genesio, 10090, Italy
Description: Commanding a dominant position in the heart of this small hamlet, this historic restaurant — lovingly maintained through the years — has found renewed vigour since 2017 under a passionate and accomplished stewardship (here, fittingly, sommelier Simone’s christening was once celebrated). From the dining room and expansive terrace, one’s gaze sweeps across the surrounding landscape, and on the clearest days the vista extends even further, offering a panorama of considerable enchantment.The kitchen remains faithful to tradition, yet interpreted with contemporary freshness in its presentations and through certain pairings that lend character to the offering. The wine list, too, is of excellent calibre, intelligently structured and rich in both breadth and depth, spanning Piedmont, Italy and beyond.

Name: San Lorenzo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated within the Clitunno hotel, this well-managed family-run restaurant serves classic, seasonal meat and fish dishes, including generous portions of black truffles in some dishes. Recently refurbished, the intimate, elegant dining room also occasionally features live music at weekends, while the outdoor terrace on the small square offers pleasant alfresco dining. Guests are advised to park outside the ZTL (restricted traffic zone) and make their way on foot, via a short walk through the beautiful historic centre.

Name: San Marco
Description: This long-established restaurant in the Asti region has been open for over 70 years and is still renowned for its regional cuisine served in a classic-style dining room. Dishes include cardoons with Raschera cheese fondue, the famous agnolottini del plin (a type of ravioli), and the Piedmontese bunet which is part of a trio of desserts that includes hazelnut tart and zabaglione with Canelli muscat wine.

Name: San Martino 26
Address: Via San Martino 26, San Gimignano, 53037, Italy
Description: Situated in the heart of San Gimignano’s historic centre, this elegant restaurant offers contemporary cuisine presented through two tasting menus: Visione, a five-course menu, and Identità, a seven-course menu, alongside the option to choose freely from the à la carte menu. The menu stands out for its technique, balance and attention to the ingredients, with dishes that showcase the local area through a contemporary approach. Among the most impressive dishes, the suckling pig stands out, with its impeccably crispy skin and intense flavour, enhanced by the harmonious sweet-and-sour contrast of beetroot and raspberry.

Name: San Michele
Address: Via Castello di Fagagna 33, Fagagna, 33034, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Adjacent to the ancient castle ruins and the little church of San Michele, this charming 13th-century building, which was probably once the guardhouse, is now home to a sophisticated restaurant. The cuisine showcases the region and seasonal produce, putting a contemporary spin on traditional ingredients and recipes with a modern sensitivity and meticulous presentation. One of the most interesting dishes is the tuna goulash, an original take on the famous classic, flavoured with paprika and full of flavour. The wine list is also well-curated, starting with Friuli and ranging across Piedmont, Tuscany and France. Some rooms also offer the option of extending your stay in this charming historic setting.

Name: San Quintino Resort
Description: Once you have crossed the plain and climbed up into the San Quintino hills, you come to this restored farmhouse surrounded by an attractive garden. The restaurant is divided into a brick - walled dining room and a winter garden, while the charming guestrooms make this a romantic place to stay. Creative dishes with a focus on local ingredients and a few fish specialities feature on the menu.

Name: San Tommaso 10
Description: It was here, in 1895, that Luigi Lavazza opened a grocer’s shop and immediately began blending coffee. Today, the same establishment is home to a contemporary restaurant, led by a chef from Le Marche who offers one of the city’s most convincing interpretations of Piedmontese gastronomy, enriched by a creative touch. The menu showcases Piedmontese and Italian traditions through a well-balanced selection of dishes, which reinterprets the flavours of the past with a contemporary sensitivity, offering a convivial and authentic dining experience. The wine list is also very interesting, organised according to a colour-coded system that identifies the different types – from ‘voluptuous’ to ‘purple’, from ‘luminous’ to ‘veiled’ – a sophisticated approach that invites you to explore and choose the ideal pairing for each palate and occasion.

Name: Santa Teresa
Address: Via di Porta Soprana 55 r, Genoa, 16123, Italy
Description: Just a stone's throw from the alleged home of Christopher Columbus and Piazza De Ferrari, you will find cosy rooms and lounges, as well as a handy outdoor area in the pedestrian zone. Here, the expert hand of the Scala family, which also runs the renowned San Giorgio, will make you appreciate market and regional cuisine, especially seafood. You will often find the famous Genoese cappon magro, but there is no shortage of good meat-based alternatives, revisited in a slightly contemporary key and carefully plated. It will be easy to find a good match, even by the glass, thanks to a fine selection of wines.

Name: Santamonica
Description: Head down a small street along Corso Italia in the Albaro neighborhood toward the beach, where both the interior dining room and summer terrace offer sweeping sea views. The majority of the menu’s ingredients come directly from those waters (half a page is dedicated to raw preparations). The chef ventures into modern recipes with an emphasis on striking final presentations.

Name: Sant’Agostino
Description: Tucked beside the deconsecrated church of Sant’Agostino, a beautifully kept cloister ushers guests into the culinary world of chef Mauro Brina, a young talent with a stated preference for meat, yet one who truly comes into his own with seafood. Little wonder, then, that we recommend his marine preparations: the pisarei with shellfish or the fish soup brimming with tomato, crustaceans, mussels, cuttlefish, and the day’s catch. In fine weather, make a point of securing a table on the terrace, an evocative setting steeped in history and the timeless charm of the ancient convent.

Name: Sapereta
Address: Via Provinciale Ovest 73, Località Mola, Porto Azzurro, 57036, Italy
Description: A working farm (producing wine and olive oil) that features charming interiors, though the real highlight is outdoor dining beneath a pergola draped with fragola grapes, overlooking a meadow. The menu features both meat and seafood, rooted in Tuscan tradition but often elevated with creative flair.

Name: Satricvm
Description: Creative cuisine with a modern twist for a restaurant that places the Agropontino region and its extraordinary produce at the heart of its culinary creations. The tasting menu, which is seasonal and built around a theme, allows Chef Cotilli to fully express his vision. Proposals include carefully crafted dishes that respect the local terroir and are beautifully presented: from black rice with mussels and beurre blanc to Lara Peri’s pigeon, roasted to perfection and served with castagnaccio and an excellent jus. The outdoor area also serves as a winter garden, filled with plants, bamboo and soft lighting that create a pleasant atmosphere. And, weather permitting, it is well worth visiting the archaeological site of the same name, just a few metres away.

Name: Saur
Description: An unexpected restaurant hidden among the fields of a small hamlet in the Bassa Bresciana region. Although the menu features a few regional dishes, the focus here is on creative cuisine with an emphasis on herbs and vegetables, some of which are grown in the restaurant’s own kitchen garden.

Name: Savô
Description: Overlooking the sea and set within the elegant surroundings of the Hotel Windsor, Savô offers contemporary cuisine that showcases regional ingredients and seasonal produce. The menu focuses primarily on seafood, while still offering a range of interesting land-based options in each section. Guests can choose from tasting menus, including one dedicated to traditional Ligurian flavours, or browse the à la carte menu, where fish, meat and vegetable dishes are given a modern twist. Rounding off the experience is a carefully curated selection of wines and cocktails from the elegant Windsor Bar, which can be enjoyed in the retro-style interiors or on the pleasant terrace overlooking the beach.

Name: Scatto
Description: From Turin’s beautiful Piazza San Carlo, you head through an inner courtyard to this restaurant’s modern dining room with its open-view kitchen. Whether you opt for the à la carte or tasting menu, you’ll find a balance of traditional Piedmontese and more creative dishes, all of remarkable quality, in keeping with the superb wine list.

Name: Scola
Description: Situated in the heart of the Ligurian hinterland, this country house is a real gem, surrounded by a garden that resembles a painting with an English-style lawn that ripples in the wind. Since 1926, the Scola family, now in the fourth generation, have offered guests a friendly welcome here, serving cuisine that is a delight for the tastebuds. In the warm dining room, where the wooden floor and exposed beams hint at the building’s history, guests enjoy traditional local dishes that have been reinterpreted with a modern twist, such as spaghetti with grapefruit, purple prawns and sea lettuce – an explosion of flavours!

Name: Scrigno del Duomo
Description: In the city’s elegant drawing-room quarter, amid the striking palazzi of the historic center, the same refined atmosphere pervades the restaurant’s dining rooms. Seafood plays a minor role here; instead, the kitchen embraces regional specialties such as canederli, polenta, freshwater fish, roasted meats, and, naturally, strudel.

Name: Scuderie Sabaude
Address: Via Amedeo di Savoia 5, Pollenzo, 12042, Italy
Description: Just steps from the University of Gastronomic Sciences in Pollenzo, the restaurant is reached through a timeless courtyard, enhanced by a meticulously tended garden. Within the rustic spaces of the former royal stables, a cuisine takes shape that showcases a selection of top-tier meats, cooked strictly over charcoal. Center stage is Piedmontese scottona (young heifer offered in various aging stages) alongside cuts of Chianina and Alpina beef, the result of careful sourcing and expert preparation designed to highlight texture and flavor.

Name: Seasons
Description: Directly on the seafront promenade, the venue offers spectacular tables set right on the sand, perfect for an experience just steps from the sea. The atmosphere is that of a relaxed, light-filled beach bar, dominated by white tones that enhance the natural light and setting. The gastronomic offering centres on seafood, with a quick and appealing lunch menu, while in the evening it expands into two more structured menus, evocatively named Onda Corta and Onda Lunga. Among the protagonists, the catch of the day, presented directly at the table on a platter for an informed choice, alongside the house’s great classics such as lobster and mantis shrimp, interpreted in the spirit of freshness and simplicity.

Name: Seguire le Botti
Description: Stemming from the experience of Cantina Sant’Andrea, a historic Lazio-based winery owned by the Pandolfo family, this project has given rise to a genuine rural ecosystem comprising vineyards, poultry farms, apiaries and extra virgin olive oil production. The restaurant embodies this philosophy through its cuisine, which chiefly focuses on regional ingredients, featuring tasting menus and an extensive, well-structured à la carte menu. In the warmer months, you can dine al fresco, surrounded by the romantic atmosphere of the large garden, while five rooms allow you to round off the experience with a pleasant stay among nature and the flavours of the region.

Name: Selvatico
Address: Via Silvio Pellico 19, Rivanazzano Terme, 27055, Italy
Description: Opened in 1912 and now run by the fourth generation of the same family, this is one of the best restaurants in the Oltrepò Pavese area. If you’re looking to sample the gastronomic delights of this region, you’ll find a whole host of delicious specialities on offer, from charcuterie and stews to boiled meats and excellent fresh pasta. Attractively furnished guestrooms with the same nostalgic feel as the restaurant are also available.

Name: Serpillo
Address: Via di Mezzo 1, località Torre del Colle, Bevagna, 06031, Italy
Description: Situated in a charming medieval village which is also home to a couple of small hotels, this attractive, rustic restaurant in an old olive mill acts as the backdrop for regional and Italian cuisine. Dishes with a touch of modern flavour are presented on a menu which, although not extensive, offers good value for money.

Name: Seta Sushi Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: It was friendship and passion for Japanese cuisine that prompted two young business partners to open this quiet, welcoming restaurant in the heart of Bologna. Situated in a courtyard with medieval origins, Seta Sushi Restaurant has a modern bistro-style dining room, as well as plenty of outdoor space for summer dining. The menu features an impressive selection of traditional Japanese dishes with the occasional personalised touch, all made from top-quality ingredients. Don’t worry if you’re new to Japanese cuisine – Maurilio is front of house to offer guests friendly, expert advice on both food and beverage. The latter includes a choice of sake for those wishing to immerse themselves fully in the Japanese dining experience.

Name: Shiroya
Description: In the heart of the historic centre, this authentic Japanese restaurant well frequented by an Oriental clientele offers an intimate and carefully considered experience: covers are few, both inside and on the pleasant street terrace, which makes a reservation warmly advisable. A courteous welcome and professional service accompany an offering that traverses the great classics of the Japanese tradition: hand-made gyoza with various fillings, tempura and other fried preparations executed with precision, raw fish in the most canonical combinations, ramen, rice in various preparations and much more besides. To drink, alongside both craft and mainstream beers, saké, tea and Japanese spirits such as shōchū, a selection of wines is also available for those who prefer to remain on familiar ground.

Name: Sibilla
Description: This long-established family-run restaurant occupies a stunning location at the foot of the Temple of Vesta, which can be admired from the attractive outdoor terrace. The classic cuisine served here is prepared mainly with local ingredients, although a few fish dishes also feature. Grilled dishes are among the house specialities.

Name: Sichelburg
Description: Treat yourself to a great meal in an idyllic setting in this village restaurant occupying the first floor of a castle dating back to the 13C. The romantic dining rooms are furnished with wood, while the creative cuisine focuses on typical mountain produce.

Name: Signore te ne ringrazi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At this restaurant in the charming historic centre of Macerata, chef Michele Biagiola serves dishes inspired by rural culinary traditions, with herbs foraged from the fields nearby featuring in some of his recipes. The chef’s signature dishes and gourmet cuisine are served at lunchtime, while the evening menu focuses on more traditional fare served in a relaxing and informal atmosphere.

Name: Silvestro
Description: A cosy, welcoming restaurant with a contemporary feel situated on the edge of Monza’s park. Owner-chef Giuseppe Silvestro is young and talented, with excellent experience in renowned restaurants, and very precise ideas about the type of cuisine he wants to serve here, namely personalised and imaginative dishes inspired by the region and the Mediterranean. We particularly enjoyed the morone fish served with a Piennolo cherry tomato cream and the “mantecato” made with fish scraps.

Name: Soho
Address: Via al Ponte Calvi 20 r, Genoa, 16124, Italy
Description: In the heart of the old town, just a short walk from the aquarium, is a venue with evening tones, but with large windows that make it welcoming even at lunchtime. During warm weather, a few tables outside allow people to enjoy the busy promenade. Although the fish for sale counter of the early days is no longer there, the sea continues to take centre stage with excellent raw materials and classic dishes, always generous in portions.

Name: Solociccia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: One of Italy’s most celebrated butchers, this establishment offers an original and strongly individual gastronomic experience: a single tasting menu entirely dedicated to meat – with a vegetarian alternative available – is served across several rooms and intimate spaces according to a convivial format at fixed sittings. Guests are seated at shared tables, immersed in a lively and authentic atmosphere, amid straw-covered Chianti bottles and a pleasant hum of conversation. A frank and informal experience that finds its most genuine expression at lunch: Solociccia, in fact, opens exclusively at midday.

Name: Soprattutto
Address: Via Noalese 124, Santa Maria di Sala, 30036, Italy
Description: This tiny, welcoming restaurant with a bright, simple decor has long since come of age, having been opened and run by the same family for years. The wife supervises the front of house, while the husband (whose past experience includes working as a metalworker as well as a chef) is at the helm in the kitchen, where he creates classic fish dishes which are full of flavour and simply prepared from top-quality ingredients. As the restaurant is very popular with its regular clientele, booking in advance is essential – you won’t be disappointed!

Name: Sora Maria e Arcangelo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The very quintessence of the Lazio trattoria: the same family management since 1949, interiors that are typical and steeped in atmosphere. Here you’ll find an extraordinary interpretation of the regional cuisine, based on excellent produce, neither commonplace nor pitched at the tourist trade, its flavours intense and unforgettable. Over so many years, certain dishes have acquired legendary status: cannelloni filled with young beef and gratin with tomato and fior di latte, pappardelle with white farmyard ragù, the trilogy of Roman abbacchio, and naturally the offal (the lamb abbuoto cooked over the grill being quite exceptional). A place of the heart, to which one never tires of returning.

Name: Sostansa
Description: In the heart of the city, just beyond the restricted traffic zone, this venue tells culinary stories through dishes with a distinctly urban character. Here, the finest market offerings are selected with respect for seasonality, then transformed into generous, seductive creations: from the land, bergamot-lacquered squab with Treviso radicchio, its legs served in a salad with pears and walnuts; from the sea, turbot paired with broccoli rabe perfumed with garlic, olive oil, and chili. An experience that plays between tradition and modernity, with bold flavors and surprising harmonies.

Name: SottoSopra
Description: A pleasant and colourful restaurant in the village centre, divided into several dining rooms. The owner-chef prepares a range of eclectic dishes with passion and enthusiasm, offering a menu which includes meat dishes alongside fish options (salt- and freshwater), as well as a few regional specialities.

Name: Soul & Fish
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: From the centre of Sorrento, you follow a succession of roads downhill to Marina Grande, the town’s old, picturesque fishing village that is well worth a visit. Here, facing the water, you’ll find Soul & Fish, a seemingly traditional seaside restaurant that actually serves superb fish and seafood on a menu that combines traditional dishes with more creative options.

Name: Soul Restaurant
Description: Having spent a long period of time gaining experience abroad, the enthusiastic couple at the helm of this restaurant have returned to Italy where they delight their guests with imaginative and creative cuisine that focuses on top-quality ingredients and beautiful presentation. They serve three tasting menus, with the additional option of choosing courses à la carte style. Special mention should be made of the warm welcome, excellent service and skilful wine selection, all of which make the dining experience here even more enjoyable.

Name: Specus
Description: This charming restaurant’s name comes from the Latin and refers to the small grotto carved out of the tufa rock in the courtyard, which is home to just a few tables. The restaurant is run by a young couple, with Flavia front of house and Alessio at the helm in the kitchen. The cuisine is authentic in style, with imaginatively named dishes such as “Quel viaggio che non scordo” (“This journey I’ll never forget”) and “Dal 2014” (“From 2014”). The Riso Acquerello with fermented goat’s cheese, black truffle and herb pesto is truly memorable, while the desserts (especially the apple strudel) are equally delicious.

Name: Spoon
Description: Located in the heart of the historic centre, just a stone’s throw from the beautiful 13C cathedral, this small, simple restaurant with an outdoor space is home to owner-chef Marco Cozzi, whose cuisine is the main attraction here. Having trained with Niko Romito, this chef creates dishes from seasonal, regional ingredients, reinterpreting traditional recipes to give them a contemporary flavour (for example, he transforms pancotto into a cream of bread and Navelli saffron, which he then crowns with Robiola cheese, cime di rapa and triangles of cured pork loin). His two tasting menus focus entirely on meat and feature an impressive selection of vegetables.

Name: Stefano Mocellin al Padovanino
Description: Situated in the historic centre of Padova, this restaurant is home to owner-chef Stefano Mocellin, whose colourful, creative and personalised cuisine is influenced by his past culinary experience in cities such as Milan and Venice. From Milan, for example, he has taken the legendary “cassoeula”, to which he gives a lighter touch thanks to his use of more than one type of meat (pork and duck), while his “saor” and the sardines that he uses to stuff his plin pasta are inspired by Venice. Underlying all of this is his passion for cooking over the barbecue grill, the main focus of almost all the dishes on the menu.

Name: Stefano Paganini alla Corte degli Alfieri
Description: Within the walls of Castello di Magliano Alfieri – a place suspended in time, with a magnificent frescoed hall and soaring ceilings overlooking the hills of Langhe and Roero – chef Paganini’s cuisine takes shape, deftly balancing local tradition and innovation. Two main offerings are available: the traditional menu, “Viaggio in Piemonte (Journey Through Piedmont),” and the “A Occhi Chiusi (Eyes Closed)” menu, customizable in three, four, or five courses according to guests’ preferences. It is in this latter menu that the chef gives full rein to his creativity, crafting bespoke dishes and personalized interpretations designed to make every experience unique.

Name: Stefenelli Desk
Description: This restaurant is situated in an alleyway in the historic centre of Aoste. Full of character and accessed via a staircase from the entrance hall, the dining room is housed in what were probably the palazzo’s 18C stables. Under a brick-vaulted ceiling and arches, enjoy cuisine from the Aosta valley with a creative twist.

Name: Stella d'Italia
Description: Run by the same family since 1962, the establishment actually dates back to 1875: warm, elegant interiors complement lovely summer garden service offering glimpses of the lake. The kitchen draws primarily from Venetian traditions, with a nod to nearby Lake Garda, as in the marinated pike in carpione with polenta among the starters. To follow, we recommend the hand-pressed bigoli with guinea fowl salmì or the excellent meat tortellini; among the main courses, for those wishing to stay within the regional tradition, calf’s liver with onions, while a dedicated section of the menu is reserved for snail dishes, the house specialty.

Name: Stilla
Address: Località Casette 1, Colognola ai Colli, 37030, Italy
Description: Run by an enthusiastic and committed young couple who left the big city to restore the family home and transform it into an elegant, welcoming restaurant, Stilla stands in a tranquil location surrounded by vineyards. Here, Silvia creates original, generous and colourful cuisine which is showcased on an à la carte with just a few dishes which change regularly. We particularly enjoyed the freshly seared bonito served with wild spinach, sour cherries and a cherry barbecue sauce. Meals are served on the outdoor terrace in summer. Accommodation is also available in five beautiful yet functional guestrooms. Well worth a visit.

Name: Strattoria
Description: Perched on the first hills overlooking Lake Maggiore, this venue – with its welcoming and relaxed atmosphere – has now been completely refurbished, thanks to a recent renovation project that has combined comfort, elegance and a focus on energy efficiency. In the kitchen, the young chef offers his own take on contemporary Italian cuisine, featuring meticulously prepared dishes that are vibrant in colour and well-balanced in flavour. Meat and fish feature equally prominently on a menu that focuses primarily on Piedmont and its produce, while still incorporating creative and seasonal touches. The daily specials, expertly recommended by the waiting staff, help to ensure that each visit is different from the last. At lunchtime, the menu is expanded to include a more informal, bistro-style offering, though still offering just an à la carte selection.

Name: Stua Noa Fine Dining
Description: Within the Hotel Concordia, the restaurant unfolds across two small and modern stube, reached by passing through the hotel’s main dining room. Here one may order à la carte or entrust oneself to one of the tasting menus – available also in a vegetarian version – for a contemporary cuisine that is measured and well-grounded in the flavours and produce of the territory.

Name: Stube Ladina
Description: Inside the elegant Hotel Alpenrose, guests are welcomed into a cosy stube with light wood panelling and an intimate atmosphere, enhanced by soft lighting. The cuisine pays tribute to Ladin tradition through authentic recipes that showcase the quality of local produce. Among the specialities not to be missed are Schlutzkrapfen, traditional rye-flour half-moons stuffed with spinach and cheese, served with melted butter and locally produced smoked ricotta: an iconic dish that, on its own, encapsulates the connection between the local cuisine and the Dolomites.

Name: Su Murruai
Address: Via Giuseppe Garibaldi 36, Riola Sardo, 09070, Italy
Description: In a small village overlooking the Sinis Peninsula, the restaurant has been established within an old mill and is dedicated to 'su murruai', Sardinian for the scent of aged Vernaccia. Contemporary Mediterranean cuisine is curated by young chef Ivan Matarese, who seeks quality regional ingredients—from both the mainland and the Gulf of Oristano—to reimagine modern recipes. Additionally, some Campania influences—being the chef's origin—are evident, especially in the desserts, half of which draw inspiration from renowned Campanian sweets (reimagined pastiera and babà).

Name: Sunrise Restaurant
Description: One of the most attractive restaurants in the city centre, Sunrise occupies the ground floor of an old Bourbon palazzo, extending right to the back of the building where you’ll find the delightful “literary veranda” and, beyond the large windows, a beautiful outdoor space surrounded by a garden planted with citrus trees.
