The menu has an exclusive focus on fish, with a combination of classic options and light, modern dishes, while an entire page is dedicated to raw fish and seafood. The wine list includes several champagnes.

Name: Suscettibile Salerno
Description: Separated from a street in the centre of Salerno by an inner courtyard, this restaurant is a peaceful oasis with comfortable chairs arranged on a modern veranda (which opens almost completely in summer) and in an equally elegant dining room. The cuisine is imaginative and appealing, with excellent fish and seafood served in modern, interesting recipes. The menu also includes a delicious selection of raw dishes.

Name: Sushi Matsu Omakase
Description: Just 14 guests, seated in a horseshoe arrangement around two chefs, witness the preparation of each dish in real time. Fish, in all its variations, takes shape before your eyes, while conversation with those preparing it becomes an integral part of the ritual, essential for unlocking the secrets of the Japanese art of sushi. Eating with your hands is encouraged, as tradition dictates, and we recommend pairing the experience with one of the sakés offered by the glass, to complete the Japanese immersion. At lunch, the menu is more streamlined, but it’s worth taking the time to savor every detail. Among the creations that won over our inspectors: the Japanese scallop and squid tartare, enhanced by delicate notes of soy and yuzu in perfect balance, with wasabi applied with masterful restraint.

Name: Sushisen
Description: Two carefully designed spaces offer two distinct experiences, united by consistent quality. On one side is the Sushisen Experience, devoted to Japanese cuisine with a gourmet slant and the omakase tasting journey; on the other, Sushisen Kaitenzushi, where the same omakase – now also served here, exclusively for two guests and at dinner – is offered alongside counter seats facing the conveyor belt, animated by a convivial succession of small, inviting creations. The drinks list is extensive and well conceived, with numerous wines and sakes also available by the glass. The all-female service team is warm, attentive and precise.

Name: Svevia
Description: In the evocative former stables of the palace, or, if weather permits outdoor dining, in the square facing Termoli’s enchanting cathedral, the cuisine, almost exclusively seafood-based, features various classic fish dishes, sometimes with more creative reinterpretations.

Name: Sücar Brüsc
Description: A restaurant of young and contemporary character, with a lively entrance where a carefully considered display of wines – available for purchase – immediately signals the attention dedicated to the bottle. The offering focuses on a cuisine with a well-defined identity, built upon clean flavours and well-executed ideas. Among the most representative dishes, the tortelli duo deserves particular mention, half ‘sweet’ and half ‘bitter’, mantecati with artisan butter and sage, as does the Bove, a satisfying trio of beef that brings together braised stracotto, oven-roasted tongue and steamed cheek, served with soft potato and a fragrant salsa verde. Indulgent, satisfying and well-constructed dishes, perfectly suited to conveying the style of the house.

Name: Tana de 'l Ors
Address: Via Roma 28, Forno di Zoldo, 32012, Italy
Description: A favourite with food-lovers, this restaurant serves lighter meals at lunchtime which are nonetheless carefully and imaginatively prepared (don’t miss the orsoburger!). In the evening, the best daily ingredients are prepared with a lightly modern touch – meat is the undisputed start of the show, although a few fish dishes also feature. One-room and two-room apartments are also available.

Name: Tano Passami l'Olio
Description: In an elegant residential neighbourhood, Tano Simonato's restaurant welcomes guests with modern design and a refined atmosphere, a prelude to cuisine that tantalises the senses. Italian tradition is clothed in creativity in the dishes: the famous “tirami su” made with cuttlefish and potatoes releases marine aromas and velvety notes, while the honey-glazed pigeon, baked in salt, delights the palate with contrasting sweet and savoury flavours, accompanied by spinach and savoury cherries. Tano sees food as a source of pleasure and enjoyment: the chef comes to the table, tells stories and suggests pairings, with every glass of wine becoming part of an experience that seduces all the senses.

Name: Tanzer
Description: Located beneath the belltower in a small hamlet, this restaurant has two romantic 17C Stube-style dining rooms, where Melanie and her sommelier husband Michael delight guests with regional, modern and imaginative cuisine. Most of the ingredients are sourced locally, including from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden. The home-made syrups and jams are highly recommended.

Name: Taverna Kus
Address: Contrada Castello 14, San Zeno di Montagna, 37010, Italy
Description: An attractive restaurant situated on the western slopes of Monte Baldo overlooking Lake Garda, with a number of rustic yet elegant and welcoming dining rooms, including a bright veranda with partial views of the lake (enjoy the full vista from the outdoor terrace). Various culinary options feature on the menu, including meat, fish and vegetarian dishes, all colourful, full of flavour and beautifully cooked and prepared using mainly local and seasonal ingredients. The well-stocked and carefully chosen wine list deserves a special mention: among the 1 000 or more bottles stored in the old giasàra (underground cellar), you’re sure to find something you’ll enjoy.

Name: Taverna La Cialoma
Description: This restaurant housed in Marzamemi’s old tuna fishery boasts an outdoor terrace with tables overlooking one of the most picturesque squares in Sicily, as well as an indoor dining room and another terrace to the rear facing the sea. Wherever you choose to sit, you’ll find authentic Sicilian cuisine on the menu, with just a few simply prepared dishes in which the full flavours of fresh fish shine through.

Name: Taverna Rovita
Description: Since 1981, Taverna Rovita has been a staple of Marateo’s restaurant scene. Just a stone’s throw from the main square of the old town, this charming venue retains a picturesque 18th-century kitchen and rooms adorned with traditional Vietri ceramics. The menu passionately showcases the Lucanian region, highlighting its signature produce and recipes, such as the delicious Lucanian panata: a thin slice of lamb coated in a mixture of dry breadcrumbs, pecorino cheese, parsley and garlic, then baked in the oven. To round off the experience, there is an extensive and carefully curated wine list, the result of Mariastella’s expertise and passion, with a particular focus on small-scale Italian and international producers. For a special occasion, small groups can dine in the cosy cellar dining room, surrounded by historic bottles and prized collectable wines.

Name: Taverna Trilussa
Description: A true bastion of Roman gastronomy, set in the city’s most quintessential neighbourhood for such an “attraction”. With a history stretching back over a century – it was founded in 1910 – the restaurant upholds tradition as its standard, served in a rustic yet surprisingly refined setting, supported by attentive and accomplished service. Among the first courses, beyond the timeless cacio e pepe, carbonara, amatriciana and gricia, stands out an award-winning speciality: Ravioli Mimosa, prepared according to a secret recipe that is neither meat nor fish. There follow all the great classics of Roman cuisine, from lamb to tripe, culminating in the house’s signature dish: beef fillet cooked over charcoal.

Name: Taverna del Castello
Description: Park in the small car park close to the village, then make your way on foot to this restaurant, admiring the village’s beautiful stone houses along the way. Inside the restaurant, the service is informal yet professional, while the cuisine served on the first floor includes emblematic local specialities such as tortelli alle erbette (stuffed pasta with herbs) and local salumi (including Parma ham). The wine list boasts a good selection of local and Italian wines – finding a label to suit your taste and budget will not be a problem!

Name: Taverna dello Spuntino
Description: This Roman trattoria has a particularly striking interior. From its old tufa passageways converted into a wine cellar in the basement, to its charming dining rooms with brick - vaulted arches where hams, flasks of wine, fruit and antipasti all form an attractive display.

Name: Taverna e' Mare
Address: Via Principal Marina, 16, Torre del Greco, 80059, Italy
Description: In an elegant setting facing the harbour and the sea, the dining room at this restaurant is a terrace with large picture windows boasting beautiful views that also include Capri. The sea takes pride of place on the menu, which features fresh fish and plenty of local produce in the cuisine served here. Don’t miss the raw fish options, which include a selection of oysters, tartares and ceviche. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the roll of sea bass stuffed with spinach, fior di latte, beurre blanc sauce, parsley oil and onions.

Name: Tavola MoS - Stefano Zanini
Address: Via Ugo da Como 8, Lonato del Garda, 25017, Italy
Description: Accomplished chef Stefano Zanini showcases his considerable talent in the evocative setting of the Rocca di Lonato. His recently opened establishment occupies the spaces of the former apartment of the librarian to Senator Ugo da Como, to whom the Foundation owes its name: a luminous and carefully appointed room, almost a veranda-like dining space suspended above the gardens, where history and elegance converse in natural harmony. The kitchen presents creative Italian cuisine, consistently well-presented and guided by a refined hand. The sea bass, rapidly cooked on the skin side and finished with a sauce of anchovy essence and extra virgin olive oil, accompanied by seasonal vegetables interpreted with intelligence, is particularly convincing; the pigeon too merits attention. At lunch, in addition to the à la carte menu, a lighter formula is available.

Name: Tenne Lodges
Description: Situated near the ski slopes in the Gourmethotel Tenne Lodges, this restaurant is decorated with a profusion of wood. The large dining room is the backdrop for delicious modern cuisine which is regional in focus yet also influenced by the chef’s professional experience around the world. Excellent wine list offering plenty of choice, plus a stone wine cellar which makes a charming setting for a pre-dinner drink.

Name: Tenuta Casa Virginia
Address: Via Cascina Violo 1, Villa d'Almè, 24018, Italy
Description: Surrounded by the property’s own vineyards, this restaurant nestlings at the bottom of a gentle hill features an elegant dining room and a beautiful terrace for outdoor dining in fine weather. The cuisine is contemporary (yet not excessively so), with a few freshwater fish also featuring on the menu, while the wine list showcases a good selection of wines. The property’s own wines are available for purchase in the shop.

Name: Tenuta del Gallo
Description: Whether you dine indoors in the charming, romantic dining room or outdoors with views of the surrounding countryside, you’ll enjoy traditional local cuisine and classic Italian favourites at this restaurant. Our inspectors particularly enjoyed the excellent beef carpaccio with truffles and the local guinea fowl with chickpeas. Comfortable guestrooms are also available.

Name: Teresa dal 1968
Address: Piazza Lido di Pegli 5 r, Pegli, Genoa, 16156, Italy
Description: Over half a century has passed since this restaurant was opened in 1968 by “mamma” Teresa and “papa” Giuseppe – and it’s still going strong! And although the staff here are proud of the restaurant’s long history and sense of tradition, they are not bound by it, as demonstrated by dishes that have successfully moved with the times, incorporating modern touches to the classic recipes, while always retaining a focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients (especially when it comes to choosing fish).

Name: Terracotta
Description: Situated in the old town, this small, cosy restaurant serves delicious cuisine, with dishes sometimes inspired by Italian and international recipes, but often revisited in a unique way. In summer, you can dine on the terrace under a beautiful wisteria tree.

Name: Terradimare
Description: Overlooking a broad piazza that faces the evocative harbour basin of Trani, and a short distance from the magnificent cathedral, a masterpiece of Apulian Romanesque and enduring symbol of the city, this restaurant, modest in size yet possessed of considerable grace, has the talented Domenico Di Tondo in the kitchen. The gastronomic offering expresses clean, assured flavours and an elegant personality, favouring the catch of the day and a seafood-led kitchen that follows the arrivals closely, while not forgoing – in a nod to the restaurant’s name – some interesting meat alternatives. In the dining room, an entirely female front-of-house team, attentive and solicitous, completes what is a harmonious and carefully considered experience.

Name: Terrae by Iside De Cesare
Description: The cuisine of the prestigious Tivoli Palazzo Gaddi bears the authoritative signature of Iside De Cesari, who gracefully escorts the elegance of Renaissance walls through to the Terrae restaurant dining room. The menu, constructed by four hands with resident Apulian chef Salvatore Canargiu, is a narrative that intertwines Tuscany and its produce with evocations of Lazio drawn from the Tuscia, home to the Michelin-starred La Parolina, the beating heart of Iside’s world. What fully convinced the inspector was the artichoke stuffed with squid, poised between cooked and raw: a delicate, surprising dish of considerable personality. Canargiu’s Apulian sensitivity also merits note, capable of elevating even the bread service to a distinctive gastronomic gesture. With the warmer season, moreover, the experience is completed: first an aperitif at the rooftop lounge bar Aria, with vistas embracing Florence’s Duomo, then the pleasure of settling in the outdoor seating to dine al fresco.

Name: Terraforte
Address: Via Bagnoli Terriccio 12, Castellina Marittima, 56040, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Within the vast and evocative Tenuta Il Terriccio estate, extending across 1,500 hectares of horse breeding, olive groves and celebrated vineyards – from which the famous Lupicaia is produced, offered alongside the other estate wines also by the glass – a Tuscan landscape of rare beauty and tranquillity unfolds. The restaurant occupies the estate’s former joinery, today transformed into an elegant country house. The cuisine, developed in collaboration with chef Tomei, is rooted in authentic farm-to-table produce: the recipes celebrate the resources of the estate – from farm-reared meats to game, from poultry to vegetables, through to aromatic herbs and honey (seafood alone being an exception). The experience is freely composed by choosing the number of courses, giving way to a sequence of creative and balanced dishes that always maintain a clear identity in the raw materials. In the warmer months, a table on the evocative outdoor terrace is not to be missed and, for those wishing to extend their stay, accommodation is available at La Marrana, within the estate.

Name: Terrazza Bartolini
Address: Via A. Boito 30, Milano Marittima, 48015, Italy
Description: Overlooking the sea, with views of the beach and the picturesque little harbour, this restaurant captivates from the very first glance thanks to its romantic panoramic terrace, one of the most sought-after in the area. Alternatively, guests can choose the elegant indoor dining room, but advance booking is strongly recommended, particularly during the warmer months. The cuisine is focused on seafood, prepared in a simple style that respects the raw ingredients, with an emphasis on clean flavours and classic methods. Examples include the seafood salad, with fish, mussels and king prawns gently steamed and served on a bed of seasonal vegetables, or the seafood risotto, served in its most authentic form. There is no shortage of selections of raw seafood and dishes that showcase the famous Cervia salt, the region’s signature ingredient. In harmony with the culinary offering, the wine list favours white wines and sparkling wines, with a particular focus on Champagne, complemented by a select range of rosé wines.

Name: Terrazza Costantino
Description: In just a few years, young owner-chef Giuseppe Costantino has turned what was once the family trattoria into an elegant restaurant serving delicious reinterpretations of local specialities. There is just one tasting menu which features either meat or fish (although this can be discussed when you make your booking, which is essential). Given the excellent quality of the food here, this menu offers exceptional value for money.

Name: Terrazza Fiorella
Address: Via Vincenzo Maggio 5, Massa Lubrense, 80061, Italy
Description: Housed in the Villa Fiorella Art Hotel, this restaurant boasts a stunningly located terrace with spectacular views of the Bay of Naples and its islands. The cuisine pays tribute to Campania and its top-quality ingredients which the chef uses to create imaginative dishes reinterpreted with his own personal twist.

Name: Terrazza Gallia
Description: On the seventh floor of Hotel Gallia, with panoramic views of the square and Central Station, the restaurant’s limited seating is arranged in a room with modern furnishings and features a cuisine inspired by products and recipes from throughout Italy. A rewarding gastronomic destination in a refined setting.

Name: Terrazza Tiberio
Description: Housed on the first floor of the Tiberio hotel, this elegant restaurant boasts a terrace overlooking the rooftops of Capri. The regional and island specialities on the menu leave a lasting memory, such as the “montanara” (fried pizza), “casatiello” (a savoury bread from Naples) and the caprese-style ravioli, although more creative options also feature, especially among the desserts. All in all, an elegant dining experience.

Name: Terre Alte
Address: Via Olmadella 11, Località Balignano, Longiano, 47020, Italy
Description: One of the best-known addresses in this region for fish enthusiasts, this restaurant serves freshly caught fish prepared in simple, traditional dishes that allow the quality of the flavour to shine through. A good wine list (particularly champagnes) and a panoramic terrace add to the appeal.

Name: The Tasting Room by Marcello Corrado
Description: In Merano, within the elegant setting of Villa Eden, an intimate dining room with gilded accents and just four tables sets the stage for an exclusive gastronomic experience, woven around the discreet allure of candlelight. Here, chef Marcello Corrado presents a multisensory journey of singular identity: the eight-course tasting menu ‘OTTO ELEMENTI’ is a sincere expression of his culinary philosophy, his creativity, and a talent in constant dialogue with the territory and its extraordinary biodiversity. As an alternative, ‘EDEN ESSENCE’ offers a carefully curated selection of the most emblematic dishes from OTTO ELEMENTI, distilling their essence into a more concise yet equally evocative form. The cooking moves gracefully between lightness and satisfaction, with dishes crafted with an elegant hand and measured imagination, while the attentive and impeccable service completes a gastronomic visit of rare refinement.

Name: The View Milano by Valerio Braschi
Description: On the first floor, overlooking the piazza and set within surroundings of distinct historical character with glimpses of the Duomo and the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele, chef Valerio Braschi presents a culinary offering that sets recipes of the tradition alongside creations of a more contemporary spirit. The Contaminazioni menu traces a journey through Italian flavours and international influences, with South American and Asian forays conceived to intensify the taste. Worthy of particular note is the calamari salad, lifted by a well-judged chimichurri and tarragon, as is the costoletta alla milanese, reinterpreted with quiet grace in a pleasingly modern reading of the great Milanese classic. The spaces, elegant and formal in equal measure, are completed by the Terrazza Duomo, ideal for an aperitivo or after-dinner drink, with one of the most arresting views of the centre of Milan.

Name: Thelema - Maison de Cuisine
Address: Via Marta Lodi 54, San Vito, 20083, Italy
Description: “Thelema”, an ancient Greek word evoking the concept of will and desire, becomes the manifesto of the young and talented chef Simone Tricarico, who after a lengthy journey through exceptional kitchens in Italy and France has chosen to strike out on his own, giving form to a cuisine that is personal, creative and deeply rooted in identity. The restaurant welcomes guests into a warm and relaxing environment, dominated by wood and a luminous dining room punctuated by large windows overlooking the well-tended garden beyond. The culinary offering is a harmonious blend of originality and technique, featuring an array of dishes that leaves diners with a delightful dilemma when it comes time to choose. Impossible not to be tempted by the rich “saffron rice and Milanese veal” or the intense “braised milk-fed lamb, caciocavallo and turnip tops”, which speak of the chef’s assured hand. In the dining room, the attentive and punctual service is guided by Daniele Miceli, who accompanies guests with professionalism through the wine selection and orchestrates the timing of the tasting with precision.

Name: Tiffany Bistrot di Mare
Description: In a discreet location and open at lunchtime only – booking is strongly recommended – this simple, intimate restaurant serves seafood cuisine in which the crudités take centre stage. The cooked dishes however also deserve attention, thanks to the freshness of the ingredients and the generous portions, all underpinned by a classic, reassuring style. Alongside the selection available via the digital menu are the valuable recommendations of proprietor Sabino Di Muro, who has succeeded in transforming a former bar into a venue dedicated to the pleasures of the table, sometimes with a nod to tradition, as in the excellent tajarin with sea urchins. It is well worth following his advice for wine pairings too, always chosen to bring out the best in the cuisine.

Name: Tinello Bistrot
Address: Via Vigna di Corte 6, Castel Gandolfo, 00073, Italy
Description: A short distance from the striking piazza overlooked by the papal palace, yet occupying a more discreet location, you will find a pleasant and informal dining room, managed by staff both charming and knowledgeable. The dishes are not necessarily rooted in Lazio’s culinary traditions; there are also offerings of varied provenance, occasionally with a more creative flourish.

Name: Toe Drûe
Address: Via Corsi 44 r, Sestri Ponente, Genoa, 16154, Italy
Description: Opened at the beginning of the 20th century to feed shipyard workers, this historic establishment still retains the authentic flavour of its origins. The name “Toe Drue”, which means “thick tables”, refers to the sturdy tables of the old inn. Today, the restaurant continues to celebrate Genoese tradition in an informal and welcoming atmosphere, with iconic dishes such as “cappon magro”, stockfish and other Ligurian specialities that tell a story of sincere and timeless cuisine.

Name: Tola Rasa
Description: This elegant, minimalist-style restaurant serves two tasting menus (Classici and Contemporanei – the names tell you all you need to know!) from which dishes can also be chosen à la carte style. When we ate there in late autumn, we particularly enjoyed the rabbit with saffron and porcini mushrooms prepared in the open-air kitchen. There are just a few beautifully laid tables, plus a wine list that includes a selection of labels from Italy and France.

Name: Tosca
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Set within the ancient Castello di Casole, Tosca establishes itself as a venue of great character, where warm and refined atmospheres take shape among exposed stone, sumptuous fabrics, and elegantly crafted furnishings. The menu celebrates Tuscan tradition through contemporary cuisine that showcases local and seasonal ingredients with sensitivity and precision. At the heart of its philosophy lies the “Territori” project, developed in collaboration with Norbert Niederkofler, which showcases the local area through simple, authentic dishes that show deep respect for nature. This approach finds fertile ground within the vast organically farmed estate surrounding the castle and helps to strengthen the link between cuisine and the landscape. Finally, in the warmer months, the experience is rounded off with an aperitif served al fresco, while surrounded by the tranquillity and beauty of the Tuscan countryside.

Name: Trattoria 'petito
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located on the outskirts of Forlì’s charming historic centre, this simple, modern yet attractive restaurant serves eclectic and varied cuisine. More traditional fare on offer includes an excellent selection of hams and grilled meats, as well as delicious tagliatelle al ragù, while the menu also features a few more creative options including a few fish dishes.

Name: Trattoria Al Passo
Description: Successive generations of the same family have run this pleasant restaurant just outside the city for over 70 years. Enjoy a selection of fish and seafood dishes (raw, grilled or fried with numerous condiments to accompany your starters) in a maritime themed dining room or on the light and airy veranda. There is a good selection of desserts to round off your meal.

Name: Trattoria Battibecco
Description: Although it calls itself a trattoria, this restaurant situated in a narrow street in the city centre has an elegant ambience, welcoming guests with friendly service and serving an equal balance of meat and fish dishes. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the foie gras sautéed with Lambrusco blueberries and pan brioche, and the “finché c’è bottarga c’è speranza” (“while there’s bottarga, there’s hope”) spaghetti served with tuna tartare, mullet roe, lime and pistachios.

Name: Trattoria Ceriati
Address: Località Cangelasio Ceriati 18, Salsomaggiore Terme, 43039, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in attractive countryside where the plains give way to rolling hills (a perfect destination for a Sunday outing), this simple yet well-kept trattoria serves all the usual traditional local specialities. The typical fresh pasta and the desserts are all home-made.

Name: Trattoria Da Lorenzo
Address: Via Fra' Gerardo Sasso 8, Scala, 84010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Slightly off the beaten track in the lesser-known village of Scala opposite Ravello, this authentic family trattoria offers an informal change from the many Michelin-starred luxury restaurants dotted along the Amalfi Coast. Da Lorenzo has been serving simple yet excellent fish and seafood cuisine for decades, with a wonderful and highly recommended array of fresh fish on display. A popular panoramic terrace adds to its appeal.

Name: Trattoria Glisenti
Description: Situated on the lakefront with some tables set out on a panoramic terrace, this restaurant has been run by the same family since 1890 and is renowned for its typical lake cuisine. Fish and shellfish such as trout, char, shrimp and perch take pride of place on the menu, which also features a few meat dishes and vegetarian options.

Name: Trattoria Guallina
Address: Via Molino Faenza 19, località Guallina, Mortara, 27036, Italy
Description: Situated in a small house in an outlying village in the countryside, this is a simple, inviting restaurant where you can enjoy seasonal local cuisine. Excellent wines.

Name: Trattoria I Masenini
Description: In a beautiful part of Verona, right opposite the famous Castelvecchio, this restaurant offers a very relaxing ambience with wood ceilings and informal classic furnishings, subtle lighting and soft background music. The menu features both regional and Italian dishes, with specialities including spit-roast meat and fish. Alfresco dining is offered in summer.

Name: Trattoria La Barca
Description: Run by the Virgilio family since 1967, this popular restaurant pays tribute to historic Bari with its delicious fish dishes and specialities from Puglia. Don’t miss the grilled fish and the reinterpreted cannolo dessert made with sheep’s milk ricotta, pear sauce and pistachio waffles.

Name: Trattoria Le Viole
Address: strada nuova di Castelnuovo 60/a, Castelnovo di Baganzola, 43126, Italy
Description: Regionally based cuisine with the occasional hint of creativity and a good choice of à la carte dishes are the highlights at this friendly restaurant on the outskirts of Parma. An authentic, genuine welcome, with an attractive lounge near the entrance and the warm ambience of a private home.

Name: Trattoria Leoni
Description: Nestled among the hills of Felino, amid the lush greenery of the Parma countryside, this trattoria in Barbiano has long been a point of reference for those in search of authenticity and the flavours of another age. The cooking of the Leoni family celebrates local tradition, drawing upon recipes handed down from grandmother Erminia and interpreted with care and deep respect. Among the most iconic dishes stands the delicious rabbit alla cacciatora: already boned, enveloped in a tomato sauce fragrant with aromatic herbs, it represents at its finest the substance and richness of Parma cuisine. Not to be missed either is a taste of the Felino salame, aged at length in the family cellar, which speaks with honesty and conviction of the soul of the territory.

Name: Trattoria Margherita
Description: Don’t be fooled by the relatively simple ambience of this trattoria which is situated in the centre of a town with an interesting history linked to the reclamation of the marshes and the dairy industry. Dedicated to the owner’s two grandmothers, the restaurant serves some of Sardinia’s best-known meat and fish specialities.

Name: Trattoria Pomposa - Al Re gras
Description: It’s not just the competitive prices that will bring you back, but above all the fragrant authenticity of Emilian cooking. Among the first courses, the “golden” specialties stand out, namely the fresh egg pastas: tortellini with 24-month Parmigiano cream and traditional lasagne verdi. The main courses are dominated by the indulgent cotechino with stewed beans and an impeccable bollito misto, while the ideal finale is entrusted to the celebrated zuppa inglese. In warmer months, tables in the intimate Piazza della Pomposa lend an even more charming atmosphere.

Name: Trattoria Rensin
Description: To his friends, he was simply ‘’u Rensin’: it was he who founded this charming family-run trattoria in the Ligurian hinterland. Today, it is his sons, Simone and Roberto, who carry on his legacy, continuing to prepare traditional regional recipes with passion and genuine hospitality. The cuisine is simple, generous and full of flavour, featuring seafood specialities such as fish soups and mussels marinara, alongside tasty meat dishes. Don’t miss the fresh, hand-rolled pasta, particularly the famous green lasagne with pesto. Given its long-standing popularity, we recommend booking well in advance.

Name: Trattoria Toscana al Vecchio Forno
Address: Via Poliziano 18, San Quirico d'Orcia, 53027, Italy
Description: In the heart of San Quirico d’Orcia, an intimate trattoria welcomes guests with two small rooms on the upper floor, a main dining room animated by the warmth of the fireplace and an elegant pergola garden that opens during the warmer months. The setting, rustic and genuine, provides the backdrop for cooking deeply rooted in tradition: meats and game, the aromas of truffle and hand-rolled pasta tell the story of the territory with authenticity. Completing the experience, a well-constructed wine list, rich in local labels, accompanies the gastronomic journey with understated expertise.

Name: Trattoria al Pompiere
Description: Founded by a firefighter over a century ago, this venue delivers all the warmth and character of a quintessential Italian trattoria. Wine bottles, wood paneling, checkered tablecloths, cured meats, cheeses, and vintage photographs lining the walls: everything in the dining room creates an informal, relaxing atmosphere. Unsurprisingly, the menu draws inspiration from Venetian classics.

Name: Trattoria al Ponte
Address: Via Bertolda 27, località Bornio, Lusia, 45020, Italy
Description: Recognized as the only “Historic Establishment of Italy” in the province of Rovigo, this inviting, family-run trattoria offers traditional cooking with a strong emphasis on meat dishes, served in typically generous portions. The menu is enhanced by daily specials, shared verbally, which can be enjoyed in the warm, welcoming dining rooms or on the charming terrace at the entrance. A park with a natural pond and swimming pool provides an ideal setting also for events.

Name: Trattoria alla Pergola
Description: An old-fashioned trattoria with a simple, homely atmosphere which attracts guests from all over the province who are drawn here by the classic, unfussy regional cuisine. Although the menu is concise, it includes specialities such as tortelli, tortellini, the region’s famous risottos (this is rice-growing country) and renowned boiled meats. Make sure you leave room for the tempting dessert trolley.

Name: Trattoria da Me
Description: Lively and much frequented, this trattoria guided by the energetic Elisa owes its success to a well-judged balance between dishes of the tradition – with fresh pastas prepared by the sfogline and also available for purchase in the adjoining shop – and offerings that draw upon more contemporary techniques. Among the specialities not to be missed are the tagliolini with friggione and squacquerone cream: a thoroughly satisfying and well-balanced dish. For those drawn to the flavours of another age, Sunday is the day to seek out the classic lasagne alla bolognese on the menu, prepared according to time-honoured tradition. The terrace, available even in winter, lends a further note of pleasure to the experience.

Name: Trattoria da Pina di Maniaci
Description: It is definitely worth travelling the 15 kilometres from Vulcano Porto, all across the island, to reach this historic, family-run trattoria, overlooking the sea in the small hamlet of Gelso. Founded by our great-grandparents in 1958, the same family still preserves its identity today, faithfully upholding the Aeolian tradition through authentic, aromatic cuisine deeply rooted in the island’s local heritage: must-try dishes include the raw seafood platters, the pasta dishes – from the classic ‘alla Norma’ to those with sardines – and, to follow, the catch of the day, served fried or grilled, with specialities such as ‘pesce alla cipollata’, a little house speciality. As it is very well-known and popular, it is advisable to book well in advance to secure a table.

Name: Trattoria dall'Antonia
Description: Situated just outside Venice in a quiet area dotted with splendid private villas, this historic restaurant occupies a delightful 19C mansion overlooking the Brenta canal. In the fully renovated, simple and welcoming dining room, fish and seafood reign supreme, with dishes such as raw pink or red Sicilian prawns, Adriatic scampi and tender, lightly seared octopus on the menu. The first courses include classic fish and seafood options, while delicious mixed fried fish from the Adriatic and local turbot are among the stand-out main courses.

Name: Trattoria del Bivio
Description: Situated at an altitude of 700 metres, in the heart of the Alta Langa, this establishment offers a compelling take on Piedmontese tradition in surroundings that combine rustic charm with contemporary comfort. The cuisine showcases the region’s finest produce, from mushrooms to truffles, including fresh homemade pasta such as tajarin and agnolotti del plin, right through to the excellent local meats. Particular attention is also paid to bread-making, with naturally leavened bread and focaccia deserving a special mention. The experience can be rounded off with a stay in one of the property’s few rooms and, in the warmer months, with lunch or dinner on the panoramic terrace, caressed by the cool breeze from the hills.

Name: Trattoria del Bollito
Address: Via Don Giacomo Alberione 3/e, Alba, 12051, Italy
Description: This trattoria in the heart of Alba welcomes guests into a warm, family atmosphere, where wood panelling and smiling staff create a sense of intimacy. The service is dynamic and polite, while aromas from the kitchen evoke Piedmontese tradition. The carefully curated wine list celebrates local labels from throughout the Langhe, inviting guests to discover authentic flavours. One of the most popular dishes is tajarin with rabbit and hazelnuts: thin strands of pasta paired with delicate meat and crunchy hazelnuts, creating a delicious and comforting balance.

Name: Trattoria del Cimino dal 1895
Description: A long, uphill straight runs through the historic centre of Caprarola and leads to the extraordinary Palazzo Farnese. Before reaching it, on the left, lies a stop no less famed, at least gastronomically speaking. The figures alone are impressive: housed in a building dating back to 1370, run by the same family since 1895 and now in its fifth generation, this is a temple of Tuscia cuisine, northern Lazio, albeit with some Tuscan influence. Here one finds dishes so full of flavour that one would happily eat them every day. No less significant is the wine service: around 900 labels, with a wide choice also available by the glass, expertly managed by Samuele Calistri, the cook’s son, who returned to the family after significant international experience in starred restaurants to carry on the legend of this extraordinary trattoria.

Name: Trattoria del Nuovo Macello
Description: Named after the slaughterhouse opened opposite the premises in 1927, this restaurant was taken over 30 years later by the grandfather of one of the current partners, as he was convinced that the restaurant’s busy location would contribute to its success – and he wasn’t wrong! The traditional, regional cuisine served here is reinterpreted with a contemporary flavour and includes delicious specialities such as cotoletta alla milanese made from meat matured for 40 days.

Name: Trattoria del Pesce
Description: A good selection of fresh and raw fish dishes served in a welcoming, vaguely bistro-style restaurant with young and competent staff. Parking can be difficult, but your patience is definitely rewarded!

Name: Trattoria del Vicolo
Description: Overlooking the piazza for almost 50 years, this restaurant has been modernised but has nonetheless managed to retain its friendly ambience, especially in the outdoor space facing the narrow alleyway. The owner-chef serves regional specialities reinterpreted with his own individual twist, such as his famous swordfish rolls served in a type of pie.

Name: Trattoria della Posta
Description: Standing in open countryside, this country restaurant is decorated with elegant and romantic touches, such as silverware and candles. The menu features regional cuisine, including an excellent selection of the best local cheeses. Friendly welcome and experienced service.

Name: Trattoria di Campagna
Description: This famous trattoria, now run by the third generation of the same family, serves traditional, seasonal cuisine from the Aosta valley, enhanced by the occasional imaginative and personalised touch. The new well-stocked wine cellar includes a table for a dozen guests, while sommelier Beatrice is on hand to assist guests with their choice of bottle. Excellent array of delicacies from the dessert trolley.

Name: Trattoria di Coronate
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a splendid 16C farmhouse just a few minutes from the beautiful Morimondo abbey, this restaurant has an elegant and friendly ambience. The wooden ceiling and furniture in the dining room gives it a warm and welcoming feel, while the cuisine, deeply rooted in the region, is reinterpreted with a contemporary twist. The delicious options on the menu include highlights such as quail breast with a thigh-meat “lollipop” and ravioli stuffed with braised beef.

Name: Trattoria la Colonna
Address: Via Emilia Est 6, località San Nicolò, Rottofreno, 29010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This classic-style restaurant with a recently renovated dining room is situated on the street that runs through the village of San Nicolò. Although the menu features some meat dishes (on Sundays in winter, this includes specialities such as boiled meats, preceded by anolini pasta in broth and ending with typical desserts such as ciambella cake with zabaione), it is particularly renowned for its wide selection of fish dishes. At lunchtime during the week, there’s a choice of simpler recipes, but if you ask, staff will be happy to offer you the longer evening menu.

Name: Trattoria la Rosa 1908
Address: Via del Bosco 2, ang. via Facchini, Sant'Agostino, 44047, Italy
Description: On the outskirts of Ferrara, this classic-style restaurant, run reliably by the same family for five generations, serves cuisine based mainly around local ingredients. Highlights include homemade fresh pasta (their tortellini in broth or served with a delicious creamy Parmigiano Reggiano sauce are excellent) and truffles, served mainly on fresh-egg pasta and risottos but also on some main courses such as foil-baked guinea fowl with fried cream and roast potatoes.

Name: Tre Galline
Description: A bastion of traditional Piedmontese cuisine, the main dining room at this restaurant boasts a profusion of wood from its parquet flooring to the wood panelling and exposed roofbeams. The warm, hearty cuisine features local specialities such as vitello tonnato, agnolotti pasta with roast meat sauce and a selection of mixed boiled meats, as well as a cheese trolley.

Name: Tre Noci
Description: Situated in the centre of a village in the Bassa Bergamasca area, this long-established, family-run restaurant has a rustic decor softened by the owners’ female touch. The overall feel is that of an elegant trattoria, which provides a pleasant backdrop for delicious specialities from this lowland region, including meat cooked over the large grill in the dining room. There’s also a gazebo for alfresco dining in summer.

Name: Tre Scalini
Description: The menu at this restaurant features meat and seasonal ingredients served in personalised recipes and contemporary-style dishes. There are also three tasting menus: the main one consists of eight courses prepared by the talented chef. The restaurant brings to mind a modern bistro with its warm ambience and attentive service.

Name: Trequarti
Address: Piazza del Donatore 3/4, Val Liona, 36044, Italy
Description: A minimalist-pop, contemporary setting brimming with character, offering a constantly evolving culinary experience that takes a creative approach to modern cuisine. Chef Alberto Basso creates original and thoughtfully crafted dishes, such as Scardovari mussels in a light soup with parsley and candied orange, venison carpaccio with rosemary shortcrust pastry and raspberries, or yuzu and Sichuan pepper namelaka served with an exotic soup. As well as the à la carte menu, you can choose the ‘Fun Dining’ tasting menu or the cicheti set menus, available as sets of five, six or seven samples.

Name: Tribuna Campitelli
Address: Via della Tribuna di Campitelli 18, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: Overlooking a quiet area, mere steps from the Isola Tiberina and the Palatine, the establishment presents itself in the warmer months with a pleasant outdoor seating that welcomes the guest immediately. The culinary proposal follows a clean and Mediterranean line, with a broad menu ranging from raw fish to oysters, passing through well-executed first courses, such as the accomplished Felicetti squid pasta with raw and cooked prawns. Among the main courses, characterful preparations stand out, above all the Campitelli fish soup, the authentic signature of the chefs and a true indulgence. The spaces, modern and carefully appointed, are arranged in rooms capable of guaranteeing an intimate atmosphere. In service, professionalism and savoir-faire complete the experience.

Name: Trippi
Address: Via Stelvio 297, Loc. Montagna in Valtellina, Sondrio, 23020, Italy
Description: This long-established restaurant just outside Sondrio has been run for the past decade by Gianluca, whose experience injects new life into traditional dishes from the local region, as well as introducing the occasional Mediterranean twist. There’s a simpler menu at lunchtime, plus a good selection of local wines and cheeses on sale at takeaway prices near the restaurant entrance.

Name: Trippini
Address: Via Italia 14, Civitella del Lago, 05023, Italy
Description: Just a few tables and spectacular views of Lake Corbara characterise this restaurant, which has been run by the same family since 1964. The delicious cuisine is regional in flavour, showcasing home-cooked recipes and typical Sunday favourites yet with a contemporary twist that incorporates plenty of intense flavours.

Name: Trita Pepe
Address: Via Gabriele D'Annunzio 4, Manoppello Scalo, 65024, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the road that passes through Manoppello Scalo, this restaurant with a car park right in front of the building boasts a spacious, simple dining room and is our recommended choice in the region for anyone keen to try typical Abruzzo cuisine. Meat takes pride of place among the main courses (with an exception for salted cod), while menu highlights include excellent fried gnocchi with local salumi and cheese.

Name: Truth Restaurant
Description: A contemporary-style restaurant with an open-view kitchen where two different styles of cuisine can be enjoyed: creative tapas influenced by different traditions, or more classic local dishes. The restaurant is particularly renowned for its choice of around a dozen imaginative small appetisers.

Name: Tubladel
Description: Although this restaurant with wood-adorned dining rooms has the rustic and romantic ambience of an old Alpine hut (the name “tubladel” is the Ladin for hay barn), it is actually situated just a stone’s throw from the centre of Ortisei. The cuisine focuses on local ingredients such as meat and game, with dishes such as venison pappardelle and roast pork shank on the menu, and very few fish options. Good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Tuorlo
Description: Decorated in elegant bistro style and skilfully renovated with contemporary furnishings, Tuorlo serves dishes based on traditional Piedmontese recipes reinterpreted with modern techniques and personal touches. Good choice of wines, plus an attractive little courtyard to the rear for relaxed summer dining.

Name: Téa del Kosmo
Description: Leaving one’s car in the car park, a lift carries guests directly to the third floor, where the restaurant Kosmo Taste the Mountain is situated; from here one is accompanied through to the Téa del Kosmo, its gourmet offshoot. ‘Téa’ means mountain chalet in the Valtellina dialect, and the atmosphere evokes precisely that of a modern alpine refuge, clad in reclaimed timbers, with a fireplace at its centre and just four tables arranged around it, for an intimate and quietly immersive experience. Booking online allows guests to choose between two or three tasting menus (depending on the season) all built upon alpine ingredients and the careful use of vegetables from the house kitchen garden, interpreted with creativity by chef Michele Talarico. Apulian by origin – as the excellent bread readily suggests – he is deeply enamoured of these mountains and brings to the table a cuisine that seeks to honour every part of the ingredient. Not to be missed is the spaghetti alla chitarra, made in-house with stale bread and dressed with a sauce of dill, garum and trout bottarga, both crafted by the chef himself. Equally unmissable are his vegetarian studies, such as the celeriac or the ‘100% carrot’: dishes that linger long in the memory.

Name: U' Vulesce
Description: Born as a delicatessen over sixty years ago, and now enhanced by an offering of aperitifs accompanied by small plates, the Di Donna family has created a solid and well-structured restaurant dedicated to the finest products of this generous region. Spanning land and sea, cured meats and cheeses, it is above all patron Rosario who guides guests through their choices, enhancing each proposal with a carefully curated wine selection.

Name: UMA Roma
Description: A restaurant with an innovative concept, placing at the heart of the experience three chefs working on two distinct tasting menus: one entirely plant-based and one that also includes animal proteins. The guiding idea is clear and well expressed in the dishes: a single ingredient becomes the absolute protagonist, explored through different techniques and showcased in all its parts. For those seeking creative cooking with an excellent quality-price ratio, this is the right place. The setting is pleasant, refined and defined by pared-back design; the majority of tables overlook the open kitchen directly, allowing guests to follow the crew’s work closely and experience the meal with an engaging extra touch.

Name: Ulìa
Address: SP 59 bis direzione baia Sardinia, in Località Cascioni, Arzachena, 07021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled in the heart of nature, within an 18-hectare park dotted with over 3,000 olive trees – from which the estate’s olive oil is produced – the Cascioni Eco Retreat (1 Michelin Key), housed in an old farmhouse with rustic-bohemian charm, has for the past two seasons welcomed chef Salvatore Camedda to its restaurant, Ulìa. Camedda previously headed up the Michelin-starred restaurant Somu in Baia Sardinia (currently closed). His cuisine is modern with a Mediterranean influence, sensitively showcasing the Sardinian region through balanced, contemporary dishes; his work with lamb is particularly noteworthy, featuring prominently in a range of dishes – from charcoal-grilled lamb to croquettes and cured meats – demonstrating both technical skill and creativity. Far from the hustle and bustle of the Costa Smeralda, the restaurant is set in a setting of absolute tranquillity: the ideal spot to treat yourself to a moment of genuine relaxation while savouring the chef’s cuisine on the terrace overlooking the swimming pool.

Name: Umami
Address: Via Ugo Secondo Partigiano 1, Badalucco, 18010, Italy
Description: A young chef, strengthened by experience in important kitchens, has brought the village’s old nursery school back to life, carefully restoring it and transforming it into a restaurant that proposes contemporary cooking with more or less overt ties to the local area. The offering is structured around tasting menus, from which individual dishes may also be chosen à la carte. Among the dishes not to be missed is the marinated brown meagre fillet with seasonal vegetables: impeccable cooking, convincing pairings and a harmonious balance that leaves its mark. In summer, a wonderful outdoor space, almost overlooking the banks of the Argentina river – which gives its name to the entire valley – provides a particularly evocative setting, perfect for completing the gastronomic experience.

Name: Umberto De Martino
Address: Via Madonna d'Argon 4/6, San Paolo d'Argon, 24060, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Part of the Florian Maison hotel in a bucolic setting of rolling hills, this large, elegant restaurant serves as a backdrop for tasting menus from which guests can choose dishes (three or more) à la carte style on weekday lunchtimes. Originally from the Sorrentine peninsula, chef Umberto Sorrentino’s origins clearly influence some of his recipes, which feature vegetables and plenty of fish alongside a few meat options.

Name: Un Posto a Milano
Description: In the heart of Cascina Cuccagna, among green courtyards and an atmosphere of times gone by, nestled within the urban fabric of Milan, this restaurant offers a pleasant retreat where you can enjoy a break in the open air. The cuisine celebrates Italian tradition, sometimes with a contemporary twist, using fresh and, where possible, organic-certified ingredients. The holm oak charcoal grill produces dishes full of character, such as free-range cockerel, marinated and slow-cooked before being grilled over the coals, served with golden, crispy roast potatoes. The experience is rounded off by the farmstead’s lively cultural programme, which, from October to May, features jazz concerts on Tuesday evenings during dinner.

Name: Urubamba
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In the heart of one of Naples’s most exclusive districts, among luxury boutiques and historic palazzi, the experience unfolds on the first floor: an intimate dining room bathed in soft lighting, conveying a romantic and sophisticated atmosphere. On fine days, the additional privilege of a private terrace makes for a dinner of even greater allure. The cuisine proves equal to the elegance of its surroundings, with an offering that successfully embraces the world of Nikkei cuisine, the now-iconic meeting of Peru and Japan. A harmonious gastronomic dialogue, in which technique, flavour and cross-cultural influence intertwine in balanced, contemporary dishes.

Name: Vairo del Volturno
Address: Via IV Novembre 58, Vairano Patenora, 81058, Italy
Description: Situated in the beautiful Volturno valley, this excellent restaurant boasts classic decor and a relaxed atmosphere. Here, owner-chef Renato Martino succeeds in expressing his love for the region in his dishes, which include the famous Black Casertano suckling pig, duck, lamb and the renowned buffalo mozzarella. The fish is also excellent, with mullet, John Dory and bream all featuring on the menu.

Name: Valli di Lanzo
Description: The sign outside this restaurant in the centre of the typical village of Céres bears the words “Ristourànt Valàdess at Lanss con Oubèrgi”. Enjoy regional cuisine with a personalised twist, with local products from the valley featuring in many of the specialities served here, all accompanied by a good selection of regional, Italian and international wines. Outdoor dining area available in summer.

Name: VeRo - Venetian Roots
Description: Within the elegant Ca’ di Dio, in the beating heart of the Biennale, VeRo is an exclusive restaurant with contemporary flair. The cuisine reflects the chef’s soul: essential, personal, never predictable. Two tasting journeys, with freedom to choose between dishes and desserts, complete the experience.

Name: Vecchia Sorni
Description: In this small, charming village, you can dine in the traditional dining rooms with their stone-vaulted ceilings, or opt for the breathtaking view of the valley from the covered veranda. Creative cuisine, featuring both meat and fish.

Name: Vecio Macello
Description: A former early 20th-century slaughterhouse, today you’ll find a restaurant with a pleasantly classic atmosphere and a kitchen that, despite the building’s original purpose, serves predominantly seafood dishes, though with some meat classics.

Name: Ventuno.1
Description: Major refurbishment at this renowned restaurant has given it the feel of an informal, welcoming contemporary bistro. Don’t miss the “Napule” tasting menu, which offers just four courses that include anchovies, cavatelli pasta and Neapolitan meatballs in a nod to the owner’s origins. Over time, the wine list has been extended and improved, with wines now stored in a new cellar. Some of the ingredients used in the dishes can also be purchased to take home.

Name: Veranda
Description: Alberto Faccani, the chef at the Magnolia restaurant in the hills inland from Cesenatico, oversees the cuisine at this restaurant, which occupies an elegant veranda on the town’s main avenue – a busy promenade in summer. Fish takes centre stage here, in unfussy dishes that faithfully reflect the maritime traditions of the Adriatic. The menu, alongside daily specials announced at your table, features dishes that include raw fish and seafood, gratins, seafood salads, pasta and risotto, while the main courses feature a selection of grilled, baked and fried fish.

Name: Verbano
Address: Via Ugo Ara 2, Isola dei Pescatori, Stresa, 28838, Italy
Description: Within the confines of the small, charming Verbano hotel on the beautiful island of Pescatori, chef Marco Sacco serves top-quality cuisine in what can only be described as a stunning setting. The contemporary-style dining room boasts panoramic windows, while the outdoor terrace with its views of Palazzo Borromeo and Isola Bella is the perfect setting for dinner in fine weather.

Name: Vescovo Moro
Description: Situated 50 metres from the basilica of San Zeno (the patron saint of Verona), this restaurant housed in a renovated workshop boasts plenty of outdoor space for summer dining. Here, enjoy eclectic cuisine with an equal balance of Mediterranean and traditional flavours, including an excellent array of raw fish dishes and a small selection of Italian caviar.

Name: Vesta Versilia
Address: Viale Roma 2, Marina di Pietrasanta, 55044, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within Twiga beach establishment, in a setting where glamour reigns supreme, multifunctional and equipped with a fully-fledged cocktail bar, the cuisine favours classic recipes and cooking methods, but equally dedicates substantial attention to raw seafood and pizza. From our last visit, the seafood salad—boasting excellent varied citronette-dressed products—and the roast turbot with lemon potato cream and asparagus stand particularly memorable.

Name: Vico Astemio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Hidden among the lanes of the historic centre, this small restaurant wins over its guests through substance rather than spectacle. The tables are distributed along an evocative narrow alleyway, while inside a dining room framed by ancient stone arches preserves all the character of the historic building. The atmosphere and service maintain a simple and informal character, leaving the dishes to capture the attention. Chef-patron Massimiliano Vasta presents a cuisine that is essential and rigorous, founded on the absolute quality of the raw material and on preparations that bring out its identity without unnecessary artifice. Emblematic is the beef antipasto, enhanced by a grating of salted egg yolk, as are the fish dishes, in which freshness and precision of execution prevail over any pursuit of special effects. The wine list – centred primarily on Sicily yet enriched by interesting forays into Slovenia, Austria, Germany and France – offers labels of excellent quality at fair prices, with a selection also available by the glass.

Name: Villa Arcadio
Address: Via Palazzina 2, Località Villa di Salò, Salò, 25087, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: The new chef at this restaurant prioritises beautiful presentation in his modern interpretations of Italian dishes, which are even more enjoyable in summer when meals are served outdoors, surrounded by greenery and with fine views of the southern part of Lake Garda and its shoreline.

Name: Villa Baroni
Description: Overlooking the lake and set among lush greenery, this small historic villa captivates visitors with its romantic charm and cosy atmosphere. Guests can choose between the elegant indoor dining room and a stunning panoramic terrace, which is ideal for enjoying the view while savouring high-quality cuisine that places particular emphasis on seafood specialities. The holiday experience is rounded off by cosy Provençal-style rooms and a lovely swimming pool set among the grounds, reserved for guests of the hotel. A place that combines hospitality, tranquillity and fine dining in one of the area’s most picturesque lakeside settings.

Name: Villa De Winckels
Address: Via Sorio 30, Località Marcemigo, Tregnago, 37039, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This 16C villa, a period residence with many intimate dining rooms, boasts a picture-postcard setting. The cuisine is typical of the Veneto region, with dishes such as home-made pasta (with or without stuffing) and home-produced charcuterie on the menu. Named after General De Winckels who once lived here, the Cantina del Generale offers a wide selection of the best vintages which include local wines and labels from further field, with a focus on Amarone wines.

Name: Villa Fiordaliso
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Villa Fiordaliso is one of the beautiful early 20C villas that line the lake front. Surrounded by verdant grounds and extending out into the lake on a pontoon, the restaurant serves creative, modern cuisine. The chef is equally at ease with fish and meat dishes, while the extensive wine list suggests that you’ll have no problem finding your favourite wine here.

Name: Villa Giulia - Al Terrazzo
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Housed within an elegant late-19C hotel overlooking the lake, this romantic restaurant offers stunning views from its outdoor terrace. The cuisine is mainly Italian, with the occasional modern and imaginative twist. Add in a charming stone wine cellar stocked with top-quality labels, plus modern guestrooms for anyone wanting to prolong their stay.

Name: Villa Pignano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: A veritable Garden of Eden just 15km from Volterra, this 300ha estate is home to a restaurant with a strong zero-mile philosophy. This is backed up by its careful use of ingredients grown or produced on the estate itself, such as vegetables, olives and grains, as well as chicken, pork and honey – a sustainable approach that results in delicious, contemporary cuisine. The dishes here are fresh and full of flavour yet elaborate and modern in style (note the simpler menu at lunchtime). The interesting wine list explores Tuscany through its choice of top-quality organic labels as well as including wines produced from the estate’s own vines.

Name: Villa Salina
Description: Named after Edoardo Salina, the chef to the House of Savoy, this villa from the mid-1800s features several rooms embellished with frescoed ceilings. The bold owner-chef here has completely restored the building, bringing it back to life and using it as a backdrop for his evolving culinary skills which started out in the family pasticceria. Nowadays, this “multi-tasking” modern restaurant offers a regionally inspired à la carte alongside fish dishes and a business menu option at lunchtime, while in the evening the menu includes a selection of high-quality pizzas. In summer, the dining room opens out onto a beautiful veranda and guests can also wander through the well-kept garden, which is now owned by the local municipality.

Name: Villa Tiboldi
Address: Via Case Sparse 127, Località Tiboldi, Canale, 12043, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: A delightful combination of good food and a romantic ambience in this old restored farmhouse surrounded by hills. Top - quality cuisine and a wine cellar that is well worth a visit.

Name: Vincenzo Degasperi
Description: Situated in the busy heart of the town, the Zur Post hotel offers its guests a warm, homely welcome, discreet charm and Alpine elegance, while its contemporary-style wine-bar boasts a relaxed and friendly atmosphere. Here, Vincenzo Degasperi, the soul of the restaurant, oversees his guests’ experience with elegant professionalism and genuine hospitality, serving delicious Italian cuisine prepared from the best fresh ingredients. The superb wines are showcased on a skilfully chosen wine list, from which intriguing pairings are also available by the glass.

Name: Vini da Gigio
Address: Calle Stua Cannaregio, sestiere Cannaregio 3628, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description: In the district of Cannaregio, a rustic environment and informal service in an inn where you can see into the kitchen, and which offers both fish and meat dishes; a good choice of wines.

Name: Vino Buono
Address: Via Castello 20, Grumello del Monte, 24064, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In an atmospheric 17th-century barn, adjacent to the cathedral bell tower, takes shape a wine bar of considerable charm. Here to welcome guests is Roberto, patron and cellarman at once, discreet and warm, always ready to share the stories of wines and their local areas. In accompaniment, simple, straightforward cooking with a homely, traditional character, well executed and full of personality, with occasional forays into seafood. Not to be missed are the selection of cured meats and cheeses and the excellent primi piatti, genuine highlights of the offering.

Name: Viride by Carlo Cracco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: A stone’s throw from Montecitorio, the newly opened Corinthia houses Viride, the gastronomic offering signed by Carlo Cracco and entrusted to the kitchen of Alessandro Buffolino, a young Campanian chef with a solid and mature path. The menu reflects a balance between identity and contemporaneity, with particular attention given to dishes for sharing, the true protagonists of the experience: among these, preparations such as the guinea fowl or the grilled veal, designed for two, stand out for their depth of flavour and their spirit of conviviality. Considerable space, befitting Cracco’s declared passion, is dedicated to wine, with an extensive and carefully curated cellar that includes interesting selections offered also by the glass. It is worthwhile entrusting yourself to the guidance of the sommelier team led by Stefania Ruggieri. The welcoming open-air internal garden, of authentically Roman charm, completes it all.

Name: Visione Restaurant and Living
Address: Strada Nicolini Basso 34, loc. Tre Stelle, Barbaresco, 12050, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Set within the elegant Casa Nicolini hotel, nestled in a peaceful and scenic spot among the hills, the restaurant offers a dining experience that combines local produce, creativity and character. From the dining room’s large windows, the view stretches out over the surrounding landscape, while in the warmer months the terrace becomes the ideal spot to enjoy the outdoor atmosphere, also hosting the bar and the Bistrot’s more casual menu in a dedicated area. In the kitchen, Samuele Di Murro crafts his culinary narrative through three tasting menus: one inspired by tradition, one with a more contemporary and creative approach, and a third ‘freestyle’ menu, guided by the inspiration of the moment and the availability of the finest ingredients. All dishes are also available à la carte, giving you greater freedom in composing your meal. In the dining room, Luca Orilia leads a young, well-trained and close-knit team, capable of attending to guests with precise and professional explanations, with discretion and natural warmth.

Name: Visteria
Description: Situated in the Royal Victoria hotel on picturesque Varenna’s small central piazza, this restaurant has just a few tables overlooking one of the most spectacular sights on Lake Como, namely the Bellagio promontory flanked on either side by the two branches of the lake. Talented chef Francesco Sarno, originally from Salerno, is at the helm in the kitchen here – the colour and intense flavours of his native Campania are evident in some of his dishes.

Name: Vita Pugliese
Description: Situated a stone’s throw from the castle and the cathedral in the historic centre, this restaurant boasts an attractive outdoor space in an alleyway and traditional dining rooms with barrel-vaulted ceilings. Here, enjoy authentic dishes from Puglia with the occasional creative twist and careful attention to presentation.

Name: Vite
Address: Via Montepirolo 7, Località Cerasolo, Coriano, 47853, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated within the San Patrignano community, which grows its own crops, raises its own livestock and makes its own cheeses, Vite is now the setting for new, talented chef Giuseppe Biuso’s cuisine, which is made from top-quality ingredients using modern, creative techniques. His Mediterranean dishes are also inspired by his native Sicily, and include several vegetarian specialities. In summer, don’t miss the outdoor dining space which offers fine views of the surrounding countryside.

Name: Vitello d'Oro
Description: In the heart of the historic center, this restaurant traces its roots to 1849 and intertwines its story with that of the Sabinot family, guardians of tradition since the 1960s. The interiors surprise with sober, contemporary design that dialogs with the memory of the place. Don’t be misled by the name: fish takes center stage, with iconic dishes such as the spaghetto enveloped in bottarga and clams, while seasonal vegetables add freshness and color. Those who prefer meat will also find thoughtfully crafted options.

Name: Vitis
Description: A modern wine bar in the centre of Bressanone (Brixen), situated in the same building as the delightful family restaurant, the Oste Scuro. Here, small armchairs, benches and stools are dotted among low square tables and higher tables, all surrounded by walls completely lined with wine bottles. The contemporary cuisine features tempting, generous dishes such as cod with cauliflower, cavolo nero and beurre blanc. Accommodation is available just two minutes’ away in the historic Adler Historic Guesthouse run by the same owners.

Name: Vivilo
Address: Via Nazario Sauro 15, Corte Franca, 25040, Italy
Description: An old hay barn has been converted into this elegant restaurant offering impeccable service and delicious cuisine with a focus on classic dishes, including a vegetarian menu, an excellent cheese trolley and not-to-be-missed desserts. In other words, everything you need for a superb dining experience among the Franciacorta vineyards!

Name: Voce Aimo e Nadia
Description: Situated in the heart of Milan, this restaurant owned by the historic Aimo e Nadia in Via Montecuccoli is accessed via its bar-cum-pastry shop which includes a bistro serving a selection of simpler dishes. From here, you enter the main dining room with an open-view kitchen serving excellent Italian dishes reinterpreted in contemporary style. Voce in Giardino, the restaurant’s outdoor summer dining space adorned with interesting sculptures, is a green oasis in the heart of the city.

Name: Voltalacarta
Description: A tiny doorway leads to this simple, friendly and intimate restaurant with just a few tables, where booking in advance is highly recommended given the restaurant’s excellent reputation in the city. Its renown stems from the owner-chef’s cuisine, which focuses mainly on top-quality fish prepared in imaginative and personalised recipes using classic techniques. If it’s on the menu, make sure you try the “cappon magro” (a type of seafood salad), which is so good that it even has its own identity card!

Name: Waby
Address: Via Carlo De Cristoforis 2, Milan, 20124, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: Milan is becoming increasingly known in Italy for its impressive choice of ethnic cuisine, and one example among many is this excellent restaurant behind Corso Como and Piazza Gae Aumenti. With its contemporary design, including a counter with stools to the rear, and international ambience, the restaurant serves modern, attractive Japanese cuisine, including creative raw dishes (such as raw tuna noodles in dashi broth with a sprinkling of yuzu, topped with salmon roe marinated in sake), sushi and sashimi, uramaki and gozya, robata and much more, with a constant focus on top-quality ingredients. The excellent wine selection features labels from Italy and France (including a number of champagnes), as well as a good choice of sake, also available by the glass.

Name: Walser Schtuba
Description: This delightful Alpine - style restaurant stands in the picturesque upper section of the Val Formazza. The menu features local specialities reinterpreted with a light, modern twist. Outdoor dining in summer.

Name: Walter Redaelli
Description: In this old 18C farmhouse with exposed brickwork, roof beams and an impressive fireplace, enjoy delicious Tuscan cuisine prepared from local ingredients, with a particular focus on meat. Specialities on the menu include pappa al pomodoro, home-made pici pasta, and sliced veal. Comfortable chairs add to the cosy and enjoyable dining experience.

Name: Wicky's Innovative Japanese Cuisine
Description: Although the contemporary, minimalist-style decor is typical of Japanese restaurants, the cuisine will come as more of a surprise, with its magical blend of classic Japanese dishes made from Mediterranean ingredients, beautifully presented and full of flavour. There are two dining rooms: one overlooking the road, and the other with an open-view kitchen and sushi bar, where the chef serves an evening tasting menu for guests happy to put their faith in his imaginative improvisational skills.

Name: Wine & Dine
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: In the center of Canazei, this restaurant within the Croce Bianca hotel occupies wood-paneled rooms that foster a relaxed, informal atmosphere, with a few charming alcoves for more intimate seating. Meat reigns supreme, notably a dedicated selection of grilled main courses. A good assortment of wines by the glass.

Name: Winter Garden Florence
Description: Once entered by carriages, the ancient courtyard of the St. Regis – generous in scale and dramatic in its proportions – has today been transformed into a refined winter garden. Among the sofas and armchairs embracing the cocktail bar – where the aperitivo is an almost indispensable ritual – this venue preserves a charm of another era, with precious marbles, carpets, plants and Murano glass chandeliers, while at the centre a pianist provides an elegant accompaniment to the atmosphere. In the kitchen, the chef navigates a line that balances contemporary ambition with classic reassurance, drawing on the Mediterranean tradition of both land and sea. The dishes stand out for their simplicity and attention to seasonality, with few ingredients elevated through precise technique and measured flavour.

Name: ZELO
Description: The elegant ZELO restaurant enjoys a beautiful setting in the garden of a 15C inner courtyard, which also boasts an attractive summer terrace. The cuisine is modern in style, created by a chef who uses the best Italian ingredients to prepare creative and contemporary dishes, as well as a few Italian classic favourites such as vitello tonnato and breaded veal. Some dishes are not available at lunchtime, when they are replaced by salads, while in the evening raw fish and seafood options take centre stage.

Name: Zamù
Description: This restaurant’s name comes from the initial syllables of the two restaurants that once stood here, which were combined and refurbished a few years ago. Now in the style of a modern bistro, Zamù serves traditional and generously portioned cuisine, plus a reasonably priced business menu at lunchtime. There’s an equal emphasis on meat and fish on the menu, while the clearly displayed blackboard lists the daily specials available.

Name: Zanze XVI
Address: Fondamenta dei Tolentini, Sestiere Santa Croce 231, Venice, 30135, Italy
Description: Although the setting and convivial atmosphere in this restaurant recall that of a typical Venetian bàcaro , the cuisine is completely different in feel. The ingredients are sourced from the best markets and local producers, resulting in unique dishes that reflect the culinary traditions of the lagoon and its surrounding area. The few tables arranged outdoors with views of the tranquil canal add to the appeal, while the professional yet friendly service helps to put guests completely at ease.

Name: Zero Milano
Description: “Zero” compromises when it comes to care and quality: the cuisine here is built on exceptional ingredients and rigorous Japanese technique. Under the guidance of Hide Shinohara, the crew presents pure Japanese gastronomy, centered on the highest quality products and the art of form. Beyond the à la carte, the Omakase tasting menu is highly recommended, where the chefs construct a blind journey of great interest and refinement. The dining room features white onyx panels, elegant minimalism, and soft lighting; at the traditional counter, in addition to observing the chefs’ dexterity up close, you can opt for a tasting prepared in the moment, further elevating the sensory experience.

Name: Zest
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Situated within the luxury Grand Hotel La Favorita in the centre of Sorrento, this restaurant has the traditional, opulent style of a grand hotel, while the outdoor terrace boasts the romantic charm that is typical of Sorrento. In the kitchen, the chef creates top-quality cuisine influenced by Campania and enhanced by his own creative touches, resulting in dishes such as marinated tuna with tonka beans, lemon gel and ginger mousse. There’s also a vegetarian tasting menu. A recently opened restaurant that is growing in popularity.

Name: Zivieri
Description: The produce of the hills come down into the city: this, in essence, is the restaurant.
