Within the mediaeval Torre Alberici, in the heart of the historic centre, the simple dining room furnished in a contemporary style showcases the produce that the Zivieri farm itself rears and cultivates in the Apennines. Regional cookery, therefore, of an excellent standard, with charcuterie and meats as the jewel in the crown, which moreover can also be purchased, along with cheeses and other foods, from their adjacent butcher’s shop.

Name: Zum Löwen
Description: The elegance and warmth of this restaurant remain unchanged, like a timeless signature. The cuisine, always attentive and in tune with contemporary tastes, offers more essential and straightforward dishes that convey local flavors with refined simplicity in the new "Wine & Dine" concept by Elisabeth. The charming interiors result from the skillful renovation of an old farmhouse, from the barn to the old stables, incorporating what was once outside; everything has been restored and enhanced with modern touches. A commendable service and an excellent wine cellar, built over the years, complete the delightful experience.

Name: Zur Kaiserkron
Description: In the heart of Bolzano, on the ground floor of the refined Palazzo Pock which grandly overlooks the piazza, Zur Kaiserkron (The Imperial Crown) welcomes guests in elegant, contemporary surroundings enhanced by striking vaulted ceilings that lend a touch of theatricality to the experience. Since 2025, chef Sinisgalli’s vision unfolds along two distinct paths, designed to suit different guests and moments of the day. The first offers a light, dynamic cuisine firmly anchored to the territory, where traditional flavors are reinterpreted with contemporary spirit, ideal for a city in constant motion. The second, housed in a gilded dining room with an almost suspended charm, represents the chef’s deeper, more creative soul: a gastronomic journey that delves into research, technique, and imagination, delivering an immersive experience of great intensity.

Name: Zàghara Restaurant
Description: Housed in the elegant Relais Villa Flora, this restaurant occupies a natural terrace with breathtaking views of the Nissene hills. The dishes are predominantly regional in style yet reinterpreted with a modern twist. There’s also a good wine selection with a focus on Sicilian and Italian labels.

Name: [bu:r]
Description: Eugenio Boer offers a 100% Italian menu which focuses on local ingredients, with the aim of showcasing some of Italy’s favourite dishes while at the same time supporting small-scale producers. However, this philosophy is in no way limited to respecting traditions – on the contrary, it offers the chef the freedom to express his own creativity via a selection of dishes which combine past and present. As a result, guests can choose between a concise à la carte and two different tasting menus: “I Classici” (meat-based dishes) and “Le Aromatiche”, which changes perspective by placing aromatic plants centre stage. In short, a flexible approach which offers guests a culinary experience that will certainly make an impression!

Name: da Omar
Address: Via Dante Alighieri 21, Lido di Jesolo, 30016, Italy
Description: Passion and enthusiasm overcome all obstacles and lead to the best results: this summarises the professional journey of the chef at this restaurant. He prepares fish dishes inspired by classic Italian cuisine, sometimes with a modern twist, but always using the best quality produce.

Name: i-Fame
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A delightful journey into the future: modern, bright rooms featuring a play of white, mirrors, and glass. The cuisine also looks forward without forgetting the past: the chef from Rimini starts with mostly local ingredients (a lot of Adriatic fish on the menu, but also some meat) to create modern recipes, always rich in flavor and substance. The dessert “i-CLOUD” is very good and refreshing: a cloud of soft and delicious yogurt foam covering a yogurt and vanilla panna cotta, accompanied by various sorbets. The outdoor space with greenery is also attractive.

Name: iPalici
Address: Via Antonello da Messina 3, Viagrande, 95029, Italy
Description: Set within a stunning estate with a swimming pool, this restaurant offers two complementary experiences: an informal à la carte lunch, to be enjoyed in a relaxed atmosphere, and a fine-dining dinner, which is more elaborate and ambitious. At the helm of the kitchen is chef Giuseppe Corda, who, following significant experience in Taormina’s finest restaurants, has developed a personal style that skilfully blends Sicilian tradition with elegant Japanese influences. Ingredients such as yuzu, wasabi, seaweed and yakitori thus complement local produce, giving rise to contemporary, well-balanced dishes full of character. The dinner centres on three five-course tasting menus – vegetarian, seafood and meat – designed to cater for different culinary preferences. The flexibility of the concept is particularly commendable, as it allows guests to freely combine dishes from the various menus, creating a bespoke culinary journey without compromising on the coherence and quality of the experience.

Name: il Pozzo
Address: Piazza Castello, Sant'Angelo in Colle, 53020, Italy
Description: In the heart of one of Tuscany’s most evocative medieval hamlets, Sant’Angelo in Colle, sisters Franca and Paola preserve and thoughtfully reinterpret the age-old recipes of regional tradition. What arrives at the table are dishes of authentic, honest flavour, lightened and brought up to date without ever betraying the identity and origin of the preparations. The dessert chapter is not to be missed, every offering executed with great care: the Yogurt Cake with strawberries stands out, indulgent and appealing, winning hearts from the very first taste thanks to its perfect balance of freshness and softness.

Name: l' Ciocio - Osteria di Suvereto
Description: Situated in the historic centre of the picturesque village of Suvereto, this restaurant boasts a traditional decor of wood and stone. The menu includes dishes made from the restaurant’s own grains, as well as a selection of meat and fish specialities.

Name: med
Address: Piazza del Quartiere Latino 13, Treviso, 31100, Italy
Description: In the pedestrian area of the town, with views of the Sile river from the ground floor, this attractive restaurant serves regional cuisine with a focus on local ingredients, prepared in a classic style attentive to modern tastes. There’s an excellent wine list, plus live music and a pleasant outdoor space for fine weather dining.

Name: À Putia - Enoteca e Cucina
Address: Via Umberto I° 456, Giardini Naxos, 98035, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: This restaurant began life in 1946 as a grocery store (the name is the Sicilian word for shop) which, forty years later, was transformed into a very simple yet attractive trattoria-cum-wine bar (don’t be shocked by the paper tablecloths!). The cuisine focuses mainly on fish, seafood and fresh market produce, while the wines come from Sicily and further afield. Booking ahead is essential here, partly because there are only a few tables but also because the opening hours vary depending on the season. You may find it difficult to find somewhere to park between the main street and the seafront in the busy town centre, but it’s well worth the effort.
